chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning Da'wah Towards Allaah and His Rasool
intro: This chapter highlights how calling people towards Allaah and towards Rasulullaah ﷺ was the action that Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah loved more than anything else. It also draws attention to the fact that their ardent desire was for mankind to be guided towards the Deen of Allaah and to enter its fold so that they may be immersed in Allaah's mercy. In addition to this, it focuses on their tireless efforts to achieve this so that the creation could be linked to their Creator.

chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning the Bay'ah
intro: This chapter highlights how the Sahabah (RA) pledged allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ and to the Khulafaa after Rasulullaah ﷺ and the conditions on which they pledged their allegiance

chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning the Hardships that Were Borne for The Pleasure of Allaah
intro: This chapter highlights how Rasuiullaah and the Sahabah (RA) endured hardships and difficulties, hunger and thirst to propagate the sound Deen and how they attached little importance to themselves when striving to elevate the word of Allaah Enduring Hardships for the Pleasure of Allaah

chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning Hijrah (Migration)
intro: "This chapter highlights how the Sahabah (RA) left their dearly loved homelands, an act that is extremely difficult for a person. They also left with the intention of never returning until their deaths. This chapter also highlights the fact that doing this was more beloved to them than the world and all its pleasures and that they gave preference to the Deen above mundane pleasures and were not concerned when these pleasures were lost. The chapter also emphasises how the Sahabah (RA) travelled from place to place to protect the Deen from evil, as if they were specially created for the Aakhirah and were its sons. It therefore appeared as if this world was created for them."

chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning Jihaad (Striving in the Path of Allaah)
intro: This chapter highlights how Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) strove in the path of Allaah and how they went out to give towards Allaah and towards His Rasool ﷺ regardless of whether their circumstances were favourable or unfavourable, or whether they had a choice or not. The chapter also makes clear how they prepared for this during times of difficulty and ease, summer or winter.

chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning the Importance that the Sahabah (RA) Attached to Unity
intro: This chapter highlights how the Sahabah (RA) attached great importance to unity in word and in deed and how they abstained from dissension and dispute in matters that had ramifications on Da'wah to Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ and matters of Jihaad.

chapters.title: The Chapter About How the Sahabah spent in the Path of Allaah
intro: This chapter highlights how Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) spent their wealth and everything that Allaah granted them in the pajh of Allaah and in avenues where Allaah's pleasure is found. The chapter also highlights how they loved this more than spending on themselves and how they preferred others above themselves even though they suffered poverty

chapters.title: The Chapter About How the Sahabah (RA) Relinquished their Carnal Desires
intro: This chapter highlights how the Sahabah (RA) relinquished the instinctive feelings they had for their parents, their children, their brothers, their spouses, their families, their wealth, their businesses and their homes so that they could cling to the loveof Allaah, the love of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the love of every Muslim attached to Allaah and Rasulullaah ﷺ, The chapter also highlights how honoured every person who had been attached to Rasulullaah ﷺ in anyway

chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning the Character of the Sahabah (RA) and their Noble Traits
intro: This chapter highlights the character and traits of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) and how they interacted with each other

chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning the Belief that the Sahabah (RA) Had in the Unseen
intro: This chapter highlights how the Sahabah (RA) believed in the unseen and how for the news Nabi ﷺ gave them, they forsook temporary pleasures, human evidence, transitory opinions and worldly experiences. It was as if they were actually witnessing the unseen and rejecting what they witnessed.

chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning the Sahabah (RA) Getting Together for Salaah
intro: ttttranra Getting Together for salaah This chapter highlights how Nabi ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) gathered together in the Masjid for salaah, how great was their fervour for this, how they encouraged others to do the same and how they understood that as they proceeded from salaah to salaah, they were required to allow their lives to progress from ene command of Allaah to another. It also highlights how they forsook their occupations to do the acts Allaah had commanded, which contributed to the strength of their Imaan and the features of their Imaan. The chapter also tells us how they spread their knowledge together with the deeds linked to knowledge, how they added life to Dhikr and made du'aa with all its requirements for acceptance. They therefore never turned their attention towards the apparent means and took no benefit except from the Creator of these means and the One Who controls them.

chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning Knowledge and The Fervour the Sahabah (RA) had for Knowledge
intro: This chapter highlights the tremendous fervour that Nabi ﷺ and the Sahabah had for divine knowledge and how they encouraged it. It further discusses how they taught and learnt knowledge pertaining to Imaan and good deeds and also how they preoccupied themselves with it whether they were on journey or at home, undergoing hardship or enjoying prosperity. Also highlighted is how they dedicated themselves to teaching guests who arrived in Madinah Munawwarah (may millions of salutations and greetings go to the master of the place). Furthermore, the chapter illustrates how they blended the dissemination of divine knowledge with Jihaad and earning a living. In addition to this, it describes how they dispatched individuals to cities to disseminate divine knowledge and how they also gave importance to inculcating within themselves qualities that promote the absorption of this knowledge.

chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning The Fervour the Sahabah (RA) had for Dhikr and the Encouragement they Gave Towards it
intro: This chapter highlights the tremendous fervour that Nabi ﷺ and the Sahabah had for the Dhikr of Allaah It further discusses how they were regular with it every morning and evening, during the days and the nights and on journey and at home. Further discussed is how they prompted and encouraged others towards Dhikr and what forms of Dhikr they engaged in.

chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning The Du'aas that the Sahabah (RA) Made
intro: This chapter highlights how Nabi ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) sobbed before Allaah U when making du'aa. It further discusses the reasons for which they made du'aa, the times when they made du'aa and describes what their du'aas were like.

chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning The Lectures of the Sahabah (RA)
intro: This chapter highlights how Nabi ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) addressed the people in Jumu'ah sermons, when in congregation, on the occasions of Hajj and Umrah and on various other occasions. It discusses how they motivated the people to carry out the commands of Allaah, even though these seemed to oppose experience and what was apparent. It further discusses how they made people abstain from this world and its temporary pleasures and yearn for the Aakhirah and its eternal delights. Those firmly stationed every category of the Ummah whether rich, poor or prominent on the consciousness that they should fulfil the commands coming to them from Allaah and Rasulullaah ﷺ even if it meant spending their very lives and all their wealth. The discussion makes it clear that they did not build people's conviction on the temporary and short-lived wealth and resources of this world.

chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning The Advices of the Sahabah (RA)
intro: This chapter discusses how Nabi ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) advised people and accepted the advice given to them, regardless of whether they were at home or on journey. It also highlights how they turned their attention away from the material things of this world and its pleasures to focus on the bounties of the Aakhirah. They so vehemently cautioned people to beware of disobeying Allaah that tears flowed and hearts became overawed. It appeared as if the Aakhirah and the conditions on the Plain of Resurrection were plain before their eyes. This chapter illustrates how they led the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ by the hand through their advices and turned their attention towards the Creator of the heavens and the earth, thereby severing the arteries of every open and discreet form of Shirk.

chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning The Unseen Assistance that the Sahabah (RA) Received
intro: This chapter discusses how Nabi ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) received unseen assistance when they left the material means, held firmly on to spiritual means and when the Sahabah (RA) shared the concern that Rasulullaah had for the guidance of people and calling them towards Islaam. It also highlights how the Sahabah (RA) imbued within themselves the same character traits and noble qualities of Rasulullaah ﷺ.

chapters.title: The Chapter Concerning the Reasons behind the Unseen Assistance that the Sahabah (RA) Received
intro: This chapter discusses the reasons why Nabi ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) received unseen assistance, how they adhered to these and turned their gazes away from the material means and the temporary commodities of this world.

narrations.summary: Another report says Abu Taalib died without reciting the Kalimah while Abu Jahal and Abdullaah bin Abi Umayyah repeated their objections, and that the two verses were revealed afterwards.

narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah narrates that the Prophet asked Abu Taalib on his death-bed to say Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, and Abu Taalib refused for fear of Quraysh ridicule; the verse Qasas 56 was revealed on that occasion.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aqeel bin Abi Taalib (the son of Abu Taalib) narrates that on one occasion when members of the Quraysh approached Abu Taalib (to discuss Rasulullaah ﷺ, Abu Taalib…
narrations.summary: Aqeel bin Abi Taalib narrates that Abu Taalib asked the Prophet to stop saying things that hurt the Quraysh, and the Prophet refused, saying he could not stop what he was sent to do.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Bayhaqi reports that Abu Taalib called for Rasulullaah ﷺ and told him that the people had come to him and told him many things about what Rasulullaah ﷺ was…
narrations.summary: Abu Taalib asks the Prophet to stop, and the Prophet refuses even if the sun and moon were placed in his hands; Jaabir then narrates how Utba bin Rabee'ah failed to bargain the Prophet off and was moved by his recitation of Surah Sajdah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that some members of the Quraysh once gathered to discuss about Rasulullaah ﷺ as Rasulullaah ﷺ sat in the Masjid (the Masjidul…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar narrates that Utba bin Rabee'ah offered the Prophet wealth, position and leadership to stop his preaching; after the Prophet recited Surah Sajdah, Utba told the Quraysh to leave him alone.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhrama (RA) and Hadhrat Marwaan (RA) have reported a lengthy narration concerning the incident leading to the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, which will be…
narrations.summary: Miswar and Marwaan report that Budayl bin Waraqa told the Prophet that the Quraysh were ready to fight, and the Prophet replied that he came only for Umrah and offered a treaty, vowing to fight if they refused Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Tabraani, also narrated by Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhrama (RA) and Hadhrat Marwaan (RA), ends with the words, "Woe be to the Quraysh! Waging war has certainly…
narrations.summary: The Tabraani version, also from Miswar and Marwaan, has the Prophet declare that he will fight the Quraysh for the Deen until victory or his death if they refuse Islaam and still fight.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sahal bin Sa'd (RA) narrates that during the Battle of Khaybar, Rasulullaah ﷺ announced, "Tomorrow I shall give the flag to the person on whose hands Allaah shall…
narrations.summary: Sahal bin Sa'd narrates that at Khaybar the Prophet gave the flag to Ali, who was cured of eye pain by the Prophet's saliva, and that Ali was told to invite the people to Islaam before fighting.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Miqdaad bin Amr (RA) narrates that when he took Hakam bin Kaysaan prisoner (during one of the battles), his commander wanted Hakam executed. However, he (Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Miqdaad bin Amr narrates that he took Hakam bin Kaysaan prisoner, Umar wanted him executed, and the Prophet kept inviting Hakam until he accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent a messenger with the invitation of Islaam to Wahshi bin Harb who was responsible for killing Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates that Wahshi bin Harb, who killed Hamza, asked whether he could be forgiven; after a series of verses that answered each objection, he accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that some Mushrikeen who had committed murder and adultery in abundance approached Rasulullaah ﷺ. They said, "What you are…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates verses revealed for murderers and adulterers who asked about expiation; a second report from Abu Tha'laba Khushani describes Faatima weeping at the Prophet's pale, tired appearance after a journey.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tarneem Daari (RA) narrates that he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "This Deen shall definitely reach wherever the day and the night reach. Allaah shall enter this Deen…
narrations.summary: Tameem Daari narrates the Prophet's saying that Islaam will reach every home, bringing honour to Muslims and disgrace to the disbelievers, and says he saw this come true in his own family.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) sent him to give the news of the conquest of Tustar to Hadhrat Umar (RA). He says that Hadhrat Umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: Anas narrates Umar's wish to win back six apostates from Bakr bin Waa'il by inviting them back before any execution; a second report from Abdur Rahmaan Al Qaari gives Umar's ruling on a man who reverted, and a third has Amr bin Al Aas asking how to treat a man who reverted repeatedly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) once wrote to Ammerul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Umar to ask him what was to be done about a person who had reverted to kufr after accepting Islaam,…
narrations.summary: Amr bin al-Aas asks Umar what to do about a man who repeatedly left Islaam and returned to it, and Umar rules that he should be invited to Islaam again, then freed if he accepts or otherwise executed.

narrations.excerpt: Abu Imraan Jowni narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by a monk and remained standing there. Someone called the monk and told him that the Ameerul Mu'mineen was…
narrations.summary: Abu Imraan Jowni narrates that Umar wept on seeing a Christian monk worn out by worship, because the Qur'aan says such labour still ends in the Fire.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha SSI narrates that her father Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was a close friend of Rasulullaah ﷺ even during the Period of Ignorance. One day, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr, a close friend of the Prophet, accepts Islaam immediately when the Prophet calls him, and several leading Companions then follow him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once prayed to Allaah saying, "O Allaah! Strengthen Islaam by means of either Umar bin Khattaab or Abu…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood narrates that the Prophet prayed that Islaam be strengthened through Umar or Abu Jahal, and Allaah answered the prayer in Umar's favour.

narrations.excerpt: A narration reported by Hadhrat Thowbaan discussing the suffering of Hadhrat Umar's sister Faatima and her husband Sa'eed bin Zaid shall be quoted in a forthcoming…
narrations.summary: Thowbaan's report, promised for a later chapter, is summarised here: Umar, after leaving his sister's house, came to the Prophet, who shook him and asked what he wanted, and Umar accepted Islaam on the spot.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said to them, "Do you want to hear about how I came into the fold of Islaam?" When those present begged to be informed,…
narrations.summary: Aslam narrates Umar's own account of how the Prophet seized his collar and called him to Islaam, and Umar testified to the Kalimah on the spot.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Uthmaan reports that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) said, "I wa,s once visiting my aunt Arwa bint Abdil Muttalib (my mother's sister) when, Rasulullaah Wife arrived…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Uthmaan reports Uthmaan's account of meeting the Prophet at his aunt Arwa's house; after the Prophet recited Surah Dhaariyaat on the Hereafter, Uthmaan followed him out and accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Ibn is'haaq narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) came to Rasulullaah ﷺ while Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Khadeeja (RA) were performing salaah. Hadhrat Ali asked Rasulullaah ﷺ, "O…
narrations.summary: Ibn Is'haaq reports Ali's acceptance of Islaam after he found the Prophet and Khadeeja praying; Ali later recalls his father Abu Taalib's remark on seeing them pray, and Habba Urani reports seeing Ali laugh at it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Abdillaah narrates that Hadhrat Abu Umaama (RA) once asked Hadhrat Amr bin Abasa (RA) why he claimed to be the fourth person to accept Islaam. He…
narrations.summary: Shaddaad bin Abdillaah reports Amr bin Abasa's account of meeting the Prophet in Makkah, accepting Islaam there, and being told to go home until the Prophet became dominant.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Abasa (RA) has narrated yet another Hadith. He says that he once asked Rasulullaah ﷺ, "With what message did Allaah send you?" He replied, "Allaah has…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Abasa reports the Prophet's message of joining family ties, preserving life and roads, and worshipping one Allaah; a second account has Khaalid bin Sa'eed beaten and cast out by his father Sa'eed bin Al Aas for following the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sa'eed bin Al Aas was one of the first people to accept Islaam. He was of the first of his brothers to accept Islaam. His path to Islaam started with…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Sa'eed accepted Islaam after a dream, was beaten and cut off by his father for it, and then stayed constantly with the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Dimaad (RA) was a man from the Azdishanu'ah tribe who used to cure insane people and people affected with evil…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates Dimaad's conversion: he came to cure the Prophet, heard the Prophet's sermon and pledged Islaam; he later refused Abu Jahal's mockery, and Ali returned camels taken from his people.

narrations.excerpt: Husayn The Quraysh highly respected Hadhrat Husayn (RA). One day some members of the Quraysh approached Hadhrat Husayn (RA) and said to him, "Go to this person…
narrations.summary: The Quraysh send Husayn to speak to the Prophet, who asks how many gods he worships; Husayn accepts Islaam on the Prophet's advice, and his son Imraan kisses his head, hands and feet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Tameema Hujaymi (RA) narrates from a man of his tribe that he once came to meet Rasulullaah ﷺ. It could have been such that Hadhrat Abu Tameema was present…
narrations.summary: Abu Tameema Hujaymi narrates from a man of his tribe, who came to the Prophet, heard about Allaah, accepted Islaam immediately, and was then advised not to swear oaths.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Haydah (RA) narrates that he once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I have not come to you before this because I have sworn more…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Haydah narrates that he came to the Prophet, asked what Islaam is, and was told about surrender to Allaah, salaah, zakaah and the brotherhood of Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Adi bin Haatim (RA) narrates, "When I heard about the coming of Rasulullaah ﷺ, I disliked this very greatly. So I left and found myself close to Rome (according…
narrations.summary: Adi bin Haatim narrates that he first fled from the Prophet, then came to him and accepted Islaam after the Prophet addressed his objections, and was told of the coming conquest of Kisra's treasures and safe travel from Heera.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Adi bin Haatim (RA) narrates that he and some others were at a place called Aqrab when a group of horsemen sent by Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived there. They captured some…
narrations.summary: Adi bin Haatim narrates that his captured aunt was freed by the Prophet, who then spoke to Adi; Adi accepted Islaam, and the Prophet urged charity even of a date and foretold wealth and safety.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dhi Jowshin Dhababi (RA) narrates, "I came to Rasulullaah ﷺ after the Battle of Badr and brought with him the foal of my horse Qar'haa. I said to Rasulullaah ﷺ,…
narrations.summary: Dhul Jowshin Dhababi narrates that after Badr he refused the Prophet's invitation to Islaam, and later regretted it when he heard the Prophet had taken control of the Kabah; the Prophet had Bilaal fill his satchel with dates.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Basheer bin Khasaasiyah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ invited him to accept Islaam on one occasion. (After he accepted Islaam,) Rasulullaah H asked him, "What…
narrations.summary: Basheer bin Khasaasiyah narrates that after accepting Islaam he was renamed Basheer and placed in Ahl us-Suffa, and that he followed the Prophet to the graveyard, where the Prophet greeted the dead.

narrations.excerpt: A person from the Baladawiyyah tribe narrates the following from his grandfather: "As I was coming to Madinah, I pitched my tent in a valley where I saw two persons…
narrations.summary: A man from the Baladawiyyah tribe, reporting from his grandfather, describes the Prophet, whom he saw trading, teaching leniency in buying and selling; he later accepted Islaam. Anas then narrates a separate story about inviting an uncle of the Banu Najjaar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once visited a Jewish boy who used to serve him but had fallen ill. Sitting by his head, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to the boy,…
narrations.summary: Anas narrates that the Prophet visited a sick Jewish boy who served him, asked him to accept Islaam, and the boy did so with his father's consent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) has also narrated that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to a person, "Accept Islaam and you will remain in peace." The person said, "But I dislike it."…
narrations.summary: Anas narrates that the Prophet told a man to accept Islaam and he would be at peace; the man said he disliked it, and the Prophet replied, 'Even though you dislike it.'

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asma bint Abi Bakr (RA) reports that it was on that day that Muslims conquered Makkah when Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Hadhrat Abu Quhaafa (RA), "Accept Islaam and…
narrations.summary: Asmaa bint Abi Bakr reports that on the day Makkah was conquered, the Prophet told Abu Quhaafa to accept Islaam and remain in peace.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asma bint Abi Bakr (RA) also reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ entered Makkah and was peacefully sitting in the Masjidul Haraam, Hadhrat Abu Bakr brought his father…
narrations.summary: Asmaa reports that when the Prophet entered Makkah, Abu Bakr brought his father Abu Quhaafa to him; the Prophet had him sit before him, he accepted Islaam, and the Prophet advised him on his white hair.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mughiera bin Shu'ba (RA) narrates that the first time he came to know who Rasulullaah ﷺ was when Rasulullaah ﷺ met him walking with Abu Jahal in one of the…
narrations.summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba narrates that the Prophet invited Abu Jahal to Islaam in a Makkah alley, and Abu Jahal refused, saying that the Bani Qusay had taken each office in turn and he would never accept a Nabi from among them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once recited a part of the Qur'aan to Waleed bin Mughiera who had come to him. This caused Waleed's heart to…
narrations.summary: Abu Jahal persuades Waleed bin Mughiera to dismiss the Qur'aan he had been moved by, calling it magic.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) narrates that he was a young boy riding his donkey while his father Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) was riding another animal with his wife Hind sitting…
narrations.summary: The Prophet warns Abu Sufyaan and Hind of death and the Hereafter and recites the Qur'aan to them, and Abu Sufyaan vouches for him against Hind's accusation.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed bin Roomaan narrates that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and Hadhrat Talha (RA) followed Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) to Rasulullaah ﷺ. When the two (Hadhrat Talha (RA) and…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan and Talha follow Zubayr to the Prophet and accept Islaam, and Uthmaan then reports a vision he had on his way back from Shaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amaar bin Yaasir (RA) narrates, "I met Suhayb bin Sanaan at the door of Arqam's house. I asked him, 'What are you doing here?' He asked me, ■What are you doing…
narrations.summary: Ammaar bin Yaasir and Suhayb meet at Arqam's house, hear the Prophet and accept Islaam, then leave secretly in the evening.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khubayb bin Abdir Rahmaan narrates that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Zurarah and Dhakwaan bin Abd Qais came to Makkah to have Utba bin Rabee'ah settle a dispute. When they…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Zurarah and Dhakwaan bin Abd Qais go to Makkah to settle a dispute, accept Islaam from the Prophet, and become the first from Madinah to do so.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that it was after sunset when several leaders of the Quraysh gathered behind the Kabah for a meeting. Among them were Utba and…
narrations.summary: The Quraysh leaders offer the Prophet wealth, honour and kingship, then demand miracles; he refuses them all, and Abdullaah bin Abi Umayyah walks out unconvinced.

narrations.excerpt: Mahmbod bin Labeed from the Banu Abdil Ash'hal tribe narrates Abul 'Haysim Anas bin Raafi and some youths from the Banu Abdil Asb/hal tribe arrived in Makkah to conclude…
narrations.summary: The Prophet calls Abul Haysim and some young men of the Banu Abdil Ash'hal to Islaam, and Iyaas bin Muaadh accepts and dies reciting the Kalimah.

narrations.excerpt: Rasulullaah ﷺ invites his close relatives to Islaam together with various tribes of the Quraysh upon the revelation of a verse Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates…
narrations.summary: As Surah Shu'araa is revealed, the Prophet climbs Marwah and calls the Quraysh tribes to Islaam, and Abu Lahab rejects him, prompting the revelation of Surah Lahab.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ climbed the hill of Safa when the following verse of the Qur'aan was revealed: (O. Rasulullaah ﷺ First) Warn…
narrations.summary: The Prophet calls the family of Abdul Muttalib and others from Safa to hear a warning, and Abu Lahab rejects him, leading to the revelation of Surah Lahab.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ka'b bin Maalik (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ gave Da'wah secretly for the first three years. It was during the fourth year that he openly began…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ka'b describes the years of secret and open da'wah in Makkah and the approaches at Hajj; Maysara later recounts the Jewish description of the Prophet and his own acceptance of Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Waabisa narrates from his grandfather (RA) that their tribe was stationed close to the first Jamara in Mina near the Masjid Khayf when Rasulullaah ﷺ came to them…
narrations.summary: Waabisa reports how the Prophet invited the Banu Abs to Islaam near Mina, and how Maysara bin Masrooq later accepted Islaam after the Jews described the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Roomaan, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abi Bakr (RA) and others have reported that Rasulullaah ﷺ approached the Kindah tribe at their camping place near the market of…
narrations.summary: The Prophet calls the Kindah tribe at their camp near Ukaaz; they hesitate and withdraw, and a Jew later tells them they had missed a golden opportunity.

narrations.excerpt: Abdur Rahmaan Al Aamiri narrates from the elders of his tribe that they were in the marketplace of Ukaaz when Rasulullaah ﷺ approached them. When he asked them which…
narrations.summary: The Prophet asks the Banu Aamir for protection to convey his message; an old man named Bujra Qushayri says his claim to prophethood is true, but the tribe refuses to accept it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat ?uhri (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ met the Banu Aamir bin Sa'sa'ah tribe and placed Islaam and himself before them (invited them to accept Islaam and to…
narrations.summary: Zuhri reports that the Prophet invited the Banu Aamir and then the Kindah tribe, and both refused; Bajeera bin Firaas objected that kingship would go to others, and an old man of the Banu Aamir later said the Prophet's claim was true.

narrations.excerpt: Muhammad ﷺ bin Husayn narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ approached a family of the Banu Kalb tribe called the Banu Abdullaah at the place where they were staying. Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: The Prophet invites a family of the Banu Kalb to Allaah and asks them to accept Islaam and assist him, and they reject his message.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah. bin Ka'b bin Maalik (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ approached the Banu Haneefah tribe at the place where they were staying. Rasulullaah ﷺ invited…
narrations.summary: The Prophet calls the Banu Haneefah to Allaah and asks them to assist him, and they reject him more harshly than any other Arab tribe.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to him, "I do not see any help forthcoming from yourself and your brother. Will you not take me to the…
narrations.summary: Abbaas shows the Prophet the camps of the Arab tribes at Hajj; the Kindah and Banu Bakr refuse his call, and Abu Lahab tells the people that the Prophet is insane.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rabee'ah bin Ibaad (RA) narrates that he was a youngster with his father at Mina when Rasulullaah ﷺ stopped at the camps of various Arab tribes saying to them, "O…
narrations.summary: Rabee'ah bin Ibaad, as a boy with his father at Mina, hears the Prophet call the tribes to Allaah while his uncle Abu Lahab follows him and denounces him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mudrik (RA) narrates that when he performed Hajj with his father and they found themselves amongst a large group of people, he asked his father, "What is this…
narrations.summary: Mudrik asks his father about a gathering at Mina and sees the Prophet telling the people to say La Ilaaha Illallaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haarith bin Haarith Ghaamidi (RA) narrates that he asked his father at Mina, "What is this gathering about?" His father replied, "They have gathered for that…
narrations.summary: Haarith sees the Prophet calling people at Mina, and Hassaan bin Thaabit reports Umar torturing slave women before he became a Muslim.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) says, "When Allaah commanded His Nabi ﷺ to present himself to the Arab tribes, Rasulullaah ﷺ left for Mina with me and Hadhrat Abu Bakr…
narrations.summary: The Prophet, Abu Bakr and Ali call the Banu Shaybaan to Islaam; they decline but pledge support, and the Prophet later announces the Banu Rabee'ah victory over the Persians.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to them, "The only people who can establish the Deen of Allaah are those who protect it from every angle." Thereafter,…
narrations.summary: The Prophet asks the Banu Shaybaan to protect the Deen, Nu'maan bin Shareek pledges support, and Ali relates the Prophet's foretold victory over the Persians at Quraqir, after which the Banu Rabee'ah became Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: One day, while mentioning the virtues of the Ansaar and that the fact that they were pioneers in Islaam, Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) said, "The person who does not…
narrations.summary: Ali praises the Ansaar for nurturing Islaam, and Umm Sa'd bint Sa'd describes the first Aqaba pledge made by six or seven men of Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aqeel bin Abi Taalib (RA) and Hadhrat Zuhri narrate that one day during the period when the Mushrikeen started harassing Rasulullaah ﷺ to a great degree, he said…
narrations.summary: Aqeel and Zuhri report that the Prophet asked Abbaas to take him to the tribes at Ukaaz, and six men of Aws and Khazraj accept Islaam at Aqaba after hearing Surah Ibraheem.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rabee'ah bin Ibaad (RA) belonged to the Banu Deel tribe who had all accepted islaam after passing through the Period of Ignorance. He narrates that during the…
narrations.summary: Rabee'ah bin Ibaad, Taariq bin Abdillaah and another man report the Prophet calling people to Laa Ilaaha Illallaah in the Dhul Majaaz market, while Abu Lahab and Abu Jahal oppose him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Taariq bin Abdillaah (RA) narrates that he was in the Dhul Majaaz marketplace when a man passed by wearing a shawl with red threads. He was saying to the people,…
narrations.summary: Taariq bin Abdillaah sees the Prophet calling people to say Laa Ilaaha Illallaah in the Dhul Majaaz market while Abu Lahab follows him and Abu Jahal throws sand at him, and a second narrator describes the Prophet's appearance.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ gathered his family members when Allaah revealed the verse: (O Rasulullaah ﷺ First) Warn your closest relatives (about…
narrations.summary: The Prophet gathers his close relatives and tells his daughter Faatima and his aunt Safiyya that he cannot help them against Allaah's punishment.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ gathered his family members when Allaah revealed the verse: (O Rasulullaah ﷺ First) Warn your closest relatives (about the…
narrations.summary: Ali reports a meal the Prophet gave for the family of Abdul Muttalib, where he asked who would settle his debts and become his successor, and Ali volunteered.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) has also napated that Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed him to prepare a meal using the leg Qf an animal and a "saa" ^ of wheat flour (for bread) when the…
narrations.summary: Ali reports a third meal for the Banu Haashim, where the Prophet repeated his request for someone to settle his debts; Ali accepted while Abbaas stayed silent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd (Aslami) (RA) was the guide who directed Rasulullaah ﷺ through the Rakoobah valley. His son (Abdullaah) says, "My father informed us that Rasulullaah ﷺ came…
narrations.summary: Sa'd Aslami guides the Prophet through the Rakoobah valley, where two thieves of Aslam accept Islaam, and the Prophet tells them to join him in Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that they were once traveling with Rasulullaah ﷺ when a villager passed by them. As he drew close, Rasulullaah asked him, "Where…
narrations.summary: A villager on a journey is invited to Islaam, and the Prophet calls a tree to bear witness to his message before the villager says he will come to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aasim Aslami (RA) narrates that while Rasulullaah ﷺ was migrating from Makkah to Madinah, Hadhrat Buraydah bin Khusayb (RA) met him at a place called Ghameem.…
narrations.summary: Buraydah bin Khusayb and about eighty families accept Islaam at Ghameem during the hijrah, and the Prophet leads them in the Isha salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) narrates that after his uncle Abu Taalib had passed away, Rasulullaah ﷺ travelled on foot to Taa'if to invite the people to Islaam.…
narrations.summary: After Abu Taalib's death the Prophet walks to Taa'if to invite its people, is rejected, and on the return journey makes a du'aa under a tree.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ would never fight any nation until he had already conveyed the Da of Islaam to them. Rasulullaah ﷺ Instructs…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas and Abdur Rahmaan bin Aa'idh report that the Prophet never fought a nation before inviting it to Islaam, and he told his battalions to win people's confidence first.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) narrates that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed someone as commander of Muslims troops, he would instruct him to fear Allaah with regard to his…
narrations.summary: Buraydah reports the Prophet's instructions to his commanders: invite enemies to Islaam, then to migrate, then to pay jizya, and fight only if they refuse all three.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) as commander of a battalion to fight a battle. Thereafter,…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik and Ibn Raahway report that the Prophet sent Ali out with the order not to fight an enemy until he had invited them to Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) has also mentioned that when Rasulullaah ﷺ sent him, he said, "Never fight a nation until you have invited them to accept Islaam." The narration of…
narrations.summary: Ali reports the Prophet's instruction never to fight a nation before inviting them to Islaam, and his saying that guiding one person is better than red camels.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Farwa bin Musayk (Ghutayfi) (RA) narrates that he came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and asked, "Should I not take those of my people who have progressed (accepted Islaam) to…
narrations.summary: Farwa Ghutayfi asks to fight those of his people who refused Islaam, and the Prophet tells him to invite them first and not to be hasty with those who refuse.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Farwa (RA) narrates that he came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and asked, "Should I not take those of my people who have progressed (accepted Islaam) to fight those of them…
narrations.summary: Farwa Ghutayfi asks again about fighting and is told to invite before fighting, and then asks about Saba, which the Prophet explains is a man with ten sons.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sa'eed (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched him to Yemen, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "If you hear the Adhaan being called out among any…
narrations.summary: The Prophet tells Khaalid bin Sa'eed, sent to Yemen, to leave a nation alone if he hears the adhaan there, and to invite it to Islaam if he does not.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) narrates that when some captives from Laat and Uzza were brought before Rasulullaah ﷺ, he asked (the Muslims who captured them), "Did you…
narrations.summary: Captives from Laat and Uzza are freed because their captors never invited them to Islaam, and the Prophet recites Qur'aan verses on his mission as a warner.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched a battalion to the vicinity where the idols Laat and Uzza stood, they attacked an Arab tribe living there and…
narrations.summary: A battalion that attacked an Arab tribe near Laat and Uzza without inviting it to Islaam is told by the Prophet to free the captives and invite them first.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) narrates that wrjen the Ansaar heard what Rasulullaah ﷺ had to say, became convinced and completely satisfied with his message, they believed…
narrations.summary: The Ansaar accept Islaam and ask for a teacher, so the Prophet sends Mus'ab bin Umayr to Madinah, where he teaches and most homes come to Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ifcif sent him to invite his people to Allaah and to present the injunctions of Islaam to them. When he arrived, his…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah is sent to his Baahilah tribe, is refused water after they reject him, and after a dream of a drink the whole tribe accepts Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ahnaf bin Qais (RA) narrates that he was once performing Tawaaf around the Kabah when a man from the Banu Layth tribe grabbed hold of his hand saying, "Shall I…
narrations.summary: Ahnaf bin Qais, who once dismissed a man's invitation to Islaam, was reminded of it later and of the Prophet's prayer for his forgiveness, which he valued above his good deeds.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent one of the Sahabah (RA) to give Da'wah to a person who was influential during the Period of Ignorance. The person…
narrations.summary: The Prophet sent a Companion to a powerful Jahiliyyah leader who mocked the message, and the leader was struck by lightning, after which a verse of Surah Ra'd was revealed.

narrations.excerpt: A report of Bazzaar states that the person was one of the tyrannical Arab leaders and that the Sahabi said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ He is more tyrannical than Fir'oun. This…
narrations.summary: A Bazzaar report says the leader was a tyrant, worse than Fir'oun, and was killed by lightning while still being invited to Islaam, followed by editorial cross-references to Khaalid bin Sa'eed and Amr bin Murra.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once summoned Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) and said to him, "Prepare yourself because I want to send you…
narrations.summary: The Prophet sent Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf with a group to Dowmatul Jandal, where the Christian chief Asbagh bin Amr Kalbi accepted Islaam, and the Prophet then directed Abdur Rahmaan to marry Asbagh's daughter.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan Tameemi (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas out (RA) to encourage the Arabs to accept Islaam. Rasulullaah ﷺ sent him to the…
narrations.summary: The Prophet sent Amr bin Al Aas to the Banu Baliy to call the Arabs to Islaam, and when he sensed danger at Salaasil he asked for reinforcements, so a battalion under Abu Ubaydah was sent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib (RA) narrates that he was among the group that Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched to Yemen under the leadership of Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed to invite the…
narrations.summary: Baraa bin Aazib recounts the Yemen mission under Khaalid bin Waleed, which won no one until Ali was sent to relieve him, after which the whole Hamdaan tribe accepted Islaam and the Prophet prayed peace upon them.

narrations.excerpt: Ibn Is'haaq narrates that Rasulullaah ijcii once dispatched Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed to Najraan with instructions to invite the Banu Haarith bin Ka'b to Islaam for…
narrations.summary: Ibn Is'haaq reports that the Prophet sent Khaalid bin Waleed to Najraan to invite the Banu Haarith bin Ka'b for three days before fighting, and they all accepted Islaam; the report breaks off at the start of Khaalid's letter.

narrations.excerpt: In the name of Allaah the Most Kind, the Most Merciful To Muhammad the Nabi and Rasool of Allaah From Khaalid bin Waleed May peace be to you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ and the…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed writes to the Prophet to report that the Banu Haarith bin Ka'b accepted Islaam without a fight and that he is teaching them the injunctions of Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: The Letter that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent in reply to Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) In the name of Allaah the Most Kind, the Most Merciful From Muhammad the Nabi and Rasool of…
narrations.summary: The Prophet replies to Khaalid, welcoming the Banu Haarith's acceptance of Islaam, telling him to give them good news of Jannah and warn them against Jahannam, and asking him to return with a delegation.

narrations.excerpt: (After receiving the letter from Rasulullaah ﷺ) Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed returned to Rasulullaah ﷺ by a delegation from the Banu Haarith bin Ka'b tribe. When…
narrations.summary: The Banu Haarith delegation comes to Madinah; the Prophet praises their acceptance, Yazeed bin Abdil Madaan answers for them, and the Prophet appoints Qais bin Husayn as their leader.

narrations.excerpt: Rasulullaah ﷺ invites Hadhrat Jareer (RA) towards Imaan, Reciting the Shahaadah and fulfilling the Faraa'idh Hadhrat Jareer bin Abdillaah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Jareer bin Abdillaah comes to accept Islaam, the Prophet teaches him the Shahaadah, Imaan, salaah and zakaah, and the Prophet honours him, always smiling when he saw him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen, he said to him, "You will certainly meet people from the…
narrations.summary: The Prophet instructs Mu'aadh bin Jabal before he goes to Yemen: first invite the People of the Book to Tawheed and the Prophethood, then salaah and zakaah, and avoid taking their best wealth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Howshab Dhi Dhulaym (RA) narrates that when Allaah granted dominance to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he sent a letter with Abd Sharr and a band of forty horsemen to Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Howshab Dhi Dhulaym relates that Abd Sharr came with a letter and forty horsemen, pledged to the Prophet on salaah, zakaah and enjoining good, was renamed Abd Khayr, and that Howshab then also accepted Imaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when a delegation from the Abd Qais tribe met Rasulullaah ﷺ, he said to them, "Welcome to people who shall suffer neither…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates that the Prophet welcomed the Abd Qais delegation and commanded them to believe in Allaah, pray, pay zakaah, fast in Ramadhaan and pay one third of the spoils, and forbade four kinds of drinking vessels.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Alqama (RA) narrates that he was one of seven people from his tribe who came to meet Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied to their greeting and when they spoke to…
narrations.summary: Alqama describes how he and six others came to the Prophet and listed the attributes of their Imaan, and the entry then runs into a second report about the Prophet sending Companions to distant kings and rulers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that before his death, Rasulullaah ﷺ sent letters to emperors of Persia, Rome and Abyssinia as well as to every dictatorial leader, inviting…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that shortly before his death the Prophet sent letters to the emperors of Persia and Rome and to every oppressive ruler, inviting them to Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that before his death Rasulullaah ﷺ sent letters to the Emperors of Persia and Rome and to every other dictatorial leader.
narrations.summary: Jaabir narrates that shortly before his death the Prophet sent letters to the emperors of Persia and Rome and to other rulers.

narrations.excerpt: With reference to Hadhrat Ja'far bin Abi Taalib (RA) and other Sahabah (RA) (who had migrated to Abyssinia), Rasulullaah ﷺ sent the following letter with Hadhrat Amr bin…
narrations.summary: The Prophet writes to Najaashi, King of Abyssinia, inviting him to Islaam and affirming Isa's true status, and sends his cousin Ja'far and the Muslims in Abyssinia with Amr bin Umayyah Dhamri as the letter's bearer.

narrations.excerpt: Najaashi sent the following letter in reply to Rasulullaah ﷺ In the name of Allaah the Most Kind, the Most Merciful To Muhammad the Rasool of Allaah i From Najaashi…
narrations.summary: Najaashi As'ham replies to the Prophet, affirming Isa as he was described, testifying that Muhammad is the true Rasul, saying he accepted Islaam at Ja'far's hands, sending his son Areeha, and offering to come in person.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dihya Kalbi (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent him with a letter to the Emperor of Rome. When he arrived there and handed over the letter, the emperor's nephew…
narrations.summary: Dihya Kalbi delivers the Prophet's letter to Heraclius, who consults his high priest and Abu Sufyaan, recognises the signs of prophethood but refuses to give up his kingship, and the high priest is later killed after publicly testifying to Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) told him that he went to Shaam with a trade caravan of the Quraysh during the period when…
narrations.summary: Abu Sufyaan recounts being questioned by Heraclius at Ilyia about the Prophet's lineage, followers and treaties, whose answers Heraclius took as signs of prophethood, and then the court's reaction to the Prophet's letter.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas IS narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent a messenger with a letter addressed to Kisra, instructing the messenger to hand the letter over to the…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates that the Prophet sent a letter to Kisra through the governor of Bahrain, that Kisra tore it up, and that the Prophet cursed him, as relayed by Ibn Musayyib.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abd Qaari (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ stood on the pulpit one-day to deliver a sermon. After praising Allaah, and reciting the Shahaadah,…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abd Qaari and Abu Salam report that Shujaa bin Wahab delivered the Prophet's letter to Kisra, who tore it; Kisra then ordered Baadhaan to bring the Prophet to him, the Prophet foretold Kisra's death, and Baadhaan accepted Islaam after Sherway killed Kisra.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Abi Habeeb narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Abdullah bin Hudhaafa with a letter for Kisra bin Hurmuz who was the Emperor of Persia. The letter…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Abi Habeeb reports the letter Abdullah bin Hudhaafa carried to Kisra, which Kisra tore up, and the Prophet's reply to two envoys with shaven beards that his Rabb had commanded him to grow his own beard.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakrah (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was sent to propagate the message, Kisra sent a message to his governor over Yemen and the surrounding areas of…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakrah reports that Kisra ordered Baadaam, his governor over Yemen, to stop the Prophet, and that the Prophet told Baadaam's envoy his Rabb had killed Kisra and Caesar, which the envoy found had come true.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dihya Kalbi (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent him with a letter addressed to the Caesar. The Hadith is similar to that mentioned under the heading "The Letter…
narrations.summary: Dihya Kalbi reports the letter to Caesar, then the envoys of the San'aa governor, who were told that the Prophet's Rabb had killed Kisra that very night, which was later confirmed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullah bin Abd Qaari (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Haatib bin Abi Balta'ah (RA) with a letter addressed to Maqoqis the king of Alexandria. When…
narrations.summary: Abdullah bin Abd Qaari reports that Haatib bin Abi Balta'ah took the Prophet's letter to Maqoqis of Alexandria, who received him well and sent gifts, including the slave woman Maariya, mother of Ibraheem, and another woman given to Muhammad bin Qais Abdi.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haatib bin Abi Balta'ah (RA) narrates that "Rasulullaah ﷺ sent him to Maqoqis the king of Alexandria. When he delivered the letter, Maqoqis hosted Hadhrat Haatib…
narrations.summary: Haatib bin Abi Balta'ah narrates his debate with Maqoqis over the Prophet's status and why he did not curse his people, after which Maqoqis sent gifts, including a slave woman who became the mother of Ibraheem, and the Prophet gave another woman to Hassaan bin Thaabit.

narrations.excerpt: The grandfather of Abd Yasoo who was a Christian before accepting Islaam narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent a letter to the people of Najraan before Surah Sulaymaan" (Surah…
narrations.summary: The grandfather of Abd Yasoo reports the Prophet's letter to the people of Najraan and the mubaahala challenge, which they declined in favour of a treaty; the Prophet then wrote a letter guaranteeing the protection of their priests and property.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.5 Pg.55) adds that the witnesses to this treaty were Abu Sufyaan bin Harb, Ghaylaan bin Amr, Maalik bin Auf of the Banu Nasr…
narrations.summary: Witnesses to the Najraan treaty carry the Prophet's letter back to Najraan, where Basheer (Abu Alqama) accepts Islaam after cursing the Prophet in a fall, the monk Ibn Abi Shimr goes to meet the Prophet, and the Prophet's letter of protection for the priests of Najraan is written by Mughiera.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Marthad bin Dhabiyaan (RA) narrates that a letter from Rasulullaah reached them and that they could find no one in their tribe to read it until a man from the…
narrations.summary: Marthad bin Dhabiyaan reports that a letter from the Prophet was read out to the Bakr bin Waa'il tribe, calling them to accept Islaam and live in peace.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ma'bad Judhaami (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Rifaa'ah bin Zaid Judhaami met with Rasulullaah ﷺ, he wrote the following letter for them: From Muhammad the…
narrations.summary: Ma'bad Judhaami reports that the Prophet wrote a letter to Rifaa'ah bin Zaid Judhaami to invite his people to Allaah and His Rasool, and that they all accepted Imaan when he reached them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) narrates that when Allaah decreed that Hadhrat Zaid bin Su'na (RA) should accept Islaam, Hadhrat Zaid bin Su'na himself said, "When I…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Salaam reports how the Jewish rabbi Zaid bin Su'na tested the Prophet's patience and was rebuked by Umar, then accepted Islaam and vowed to give half his wealth as charity to part of the Ummah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhrama (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ left .Madinah on the occasion of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, he said to the Sahabah when they had reached…
narrations.summary: Miswar bin Makhrama reports that on the way to Hudaybiyyah, the Prophet's camel Qaswa halted, the Prophet declared he would grant the Kuffaar any request that respects what Allaah has made sacred, and water gushed from a spring after he had an arrow placed in it.

narrations.excerpt: While the Muslims were camped at Hudaybiyyah, Budayl bin Warqa Khuzaa'ee arrived with a group of his tribesmen from the Banu Khuzaa'a. This was the tribe who were…
narrations.summary: Budayl bin Warqa warns the Prophet that the Quraysh's tribes are ready to fight, the Prophet says he came only for Umrah and offers a treaty, and Budayl relays this to the Quraysh.

narrations.excerpt: Urwa bin Mas'ood then stood up and said, "O peoplel Am I not like a father unto you?" "Indeed," they replied. He added, "And are you not like my children?" "Certainly,"…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Mas'ood addresses the Quraysh and then negotiates with the Prophet, but Abu Bakr rebukes him and Mughiera bin Shu'ba strikes his hand from the Prophet's beard, and Urwa returns to say the Sahabah honour the Prophet more than any ruler's followers.

narrations.excerpt: Thereafter, someone from the Kinaana tribe said, "Allow me to meet him." "Go see him," the others said. When the man came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA),…
narrations.summary: A man of the Kinaana tribe, then Mikraz bin Hafs, go to the Prophet, and Mikraz begins negotiating before the report breaks off at the arrival of a man named only 'bin Amr'.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ma'mar iS narrates from Ayyoob and Ikrama that when Suhayl bin Amr arrived, Rasulullaah Wife (took a good omen from his name and) said, "Allaah has now made…
narrations.summary: Ma'mar, relaying from Ayyoob, Ikrimah and Zuhri, reports the Hudaybiyyah negotiations: Suhayl bin Amr objects to the opening formula and to the clauses, and the Prophet accepts his terms.

narrations.excerpt: Negotiations were still underway when Hadhrat Abu Jandal (RA) the son of Suhayl bin Amr arrived there chained in fetters. He had just left the lower part of Makkah and…
narrations.summary: Abu Jandal arrives in chains and Suhayl insists on his return under the treaty; Umar and Abu Bakr reassure each other that the Prophet will reach the Kabah, the Prophet's companions follow his example of sacrifice, and verses on women migrants are revealed, after which Umar divorces two wives who remained mushrik.

narrations.excerpt: After the incident at Hudaybiyyah, Rasulullaah ﷺ returned to Madinah where a Muslim from the Quraysh called Abu Baseer US came to him. However, the Quraysh had dispatched…
narrations.summary: Abu Baseer is handed back to two men sent under the treaty, kills one of them on the road, and after the Prophet's remark that he was a warmonger, he leaves Madinah for the coast.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Jandal (RA) the son of'Suhayl bin Amr managed to escape from the Quraysh and joined up with Hadhrat Abu Baseer (RA). Thereafter, every man who accepted Islaam…
narrations.summary: Abu Jandal escapes from the Quraysh and joins Abu Baseer, and their growing group attacks Quraysh caravans until the Quraysh ask the Prophet to call them to Madinah, after which verses of Surah Fath (24-26) are revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Recounting Rasulullaah ﷺ's stay at Hudaybiyyah, Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that the Quraysh became very scared when Rasulullaah ﷺ camped at Hudaybiyyah. Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: During the stay at Hudaybiyyah, Umar suggests and Rasulullaah ﷺ sends Uthmaan to Makkah with a message of peace; Uthmaan gives the Quraysh da'wah and is guaranteed safe passage.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ entered into a peace treaty with the people of Makkah and conceded to many things.…
narrations.summary: Umar says Rasulullaah ﷺ made concessions in the treaty of Hudaybiyyah and that he would have obeyed any Ameer who acted as the Prophet did.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) used to say, "There has never been a victory in Islaam greater than the victory at Hudaybiyyah but the people on that day were unable to understand…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr says Hudaybiyyah was the greatest victory in Islaam, and recounts how Suhayl bin Amr, who had refused the title Rasool at the treaty, later honoured the Prophet at the Farewell Hajj and was guided to Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) narrates that when they left the trench after the Battle of Ahzaab, he gathered some people from the Quraysh who usually shared his opinions…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Al Aas plots against the Prophet's envoys, then goes to Najaashi and accepts Islaam; he travels with Khaalid bin Waleed and Uthmaan bin Talha to Madinah and pledges allegiance to the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) says that when Allaah decided that good head his way, Allaah created the desire within his heart to accept Islaam and opened many avenues…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed recounts how he came to Islaam after the treaty of Hudaybiyyah, after reading his brother Waleed's letter, dreaming, and meeting Safwaan, Ikrama, Uthmaan bin Talha and Amr bin Al Aas on the way to Madinah, where the Prophet prayed for his forgiveness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ lea Madinah (for Makkah), he appointed Abu Ruhm Kulthoom bin Husayn Ghifaari as the Ameer of Madinah.…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ left Madinah for Makkah on the tenth of Ramadhaan with ten thousand Sahabah, appointing Abu Ruhm Kulthoom as Ameer of Madinah, and camped at Marruz Zahraan.

narrations.excerpt: By the time Rasulullaah ﷺ reached Marruz Zahraan, the Quraysh were still in the dark. No news about Rasulullaah ﷺ had reached them and they had no idea what he was doing,…
narrations.summary: Abu Sufyaan, Hakeem bin Hizaam and Budayl set out to spy on the Muslims; Abu Sufyaan bin Haarith and Abdullaah bin Abi Umayyah, the Prophet's cousins, are admitted after Umm Salma interceded and both accept Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: When the Muslims camped at Marruz Zahraan, Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) said, "The Quraysh are destroyed! By Allaah! If Rasulullaah ﷺ were to enter Makkah by force before the…
narrations.summary: Abbaas tells the Quraysh that they are doomed unless they seek amnesty before the Muslims enter Makkah by force, and rides the Prophet's white mule out to find someone to warn them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) continues to say that he was still searching for someone when he heard the voices of Abu Sufyaan and Budayl bin Waraqa, who were talking to each…
narrations.summary: Abbaas meets Abu Sufyaan by night and brings him to the Prophet on the mule; Umar protests, and the Prophet grants Abu Sufyaan safe passage through Abbaas.

narrations.excerpt: When Rasulullaah ﷺ saw Abu Sufyaan, he said, "Shame on you, O Abu Sufyaan! Has the time not come for you to testify that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah?" Abu…
narrations.summary: Abu Sufyaan testifies to Tawheed and then to the Prophet's Risaalah after Abbaas urges him to accept Islaam before he is executed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) then said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Abu Sufyaan enjoys fame, so allow him some." Rasulullaah ﷺ agreed and said, "Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyaan shall…
narrations.summary: Abbaas asks for honour to be given to Abu Sufyaan, the Prophet grants safety to whoever enters Abu Sufyaan's house, locks his door or enters the Masjid, and Abu Sufyaan warns Makkah as the tribes pass by.

narrations.excerpt: Ibn Asaakir has narrated from Waaqidi a just like that of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas that Tabraani has narrated above. It also mentions that when Abu Sufyaan left (the…
narrations.summary: As the Muslims enter Makkah, Abu Sufyaan watches the tribal battalions pass with Abbaas, including those led by Khaalid, Zubayr, Abu Dharr and Sa'd bin Ubaadah, and the Prophet has Sa'd's flag handed to his son Qais.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Layla (RA) who reports that they were with Rasulullaah ﷺ when he informed them that Abu Sufyaan was at a place called Araak. The Sahabah (RA) then went there…
narrations.summary: Abu Layla reports that Abu Sufyaan was captured by the Sahabah at Araak and brought to the Prophet, who offers him Islaam and safety, and Abu Sufyaan remarks on the greatness of the Prophet's kingdom as the Ansaar pass by.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ left (Madinah) with an army of twelve thousand comprising of the Muhaajireen, the Ansaar, the Aslam tribe, the Ghifaar…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that Abu Sufyaan and Hakeem bin Hizaam were captured on their way to the Prophet, that Abbaas protected Abu Sufyaan, who accepted Islaam, and that the Prophet sent Abbaas to announce amnesty for Makkah while Hind attacked her husband.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Suhayl bin Amr (RA) narrates that he entered his house and locked the doors when Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived victoriously in Makkah. He then sent his son Abdullaah bin…
narrations.summary: Suhayl bin Amr locks his house at the conquest, his son secures amnesty for him, the Prophet ﷺ praises him, and Suhayl later accepts Islaam at Ji'irraanah and is given a hundred camels.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was in Makkah on the day that Makkah was conquered, he sent for Safwaah bin Umayyah, Abu Sufyaan bin Harb and Haarith…
narrations.summary: Umar reports that the Prophet ﷺ, after the conquest, compared his own treatment of the Quraysh with Yusuf and his brothers and pardoned Safwaan, Abu Sufyaan and Haarith, and Umar was embarrassed at his own eagerness for revenge.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Abi Husayn narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ Conquered Makkah, he entered the Kabah and when he. came out, he placed his hands on the frames of the door and…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abi Husayn and Abu Hurayrah report the Prophet ﷺ at the door of the Kabah pardoning the Quraysh with Yusuf's words, after which the people accept Islaam, and a version from Bayhaqi is added.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) narrates that on the day that Makkah was conquered, Ummu Hakeem bint Haarith bin Hishaam accepted Islaam. She was the wife of Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Ummu Hakeem accepts Islaam on the day of the conquest and secures amnesty for her husband Ikrama, who had fled to Yemen; she follows him to bring him back, and Ikrama kills the Roman slave who had tried to seduce her.

narrations.excerpt: When Hadhrat Ikrama drew close to Makkah, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to the Sahabah (RA), "ikrama the son of Abu Jahal is coming to you as a Mu'min and a Muhaajir so do not curse…
narrations.summary: Ikrama comes to the Prophet ﷺ as a Muhaajir, is granted amnesty and wife, and accepts Islaam by testifying to the kalimah after the Prophet ﷺ tells the Sahabah not to curse his dead father.

narrations.excerpt: Rasulullaah ﷺ then said to Hadhrat Ikrama (RA), "I shall grant you anything you ask for if 1 am able to." Hadhrat Ikrama (RA) asked, "I ask you to seek forgiveness from…
narrations.summary: Ikrama asks the Prophet ﷺ to pray for forgiveness for his past enmity and vows to spend double and fight double in the path of Allaah, while Suhayl bin Amr mocks his past opposition at Hunayn.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) has also narrated their incident but in fewer words. He says that when Hadhrat Ikrama (RA) reached the door of Rasulullaah ﷺ,…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr and Urwa bin Zubayr each give a shorter account of Ikrama's acceptance of Islaam, the Prophet's du'aa for his forgiveness, and Ikrama's vow to spend and fight double in the path of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ikrama (RA) continued fighting in Jihaad and in turn he was martyred in the Battle of Ajnaadeen during Khilaafah of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed…
narrations.summary: Ikrama is martyred in the Battle of Ajnaadeen during Abu Bakr's caliphate, having been appointed by the Prophet ﷺ to collect the zakaah of Hawaazin in the year of the farewell Hajj.

narrations.excerpt: Wahab Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) narrates that when Makkah was conquered, the wife of Hadhrat Safwaan bin Umayyah (RA) accepted Islaam. Her name was Baghoom bint…
narrations.summary: Safwaan bin Umayyah flees Makkah; his wife Baghoom accepts Islaam, and Umayr bin Wahab goes to Safwaan to tell him that the Prophet ﷺ has granted him amnesty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Safwaan (RA) then said, "By Allaah! I shall never return with you (to Makkah) until you bring me a sign which I may identify." (When Hadhrat Umayr returned to…
narrations.summary: Safwaan asks for a sign of the amnesty, Umayr brings the Prophet's turban, and after the Prophet grants him a four-month grace period Safwaan returns and dismounts to meet him.

narrations.excerpt: When Rasulullaah ﷺ marched against the Hawaazin tribe, Hadhrat Safwaan marched with him while still a Kaafir. Rasulullaah ﷺ sent someone to him to request that he loan…
narrations.summary: Safwaan lends a hundred coats of armour for the Battle of Hunayn, and when the Prophet ﷺ gives him a valley of camels and shepherds at Ji'irraanah, Safwaan accepts Islaam on the spot.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes from Hadhrat Safwaan (RA) that Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him to give some weapons on loan. He said, "Are you taking it away from me by force?"…
narrations.summary: Another narration of Safwaan's loan of armour: some of the coats are destroyed, the Prophet offers to pay for the damage, and Safwaan declines compensation because he wants to accept Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mundhir bin Jahm (RA) narrates from Hadhrat Huwaytib bin Abdil Uzza that he was terrified when Rasulullaah ﷺ entered Makkah when it was conquered. He left his…
narrations.summary: Mundhir bin Jahm reports that Huwaytib, terrified after the conquest, is persuaded by Abu Dharr to come to the Prophet ﷺ and accepts Islaam, and the Prophet ﷺ then grants him a loan and a share of the Hunayn booty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ikrama (RA) narrates that when Makkah was conquered, Haarith bin Hishaam and Abdullaah bin Abi Rabee'ah went to Hadhrat Ummu Haani Is the daughter…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ikrama reports that Ummu Haani granted protection to Haarith bin Hishaam and Abdullaah bin Abi Rabee'ah, that Ali tried to attack them and was stopped, that the Prophet ﷺ upheld her protection, and that Haarith then accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Muhammad bin Shurahbeel Abdari narrates that Hadhrat Nudhayr bin Haarith was amongst the most learned of people and used to say, "All praises belong to Allaah Who has…
narrations.summary: Nudhayr bin Haarith, one of the most learned of the Quraysh, is made steadfast by the Prophet's du'aa, accepts Islaam, and then receives a gift of a hundred camels from the Prophet ﷺ which he shares with a man of the Banu Duwal.

narrations.excerpt: Ibn is'haaq narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ left the Thaqeef tribe, Hadhrat Urwa bin Mas'ood (who belonged to the Thaqeef) followed him and caught up with him just…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Mas'ood follows the Prophet ﷺ after he leaves Thaqeef, accepts Islaam, and asks to go back to his people, despite the Prophet warning that they would kill him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Mas'ood (RA) then left to invite his people to Islaam expecting that they would not oppose him because of his high status among them. However, when he…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Mas'ood invites his people to Islaam from his house balcony, is struck by arrows and martyred, and the Prophet ﷺ compares his example among his people to the man in Surah Yaaseen.

narrations.excerpt: It was only a few months after killing Hadhrat Urwa bin Mas'ood (RA) that the Thaqeef tribe consulted with each other and decided that they did not have the strength to…
narrations.summary: The Thaqeef send a delegation to the Prophet ﷺ, Mughiera bin Shu'ba meets them, and their conditions are negotiated, including the Prophet refusing to exempt them from salaah, while Abu Sufyaan and Mughiera are sent to destroy their idol.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Wahab (RA) narrates that he asked Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) about the Thaqeef (delegation) when they pledged their allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ. He replied by saying…
narrations.summary: Wahab asks Jaabir about the Thaqeef's conditions, and Jaabir says the Prophet ﷺ accepted them while predicting that they would later pay zakaah and wage jihaad without being told.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aws bin Hudhayfa (RA) narrates, "We came to meet Rasulullaah ﷺ with the Thaqeef delegation. While the allies of the Thaqeef stayed with Hadhrat Mughiera bin…
narrations.summary: Aws bin Hudhayfa, who came with the Banu Maalik delegates, describes the Prophet ﷺ addressing them standing each night after Isha, and explains once that he came late because he had not finished his daily Qur'aan recitation.

narrations.excerpt: Ibn Is'haaq narrates, "When Hadhrat Abu. Bakr (RA) accepted Islaam and made his Islaam known, he started inviting people towards Allaah. He was well acquainted with the…
narrations.summary: Ibn Ishaaq reports that Abu Bakr gave da'wah to the people who confided in him, and that Zubayr, Uthmaan, Talha, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas and Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf accepted Islaam through him and then met the Prophet ﷺ.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asbaq narrates that he was a slave of Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) and a Christian. Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to present islaam to him saying, "If you accept…
narrations.summary: Asbaq, a Christian slave of Umar, is invited to Islaam and is freed on Umar's deathbed; Aslam reports Umar inviting an old Christian woman to Islaam after making wudhu with her water.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam (also a slave of Hadhrat Umar (RA)) narrates that when they were in Shaam, he brought some water for Hadhrat Umar (RA) to make wudhu with. Hadhrat Umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: Aslam relates that Umar made wudhu with water from an old Christian woman's house, invited her to Islaam, and when she said she was about to die, called on Allaah to witness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abi Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm and many others narrate that Hadhrat As'ad bin Zuraarah (RA) took Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Umayr to the locality of…
narrations.summary: As'ad bin Zuraarah brings Mus'ab bin Umayr to the Banu Abdil Ash'hal, Usayd bin Hudhayr is sent to confront them, and Usayd listens, accepts Islaam and sends Sa'd bin Mu'aadh to them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Usayd (RA) then took his spear and went to the place where Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh and his people were sitting in a gathering. When Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA)…
narrations.summary: Mus'ab gives da'wah to Sa'd bin Mu'aadh, who first reproaches As'ad, then listens to the Qur'aan recited by Mus'ab, and accepts Islaam after bathing, cleansing his clothes and praying two rakaahs.

narrations.excerpt: When his people saw him return, they said, "We swear by Allaah that Sa'd is returning to you with a look very different to the one he left you with." When Hadhrat Sa'd…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Mu'aadh tells the Banu Abdil Ash'hal that he will not speak to them until they believe, and the whole clan accepts Islaam by evening, after which Mus'ab continues his da'wah among the Ansaar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ibraheem bin Haarith (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Tulayb bin Umayr (RA) accepted Islaam, he went to his mother Arwa who was the daughter of Abdul…
narrations.summary: Tulayb bin Umayr accepts Islaam in the house of Arqam and persuades his mother Arwa bint Abdil Muttalib, who testifies to the kalimah and keeps encouraging him to support the Prophet ﷺ.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr narrates that shortly after their defeat at Badr, Umayr bin Wahab Jumhi who had been a Shaytaan from amongst the Shayaateen of the Quraysh was…
narrations.summary: Umayr bin Wahab sets out to kill the Prophet with a poisoned sword after plotting with Safwaan bin Umayyah, and Umar sees him at the Masjid and raises the alarm.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) then came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Nabi of Allaah! The enemy of Allaah Umayr bin Wahab has come with a sword hanging from his neck. Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Umar drags Umayr bin Wahab to the Prophet, who reveals the secret plot and then forgives him.

narrations.excerpt: Umayr exclaimed, "I testify that you are certainly the Rasool of Allaah. O Rasulullaah ﷺ We used to treat as a lie everything that you brought to us from the heavens and…
narrations.summary: Umayr bin Wahab accepts Islaam, asks leave to go to Makkah to call people to it, and Safwaan bin Umayyah swears never to speak to him again.

narrations.excerpt: Ibn Jareer has also narrated this incident from Hadhrat Urwa (RA) but with the addition that when Hadhrat Umayr (RA) arrived in Makkah, he stayed there inviting people to…
narrations.summary: Umayr bin Wahab invites people to Islaam in Makkah, and a large number accept at his hands.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) has also reported a narration which states that the Muslims were overjoyed when Hadhrat Umayr bin Wahab (RA) accepted Islaam. Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Umar says he now loves Umayr more than some of his own children, and Umayr confronts Safwaan in the Hateem, who stays silent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Umayyah (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Umayr (RA) returned to Makkah after accepting Islaam, he proceeded straight to his house without meeting Safwaan…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Umayyah relates that Umayr bin Wahb, after accepting Islaam, invited Safwaan bin Umayyah to Islaam at the Hateem, and Safwaan stayed silent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) says that he used to invite his mother to Islaam when she was still a Mushrik. One day as he was giving her the Da'wah, she told him things about…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah invites his mother to Islaam, the Prophet prays for her guidance, and she accepts Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) invites Hadhrat Abu Talha to Islaam when he Proposes to Her and he Accepts Islaam Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that before he accepted Islaam,…
narrations.summary: Ummu Sulaym makes Islaam the condition for marrying Abu Talha, who accepts Islaam, and Anas bin Maalik performs the nikaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that the Banu Sa'd bin Bakr tribe sent Hadhrat Dimaam bin Tha'laba (RA) as their representative to Rasulullaah When he arrived…
narrations.summary: Dimaam bin Tha'laba comes to Madinah as the representative of Banu Sa'd bin Bakr, questions the Prophet about the basics of Islaam, and accepts it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dimaam (RA) went to his camel, untied the rope and then rode away until he reached his people. The first thing he said was, "Laat and Uzza are most terrible!" The…
narrations.summary: Dimaam bin Tha'laba returns to his tribe, rejects the idols, and the people present with him accept Islaam by that evening.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Murrah (RA) narrates that he once performed Hajj with a group of his people during the Period of Ignorance. While in Makkah he had a dream in which he saw…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Murrah Juhani dreams in Makkah of a light and voices announcing the sealing of the Prophets and the destruction of idols, and tells his people.

narrations.excerpt: When Hadhrat Amr bin Murrah (RA) reached his locality, the news reached him that a person called Ahmad has been sent as a Rasul. He left home and came to Rasulullaah ﷺ.…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Murrah Juhani accepts Islaam from the Prophet, is sent back to call his tribe, and a man among them answers with verses of abuse, and Amr's curse on him is fulfilled.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Murrah (RA) left his locality with those of his people who accepted Islaam and came to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ greeted them and welcomed them. He…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Murrah Juhani brings the members of his tribe who accepted Islaam to the Prophet, who welcomes them and has a letter of terms written, which Qais bin Shammaas scribes.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) narrates that when the Muslims started performing Hajj during the ninth year after Hijrah, Hadhrat Urwa bin Mas'ood came to Rasulullaah ﷺ as…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Mas'ood, newly Muslim, asks the Prophet's leave to return to his people of Thaqeef to call them to Islaam, and they kill him.

narrations.excerpt: Numerous scholars have reported this narration at length. Their reports mention that Hadhrat Urwa bin Mas'ood (RA) reached home at night and went to his house. The people…
