narrations.summary: Mortally wounded by an arrow, Urwa bin Mas'ood forbids his people to take revenge for him, welcomes martyrdom and asks to be buried with the martyred Sahabah.

narrations.excerpt: Muhammad bin Is'haaq says that despite the harsh treatment that Rasulullaah saw his people mete out to him, he exerted 'all his efforts to guide them and to save them…
narrations.summary: The Quraysh warn Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi against the Prophet, and he resolves not to listen to him and stops his ears with wool.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tufayl bin Amr (RA) says, "When I went to the Masjid in the morning, Rasulullaah ﷺ was standing there, performing salaah near the Kabah. I stood close to him and…
narrations.summary: Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi hears the Prophet recite at the Ka'bah, follows him home, and accepts Islaam after the Qur'aan is recited to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tufayl (RA) says that he then went to his people and was at a valley from which he could see the people present there when a light radiated from between his eyes…
narrations.summary: Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi's prayer moves a light from between his eyes to the top of his whip, and it serves as a sign to his people as he approaches them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tufayl (RA) narrates that when he came to his people, his father who was an extremely old man came to him. Hadhrat Tufayl (RA) said, "Keep away from me, O father…
narrations.summary: Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi invites his father and his wife to Islaam, and both accept, while the rest of his tribe is slow to respond.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tufayl (RA) then went to Rasulullaah ﷺ in Makkah and said, "O Nabi of Allaah! The Dows tribe has overpowered me. Please invoke Allaah's curses on them." (instead)…
narrations.summary: Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi asks the Prophet to curse the Dows tribe, but the Prophet prays for their guidance, and Tufayl later brings them to Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) has also narrated from Hadhrat Tufayl bin Amr the story of how he accepted Islaam, how he gave Da'wah to his father, his wife and his…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas recounts Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi's Islaam, and adds that the Prophet sent him to burn an idol before he was martyred at Yamaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Tufayl (RA) arrived in Makkah, some people from the Quraysh told him about Rasulullaah ﷺ and requested him to assess…
narrations.summary: Another account of Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi's Islaam, then of Jundub bin Amr and seventy-five Dows accepting Islaam at the Prophet's hand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hishaam bin Al Aas Umawi (RA) narrates that (during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) he and another person we/e sent with the invitation to Islaam to…
narrations.summary: During Abu Bakr's caliphate, Hishaam bin Al Aas Umawi and companions go to Jabala bin Ayham in Damascus with the invitation to Islaam, and predict the conquest of his kingdom.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ziyaad bin Haarith Sudaa'ee JU narrates that he met Rasulullaah subheading "Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatches Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) to his people the Baahilah tribe".…
narrations.summary: Ziyaad bin Haarith Sudaa'ee accepts Islaam and his people follow; when the Prophet appoints him their leader and he asks for a share of zakaah, he withdraws the request after the Prophet's warnings, and the Prophet appoints another man from the delegation.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Ka'b narrates that the two sons of Zuhayr who were Bujayr and Ka'b left on a journey and had reached a spring called Abraqal Azzaaf. Bujayr then…
narrations.summary: Bujayr bin Zuhayr accepts Islaam and writes to his brother Ka'b bin Zuhayr, who, after the Prophet orders his execution, comes to Madinah and accepts Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Moosa bin Aqba says that Hadhrat Ka'b bin Zuhayr (RA) recited his poem "Baanat Su'aad" to Rasulullaah ﷺ in his Masjid in Madinah until he reached the couplets…
narrations.summary: Ka'b bin Zuhayr recites his poem Baanat Su'aad in the Prophet's Masjid, the Prophet signals the Sahabah to listen, and Bujayr's letter urging Ka'b to Islaam is also quoted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) wrote the following letter to the Persian people, inviting them to Islaam. in the name of Allaah The…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed writes to the Persian leadership, Rustam and Mahraan, inviting them to Islaam and offering the Jizya as the alternative to war.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi (RA) narrates that Banu Buqayla read to him the letter that Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) wrote to the people of Madaa'in. It read: From Khaalid bin…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed's letter to the Persian leadership at Madaa'in, offering Islaam, the Jizya or war, is read to Sha'bi and alarms the Persians in 12 AH.

narrations.excerpt: Imaam Sha'bi says that Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) wrote a letter to Hurmuz before he left with Uzaadhiba the father of Ziyaadhiba, who was from Yamaamah. In those…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed sends letters to the Persian commander Hurmuz and to the Persian royal family, offering Islaam, protection for the Jizya or war, and two envoys carry them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haarith bin Muslim Tameemi (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah Wife once sent them on a military expedition. When they reached the place they intended to attack, he…
narrations.summary: Haarith bin Muslim Tameemi gets a town to say Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, and the Prophet rewards him with a sealed letter that Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan each honour.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zuhri (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Ka'b bin Umayr Ghifaari with a group of fifteen men. They rode to a place in Shaam called Dhaat Itlaa where…
narrations.summary: Ka'b bin Umayr Ghifaari is sent with fifteen men to invite people at Dhaat Itlaa in Shaam, and after they are refused, all but one are martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Imaam Zuhri narrates that it was in Dhul Hijjah 7 A.H. that Rasulullaah ﷺ returned from performing the Umrah he had missed. He then sent Hadhrat Ibn Abil Awjaa Sulami…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abil Awjaa Sulami invites a large enemy force to Islaam, which they refuse, and most of his fifty men are martyred before the survivors return to Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyab (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr sent armies to Shaam, he appointed Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abi Sufyaan Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) and…
narrations.summary: When Abu Bakr sends armies to Shaam, he walks with the commanders to see them off and gives them instructions to invite the enemy to Islaam, then to the Jizya, before fighting, and forbids harming women, children and the monks.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) sent Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed to fight those Arabs who had forsaken Islaam (the Murtaddeen), he instructed…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr instructs Khaalid bin Waleed, sent against the apostates, to invite them back to Islaam, to accept any who return, and to fight only those who refuse.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalih bin Kaysaan (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed arrived in Heera, the nobles of Heera accompanied by Qabeesa bin Ayaas bin Hayya Taa'ee left…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed invites the nobles of Heera, led by Qabeesa and Haani, to Islaam, and when they refuse war they agree to pay seventy thousand Dirhams as Jizya.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that when the two armies faced each other before the Battle of Yarmook, Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) and Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abi Sufyaan…
narrations.summary: Before the Battle of Yarmook, Abu Ubaydah and four other Sahabah go to meet Tadhaaruk, Heraclius' brother, and invite him to Islaam, but the treaty does not materialise and the battle is fought.

narrations.excerpt: Waaqidi reports that during the Battle of Yarmook, one of the most senior Roman commanders by the name of Jarja stepped forward from the line of soldiers and asked to…
narrations.summary: During the Battle of Yarmook, the Roman commander Jarja asks to meet Khaalid bin Waleed and questions him about the Prophet and the sword he was given.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) Allaah sent His Nabi amongst us who preached to us. However, we expressed resentment and kept our distance from him. Even I was amongst those who…
narrations.summary: Khaalid explains that the Prophet called him a sword of Allaah and that the Muslims call people to testify that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah and that Muhammad is His servant and Rasul, and Jarja asks what they call people to.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) They will have to pay the Jjzya and we will protect them. jarja: What if they do not pay it? Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) We then declare war against them…
narrations.summary: Khaalid answers Jarja on the Jizya, the equal standing of all believers and the reward of later converts, then Jarja accepts Islaam, prays two rakaahs and dies of wounds in the battle that day.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) once delivered a lecture to the Muslims and encouraged them to go to the non-Arab countries and leave the…
narrations.summary: Khaalid urges the Muslims to leave Arabia for the fertile lands of the non-Arabs and fight for them, even apart from the obligation of jihaad and da'wah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abi Habeeb narrates that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab JU! wrote to Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) saying, "I have already written to you to tell you…
narrations.summary: Yazeed bin Abi Habeeb relates Umar's letter to Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas ordering that enemies be invited to Islaam for three days before fighting, with the booty rules for those who accept before or after battle.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari narrates that when a Muslim army under the command of Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) laid siege to a Persian fortresses, the soldiers said to him, "O…
narrations.summary: Salmaan Faarsi invited the Persians of a besieged fortress to Islaam for three days before his army attacked.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) was the commander of the Muslim army and had been appointed to invite the enemy to Islaam. Hadhrat Atiyya (RA)…
narrations.summary: Salmaan Faarsi was appointed to invite the people of Bahursher and Qasrul Abyadh to Islaam, giving each three days, as Atiyya reports.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas Ji sent a group of leading Sahabah (RA) to invite Rustam to Islaam. The group included Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Muqarrin, Hadhrat Furaat bin…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas sends leading Companions to invite Rustam to Islaam at Qaadisiyyah; they tell him they are sure of victory, and Rustam recounts a dream in which the Persian weapons were handed to the Prophet and then to Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sayf narrates from his teachers that when the two armies (Muslim and Persian) faced each other, Rustam sent a message to Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas requesting…
narrations.summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba explained Islaam to Rustam, the Persian commander, before the Battle of Qaadisiyyah, and Rustam asked questions about it.

narrations.excerpt: The narrators state further that at the request of Rustam, Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) sent another envoy who happened to be Hadhrat Rib'ee bin Aamir (RA). When Hadhrat Rib'ee ii…
narrations.summary: Rib'ee bin Aamir, sent by Sa'd, invited Rustam to Islaam in his court and refused his request for more than three days to decide.

narrations.excerpt: The next day, the Persians asked for another person and Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) sent Hadhrat Hudhayfa bin Mihsin (RA) who addressed them in the manner that Hadhrat Rib'ee (RA)…
narrations.summary: On the second and third days Hudhayfa bin Mihsin and Mughiera bin Shu'ba presented Islaam to Rustam, who answered with a parable and threatened to kill them all.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il (RA) narrates, "Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) marched with the Muslim army until they set up camp at a place called Qaadisiyya. I cannot tell, precisely but we…
narrations.summary: Before the Battle of Qaadisiyyah Mughiera bin Shu'ba went to Rustam, mocked the Persians' taunts, and presented Islaam and Jizya, and the Muslims then defeated the Persians at the river crossing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Qurra (RA) narrates that when the Battle of Qaadisiyya took place, Hadhrat Mughiera (RA) was sent to meet the Persian leader. Hadhrat Mughiera (RA)…
narrations.summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba was sent to the Persian leader before Qaadisiyyah and told him the Muslims had come to call to Islaam and to fight, not for food.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sayf narrates that Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) sent a group of Sahabah (RA) to the Persian leader to invite him to Islaam before the battle. When they requested permission…
narrations.summary: Sa'd's envoys, led by Nu'maan bin Muqarrin and Mughiera bin Shu'ba, invited the Persian king Yazdajird to Islaam before the battle, and Mughiera answered his threats.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad ﷺ, Hadhrat Talha (RA) and others narrate that during the Battle for Tikrit, the Romans saw that every offensive they launched against the Muslims…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mu'tam invited the Arab tribes of Taghlib, Iyaad and Namir to testify to the Kalimah and accept what the Prophet brought, and they accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) and Hadhrat Ubaadah (RA) narrate that Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas marched to Egypt after Hadhrat Umar (RA) had returned to Madinah (from Shaam). Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Al Aas offered the Egyptian priests Islaam or Jizya before the battle for Egypt, and after a night attack the Egyptians came out to negotiate at Aynush Shams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Buraydah narrates that whenever a Muslim regiment was gathered, the Ameerul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Umar (RA) appointed someone with knowledge and sound…
narrations.summary: Umar appointed Salama bin Qais Ash'jaee as commander of a regiment and told him to offer the enemy Islaam, then Jizya, and only then fight.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Bau Umayya narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) set up camp at Isfahan, he invited the people to accept Islaam. When they refused to accept Islaam,…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari invited the people of Isfahan to Islaam and then offered Jizya, but they broke the night's agreement and attacked, and the Muslims were given victory.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh (RA) Accepts Islaam and the Role that his son and Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) Played In this Ibn Is'haaq narrates that after some of the Ansaar…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Jamooh, who kept an idol, was won over when the young Muslims of Banu Salma repeatedly disgraced it, and he then accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when a few members of the Banu Salma tribe accepted Islaam, the wife and son of Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh (RA) also accepted Islaam. Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Jamooh's son recited the opening verses of the Qur'aan to his father, who consulted his idol, broke it, and accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Waaqidi says that it is commonly believed that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) was the last person from his family to accept Islaam. He was extremely dedicated to the worship of…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Rawwaaha smashed Abu Dardaa's idol, and Abu Dardaa, seeing that it could not defend itself, went to the Prophet and accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ziyaad bin Jaz Zubaydi narrates a lengthy report about what happened after the Muslims conquered Alexandria during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Umar In this report he…
narrations.summary: Umar's letter to Amr bin Al Aas set the terms for Alexandria's Jizya and for the prisoners, who were to be offered Islaam or their own religion.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ziyaad bin Jaz states further, "Hadhrat Arrtr bin Al Aas (RA) then sent a letter to the king of Alexandria, explaining to him the instructions that the Ameerul…
narrations.summary: After the prisoners of Alexandria were each offered Islaam or Christianity, Abdullaah bin Abdur Rahmaan, known as Abu Maryam, accepted Islaam despite his family's opposition.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that when (the Ameerul Mu'mineen) Hadhrat Ali (RA) once went to the marketplace, he found a Christian selling a coat of armour. Recognising the…
narrations.summary: Ali's armour was found with a Christian, and when the judge Shuray ruled that Ali needed proof, the Christian accepted Islaam and Ali gave him the armour.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Haakim states that the armour of Hadhrat Ali (RA) once fell off his camel and was found by a person who sold it. When the armour was found in ther…
narrations.summary: Ali's armour was found with a Jew, the judge Shuray refused Ali's son Hasan's testimony, and the Jew, persuaded by Ali's honesty, accepted Islaam and was given the armour with money.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jareer (RA) narrates, ""The condition on which we (the male Sahabah pledged allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ was similar to the conditions on which the females pledged…
narrations.summary: Jareer reports the conditions the male Sahabah pledged to the Prophet, which matched those the women pledged, with the promise of Jannah for keeping them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aswad (RA) narrates he saw people pledging their allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ on the day that Makkah was conquered. Rasulullaah ﷺ sat at a place called Qarn…
narrations.summary: Aswad saw people pledge to Islaam and the Shahaadah on the day of the Conquest of Makkah, and his teacher explained what the Shahaadah required.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Bayhaqi adds that everyone from the youngsters to the elders as well as men and women all pledged their allegiance to Islaam and to the Shahaadah at the…
narrations.summary: Bayhaqi reports that people of every age and both sexes pledged to Islaam and the Shahaadah at the Prophet's hands.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaashi bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that he and his brother went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and he said, "Accept our pledge of allegiance to Hijrah." Rasulullaah ﷺ said to…
narrations.summary: Mujaashi bin Mas'ood asked to pledge to Hijrah after the conquest, and the Prophet instead took his pledge to Islaam and Jihaad, since Hijrah had ended.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ziyaad bin Ilaaqa narrates that when Hadhrat Mughiera bin Shu'ba passed away, he heard Hadhrat Jareer bin Abdillaah (RA) address the people saying, "I advise you…
narrations.summary: After Mughiera bin Shu'ba died, Jareer bin Abdillaah urged the people to fear Allaah and wish well for every Muslim, and Ziyaad bin Haarith Sudaa'ee's pledge to Islaam is also recorded.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Basheer bin Khasaasiyyah (RA) narrates that when he approached Rasulullaah (jjjjr to pledge his allegiance, he asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ To what should I pledge my…
narrations.summary: Basheer bin Khasaasiyah asked, when pledging, to keep the conditions only as far as he was able, and this concession was allowed for everyone after him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jareer (RA) narrates that he pledged allegiance at the hand of Rasulullaah ﷺ that he would establish salaah, pay zakaah and wish well for every Muslim.
narrations.summary: Jareer bin Abdullaah pledged to the Prophet to establish salaah, pay zakaah and wish well for every Muslim.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states from Hadhrat Jareer (RA) states that he said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Do state the conditions (of the pledge) for you are best aware of the conditions."…
narrations.summary: Jareer asked the Prophet to state the conditions of the pledge, and he set out worship of Allaah alone, salaah, zakaah, wishing well for Muslims and rejecting shirk.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Jareer (RA) came to Rasulullaah /Rasulullaah asked him to stretch out his hand (to pledge his allegiance). Hadhrat Jareer (RA)…
narrations.summary: When Jareer came to pledge, the Prophet asked him to commit to surrendering to Allaah and wishing well for every Muslim, and Jareer accepted as far as he was able.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik Ash'ja'ee (RA) narrates that he was with seven, eight or nine persons in the company of Rasulullaah ﷺ when he said, "Will you not pledge allegiance…
narrations.summary: Awf bin Maalik Ash'ja'ee and his companions pledged to worship Allaah alone, pray the five salaahs and never ask anyone for anything.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once asked, "Who would like to pledge their allegiance?" Hadhrat Thowbaan (RA) who was the slave of Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Thowbaan pledged to the Prophet never to ask anyone for anything, and Abu Umaamah reports him dismounting to pick up his own fallen whip, as Abu Bakr also did.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates that he pledged allegiance at the hands of Rasulullaah ﷺ five times, that Rasulullaah ﷺ took promises from him seven times and Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr reports the pledges he gave the Prophet: to fear no critic for Allaah's sake, never to ask anyone for anything, and never to accept a trust.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sahl bin Sa'd (RA) that he was with Hadhrat Abu Dharr, Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit, Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri, Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama and a sixth Sahabi when…
narrations.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that Abu Dharr, Ubaadah bin Saamit, Abu Sa'eed Khudri, Muhammad bin Maslama and a sixth Sahabi pledged never to be swayed by critics in Allaah's cause, and the Prophet released the sixth when he asked.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) narrates that he was with a few leaders (of Madinah) who pledged their allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ. He adds that they pledged that they…
narrations.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit reports the pledge taken from Madinah's leaders: no shirk, theft, fornication, unlawful killing, plunder or disobedience, with Jannah promised for keeping it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) narrates that they were with Rasulullaah when he said, "Pledge allegiance at my hand that you will not ascribe any as partner to Allaah,…
narrations.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit relays the Prophet's pledge against shirk, theft and fornication, and says that a sinner's fate is then left to Allaah's forgiveness or punishment.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit iS narrates that they were eleven persons when the pledge of allegiance was taken for the first time at Aqaba. He says that because fighting in…
narrations.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit relates that eleven men made the first Aqaba pledge, promising not to associate partners with Allaah, steal, commit adultery, slander, kill their children, or disobey the Prophet in good, and that the same men returned the next year.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ya'la bin Munyah (RA) narrates that he approached Rasulullaah ﷺ the day after Makkah was conquered and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ. Allow my father to pledge that he…
narrations.summary: Ya'la bin Munyah asked to pledge his father to Hijrah after the conquest of Makkah, and the Prophet instead took a pledge of Jihaad because Hijrah had ended.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haarith bin Ziyaad Saa'idi (RA) narrates that he approached Rasulullaah ﷺ during the Battle of Khandaq while people were busy pledging their allegiance to Hijrah…
narrations.summary: During the Battle of Khandaq the Prophet declined a Hijrah pledge from outside Madinah and praised the Ansaar, saying whoever loves them will be loved by Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that during the ten years that Rasulullaah ﷺ lived in Makkah (after announcing his Nabuwaat), he would visit people at the places where they…
narrations.summary: Jaabir describes how the Prophet sought asylum at the Hajj markets, how the Ansaar of Yathrib offered it, and how seventy of them pledged at Aqaba to protect him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ka'b bin Maalik ij narrates that when they (the Ansaar) gathered in the valley (of Aqaba), they waited for Rasulullaah ﷺ until he arrived with Hadhrat Abbaas bin…
narrations.summary: Ka'b bin Maalik describes the Ansaar gathering at Aqaba with the Prophet and Abbaas, who asks them to guarantee his protection; Baraa bin Ma'roor pledges to protect him as they protect their families, and Abul Haytham bin Tayyihaan asks about the Jews and whether the Prophet will return to his people, and the Prophet answers that he shares their fate.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ka'b (RA) narrates further that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to them, "Send to me twelve leaders from among you who will head their people in all matters." The Ansaar then…
narrations.summary: Ka'b bin Maalik reports that the Prophet asked the Ansaar for twelve leaders to head their people, and they chose nine from Khazraj and three from Aws.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that amongst the first people to pledge allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ was Hadhrat Abul Haytham bit Tayyihaan (RA). He said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that Abul Haytham bin Tayyihaan was among the first to pledge, and after asking whether his people would help the Prophet, they all followed him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aasim bin Umar bin Qataadah (RA) narrates that when the Ansaar gathered to pledge their allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Abbaas bin Ubaadah bin Nadhla who…
narrations.summary: Abbaas bin Ubaadah warned the Ansaar of the cost of the pledge before they took it for Jannah, and when he offered to attack Mina the Prophet said he had not been commanded to fight.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ went to the trench (before the Battle of Ahzaab) early one morning, he found the Muhaajireen and Ansaar digging in the…
narrations.summary: Before the Battle of Ahzaab the Prophet ﷺ prayed for the Muhaajireen and Ansaar digging the trench in cold and hunger, and they pledged to wage jihaad as long as they lived; similar pledges by Basheer, Ya'la and Mujaashi are cited.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salama bin Akwa (RA) narrates that after he pledged allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he took shade beneath a tree. When there were fewer people, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to…
narrations.summary: After pledging allegiance under a tree, Salama bin Akwa was asked by the Prophet ﷺ to pledge again, and the pledge he gave was to death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zaid (RA) reports that during the Battle of Harra (in 63 A.H.), someone came to him and said that people were pledging to die at the hands of Ibn…
narrations.summary: During the Battle of Harra, Abdullaah bin Zaid said that no one may pledge to die after the demise of the Prophet ﷺ, when people were pledging to die against Ibn Handhala.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaydullaah bin Raafi (RA) narrates that when a few containers of wine arrived from somewhere, Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) tore them open. He then said, "We…
narrations.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit, having torn open a shipment of wine, recounted the terms of his pledge to the Prophet ﷺ: to listen and obey, to spend in hardship and ease, to speak the truth and to protect the Prophet ﷺ, in exchange for Jannah. A second version of his words follows.

narrations.excerpt: Ibn jareer narrates from Hadhrat Jareer (RA) that he pledged to listen, to obey and wish well for all Muslims. Ibn Jareer also, reports another narration from Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Jareer bin Abdillaah pledged to listen, obey and wish well for all Muslims; the Prophet ﷺ told him to pledge only to the best of his ability. Jareer's custom in trade of letting the other party decide is also recorded.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that whenever the Sahabah (RA) pledged to listen and to obey at the hands of Rasulullaah ﷺ, he told them to add the clause: "To…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that when the Sahabah pledged to listen and obey, the Prophet ﷺ told them to add the clause 'to the best of my ability'.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Utba bin Abd (RA) narrates that he pledged allegiance to Rasulullaah seven times. On five occasions he pledged obedience and on two he pledged his love.
narrations.summary: Utba bin Abd narrates that he pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ seven times, five of them pledges of obedience and two of love.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "With these very hands did I pledged allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ that I would listen and obey to the best of my ability."
narrations.summary: Anas says that with his own hands he pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ to listen and obey to the best of his ability.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Atiyya (RA) narrates all the women of the Ansaar gathered in a house when Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Madinah. Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Umar to them and…
narrations.summary: Ummu Atiyya relates how the Prophet ﷺ sent Umar to the women of the Ansaar and took their pledge not to associate partners with Allaah, steal, commit adultery, kill their children, slander or disobey him in good. Umar then gave instructions on the Eid salaah, funerals and Jumu'ah for women.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salma bint Qais (RA) was one of Rasulullaah ﷺ's maternal aunts. She belonged to the Banu Adi bin Najjaar tribe and had performed salaah facing both Qiblas behind…
narrations.summary: Salma bint Qais, the Prophet's maternal aunt, pledged with the Ansaar women. Uqayla bint Ateeq and Umaymah bint Ruqayqah each give their own pledges, and the Prophet ﷺ says his pledge to women is confirmed by speech, not by handshake.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uqayla bint Ateeq bin Haarith (RA) narrates that she, her mother Qareera, bint Haarith Utwaariyyah and other women from the Muhaajireen approached Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Uqayla bint Ateeq describes her and her mother Qareera's pledge to the Prophet, which he took without touching their hands, and Umaymah bint Ruqayqah describes the women's pledge, which the Prophet confirmed by speech alone.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umayma bint Ruqayqa approached to pledge her allegiance to Islaam. Rasulullaah ﷺ said to her, "I require you to…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr relates how Umayma bint Ruqayqa came to pledge to Islaam, and the Prophet ﷺ set out the clauses: no shirk, theft, adultery, killing children, slander, wailing, or display like the women of the Period of Ignorance.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Faatima bint Utba bin Rabee'ah came to pledge her allegiance at the hand of Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ asked her to pledge…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha relates that Faatima bint Utba came to pledge; the Prophet ﷺ asked her to pledge the clauses of the Qur'aanic verse, and she accepted after Aa'isha confirmed that all the women had agreed to them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Azza bint Khaabil (RA) approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and pledged that she would not fornicate, would not steal and would not bury her children alive neither in public…
narrations.summary: Azza bint Khaabil pledged not to commit adultery, steal or bury her children alive, and explains her understanding that burying them alive in secret means spoiling them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Faatima bint Utba bin Rabee'ah bin Abdish Shams narrates that Hadhrat Abu Hudhayfa bin Utba (RA) took her along with (her sister) Hadhrat Hind bint Utba to…
narrations.summary: Faatima bint Utba and her sister Hind bint Utba come with Abu Hudhayfa to pledge. Hind is permitted by her husband Abu Sufyaan to take food from his house, and her gold bangles are described as coals of Jahannam if zakaah is not paid. The Prophet ﷺ says no one has true Imaan until he is more beloved to them than their children and parents.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Hind bint Utba (RA) came to pledge allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he looked at her hands and said, "Go and transform your…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha relates that Hind bint Utba was told to go and dye her hands with henna before pledging, that she pledged to avoid shirk, theft, adultery and killing children, and that the Prophet called her gold bangles coals of Jahannam if their zakaah was not paid.

narrations.excerpt: Another famous narration states that when Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "That you do not commit adultery", she said, "Does a free woman ever commit adultery?" and when Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Further accounts of Hind bint Utba's pledge: she goes with Umar to the Prophet ﷺ after Abu Sufyaan's remark, and Abu Sufyaan pardons her past taking of his wealth. The Prophet ﷺ recognises her, takes her pledge and recites its clauses, including the prohibition of wailing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Usayd bin Abi Usayd Barraad narrates from one of the women who pledged allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ that amongst the things that Rasulullaah required them to…
narrations.summary: Usayd bin Abi Usayd Barraad relates from one of the women who pledged that the Prophet required them not to disobey him in good, scratch their faces, dishevel their hair, tear their collars or pray for destruction.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ali bin Husayn (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ accepted the pledge of allegiance from Hadhrat Hasan, Husayn, Abdullaah bin Abbaas and Abdullaah bin…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Ali bin Husayn relates that the Prophet ﷺ accepted the pledge of Hasan, Husayn, Abdullaah bin Abbaas and Abdullaah bin Ja'far while they were still young boys, and accepted pledges from no other children except those of his household.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) have stated that they went to pledge their allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ when they were only seven…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr and Abdullaah bin Ja'far say they went to pledge to the Prophet ﷺ at the age of seven. He smiled, stretched out his hands and accepted their pledges.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hirmaas bin Ziyaad (RA) narrates that he was still a child when he stretched out his hands to pledge his allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ, but Rasulullaah ﷺ did not…
narrations.summary: Hirmaas bin Ziyaad recounts that as a child he stretched out his hand to pledge to the Prophet ﷺ, but the pledge was not accepted from him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muntashir narrates from his father that when the Sahabah (RA) pledged their allegiance at the hands of Rasulullaah ﷺ, he stipulated that their pledges be solely…
narrations.summary: Muntashir relates the terms on which the Sahabah pledged to the Prophet ﷺ, and Abu Bakr's condition that they obey him only while he obeys Allaah. Ibn Afeef describes Abu Bakr taking pledges after the Prophet's demise, to obey Allaah, His Book and the Ameer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Afeef (RA) narrates that he saw Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) accepting the pledge of allegiance form people after the demise of Rasulullaah Wife. When a group of…
narrations.summary: Ibn Afeef recounts that Abu Bakr took allegiance from the Companions to obey Allaah, His Book and the Ameer, and that Ibn Afeef later came to pledge on the same terms and was accepted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Safar (RA) narrates that whenever Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) sent an army to Shaam, he would make them pledge that they would fight with spears (if need be) and…
narrations.summary: Abu Safar relates that whenever Abu Bakr sent an army to Shaam he made the soldiers pledge to fight with spears if needed and to stay steadfast in a plague.

narrations.excerpt: Hssadhrat Anas narrates, "I arrived in Madinah after Hadhrat Abu Bakr had passed away and Hadhrat Umar (RA) had assumed the post of Khalifah. I said to Hadhrat Umar (RA),…
narrations.summary: Anas went to Madinah after Abu Bakr's death and asked Umar to let him pledge as he had to Abu Bakr. Umayr bin Atiyya and Abdullaah bin Ukaym also pledged to Umar, who said the pledge gives each side rights over the other.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umayr bin Atiyya Laythi (RA) narrates that he went to Hadhrat Umar and said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Raise your hand - may Allaah always keep it high - so that I…
narrations.summary: Umayr bin Atiyya Laythi asks Umar to raise his hand so he can pledge to him as the Prophet's pledge was taken, and Umar says the pledge gives rights on both sides; Abdullaah bin Ukaym adds that he pledged to Umar with these hands.

narrations.excerpt: Saleem Abu Aamir narrates that a delegation from Hamraa came to Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and pledged that they would not ascribe anything as partner to Allaah, would…
narrations.summary: Saleem Abu Aamir relates that a delegation from Hamraa pledged to Uthmaan not to associate partners with Allaah, to establish salaah, pay zakaah, fast in Ramadhaan and give up the festivities of the fire-worshippers. Uthmaan accepted their pledge only after they agreed to all of these.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhrama (RA) narrates that the group (of six Sahabah that Hadhrat Umar (RA) had appointed (to select a Khalifah from amongst themselves) had gathered…
narrations.summary: Miswar bin Makhrama relates how the six Sahabah appointed by Umar consulted, and Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf took their choice. After private talks with Ali and Uthmaan he pledged to Uthmaan, and the Muhaajireen, Ansaar, army leaders and the public followed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nufayr narrates that they were once sitting with Hadhrat Miqdaad bin Aswad Ji when someone passed by. The person said, "Blessed are the eyes that saw Rasuiullaah…
narrations.summary: Nufayr relates that Miqdaad bin Aswad rebuked a man who wished he had lived in the Prophet's time. He reminded him of the darkness before Islaam, of the Qur'aan separating truth from falsehood even between father and son, and of the hardships believers bore, citing Surah Furqaan 74.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi narrates that a person from Kufa once asked Hadhrat Hudhayfa (RA), "O Abu Abdillaah! Did you people see Rasulullaah ﷺ and associate with…
narrations.summary: A man from Kufa asks Hudhayfa what life was like with the Prophet ﷺ. Hudhayfa describes the fear, hunger and bitter cold of the Battle of the Trench and tells him not to wish for such a time.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I have been harassed for the sake of Allaah like none other and I have been threatened for the sake of Allaah like…
narrations.summary: Anas reports the Prophet ﷺ saying that he was harassed and threatened for Allaah's sake more than anyone, and that for thirty days and nights he and Bilaal had almost no food.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aqeel bin Abi Taalib JI narrates that members of the Quraysh approached Abu Taalib and complained, "Your nephew (Rasulullaah ﷺ) comes to us in our homes and…
narrations.summary: Aqeel bin Abi Taalib relates that the Quraysh complained to Abu Taalib about the Prophet's preaching, and when Abu Taalib asked him to stop, the Prophet said he could not abandon his mission; Abu Taalib then assured the Quraysh that his nephew never lies.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Bayhaqi reports that Abu Taalib called for Rasulullaah ﷺ and told him that the people had come to him and told him many things about what Rasulullaah ﷺ was…
narrations.summary: Abu Taalib asks the Prophet to stop, and the Prophet refuses even if the sun and moon were placed in his hands; Jaabir then narrates how Utba bin Rabee'ah failed to bargain the Prophet off and was moved by his recitation of Surah Sajdah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) narrates that when Abu Taalib passed away, a fool from amongst the fools of the Quraysh approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and threw sand at him.…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ja'far relates that after Abu Taalib died a foolish man of the Quraysh threw sand at the Prophet ﷺ. His daughter wiped it away and wept, and he told her that Allaah would protect her father. He also said the Quraysh had not dared harm him while Abu Taalib lived.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) had mentioned that when Abu Taalib passed away, the Quraysh started treating Rasulullaah ﷺ very harshly. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "O my uncle! I…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that after Abu Taalib died the Quraysh treated the Prophet ﷺ very harshly, and the Prophet ﷺ said he was quickly feeling his uncle's loss.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haarith bin Haarith (RA) narrates that he once asked his father, "What is this gathering all about?" His father replied, "These people have gathered around an…
narrations.summary: Haarith bin Haarith recounts seeing the Prophet ﷺ calling people to Tawheed and Imaan and being harmed, until a girl, Zaynab, brought him water and a cloth. Muneeb Azdi describes the Prophet ﷺ calling people to La ilaaha illallaah while being abused, and the same girl bringing him water.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that he once asked Hadhrat Abul Aas (RA) about the worst thing that the Mushrikeen did to Rasulullaah ﷺ. He said, "When Rasulullaah gjgjj was…
narrations.summary: Abul Aas describes the worst thing the mushrikeen did to the Prophet ﷺ: Uqba bin Abi Mu'eet throttled him with a cloth while he prayed at the Hateem, until Abu Bakr pushed Uqba away and recited Surah Mu'min 28.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) narrates that he had never seen the Quraysh try to assassinate Rasulullaah ﷺ except on one occasion when a group of them were sitting together…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Al Aas recounts the one time he saw the Quraysh try to kill the Prophet ﷺ: Uqba bin Abi Mu'eet throttled him while he prayed near the Maqaam of Ibraheem, and Abu Bakr rescued him. The Prophet ﷺ then warned the Quraysh that he had been sent to slaughter them, and Abu Jahal replied to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) narrates that he once asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr, "In venting their enmity, what was the worst that you saw the Quraysh do to harm…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr asks Abdullaah bin Amr about the worst Quraysh treatment of the Prophet ﷺ. Abdullaah describes their mockery and their final confrontation with the Prophet ﷺ, when Abu Bakr defended him. Asmaa bint Abi Bakr adds her own account of the attack and of her father being beaten.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that the Mushrikeen once beat Rasulullaah ﷺ up so badly that he fell unconscious. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said, "Shame on you…
narrations.summary: Anas relates that the mushrikeen beat the Prophet ﷺ until he was unconscious, and Abu Bakr protested that they were killing a man for saying Allaah is his Rabb. Another report says the attackers then turned on Abu Bakr.

narrations.excerpt: While addressing the people, Hadhrat Ali (RA) once asked, "O people! Who is the most courageous person?" "You are, O Ameerul Mu'mineen," the people submitted. Hadhrat Ali…
narrations.summary: Ali asks the people who is most courageous and answers Abu Bakr: at Badr he stood guard by the Prophet ﷺ with a drawn sword, and when the Quraysh seized the Prophet ﷺ he alone defended him. Ali says a moment of Abu Bakr's life is better than the believer of Fir'oun's court, who hid his Imaan, since Abu Bakr made his Imaan public.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that while Rasulullaah ﷺ was performing salaah in the Masjidul Haraam, seven members of the Quraysh were sitting in the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood relates that Hamza, angered on learning what Abu Jahal had done to the Prophet ﷺ at the Ka'bah, struck Abu Jahal with his bow and then accepted Islaam. Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi gives a second version in which Hamza struck Abu Jahal's head with his bow near Safa and Marwa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ya'qoob bin Utba narrates that Abu Jahal once approached Rasulullaah W at Safa and caused him great harm. During those days, Hadhrat Hamza was an avid hunter and…
narrations.summary: Abu Jahal harassed the Prophet at Safa, and Hamza, angered on hearing of it, struck Abu Jahal with his bow in the Masjidul Haraam and then accepted Islaam, which strengthened the Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) narrates that he was once in the Masjidul Haraam when Abu Jahal arrived and said, "I have vowed for Allaah that if I see Muhammad in Sajdah, I will…
narrations.summary: Abbaas relates that Abu Jahal vowed to trample the Prophet ﷺ's neck if he saw him in sajdah. The Prophet ﷺ went to the Masjid in anger, recited Surah Alaq and prostrated, and Abu Jahal said the horizons had closed in on him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Barra bint Abi Tajra (RA) narrates that Abu Jahal and few others once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and cause him much harm. Tulayb bin Umayr went to Abu Jahal and…
narrations.summary: Barra bint Abi Tajra relates that Tulayb bin Umayr struck Abu Jahal's head when Abu Jahal harmed the Prophet ﷺ, and Abu Lahab stood up to defend Tulayb. Arwa, Tulayb's mother, called it his best day. Later Arwa accepted Islaam, and when Abu Lahab reproached her she told him to defend his nephew, the Prophet ﷺ.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qataada narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ's daughter Ummu Kulthoom was married to Utayba the son of Abu Lahab. At the same time, (Rasulullaah ﷺ's other daughter)…
narrations.summary: Qataada relates that Abu Lahab's sons Utayba and Utba divorced the Prophet ﷺ's daughters after Surah Lahab was revealed. Utayba rejected the Prophet ﷺ's religion, assaulted him, and was killed by a lion on a trade journey, as the Prophet ﷺ had said. Uthmaan later married Ummu Kulthoom.

narrations.excerpt: Rabee'ah bin Ubayd Deeli once said to the people around him, "I hear you people talking a lot about the difficulties that the Quraysh gave Rasulullaah ﷺ. I have seen much…
narrations.summary: Rabee'ah bin Ubayd Deeli says the Prophet ﷺ's house lay between those of Abu Lahab and Uqba bin Abi Mu'eet, and filth and entrails were hung on his door. The Prophet ﷺ cleared them away with his bow and said the two were terrible neighbours.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates from Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) the wife of Rasulullaah ﷺ that she once asked Rasulullaah ﷺ, "Have you experienced a day more difficult than the day…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha asks whether the Prophet ever had a harder day than Uhud, and he recounts the rejection at Taa'if, after which Addaas, a Christian slave of Utba and Shayba, recognised his words and honoured him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat urwa bin Zubayr (RA) narrates that after Abu Taalib passed away, the harassment that Rasulullaah ﷺ experienced increased tremendously. He then went to the Thaqeef…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr relates the Prophet's journey to Taa'if after Abu Taalib's death, where three Thaqeef chiefs reject him, the crowd pelts him with stones, and Addaas, a Christian slave of Utba and Shayba, shows reverence after the Prophet speaks to him about Yunus.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that the people of Taa'if sat in two rows along the road of Rasulullaah ﷺ and when he passed, he could not even lift a foot or put it down…
narrations.summary: The people of Taa'if lined the road and stoned the Prophet until he bled, and he sheltered in the orchard of Utba and Shayba before returning to Makkah.

narrations.excerpt: Once Rasulullaah ﷺ felt that he was safe from the Taa'if mob, he made the following du'aa: TRANSLATION "O Allaah! Only to you do I communicate my weakness, my lack of…
narrations.summary: Once safe from the Taa'if mob, the Prophet made a du'aa confessing his weakness and asking Allaah for protection from His anger.

narrations.excerpt: When utba and Shayba, the two sons of Rabee'ah saw what had happened to Rasulullaah ﷺ, their kinship with Rasulullaah ﷺ moved them and they said to their Christian slave…
narrations.summary: Utba and Shayba send grapes by their Christian slave Addaas, who recognises the Prophet's words, learns of Yunus from him, and kisses his head, hands and feet, and his masters rebuke him.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Addaas said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, "I testify that you are the servant and messenger of Allaah." Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that (her father)…
narrations.summary: Addaas says he testifies that the Prophet is Allaah's servant and messenger, and Aa'isha relays her father Abu Bakr's account of the climb to the cave of Thowr, when the Prophet's feet were bleeding.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that the canine teeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ were broken during the Battle of Uhud and he was severely injured on the head. Wiping the blood from his…
narrations.summary: At Uhud the Prophet's canine tooth was broken and his head injured, and he asked how a nation could prosper after this; Maalik bin Sinaan then wiped and swallowed his blood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that whenever Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) spoke about the Battle of Uhud, he would say, "Every credit for that day goes to Talha." He then…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha relays Abu Bakr's account of Uhud: Talha defended the Prophet, Abu Ubaydah pulled the helmet links from his face at the cost of two front teeth, and they then nursed Talha's many wounds.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) insists on Preaching Islaam Openly and is Grievously Hurt after Delivering a Sermon Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that on one occasion when the…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr openly preached at the Ka'bah and was beaten almost to death, his tribe carried him home, Ummul Khayr and Ummu Jameel tended him, and after the Prophet prayed for her, his mother accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa for (Allaah to guide) Hadhrat Umar (RA) or Abu jahal bin Hishaam. The du'aa was made on a Wednesday and Hadhrat Umar accepted Islaam on Thursday.…
narrations.summary: Umar accepts Islaam after the Prophet's du'aa, openly declares it at the Ka'bah, and drives off anyone who tries to attack him, while Abu Jahal and the Quraysh look on.

narrations.excerpt: Meets Ibnud Daghina Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "I never knew my parents to be adherents of any religion besides the Deen of Islaam. Not a day passed when Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says her parents followed only Islaam, and Abu Bakr planned to emigrate to Abyssinia until Ibnud Daghina took him under protection on condition he worship at home; when he built a courtyard prayer place, the Quraysh asked Ibnud Daghina to withdraw the protection.

narrations.excerpt: A similar narration of ibn is'haaq states that after leaving Makkah with the intention of migrating, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was one or two days journey away when Ibnud…
narrations.summary: In Ibn Is'haaq's version, Ibnud Daghina brings Abu Bakr back to Makkah under his protection, then withdraws it when Abu Bakr's public worship annoys the Quraysh, and Abu Bakr releases him from it.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration of Ibn Is'haaq states that after Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) gave up the protection that Ibnud Daghina had given him, one of the foolish people from the…
narrations.summary: After Abu Bakr gave up Ibnud Daghina's protection, a Quraysh man threw dust on his head and he was beaten; Asmaa recalls her father's words as the mob turned on him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates, "When (my father) Hadhrat Umar accepted Islaam, he asked, "Which person of the Quraysh is the best informant?' When he was told…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar describes his father Umar accepting Islaam and going to Jameel bin Ma'mar to announce it, after which the Quraysh mobbed Umar until an old man of Banu Adi sent them away; a second report gives Aas bin Waa'il's protection of Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ibraheem Taymi narrates that when Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan accepted islaam, his uncle Hakam bin Abil Aas bin Umayyah securely bound him in ropes.…
narrations.summary: Hakam bin Abil Aas bound his nephew Uthmaan in ropes after he accepted Islaam, and released him when he saw Uthmaan would not give up his new faith.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mas'ood bin Khiraash (RA) narrates, "While we were walking between Safa and Marwa, we saw a large group of people following a young man whose arm was in a sling…
narrations.summary: Mas'ood bin Khiraash saw Talha bin Ubaydillaah, who had accepted Islaam, walking between Safa and Marwa with his arm in a sling while his mother Sa'ba cursed him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat ibraheem bin Muhammad bin Talha narrates that Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydillaah once told him, "I once visited the fair in Busra (in Shaam) when I heard a monk…
narrations.summary: Talha recounts a monk at the Busra fair asking whether the Prophet Ahmad had appeared yet, which drove him back to Makkah, where he learned that Muhammad had appeared; the text breaks off there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Aswad narrates that Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awwaam (RA) accepted islaam when he was only eight years of age and migrated (to Madinah) when he was eighteen years…
narrations.summary: Zubayr bin Awwaam accepted Islaam at eight years old, and his uncle hung him over smoke and urged him to return to kufr, which he refused.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hafs bin Khaalid narrates that an old man from Mosul came to them and said that he had accompanied Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awwaam (RA) on a journey. He said, "We were…
narrations.summary: Hafs bin Khaalid reports an old man from Mosul who saw Zubayr's body covered in sword scars, each received alongside the Prophet in the path of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali bin Zaid narrates (RA) Zubayr informed him that there were scars resembling eyes on his chest which were made by arrows and spears.
narrations.summary: Zubayr told Ali bin Zaid that his chest bore scars shaped like eyes, made by arrows and spears.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that seven persons were the first to make their conversion to Islaam public. These were Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA),…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood names the first seven to make their Islaam public, and says that those without tribal protection were tortured, with Bilaal dragged through Makkah repeating 'Ahad! Ahad!'.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Mujaahid states that the other Muslims were made to wear coats of steel armour and then left to swelter in the sun. They therefore suffered terribly from…
narrations.summary: Mujaahid reports that the other Muslims were left in steel armour under the sun, and Abu Jahal came at night with his spear to taunt and threaten them.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration of Hadhrat Mujaahid states that the Mushrikeen used to lead Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) through the two mountains of Makkah with a rope around his neck.
narrations.summary: Mujaahid reports that the Mushrikeen led Bilaal through the two mountains of Makkah with a rope around his neck.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) was a slave of a lady from the Banu Jumh tribe. The Mushrikeen used to torture him on the burning sands of…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports that Umayyah tortured Bilaal on the sand until Abu Bakr bought and freed him, after Waraqa bin Naufal had promised to make the grave of Bilaal a place of blessing if he were killed.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Ibn Is'haaq states that when the afternoon heat grew intense, Umayyah would take Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) outside and throw him down on the burning sands of…
narrations.summary: Umayyah threw Bilaal onto the burning sand with a heavy rock on his chest, demanding he reject Muhammad and worship Laat and Uzza, and Bilaal kept saying 'Ahad! Ahad!'; the item then introduces Ammaar reciting couplets about Abu Bakr's freeing of the slaves.

narrations.excerpt: Ateeq and humiliate Faakih and Abujahal I shall never forget the night when the two of them resolved to hurt Bilaal Without having a concern for doing the evil that…
narrations.summary: Ammaar's verses praise Abu Bakr for freeing Bilaal, condemn Abu Jahal and Faakih for torturing him, and affirm Bilaal's stand on the Oneness of Allaah, citing the prophets Ibraheem, Yunus, Moosa and Isa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by Hadhrat Ammar (RA) and his family (his parents) as they were being tortured by the Mushrikeen, he…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports the Prophet telling the family of Yaasir to be patient, as Jannah is their promised home, and Uthmaan reports the same scene while Ammaar and his parents were tortured in the sun, with the Prophet praying for their forgiveness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) narrates that he was once walking with Rasulullaah in Bat'haa (a rocky area of Makkah) when they saw Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) and his parents being…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan relates that while walking with the Prophet in Bat'haa they saw Ammaar and his parents tortured in the sun, Yaasir cried out, and the Prophet told the family to be patient and prayed for their forgiveness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by Hadhrat Ammar (RA) and his family (his parents) as they were being tortured by the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ja'far reports the Prophet's words to the family of Yaasir, and Kalbi adds that Sumayya was killed when Abu Jahal thrust a spear into her, Yaasir died under torture, and Abdullaah bin Yaasir was shot dead by an arrow.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaahid stated, "The first martyr was Hadhrat Sumayya (RA) the mother of Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) who was martyred tluring the early days of Islaam when Abu jahal…
narrations.summary: Mujaahid states that Sumayya, the mother of Ammaar, was the first martyr in Islaam, killed when Abu Jahal thrust a spear into her.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Muhammad bin Ammaar narrates that the Mushrikeen captured Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) and tortured him so brutally that (to save his life) he was…
narrations.summary: Ammaar, tortured until he spoke against the Prophet and praised the Mushrikeen's gods, tells the Prophet his heart still held Imaan, and the Prophet allows him to say it again if the torture recurs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ammaar narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ met Hadhrat Ammaar as he was weeping. Wiping the tears from his face, Rasulullaah said, "The Kuffaar captured you…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Ammaar reports the Prophet wiping Ammaar's tears and saying he may repeat the forced words, and Ameerul Mu'mineen bin Maymoon reports the Prophet's prayer over Ammaar while he was being burned, and the Prophet's word that rebels would kill him.

narrations.excerpt: imaam Sha'bi narrates that when Hadhrat Khabbaab bin Arat (RA) once came to the gathering of Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA), Hadhrat Umar (RA) made him sit on his own…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that when Khabbaab came to Umar's gathering, Umar gave him the cushion of honour, saying only Bilaal deserved it more, and Khabbaab showed the back that had been burned.

narrations.excerpt: Imaam Sha'bi narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked Hadhrat Khabbaab about the tortures he suffered at the hands of the Mushrikeen, he said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports Umar asking Khabbaab about his torture, and Khabbaab shows his back and says only the fat on it put out the fire the Mushrikeen had lit under him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Layla Kindi narrates that when Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) came to Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Umar (RA) told the people to allow him to -come to the front and said,…
narrations.summary: Abu Layla Kindi reports that Umar had Khabbaab brought to the front, calling Ammaar bin Yaasir the only man more deserving of that place, and Khabbaab showed him the scars left by the Mushrikeen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) says, "1 was a blacksmith and Aas bin Waa'il owed me some money. When I approached him to settle the debt, he said, 'By Allaah! I shall never pay…
narrations.summary: Khabbaab, a blacksmith, says Aas bin Waa'il refused to repay his debt unless he rejected Muhammad, and Khabbaab refused; the Qur'aan verses on Aas's claim to wealth and children in the Aakhirah are then quoted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) narrates that he once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ as he lay in the shade of the Kabah using a shawl as a pillow. It was a time when the Muslims were…
narrations.summary: Khabbaab asks the Prophet to pray for relief from the persecution, and the Prophet replies that earlier believers endured worse, and that Allaah will complete this Deen until a lone rider travels safely from Sa'aa to Hadramaut.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Dharr heard that Rasulullaah ﷺ was sent as a Rasul, he said to his brother, "Ride to that valley (of…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Abu Dharr sent his brother to Makkah to find the man claiming to be a Rasul, and the brother returned describing good character and words that were not poetry, which did not satisfy Abu Dharr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) took some provisions and a filled waterbag along with him and rode off to Makkah. When he entered the Masjidul Haraam, he searched for Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Ali takes Abu Dharr home for three nights until he leads him to the Prophet, who tells him to return to his people; Abu Dharr then proclaims the testimony at the Masjidul Haraam, is beaten, and is shielded by Abbaas.

narrations.excerpt: imaam Muslim describes Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA)'s entry into Islaam quite differently. He reports from Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) that after his brother returned from Makkah,…
narrations.summary: In Muslim's account, Abu Dharr is stoned in Makkah after his brother's visit, hides near the Ka'bah for fifteen days, then meets the Prophet and Abu Bakr, and is the first to greet him with the greeting of Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) stated that he stayed a while in Makkah with sacrifices, making them red. Here Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) refers to his appearance as a person covered…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr declared his Islaam openly in the Masjidul Haraam, was beaten until he looked like a red idol, and was told by the Prophet to return to his people until he heard of victory.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) Hits Hadhrat Sa'eed (RA) and his Wife Faatima and then Accepts Islaam by Virtue of the Du'aa of Rasulullaah igi? Hadhrat Qais narrates that in the…
narrations.summary: Qais reports that Sa'eed bin Zaid, speaking in the mosque of Kufa, recalled being tied with ropes by Umar after he accepted Islaam, and began the complete account.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that he said, "If only you had seen me bound in ropes by Hadhrat Umar (RA) when he was not yet a Muslim because I had accepted Islaam."
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Zaid says that Umar bound him in ropes before Umar became a Muslim, because he had accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once left home with his sword hanging from his neck when a person from the Banu Zuhra tribe asked him where he was…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Umar set out to kill the Prophet, was turned back by the recitation of Surah Taa-Haa in his sister's and brother-in-law's house, and after reading it himself went to the Prophet, who prayed for him, and Umar accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thowbaan (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed, "O Allaah! Strengthen the Deen with Ulnar bin Khattaab." Early one night, Hadhrat Umar had heard his sister…
narrations.summary: Thowbaan reports the Prophet's du'aa for Umar; Umar beat his sister after hearing her recite Surah Alaq, then went to the Prophet's door, where Bilaal let him in, and he accepted Islaam when asked to testify.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s slave Aslam narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked him, "Do you wish to know about the days when I first accepted islaam?" When Hadhrat Aslam…
narrations.summary: Umar recounts how, angered to hear that his sister had accepted Islaam, he struck her and then took the manuscript she was reading.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) noticed that while he could walk about in safety under the protection of Waleed bin Mughiera, the other…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan bin Madh'oon gives up Waleed bin Mughiera's protection, then is slapped in the eye for disputing a poet's couplets with the Quraysh.

narrations.excerpt: Have you become grieved and weep like a distraught person? Or do you weep in thinking of foolish people Who harshly oppress those who invite towards the Deen These people…
narrations.summary: A poem lamenting those who struck Uthmaan bin Madh'oon and warning that Allaah will punish them.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Ibn Is'haaq states that Waleed invited Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon to return to his protection, but Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon refused.
narrations.summary: Waleed asks Uthmaan bin Madh'oon to return under his protection, and Uthmaan refuses.

narrations.summary: Mus'ab bin Umayr, once Makkah's most pampered youth, accepts Islaam in secret, is jailed by his family, and endures hardship after returning from Abyssinia.

narrations.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet never filled himself for three days in a row, though they could have, because he preferred to give to others.

narrations.summary: Anas narrates that Faatima gave the Prophet a piece of barley bread, which he said was the first food he had eaten in three days.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Qataadah (RA) who participated in the Battle of Uhud says that Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh (RA) who was crippled once approached Rasulullaah and said, "O…
narrations.summary: Abu Qataadah reports that Amr bin Jamooh asked the Prophet whether he would walk in Jannah with a healthy leg if martyred, and the Prophet said he could see him doing so after his death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Abdul Hameed' narrates from his grandfather that an arrow struck Hadhrat Raafi bin Khadeej (RA) during either the Battle of Uhud or the Battle of. He…
narrations.summary: Yahya bin Abdul Hameed reports that Raafi bin Khadeej, struck by an arrow, chose to have only the shaft removed so the Prophet could bear witness to his martyrdom, and that he died later under Mu'aawiya.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that after the Hajj season, Rasulullaah ﷺ was in Makkah during the remaining days of Dhul Hijjah, Muharram and Safar. The Mushrikeen then…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that the Quraysh plotted to seize, kill or exile the Prophet, that Allaah revealed the plan to him, and that he was warned of a plot to kill him in his sleep on the day he went to Abu Bakr's house.

narrations.excerpt: Under the veil of the night, Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) left for the cave in the Thowr mountain, which is mentioned in the Qur'aan(1). Hadhrat Ali bin Abi…
narrations.summary: Ali sleeps in the Prophet's bed while the Prophet and Abu Bakr hide in the cave of Thowr, where Allaah sends tranquillity when the Mushrikeen reach it; Aamir bin Fuhayra and Abdullaah bin Abi Bakr look after them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ never failed to visit Hadhrat Abu Bakr during one of the ends of the day. He either visited during the mornings or during…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha recounts how the Prophet told Abu Bakr at midday that he was permitted to migrate, Abu Bakr asked to accompany him, and Abu Bakr had camels ready; a second report says the Prophet insisted on buying one.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) whowas the daughter of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) narrates that that when they were staying in Makkah Rasulullaah ﷺ usually visited them twice each day.…
narrations.summary: Asmaa bint Abi Bakr recounts preparing provisions for the Hijrah and tying them with her belt, and how the Prophet and Abu Bakr hid in the cave while the Quraysh searched for them.

narrations.excerpt: (After three nights) Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) left the cave and took a route along the coast. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) travelled in front of Rasulullaah ﷺ but…
narrations.summary: Rasulullaah and Abu Bakr travel along the coast toward Madinah, and Suraaqa bin Maalik sets out after them when told of two riders.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Seereen narrates that during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Umar (RA), mention was made of some Sahabah (RA) and it appeared as if the people regarded Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Umar praises Abu Bakr's devotion, recalling how Abu Bakr walked ahead and behind the Prophet and cleaned the cave before him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan Basri narrates that that when Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr went to the cave, the Quraysh came to search for Rasulullaah ﷺ. However, when they saw that…
narrations.summary: In the cave, Abu Bakr fears for the Prophet when the Quraysh come searching, and the Prophet tells him that Allaah is with them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) told him, "(When we were in the cave) I said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, 'if any of them has to look to his feet, he would…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr tells Anas that in the cave he warned the Prophet that a pursuer looking down would see them, and the Prophet asked what he thought of two whose third is Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once bought a saddle from (his father) Hadhrat Aazib (RA) for thirteen Dirhams. Hadhrat Abu Bakr then asked…
narrations.summary: Baraa bin Aazib reports that Abu Bakr bought a saddle from his father and asked that the Banu Najjaar be honoured, and that the Prophet stayed where he was commanded the next morning.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr SSI narrates that Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) who was with a caravan of Muslim traders met Rasulullaah ﷺ as they were returning from Shaam. He gave both…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr relates the Prophet's arrival at Madinah: Zubayr met him with white clothing, the people welcomed him at Harra, he stayed with Banu Amr bin Awf, and he founded the Masjid on land bought from two orphans, carrying bricks himself.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) says, "I was one of the children running as the people said, 'Muhammad ﷺ has arrived!' I ran on but could not see anything. When the people…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik, as a child, describes the crowds in Madinah who came out to welcome the Prophet and Abu Bakr on their arrival.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, the women and children sang: "The full moon has risen above us from the Valley of Wadaa Gratitude is…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that the women and children sang a welcoming verse when the Prophet arrived in Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib (RA) says, "The first Muslims (from Makkah) to migrate to us (in Madinah) were Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Umayr (RA) and Hadhrat Ibn Ummu Maktoom (RA).…
narrations.summary: Baraa bin Aazib says the first emigrants to reach Madinah were Mus'ab bin Umayr and Ibn Ummu Maktoom, followed by Ammaar, Bilaal, Sa'd and Umar, and that the people of Madinah were overjoyed.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib (RA) said, "The first from amongst the Muhaajireen to come to us was Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Umayr who belonged to the…
narrations.summary: A variant report by Baraa names Mus'ab bin Umayr, Ibn Ummu Maktoom and Umar as the first emigrants to reach Madinah, and says the Prophet and Abu Bakr arrived after them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) says, "When I decided to migrate to Madinah, Ayaash bin Abi Rabee'ah, Hishaam bin Aas and I arranged to meet at the valley of Tanaadhib which was a…
narrations.summary: Umar recounts how Abu Jahal and Haarith bin Hishaam tricked their cousin Ayaash bin Abi Rabee'ah back to Makkah and made him forsake Islaam, and how Hishaam bin Aas, also held back, later received the verses of Surah Zumar that gave him hope.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) Migrates to Abyssinia and Becomes the First Person After Hadhrat Loot (RA) to migrate with his Family for the Pleasure of Allaah Hadhrat Qataadah…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan bin Affaan becomes the first to emigrate with his family for Allaah's pleasure, travelling to Abyssinia with his wife Ruqayya, and the Prophet prays for them.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that when Rasulullaah ﷺ received no news of them, he went out of his house to wait for some news. Eventually a woman came to him and gave him news…
narrations.summary: A variant adds that the Prophet went out to wait for news of the emigrants until a woman brought him word about them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ left for the Hijrah to Madinah, he told me to stay behind to return the trusts that people had left with him. It was because of…
narrations.summary: Ali recounts that the Prophet left him in Makkah to return the trusts people had deposited with him, and that Ali followed three days later and stayed at Kulthoom bin Hidm's house in Quba.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Haatib (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "I have seen (in a dream) a land of dates. You people should go there." Consequently, (my father)…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Haatib reports the Prophet's dream of a land of dates, after which Haatib and Ja'far sailed to Abyssinia, and Ja'far asked leave to worship Allaah without fear.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Salama (RA) narrates that a time came when it became too difficult for the Sahabah (RA) to live in Makkah. They were being tortured and put through many…
narrations.summary: Ummu Salama recounts that the Prophet sent the Muslims to Abyssinia to escape persecution, and that the Quraysh sent Amr bin Al Aas and Abdullaah bin Abi Rabee'ah with gifts to have them returned.

narrations.excerpt: When the Muslims came to Najaashi, they greeted him with Salaam without prostrating before him. Najaashi said, "O people! Tell me why you have not greeted me (by…
narrations.summary: At Najaashi's court, Ja'far explains the Muslims' faith and recites about Isa and Maryam, Najaashi refuses the Quraysh's demand, and the report also tells of Zubayr's news of Najaashi's victory and the Muslims who returned to the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed them to leave for Abyssinia with Hadhrat Ja'far bin Abi Taalib (RA). when the news reached the…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports the same account, adding that Najaashi said he would have gone to the Prophet and kissed his feet, and then let the Muslims stay wherever they liked.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ja'far bin Abi Taalib (RA) says that the Quraysh sent Amr bin Al Aas and Umaarah bin Waleed to ,Najaashi with gifts from Abu Sufyaan. When the Muslims were…
narrations.summary: Ja'far reports that Amr bin Al Aas and Umaarah bin Waleed, sent with gifts from Abu Sufyaan, demanded the Muslims be handed over; Najaashi heard them out, questioned the Muslims about Isa, and set a penalty for harming them that he doubled.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ja'far (RA) narrates further that when Rasulullaah ﷺ migrated to Madinah and was dominant, the Muslims approached Najaashi and said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ has become…
narrations.summary: Ja'far reports that Najaashi, having testified to the Prophet's Risaalat and asked for his forgiveness, sent the Muslims back to Madinah with provisions, and the Prophet prayed for Najaashi's forgiveness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Abdillaah bint Abi Hathma (RA) says, "By Allaah! We were preparing to leave for Abyssinia when (my husband) Aamir had to leave for something we needed. In…
narrations.summary: Ummu Abdillaah bint Abi Hathma recounts that Umar, still a Mushrik, showed unusual gentleness when they left for Abyssinia, and her husband Aamir doubted he would ever accept Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sa'eed bin Al Aas and his brother Amr were amongst those wfio migrated to Abyssinia. He narrates that it was a year after the Battle of Badr that they…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Sa'eed and his brother Amr return from Abyssinia after Badr, and the Prophet tells them they made two Hijrahs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) narrates that they lived in Yemen and when they heard that Rasulullaah ﷺ had migrated to Madinah, his brothers and he migrated to…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari recounts his migration from Yemen with his brothers and about fifty others by ship to Abyssinia and then to Madinah, Umar's remark to Asmaa bint Umays, and the Prophet's praise of the Ash'ariyyeen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asmaa bint Umays (RA) narrates that she once asked, "O Rasulullaah Some people are boasting to us and saying that we are not amongst the first Muhaajireen."…
narrations.summary: Asmaa bint Umays asks the Prophet about people who boast that they came first, and he tells her that she and those with her made two Hijrahs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Salama (RA) says, "When (my husband) Hadhrat Abu Salama decided to migrate to Madinah, he tied a carriage for me on his camel and put me on it. He then put…
narrations.summary: Ummu Salama recounts how the Banu Mughiera kept her from her husband Abu Salma and son, how they were reunited after a year, and how Uthmaan bin Talha escorted her alone to Quba.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I have been shown the place to which you people will migrate. It is a salty land that lies between two rocky…
narrations.summary: Suhayb reports that the Prophet told him of the land of migration, that youngsters of Quraysh held him back until he paid them gold, and that on reaching Quba the Prophet said his transaction had been profitable.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) left to migrate to Rasulullaah ﷺ, a group of Mushrikeen from the Quraysh pursued him. Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Suhayb, pursued while migrating, emptied his quiver and offered to show the pursuers his wealth in Makkah if they left him alone, and that Surah Baqarah 207 was revealed about him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ikrama narrates that when Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) left to migrate to Madinah, some people of Makkah pursued him. Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) emptied his quiver and found…
narrations.summary: Ikrama reports that the pursued Suhayb emptied a quiver of forty arrows and offered the pursuers Abdullaah bin Umar's two slave women in Makkah if they let him go.
