narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas has narrated similar report with the addition that it was on that occasion that Allaah revealed the following verse of the Qur'aan: From mankind is he who…
narrations.summary: Anas gives a similar account of Suhayb's encounter with the Quraysh and adds that Surah Baqarah 207 was revealed on that occasion.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) narrates that when he decided to migrate from Makkah to Rasulullaah ﷺ, the Quraysh said to him, "O Suhayb! When you came to us, you had no wealth. You…
narrations.summary: Suhayb reports that the Quraysh let him leave Makkah only after he gave them all his wealth, and the Prophet told him he had earned a grand profit.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Zaid narrates that whenever Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar passed by his house (in Makkah) from which he migrated, he would close his eyes and would not…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Zaid reports that Abdullaah bin Umar would close his eyes and not look at or stop at the house in Makkah he had left when he migrated.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that whenever Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) spoke about Rasulullaah ﷺ, he would cry and whenever he passed his house (in Makkah), he would…
narrations.summary: Another report says Abdullaah bin Umar wept whenever he spoke of the Prophet and closed his eyes when passing his former house in Makkah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Jahash (actually his brother Abd bin Jahash, as it will become clear from the next Hadith) was the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Abd bin Jahash left Makkah secretly for the Prophet in Madinah against his wife's wishes, Abu Sufyaan became angry, and a poem about the migration follows.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Jubayr (RA) narrates that many poor Muslims in Makkah thought that they were exempted from making Hijrah when the following verses of the Qur'aan were…
narrations.summary: Verses of Surah Nisaa on Hijrah are revealed, and Dhamra bin Abil Ees, a blind and wealthy man, sets out to migrate despite illness and dies at Tan'eem, which prompts a further verse.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Dhamra bin Jundub left his house to make Hijrah, he told his family members, "Put me on my mount. Remove me…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Dhamra bin Jundub died on the way to the Prophet, and that Surah Nisaa 100 was then revealed about one who dies while making Hijrah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa (RA) narrates that he left home with the intention of accepting Islaam and came to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Since Rasulullaah ﷺ was leading the salaah at…
narrations.summary: Waathila bin Asqa reports that he joined the Prophet's prayer at the back, was asked whether his Hijrah would be Baadi or Baati, and pledged obedience as far as he is able.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salama bin Akwa (RA) narrates that when the Banu Sulaym tribe were affected by an epidemic, Rasulullaah ﷺ advised them to live outside the town. They said, "We…
narrations.summary: Salama bin Akwa reports that the Prophet advised the epidemic-stricken Banu Sulaym to live outside the town, and told them they would be counted as Muhaajireen wherever they were.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Junaadah bin Abi Umayyaah Azdi (RA) narrates that there was a difference of opinion amongst them when they made Hijrah during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ While some…
narrations.summary: Junaadah bin Abi Umayyah asks the Prophet whether Hijrah has ended, and the Prophet says it continues as long as Jihaad is waged against the disbelievers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Sa'di (RA) narrates, "I was the youngest amongst a delegation of seven or eight people from the Banu Sa'd bin Bakr tribe. When the delegation met…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Sa'di reports that he asked the Prophet about the claim that Hijrah had ended, and was told that his need was better than theirs because Hijrah continues while Jihaad is waged.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that while Hadhrat Safwaan bin Umayyah was in the upper part of Makkah, he was told that the person who did not undertake…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Safwaan bin Umayyah came to Madinah because he had heard that the one who makes no Hijrah has no Deen, and the Prophet told him Hijrah had ended with the conquest of Makkah, so he should return home and answer calls to Jihaad.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that someone said to Hadhrat Safwaan bin Umayyah that the person who did not perform the Hijrah is destroyed. Hadhrat Safwaan swore an oath that…
narrations.summary: Safwaan bin Umayyah asks whether the one who does not make Hijrah is destroyed, and the Prophet replies that Hijrah ended after the conquest of Makkah but Jihaad and its intention remain.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalih bin Basheer bin Fudayk narrates that his grandfather Hadhrat Fudayk once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and asked, "O Rasulullaah Some people say that the person…
narrations.summary: Saalih bin Basheer relates that his grandfather Fudayk asked whether a man who does not migrate is lost, and the Prophet told him that establishing salaah and paying zakaah while avoiding evil makes him a migrant; Ataa relates Aa'isha's view that compulsory hijrah had ended, though jihaad and intention remain.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ made Hijrah, he left us and his daughters behind (in Makkah). When he had settled, he sent Hadhrat Zaid bin Haaritha…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha recounts how the Prophet sent Zaid bin Haaritha and Abu Raafi to bring his family from Makkah, and how her own family travelled to Madinah with Abu Bakr's arrangements.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) quotes that she said, "As we were making Hijrah, we were passing by a difficult (dangerous) valley when the camel I was on…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha recounts her camel bolting on the journey of Hijrah and how it stopped when someone told her to throw down its reins.

narrations.excerpt: Rasulullaah ﷺ's daughter Hadhrat Zaynab (RA) says, "As I was preparing the provisions for my journey (Hijrah), Hind bint Utba met me. She said, 'O daughter of Muhammad!…
narrations.summary: Zaynab, daughter of the Prophet, recounts how Hind bint Utba tried to dissuade her from Hijrah, and how Kinaana then escorted her out of Makkah and was confronted by Abu Sufyaan at Dhu Tuwa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) narrates that as someone was leaving (Makkah) with Hadhrat Zaynab Sitings the daughter of Risulullaah, they were intercepted by two men from…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports that Zaynab was attacked by Quraysh men on her Hijrah, miscarried, and died later from the injury, and so was regarded as a martyr.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) states that after Rasulullaah ﷺ had left Makkah, his daughter Hadhrat Zaynab (RA) also left with Kinaana or his brother. The…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha describes how Habbaar bin Aswad injured Zaynab on her Hijrah and how she was cared for in Makkah, and the Prophet then sent Zaid bin Haaritha to bring her to Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) and Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir all report that when Hadhrat Durra (RA) the daughter of Abu Lahab made Hijrah, she…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar, Abu Hurayrah and Ammaar bin Yaasir report that Durra bint Abu Lahab was insulted by Banu Zurayq women after her Hijrah, and that the Prophet consoled her and spoke of interceding for his family.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "We reached Rasulullaah ﷺ five years after he had made Hijrah and were with the Quraysh when they marched during the year in which…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas recounts how, as a child of eight, he and his brother Fadl lost their way on the road from Makkah and reached the Prophet at the trench during the Battle of Ahzaab.

narrations.excerpt: This chapter highlights how rendering assistance to the upright Deen and the Straight Path was more beloved to the Sahabah (RA) than everything else and how they prided…
narrations.summary: The author introduces the chapter on how the Sahabah valued assisting the Deen above worldly honour and sacrificed for it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Every year Rasulullaah ﷺ used to present his case to the various Arab tribes, asking them to grant him asylum with their people so that he…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet presented his message to the Arab tribes each year, offering Jannah, until Allaah brought the Ansaar to grant him a place to migrate to.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ stayed in Makkah, he went to every Arab tribe and presented his case to them during the Hajj season. However, he could find…
narrations.summary: Umar recounts that the Prophet presented himself to every Arab tribe during the Hajj season until Allaah brought the Ansaar, who gave him sanctuary and help.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "By Allaah! We failed to fulfil the pledge we made with the Ansaar when we said to them that while we remain the…
narrations.summary: Umar says that the Muhaajireen failed to keep their pledge to the Ansaar, and that if he lived a year every governor would be from the Ansaar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdillaah (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ presented his case to the people as they stayed at their camps (during the Hajj season). He would say, "Who will…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Abdillaah relates that the Prophet sought support from people during the Hajj season, and that a man from Hamdaan and then a delegation of the Ansaar came to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that when one of the Hajj seasons arrived, a group of individuals from the Ansaar left for Hajj. Amongst them from the Banu Maazin bin Najjaar…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that a group of Ansaar on Hajj, including Mu'aadh bin Afraa and As'ad bin Zuraarah, accepted the Prophet's message and promised to return and invite their people, after which many Ansaar homes had Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed narrates from an old lady from the Ansaar that she used to see Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) frequently visit Hadhrat Sirma bin Qais to learn…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas learns couplets from Sirmah bin Qais that praise how the Ansaar welcomed the Prophet and supported the Muhaajireen with their wealth and lives.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) arrived in Madinah, Rasulullaah ﷺ established a bond of brotherhood between him and Hadhrat Sa'd…
narrations.summary: Anas recounts that the Prophet made Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf a brother to Sa'd bin Rabee, that Abdur Rahmaan then traded and married, and that the Prophet advised him to host a waleema.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when the Muhaajireen first arrived in Madinah, a Muhaajir would inherit from his Ansaar brother because of the bonds of…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas explains that the early practice of inheritance between Muhaajireen and Ansaar brothers, made by the Prophet, was abrogated first by the verse on relatives in Surah Anfaal and then fully by Surah Ahzaab.

narrations.excerpt: Sharing Dates and an Ansaari Refuses to be Paid Back Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) narrates that the Ansaar once said to Rasulullaah "Share out our date plantations between us…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah and Abdur Rahmaan bin Zaid bin Aslam report that the Ansaar offered to share their date plantations with the Muhaajireen, and the Prophet suggested they let the Muhaajireen work them and share the dates.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that the Muhaajireen said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ We have never seen people better than those to whom we have come (the Ansaar). They are prepared to…
narrations.summary: Anas and Jaabir report the generosity of the Ansaar toward the Muhaajireen, including the harvest-sharing trick and the offer to hand over their Khaybar shares, which the Prophet accepted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that whenever the Ansaar harvested their crops, they would divide the crop into two parts, the one part being smaller than the other. They…
narrations.summary: Jaabir relates that the Ansaar gave the Muhaajireen the larger share of their harvests, and after Khaybar the Ansaar, having fulfilled their duty, asked the Prophet for Jannah in return, which he granted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once called for the Ansaar to distribute the land of Bahrain amongst them. However, they refused to have any of it unless…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that when the Prophet asked the Ansaar to share the land of Bahrain, they refused unless the Muhaajireen received an equal share, and the Prophet told them to be patient.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdillaah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah (jfgi once said, "Who is there to see Ka'b bin Ashraf because he has caused great harm to (the Deen of) Allaah…
narrations.summary: On the Prophet's request, Muhammad bin Maslama and companions deceive and kill Ka'b bin Ashraf, who had harmed Islaam, and report back to the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ka'b bin Maalik (RA) says that amongst the many advantages that Allaah had granted Rasulullaah ﷺ (to facilitate the effective propagation of Deen)…
narrations.summary: Five men from the Khazraj kill Abu Raafi Sallaam bin Abul Huqayq at Khaybar at night, and when they report back the Prophet inspects their swords.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent some men from the Ansaar to kill the Jew Abu Raafi. Rasulullaah (ill appointed Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ateek as their…
narrations.summary: Baraa and Abdullaah bin Ateek describe how the Ansaar, sent by the Prophet, entered a fortress at Khaybar and killed Abu Raafi, and the Prophet healed Abdullaah's injured leg.

narrations.excerpt: The daughter of Hadhrat Muhayyisa (RA) narrates from her father that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once permitted the Sahabah (RA) to kill any Jew they could, Hadhrat Muhayyisa (RA)…
narrations.summary: Muhayyisa kills the Jewish trader Ibn Shayba on the Prophet's permission, and his brother Huwayyisa, angered at first, accepts Islaam after hearing that Muhayyisa would have killed him if the Prophet had commanded it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that after Rasulullaah ﷺ had defeated the Quraysh in the Battle of Badr, he gathered the Jews (of Madinah) in the marketplace…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas recounts how the Prophet called the Jews of Madinah to Islaam after Badr, how they boasted of their strength, and how verses about Badr were revealed in reply.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that the Jews -said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, "O Muhammad! Do not pride yourself on the fact that you have killed some people of the Quraysh jwhe-wefe…
narrations.summary: The Jews taunt the Prophet about Badr, and Ubaadah bin Saamit renounces his Jewish friends while Abdullaah bin Ubay insists on keeping them, after which verses forbidding taking Jews and Christians as friends are revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when the Jewish Banu Qaynuqah tribe started hostilities against Rasulullaah ﷺ, Abdullaah bin Ubay bin Salool sided with them and stood in…
narrations.summary: When the Banu Qaynuqah turned hostile to the Prophet, Ubaadah bin Saamit renounced his alliance with them, while Abdullaah bin Ubay bin Salool stood by them, and verses on not taking Jews and Christians as friends were revealed.

narrations.excerpt: A Sahabi narrates that before the Battle of Badr, the Kuffaar of the Quraysh wrote to (the hypocrite) Abdullaah bin Ubay and others like him who worshipped idols. In…
narrations.summary: Before Badr the Quraysh try to turn Abdullaah bin Ubay against the Muslims, and after Badr the Banu Nadheer plot against the Prophet, are besieged, and are expelled to Shaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ maintained the siege of the Banu Nadheer until they could not hold out any longer and were forced to give in…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas describes the terms on which the Prophet besieged the Banu Nadheer and expelled them, allowing one camel and water bag per three people, with a variant that Muhammad bin Maslama gave them ten days to leave.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "I came out of the house during the Battle of Khandaq and was following the people when I heard footsteps on the ground behind me. It was Sa'd…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports the Battle of Khandaq: Sa'd bin Mu'aadh was struck by an arrow and prayed to live until the fate of Banu Qurayzah, then after their surrender chose execution of the warriors, and Sa'd died, and the Prophet and Sahabah wept for him.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Rasulullaah ﷺ returned from the burial of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA), his tears flowed on to his beard.
narrations.summary: Another narration states that the Prophet's tears flowed onto his beard as he returned from the burial of Sa'd bin Mu'aadh.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas ig says that on one occasion the Aws and Khazraj tribes boasted to each other. The Aws said, "Amongst us was the person whom the angels bathed (after his…
narrations.summary: Anas relates that the Aws and Khazraj boasted of their Companions: the Aws named Handhala, Sa'd bin Mu'aadh, Aasim and Khuzayma, and the Khazraj named the four who memorised the whole Qur'aan, Zaid bin Thaabit, Ubay bin Ka'b, Mu'aadh bin Jabal and Abu Zaid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rabaah il says, "Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) and I were part of many delegations that came to Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) during Ramadhaan. We used to…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Rabaah relates Abu Hurayrah's account of the conquest of Makkah: the Prophet had the Ansaar clear the Quraysh resisters, Abu Sufyaan asked whether the Quraysh would be wiped out, the Prophet promised safety to those who closed their doors or entered Abu Sufyaan's house, broke the idol at the Kabah, and told the Ansaar he had made hijrah towards Allaah and towards them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that when the Battle of Hunayn took place, the Hawaazin, Ghitfaan and other tribes came (to the battlefield) with their stock animals as well…
narrations.summary: At Hunayn, when the Muslim army fled and the Prophet was left alone, he called the Ansaar, who answered that they were with him, and he reassured them, and the Ansaar wept and accepted his distribution.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ received the booty from the Battle of Hunayn, he distributed it amongst the members of the Quraysh whose…
narrations.summary: After the Battle of Hunayn the Ansaar felt hurt at the distribution of booty, and the Prophet gathered them, reminded them of Allaah's favour, and told them he would return home with them rather than with the goats and camels.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saa'ib bin Yazeed (RA) narrates that as a gesture of goodwill, Rasulullaah ﷺ distributed the booty received from the Hawaazin in the Battle of Hunayn amongst the…
narrations.summary: After Hunayn the Prophet explains to the Ansaar, who were upset that he gave booty to the Quraysh and others, that he did so to win hearts, and the Ansaar weep with him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that when Allaah gave the wealth of the Hawaazin tribe as booty to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he started giving as much as a hundred camels to…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that after Hunayn the Prophet gave booty to newer Muslims, that some Ansaar complained, and that the Prophet told them to be patient and to return home with him.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Anas (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to the Ansaar, "You are like under clothing to me while others are like outer garments. Does it…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet told the Ansaar they were close to him like under-clothing while others were like outer garments, and that he would walk the valley of the Ansaar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that when some wealth came to Rasulullaah ﷺ from Bahrain whilst the Muhaajireen and Ansaar heard about it from each other, they came to…
narrations.summary: Anas reports the Prophet's words to the Muhaajireen and Ansaar after wealth came from Bahrain: the Ansaar turn out in large numbers in hazards but in small numbers when something is distributed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to Hadhrat Abu Talha, "Convey my Salaam to your people (the Ansaar) and inform them that as far as I know, they…
narrations.summary: Anas and then a second narration report that the Prophet sent greetings to the Ansaar through Abu Talha, describing them as extremely chaste and patient, including during the Prophet's final illness.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Anas (RA) states that when Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) visited Rasulullaah ﷺ during the illness in which Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Anas relates that during the Prophet's final illness Abu Talha visited him, and the Prophet sent his salaam to the Ansaar, praising them as extremely chaste and patient.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Shaddaad (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ visited Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA) as he was on his deathbed. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O chief of his…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Shaddaad reports that the Prophet visited Sa'd bin Mu'aadh on his deathbed and told him that he had fulfilled his pledge to Allaah and that Allaah would fulfil His pledge to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "No harm can come to a woman whether she stays between two homes of the Ansaar or between her own parents."
narrations.summary: Aa'isha (RA) reports the Prophet's words on the Ansaar, and his question about a set of clothing he had given to a veteran of Badr, Uhud and Aqaba, which a Quraysh youth then bought.

narrations.excerpt: The Hospitality of the Ansaar and the Story of Hadhrat Usayd bin Hudhayr (RA) Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Usayd bin Hudhayr (RA) once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Usayd bin Hudhayr asked the Prophet to remember needy Ansaar families, who received a share of the Khaybar barley and dates; later Umar gave Usayd a garment, and Usayd recalled the Prophet's warning that others would be preferred over the Ansaar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) narrates that as he was going to the Masjid, he noticed a man from the Quraysh wearing a set of (good) clothing. When he asked the man…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) reports that Umar (RA) questioned him after he called takbeer in the Masjid, because he had seen Quraysh men and an Ansaari wearing clothes that Umar had given; Umar wept and vowed never again to favour the Quraysh over the Ansaar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) once visited Rasulullaah ﷺ with his son. When he greeted with Salaam, Rasulullaah iii said,…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) reports that the Prophet honoured Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) and his son, welcomed the Ansaar, told them others would be preferred over them after his death, and urged patience until they meet him at the Pond of Kawthar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Jareer (RA) served him greatly as they travelled together on a journey. Hadhrat Jareer (RA) said, "I have seen the Ansaar do great…
narrations.summary: Anas (RA) reports that Jareer (RA) served him greatly on a journey, because Jareer had seen the Ansaar serve the Prophet and so served every Ansaari he met.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Habeeb bin Abi Thaabit narrates that Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob Ansaari once went to Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) to complain about a debt he had (asking Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA)…
narrations.summary: Habeeb bin Abi Thaabit reports that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA), refused the financial help he asked for from Mu'aawiya (RA), recalled the Prophet's words that the Ansaar would be outranked later and was told to be patient; he then stayed with Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) in Basra, who gave him his household and generous provision.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) then went to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas in Basra, who had been appointed as its governor by Hadhrat Ali (RA).…
narrations.summary: A variant report says Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA) went to Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) in Basra, who had been appointed governor by Ali (RA), and Ibn Abbaas gave him his household's furnishings and five times the grant he had asked for, plus forty slaves.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hassaan bin Thaabit (RA) narrates that they were a group of the Ansaar who needed to place a request before the Ameerul Mu'mineen who was either Hadhrat Umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: Hassaan bin Thaabit (RA) reports that Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) pressed the Ansaar's request before the Ameerul Mu'mineen, arguing until it was granted, and that Hassaan then praised him in verse.

narrations.excerpt: "You have been created as an ally- of affection and benevolence And as an orator without being inefficient nor incompetent" The Ameerul Mu'mineen said, "In using the word…
narrations.summary: Hassaan bin Thaabit (RA)'s verse praising Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) is continued, and the Ameerul Mu'mineen says that the word 'inefficient' in it was aimed at him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that when it became difficult for the Ansaar to continuously use camels to draw and carry water, they gathered before Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik (RA) reports that the Ansaar asked the Prophet to pray for their forgiveness, and he prayed for the Ansaar, their children and grandchildren, and by variant reports their spouses and neighbours.

narrations.excerpt: Another report mentions that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Allaah! Forgive the Ansaar, the children of the Ansaar and the friends of the Ansaar." Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) narrates…
narrations.summary: A variant report has the Prophet praying for the Ansaar, their children and their friends; Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) then reports the Prophet's saying that imaan belongs to Yemen, and his prayer to honour the Ansaar, who gave him shelter, support and undaunted loyalty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Muhammad ﷺ narrates that in one of his sermons, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) related the relationship between the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar to the poem that…
narrations.summary: A narrator reports Abu Bakr (RA) relating the bond between the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar in a sermon, quoting verses of poetry in praise of the Ansaar who stood by them in hardship.

narrations.excerpt: What Rasulullaah ﷺ said about the Quraysh Hadhrat Humayd bin Abdur Rahmaan Himyari narrates that when Rasulullaah passed away, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was at one end of…
narrations.summary: Humayd bin Abdur Rahmaan Himyari reports that when the Prophet died, Abu Bakr (RA) and Umar (RA) went to the Ansaar who were gathered over the Khilaafah, and Abu Bakr cited the Prophet's words that the Quraysh are the successors; Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) accepted this.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates that after Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, several speakers from the Ansaar delivered lectures (in the orchard of the Banu Saa'idah…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports the debate in the Banu Saa'idah hall over the Khilaafah, where Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) argued that the leader should be from the Muhaajireen, Abu Bakr (RA) answered, and Zaid then took his hand and pledged allegiance to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, the Ansaar gathered around Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA). Hadhrat Abu Bakr, Hadhrat Umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: Qaasim bin Muhammad reports the pledge at the Banu Saa'idah hall: Hubaab bin Mundhir (RA) raised the Ansaar's concern, Umar and Abu Bakr (RA) answered, Basheer bin Sa'd (RA) pledged first, and Abu Bakr would not take back a share he had sent an old woman of the Banu Adi bin Najaar, who refused it because she would not be bribed from her Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA) narrates that they were all in Madinah when Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I have been informed that the trade caravan of Abu Sufyaan is arriving…
narrations.summary: Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA) and Anas (RA) report the Prophet's consultation before the march to Badr: Miqdaad (RA) said the Muslims would not fail to fight, Abu Bakr and Umar gave their views, and the Ansaar pledged to follow him even to the distant city of Barkul Ghimaad, after which a verse was revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ consulted with the Sahabah (RA) to march to Badr, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) gave his opinion (in favour of marching).…
narrations.summary: Anas relates that when the Prophet consulted the Companions about marching to Badr, Abu Bakr and Umar spoke first, and then an Ansaar man pledged to follow the Prophet even to a distant city, refusing to say what the Banu Israa'eel said to Moosa.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Anas (RA) states that when Rasulullaah ﷺ heard about the arrival of (the caravan of) Abu Sufyaan, he consulted with the Sahabah (RA). When…
narrations.summary: Anas (RA) reports that the Prophet consulted about marching on Abu Sufyaan's caravan; he turned away from the views of Abu Bakr (RA) and Umar (RA), then Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) said the Ansaar would follow him wherever he went, and the Prophet gave the order to march.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Alqama bin Waqqaas Laythi (RA) narrates that after leaving for Badr, when he reached a place called Rowhaa, Rasulullaah ﷺ addressed the Sahabah (RA) asking, "What…
narrations.summary: Alqama bin Waqqaas Laythi (RA) reports the Prophet's consultation at Rowhaa after leaving for Badr: Abu Bakr and Umar gave their views, Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA) pledged that the Ansaar would follow him anywhere, and a verse was revealed in praise of this; a further report and Ibn Is'haaq add Sa'd's words and the Prophet's promise of victory over one of two groups.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Basbas to spy on what the caravan of Abu Sufyaan was doing. When he reported back to Rasulullaah there was none with him in…
narrations.summary: Anas (RA) reports that the Prophet sent Basbas (RA) to spy on Abu Sufyaan's caravan and marched to Badr; he promised the Sahabah Jannah, which Umayr bin Hamaam (RA) took up, throwing down his dates and fighting until he was martyred. Ibn Is'haaq and Ibn Jareer report the same encouragement.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says that he came to Rasulullaah ﷺ six months after Rasulullaah ﷺ returned from Taa'if. Allaah had then commanded Rasulullaah ﷺ to march…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports the Tabook expedition: the Prophet urged spending, Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) and Umar (RA) gave large sums, Aasim Ansaari and Abu Aqeel gave dates, the hypocrites mocked the small gifts, Jadd bin Qais asked to be excused, Khaalid bin Waleed captured a ruler, and Uthmaan (RA) provided two hundred camels; a verse of Surah Baraa'ah was revealed on the hypocrites.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that as Rasulullaah ﷺ was preparing for the expedition to Tabook, he asked Jadd bin Qais, "What do you say about fighting the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that the Prophet asked Jadd bin Qais to march to Tabook, and Jadd asked to be excused for fear of the Roman women, after which a verse was revealed about him.

narrations.excerpt: Ibn Asaakir narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Sahabah (RA) to several tribes and to Makkah to recruit people to fight their enemies. For this purpose, Rasulullaah ﷺ sent…
narrations.summary: Ibn Asaakir reports that the Prophet sent Sahabah to Makkah and to various tribes to recruit people for jihaad, including Buraydah bin Husayb (RA) to Banu Aslam, Raafi bin Makeeth (RA) and Jund bin Makeeth (RA) to Juhayna, Nu'aym bin Mas'ood (RA) to Ash'ja, and Budayl bin Waraqa (RA) among those sent to Banu Ka'b bin Amr.

narrations.excerpt: Rasulullaah ﷺ gave the Sahabah (RA) plenty of encouragement to fight in jihaad and asked them to spend for the pleasure of Allaah. The Sahabah (RA) therefore donated most…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr (RA) gives all he owns and Umar (RA) half, Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA), Talha (RA) and others give large sums, and Uthmaan (RA) equips a third of the army; women send jewellery, and the army camps at Thaniyyatul Wadaa. The Prophet insists that the army of Usaama (RA) be sent even while ill, despite Ummu Ayman's request to keep him back.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Usaama bin Zaid (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ gave him instructions to attack the inhabitants of Ubna (in Palestine) at dawn and to raze their town to the…
narrations.summary: The Prophet appointed Usaama bin Zaid to lead an army against Ubna, rebuked those who objected to the young commander, and insisted the army leave even while he was ill.

narrations.excerpt: As Hadhrat Usaama (RA) was preparing to leave from Jurf, a messenger came to him from Hadhrat Ummu Ayman (RA) who was his mother. The messenger informed him that was in…
narrations.summary: Usaama (RA) turns back from Jurf on news from Ummu Ayman that the Prophet is dying, reaches Madinah with Umar and Abu Ubaydah after the Prophet's passing on Monday, and Buraydah bin Husayb (RA) plants Usaama's flag at the Prophet's door, which Abu Bakr then orders to be kept there until Usaama leads the army.

narrations.excerpt: When the news of 's demise reached the other Arabs, many of them renounced Islaam. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said to Usaama, "Proceed whence had commanded you to go."…
narrations.summary: After news of the Prophet's death, Abu Bakr (RA) insisted on sending Usaama's army despite objections from senior Sahabah, asked that Umar stay behind, required all who had marched before to go, and sent Usaama off from Jurf with three thousand men and a thousand horses; Hurayth was sent ahead as a spy to find the enemy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan bin Abil Hasan narrates that before he passed away, formed an army comprising of the people of Madinah and surrounding areas, included in this army was…
narrations.summary: Hasan bin Abil Hasan reports that Usaama asked Umar to seek permission to bring the army back to Madinah, since the Prophet had died and he had the leading Sahabah with him; some Ansaar asked for an older commander, but Abu Bakr refused to reverse the appointment and seized Umar by the beard.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then proceeded to see the army off and to give them encouragement. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) walked as Hadhrat Usaama (RA) rode while Hadhrat Abdur…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr (RA) walks beside Usaama's mount as the army sets off, refuses to ride or let Usaama dismount, and asks for Umar to stay, which Usaama grants.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that after the Sahabah (RA) had pledged their •allegiance (to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)) and were satisfied, Hadhrat Abu Bakr said to Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Urwa (RA) reports that Abu Bakr (RA) refused to recall Usaama's army despite objections from Muhaajireen and Ansaar, saying he would not hold back an army he had dispatched and that the tribes refusing zakaah must be fought; he then appointed Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) to lead the force against the Murtaddeen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that when the pledge of allegiance was taken on the hand of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), the Ansaar became united in the matter of Khilaafah about…
narrations.summary: Urwa (RA) reports that after the pledge the Ansaar united, and when people asked Abu Bakr to hold back Usaama's army amid the wave of apostasy and hypocrisy, he refused, saying he would not hold back an army he had dispatched.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "After (RA) passed away, all the Arab tribes renounced Islaam and hypocrisy reared its ugly head. By Allaah! Such conditions faced my father…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha (RA) describes how after the Prophet's death all the tribes apostatised and hypocrisy rose, and Abu Bakr alone held the affairs together; Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Usaama's army was sent to Dhi Khushub, that Abu Bakr refused to recall it, and that it returned victorious.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) says, "I swear by the Being besides Whom none other is worthy of worship that none would have been worshipping Allaah had Abu Bakr not been…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah says that no one would worship Allaah had Abu Bakr not become Khalifah, and that after the Prophet's death, when tribes renounced Islaam, Abu Bakr refused to recall Usaama bin Zaid's army of seven hundred, which went out, defeated the Romans and returned, and the wavering tribes stayed Muslim.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sayf narrates that after Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) had left for Shaam, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) fell ill. It was as a result of this illness that he passed…
narrations.summary: Sayf reports that after Khaalid bin Waleed left for Shaam, Abu Bakr (RA) fell ill and appointed Umar (RA) as successor, telling him to send Muthanna (RA) and the people to Shaam at once and never let any hurdle prevent the matters of the Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Ensures that Jihaad is Waged Against the Murtaddeen and Those Who Refused to Pay Zakaah Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Consults with the Muhaajireen and the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that after the Prophet's death Abu Bakr (RA) consulted the Muhaajireen and Ansaar about the tribes refusing zakaah; Umar, Uthmaan and Ali (RA) first advised leniency, Abu Bakr refused, and vowed to fight anyone who separated salaah from zakaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalih bin Kaysaan (RA) narrates that when people started leaving the fold of Islaam (after the demise of), Hadhrat Abu Bakr stood up to address the Muslims.…
narrations.summary: Saalih bin Kaysaan (RA) reports Abu Bakr's sermon as the tribes left Islaam, recalling that the Prophet's few companions were made into the best nation, quoting Aal-Imraan 144 and Noor 55, and vowing to fight those who refused zakaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates that when the Arab tribes forsook Islaam, the Muhaajireen together with himself arrived at a common conclusion. They said to Hadhrat Abu Bakr…
narrations.summary: Umar (RA) reports that when the tribes left Islaam, the Muhaajireen with him asked Abu Bakr to leave those who prayed without zakaah alone, but Abu Bakr refused, and Umar says that day of Abu Bakr's resolve outweighed the deeds of Umar's whole family.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates that when (RA) passed away, many Arab tribes left the fold of Islaam when they said that they would perform salaah without paying zakaah. He…
narrations.summary: Umar (RA) reports that when the tribes left Islaam, he counselled Abu Bakr to show mercy towards those who refused zakaah, but Abu Bakr refused, saying he would fight them while his hand could hold a sword, and Umar found him the more capable of the two.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dabba bin Mihsin Anzi narrates that he once asked Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab, "Are you better than Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Hadhrat Umar began to weep and said, "A…
narrations.summary: Dabba bin Mihsin Anzi (RA) reports asking Umar whether he was better than Abu Bakr; Umar wept and recounted Abu Bakr's night of following the Prophet out of Makkah in the Hijrah and his day of standing firm when the tribes apostatised, with Umar's counsel.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) narrates that after had passed away and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) succeeded him, many Arab tribes forsook Islaam. It was then that Hadhrat Umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that when the tribes left Islaam, Umar (RA) asked how they could be fought given the Prophet's words to fight people until they say La ilaaha illallaah; Abu Bakr replied that he would fight whoever separates salaah from zakaah, and Umar then accepted this.

narrations.excerpt: In a narration reported by Hadhrat Qaasim bin Mahmood (RA), it is ' mentioned that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once stood up to deliver a sermon. After praising Allaah and…
narrations.summary: Qaasim bin Mahmood (RA) reports a sermon of Abu Bakr (RA): every matter has its principles, deeds without imaan or niyyah earn nothing, and the rewards for jihaad are a trade pointed to by Allaah that brings honour in both worlds.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Is'haaq bin Yasaar narrates from Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) that they were still on the battlefield of Yamaamah after the battle when Hadhrat Abu Bakr ip…
narrations.summary: Ibn Is'haaq bin Yasaar reports, from Khaalid bin Waleed (RA), a letter from Abu Bakr (RA) after the battle of Yamaamah ordering Khaalid and the Muhaajireen and Ansaar to march to Iraq, urging jihaad for the sake of Allaah and promising Allaah's reward.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abi Awfa (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr intended launching a military offensive against the Romans, he first called for Hadhrat Ali (RA),…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abi Awfa (RA) reports that Abu Bakr (RA) consulted senior Sahabah, including Ali, Umar, Uthmaan, Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, Sa'eed bin Zaid and Abu Ubaydah, about marching against the Romans in Shaam to elevate the Kalimah, and said his view was only his own opinion.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) then stood up and said, "All praises are due to Allaah Who blesses those of His servants with good Whom He pleases. By Allaah! Whenever we competed for…
narrations.summary: Umar (RA) answers Abu Bakr's proposal to march against the Romans by praising Abu Bakr's precedence in every good, and advises dispatching cavalry and infantry in succession so that Allaah assists the Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Thereafter, Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) stood up and said, "O Khalifah of They are Romans and the progeny of Romans. They are extremely powerful and as solid as a…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf advises raiding the Romans' borders with cavalry several times and gathering the tribes of Yemen before a full attack.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then asked the others what their opinions were. A response came from Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) who said, "(O Khalifah of I believe that you are truly a…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan backs Abu Bakr's plan for the Shaam campaign, and the leading Muhaajireen and Ansaar, including Talha, Zubayr and Sa'd, pledge to support him.

narrations.excerpt: (Addressing Hadhrat Ali (RA)) Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "What is your opinion, O Abul Hasan?" Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "I feel that whether you march against them…
narrations.summary: Ali tells Abu Bakr that Allaah will grant victory, Abu Bakr is glad, and he then urges the people to march against the Romans in Shaam.

narrations.excerpt: (After listening to the address of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)) The Sahabah (RA) were silent without any of them offering any response. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "O assembly…
narrations.summary: Umar rebukes the Sahabah for their silence, Amr bin Sa'eed and Khaalid bin Sa'eed answer, and Abu Bakr orders the army for Shaam and writes to Yemen.

narrations.excerpt: In the name of Allaah the Most Kind the Most Merciful From the Khalifah of to every Muslim and Mu'min of Yemen to whom this letter is read. Peace be to you. Before you…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr's letter calls the people of Yemen to jihaad against the Romans, promising martyrdom or victory and booty, and Anas bin Maalik carries it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Jubayr (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr was seeing the army off to Shaam, he stood up amongst them. He praised Allaah, instructed them…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr advises the army leaving for Shaam not to be proud and to keep ten rules, starting with not killing a helpless old man.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad narrates that Hadhrat Muthanna bin Haaritha once addressed the people saying, "O people! You should never regard marching against the Persians…
narrations.summary: Muthanna bin Haaritha urges a march on Persia, Umar answers that Abu Ubayd bin Mas'ood should lead, and Umar gives him advice on warfare.

narrations.excerpt: In another report narrated by Hadhrat Sha'bi (RA), it is mentioned that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was told to appoint a Sahabi as commander, he said, "The virtue of the…
narrations.summary: Umar says the Sahabah who volunteered first deserve command, and he appoints Abu Ubayd bin Mas'ood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar bin Abdul Azeez says that when the news of the martyrdom of Hadhrat Abu Ubayd bin Mas'ood reached Hadhrat Umar (RA) and he learnt that the Persians aligned…
narrations.summary: After Abu Ubayd's martyrdom, Umar consults the Sahabah about marching on Persia, Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf argues against it, and Sa'd bin Maalik is chosen as commander.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Saalih who was the freed slave of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) narrates that he heard Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) saying from the pulpit, "O people! 1 had kept secret from…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan tells the people from the pulpit a Hadith that a day guarding the borders for Allaah's pleasure is better than a thousand days elsewhere.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Thaabit bin Abdullaah bin Zubayr narrates that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) mentioned the following in a sermon from the pulpit: "I intent narrating to you a…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan repeats the same Hadith from the pulpit, adding that guarding the borders is better than a thousand days of salaah and fasting.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once stood up to address the people. He said, "All praises belong to Allaah Who when He crushes something, none can…
narrations.summary: Ali praises Allaah, tells the people that tomorrow they face the enemy, and urges them to pray at night, recite Qur'aan and seek help from Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Amra Ansaari narrates that when giving courage to the Muslims during the Battle of Siffeen, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Allaah has shown you a trade which will…
narrations.summary: At Siffeen, Ali urges the Muslims to trade Imaan and jihaad for forgiveness and Jannah, and to stand in straight, firm rows.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Wadaak Hamdaani narrates that when Hadhrat Ali (RA) camped at a place called Nukhayla (close to Kufa) and had lost hope in the Khawaarij, he stood up (to…
narrations.summary: Ali, having lost hope in the Khawaarij, warns that those who abandon jihaad face ruin and tells the army to prepare to march against them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab narrates that in his first address to the Muslims after the Battle Nahrwaan, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "O people! Prepare to march against the enemy…
narrations.summary: After the Battle of Nahrwaan, Ali rebukes the people for refusing to march and sets out the mutual rights between ruler and people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdul Waahid Damishqi narrates that during the Battle of Siffeen, Howshab Himyari called to Hadhrat Ali (RA) saying, "O son of Abu Taalib! Leave us alone for the…
narrations.summary: During Siffeen, Howshab Himyari calls on Ali to leave the fighting so that Muslim blood is spared, and Ali refuses to compromise the Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad, ﷺ Talha and Hadhrat Ziyaad (SI all narrate that during the Battle of Qaadisiyyah, Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) stood up to address the Muslims.…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas addresses the Muslims before Qaadisiyyah, reminding them of Allaah's promise to give them the land, of the Persian army of about two hundred thousand, and warning that losing courage would cost them their Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Thereafter, Hadhrat Aasim bin Amr (RA) stood up and said, "Allaah has subjected the people of this land (of Iraq) to you for the past three years and the harm you have…
narrations.summary: At Qaadisiyyah, Aasim bin Amr tells the army that victory depends on steadfastness with the sword and spear, and that they must seek the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that he got ready to join when intended leaving for the Battle of Badr. His uncle Hadhrat Abu Burda bin Niyaar (RA) advised him to…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah stays home with his mother instead of going to Badr, as his uncle Abu Burda advised, and later leads the funeral prayer for her.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) is reported to have said, "1 would have preferred to meet Allaah had it not been for three things; for walking in the path of Allaah, for placing my…
narrations.summary: Umar says he would have preferred to meet Allaah except for three things: walking in the path of Allaah, prostrating to Allaah, and sitting with people who choose their words as the best dates are selected.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) is also reported to have said (to the people), "Ensure that you perform Hajj for it is a virtuous deed that Allaah has commanded. However, Jihaad is…
narrations.summary: Umar tells the people to perform Hajj, which Allaah has commanded, but says Jihaad is even more virtuous.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once said, "When I was brought before to participate in the Battle of Badr, thought that I was too young and did not accept me. I had…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says he was refused for Badr as too young and wept all night until he was accepted the next year, and he admits the Muslims turned their backs at Uhud but that Allaah forgave them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that a man came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) and requested, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Please provide me with transport because I want to proceed in…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Umar gave a man who wanted to go on Jihaad a mount and provisions, and the man, refusing the gold and silver in the treasury, prayed for Umar's reward.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Artaat bin Mundhir narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked those sitting in his company, "Which person deserves the greatest rewards?" The people started…
narrations.summary: Umar asks who deserves the greatest reward, then names a man guarding Madinah from the Shaam side as better than the Ameerul Mu'mineen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ka'b bin Maalik (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to say, "The departure of Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) to Shaam was an event that presented much…
narrations.summary: Umar regrets that Mu'aadh bin Jabal left for Shaam and was not kept in Madinah, and Abu Bakr refused to hold him back.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naufal bin Amaarah narrates that Hadhrat Haarith bin Hishaam and Hadhrat Suhayl bin Amr (RA) came and sat with Hadhrat Umar (RA) in a manner that he was between…
narrations.summary: Umar moves Haarith bin Hishaam and Suhayl bin Amr aside for the early Muhaajireen, and he tells them the way to gain status is Jihaad on the Roman border.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan (RA) narrates that several persons came to the door of Hadhrat Umar (RA). Amongst them were Hadhrat Suhayl bin Amr (RA), Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan bin Harb (RA)…
narrations.summary: Suhayl bin Amr tells the Quraysh leaders that they cannot match those who accepted Islaam early, and that they should go out for jihaad, and then leaves for Shaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed bin Fudaala (RA) was a Sahabi who narrated, "Hadhrat Suhayl bin Amr and myself went together to Shaam. I heard him say, 'I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'A…
narrations.summary: Suhayl bin Amr quotes the Prophet that a moment standing in Allaah's path is better than a lifetime of deeds, and he stays at the border until he dies in the plague of Amwaas.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Naufal bin Abi Aqrab narrates that when Hadhrat Haarith bin Hishaam left Makkah, the people of Makkah became extremely sad and besides suckling infants,…
narrations.summary: Haarith bin Hishaam leaves Makkah for Jihaad despite the grief of the people, saying that the early Muslims excelled them and that he hopes to equal them in the Aakhirah, and he is later martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ziyaad who was a freed slave of the family of Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed is narrates that on his deathbed, Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed said, "There is no night on…
narrations.summary: On his deathbed Khaalid bin Waleed says he loves a freezing night on a Jihaad expedition more than a wedding night, and that his Jihaad left him little time to learn the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il narrates that when Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) was about to pass away, he said, "I searched for martyrdom wherever I anticipated it to be but I was…
narrations.summary: On his deathbed Khaalid bin Waleed says he hoped for martyrdom and wanted his weapons and horse given in Allaah's path, and Umar says the family may weep but must not tear clothes or wail.

narrations.excerpt: The fathers of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Muhammad, Umar bin Hafs and Ammaar bin Hafs all narrate from their fathers that Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) once approached Hadhrat Abu Bakr…
narrations.summary: Bilaal asks Abu Bakr for permission to guard the borders until he dies, Abu Bakr asks him to stay, and after Abu Bakr's death Umar appoints Sa'd to call the Adhaan in his place.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ibraheem Taymi narrates that after the demise of Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) called out the Adhaan before was buried. The people in the Masjid started to…
narrations.summary: After the Prophet's burial, Bilaal calls the Adhaan and the people weep. Abu Bakr then releases him to go to Shaam for jihaad, and Bilaal dies there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Yazeed Makki narrates that Hadhrat Miqdaad (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob used to say, "We have been commanded to proceed in Jihaad in all conditions." This was…
narrations.summary: Miqdaad and Abu Ayyoob hold that Surah Taubah's command to proceed in jihaad 'when light or heavy' applies in all conditions.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Raashid Habraani (RA) narrates that he once happened to meet Hadhrat Miqdaad bin Aswad (RA) who was part of's cavalry. He was sitting on the box of a currency…
narrations.summary: Miqdaad keeps planning to join a jihaad expedition despite his weight, quoting Surah Taubah's verse 'when light or heavy', and Abu Raashid and Jubayr bin Nufayr report his answers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jubayr bin Nufayr (RA) narrates that they were sitting in the company of Hadhrat Miqdaad bin Aswad (RA) in Damascus. Hadhrat Miqdaad (RA) was sitting on a box…
narrations.summary: Miqdaad bin Aswad refused to sit out jihaad because of his weight, citing the Qur'anic command to march out light or heavy, as Jubayr bin Nufayr reports.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) was reciting Surah Baraa'ah when he came to verse: 'Proceed (in the path of Allaah) when light or heavy' (Surah…
narrations.summary: Abu Talha, reciting the verse calling believers to march light or heavy, insisted on joining the naval expedition despite his age, and his body was found undecayed when buried on an island after seven days at sea.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen (RA) has mentioned that Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob Ansaari was present at the Battle of Badr with. Thereafter, apart from one year, he never missed a…
narrations.summary: Abu Ayyoob Ansaari, who missed only one campaign after Badr, asked Yazeed bin Mu'aawiya to carry his body as far into enemy land as possible and bury him there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dhabyaan narrates from his teachers from Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob Ansaari that he fell ill as he was on a military expedition during the rule of Hadhrat Mu'aawiya…
narrations.summary: Abu Dhabyaan reports that in Mu'aawiya's time Abu Ayyoob asked his companions to bury him in front of the enemy lines on campaign, and the report continues.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dhabyaan also narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) was on a military campaign under the command of Yazeed bin Mu'aawiya, he said, "Take me to enemy…
narrations.summary: On a campaign under Yazeed bin Mu'aawiya, Abu Ayyoob asks to be buried beneath the feet of the army where it meets the enemy, and says whoever dies without shirk enters Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Is'haaq (RA) narrates that it was a few days after had already left (for Tabook) that Hadhrat Abu Khaythama returned home on an extremely hot day. He found…
narrations.summary: Abu Khaythama, having missed the march to Tabook, hurries after the army in the heat, and the Prophet commends him and prays for him when he arrives.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Is'haaq says that the report reached him that Hadhrat Ibn Yaameen Nasri once met Hadhrat Abu Layla (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mughaffal, both of whom were…
narrations.summary: Ibn Yaameen Nasri gives Abu Layla and Abdullaah bin Mughaffal a camel and provisions so they can join the Prophet on jihaad, and Ulba bin Zaid gives Sadaqah in the night, which the Prophet praises as accepted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Abs bin Jabar narrates that amongst the companions of was Hadhrat Ulba bin Zaid bin Haaritha (RA). When the Sahabah (RA) were encouraged to spend in Sadaqah,…
narrations.summary: Ulba bin Zaid, with nothing to give in Sadaqah, gives up his honour for the Muslims in the night, and the Prophet tells him his Sadaqah is accepted.

narrations.excerpt: Censures Hadhrat Ibn Rawaaha Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when dispatched an army to Mu'ta, he appointed Hadhrat Zaid bin Haaritha (RA) as the…
narrations.summary: The Prophet sends an army to Mu'ta under Zaid bin Haaritha, with Ja'far and Ibn Rawaaha as successors, and rebukes Ibn Rawaaha for staying behind to pray Jumu'ah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that it happened to be the day of Jumu'ah when Rasulullaahgjsijf dispatched Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha iii with an army.…
narrations.summary: On a Jumu'ah day the Prophet sends Abdullaah bin Rawaaha with an army, he stays to pray Jumu'ah first, and the Prophet tells him no deeds can match the morning of the army's march.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Anas (RA) narrates that once commanded some Sahabah (RA) to march on a military expedition. One of them said to his wife, "I shall stay behind to…
narrations.summary: The Prophet rebukes a Companion who stayed behind to pray with him and say farewell to his family, saying the companions who left are far ahead in virtue.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) narrates that (RA) once commanded a battalion to leave. They asked, "O Should we leave tonight or wait until the morning?" said, "Would you not…
narrations.summary: The Prophet orders a battalion to leave, and when they ask whether to leave that night or in the morning, he asks if they would not like to spend the night in a garden of Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Zur'ah bin Amr bin Jareer narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once dispatched an army that included Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA). After the army had left,…
narrations.summary: Umar scolds Mu'aadh bin Jabal for delaying his departure to jihaad after the army had already left, citing the virtue of one morning or evening in the path of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ka'b bin Maalik (RA) says, "Besides the military expedition to Tabook, I did not miss a single military expedition in which participated. Of course, I did miss…
narrations.summary: Ka'b bin Maalik tells how he stayed behind from Tabook without excuse, was boycotted for fifty days, and was forgiven after he chose to speak the truth; the Qur'aan revealed his case.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Imraan (RA) narrates that they were in Constantinople with Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir (RA) as the commander of the Egyptian forces and Hadhrat Fudhala bin Ubayd…
narrations.summary: Abu Imraan reports from Constantinople that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari explained the verse 'do not throw yourselves into destruction' as a warning against staying home to tend fields instead of fighting; a second report repeats the same warning.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Imraan narrates that someone from amongst the Muhaajireen attacked the ranks of the enemy soldiers at Constantinople and actually penetrated them. To this,…
narrations.summary: Abu Imraan reports that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari answered those who called a Muhaajir's solo charge self-destruction, explaining that the verse referred to Ansaar who wanted to stay with their families and wealth instead of fighting.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abi Habeeb narrates that the news reached Hadhrat Umar that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Harr Anasi (RA) had started farming on his land in Shaam. Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Umar takes land away from Abdullaah bin Harr Anasi after he started farming in Shaam instead of jihaad, and gives it to someone else.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Abi Amr shaybaani narrates that a group of people from Yemen once passed by Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas. They asked him, "What is your comment…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas tells Yemeni visitors that the man who takes over a non-Muslim farmer's land in Shaam, with its jizya, and stops jihaad has turned back, not the man who returns to serve his parents.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) narrates that they (the Sahabah (RA)) were once on an expedition when someone from the Muhaajireen punched another Sahabi from the…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that a quarrel between a Muhaajir and an Ansaari on an expedition was defused by the Prophet, who called their tribal shouting the calls of the Period of Ignorance; Umar offered to kill Abdullaah bin Ubay, which the Prophet refused.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) and Hadhrat Amr bin Thaabit Ansaari (RA) narrates that was on the expedition of Muraysee when he demolished the idol Manaat that stood…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr and Amr bin Thaabit report that on the Muraysee expedition the Prophet had Khaalid bin Waleed destroy the idol Manaat; Abdullaah bin Ubay's remark led Umar and Usayd bin Hudhayr to offer to kill him, which the Prophet refused, and Surah Munaafiqoon was revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Abi Habeeb narrates that when a man once came to Hadhrat Umar, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Where have you been?" "I have been guarding the borders," the…
narrations.summary: Umar rebukes a man who had guarded the borders for thirty days, asking why he did not complete forty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn jurayj narrates that someone whom he regards to be a truthful person informed him that as Hadhrat Umar (RA) was patrolling (the streets of Madinah), he…
narrations.summary: Umar, patrolling Madinah, hears a woman lamenting her long-absent husband and rules that no army may be kept away from home for more than four months, after consulting his daughter Hafsa; a second chain gives the same account from Abdullaah bin Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates Hadhrat Umar (RA) once left the house at night. He then happened to overhear a woman recite the following couplet: "The night is…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar, overhearing a woman's lament at night, asked his daughter Hafsa how long a woman can be without her husband, then resolved not to keep an army away from home beyond that period.

narrations.excerpt: Rebukes those who Disliked experiencing Dust While out in the Path of Allaah Hadhrat Rabee bin Zaid (RA) narrates that while was once in the centre of the road, he…
narrations.summary: Rabee bin Zaid reports that the Prophet told a Quraysh youth who avoided walking in the dust that the dust of the path of Allaah is a fragrance from Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Musabbih Muqra'ee narrates that they were once travelling in the Roman territories as a group under the command of Hadhrat Maalik bin Abdullaah Khath'ami.…
narrations.summary: Abul Musabbih reports that Maalik bin Abdullaah Khath'ami urged Jaabir bin Abdullaah to ride; Jaabir replied loudly that he had heard the Prophet say Jahannam is forbidden for feet that become dusty in Allaah's path, and everyone dismounted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that on a certain expedition with, some of them were fasting while others were not. When they stopped to set up camp, the heat was extreme and…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that on a journey the fasting Companions collapsed in the heat while those not fasting pitched tents and watered the animals, and the Prophet said those not fasting had taken all the reward.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Bukhari states that those with the most shade with Rasulullaah were those who used their shawls to shade themselves. Whereas the fasting ones could do…
narrations.summary: A narration cited as Bukhari says the Prophet praised those not fasting on an expedition who served the fasting Companions, giving them all the reward.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Qilaaba (RA) narrates that after returning from a journey, the Sahabah (RA) were full of praise for one of their companions. They said, "We have not seen…
narrations.summary: Abu Qilaaba reports that the Companions praised a man who recited the Qur'aan and prayed on every journey, and the Prophet said those who served his travelling needs had gained all his reward.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ahmaf (RA) who was the freed slave of Hadhrat Ummu Salma (RA) narrates that they were travelling with Rasulullaah ﷺ on an expedition when they passed by a stream.…
narrations.summary: Ahmar, the freed slave of Umm Salama, ferried people across a stream on an expedition, and the Prophet remarked that he was a ship that day.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaahid (RA) narrates, "l used to accompany Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar on his journeys. Whenever I would mount my animal, he would come and hold the stirrup and…
narrations.summary: Mujaahid recounts that Abdullaah bin Umar held his stirrup and straightened his clothes on journeys, and when Mujaahid objected, Ibn Umar called him straitened in personality.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) says, "I saw us on some journeys with Rasulullaah during such extreme heat that people would place their hands over their heads because of the…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says that on journeys with the Prophet in extreme heat, only the Prophet and Abdullaah bin Rawaaha fasted.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that this was during the month of Ramadhaan. Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) says, "We went on expeditions with Rasulullaah ﷺ during the month of…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that on expeditions in Ramadhaan, those who fasted and those who did not each accepted the other's choice without resentment.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that during the Battle of Yamaamah he approached Hadhrat Abdullaah bin (RA), who was lying on the ground. When Hadhrat Abdullaah…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that during the Battle of Yamaamah, Abdullaah bin Makhrama, lying on the ground and fasting, asked for water to break his fast, but had died before Abdullaah bin Umar returned with it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Miidrik bin Awf Ahmis states that he was once with Hadhrat Umar when a messenger from Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Muqarrin (RA) arrived. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him…
narrations.summary: Mudrik bin Awf reports Umar's answer to a rumour that his uncle Awf bin Abi Hayya had thrown himself into destruction: Umar said Awf had bought the Aakhirah with this world; Awf kept fasting while wounded until he died.

narrations.excerpt: In the chapter entitled "Enduring Thirst when Inviting People Towards Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ it has already been narrated from Hadhrat Muhammad bin Hanafiyyah who says,…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Hanafiyyah reports that Abu Amr Ansaari, fasting and parched in battle, fired three arrows after recalling the Prophet's saying that an arrow fired in Allaah's path is a light on the Day of Qiyaamah, and was martyred before sunset.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "There was not a single horseman amongst us during the Battle of Badr besides Miqdaad MISS I noticed that each one of us was asleep (the night…
narrations.summary: Ali reports that on the night before Badr every Muslim slept except the Prophet, who prayed under a tree and wept until dawn, and that Miqdaad was the only horseman among them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that they were with Rasulullaah at a place called Usfaan when the Mushrikeen army under the command of Khaalid bin Waleed…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that at Usfaan the Mushrikeen under Khaalid bin Waleed failed to attack while the Prophet led the Zuhr prayer, and that the Salaatul Khawf verses were revealed between Zuhr and Asr.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Muslim from Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) states that the Mushrikeen said, "There shall soon come a salaah which is more beloved to them than even their own…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that the Mushrikeen said a prayer was soon coming that the Muslims loved more than their children.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that they were accompanying Rasulullaah ﷺ to a place called Nakhl during the expedition of Dhaatur Riqaa. It so happened that one of the…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that on the expedition of Dhaatur Riqaa the Prophet appointed Ammaar bin Yaasir and Abbaad bin Bishr to guard the camp; a Mushrik shot Abbaad three times while he prayed, and Abbaad finished his prayer before waking Ammaar.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration state that while Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) went to sleep, Hadhrat Abbaad (RA) stood in salaah. The narration also adds that Hadhrat Abbaad said, "I was…
narrations.summary: Three items: Abbaad bin Bishr keeps praying while Ammaar sleeps; Heraclius asks why the Romans are being defeated and is told the Muslims pray at night and fast by day; and Hind tells Abu Sufyaan that the night worship in the Masjid was unlike anything she had seen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Unays (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once called him and said, "I have intelligence that Khaalid bin Sufyaan bin Nubay of the Banu Hudhayl tribe…
narrations.summary: The Prophet sent Abdullaah bin Unays to kill Khaalid bin Sufyaan, who was mustering forces against him; Abdullaah prayed Asr while walking to him, killed him, and was given a staff as a token for the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that when the two armies confronted each other for the Battle of Yarmook, Qubqulaar (a Roman commander) dispatched an Arab (to spy on the…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that the Muslims at Yarmook were known for night worship and day fighting, and Hind bint Utba, once hostile, admits she had never seen Allaah worshipped as the Muslims worshipped that night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib (RA) narrates that on the night after the Muslims entered Makkah as conquerors, they continuously recited "Allaahu Akbar", "Laa Ilaaha…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that after the conquest of Makkah the Muslims recited takbeer and tahleel and made tawaaf until dawn; the Prophet repeated to Abu Sufyaan what he had said privately to Hind, and Abu Sufyaan testified to his prophethood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ left on a military expedition to Khaybar, the Sahabah (RA) had reached a valley when they raised their…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports that on the way to Khaybar the Prophet stopped the Companions from shouting takbeer in a valley, and taught him 'there is no power or might except with Allaah' as a treasure of Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that whenever they (the Sahabah (RA)) ascended an incline, they recited Takbeer and whenever they descended from an incline, they recited…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that the Companions on the journey said takbeer when climbing an incline and tasbeeh when descending.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "On an expedition, people are of two types. One type are those who go out and abundantly engage in the Dhikr of Allaah together with…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar describes two kinds of people on an expedition: those who stay conscious of Allaah and spend generously, and those who lack dhikr, avoid the fighting, boast, and misappropriate the booty, and so have no share of the reward.

narrations.excerpt: Making Du'aa when Leaving a Place.
narrations.summary: Section heading only: 'Making Du'aa when leaving a place', with no narration.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin is'haaq says that he was informed that when Rasulullaah ﷺ left Makkah to make Hijrah to Madinah for the pleasure of Allaah, he said, "All praises…
narrations.summary: Ibn Is'haaq reports the du'aa the Prophet made when leaving Makkah for Madinah, asking Allaah for protection, companionship and steadfastness.

narrations.excerpt: The grandfather of Hadhrat Abu Marwaan Aslami narrates that they accompanied Rasulullaah ﷺ to Khaybar. When they got close (to Khaybar) and could see it, Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: The grandfather of Abu Marwaan Aslami reports the du'aa the Prophet made on seeing Khaybar, asking for the good of the town and protection from its evil, then ordering the Companions to advance in Allaah's name.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Tabraani states that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make this du'aa each time he entered a town.
narrations.summary: A narration cited as Tabraani says the Prophet made this same du'aa each time he entered a town.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates that on the day of the Battle of Badr, Rasulullaah looked at his Sa'habah who numbered just over three hundred. He then looked at the…
narrations.summary: Umar reports that at Badr the Prophet, facing many more enemies, prayed towards the Qiblah until his upper garment fell off; Abu Bakr put it back and reminded him of Allaah's promise, and Surah Anfaal 9 was revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas US narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ left for Badr with three hundred and fifteen men. When they reached. Badr, Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed, "O…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports the du'aa the Prophet made as he set out for Badr with 315 men, asking Allaah to provide transport, clothing and food for his Companions, and how Allaah granted this after the victory.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) says that he had never heard a du'aa more persistent than the du'aa Rasulullaah ﷺ made on the occasion of the Battle of Badr. He…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that the Prophet's du'aa at Badr, pleading on Allaah's promise, was the most persistent he had heard, and that the Prophet then said he could see where the dead Mushrikeen would fall by nightfall.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that on the day that the Battle of Uhud was fought, Rasulullaah ﷺ repetitively said, "O Allaah! (Do assist us) If You (choose not to assist us)…
narrations.summary: Two reports: Anas says the Prophet repeatedly prayed for help at Uhud, and Abu Sa'eed Khudri says that at the Battle of the Trench the Prophet taught the Companions a du'aa after which Allaah sent a powerful wind against the enemy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates that on the occasion of the Battle of Khandaq; the Sahabah (RA) asked Rasulullaah ﷺ, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Is there any du'aa that we…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports the du'aa the Prophet taught the Companions during the Battle of Khandaq, after which Allaah sent a powerful wind against the enemy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once went to Masjid Ahzaab and placed his shawl aside. He then stood up and stretched his hands out to curse the…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that at Masjid Ahzaab the Prophet stood and cursed the Mushrikeen without prayer the first time, then cursed them again and prayed two rakaahs.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Bukhari and Muslim state that Rasulullaah ﷺ cursed the conglomeration of Kuffaar forces (when they attacked Madinah) by saying, "O Allaah Who has revealed…
narrations.summary: Three narrations: the Prophet cursed the confederate forces attacking Madinah, asking Allaah to defeat and shake them; another du'aa asks for victory; and Abu Hurayrah relates a du'aa praising Allaah as the one who alone defeated the coalition.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "After fighting for a while during the Battle of Badr, I rushed to see how Rasulullaah ﷺ was keeping. When I arrived there, Rasulullaah ﷺ was in…
narrations.summary: Ali reports that during Badr he went to check on the Prophet, who was in sajdah repeatedly saying 'Yaa Hayyu, Yaa Qayyoom' and kept doing so until Allaah granted victory.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates that on the night before the Battle of Badr, Rasulullaah ﷺ spent the night in salaah praying, "O Allaah! If this group is destroyed, You will…
narrations.summary: Ali reports that on the night before Badr the Prophet prayed through the night for the destruction of that group, and that rain fell, making the ground firm for the Muslims and muddy for the enemy.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Ali (RA) states that although Rasulullaah ﷺ was a Musaafir (traveller), he had spent the entire night in Ibaadah till the morning that the…
narrations.summary: Ali reports that although the Prophet was a traveller, he spent the whole night before Badr in worship until morning.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rifaa'ah Zuraqi (RA) narrates that when the Mushrikeen had returned after the Battle of Uhud, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Stand straight so that I may praise my Rabb…
narrations.summary: Rifaa'ah Zuraqi relates the Prophet's long du'aa of praise after Uhud as the Sahabah stood in rows, and Abdullaah bin Abbaas explains that some should stay behind on jihaad to learn Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ahwas bin Hakeem bin Umayr Absi narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote the following in a letter addressed to the commanders of the various Muslims armies,…
