narrations.summary: Ahwas bin Hakeem bin Umayr Absi relates Umar's letter to the army commanders urging them to gain a deep understanding of Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hitaan bin Abdullaah Raqaashi narrates that they were once part of an army under the command of Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA). They were travelling along the…
narrations.summary: Hitaan bin Abdullaah Raqaashi relates that Abu Moosa Ash'ari stopped people from renewing their wudu without need on the march and warned that knowledge would vanish and ignorance spread.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Mas'ood Ansaari (RA) narrates that a man came with a reined camel and said, "(I am donating) This camel in the path of Allaah." Rasulullaah said, "You shall…
narrations.summary: Abu Mas'ood Ansaari relates that a man donated a reined camel in the path of Allaah, and the Prophet promised him seven hundred camels in return on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Saamit narrates, "I was with Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) when he received his allowance (from the state treasury). Hadhrat Abu Dharr had his slave girl…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Saamit relates how Abu Dharr spent his whole allowance in the path of Allaah, and the Prophet's warning that unspent gold and silver becomes live coal is quoted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Sala Ansaari (RA) narrates that his brothers laid a complaint (against him) before Rasulullaah ﷺ when they alleged that he wasted his wealth and gave out…
narrations.summary: Qais bin Sala Ansaari says his brothers complained that he gave away too much wealth, and the Prophet told him to keep spending so that Allaah would spend on him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal is narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Glad tidings for the person who abundantly engages in the Dhikr of Allaah while out in Jihaad in the path…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal relates the Prophet's words on the reward of dhikr and spending in jihaad, and explains that spending while out on an expedition earns far more than spending from home.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA), Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA), Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA), Hadhrat Abu Umaama (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas, Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) and Hadhrat Imraan…
narrations.summary: Several Companions relay that spending while staying at home earns seven hundred times its reward and spending on an expedition seven hundred thousand times, and the Prophet recites Surah Baqara verse 261.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) narrates that someone asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ (Tell me about) A person who intends to wage Jihaad and also has the intention of earning some…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that when a man asked about a fighter who seeks worldly gain, the Prophet said he receives no reward, and repeated this each time he was asked, three times in all.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that a man approached Rasulullaah ﷺ with the query, "Tell me about a person who wages Jihaad in search of fame and fortune. What is…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah relates that the Prophet said a man who fights for fame and fortune gets nothing, and that Allaah accepts only deeds done solely for His pleasure.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aasim bin Amr bin Qataadah JE narrates that a man lived amongst them whose identity no one really knew. He was only known as Quzmaan. Whenever his name was…
narrations.summary: Aasim bin Amr bin Qataadah tells how Quzmaan, whom the Prophet called a man of Jahannam, fought fiercely at Uhud only for his people's honour and then killed himself when his wound became unbearable.

narrations.excerpt: It is reported that Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) used to often ask (the people around him), "Tell me about the person who entered Jannah without ever performing a single…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah names Usayram as the man who entered Jannah without a single salaah, and Mahmood bin Labeed relates how he accepted Islaam on the day of Uhud and was martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) narrates that because Hadhrat Amr bin Uqaysh had given out a loan on interest during the Period of Ignorance, he disliked accepting Islaam until…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that Amr bin Uqaysh put off Islaam until his interest-bearing loans were repaid, then fought fiercely at Uhud, and when asked by Sa'd bin Mu'aadh's messenger he said he fought for Allaah and His Rasool.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shaddaad ibnul Haad narrates that a Bedouin once came to Rasulullaah (Jiii, accepted Imaan and became a devoted follower of Rasulullaah ﷺ. He then undertook to…
narrations.summary: Shaddaad ibnul Haad relates that a Bedouin who had followed the Prophet hoping for martyrdom was struck in the throat by an arrow exactly where he had pointed, and the Prophet led his janaazah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that a man came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I am a man with a black skin, an ugly face and without any wealth. Will I enter…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik relates that a dark-skinned man who asked whether fighting would take him to Jannah was martyred, and the Prophet saw two wide-eyed damsels of Jannah disputing over his body.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent a message to him stating, "Get your clothes and weapons on and come to me." When he got to Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Al Aas says he accepted Islaam for love of Islaam and not for wealth, when the Prophet offered to send him in command of an army, and the Prophet replies that good wealth is a fine thing for a good man.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari Taa'ee narrates that many people in Kufa gathered with Hadhrat Abul Mukhtaar the father of Mukhtaar bin Abu Ubayd at the bridge of Abu Ubayd. This…
narrations.summary: Umar rebukes men who called their martyred comrades martyrs, saying every fighter is raised according to the intention he died with, and Maalik bin Aws relates the same teaching from Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maalik bin Aws bin Hadathaan (RA) narrates that they were busy discussing an army that was martyred during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Umar when one of them…
narrations.summary: Maalik bin Aws reports Umar's teaching that the reward of those who fall in an army depends on their intention, and that true martyrs are those who fight with perseverance seeking Allaah's reward.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that when mention was made of some martyrs in front of Hadhrat Umar (RA), he addressed the people saying, "Whom do you regard to be martyrs?" The…
narrations.summary: Umar asks who the martyrs are, and when told they are those killed in battle, explains that the true martyr gives his life hoping for Allaah's reward, and defines the true Muhaajir and the true Muslim.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dimaam narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) sent a message to his mother (Hadhrat Asmaa (RA)) saying, "People have deserted me while those people (my…
narrations.summary: Asmaa tells her son Abdullaah bin Zubayr that if he fights to revive the Book and Sunnah he should die upon the truth, but if he seeks worldly gain there is no good in him, alive or dead.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Maalik Ash'ari (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ sent us on an expedition and appointed Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) as our commander. We set out and later…
narrations.summary: Abu Maalik Ash'ari relates that a man left the camp without the Ameer's permission, and Abu Moosa Ash'ari rebukes him and tells him to start afresh to undo his sin.

narrations.excerpt: Rasulullaah ﷺ Criticises Separating in Valleys and Sealing Roads Hadhrat Abu Tha'laba Khushani (RA) narrates that when the Muslims camped at a valley, they separated and…
narrations.summary: Abu Tha'laba Khushani relates that the Prophet called it Shaytaan's work when Muslims camped separately in valleys on expedition, and after that they always stayed together.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration' adds that (the Sahabah (RA) stayed so close together thereafter that) if a sheet was thrown over them, it would cover them all. Hadhrat Mu'aadh Juhani…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh Juhani reports the Prophet's ruling that whoever crowds the camp or blocks a road earns no reward for jihaad, and a separate narration adds that the Companions stayed close together on campaign.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sahl bin Handhaliyya (RA) narrates that they marched with Rasulullaah ﷺ for the Battle of Hunayn and were marching with great speed until the afternoon. Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Sahl bin Handhaliyya relates that at Hunayn the Prophet asked for a night guard, Anas bin Abi Marthad Ghanawi volunteered and kept watch at the ravine, and the Prophet told him he had made Jannah compulsory for himself.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Atiyya (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once sitting when he was informed that a man had passed away. Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Has any of you seen him do any…
narrations.summary: Abu Atiyya relates that when the Prophet was told a man had died, he asked whether anyone had seen good in him, and a Sahabi said he had stood guard with him, so the Prophet led the janaazah and testified that he was of Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Atiyya (RA) narrates that when a person passed away during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, some of the Sahabah (RA) said, "O Rasulullaah Do not lead the Janaazah…
narrations.summary: Abu Atiyya and Abu Aa'idh relate that when some Companions asked the Prophet not to lead a janaazah, he asked whether anyone had seen any good deed by the dead man, and Umar objected that the man was sinful.

narrations.excerpt: The Hadith of Hadhrat Abu Rayhaana (RA) has passed in the chapter entitled "Enduring Extreme Cold when Inviting People Towards Allaah" In the narration, he states,…
narrations.summary: Abu Rayhaana relates that the Prophet prayed for the volunteers who guarded the camp at night and said the eye that stands guard in the path of Allaah is safe from Jahannam, and Jaabir adds that Ammaar bin Yaasir and Abbaad bin Bishr guarded the mouth of the valley.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Whenever a Mu'min is hurt on his body, Allaah uses it as a means to annul some of his sins." Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri relates that the Prophet said illness annuls sins, and Ubay bin Ka'b prayed for a fever that would never stop him from worship, and it stayed with him until his death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates that a person came to Rasulullaah and asked, "Tell me what we receive in exchange for these illnesses that keep afflicting us?"…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that Ubay bin Ka'b asked Allaah for a fever that would stay with him until death without preventing Hajj, Umrah, jihaad or congregational salaah, and it did.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jundub bin Sufyaan (RA) reports that as Rasulullaah ﷺ was walking, his foot struck a stone and he fell. This caused his finger to start bleeding. Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Jundub bin Sufyaan relates that when the Prophet's finger bled from a fall, he said it was only a finger that bled and whatever it suffered was in the path of Allaah; Anas adds the injuries the Prophet took at Uhud.

narrations.excerpt: The Hadith has also passed in which Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that whenever Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) spoke about the Battle of Uhud, he would say, "Every credit for that…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha relays Abu Bakr's account of Uhud: the Prophet told them to tend to Talha, who had over seventy wounds, and Abu Bakr said every credit for that day went to Talha.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Sa'd says that the report reached him that during the Battle of Uhud, Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) sustained twenty one wounds. An injury to…
narrations.summary: Ibraheem bin Sa'd reports that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf sustained twenty-one wounds at Uhud, and an injury to his leg left him limping.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) says that his paternal uncle, Hadhrat Anas bin Nadhar bitterly regretted his inability to participate in the battle of Badr. He addressed…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik relates how his uncle Anas bin Nadhar, who had missed Badr, fought at Uhud until he was martyred with over eighty wounds, and how the verse of Surah Ahzaab about men like him was revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates, "My paternal uncle after whom I was named did not participate in the Battle of Badr at the side of Rasulullaah ﷺ. This was…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik tells how his uncle Anas bin Nadhar, who missed Badr, fought at Uhud with over eighty wounds until he was martyred, and how a verse of the Qur'aan was understood to refer to men like him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed Hadhrat Zaid bin Haaritha (RA) as commander of the expedition to Mu'ta. Rasulullaah ﷺ then added, 'If…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar relates that the Prophet named Zaid bin Haaritha commander at Mu'ta with Ja'far and Abdullaah bin Rawaaha as successors, and that Ja'far's body had over ninety wounds, none on his back.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Shurahbeel (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh was struck with an arrow during the Battle of Khandaq, his blood spilled on Rasulullaah ﷺ.…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Shurahbeel relates that when Sa'd bin Mu'aadh was struck by an arrow at the Battle of the Trench and his blood spilled onto the Prophet, Abu Bakr and Umar cried out in shock.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Ubayd Thaqafi (RA) reports, "During the battle at Taa'if, I spotted Abu Sufyaan bin Harb sitting and eating on the wall of Abu Ya'la. I shot an arrow…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Ubayd Thaqafi relates that he shot Abu Sufyaan bin Harb in the eye at Taa'if, and when Abu Sufyaan offered it as an injury in Allaah's path, the Prophet offered to pray for its return or give him Jannah, and he chose Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qataadah bin Nu'maan (RA) narrates that when his eye was injured during the Battle of Badr, his eyeball hung on his cheek and the Sahabah (RA) wanted to cut it…
narrations.summary: Qataadah bin Nu'maan relates that his eye was injured at Badr, and Rifaa'ah bin Raafi relates that an arrow ruptured his eye, which the Prophet treated with his saliva and prayer, leaving no pain.

narrations.excerpt: The incident reported by Hadhrat Yahya bin Abdul Hameed has already passed in which he narrates from his grandfather that an arrow struck Hadhrat Raafi bin Khadeej in the…
narrations.summary: Raafi bin Khadeej asks the Prophet to remove an arrow from his chest, and separately a man from Banu Abdul Ash'hal and his wounded brother join the pursuit after Uhud, with the man carrying his brother at times.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that during the battle against Musaylama (Kadhaab), Hadhrat Baraa (RA) threw himself on to the people in the orchard (the defenders of Musaylama…
narrations.summary: Anas relates that during the battle against Musaylama, Baraa bin Maalik scaled an orchard wall and opened its gate, suffering over eighty wounds, and that Khaalid bin Waleed nursed him for a month.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Is'haaq bin Abdullaah bin Abu Talha narrates that Hadhrat Anas and his brother were (fighting) at an enemy fortress in Hareeq, a place in Iraq. The Kuffaar were…
narrations.summary: Is'haaq bin Abdullaah bin Abu Talha relates that when Anas was being pulled up by a burning hook at an enemy fortress in Hareeq, Baraa bin Maalik held the chain until the rope gave way, burning his hand to the bone, and Allaah saved Anas.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that the hooks caught Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) and the Kuffaar started pulling at him until he was lifted off the ground. While his brother…
narrations.summary: Another narration says the hooks caught Anas and lifted him off the ground, and Baraa ran, jumped onto the wall and tugged the chain until the rope gave way, his hands burnt to the bone.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) reports that he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "I swear by the Being Who controls my life! I would not have missed a single expedition in the path of…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that the Prophet swore he would have joined every expedition if not for men he could not provide transport for, and wished to be killed in the path of Allaah and given life again, repeatedly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Allaah stands surety for the person who goes out in the path of Allaah. (Allaah says) For the person who…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah narrates the Prophet's promise of reward for whoever goes out in Allaah's path, and his wish to be martyred and brought back to life again and again.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Abi Haazim narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once delivered a sermon in which he said, "There is a palace in the everlasting Jannah that has five hundred…
narrations.summary: Qais bin Abi Haazim narrates Umar's sermon on the palace in Jannah for prophets and siddeeqs, and Umar's wish for martyrdom.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) says, "Allaah then gave martyrdom to him at the hands of the worst of creation who was a slave of Mughiera.
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that Allaah granted Umar martyrdom at the hands of a slave of Mughiera, but the report is cut off before the rest.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to make the following du'aa: "O Allaah! Bless me with martyrdom in Your path and make my death in the city of Your…
narrations.summary: Aslam, a freed slave of Umar, narrates Umar's du'aa for martyrdom in Allaah's path and for his death in the city of the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Hafsa (RA) states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) prayed, "O Allaahl Let me be killed in Your path and have my death in the city of Your Nabi ﷺ When…
narrations.summary: Hafsa narrates Umar's prayer to be killed in Allaah's path and to die in the city of the Prophet, and his answer when she asked how that could happen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) says that on the day that he Battle of Uhud was to take place, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Jahash (RA) said to him, "Will you not make du'aa…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas narrates the du'aas he and Abdullaah bin Jahash made before Uhud, and how Abdullaah's prayer for martyrdom was answered.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Jahash said, "O Allaah! I beseech You on oath that I should meet an enemy tomorrow who should kill…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates Abdullaah bin Jahash's prayer to meet an enemy who would kill him and mutilate him, and says he hopes Allaah will also grant the rest of that prayer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "There are many people 498 (Vd-p wearing two old pieces of cloth and who are not given any attention but Allaah will…
narrations.summary: Anas reports the Prophet's words about Baraa bin Maalik, who, when the Muslims were losing at Tustar and asked him to make a vow, prayed for the enemy's shoulders and was then martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "There are many weak people whom others regard as weak and who wear two old pieces of cloth. However, Allaah will…
narrations.summary: Baraa bin Maalik made vows at two battles, asking Allaah for the enemy's shoulders; the Muslims won at the first, and after the second, at the bridge of Sus, he was martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Humayd bin Abdur Rahmaan Himyari narrates that a Sahabi by the name of Hadhrat Humama iS once fought a battle in Isfahan during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: Humayd bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that Humama, who prayed to Allaah for martyrdom or death in His path, died at Isfahan in Umar's caliphate, and Abu Moosa testified that he was a martyr.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Imaam Ahmad adds that Hadhrat Humama (RA) also said, "Give Humama death in Your path even though he dislikes it. O Allaah! Let Humama not return home from…
narrations.summary: A narration cited to Imaam Ahmad adds Humama's prayer and says he died of a stomach illness at Isfahan, and Abu Moosa declared him a martyr on what he had heard from the Nabi.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ma'qal bin Yasaar (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once consulted with the Hurmuzaan (a Persian leader who accepted islaam after being defeated by the…
narrations.summary: Ma'qal bin Yasaar narrates that Umar consulted Hurmuzaan on the Persian campaign, appointed Nu'maan bin Muqarrin to lead at Isfahan, and that Nu'maan prayed for martyrdom and was the first to fall.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jubayr (RA) has narrated the Battle of Nahaawind in detail. In his narration he quotes (the following words of Hadhrat Nu'maan (RA)), "Whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Jubayr narrates Nu'maan bin Muqarrin's words at the Battle of Nahaawind, in which he prayed for victory for Islaam and then for martyrdom.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Bilaal narrates that as Rasulullaah ﷺ was leaving for the Battle of Badr, Hadhrat Sa'd bin Khaythama (RA) and his father Hadhrat Khaytama both…
narrations.summary: Sulaymaan bin Bilaal narrates that Sa'd bin Khaythama and his father both wanted to go to Badr, lots sent Sa'd, and Sa'd was later martyred by Amr bin Abd Wadd.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ali bin Husayn narrates that when Utba called for challengers during the Battle of Badr, Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) stood up to challenge Waked…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Ali bin Husayn describes the single combats at Badr: Ali killed Waleed bin Utba, Hamza killed Shayba, and Ubaydah bin Haarith was mortally wounded by Utba, after which the Prophet laid his head on his lap and Ubaydah asked whether he was a martyr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zuhri narrates that when Hadhrat Ubaydah (RA) and Utba exchanged blows, the blow of each one incapacitated the other. Returning to the battlefield, Hadhrat Ali…
narrations.summary: Zuhri gives a second account of the Badr duels, in which Ubaydah and Utba wounded each other, Ali and Hamza finished Utba, and they brought Ubaydah to the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: The Incident of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and his brother Zaid Concerning not Wearing Armour with the Intention of being Martyred Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that on…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar narrates that before Uhud Umar asked his brother Zaid to take his armour, Zaid said he wanted martyrdom as much as Umar did, and the two of them left the armour behind.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Mansoor reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Once the people had left Rasulullaah ﷺ during the Battle of Uhud, I looked through all the dead and did…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Mansoor reports Ali's account of searching the dead after Uhud, failing to find the Prophet, resolving to fight until he was killed, and then seeing the Prophet among the enemy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Raafi Si who belonged to the Banu Adi bin Najjaar tribe narrates that Hadhrat Anas bin Nadhar (RA) the uncle of Hadhrat Anas bin…
narrations.summary: Qaasim bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that Anas bin Nadhar rebuked men who had lost heart after the report of the Prophet's martyrdom, then fought on until he was killed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ammaar Khatmi (RA) reports that Hadhrat Thaabit bin Dahdaaha came before the Muslims during the Battle of Uhud when they were all scattered and…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ammaar Khatmi reports that Thaabit bin Dahdaaha called the Ansaar back at Uhud, reminding them that Allaah is living, and that he was martyred by a spear thrown by Khaalid bin Waleed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Najeeh (RA) reports that during the Battle of Uhud, a Muhaajir passed by an Ansaari lying in a pool of blood. The Muhaajir said to the Ansaari, "Do you know…
narrations.summary: Abu Najeeh reports that a wounded Ansaari told a Muhaajir that the Prophet had delivered his message and the believers must keep fighting, and that the verse of Aal Imraan 144 was then revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) narrates, "During the Battle of Uhud, Rasulullaah ﷺ sent me to look for Hadhrat Sa'd bin Rabee (RA). Rasulullaah instructed, 'If you see…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit narrates that after Uhud the Prophet sent him to look for Sa'd bin Rabee, and that Sa'd, dying, sent salaams and said he could smell the fragrance of Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration reported by Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Sa'sa'a states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Who will see what has happened to Sa'd bin Rabee for me?" The rest of the…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Sa'sa'a narrates that the Prophet asked who would find out about Sa'd bin Rabee, and that Sa'd sent back a message of thanks to the Prophet on behalf of himself and the Ummah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when the Mushrikeen surrounded Rasulullaah during the Battle of Uhud, Rasulullaah ﷺ was with seven men from the Ansaar and one from the…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik and Jaabir describe how the Ansaar defended the Prophet at Uhud one by one until they were martyred, and how Talha alone remained at his side to hold back the enemy.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) states that after being overwhelmed during the Battle of Uhud, the Muslims dispersed from around Rasulullaah ﷺ and the only…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that at Uhud, when only eleven Ansaar and Talha remained with the Prophet, Talha repeatedly volunteered to hold back the enemy, and the Prophet told him that saying Bismillaah would have lifted him to heaven.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mahmood bin Labeed says that when Rasulullaah ﷺ marched to Uhud, Hadhrat Yamaan bin jaabir (RA) (the father of Hadhrat Hudhayfa and Hadhrat Thabit bin Qais (RA)…
narrations.summary: Mahmood bin Labeed narrates that two elderly men, Yamaan and Thaabit bin Qais, joined the Muslim army at Uhud in secret; Thaabit was killed by the Mushrikeen and Yamaan by Muslims who did not recognise him, and Hudhayfa forgave the blood money, which raised his standing with the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that the two men also said, "We shall then join up with Rasulullaah ﷺ. Perhaps Allaah shall bless us with martyrdom as we fight by the side of…
narrations.summary: A second report adds that the two old men slipped into the Muslim army to seek martyrdom, and that Hudhayfa's forgiveness of the blood money raised his standing in the eyes of the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent an expedition on a spying duty under the command of Hadhrat Aasim bin Thaabit who was the maternal…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports how Aasim bin Thaabit's spying party was surrounded by the Banu Lihyaan and killed, with Khubayb bin Adi and Zaid bin Dathana taken and sold in Makkah; Aasim bin Umar bin Qataadah then reports how the envoys sent to Rajee were betrayed to the Hudhayl.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aasim (RA) then recited some couplets which meant: "Far from being a sick man, I am a powerful archer And my bow has a sturdy string Arrows with long and wide…
narrations.summary: Aasim bin Thaabit recites couplets as he fights and is martyred; the Hudhayl then try to take his head for Sulaafa, but wasps guard his body until a flood carries it away, and Umar says Allaah protects His servant in death as in life.

narrations.excerpt: (The other three Sahabah (RA) in the group) Hadhrat Khubayb (RA), Hadhrat Zaid bin Dathana and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Taariq (RA) chose the easier option and chose to…
narrations.summary: After the Rajee betrayal, Abdullaah bin Taariq is stoned to death at Zahraan, and Zaid bin Dathana is executed at Tan'eem, where Abu Sufyaan asks whether he would rather have the Prophet in his place and Zaid says he would not let a thorn prick the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Is'haaq narrates the story of Hadhrat Khubayb bin Adi (RA) from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Najeeh who was informed by Maariya, the freed slave of Hujayr bin lhaab.…
narrations.summary: Ibn Is'haaq narrates through Maariya and Aasim bin Umar bin Qataadah how Khubayb bin Adi was held in Makkah and then executed at Tan'eem after a last prayer; Mu'aawiya recalls his father's fear of the curse, and Moosa bin Uqba relates that the Prophet announced the martyrdom of Khubayb and Zaid bin Dathana.

narrations.excerpt: A lengthy narration of Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) states that the children of the Mushrikeen killed at Badr executed Hadhrat Khubayb (RA). While he was tied to the…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr narrates that the sons of Mushrikeen killed at Badr executed Khubayb bin Adi, who refused to swear that he would prefer the Prophet to be in his place, and recited couplets while on the cross.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds the following line after the first couplet: "They all express their hatred for me and make every effort to oppose me because I am in fetters and in…
narrations.summary: Further couplets of Khubayb bin Adi, given as additions to the previous report, express his fear of the fire and his readiness to die as a Muslim for Allaah's sake.

narrations.excerpt: Several men of knowledge including Mughiera bin Abdur Rahmaan and Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazam narrate that the expert spear-thrower Abu Baraa…
narrations.summary: Mughiera bin Abdur Rahmaan and others narrate that Abu Baraa asked the Prophet to send teachers to Najd, that Mundhir bin Amr led about seventy Sahabah there, and that Aamir bin Tufayl's men killed them at Bir Ma'oona, with only Ka'b bin Zaid surviving and Amr bin Umayyah Dhamri spared.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched Hadhrat Haraam the brother of Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) together with seventy riders on an expedition. The…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik narrates that Haraam bin Milhaan, sent with the Prophet's letter to Aamir bin Tufayl, was stabbed from behind as he spoke to the enemy under a promise of safety, and cried out that he was successful; the Prophet then cursed the tribes responsible for thirty mornings.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration of Bukhari states that when Hadhrat Haraam (RA) the uncle of Hadhrat Anas (RA) was stabbed with a spear on the expedition to Bir Ma'oona, he wiped his…
narrations.summary: Another report names the man who killed Haraam bin Milhaan as Jabbaar bin Salma Kilaabi, who accepted Islaam when told that Haraam's cry meant his entry into Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent an to Mu'ta in Jumaadal Ula 8 A.H. Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed Hadhrat Haaritha as commander of the expedition.…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports that the Prophet appointed Zaid bin Haaritha, then Ja'far and then Abdullaah bin Rawaaha as commanders for Mu'ta, and that Abdullaah wept at the departure and recited couplets, fearing the crossing over Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: "May peace remain with the great man whom I have greeted amongst the date palms, wfio is the best of those who bid farewell and the best of friends"
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Rawaaha recites couplets of farewell to the Prophet as the Prophet turns back after seeing off the army.

narrations.excerpt: The expedition marched until they set up camp at a place called Ma'aan which was located in Shaam. There they received intelligence that Heraclius had arrived in Ma'aab…
narrations.summary: At Ma'aan the Muslims learn of Heraclius's army and resolve to press on, Abdullaah bin Rawaaha urges them to fight for victory or martyrdom, and at Mu'ta Zaid bin Haaritha and then Ja'far are martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration of Hadhrat Urwa (RA) states that afterwards (after the martyrdom of Hadhrat Zaid (RA) Hadhrat Ja'far (RA) grabbed hold of the flag and fought with it…
narrations.summary: Urwa narrates that after Zaid's martyrdom Ja'far took up the flag, hamstrung his red horse, fought until he was martyred, and became the first Muslim to disable his mount.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) says, "I was an orphan in the care of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha. He took me along on the journey (to Mu'ta) and seated me behind him on…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Arqam recounts that, as an orphan in Abdullaah bin Rawaaha's care on the Mu'ta journey, he wept at the couplets about dying in Shaam and was struck with a whip for it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abbaad bin Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) narrates from his foster father from the Banu Murrah clan that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha (RA) grabbed hold of the flag…
narrations.summary: Abbaad bin Abdullaah bin Zubayr reports, through his foster father of Banu Murrah, that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha took up the flag after Ja'far was martyred, dismounted, recited couplets, and fought on until he was martyred after throwing down the meat he was eating.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abbaad bin Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) narrates that his foster father from the Banu Murrah who participated in the Battle of Mu'ta said, "By Allaah! It is as if I…
narrations.summary: Abbaad bin Abdullaah bin Zubayr reports his foster father's account of Ja'far hamstringing his red horse and fighting on while reciting couplets about Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) who was the son of Hadhrat Zaid bin Khattaab narrates that (his father) Hadhrat Zaid bin Khattaab (RA) carried the flag of the Muslims during…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Zaid bin Khattaab narrates that his father Zaid bin Khattaab carried the flag at Yamaamah, rebuked the fleeing Muslims and fought on until he was martyred, after which Saalim, freed slave of Abu Hudhayfa, took up the flag.

narrations.excerpt: The daughter of Hadhrat Thaabit bin Qais bin Shammaas (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) requested the Muslim to fight against those who forsook Islaam from…
narrations.summary: During the Battle of Yamaamah, Thaabit bin Qais and Saalim dug a foxhole, refused to flee and fought until they were martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abbaad bin Bishr (RA) said to him, "O Abu Sa'eed! Last night I saw (in a dream) that the sky opened up for me and then…
narrations.summary: Abbaad bin Bishr told Abu Sa'eed Khudri of his dream of martyrdom, then led four hundred Ansaar in the attack at Yamaamah and was martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ja'far bin Abdullaah bin Aslam Hamdaani narrates that the first casualty during the Battle of Yamaamah was Hadhrat Abu Aqeel Unayfi (RA). An arrow struck him…
narrations.summary: At Yamaamah, the mortally wounded Abu Aqeel answered Ma'n bin Adi's call to the Ansaar, fought, and died after learning that Musaylama had been killed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says that when the Muslim army suffered defeat initially during the Battle of Yamaamah, he saw Hadhrat Thaabit bin Qais (RA) applying perfume (in…
narrations.summary: Before the Battle of Yamaamah, Thaabit bin Qais perfumed himself for battle, refused to join the flight and was killed fighting.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when the Muslims were being defeated during the Battle of Yamaamah, Hadhrat Thaabit (RA) said, "Shame on those people (the enemy) and…
narrations.summary: At Yamaamah, Thaabit bin Qais cursed the enemy and the retreating Muslims, killed a man standing on a wall and was martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thaabit Bunaani (RA) narrates that during a certain battle (the Battle of Yarmook), Hadhrat Ikrama bin Abu Jahal (RA) dismounted from his animal and was walking…
narrations.summary: At the Battle of Yarmook, Ikrama bin Abu Jahal dismounted and walked into the fighting against Khaalid bin Waleed's advice, and was martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Ghassaani narrates from his father that during the Battle of Yarmook, Hadhrat Ikrama bin Abu Jahal (RA) said, "I fought several battles against…
narrations.summary: At Yarmook, Ikrama bin Abu Jahal and about four hundred Muslims pledged to fight to the death in front of Khaalid's tent, and many of them, including Diraar, were martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration while most of the four hundred men were martyred, some of them survived. Amongst them was Hadhrat Diraar bin Azwar (RA). The next morning, Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: After Yarmook, Khaalid bin Waleed tended the badly wounded Ikrama and his son Amr, and said that Allaah had blessed the Muslims with martyrs although Umar had said they would not be martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari and Hadhrat Maysara narrate that Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir was fighting in the Battle of Siffeen but was not being martyred. He then approached…
narrations.summary: At Siffeen, Ammaar bin Yaasir asked Ali why he had not yet been martyred, drank the milk he had been told would be his last drink, and fought until he was martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sinaan Duwali (RA) who was a Sahabi reports that he saw Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) call to his slave to bring him something to drink. The slave brought a…
narrations.summary: Abu Sinaan Duwali saw Ammaar bin Yaasir ask for milk, drink it, and say he would soon meet the Prophet and his companions.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf narrates that during the Battle of Siffeen, which was the day when Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) was martyred, he heard…
narrations.summary: At Siffeen, Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan heard Ammaar bin Yaasir say he would meet Allaah and the damsels of Jannah, and recalled the Prophet's words that the milk would be his last provision.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates, "1 came to (my brother) Baraa bin Maalik while he was singing something. I said, 'Allaah has given you something (the Qur'aan) that is better…
narrations.summary: Anas describes his brother Baraa bin Maalik's courage, and how Baraa led a counter-attack in Persia after the Muslims retreated and was martyred there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaydullaah bin Abdullaah bin Utba (RA) says that the news reached him that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) said, "When Uthmaan bin Madh'oon died naturally without…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Khattaab said he had thought less of Uthmaan bin Madh'oon for dying a natural death, until he realised that even the best of people die naturally.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once asked, "O people! Who is the bravest person?" "You are, O Ameerul Mu'mineen," the people submitted. Hadhrat Ali (RA) then said, "Although I have…
narrations.summary: Ali said that Abu Bakr was the bravest of people, having stood guard over the Prophet with a drawn sword during the Battle of Badr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) says, "I know of no person who did not make Hijrah secretly except for Umar bin Khattaab. When he decided to make Hijrah, he hung his…
narrations.summary: Ali said that Umar bin Khattaab alone made Hijrah openly, with sword on his neck and bow on his shoulder, daring the Quraysh to stop him.

narrations.excerpt: The Poem of Hadhrat Ali (RA) after the Battle of Uhud Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that after the Battle of Uhud, Hadhrat Ali (RA) came home to Hadhrat Faatima (RA) and…
narrations.summary: After Uhud, Ali asked Faatima to take his sword and recited verses; the Prophet praised Sahal bin Hunayf, Abu Dujaana and Ibn Simma for their fighting, and Jibra'eel said Ali was from him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that after the Battle of Uhud, Hadhrat Ali (RA) came home to Hadhrat Faatima (RA) and said, "O Faatima! Take this flawless…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that after Uhud Ali brought his sword to Faatima, and the Prophet said that Sahal bin Hunayf and Abu Dujaana Simaak bin Harasha had also fought well.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaydullaah bin Ka'b bin Maalik is says that during the Battle of Khandaq, Amr bin Abd Wadd donned himself recognisable so that his presence should be noticed by…
narrations.summary: Ubaydullaah bin Ka'b reports that at Khandaq Ali invited Amr bin Abd Wadd to Allaah, His Rasool and Islaam, and when Amr refused and taunted him, Ali fought and killed him in single combat.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Ibn Is'haaq states that Amr bin Abd Wadd was covered in armour when he stepped forward and called, "Who will fight me?" Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib stood up…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Abd Wadd challenged the Muslims three times; Ali accepted despite the Prophet's caution, and after a fierce exchange killed him.

narrations.excerpt: "By his foolish judgement, he worshipped stones while by my correct judgement, I worship the Rabb of Muhammad ﷺ When I returned, I left him lying on the ground Like a…
narrations.summary: After killing Amr bin Abd Wadd, Ali recited verses, returned to the Prophet, and explained to Umar why he had not taken Amr's armour.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salama bin Akwa (RA) narrates a lengthy Hadith in which he makes mention of the Sahabah (RA) returning from fighting the Banu Fazaara. They had hardly stayed (in…
narrations.summary: Salama bin Akwa tells of the Khaybar expedition, where Aamir was killed in a fall of his own sword, and of Marhab coming out with a challenge.

narrations.excerpt: "All of Khaybar knows that I am Aamir A well-armed hero who throws himself in the thick of battle" The two men exchanged blows with their swords. When Marhab's sword got…
narrations.summary: Aamir accidentally wounded himself fatally with his own sword in his duel with Marhab; the Prophet gave the flag to Ali, cured his eyes with saliva, and Ali killed Marhab.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Raafi (RA) who was the freed slave of Rasulullaah ﷺ narrates that they marched with Hadhrat Ali iP to Khaybar, where Rasulullaah ﷺ sent him ahead with the…
narrations.summary: Abu Raafi, in Ali's party at Khaybar, describes Ali tearing a fortress door off to use as a shield, a door that a group of eight could not turn over afterwards.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that during the Battle of Khaybar, Hadhrat Ali lifted up the door of a fortress, which the Muslims used to climb over the walls. This led to…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that Ali lifted a fortress door at Khaybar so the Muslims could climb the walls, and that later forty men could not lift it back.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that seventy men had to exert themselves before they were able to put the door back on its place. Yet another narration from Hadhrat Jaabir bin…
narrations.summary: Three reports: Ali lifted the Khaybar door, Jaabir bin Samura gave a variant of it, and Talha recited verses at Uhud praising Zubayr's sword and defending the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib (RA) says that the first person to draw a sword for the pleasure of Allaah was Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awwaam (RA). He was in- Makkah one day when…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Zubayr bin Awwaam was the first to draw a sword for Allaah, going out in Makkah with it when he heard the Prophet had been killed, and the Prophet prayed for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that after accepting Islaam, Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awwaam once heard a whisper from Shaytaan stating that Rasulullaah had been captured. Although…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that as a boy of twelve, Zubayr heard a rumour that the Prophet had been captured, drew his sword and went to find him in Makkah; the Prophet prayed for him and his sword.

narrations.excerpt: Ibn Is'haaq narrates that Talha bin Abu Talha Abdari bore the flag of the Mushrikeen during the Battle of Uhud. When he called for someone to challenge him to a duel, the…
narrations.summary: At Uhud, Zubayr accepted Talha Abdari's challenge, leapt onto his camel, killed him with his own sword, and was praised by the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Ibn Is'haaq narrates that during the Battle of Khandaq, Naufal bin Abdullaah bin Mughiera Makhzoomi stepped ahead of the ranks of the Mushrikeen and issued a challenge…
narrations.summary: During the Battle of Khandaq, Zubayr answered Naufal Makhzoomi's challenge and split him in two with one blow, then returned reciting verses that defend the Nabi.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asmaa bint Abu Bakr (RA) narrates that a fully-armed man from the Mushrikeen advanced (from the ranks of the enemy) and climbed on top of a high place. He then…
narrations.summary: Asmaa bint Abu Bakr reports that at the Prophet's word Zubayr took on a mushrik who had challenged from a height, and killed him after he fell into the ditch.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) says, "During the Battle of Khandaq, myself and Umar bin Abu Salama were put with the women and children in a fortress (because we were…
narrations.summary: At Khandaq, Abdullaah bin Zubayr, a boy kept with the women and children in a fortress, describes watching his father Zubayr fight, and his father's reply.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) says that during the Battle of Yarmook, the Sahabah said to Hadhrat Zubayr (RA), "Will you not lead an attack so that we may join you?" Hadhrat Zubayr…
narrations.summary: At Yarmook, Zubayr broke through the enemy alone, was wounded on both sides of his old Badr wound, and left his ten-year-old son Abdullaah in the care of a companion.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when the Sahabah (RA) approached Hadhrat Zubayr with the same request a second time, he complied and did as he ( 1 ) ibn Jareer, as quoted…
narrations.summary: When the Sahabah asked Zubayr a second time to lead an attack, he complied as he had the first time.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zuhri reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent an expedition to a place called Raabigh that was situated on one end of Hijaaz. Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas was also…
narrations.summary: At Raabigh, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas defended the Muslims with arrows and was the first to shoot an arrow in the path of Allaah, recalling it in verse.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Shihaab narrates that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) killed three people with a single arrow during the Battle of Uhud. When the Mushrikeen first shot the…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas killed three men with one returned arrow at Uhud, and at Badr fought as effectively as a cavalryman while on foot.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) says that during the Battle of Badr, Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) fought with Rasulullaah ﷺ in the roles of both cavalry and…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that at Badr Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas fought alongside the Prophet both as cavalry and as infantry.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haarith Taymi narrates that during the Battle of Badr, Hadhrat Hamza bin Abdil Muttalib distinguished himself by wearing ostrich feathers. One of the Mushrikeen…
narrations.summary: Hamza bin Abdil Muttalib wore ostrich feathers at Badr, and the Mushrikeen said he had carried out all the major offensives against them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) says that Umayyah bin Khalaf once asked him, "O Abdul Ilaa! Who was the man who marked his chest with ostrich feathers during the…
narrations.summary: Umayyah bin Khalaf asked Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf who had marked himself with ostrich feathers at Badr, and on hearing it was Hamza, said Hamza had carried out all the major offensives against them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) narrates that as they were returning from the Battlefield of Uhud, Rasulullaah ﷺ could not find Hadhrat Hamza (RA). Someone said, "I saw…
narrations.summary: After Uhud, the Prophet searched for Hamza, wept over his mutilated body, had a cloth laid over it, and declared him the leader of the martyrs on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ja'far bin Amr bin Umayyah Dhamri says that it was during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) when he and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Adi bin Khiyaar went out. He…
narrations.summary: Wahshi tells how he killed Hamza at Uhud to win his freedom, later came to the Prophet in Madinah to accept Islaam, and at Yamaamah killed Musaylama with the same spear.

narrations.excerpt: A similar narration of Bukhari also narrated by Hadhrat Ja'far bin Amr adds that when the armies formed their rows for the battle, Sibaa stepped forward and said, "Is…
narrations.summary: A variant report of Wahshi's account: Sibaa stepped forward to challenge the Muslims, and Hamza answered and killed him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that during the Battle of Taa'if, Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Handhala bin Rabee (RA) to the people of Taa'if. However, when Hadhrat Handhala…
narrations.summary: At Taa'if, Handhala bin Rabee was captured by the people of Taa'if, and Abbaas bin Abdil Muttalib, answering the Prophet's call, snatched him back despite a barrage of stones.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Ramaan bin Auf (RA) says, "As I stood in file during the Battle of Badr, I looked to my right and left and saw two boys from the Ansaar who were very young…
narrations.summary: At Badr, two young Ansaar asked Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf to point out Abu Jahal, killed him, and the Prophet gave his possessions to Mu'aadh bin Amr bin Jamooh, whose arm had been cut off in the fight.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dujaana (RA) Takes a Sword from Rasulullaah ﷺ and Fulfils its Rights During the Battle of Uhud Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ took hold of a…
narrations.summary: Abu Dujaana takes the Prophet's sword at Uhud on condition of fulfilling its rights and fights bravely with it, as reported by Anas and then Zubayr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) narrates, "During the Battle of Uhud, Rasulullaah ﷺ took hold of a sword and announced, "Who will take this sword with its rights.' I said, 'I shall,…
narrations.summary: Zubayr describes Abu Dujaana receiving the sword with its rights at Uhud, and how he wore a red bandanna and destroyed the enemy with the sword.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awwaam (RA) is reported to have said, "I was disappointed when I asked Rasulullaah ﷺ for the sword and he refused to give it to me, giving it to Abu…
narrations.summary: Zubayr, disappointed at not getting the sword, follows Abu Dujaana, watches him kill many enemies, and sees him turn the sword away from Hind.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Moosa bin Uqba narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ offered the sword to the Sahabah (RA) Hadhrat Umar (RA) first asked for it. When Rasulullaah ﷺ ignored him,…
narrations.summary: Umar and Zubayr ask for the sword and are refused, Abu Dujaana receives it and fulfils its rights, and Ka'b bin Maalik describes him killing a Mushrik in one blow.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qataadah bin Nu'maan (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah Wife was given a bow as a gift, which he gave to me during the Battle of Uhud. 1 used it to fire arrows in front…
narrations.summary: Qataadah bin Nu'maan loses an eye shielding the Prophet's face with his own at Uhud, and the Prophet prays that the injured eye see better than the other.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qataadah (RA) narrates, "During the Battle of Uhud, I was standing in front of Rasulullaah ﷺ, shielding Rasulullaah Wife's face with my own. Also during the…
narrations.summary: Qataadah bin Nu'maan reports standing in front of the Prophet at Uhud to shield his face, while Abu Dujaana shielded his back with arrows in his body.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salama bin Akwa (RA) narrates, "It was during the period when the Peace Treaty of Rudaybiyyah was being abided by that we returned to Madinah with Rasulullaah ﷺ.…
narrations.summary: Salama bin Akwa pursues a raiding party that had taken the Prophet's camels, kills and wounds several of them, recovers the camels, and then races an Ansaari to Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hadrad (RA) says, "I married a woman from my tribe and agreed to give her a dowry of two hundred Dirhams. I then approached Rasulullaah ﷺ for some financial…
narrations.summary: Abu Hadrad asks the Prophet for help with his dowry, is sent with two others to spy on the Jusham leader, kills him, and brings back the booty and the head, which pay his dowry.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) Breaks Nine Swords During the Battle of Mu'ta Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) says, "Nine swords broke in my hand during the Battle of Mu'ta.…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed reports that nine swords broke in his hand during the Battle of Mu'ta until only a Yemeni sword remained.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aws bin Haaritha bin Laam (RA) narrates, "There was none who hated the (Muslim) Arabs more than Hurmuz. After we had finished fighting Musaylama and his people,…
narrations.summary: Khaalid kills Hurmuz in a duel at Kaadhima, and Abu Bakr gives Khaalid Hurmuz's belongings, including a crown valued at a hundred thousand Dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Zinaad narrates that when Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) was about to pass away, he started weeping. He named the various battles he had participated in and…
narrations.summary: Abu Zinaad reports Khaalid weeping on his deathbed over his wounds, and Anas reports Baraa bin Maalik at the Battle of Yamaamah defeating Muhakkam and taking his sword.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes that Hadhrat Baraa bin Maalik (RA) said, "On the day that we fought Musaylama, I encountered a man who was called the donkey of Yamaamah. He was…
narrations.summary: Baraa bin Maalik describes fighting Musaylama's army at Yamaamah, cutting down a large warrior and breaking his sword.

narrations.excerpt: Battle of Yamaamah until they were forced to take refuge in an orchard. With them was the enemy of Allaah Musaylama. Hadhrat Baraa bin Maalik (RA) then said, "O Muslims!…
narrations.summary: At the Battle of Yamaamah, Baraa bin Maalik had himself thrown over the orchard wall, opened the gate for the Muslims, and they then killed Musaylama.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) decreed that Hadhrat Baraa bin Maalik (RA) should not be appointed as the commander of any expedition because…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports that Umar decreed Baraa bin Maalik should never be made commander of an expedition, because his fearlessness would lead others into needless danger.

narrations.excerpt: Another lengthy narration from Muhammad bin Sa'd states that after joining the Muslim army, every flank that Hadhrat Abu Mihjin (RA) attacked was defeated by the…
narrations.summary: Abu Mihjin Thaqafi fights fiercely at Qaadisiyyah and is set free by Sa'd. In a second report from Sayf, Ammaar and Haashim are martyred fighting for Ali's army against the people of Shaam.

narrations.excerpt: Yaasir.
narrations.summary: Fragment: only the word 'Yaasir' remains, so no narration can be tagged.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that during the Battle of Yamaamah, he saw Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) standing on a boulder and shouting, "O Assembly of…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that at the Battle of Yamaamah, Ammaar bin Yaasir called out to the Muslims not to flee from Jannah, and fought fiercely even with his ear cut.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami (RA) says that he participated in the Battle of Siffeen by the side of Hadhrat Ali (RA). They had appointed two men to guard Hadhrat Ali…
narrations.summary: At Siffeen beside Ali, Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami reports Ali's raids and Ammaar's call to fight for Jannah, and that Haashim bin Utba took up the banner and fought in the valley.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami (RA) says, "I noticed that (during the Battle of Siffeen) whenever Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) went into any of the valleys…
narrations.summary: In another narration, Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami says Ammaar followed Haashim bin Utba into the valleys of Siffeen, both were martyred in the attack, and Ali's army then charged as one man.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maalik bin Abdullaah Khath'ami (RA) says, "I have not seen anyone step forward (to challenge an opponent) in the Battle of Yarmook who was better than a certain…
narrations.summary: Maalik bin Abdullaah reports that at Yarmook Amr bin Ma'dikarib killed challenger after challenger, then chased the fleeing enemy and fed the people gathered in his tent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Abi Haazim (RA) reports that he was present during the Battle of Qaadisiyyah with Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) commanding the Muslim army. Hadhrat Amr bin…
narrations.summary: Several reports on Amr bin Ma'dikarib at Qaadisiyyah, Umar's reinforcements, and Nahaawand, where he turned defeat into victory until an injury took him at Rowdha.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) reports that after Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) passed away, it became very difficult for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) to be subservient to…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr refuses to submit to Yazeed, is attacked in Makkah by Hajjaaj's forces, and is martyred after refusing his mother Asmaa's advice to compromise on his Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Salama Sgl once asked the wife of Hadhrat Salama bin Hishaam bin Mughiera, "Why do I not see (your husband) Salama attend the salaah with Rasulullaah ﷺ and…
narrations.summary: Umm Salama asks why Salama bin Hishaam no longer attends the prayer with the Prophet, and learns he is shamed at home for having fled at Mu'ta.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) says, "There was a problem between my cousin and myself. However, I had no reply to give him when he provoked me by saying, 'Were you not one of…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah is taunted by his cousin for having fled at Mu'ta and has no answer to give.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "I was part of an expedition that Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched. I was amongst some of them who had retreated. (As we were returning to…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar and his companions who fled at Mu'ta return to Madinah and approach the Prophet, who tells them they are those who return to fight again and that he is their base.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "Rasulullaah once dispatched us on an expedition. When we met the enemy and were defeated in the very first…
narrations.summary: A second report of Abdullaah bin Umar and the fleeing men, in which the Prophet reassures them that he is their base, with an added line from the narration of Aswad.

narrations.excerpt: A similar narration of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reads, "We then said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ We are those who have fled.' He said, 'You are only those who shall return…
narrations.summary: A third version of the same encounter, in which the men admit they had planned to sail to a foreign land, and the Prophet tells them not to do so.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that as Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zaid (RA) was passing the door of her room, she heard Hadhrat Umar JsS-SsSsi call out, "Let us hear the news, O…
narrations.summary: Umar, hearing from Abdullaah bin Zaid of the defeat at the Bridge, reassures the fleeing Muhaajireen and Ansaar that he is their base to return to.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Husayn and others report that Hadhrat Mu'aadh Qaari (RA) from the Banu Najjaar tribe was amongst those who were present and had…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh Qaari weeps over a verse on fleeing the battlefield, and Umar tells him he is the base to which he can retreat and regroup.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla (RA) says that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubayd was a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ who was with the army that was defeated on the day that Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Umar offers Sa'd bin Ubayd Qaari the chance to redeem his flight by going to Shaam, but Sa'd returns to the battlefield he fled from at Qaadisiyyah, where he is martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jabala bin Haaritha (RA) narrates that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ was not participating in a battle, he would give his weapons to Hadhrat Usaama or to Hadhrat Ali…
narrations.summary: When the Prophet is not himself fighting, he hands his weapons to Usaama or to Ali to take into battle.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a youngster from the Banu Aslam tribe said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I wish to proceed in Jihaad but do not have any wealth with which to make the…
narrations.summary: A youth from Banu Aslam asks the Prophet for means to join Jihaad, and the Prophet sends him to an Ansaari who had prepared but fallen ill, and who gives him all he had prepared.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Mas'ood Ansaari (RA) narrates that a man came to Rasulullaah and said, "Please provide transport for me because my animal has died." "I have nothing to give…
narrations.summary: A man whose animal died asks the Prophet for transport; the Prophet has none, and a Sahabi refers the man to someone who can help, and the Prophet says the one who points to good has the same reward.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was once embarking on an expedition, he said, "O assembly of Muhaajireen and Ansaar! There are many of…
narrations.summary: The Prophet asks the Muhaajireen and Ansaar to take on two or three poor brothers each for an expedition, and Jaabir describes sharing his mount with the men he took on.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa (RA) narrates, "After Rasulullaah ﷺ had announced the pending march to Tabook, I just went to my family and had returned when the first group of…
narrations.summary: Waathila bin Asqa hires an old Ansaari's help to reach the Tabook march in exchange for his share of booty, and the Ansaari returns the camels, wanting only the reward.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Providing a rope (to someone proceeding) in the path of Allaah is more beloved to me than performing Hajj after Hajj."
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that providing a rope for someone going out in Allaah's path is more beloved to him than Hajj after Hajj.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Auf bin Maalik (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ sent me on a military expedition, a man came up to me and said, 'I shall go with you on condition that you grant me…
narrations.summary: Awf bin Maalik hires a volunteer for an expedition for a fixed payment of three Dinaars on condition of a share of booty, and the account breaks off as he asks the Prophet about the booty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Daylami narrates that Hadhrat Ya'la bin Munya (RA) said, "I was an old man with no servant when Rasulullaah ﷺ announced that an expedition was to…
narrations.summary: Ya'la bin Munya hired a man for an expedition for a fixed three dinaars, and the Prophet ruled that these three dinaars were all the hired man would receive.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maymoona bint Sa'd (RA) reports that she once asked, "O Rasulullaah Inform us about a person who cannot proceed in the path of Allaah but sponsors the means by…
narrations.summary: Maymoona bint Sa'd asked the Prophet whether the reward goes to the one who funds jihaad or to the one who goes out, and he said the funder is rewarded for his wealth and the one who goes out for his intention.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Rabee'ah (RA) narrates that a man once came to Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib with his son whom he intended to send on an expedition in his place. Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: A man brought his son to Ali bin Abi Taalib to send on an expedition in his place, and Ali said he preferred the judgement of an adult to the fighting of a youngster.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) Admonishes a Youngster Who Begged from people so that he Could Proceed in the path of Allaah Hadhrat Naafi narrates that a robust and healthy youngster…
narrations.summary: Umar hires out a youth who begged for money to go on Jihaad to an Ansaari for work, and later gives him his savings and leaves the choice of going or staying to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that someone asked, "Have you heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say anything about horses?" "Yes," he replied, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood relays the Prophet's saying that horses carry good until the Day of Qiyaamah, and that one may buy and borrow for Jihaad with trust in Allaah, paying from the booty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ walked with them up to Baqee Gharqad when he sent them off on an expedition. He then said to them, "Proceed…
narrations.summary: The Prophet walks with an expedition to Baqee Gharqad and prays for them, and Abdullaah bin Yazeed reports the words of the Prophet's farewell prayer.

narrations.excerpt: In a narration discussing the dispatching of Hadhrat Usaama (RA)'s army, Hadhrat Hasan (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) left his home to meet the army. As he saw…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Abu Bakr walks beside Usaama's army as it departs, refusing to let Usaama dismount, and asks that Umar be left behind with him in Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) dispatched several armies to Shaam, he walked with Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan who was in command of…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr walks with Yazeed bin Abi Sufyaan as he sees off an army for Shaam, saying that walking in the path counts for them, and Jaabir Ru'ayni reports the same custom.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir Ru'ayni (RA) narrates that as Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was walking as he saw an army off. He then said to them, "All praises are for Allaah Who has allowed…
narrations.summary: Jaabir Ru'ayni reports that Abu Bakr, seeing an army off, said that those who help prepare it, send it off and make du'aa for it share in the reward of going out in the path of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaahid reports that as he was proceeding in the path of Allaah, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) came to see them off. As Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar was about to…
narrations.summary: Mujaahid recalls that Abdullaah bin Umar came to see off men going out in Jihaad and entrusted them to Allaah, quoting the Prophet's saying that what is entrusted to Allaah is protected.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saa'ib bin Yazeed (RA) says, "The people (of Madinah) came to welcome Rasulullaah ﷺ when he returned from the expedition to Tabook. I also met him along with…
narrations.summary: Saa'ib bin Yazeed, as a boy, went out with the people of Madinah to Thaniyyatul Wadaa to welcome the Prophet back from Tabook.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) says that it was during Ramadhaan that they marched with Rasulullaah ﷺ for the Battle of Badr and for the conquest of Makkah.
narrations.summary: Umar says the Prophet marched to Badr and to the conquest of Makkah during Ramadhaan.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "We marched on two military expeditions with Rasulullaah ﷺ during Ramadhaan; the Battle of Badr and the conquest of…
narrations.summary: Umar and Ibn Abbaas report the numbers at Badr, that the Sahabah did not fast on those two Ramadhaan campaigns, and that the Prophet left Madinah on the tenth of Ramadhaan with Abu Ruhm Kulthoom as deputy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) has also narrated that Rasulullaah ﷺ proceeded in Ramadhaan to conquer Makkah and fasted until he reached Kudayd.
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that the Prophet set out in Ramadhaan to conquer Makkah and kept fasting until he reached Kudayd.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Rasulullaah ﷺ left to conquer Makkah during Ramadhaan, he was fasting until the road passed by Qudayd at midday. The Sahabah (RA) were…
narrations.summary: On the march to Makkah during Ramadhaan the Prophet drank water in full view at midday so that the thirsty Sahabah would follow him in breaking their fast.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "No strange (non-Mahram) man should ever be alone with a strange (non-Mahram) woman and no woman…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports the Prophet's ruling that a non-Mahram man and woman must not be alone together and a woman must not travel without a Mahram, and that he told a Sahabi whose wife had gone for Hajj to perform Hajj with her instead of joining an expedition.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ka'b (RA) narrates that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ returned from a journey during the morning, he would first enter the Masjid and perform two Rakaahs salaah before…
narrations.summary: Ka'b reports that on returning from a journey in the morning the Prophet would first enter the Masjid and pray two rak'ahs.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) states that he accompanied Rasulullaah ﷺ on a journey and when they returned, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "Enter the Masjid and…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that when he returned with the Prophet from a journey, the Prophet told him to enter the Masjid and pray two rak'ahs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) has also narrated that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once returned to Madinah, he slaughtered a cow or a camel. Another narration quotes that Hadhrat Jaabir (RA)…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that the Prophet had a cow slaughtered for the Sahabah on the way back, and on reaching Madinah sent him to pray two rak'ahs before paying him the price of his camel.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) Participated in the Banu Mustaliq expedition Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ embarked on an expedition, he would draw lots between…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha recounts how she was left behind on the Banu Mustaliq expedition, was brought back by Safwaan bin Mu'attal, and how slander spread through the army and Madinah, with the Prophet hearing of it and consulting Ali, Usaama and Bareerah.

narrations.excerpt: Another detaili verses of my ii to Rasulullaah him and shal innocence.' All It was m the sland (My father) A! related to us a my innocence never support revealed the v…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha describes the revelation that confirmed her innocence, the Prophet wiping sweat from his face and giving her the good news, and his order that Mistah, Hassaan and Hamna be given the prescribed punishment.

narrations.excerpt: Another detailed narration quoted that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) added, "(After the verses of my innocence were revealed) My mother said to me, 'Stand up and go to Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that she refused her mother's urging to thank the Prophet, that Abu Bakr stopped supporting Mistah until the verse of forgiveness was revealed, and that he then resumed his support.

narrations.excerpt: A lady from the Banu Ghifaar tribe narrates, "Together with a few women from the Banu Ghifaar, I approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and requested, 'O Rasulullaah We want to…
narrations.summary: A woman of Banu Ghifaar went out with the Prophet to Khaybar to nurse the wounded; after she first menstruated he told her how to clean the saddle, and after the victory he gave her a necklace that she kept until her death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Humayd bin Hilaal narrates that a man from the Banu Tufaawa tribe often passed by them and would narrate Ahadeeth to their tribe. He once narrated, "I arrived in…
narrations.summary: Humayd bin Hilaal reports that the Prophet described a woman who lost a goat and her needle on a journey, prayed to Allaah, and had both restored by the next morning.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once visited Hadhrat Ummu Haraam bint Milhaan, where he lay down to sleep. He then woke up smiling. When she asked him why…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet dreamt of his Ummah sailing the sea in the path of Allaah, and that Ummu Haraam was promised a place in the first group; she later went on a naval expedition and died after a fall from her animal.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) narrates that several women from the Ansaar proceeded on military expeditions with Rasulullaah ﷺ, where they would provide water for the ill and…
narrations.summary: Ummu Sulaym reports that women of the Ansaar marched with the Prophet on expeditions to give water to the sick and treat the wounded.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) and other women of the Ansaar would march with Rasulullaah ﷺ on military expeditions. Their function was to…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Ummu Sulaym and other women of the Ansaar marched with the Prophet on expeditions to provide water and tend the wounded.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rubayyi Bint Mu'awwidh (RA) reports that when they (women) were with Rasulullaah ﷺ on military expeditions, they would provide water (for the soldiers), treat the…
narrations.summary: Rubayyi bint Mu'awwidh reports that when women were with the Prophet on expeditions they gave water to the soldiers, treated the wounded and brought back the dead.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration of Bukhari quotes that she said, "We (women) would proceed on military expeditions with Rasulullaah ﷺ where we would fetch water for the people, serve…
narrations.summary: Rubayyi bint Mu'awwidh, quoted by Bukhari, describes women fetching water and bringing back the dead and wounded, and Ummu Atiyya says she went on seven expeditions cooking and nursing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Atiyya (RA) who was from the Ansaar says, "I accompanied (the army of) Rasulullaah ﷺ on seven military expeditions. I would stay Behind in their camp…
narrations.summary: Ummu Atiyya, who went on seven expeditions with the Prophet's army, describes how she cooked, nursed the wounded and tended the sick in the camp.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Layla Ghifaariyya (RA) narrates, "I used to proceed on military expeditions with Rasulullaah ﷺ to nurse the wounded."
narrations.summary: Layla Ghifaariyya reports that she went on expeditions with the Prophet to nurse the wounded.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "When the Muslims suffered some defeat during the Battle of Uhud and were unable to stay with Rasulullaah ﷺ, I saw Aa'isha the daughter of Abu…
narrations.summary: Anas saw Aa'isha and Ummu Sulaym carrying water to the wounded at Uhud; Tha'laba reports that Umar gave a cloth to Ummu Saleet, who had sewn water-skins at Uhud, rather than to Ummu Kulthoom.

narrations.excerpt: The grandmother of Hadhrat Hashraj bin Ziyaad (RA) narrates that women also accompanied Rasulullaah ﷺ for the Battle of Khaybar. In her narration she mentions that when…
narrations.summary: A grandmother of Hashraj bin Ziyaad reports that women went with the Prophet to Khaybar to weave ropes, nurse the wounded and give barley porridge, and Zuhri adds that women gave water to the fighters.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Abu Zaid Ansaari (RA) narrates from Hadhrat Ummu Sa'd bint Sa'd bin Rabee that she used to go to her maternal aunt Hadhrat Ummu Ammaara and ask her to…
narrations.summary: Ummu Sa'd reports from Ummu Ammaara that at Uhud, when the Muslims were losing, she fought close to the Prophet, took many wounds, and struck Ibn Qami'a, who had wounded her, with her sword.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat umaarah bint Ghaziyyah narrates that during the Battle of Uhud, Hadhrat Ummu Ammaara (RA) killed a Mushrik horseman. Another narration quotes that Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Umaarah bint Ghaziyyah reports that at Uhud Ummu Ammaara killed a Mushrik horseman; Umar reports the Prophet saying he saw her fighting in his defence on every side, and Umar sends her a valuable shawl over Safiyya bint Ubayd.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hishaam narrates from his father that when the Muslims were being defeated during the Battle of Uhud, Hadhrat Safiyya (RA) arrived with a spear in her hand to…
narrations.summary: Hishaam, reporting from his father, says that when the Muslims were losing at Uhud Safiyya came with a spear to drive them back, and the Prophet told Zubayr to look after his mother.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abbaad narrates that (during the Battle of Khandaq), Hadhrat Safiyya bint Abdul Muttalib was in a fortress called Faari, which belonged to Hadhrat Hassaan bin…
narrations.summary: Safiyya bint Abdul Muttalib reports that during the Battle of the Trench she killed a Jewish man who was circling the fort where the women and children were, because Hassaan would not do it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narration during the Battle of Hunayn, Hadhrat Abu Talha came laughing to Rasulullaah ﷺ. He said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Have you seen (my wife) Ummu Sulaym…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that at Hunayn Ummu Sulaym kept a dagger ready to stab any Mushrik who came near her, and the Prophet asked her about it and smiled, while Abu Talha laughed about it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) that during the Battle of Hunayn, Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym took a dagger and kept it with her. When Hadhrat Abu Talha saw her with it, he said to Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Ummu Sulaym kept a dagger with her at Hunayn to deal with any Mushrik who came near her, and that the Prophet smiled at her answer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhaajir narrates that Hadhrat Asmaa bint Yazeed bin Sakan (RA) was the cousin of Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA). Using a tent peg, she killed nine Romans during…
narrations.summary: Muhaajir reports that Asmaa bint Yazeed killed nine Romans with a tent peg at the Battle of Yarmook.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Kabsha (RA) belonged to the Banu Qudhaa'a clan of the Udhra tribe. When she once requested permission from Rasulullaah ﷺ to participate in a particular…
narrations.summary: Ummu Kabsha asked the Prophet for permission to join an expedition to nurse the wounded and give water; he refused, saying he feared it would become a regular practice, and told her to stay at home.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that a woman once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I have been sent to represent all the women before you.…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports a woman's question to the Prophet about women's reward compared with men's jihaad, and his answer that obedience to a husband and fulfilling his rights equals it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that when the Battle of Uhud was to take place, a woman gave her son a sword. Because he was unable to carry it, she tied it securely to his arm…
