narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that a woman gave her young son a sword to fight at Uhud, the Prophet directed the boy's attacks, and when the boy was wounded the Prophet asked if he was frightened.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Umayr bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) back as they were proceeding to Badr because Rasulullaah ﷺ thought…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that the Prophet sent his brother Umayr back from Badr as too young, that Umayr wept until he was allowed to go, and that Sa'd tied knots in Umayr's sword belt to fit him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) says, "Before we presented ourselves to Rasulullaah ﷺ for the Battle of Badr, I noticed my brother Umayr bin Abi Waqqaas hiding from…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that his brother Umayr hid to avoid being sent back from Badr, was allowed to go after weeping, and was martyred at sixteen.

narrations.excerpt: lbn Is'haaq reports the historic sermon that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) delivered in the orchard of the Banu Saa'idah. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "It is not permissible for…
narrations.summary: Ibn Is'haaq reports Abu Bakr's sermon at the orchard of the Banu Saa'idah that two leaders for the Muslims leads to dissension, the abandonment of the Sunnah and the rise of bid'ah.

narrations.excerpt: In the narration discussing the scenario before the pledge of allegiance was "taken at the hand of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), Hadhrat Saalim bin Ubayd states that someone…
narrations.summary: Umar says two swords cannot share one sheath, and Abu Dharr, after criticising Uthmaan's four rak'ahs, quotes the Prophet's warning against disgracing rulers and the three duties owed to them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "O people! You should hold fast to obedience to your leader and preserving your unity because unity is the rope of Allaah…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood urged the people to hold to unity, described coming poverty and the signs before the Last Day, and reported that the earth will bring forth its hidden treasures.

narrations.excerpt: A man related that they once took some things for Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA). However, when they reached Rabdha (the place where he lived) and asked for him, he was not…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr criticised Uthmaan for praying four rakaahs at Mina, then rebuked a man who reported it to him, saying that causing division is worse, and quoted the Prophet on not disgracing rulers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qataadah narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Abu Bakr ig and Hadhrat. Umar (RA) all performed two Rakaahs (Fardh) salaah in Makkah and in Mina. Hadhrat Uthmaan…
narrations.summary: Qataada reports that Uthmaan began praying four rakaahs at Mina, and that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood, though he recited Innaa lillaah, prayed four behind him, saying that causing division was worse.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said (to the people), "Continue doing as you have been doing (during the terms of the previous Khalifahs) because I hate disunity. Either people…
narrations.summary: Ali says he dislikes disunity and advises people to keep the practice of the earlier caliphs; he tells Ibnul Kawwaa that the Sunnah is the Prophet's way and unity is the consensus of the truth, and Ibn Seereen says narrations from extreme groups attributed to Ali are false.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) says that (after hearing about the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) came on his animal from the Sunh district of Madinah, He…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports that Abu Bakr came after the Prophet's death, uncovered his face, kissed him, rejected Umar's claim that he had not died, and gave a sermon quoting the verse that Muhammad is only a Messenger.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) exclaimed, "is this verse in the Qur'aan? By Allaah, to this day, 1 -had never known that it was ever revealed (1 had completely forgotten about it)!"…
narrations.summary: Umar exclaims that he had forgotten the Quranic verse about the Prophet's death, and Abu Bakr recites verses stating that all will die and only Allaah remains.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) continued; "Allaah had given a lifetime to Rasulullaah and kept him alive until he established the Deen of Allaah, made the commands of Allaah…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr tells the people that the Prophet completed his mission, that whoever worshipped Allaah should know Allaah lives, that whoever worshipped Muhammad should know he has died, and that the Qur'aan is a light and a cure.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that he heard the closing sermon of Hadhrat Umar as he sat on the pulpit the day after Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) sat in…
narrations.summary: Anas reports Umar's sermon the day after the Prophet's death urging the people to pledge to Abu Bakr, and Abu Ubaydah saying he will not step ahead of the one the Prophet made imam of salaah; a second statement by Abu Ubaydah calls Abu Bakr the second of the two in the cave.

narrations.excerpt: Imaam Zuhri narrates from Hadhrat Anas (RA) that the day after the Sahabah had pledged their allegiance to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) in the orchard, Hadhrat Abu Bakr is sat…
narrations.summary: Imaam Zuhri relates from Anas that the day after the pledge in the orchard, Umar told the people he had been wrong to deny the Prophet's death, and Abu Bakr then addressed the people, asking them to obey him only while he obeys Allaah and His Rasool.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says that he used to teach the Qur'aan to (Ij Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said this because of his humility. Otherwise, the Ulema of the Ummah…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas relates Umar's warning at Mina and Madinah against anyone who calls the pledge to Abu Bakr a hasty affair, and then the events of the Saqifah: the Ansaar gathered around Sa'd bin Ubaadah, Abu Bakr spoke for the Quraysh, and Umar gave his hand to Abu Bakr first, after which the people followed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates that what actually happened after Rasulullaah passed away was that someone came and informed them that the Ansaar had gathered with Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Umar relates what happened at the Saqifah: the Ansaar gathered with Sa'd bin Ubaadah, Umar and Abu Bakr went to them, Abu Bakr named Umar and Abu Ubaydah, Umar gave his hand to Abu Bakr, and later reports tell of Abu Ubaydah refusing to step ahead of Abu Bakr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat uthrnaan bin Affaan (RA) said, "Abu Bakr is the most worthy of it (Khilaafah) because he was 'the second of the two' and the close companion of Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan bin Affaan says Abu Bakr is the most worthy of the Khilaafah, being the second of the two and the Prophet's close companion.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) declines to Accept the post of Khalifah and the statements of Hadhrat Ali and Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) he is most Worthy of the Position Hadhrat Sa'd bin…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr at first declines the Khilaafah, Ali and Zubayr object to being excluded from consultation, and Umar and Khaalid bin Sa'eed dispute the pledge to Abu Bakr.

narrations.excerpt: Another similar narration adds about the Munaafiqeen, "Even though their homes and bodies are close by, they are people who deceive each other. We have pledged our…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abjar reports that after the pledge to Abu Bakr, Abu Sufyaan went to Ali and offered to fill Madinah with cavalry and infantry against him, and Ali replied that Abu Bakr was the most worthy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Murra bin Tayyib narrates that Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan bin Harb (RA) approached Hadhrat Ali (RA) to say, "How is it that leadership has gone to that clan of the…
narrations.summary: Murra bin Tayyib reports that Abu Sufyaan offered to fill Madinah against Abu Bakr and Ali refused, and Sakhar relates how Umar tore up the silk cloak of Khaalid bin Sa'eed and argued with him about the Khilaafah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Khaalid (RA) who was the daughter of Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sa'eed narrates that her father returned from Yemen only after the Muslims had already pledged their…
narrations.summary: Ummu Khaalid reports that her father Khaalid bin Sa'eed delayed his pledge to Abu Bakr for three months, then pledged, and later prayed for Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once drew his sword and rode his animal towards Dhu Qassah, Hadhrat Ali (RA) took hold of the animal's reins and…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that Abu Bakr drew his sword to ride out to Dhu Qassah alone, and Ali stopped him by recalling the Prophet's words at Uhud.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once said, "O people! You may think that I assumed the Saaji, as quoted in Ksmzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Fg.143). Daar Qutni has also reported the narration,…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr tells the people he never sought the Khilaafah for ambition, returns the allegiance to them, and asks them to give it to whoever is just.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tsa bin Atiyya reports that the day after the Sahabah (RA) had pledged their allegiance to Hadhrat Abu Bakr isi'S he stood up to deliver a lecture. He said, "O…
narrations.summary: After the pledge, Abu Bakr tells the people to withdraw it and choose the best of them, they affirm he is best, and he counsels them on honest income and correction of leaders.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Jahhaaf narrates that for three days after people pledged their allegiance to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), he kept his door locked and on each day he would come…
narrations.summary: Abul Jahhaaf reports that Abu Bakr locked his door for three days after the pledge and then complained to Umar that judging was a burden, and Umar cites the Prophet's reward for a judge who errs after striving.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Raafi ibn Abu Raafi (RA) narrated, "After the people had appointed Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) as Khalifah, I said (to myself), 'This is the very man who told me never…
narrations.summary: Raafi ibn Abu Raafi relates that after the people appointed Abu Bakr as Khalifah, he confronted him about his earlier advice never to lead even two people, and Abu Bakr explained that he accepted the post to protect the Deen.

narrations.excerpt: A man from the family of Rabee'ah says thai news reached him that Hadhrat Abu Bakr sat at home in grief after he was appointed as Khalifah. When Hadhral Umar is! came lo…
narrations.summary: A man of the family of Rabee'ah reports that Abu Bakr sat at home grieving after becoming Khalifah and blamed Umar for forcing him into it, and Umar answered with the hadith that a judge who strives earns a double reward if right and a single reward if wrong.

narrations.excerpt: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said the following to him on his deathbed, "I have no regrets about anything…
narrations.summary: On his deathbed Abu Bakr tells Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf his regrets, including not appointing Abu Ubaydah or Umar and not asking the Prophet about the succession.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Salama bin Abdur Rahmaan and others narrate that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr grew extremely ill and was close to death, he called for Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf…
narrations.summary: On his deathbed Abu Bakr consults Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf and Uthmaan about Umar, then has Uthmaan write Umar's name as successor.

narrations.excerpt: "In the name of Allaah the Most Kind, the Most Merciful. The following is the arrangement made by Abu Bakr bin Abu Quhaafa during his last moments in the world as he…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr dictated his will appointing Umar as successor, Uthmaan wrote and sealed it, the people pledged to Umar, and Abu Bakr prayed for them; Hasan reports that Abu Bakr first asked the people to choose and then named Umar through Uthmaan's advice.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Ubaydullaah bin Abdullaah bin Umar narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was about to pass away, he summoned Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan and…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan bin Ubaydullaah reports that Uthmaan bin Affaan named Umar in Abu Bakr's will, and Talha objects, to which Abu Bakr replies that he fears Allaah's questioning.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that when (her father) Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was on his deathbed, he appointed Hadhrat umar (RA) as his successor. Hadhrat Alt (RA) and…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that Abu Bakr named Umar as his successor, and when Ali and Talha question him he replies that he knows Umar best and will answer to Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat zaid bin Haarith (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was on his deathbed, he sent for Hadhrat Umar (RA) to appoint him as his successor. Some people…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Haarith reports that Abu Bakr wanted to appoint Umar, some people objected that Umar is harsh, and Abu Bakr replies that he fears Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that when Abu Lu'lu'ah attacked Hadhrat Umar (RA), he stabbed him twice with his spear. Hadhrat umar then thought thai he had…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports Umar's assassination by Abu Lu'lu'ah, Umar's consultation with Ibn Abbaas, his naming of six men to choose the next Khalifah, and his qualities for leadership.

narrations.excerpt: In his narration concerning the assassination of Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Amr bin Maymoon also says that Hadhrat Umar (RA) told his son Hadhrat Abdullaah to check on…
narrations.summary: Ibn Sa'd reports Umar's instructions about settling his debts, his request to Aisha to be buried beside the Prophet and Abu Bakr, his six-man consultative assembly and the roles he set for his son, and Abu Bakr's last sermon naming Umar as the best to succeed him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "I served Umar in a manner that no other member of his family served him. 1 was also very informal with him in a manner that no…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas describes Umar's sigh and the qualities Umar named for a khalifah: strong without harshness, lenient without weakness, generous without extravagance, and careful with money without miserliness.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration also from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) states, "l was sitting with Umar one day when he heaved such a sigh that I thought his ribs would crack. I…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas recounts how Umar sighed and asked whom to choose as Khalifah, mentioned Ali as a candidate and the objection that he enjoys jest, and listed the qualities a Khalifah needs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) mentioned, "I used to serve Umar and always stood in awe of him. I went to his house one day as he sat there all alone. He then heaved…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas recounts his questioning of Umar, who said that Ali had merits but that a khalifah must not compromise principles and must judge fairly even against his own people.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes Hadhrat Umar (RA) as saying, "None can shoulder this responsibility from Allaah besides a person who does not compromise on principles, who does…
narrations.summary: Umar asks whether he is a Khalifah or a king, and Salmaan, Ka'b and Ibn Abil Awjaa's report affirm he is a Khalifah who takes and spends rightfully.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked them, "Am I a king or a Khalifah?" Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) replied, "If you had ever (unlawfully) taken even a…
narrations.summary: Salmaan testifies that Umar is a khalifah and not a king, and Ka'b, citing scripture, says the prophecy he found describes Umar as a khalifah in the pattern of prophethood before kingship.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was appointed as Khalifah, he delivered a lecture to the people from the pulpit of Rasulullaah ﷺ.…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports Umar's first address as Khalifah, in which Umar explained his sternness as service to the Prophet and Abu Bakr and asked the people to advise and help him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Zaid (RA) reports that Hadhrat AH (RA), Hadhrat Uthmaan, Hadhrat Zubayr (RA), Hadhrat Talha (RA), Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf and Hadhrat Sa'd (RA)…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Zaid reports that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf was asked by Ali, Uthmaan, Zubayr, Talha and Sa'd to speak to Umar about being more lenient, and Umar explained his fear of Allaah both for leniency and for sternness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "I swear by Allaah that for the sake of Allaah my heart had become so soft that it was softer than butter and at…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports Umar's saying that for Allaah's sake his heart had become softer than butter, and at other times harder than a stone.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) became the Khalifah, someone said to him, "Some people had made an effort to ensure that this post…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that when Umar became Khalifah he was told some people had tried to block him because he was too harsh, and Umar praised Allaah for filling his heart with mercy for them and theirs with awe of him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that when Hadhrat Umar is passed away, certain members of the Quraysh had already become irritated by him. They were people whom Hadhrat Umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that Umar kept certain Quraysh confined to Madinah to protect the seat of khilaafah, that Uthmaan released them and they scattered, and the text then records Umar's and others' counsel to the Prophet on the caravan of Abu Sufyaan and on the Badr prisoners, including the revelation on ransom.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zuhri narrates that when the Muslims were suffering extreme hardship (during the Battle of Ahzaab), Rasulullaah ﷺ sent for Uyayna bin Hisn and Haarith bin Auf…
narrations.summary: Under the pressure of the Battle of the Confederates, the Prophet offers the Ghatafaan leaders a third of Madinah's produce and consults Sa'd bin Mu'aadh and Sa'd bin Ubaadah, who refuse.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Haarith once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "If you do not give us half the produce of Madinah, we shall fill her with cavalry…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports Haarith's demand for half of Madinah's produce, the Prophet's consultation with the Sa'ds and others who refuse, and a separate report from Musaddad on Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) also reports that Haarith from the Banu Ghitfaan tribe once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ with the demand, "Give us half the produce of Madinah."…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when Haarith of the Banu Ghitfaan demanded half the produce of Madinah, the Prophet consulted four leading Sa'ds, and Haarith's party answered with an accusation of betrayal.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Consults with Men of Knowledge and Insight who Constituted the Consultative Assembly During his Period and the Period of Hadhrat Umar (RA) Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Qaasim reports that Abu Bakr consulted a group of senior Muhaajireen and Ansaar on matters, and that they issued rulings in his time and in Umar's.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaydah reports that Uyayna bin Hisn and Aqra bin Haabis once approached Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) saying, "O successor of Rasulullaah ﷺ There is a barren piece of…
narrations.summary: Uyayna bin Hisn and Aqra bin Haabis ask Abu Bakr for a barren piece of land, and Umar objects that it is public property and tears up the deed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Atiyya bin Bilaal and Hadhrat Sahm bin Minjaab both narrate that Aqra and Zabarqaan approached Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and said, "Hand over to us the Kharaaj from…
narrations.summary: Aqra and Zabarqaan ask Abu Bakr for the kharaaj of Bahrain in return for a guarantee against apostasy, Umar refuses to witness and tears up the deed, and Talha is angered.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once wrote to Hadhrat Amr bin Ai Aas (RA) saying, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to consult in matters of war, so…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that Abu Bakr wrote to Amr bin al-Aas to consult people in matters of war, as the Prophet used to do, and the text cross-refers to an earlier narration about Abu Bakr consulting men of knowledge before fighting the Romans.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ja'far narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) requested Hadhrat Ali for his daughter Ummu Kulthoom's hand in marriage. Hadhrat Ali said, "I had intended to marry all…
narrations.summary: Abu Ja'far relates that Umar asked Ali for his daughter Ummu Kulthoom in marriage, Ali agreed, and Umar told the Muhaajireen in the Masjid that he wished to become the Prophet's relative as well as his companion.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa bin Yasaar reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat uthmaan used to call for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) and consult with him along with those…
narrations.summary: Umar and Uthmaan consult Ibn Abbaas on difficult matters, and Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas and Umar praise his intelligence, while Umar also consulted women when needed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad, ﷺ and Ziyaad all report that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once left Madinah and dismounted at an oasis called Siraar (3 miles from Madman) where he instructed that…
narrations.summary: At Siraar Umar consults the Muhaajireen, Ansaar and army leaders, and they agree to send another companion as commander while Umar stays in Madinah to send reinforcements.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Sallaam Baykindi narrates that even during the Period of Ignorance Hadhrat Amr bin Ma'diyakrib (RA) had achieved many feats. He became a Muslim after…
narrations.summary: Umar writes to Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reinforcing him with Amr bin Ma'diyakrib and Tulayha, who are to be consulted in military matters but not given command.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi waqqaas (RA) narrates, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, the Juhayna tribe approached him with the request, 'Now that you have arrived in our…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas recounts the first expedition in Islaam under Abdullaah bin Jahash, whose men attacked a Quraysh caravan against the Prophet's wishes, and the Prophet's rebuke over disunity.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat shihaab Ambari narrates, "I was the first to set alight the gates of Tustar when Hadhrat Ash'ari iS was struck down by an arrow. When the city was conquered,…
narrations.summary: Shihaab Ambari reports that he set fire to the gates of Tustar when Ash'ari was struck by an arrow, and was then made Ameer over ten men of his tribe after the conquest.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat limar (RA) once said, ''When there are three person travelling, they should appoint one of them as Ameer. This appointment has been commanded by Rasulullaah ﷺ.
narrations.summary: Umar says that when three people travel they should appoint one of them as Ameer, as the Prophet commanded.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched an exceptionally large expedition. Rasulullaah ﷺ made each one of them recite whatever portion of…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet asked each member of a large expedition to recite what Qur'aan they knew, and a young man named several surahs including Baqara.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched an expedition towards Yemen and appointed as their Ameer someone who was the youngest amongst them.…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan relates that the Prophet sent an expedition to Yemen under its youngest man, who was healed of a leg problem when the Prophet recited over him, and that the Prophet described the Qur'aan as like a bag filled with musk.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Muhammad ﷺ reports that it was once said to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), "O successor of Rasulullaah ﷺ why do you not give command to the veterans of…
narrations.summary: Someone asked Abu Bakr why he did not give command to the veterans of Badr, and he replied that he honours them but does not want to taint them with worldly authority.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat lmraan bin Abdullaah reports that Hadhrat ubay bin Ka'b (RA) once asked Hadhrat Umar (RA), "What is it that you do not give me command'" Hadhrat Umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: Imraan bin Abdullaah reports that Ubay bin Ka'b asked Umar why he was not given command, and Umar replied that he did not want to taint his Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haaritha bin Mudarrib narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote the following letter to them: l have sent Ammaar bin Yaasir as your Ameer and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood as…
narrations.summary: Umar writes to a group of Muslims appointing Ammaar as Ameer and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood as teacher and minister, and sends Uthmaan bin Hunayf and Hudhayfa to survey Iraq's rural areas.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked, "Tell me who I should appoint to take charge of a public matter that is of great concern to me?" When the name…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that Umar sought a man for a public post, passed over Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, and agreed on Rabee bin Ziyaad Haarithi.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il Shaqeeq bin Salama reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once appointed Hadhrat Bishr bin Aasim (RA) to collect the Zakaah of the Hawaazin tribe. However,…
narrations.summary: Bishr bin Aasim, who failed to collect Zakaah for Umar, cites the Prophet's warning about public office, and Umar is alarmed until Abu Dharr confirms the warning.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once appointed Hadhrat Miqdaad bin Aswad as Ameer of a troop of cavalrymen. When he returned from the expedition, Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet made Miqdaad an Ameer of cavalry and asked him about command after him, and Miqdaad would accept it only from Abu Bakr; Abu Bakr refused to force Abaan bin Sa'eed and sent Alaa bin Hadhrami to Bahrain.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Miqdaad bin Aswad (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ sent me on an expedition. When we returned, he asked me, 'How do you find yourself?' I replied, 'I. gradually started…
narrations.summary: Miqdaad bin Aswad says that after an expedition he felt others were his servants and vowed never again to command even two people, and a second report tells of an unnamed commander who said the same, and the Prophet said leaders stand at the door of oppression.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Raafi Taa'i (RA) narrates that he accompanied Hadhrat Abu Bakr on an expedition and when they were returning, he asked Hadhrat Abu Bakr for some advice. Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Raafi Taa'i relates Abu Bakr's advice on an expedition: keep the prayers, zakaah, fasting and Hajj, and never seek command, since leaders face the longest reckoning, and Hijrah and jihaad are excellent virtues.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Raafi (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas as commander of the army that marched to the Battle of Dhaatus Salaasil. Together with…
narrations.summary: Raafi relates that Abu Bakr and Umar were with Amr bin al-Aas's expedition to Dhaatus Salaasil, that Raafi guided them, and that Abu Bakr later told him never to lead even two people; a year later, when Abu Bakr was Khalifah, Raafi reminded him, and Abu Bakr said the Khalifah must enforce the Book of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Amr bin Sa'eed bin Al Aas narrates that his uncles Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sa'eed bin Al Aas, Hadhrat Abaan bin Sa'eed bin Al Aas and Hadhrat Amr bin…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Amr bin Sa'eed bin al-Aas says that his uncles Khaalid, Abaan and Amr refused command after the Prophet and were martyred in Shaam; Abdur Rahmaan bin Sa'eed bin Yarboo reports that Umar was angry with Abaan for returning without leave, and that Abu Bakr chose Alaa bin Hadhrami for Bahrain.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once summoned him to accept a post as governor, but he refused to accept the post. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "You…
narrations.summary: Umar offers Abu Hurayrah a governorship, he refuses for fear of erring in judgement, and Umar cites Yusuf as someone who sought a post.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mowhab reports that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) once said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA), "Go and pass judgement between the people." Hadhrat Abdullaah…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan asks Abdullaah bin Umar to judge between people, and Abdullaah refuses, citing a saying of the Prophet, but the report breaks off mid-quote.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Ahmad adds that after this, Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) excused Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar and told him not to inform anyone else about it. (otherwise none would…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan wanted Abdullaah bin Umar to act as judge and excused him from it, and Abdullaah refused, quoting the Prophet that of three kinds of judges only one reaches salvation.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Uinar (RA) narrates, "it was on the day that Hadhrat Ali and Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) gathered at Dowmatul Jandal (to reconcile their differences)…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar recalls the day Ali and Mu'aawiya met at Dowmatul Jandal, when his sister Hafsa urged him to join, and Mu'aawiya asked who would risk his neck for the Khilaafah; Abdullaah chose Jannah instead.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Abu Husayn states that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) said, "Who is more worthy than us of this post (of Khilaafah)?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar said, "I wanted to…
narrations.summary: Abu Husayn reports that Mu'aawiya asked who was more worthy of the Khilaafah, and Abdullaah bin Umar began a reply about the man who struck their necks but held back for fear of losing Jannah's bounties.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of tmaarn zuhri states that when Hadhrat (Hasan bin) Ali (RA) and Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) got together, Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) announced, "Who is most worthy…
narrations.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports that when Hasan bin Ali and Mu'aawiya met, Mu'aawiya asked who was worthy of the Khilaafah, and Abdullaah bin Umar held back his reply for fear of being thought ambitious.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Saamit (RA) reports that when Ziyaad wanted to dispatch Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) as governor of Khurasan, he refused to accept the post. His…
narrations.summary: Several reports under one heading: Imraan bin Husayn refuses Khurasan and Hakam bin Amr is sent in his place, Abu Bakrah rebukes a man who mocked the Ameer, Ali relates the Prophet's ruling on obeying a commander who orders disobedience, and Umar and Alqama discuss obedience to the Ameer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA), narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed bin Mughiera Makhzoomi on expedition, with him was Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas recounts how Khaalid bin Waleed and Ammaar bin Yaasir quarrelled after Ammaar granted safety to a man who had accepted Islaam, and the Prophet upheld Ammaar's amnesty but forbade granting it without the Ameer's permission.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Auf bin Maalik Ashja'ee (RA) reports that he was amongst those Muslims who marched with zaid bin Haaritha for the Battle of Mu'ta. His companion was a man who had…
narrations.summary: Awf bin Maalik says that after the Battle of Mu'ta a Yemeni took the spoils of a Roman he had killed, Khaalid bin Waleed kept them, and when Awf complained the Prophet ordered them returned and rebuked Khaalid for disrespecting his commanders.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Raashid bin Sa'd reports that some wealth once came to Hadhrat Umar and he was distributing it amongst the people when they started crowding around him. Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Raashid bin Sa'd reports that Umar raised his whip at Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas for pushing through the crowd, and Abdullaah bin Yazeed reports that Abu Bakr stopped Umar from objecting when Amr bin al-Aas forbade fires on campaign.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jubayr bin Nufayr (RA) reports that Hadhrat Ayaadh bin Ghanam Ash'ari severely punished the governor of Daaraa when the Muslims conquered the place. Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Jubayr bin Nufayr reports that Hishaam bin Hakeem rebuked Ayaadh bin Ghanam for harshly punishing the governor of Daaraa, and Ayaadh replied that advice to a leader should be given privately, quoting the Prophet on the matter.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab reports that during the time of Hadhrat Hudhayfah some people complained to him about the Ameer. A man then entered the large (Jaami) Masjid and…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Wahab reports that Hudhayfah refused to be drawn into opposing his Ameer, and Ziyaad bin Kusayb reports that Abu Bakrah rebuked Mirdaas Abu Bilaal for mocking Abdullaah bin Aamir's dress; Ali reports a commander who ordered his men into a fire, and the Prophet said obedience is only in matters of good.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once with a group of the Sahabah (RA) when he turned to them and. said, "Do you not know that I am verily…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's teaching that obeying him is obeying Allaah, that obeying the leaders is obeying him, and that the people should pray seated if their leaders pray seated.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asmaa bint Yazeed (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abu Dharr Ghifaari used to serve Rasulullaah ﷺ and would return to the Masjid after he had completed. The Masjid was…
narrations.summary: Asmaa bint Yazeed reports that the Prophet found Abu Dharr sleeping in the Masjid and told him to follow his leaders wherever they lead, and Abu Dharr adds that he obeyed an Abyssinian slave of Uthmaan who led the prayer at Rabdha.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) went to Rabdha, he once found an Abyssinian slave of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) there. The man called out the Adhaan…
narrations.summary: At Rabdha, Abu Dharr found an Abyssinian slave of Uthmaan calling the adhaan who asked him to lead the prayer, and when Abu Dharr declined, saying the Prophet told him to obey even an Abyssinian slave, he prayed behind the slave.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Listen and obey (your Ameer) even though the person appointed as your Ameer is an Abyssinian slave with mutilated lim bs. Exercise patience if he…
narrations.summary: Umar says that a believer must obey a ruler even if he is an Abyssinian slave with mutilated limbs, bear his wrongs patiently, refuse any attempt to diminish the Deen, and stay with the Jamaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Alqama bin Alaatha once met Hadhrat Umar late at night. Because Hadhrat Umar (RA) resembled Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (Hadhrat Alqama…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Alqama bin Ulaatha met Umar at night, mistook him for Khaalid bin Waleed and complained that Umar had dismissed Khaalid; the next morning Umar asked Khaalid about it, and Alqama said obedience to leaders is owed in every condition.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Abi Mulaykah says that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by a lady suffering from leprosy as she was busy performing Tawaaf. He said to her, "O servant of Allaah!…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abi Mulaykah reports that Umar told a leprous woman to stay away from Tawaaf, and after Umar died she still refused to come out, saying it was not fitting to obey him alive and disobey him dead.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shamar narrates from a man who had been the chief of an area during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Ali (RA) that Hadhrat Ali is once issued an order to them and then…
narrations.summary: Shamar reports from a former governor under Ali that Ali ordered his men to obey, warning that otherwise the Jews and Christians would overpower them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin zubayr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent (!) From Sayf bin Amr, also narrating from Hadhrat Hasan. Hadhrat Arnr bin Al Aas (RA) (as Ameer) on a…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr relates that Umar asked Abdullaah bin Umar about sitting with rulers and then speaking differently outside, and Abdullaah says the Companions regarded this as hypocrisy in the Prophet's time.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salama bin Shihaab Abdi reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "O citizens! We (leaders) have a right that you owe to us. It is that you always wish well for…
narrations.summary: Umar tells the people that a ruler's tolerance and compassion towards his subjects is the most beloved thing to Allaah, and that a ruler's foolishness and harshness is the most detested.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates, "The senior companions of Rasulullaah ﷺ used to prevent us from certain misdeeds. They would say, 'Never speak ill of your leaders, never…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik relates that the senior Companions of the Prophet warned them never to speak ill of their leaders, betray them or disobey them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that he once approached Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar bin Khattaab and said, "O Abu Abdur Rahmaan! Sometimes we sit with these leaders of ours and…
narrations.summary: Urwa asks Abdullaah bin Umar about flattering leaders who rule unjustly, and Abdullaah replies that in the Prophet's time they regarded such behaviour as hypocrisy; further reports repeat the same view.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that they once said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar "When we enter the courts of these people (our leaders), we say the things they like to hear but…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that people told Abdullaah bin Umar they flatter their rulers in person and speak differently outside, and he says the Companions regarded this as hypocrisy in the Prophet's time.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Alqama bin Waqqaas narrates that there was a useless man who used to enter the courts of the governors and make them laugh. Hadhrat Alqama's grandfather said to…
narrations.summary: Alqama bin Waqqaas narrates how a man who made governors laugh was warned, with Bilaal bin Haarith's hadith on the weight of a single word.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfa (RA) once said, "Beware of the dens of evil!" "What are the dens of evil, O Abu Abdullaah?" someone enquired from him. He replied, "The doors of the…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfa warns against the doors of rulers, where a person confirms their lies and praises them falsely.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that his father (Hadhrat Abbaas once said to him, "Dear son I notice that the Ameerul Mu'mineen calls for you, allows you to be…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates his father Abbaas's three pieces of advice on serving the ruler: fear Allaah, never lie to him, never disclose his secrets, never backbite in his presence.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) once said to his son Hadhrat Abdullaah, "1 notice that that great man (referring to Hadhrat Umar allows you to sit close…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports Abbaas's advice to his son Abdullaah about Umar: never lie to him, never disclose his secrets, never backbite about anyone in his presence.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once refused to accept a verse or the Qur'aan from Hadhrat Ubay (RA) (saying that it is either not in the Qur'aan or…
narrations.summary: Hasan narrates that Umar refused a verse from Ubay bin Ka'b, and when Ubay said he had heard it from the Prophet, Umar admitted the truth and said there is no good in a ruler in whose presence the truth cannot be spoken.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Mijlaz reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) accused Hadhrat Ubay of lying when he recited the versed Hadhrat Ubay (RA) retorted by saying, "Your lie is worse!"…
narrations.summary: Abu Mijlaz reports that Umar accused Ubay of lying about a verse, Ubay answered that Umar's lie was worse, and then Umar confirmed Ubay had spoken the truth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Basheer (RA) reports that in a gathering of Muhaajirecn and Ansaar, Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked, "What will you people do if I were permissive in…
narrations.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer reports that when Umar asked a gathering what they would do if he became permissive, Basheer bin Sa'd promised to set him straight like an arrow.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Moosa bin Abu Isa narrates that when Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab went to the pond of the Banu Haaritha, he met Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama there. Hadhrat Umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: Moosa bin Abu Isa reports that Muhammad bin Maslama told Umar that if he strayed they would straighten him, and Umar praised Allaah for placing him among such people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Qabcel narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya Sii'SKs once ascended the pulpit on the day of Jumu'ah and said in his lecture, "The wealth is all ours and the spoils…
narrations.summary: Abu Qabeel reports that Mu'aawiya declared from the pulpit that the wealth was theirs to give or withhold, and a man objected three Jumu'ahs running; Mu'aawiya then recalled the Prophet's warning about rulers who speak wrongly and were thankful to the man for waking him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Hakeem bin Hizaam reports that when Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah was governor of Shaam, he punished some of the local (Kuffaar) persons (for not paying the…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Hakeem bin Hizaam reports that Khaalid bin Waleed rebuked Abu Ubaydah for harshly punishing non-Muslims over the jizya, citing the Prophet's warning about the severest punishment on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that when Ziyaad dispatched Hadhrat Hakam bin Amr Ghifaari as governor of Khurasan, the Muslims there managed to win a large amount of booty. Ziyaad…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that when Ziyaad appointed Hakam bin Amr governor of Khurasan, Hakam refused Mu'aawiya's order to withhold the gold and silver and distributed the booty, and Mu'aawiya had him arrested so he died in shackles.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa reports that-Ziyaad or his son once sent Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn to collect Zakaah. When Hadhrat Imraan (RA) returned, he brought nothing back. "Where is…
narrations.summary: Ataa reports that Imraan bin Husayn, sent to collect zakaah, distributed it to the needy instead of bringing it back, and Abu Khuzayma bin Thaabit reports Umar's custom of appointing governors before witnesses and holding them to account.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aswad bin Yazeed narrates that whenever a delegation came to Hadhrat umar, he would ask them about their governor. He would ask, "Does he visit the ill? Does he…
narrations.summary: Aswad bin Yazeed reports that Umar asked every delegation about its governor, and dismissed the governor if any answer was negative.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) states that whenever Hadhrat umar' dispatched governors, he would make the conditions with them that they should never ride Turkish horses, should not eat…
narrations.summary: Abu Khuzayma bin Thaabit reports that Umar set conditions for his governors on appointment, forbidding Turkish horses, fine flour, fine clothing and locked doors to the needy, and reminded them they were sent to establish salaah, share the spoils and judge justly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Saabit reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once sent for Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Aamir Jumhi (RA) and said to him, "We wish to appoint you in command of…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Saabit reports that Umar appointed Sa'eed bin Aamir Jumhi to lead a regiment for jihaad, telling him it was not to whip or humiliate them but to fight and share the booty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) once addressed the people saying, "The Ameerul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) has sent me here to teach you the Book of your…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari tells the people that Umar sent him to teach them the Book of their Lord and the Sunnah of their Nabi and to administer municipal affairs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Saalih Ghifaari narrates that Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) (while in Egypt) once wrote to Hadhrat Umar (RA) stating: "We have reserved a house for you here…
narrations.summary: Abu Saalih Ghifaari reports that Amr bin Al Aas offered Umar a house in Egypt, and Umar refused and turned the plot into a marketplace for the Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tameem jayshani (RA) reports that Hadhrat umar (RA) wrote the following letter to Hadhrat Amr bin M Aas (RA) "The news has reached me that you have had a pulpit…
narrations.summary: Tameem Jayshani reports that Umar wrote to Amr bin Al Aas ordering him to demolish a pulpit from which he rose above the people's necks.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote a letter to them when they were in Azerbaijan. He wrote: "O Utba bin Farqad! Your position and wealth has not…
narrations.summary: Abu Uthmaan reports that Umar wrote to Utba bin Farqad that his position and wealth were not his own efforts, telling him to feed the people as he feeds himself and avoid luxury, silk and imitating the mushrikeen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat urwa bin Ruwaym narrates lhat Hadhrat umar (RA) was inquiring about the condition of the people (during the Hay) when some people from Hims passed by him. "How is…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Ruwaym reports that Umar had the lofty residence of the governor of Hims burned and made him fetch water for the camels, then told him that his short time in this world did not justify such a building.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Attaab bin Rifaa'ah narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once received the news that Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) had built a mansion and had a door put on it, saying that the…
narrations.summary: Attaab bin Rifaa'ah reports that Umar sent Muhammad bin Maslama to bring Sa'd to account for his mansion, and Abu Moosa reports that Abu Ubaydah, having been ordered to move his people away from a plague, died of it himself.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once sought permission from Hadhrat umar (RA) to go to Shaam. Hadhrat Umar (RA) told him that he would be allowed to go there onlyoncondition that…
narrations.summary: Umar goes round the governors of Shaam in disguise with his slave Yarfa, finds Yazeed bin Abi Sufyaan, Amr bin Al Aas and Abu Moosa Ash'ari living in luxury and strikes each with his whip, then finds Abu Dardaa living in poverty, and the two of them remind each other of the Prophet's words in tears.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Saalih Ghifaari narrates that there was an extremely old blind lady living on the outskirts of Madinah whom Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to regularly visit at…
narrations.summary: Abu Saalih Ghifaari relates that Umar used to visit a blind old woman on the outskirts of Madinah at night to fetch her water and do her chores, and that he always found someone had already done it, until he caught Abu Bakr doing it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Awzaa'ee reports that Hadhrat Talha (RA) once spotted Hadhrat Umar coming out (of his house) late at night. Hadhrat Umar (RA) entered a house and then another…
narrations.summary: Awzaa'ee relates that Talha saw Umar going at night into houses to help a blind, crippled old woman, and Talha, on learning this, rebuked himself for having looked for faults in Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Utba bin Mas'ood says that he heard Hadhrat Umar say, "People would be taken to task by, means of revelation during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ (when…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Utba bin Masood quotes Umar saying that after revelation ended people are judged by their outward actions, and that Allaah alone judges their inner state.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan states that in the first lecture that Hadhrat Umar (RA) delivered (after becoming the Khalifah), he first praised Ailaah and then said: "(Now that 1 have…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports Umar's first sermon as Khalifah, in which Umar says he is tested through the people and they through him, and promises to deal directly with those present and to appoint capable, trustworthy agents over those absent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tawoos narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked (the people), "Tell me whether I would be discharging my responsibility if I appoint over you a person who is…
narrations.summary: Tawoos relates that Umar said that appointing the best man and ordering him to be just does not discharge a ruler's duty, which also requires inspecting whether the appointee actually does what he was commanded.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ka'b bin Maalik Ansaari that a regiment of the Ansaar were posted to Persian territory with their Ameer. Although Hadhrat Umar would continuously…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ka'b relates that an Ansaari regiment rebuked Umar for failing to relieve it on time, and Abu Moosa reports that Umar ordered Abu Ubaydah to leave the plague-hit land of Shaam, that Abu Ubaydah refused and then died of the plague himself.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that (when he read the letter from Hadhrat Umar Hadhrat Abu ubaydah (RA) said, "May Allaah forgive the Ameerul Mu'mineen. He wishes to preserve…
narrations.summary: Abu Ubaydah replies to Umar's letter that he will not leave the army to save his own life, and asks to be released from his command so he can stay with his soldiers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu ja'far reports that Hadhrat Abu Usayd (RA) once brought to Rasulullaah ﷺ some captives from Bahrain, Looking at a woman from amongst them weeping, Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Abu Ja'far reports that the Prophet asked Abu Usayd whether he had sold a weeping captive woman's son, and Muhammad bin Sallaam reports that Umar removed an official who had lost his mercy, saying those without mercy for their own children cannot show it to the masses.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) narrates that he was sitting with Hadhrat Umar (RA) one day when he heard a scream. Hadhrat Umar (RA) instructed his slave Yarfa to see where the…
narrations.summary: Buraydah relates that when Umar heard a girl screaming because her mother was being sold as a slave, Umar gathered the Muhaajireen and Ansaar and then ordered that the mother of no free woman be sold, because it severs family ties.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that after Hadhrat Umar (RA) had appointed a man from the Banu Asad tribe as governor, the man came to him to collect the certificate of…
narrations.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi relates that Umar dismissed a governor from Banu Asad who said he had never kissed a child, telling him that someone without mercy for his own children would show none to the public; Muhammad bin Sallaam gives a similar account.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that in the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ a woman stole during the conquest of Makkah. The members of her tribe (the Banu Makhzoom) hurried to Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that when the Makhzoomiyyah woman's penalty for theft was to be waived through Usaama, the Prophet refused and had her hand cut off, saying even Faatima would be punished if she stole, and afterwards she repented and married.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Qataadah (RA) reports, "After we had left with Rasulullaah ﷺ for the Battle of Hunayn and met with the enemy, we suffered a temporary defeat. When 1 saw a man…
narrations.summary: Abu Qataadah relates that after Hunayn he killed a mushrik and claimed the dead man's possessions, the Prophet confirmed his right to them, and he bought an orchard with them, his first wealth as a Muslim.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Hadrad Aslami (RA) narrates that he owed four Dirhams to a Jewish man, who then complained about him (to Rasulullaah ﷺ) saying, "0 Muhammad ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Hadrad reports that he sold his shawl and turban to a Jew to pay a four-dirham debt when the Prophet ordered him to pay, and an old woman gave him a shawl.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat ummu Salama (RA) reports that two men from the Ansaar brought to Rasulullaah ﷺ their dispute concerning some inheritance for which they could produce no evidence…
narrations.summary: Ummu Salama reports that the Prophet refused to judge in favour of the stronger claimant in an inheritance dispute between two Ansaar men, warning that it would be a yoke of Jahannam, and told them to divide the right and draw lots.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed (RA) reports that a Bedouin once came to Rasulullar'i to demand payment of a debt Rasulullaah ﷺ owed to him. He behaved very harshly with Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed reports that a Bedouin harshly demanded a debt from the Prophet, and the Prophet borrowed dates from Khowia bint Qais to repay him with extra, saying a nation whose weak cannot claim their rights without hesitation has no good in it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khowla bint Qais (RA) who was the wife of Hadhrat Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ owed a Wasaq of dates to a man from the Banu Saa'idah tribe.…
narrations.summary: Khowla bint Qais reports that the Prophet owed dates to a man from Banu Saa'idah, and when an Ansaari paid him inferior dates he refused, and the Prophet wept, said the nation whose weak cannot claim their rights is not blessed, and ordered the debt settled.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr stood up one Friday and announced, "Bring the Zakaah camels tomorrow morning so that we may distribute…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that Abu Bakr struck a man who entered the Zakaah camels without permission, then gave him the rein to take revenge, and when Umar intervened Abu Bakr compensated him with a camel, a carriage, a blanket and five dinaars.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that a dispute arose between Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Appoint someone to decide the matter…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that Umar and Ubay bin Ka'b took a dispute to Zaid bin Thaabit, who seated Umar at the head of the bedding, which Umar rejected, and Umar then took the oath as a common Muslim would; the Ibn Asaakir version gives a date-harvest dispute.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam reports that Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) had a house next to the Masjid of Madinah. Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) to sell the house to him…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports that Umar asked Abbaas to sell or give his house by the Prophet's Masjid for the expansion, and when Abbaas refused, Ubay bin Ka'b ruled that no one may be removed from his house without consent, citing the Prophet's account of Sulaymaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once intended to take the house of Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) to include it in the Masjid. However, Hadhrat Abbaas…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Ubay bin Ka'b decided in Abbaas's favour, telling the story of Sulaymaan buying land at a price he had to accept, and Abbaas then gave the house as sadaqah for the Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA) reports that his brother Abdur Rahmaan and Abu Saroo'ah both drank some wine while they were in Egypt during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that his brother Abdur Rahmaan and Abu Saroo'ah drank wine in Egypt, were punished by Amr bin Al Aas at his own request, and Umar later punished Abdur Rahmaan further, who died a month later from an unrelated cause.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once sent for a woman whose husband had gone missing. Hadhrat Umar (RA) objected to the fact that (!) Abdur Kazzaaq, as…
narrations.summary: Hasan narrates that Umar sent for a woman whose husband had gone missing, and she was so frightened that she went into labour; Umar then rebuked the one responsible for the killing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once emerged from his home with his fingers in his ears and saying, "If only I could have been at your service! If…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Wahab reports that Umar was grieved when a governor's men drowned an old man who was forced into a cold river, and Umar ordered the governor to pay the blood money and leave, saying one Muslim was worth more than all his conquests.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jareer narrates that a man who was 'with Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (in a battle) managed to gain a large booty. Although Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari gave the man…
narrations.summary: Jareer reports that Abu Moosa Ash'ari gave a man twenty lashes and shaved his head over a dispute about his share of booty, and Umar ordered that the revenge be taken in the same way, but the man forgave him for the pleasure of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hirmaazi reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote the following letter to Hadhrat Fayrooz Daylami (RA) "The news has reached me that you are very occupied with eating…
narrations.summary: Hirmaazi reports that Umar summoned Fayrooz Daylami, who slapped a Qurayshi youth in a dispute over entry, and when Umar cited the Prophet's words about Fayrooz killing the false prophet Aswad Anasi, the youth forgave him and Fayrooz gave him his sword, horse and thirty thousand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) .reports that a slave woman once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) and said, "My master has accused me of fornication and made me sit on a fire…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that a slave woman whose master burned her private parts on a false accusation of fornication was freed by Umar, who lashed the master a hundred times and cited the Prophet's ruling that no retribution is taken from a master for his slave, and that anyone burned is freed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Makhool narrates that Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) once called a non-Arab Christian farm labourer to ljold his animal next to Baytul Maqdas. When the labourer…
narrations.summary: Makhool reports that Ubaadah bin Saamit struck a non-Arab Christian labourer who refused to hold his animal, and Umar ruled that Ubaadah should pay compensation instead of allowing retaliation, after Zaid bin Thaabit objected to retaliation against Umar's brother.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Suwayd bin Ghafala (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once arrived in Shaam, a man belonging to the Ahlul Kitaab said to him, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! A man…
narrations.summary: Suwayd bin Ghafala reports that Umar, on hearing a dhimmi had been beaten by a Muslim, had Awf bin Maalik punished after learning that Awf had struck a man who raped a Muslim woman, and crucified the rapist, saying there would be no protection for such a dhimmi.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdul Malik bin Ya'la Laythi narrates that Hadhrat Bakr bin Shaddaah Laythi used to serve Rasulullaah ﷺ when he was a child. After he came of age, he approached…
narrations.summary: Abdul Malik bin Ya'la reports that Bakr bin Shaddaah confessed to killing a Jew who had insulted a Muslim's wife, and Umar acquitted him because of the Prophet's prayer that his speech be truthful.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Abi Bazza reports that a Muslim once killed a Dhimmi in Shaam. The case was brought before Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin jarraah (RA), who then wrote to…
narrations.summary: Abu Ubaydah referred the case of a Muslim who killed a Dhimmi in Shaam to Umar, who ruled that the man be executed if killing Dhimmis was his habit, but otherwise pay four thousand Dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: It is reported that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once wrote the following letter to one of the army commanders he had dispatched: "The news has reached me that some of your men seek…
narrations.summary: Umar wrote to a commander forbidding his men to kill Mushrikeen who had surrendered under a promise of safety, and warned that he would punish anyone who did.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Abu Salama states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "I swear by the Being Who controls my life! If any of you points your finger towards the sty for any…
narrations.summary: Abu Salama reports Umar's oath that he would have executed anyone who killed a Mushrik after pointing to him as a sign of safety and then surrendering to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas SiP says, "When we laid siege to the city of Tustar, (their leader) Hurmuzaan eventually surrendered on the verdict of Umar. I then brought him to Umar, When…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik says that Hurmuzaan, who surrendered at Tustar, was spared by Umar after Anas gave testimony that Hurmuzaan had been promised amnesty, and Hurmuzaan then accepted Islaam and received an allowance.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abi Hadrad Aslami (RA) narrates that when they arrived with Hadhrat Umar (RA) in Jaabiya, they came across an. old Dhimmi man begging for food. When…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abi Hadrad Aslami reports that Umar found an old, poor Dhimmi begging, excused him from jizya and fixed an allowance for him from the treasury.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by an old Dhimmi begging at the doors of the Masaajid. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "We have not treated you…
narrations.summary: Umar tells an old Dhimmi begging at the Masaajid that the state has not treated him fairly, and has an adequate allowance given to him from the public treasury.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abi Maalik reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was with the Muslims of Jaabiya when a Dhimmi reported to him that people had ransacked his vineyard. Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Yazeed bin Abi Maalik reports that when a Dhimmi complained that his vineyard had been ransacked, Umar found a Sahabi carrying grapes on a shield, let him go, and ordered the owner paid from the treasury.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that a Muslim and Jew once brought their dispute to Hadhrat Umar (RA). Because Hadhrat Umar (RA) saw that the jew was right, he…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Umar ruled in favour of a Jew against a Muslim, and when the Jew praised the verdict, Umar whipped him and asked how he knew, and the Jew explained what the Torah says about judges who rule by the truth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Iyaas bin Salama narrates from his father (Hadhrat Salama), "Hadhrat Umar once passed through the marketplace with a whip in his hand. He lightly struck me with…
narrations.summary: Iyaas bin Salama relates that his father Salama, struck lightly by Umar in the marketplace, was given six hundred Dirhams by Umar for his Hajj as compensation.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Furaat narrates that Hadhrat Uthmaan SI once said to his, slave, "1 once twisted your ears and I want you to take retribution. When the slave took hold of…
narrations.summary: Abul Furaat reports that Uthmaan asked his slave to twist his ear in retribution, and when the slave did so gently Uthmaan told him to twist harder, praising the delight of retribution in this world.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi bin Abdul Haarith narrates, "Hadhrat Umar (RA) once arrived in Makkah where he went to the Daarun Nadwa on a Friday. He intended to reach the Masjid earlier…
narrations.summary: Naafi bin Abdul Haarith relates how Umar chased a pigeon from his shawl in a room in Makkah, the pigeon was then killed by a snake, and Umar, after asking Uthmaan and Naafi for a verdict, had a three-year-old white goat paid as compensation.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Kulayb narrates that when the booty won at Isfahan came to Hadhrat Ali he divided it into seven shares. He found in it a loaf of bread and even divided that into…
narrations.summary: Kulayb reports that Ali, dividing the booty won at Isfahan into seven shares, placed a piece of a single loaf on each share and had the commanders draw lots to decide who received their share first.

narrations.excerpt: The grandfather of Hadhrat Isa bin Abdullaah Haashimi narrates that two women came to ask from Hadhrat Ali (RA). The one was an Arab woman and the other was her freed…
narrations.summary: The narrator, the grandfather of Isa bin Abdullaah Haashimi, reports that Ali gave an Arab woman and her freed slave equal shares of grain and forty Dirhams, and when the Arab woman protested, Ali said the Book of Allaah gives the Arabs no preference over the freed slave.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali bin Rabee'ah reports that Hadhrat Ja'dah bin Hubayrah once said to Hadhrat Ali (RA), "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Two people will come to you (to judge their…
narrations.summary: Ali bin Rabee'ah reports that Ja'dah bin Hubayrah urged Ali to rule for the one dearer to him, and Ali refused, saying he judges only to please Allaah, and lightly struck Ja'dah's chest.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asbagh bin Nabaatah narrates that he once accompanied Hadhrat (RA) to the marketplace. When Hadhrat (RA) noticed that the traders had trespassed their boundaries,…
narrations.summary: Asbagh bin Nabaatah reports that Ali, seeing traders in the marketplace encroach on their spaces, ruled that the Muslim market is like a place of salaah and that whoever arrives first has his place for the day.

narrations.excerpt: In a lengthy narration concerning the'Mushrikeen in the Battle of Khaybar, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawwaaha used to go to Khaybar…
narrations.summary: In a lengthy report about Khaybar, Abdullaah bin Umar says that Abdullaah bin Rawwaaha estimated the Khaybar crop fairly each year despite Jewish complaints and bribes, telling them that his love for the Prophet and his hatred of them would not make him unjust.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haarith bin Suwayd narrates that Hadhrat Miqdaad bin Aswad (RA) was once part of a military expedition that was surrounded by the enemy. The Ameer of the army…
narrations.summary: Haarith bin Suwayd relates that Miqdaad bin Aswad, seeing a man beaten by the Ameer for grazing his animal against orders, brought the man before the Ameer with his sword around his neck, secured the man's right to retribution, and then said he hoped to die while Islaam is dominant.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dahhaak reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddeeq (RA) once saw a bird perched on a tree and said, "How fortunate you are, O bird! By Allaah! I wish I had been like…
narrations.summary: Dahhaak reports that Abu Bakr, seeing a bird on a tree, wished he were a bird that eats fruit and flies off without any reckoning, and wished he had never been a human facing reckoning.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration also from Hadhrat Dahhaak bin Muzaahim states that Hadhrat Abu Bakr was once looking at a sparrow when he said, "How fortunate are you, O sparrow. You…
narrations.summary: Dahhaak bin Muzaahim reports that Abu Bakr envied a sparrow and a sheep, and said he wished he had been a hair on the body of a Mu'min rather than a human facing reckoning.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dahhaak narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "I wish that I had been the sheep of a family who fatten me up as much as they please. When I then become as…
narrations.summary: Dahhaak reports that Umar wished he were a sheep that a family fattens and then slaughters and eats, and wished he had never been a human.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir bin Rabee'ah reports that he once saw Hadhrat Umar (RA) pick up a twig from the ground and say, "I wish that l had been this twig. I wish that I had never…
narrations.summary: Aamir bin Rabee'ah reports seeing Umar pick up a twig and wish that he had been that twig, or had never been created or been born.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "If a caller from the heavens had to announce, 'O people! Each one of you shall enter Jannah besides one person' I…
narrations.summary: Umar says that if a caller from the heavens announced that everyone would enter Jannah except one person, he would fear that person was himself, and if the caller announced that everyone would enter Jahannam except one, he would wish to be that one.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once met Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) and asked him, "O Abu Moosa! Will it please you to have for…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar asked Abu Moosa Ash'ari whether he would want his deeds after the Prophet's time cancelled out so that he got neither reward nor punishment; Abu Moosa declined, and Umar said he wanted only his deeds from the Prophet's time.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "After Hadhrat Umar (RA) was stabbed, I went to him and said, 'Glad tidings to you, O Ameerul Mu'mineen because it was through you…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that after Umar was stabbed, he congratulated him on his leadership and its benefits, and Umar replied that he wished to leave office with neither reward nor sin.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah. bin Abbaas (RA) said to Hadhrat Umar (RA), "Accept the glad tidings of Jannah for you have been in the company of…
narrations.summary: Another report has Ibn Abbaas tell Umar that the glad tidings of Jannah are his, given his long companionship with the Prophet and his leadership, and Umar answers that he would ransom himself with the world from the terror ahead and wishes his leadership had neither reward nor punishment.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin ubayd bin Umayr narrates that a lengthy narration in which he states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked those around him to help him sit up. When they did…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr reports that Umar, propped up, asked Ibn Abbaas to repeat his words and then asked him to testify to them before Allaah, and Umar was very pleased with the answer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, (RA)'s head was on my lap when he was suffering the illness that eventually claimed his life. 'Put my head on the ground,' he said…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar relates that Umar, in his final illness, asked to have his head placed on the ground and said he and his mother would be ruined if his Rabb did not show mercy; Miswar reports that when Umar was stabbed he said he would ransom himself from Allaah's punishment with all the gold on earth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saa'eb bin Yazd (RA) narrates that someone. once asked Hadhrat Umar, "Is it better for me not to fear anybody's criticism in matters pertaining to Maah or to…
narrations.summary: Saa'ib bin Yazid reports that someone asked Umar whether it is better not to fear criticism or to examine oneself, and Umar replied that officials must not fear criticism in matters done for Allaah, while others should reform themselves and advise the officials.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aghar from the Banu Maalik tribe reports that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr decided to appoint Hadhrat Umar (RA) as his successor, he send for him. When Hadhrat Umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: Aghar, from the Banu Maalik, reports that when Abu Bakr decided to appoint Umar as successor, he advised him to fear Allaah, to remember that his leadership will be presented before Allaah, and to keep the people's blood, wealth and honour safe.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalim bin Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that when death came to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), he gave the following parting advices-. This is a parting repuest from…
narrations.summary: Saalim bin Abdullaah bin Umar reports Abu Bakr's parting advice on his deathbed: he had appointed Umar as successor, and he told Umar to fear Allaah, that deeds are weighed by truth and falsehood, and to beware of his own self and of people's envy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Saabit, Hadhrat Zaid bin Zubayd bin Haarith and Hadhrat Mujaahid all report that when death approached Hadhrat Abu Bakr he summoned Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Saabit, Zaid bin Zubayd bin Haarith and Mujaahid report Abu Bakr's last advice to Umar: fear Allaah, hope in His mercy and fear His punishment, and never be deceived about deeds or give up hope in Allaah's mercy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had resolved to combine the armies marching to Shaam. The first of the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm reports that Abu Bakr, seeing Amr bin Al Aas off to Shaam, walked beside his mount and advised him to fear Allaah, be a father to the people, guard the booty and be steadfast in battle, and keep his speech brief.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once wrote a letter to Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) and to Hadhrat Waleed bin Uqaba, both of whom were…
narrations.summary: Qaasim bin Muhammad reports that Abu Bakr wrote to Amr bin Al Aas and Waleed bin Uqaba, who were collecting half the Zakaah of the Qudaa'ah tribe, urging them to fear Allaah in private and in public.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muttalib bin Saa'ib bin Abu Wadaa'ah narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr wrote the following letter to Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) I have written to Khaalid bin Waleed…
narrations.summary: Muttalib bin Saa'ib bin Abu Wadaa'ah reports Abu Bakr's letter to Amr bin Al Aas about Khaalid bin Waleed, who was to reinforce him: treat him well, do not assert authority over him, and consult the others without opposing their views.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdul Hameed bin Ja'far narrates from his father that Hadhrat Abu Bakr said to Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA), "I have appointed you as Ameer of all the people you…
narrations.summary: Abdul Hameed bin Ja'far reports that Abu Bakr appointed Amr bin Al Aas over the Baliy, Udhra, Qudaa'ah and other Arab tribes, and told him to encourage them to wage jihaad, provide for them, and treat each tribe according to its status.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ibraheem bin Haarith Taymi reports that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) relieved Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sa'eed of his duties, he gave the following advice to…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Ibraheem bin Haarith Taymi reports that Abu Bakr, relieving Khaalid bin Sa'eed of his post, advised Shurahbeel bin Hasanah to honour Khaalid's status and to consult Abu Ubaydah, Mu'aadh bin Jabal and Khaalid before deciding anything.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haarith bin Fadhl reports that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) gave the flag to Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan (RA) (appointed him commander of the army), he said to…
narrations.summary: Haarith bin Fadhl reports that Abu Bakr gave the flag to Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan and appointed him over the army in Khaalid bin Sa'eed's place, then told him to honour Abu Ubaydah and Mu'aadh bin Jabal, quoting the Prophet's praise of both, and never to decide without them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) called him and said, "O Yazeed! The worst that I fear from you is that you might give preference…
narrations.summary: Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan reports that Abu Bakr warned him not to favour his relatives in appointments, quoting the Prophet's warning that whoever appoints someone out of love for them, or gives a brother's wealth to another out of love, incurs Allaah's curse.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "My parting advice to my successor is that he recognises the rights of the early Muhaajireen and upholds their honour and respect. I also…
narrations.summary: Umar, as parting advice to his successor, urges him to honour the early Muhaajireen, recognise the good Ansaar, treat the people of other cities and the Bedouins well, take from them only their surplus, and protect the Dhimmis.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "My successor should know that many close and distant people will want to take the Khilaafah away…
narrations.summary: Qaasim bin Muhammad reports that Umar told his successor that many would seek to take the Khilaafah from him, that Umar himself had to struggle to hold off challengers, and that he would rather be executed than be appointed if someone stronger were known.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalih bin Kaysaan narrates that the first letter that Hadhrat Umar wrote after becoming the Khalifah was to Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin jarraah to give him command…
narrations.summary: Saalih bin Kaysaan reports that the first letter Umar wrote as Khalifah gave Abu Ubaydah command of Khaalid bin Waleed's army, with instructions to fear Allaah, not to send Muslims to destruction for booty, to scout each camp, and not to be drawn to the world.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad and Hadhrat Talha both narrate that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once sent for Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA). When he arrived, Hadhrat Umar appointed him…
narrations.summary: Umar sends for Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, appoints him commander of the Iraq offensive and gives him detailed advice on sincerity, equality before Allaah and the Prophet's example.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdul Malik bin Umayr narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) dispatched Hadhrat Utba bin Ghazwaan (RA) to Basrah, he said to him, "O Utba! I have appointed you as…
narrations.summary: Abdul Malik bin Umayr relates Umar's advice to Utba bin Ghazwaan, sent as governor of Basrah: to fear Allaah, call people to Islaam, avoid pride, and seek only Allaah's pleasure, with Alaa bin Hadhrami and Arjafa to support him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once wrote the following letter to Hadhrat Alaa bin Hadhrami (RA) who was' in Bahrain: "Proceed to Utba bin Ghazwaan because…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi relates Umar's letter to Alaa bin Hadhrami, who was to take over Bahrain from Utba bin Ghazwaan, telling him that appointments are in Allaah's hands and urging him to focus on the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dabba bin Mihsin narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote the following letter to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) People usually develop a dislike for their rulers. I…
narrations.summary: Dabba bin Mihsin relates Umar's letter to Abu Moosa Ash'ari, warning him against luxury in clothing, food and transport, telling him to enforce the Shari'ah penalties and stay accessible to the Muslims, and warning that a corrupt governor corrupts those beneath him.
