narrations.excerpt: "Strength in leadership is attained when leaders refrain from postponing today's tasks for tomorrow. When you do this, the tasks accumulate to the extent that you do not…
narrations.summary: Umar writes to Abu Moosa Ash'ari that leaders must not postpone their duties, should prefer the Aakhirah to this world, and should fear Allaah and study the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Alaa bin Fadhl narrated from his mother that after Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) was martyred, the people searched for his wealth and found a locked box. When they opened…
narrations.summary: After Uthmaan was martyred, a locked box yielded his parting advice, which affirms tawheed, the Prophet's messengership and the reality of the Hereafter, followed by verses on patience.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Aws (RA) narrates that when the siege of Hadhrat Uthmaan's house became too difficult, he peeped out to see the people and said, "O servants of…
narrations.summary: During the siege of Uthmaan's house, Ali and his supporters drive off the rebels, Ali offers to fight them, and Uthmaan refuses to let blood be shed on his account.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Salama bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that Hadhrat Abu Qataadah and another person went to Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) while his house was under siege. They requested…
narrations.summary: During the siege, Abu Qataadah and a companion ask Uthmaan whom to follow, Uthmaan tells them to stay with the majority, and when Hasan and Ibn Umar offer to act for him he refuses to let blood be spilt.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) says, "I was under siege with Uthmaan in his house when one of our men was struck by an arrow. I said, 'O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Now that one of our…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah says that while he was under siege with Uthmaan, a man was killed, and Uthmaan ordered him to throw down his sword, which he did.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhaajir Aamiri narrates that in the letter of appointment that Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib wrote to some governors of certain towns, he wrote: "Never be away from…
narrations.summary: Ali's letter to his governors warns them not to stay away from the people, because distance breeds ignorance and injustice, and tells them to stay accessible and fair.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Madaa'ini reports that Hadhrat All (RA) wrote the following letter to some of his governors: "Slow down and imagine that you have reached your death and that your…
narrations.summary: Ali writes to some governors asking them to remember their own death and the Day when their actions will be shown to them.

narrations.excerpt: A man from the Thaqeef tribe narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once appointed him as governor of Ukbara. While the local people of the area were with him, Hadhrat Ali (RA)…
narrations.summary: Ali appoints a man of the Thaqeef tribe as governor of Ukbara and tells him not to oppress the local people when collecting what is due, taking only what is extra.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Never sell off their grains, their summer and winter clothing or their animals of labour. Never make any of them…
narrations.summary: Ali tells the governor of Ukbara not to sell the people's grain or animals and not to make them stand in the sun to extract payment, since only what exceeds their needs is to be taken.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Makhool (RA) states a Sahabi of Rasulullaah ﷺ by the name of Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Aamir bun judhaym jumhi once told Hadhrat umar that he wished to offer some…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Aamir advises Umar to fear Allaah, to keep his words and deeds consistent, and to judge fairly for all the Muslims under his rule.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Buraydah narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once gathered the people upon the arrival of a delegation. He then said to Azina bin Arqam, "Look out for…
narrations.summary: Umar tests three men who are asked to speak before a delegation; the third, Rabee bin Ziyaad, gives frank advice, and Umar appoints him under an Ash'ari commander to be watched and reported on.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Sooqa reports that he once went to Hadhrat Nu'aym bin Abu Hind who took out a paper on which the following was written: "From Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah…
narrations.summary: Abu Ubaydah and Mu'aadh write to Umar warning him about justice and about a time when people will look friendly outwardly while being enemies inside, and the letter is shown to Muhammad bin Sooqa.

narrations.excerpt: From Umar bin Khattaab to Abu Ubaydah and Mu'aadh. Your letter has reached me in which you state that you two have observed that I have always been concerned about my…
narrations.summary: Umar replies to Abu Ubaydah and Mu'aadh that he cannot manage justice without Allaah's help, that the times they warn of are not theirs, and that he always wants their counsel.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib says that when Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (t) Abu Nu'aym in his Hifya (Vol.1 Pg.238). Ibn Abi Shaybah and Hannaad have reported a similar…
narrations.summary: Abu Ubaydah, dying of the plague in Jordan, advises the Muslims to keep the salaah, fast in Ramadhaan, pay zakaah, perform Hajj and Umrah, and prepare for death; Mu'aadh leads the prayer and then addresses the people after Abu Ubaydah's death.

narrations.excerpt: Ibn Sa'd has combined Ahadeeth reported by Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar SSI Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib and others to relate that people pledged their…
narrations.summary: The text traces Abu Bakr's life as khalifah: he gave up trade for a fixed allowance, returned public money on his deathbed, and on his Umrah visit to Makkah was greeted by its leaders while his father Abu Quhaafa wept with joy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Antara narrates from Hadhrat Umayr bin Sa'd Ansaari (RA) that Hadhrat Umar (RA) send him to be the governor of Hims but after a year had still not received any…
narrations.summary: Umar suspects his governor of Hims, Umayr bin Sa'd, of keeping public wealth and recalls him, but Umayr shows he gave the money away to the poor and lived in great poverty, so Umar wishes for more men like him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Ma'daan narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) appointed Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Aamir bin Judhaym (RA) as their governor in Hims. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) visited…
narrations.summary: Umar asks the people of Hims about their governor Sa'eed bin Aamir, hears their complaints and his replies, and sends him a thousand dinaars, which Sa'eed gives to those in need; he explains his fainting by recalling Khubayb Ansaari's martyrdom.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tha'laba bin Abu Maalik Qurazi says, "It was during the period that Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) was the governor (of Madinah) for Marwaan that he came to the…
narrations.summary: Tha'laba bin Abu Maalik Qurazi recounts that Abu Hurayrah, then governor of Madinah for Marwaan, joked with him in the marketplace while carrying a bundle of wood, and Tha'laba answered him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jareer reports that they were once with Rasulullaah ﷺ one morning when some people belonging to the Mudar tribe arrived. They were barefoot and practically naked.…
narrations.summary: When tribesmen of Mudar arrive in poverty, the Prophet urges the people to give charity and recites Qur'aanic verses, and a generous Ansaari's gift starts a flood of giving, which the Prophet praises as a good practice.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that it was a Wednesday when Rasulullaah ﷺ visited the Banu Amr bin Auf tribe. The Hadith continues to the point where Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O…
narrations.summary: The Prophet reminds the Ansaar of their generosity in the Period of Ignorance and urges them not to hold back their wealth now that they are Muslims, and they respond by opening their orchards to all.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates thatin the firstsermon that Rasulullaah ilif delivered, he praised Allaah and then said, "O people! Verily Allaah has chosen Islaam to be your…
narrations.summary: Anas reports the Prophet's first sermon, in which he urges generosity and good character, describing generosity as a tree of Jannah and miserliness as a tree of Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates that a man came to ask Rasulullaah till to give him something. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I have nothing to give you, but you may give something on…
narrations.summary: A man asks the Prophet for something he cannot give; Umar objects, and an Ansaari urges the Prophet to keep giving without fear of loss, which pleases the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that someone came to ask Rasulullaah ﷺ for something and he gave it to him. Thereafter, another person came to ask for something and (because…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that Umar objected when the Prophet had nothing to give, and Abdullaah bin Hudhaafa told the Prophet to keep spending; in a second report Ibn Mas'ood says the Prophet asked Bilaal why he was storing dates.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was once given three birds as a gift, he gave one to his servant to eat. The following day, she came with the same bird…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet gave a bird to his servant, and when she kept it until the next day, he reminded her that Allaah provides each day's sustenance.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat All (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said to the people, "We have some excess funds (what should we do with it?)." The people replied, "O Ameerul…
narrations.summary: When Umar asks what to do with surplus funds, Ali argues from an earlier incident, involving Abbaas's refusal to pay Zakaah and the Prophet's Sadaqah, that Umar should not change a firm conviction into a mere assumption.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydullaah (RA) reports that some wealth once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) and he duly distributed it amongst the people. When some of it was left over,…
narrations.summary: Umar distributes wealth and asks the people what to do with the surplus; Ali says it should be distributed as the Qur'aan prescribes, the Prophet's distribution is recalled, and Ali completes the distribution, with Talha's share being 800 dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Salama (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once came to me with great concern on his face. Fearing that he was in pain, 1 asked, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ What is the…
narrations.summary: Ummu Salama and Sahl bin Sa'd report that in the Prophet's last illness he was troubled by seven dinaars he had not yet given away, and had Aa'isha send them to Ali, who gave them in charity.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "During his illness, Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed me give in Sadaqah some gold that we had. When he regained…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that during his illness the Prophet told her to give some gold in charity, and when it was still in the house he said he did not want to meet Allaah with it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaydullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) said to him, "Dear nephew! Rasulullaah ﷺ was once holding me by the hand when he said, 'O Abu…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr tells Ubaydullaah bin Abbaas that the Prophet said he would not want to die with even a qiraat of wealth left, because the Prophet desired the Aakhirah rather than this world.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates that he once went to Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan. When Hadhrat uthmaan (RA) allowed him in, he entered with a staff in his hand. Addressing…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr rebukes Ka'b Ahbaar with his staff for saying that paying zakaah leaves no further duty on wealth, quoting Qur'aanic verses on giving beyond it, and Uthmaan confirms he heard the Prophet's warning about wealth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once instructed us to spend in charity at a time when I happened to have a considerable sum of wealth with me. I therefore said to…
narrations.summary: Umar recounts that when the Prophet called for charity he brought half his wealth, but Abu Bakr brought all he had, saying he left Allaah and His Rasool for his family.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that a man once said to Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), "You wealthy people have far superseded us (poor people) on doing good because you are able to give…
narrations.summary: A man tells Uthmaan that the wealthy have outdone the poor in good deeds, and Uthmaan replies that a dirham given in hardship is better than ten thousand given in plenty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaydullaah bin Muhammad bin Aa'isha narrates that when a beggar came to the Ameerul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Ali (RA), he said to (his son) Hadhrat Hasan or Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: A man brings the Prophet a young she-camel beyond the one-year camel that was due from him as Zakaah, and the Prophet accepts it and prays for the man's wealth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent me to collect Zakaah. I passed by a man and when he gathered all his wealth together, I calculated that all that was…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Kab relates that when he was sent to collect Zakaah, a man offered a larger she-camel in place of the one-year-old male due, and the Prophet accepted it as extra charity and prayed for the man's wealth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) says, "I have never seen women as generous as Aa'isha and (her sister) Asmaa. Their forms of generosity were however different. As for…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr says that Aa'isha and Asmaa were both generous, Aa'isha by gathering things before distributing them and Asmaa by never keeping anything for the next day.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Ka'b bin Maalik narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal was an extremely generous, youthful and handsome man who was amongst the most righteous…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Ka'b reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal was so generous that he fell into debt, the Prophet had his property sold to repay creditors, and on his return from Yemen with wealth from Zakaah funds, Umar wanted it taken, but Abu Bakr refused and gave it to him as a gift.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from the son of Hadhrat Ka'b bin Maalik (RA) states that Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) was an extremely youthful, handsome and generous man who was…
narrations.summary: A second report, from an unnamed son of Ka'b bin Maalik, describes Mu'aadh bin Jabal's generosity and debts, and refers the reader back to the account already given.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jabbir (RA) reports that Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) was amongst the most handsome of people, amongst those with the best character and the most open-handed.…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal's creditors demanded payment; the Prophet had his possessions handed over, the creditors recovered only part of the debt, and Mu'aadh was later sent to Yemen and met Umar in Makkah, where Umar noticed his slaves.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports that after the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ, the people appointed Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) as his successor. Rasulullaah ﷺ had…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood reports that after the Prophet's death, Umar met Mu'aadh in Makkah; Mu'aadh had slaves from Yemen, Umar advised giving them to Abu Bakr, and Mu'aadh gave them to Abu Bakr and then freed them all.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) received a piece of land in Khaybar. He then approached Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "I have received a piece of…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar was given land in Khaybar, and on the Prophet's advice made it an endowment whose proceeds go to the poor, relatives, freed slaves, the path of Allaah and guests.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once wrote to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) to buy for him a slave woman from Jaloolaa (a place en route to Khurasan that the Muslims had conquered.…
narrations.summary: Umar asked Abu Moosa to buy him a slave woman, then freed her after reciting the verse on spending what one loves.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) then set her free.
narrations.summary: Umar then frees the slave woman.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) owned a slave woman. When his love for her became intense, he freed her and married her to one of his freed…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar freed a slave woman he loved, married her to one of his freed slaves, and later kissed the son she bore.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Urnar (RA) says, "I brought to mind everything that Allaah had given me when I heard the verse: You shall never reach (true, perfect) righteousness…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar freed his most beloved possession, his Roman slave woman Marjaana, after hearing the verse on spending what one loves.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Urnar (RA) got her married to Hadhrat Naafi and she thus gave birth to his child.
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar had the freed woman married to Naafi, and she bore Naafi a child.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi narrates, "Whenever the love of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Urnar for any of his possessions became intense, he offered it to his Rabb (gave it away as Sadaqah).…
narrations.summary: Naafi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar gave away whatever he loved most, freed slaves who showed good deeds, and marked a beloved camel for sacrifice.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration also from Hadhrat Naafi states that once while Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Urnar was riding a camel, he was very impressed by its ride. He then said, "Ikh!…
narrations.summary: Naafi reports Abdullaah bin Umar giving away a beloved camel and large sums, and freeing Naafi after Ibn Aamir's gifts troubled him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Abu Hilaal reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) was once ill when he stayed over at Juhfa. When he expressed the desire to eat fish, the people…
narrations.summary: When Abdullaah bin Umar was ill at Juhfa and had only one fish, he told a poor man who came to the house to take it.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that his wife said, "We shall give him a Dirham which will be more useful for him then the fish, while you will be able to fulfil your desire to…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar rejects his wife's suggestion to give a dirham to the poor man instead and insists his own wish be carried out.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) was the wealthiest of all the Ansaar in terms of the date plantations he owned. However, what he loved most of all…
narrations.summary: On the Prophet's advice, Abu Talha gave his beloved orchard of Bir Haa in charity and divided it among his relatives.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration of Bukhari adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I have heard what you have to say, but think that you should rather divide it amongst your relatives." Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: On the Prophet's advice, Abu Talha divided his beloved orchard at Bir Haa among his relatives and nephews.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Munkadir narrates that Hadhrat Zaid bin Haaritha brought along his horse called "Shibla" when the following verse of the Qur'aan was revealed: You…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Haaritha gave his most prized horse Shibla as charity; the Prophet gave it to Zaid's son Usaama and reassured Zaid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) stated, "There are three partners in one's wealth. (The first is) Predestination that will not consult with you as it takes your valuable and…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr says wealth has three partners, and sends his most beloved camel ahead to the Aakhirah as charity.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sahl bin Sa'd (RA) narrates that a woman once brought a shawl to Rasulullaah ﷺ. It was woven with a woven edge as well. She said, "O Rasulullaah US I have come to…
narrations.summary: A woman gave the Prophet a shawl; he wore it, and when a Sahabi asked for it he gave it, the Sahabi saying he hoped for its blessing.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Sahl bin Sa'd (RA) states that a striped set of clothing with white edging was knitted for Rasulullaah ﷺ out of black wool. Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that the Prophet gave away a new striped garment to a Bedouin who asked for it, and died before a replacement was finished.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Aqeel (RA) narrates that to earn two Saa of dates he spent an entire night drawing water from a well with a rope tied to his back. He took one Saa to his…
narrations.summary: Abu Aqeel earned two saa of dates by a night of labour, gave one to charity, and was mocked by the hypocrites, which led to a verse being revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Salama and Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrate that Rasulullaah once called on the Sahabah (RA) for contributions because he intended dispatching a military…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf gave half his wealth and an Ansaari gave the produce of a night's labour; the hypocrites mocked both until a verse was revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zaid bin Abdi Rabbihi was the Sahabi who was shown the Adhaan in his dream. He once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ This orchard…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Zaid gave his orchard to the Prophet as charity; the Prophet returned it to his parents, who had depended on it, and it passed to their son after they died.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah SSI narrates that a man came to Rasulullaah ﷺ complaining of severe hunger. Rasulullaah ﷺ then sent a message to one of his wives (to send some food)…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that a hungry Ansaari guest was hosted by an Ansaari man and his wife, who put out their lamp and pretended to eat so the guest could eat, and Allaah praised their conduct and revealed the verse about preferring others.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that a goat's head was passed between seven houses because the people of each home preferred others above themselves. Although…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that a goat's head went round seven houses because each household preferred the others to itself.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a man came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "o Rasulullaah ﷺ A particular man has a date palm with which I need to set right a wall of mine. Please…
narrations.summary: A man wanted another's date palm to repair his wall; Abu Dahdaa bought it with his orchard and gave it to the Prophet, who promised him palms in Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Dahdaa approached Rasulullaah ﷺ when Allaah revealed the verse: (Tie u-jl ij) U?y Who is it that will lend to…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that Abu Dahdaa lent his orchard of six hundred palms to Allaah when the verse on good loans was revealed, and told his wife to leave it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that whenever Rasulullaah iili was asked for anything to draw a person to Islaam or to make him steadfast in it, he readily gave it. Therefore,…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet readily gave a man goats to draw him to Islaam, and the man urged his people to accept Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) reports that an Arab once came to Rasulullaah to ask for a piece of land between two mountains. Rasulullaah ﷺ had it given to him in…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit reports that an Arab received a written grant of land from the Prophet, accepted Islaam, and urged his tribe to do the same.

narrations.excerpt: In the story of how Hadhrat Safwaan bin Umayyah (RA) accepted Islaam, it has already passed that as Rasulullaah ﷺ was walking amongst the booty to have a look at it,…
narrations.summary: Safwaan bin Umayyah accepted Islaam on the spot when the Prophet gave him the valley of livestock he had been gazing at.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) says, "When (my father) Abu Bakr left with Rasulullaah ﷺ (for Hijrah), Abu Bakr took along all the money he had, which amounted to. Ave or six thousand…
narrations.summary: Asmaa tells how she calmed her blind grandfather Abu Quhaafa about her father Abu Bakr's departure for Hijrah by showing him stones under a cloth, which he took to be the money.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Khabbaab Sulami (RA) reports that Rasulullaah once delivered a sermon in which he encouraged the Sahabah (RA) to spend on the 'expedition of…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan pledged a hundred camels with their saddles for the Tabook expedition, then a second hundred when the Prophet urged again, and the Prophet said he need do no more optional deeds.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ gave encouragement three times and that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) took it upon himself to provide three hundred camels together…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan pledged three hundred camels for Tabook after the Prophet urged three times, and the Prophet said no sin would harm him after that day.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Samura (RA) narrates that on the occasion when Rasulullaah ﷺ was preparing the 'Expedition of Difficulty', Hadhrat Uthmaan came with a thousand…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Samura reports that Uthmaan emptied a thousand dinaars into the Prophet's bag, and the Prophet said no later deed of Uthmaan would harm him.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar 5S3.11SB states that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed, "O Do not forget this deed of Uthmaan." Rasulullaah ﷺ also added, "After…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the Prophet asked that Uthmaan's deed not be forgotten and that Uthmaan need do no more optional deeds.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfa bin Yamaan (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent someone to Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) to request his assistance for the 'Expedition of Difficulty Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfa bin Yamaan reports that Uthmaan sent ten thousand dinaars for the expedition, and the Prophet prayed for his forgiveness and released him from optional deeds.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) narrates that he was present when Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) handed over to Rasulullaah ﷺ what he needed to dispatch the 'Expedition of…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf says he was present when Uthmaan brought seven hundred awqiya of gold to the Prophet for the expedition.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qataadah reports that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) donated a thousand animals for the expedition to Tabook. Amongst these were fifty horses as well. (S) Hadhrat Hasan…
narrations.summary: Qataadah and Hasan report the numbers of camels and horses that Uthmaan gave for the Tabook expedition.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that while Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was in her room, she heard a lot of noise in Madinah. "What is that?" she enquired. The people informed her,…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha heard the noise of Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf's caravan of seven hundred camels, recalled the Prophet's words about him entering Jannah, and he gave the whole caravan away.

narrations.excerpt: Imaam Zuhri reports that during the lifetime of Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, donated half his wealth in the path of Allaah, which amounted to four…
narrations.summary: Imaam Zuhri reports Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf's large donations of money, horses and camels during the Prophet's lifetime.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Imaam Zuhri states that Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf donated five hundred camels in the path of Allaah.
narrations.summary: Another report from Zuhri says Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf donated five hundred camels in the path of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Imaam Zuhri reports that during the lifetime of Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Abdur narration. Rahmaan bin Auf donated half his wealth in the path of Allaah. Thereafter, he…
narrations.summary: Imaam Zuhri reports Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf's large donations of money, horses and camels during the Prophet's lifetime.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hizaam says that they had never heard of anyone in Madinah who provided more transport for people proceeding in the path of Allaah than Hadhrat Hakeem bin…
narrations.summary: Abu Hizaam relates that Hakeem bin Hizaam, the most generous provider of transport for those going out in the path of Allaah, mended satchels with rags and bought two pregnant camels with supplies and money for two Bedouins who came asking for transport.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hakeem bin Hizaam (RA) once sold a house to Hadhrat Mu'aawiya for sixty thousand Dirhams. Some people said to him, "By Allaah! Mu'aawiya has hoodwinked you (by…
narrations.summary: Hakeem bin Hizaam sells his house to Mu'aawiya for sixty thousand Dirhams, saying he had bought it in the Period of Ignorance for a bag of wine and was giving the price away for the poor and for freeing slaves; another report gives a price of a hundred thousand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA) once sold a property of his for two hundred camels. He then donated a hundred camels in the path of Allaah and…
narrations.summary: Naafi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar sold a property for two hundred camels, gave a hundred in charity, and made the riders promise not to sell them before Waadi Qura.

narrations.excerpt: it has already passed in a chapter describing the encouragement Rasulullaah gave to the Sahabah (RA) to spend in the path of Allaah that Hadhrat Umar gave a hundred…
narrations.summary: A translator's note recalls earlier donations for Tabook by Umar, Aasim, Abbaas, Talha, Sa'd bin Ubaadah, Muhammad bin Maslama and Qais bin Sala.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said (to his wives), "The one to meet me first (after death) from all of you is the one with the longest arms." The…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet's remark about long arms meant giving in charity, and that Zaynab bint Jahash had the longest arms because she gave away what she made by hand.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) states that Hadhrat Zaynab bint Jahash used to weave cloth and give it to those proceeding in battle, who sewed it and used it…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that Zaynab bint Jahash wove cloth for those going to battle, and that the women's jewellery filled a cloth laid before the Prophet for Tabook.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umayr bin Salama Duwali (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was sleeping under a tree at midday when a Bedouin lady arrived in Madinah. She searched around (for…
narrations.summary: Umar, resting at midday, hears a poor Bedouin woman with two children complain that the Zakaah collector Muhammad bin Maslama gave her nothing; Umar sends for him, then gives her a camel with flour and oil, and two more camels at Khaybar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam says that he once left with Hadhrat Umar (RA) to the marketplace where he met a young lady who said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! My husband has passed away and…
narrations.summary: Aslam reports that Umar met a young widow, daughter of Khufaaf bin Eema Ghifaari, and gave her a loaded camel with food, money and clothing, because her father had been at Hudaybiyyah and her brother had shared in the booty of a conquest.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hassaan bin Atiyya reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) relieved Hadhrat Mu'aawiya of his post as governor of Shaam, he sent Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Aamir bin Judhaym…
narrations.summary: After Umar sends Sa'eed bin Aamir to replace Mu'aawiya as governor of Shaam, and then sends a thousand dinaars, Sa'eed spends it on the poor rather than on his family, and when his wife complains he stays out of the house during the day.

narrations.excerpt: The narration of Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Saabit Jumhi states that whenever Hadhrat Sa'eed (RA) received his salary, he bought what was necessary for his family and then…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Saabit Jumhi reports that Sa'eed bin Aamir gave his salary away in charity, told his wife the rest was a loan, and rejected a warning about his family's rights, citing the Prophet's words that the poor believers will enter Jannah seventy years before others.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi reports, "When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once fell ill, a bunch of grapes was bought for him for one Dirham, When a poor person arrived there, Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Naafi reports that when Abdullaah bin Umar was ill and a bunch of grapes was bought for him, he gave it to a poor man, and the grapes were bought back and given to the beggar three times before Abdullaah could eat them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi says, "When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once fell ill, he desired to eat grapes. I bought a bunch of grapes for him for a Dirham and then placed it in…
narrations.summary: Naafi tells the same grapes incident in his own words: after the beggar's third or fourth return he rebuked him, bought the grapes back himself, and Abdullaah finally ate them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Nadhra reports, "It was during the first ten days of Dhul Hijjah that I visited Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Abul Aas (RA) in a room that he reserved for conversing…
narrations.summary: After Abu Nadhra wished aloud that he could afford a sheep for Eid, Uthmaan bin Abul Aas sent him a bag of fifty Dirhams, having first asked a passer-by what he had paid for his sheep.

narrations.excerpt: Imaam Maalik reports that the report reached him that a poor person once came to beg from Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) the wife of Rasulullaah ﷺ. She was fasting that day and had…
narrations.summary: Imaam Maalik reports that Aa'isha, fasting with only one piece of bread at home, gave it to a beggar, and that evening was sent cooked meat; a second report says she gave a single grape to a beggar and explained the Qur'aan's teaching that an atom's weight of good is seen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan narrates that when Hadhrat Haaritha bin Nu'maan SI lost his eyesight, he tied a string from the place where he performed salaah to the door of his room.…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan reports that the blind Haaritha bin Numaan gave charity to beggars with his own hand, guided by a string, because the Prophet had said that giving to the poor personally saves one from a gruesome death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr Laythi narrates that they were with Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa when a beggar came. Hadhrat Waathila (RA) took a piece of bread, put a coin on it and then stood…
narrations.summary: Amr Laythi reports that Waathila bin Asqa handed a beggar a piece of bread with a coin on it himself, and explained that walking to give forgives sins and placing the gift in the hand forgives more.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) used to gather all of his family to eat from one platter every night. It often happened that when he heard the plea…
narrations.summary: Naafi says Abdullaah bin Umar had his whole household eat from one platter each night, and when a poor man called he gave away his share; if nothing was left over he went without food the next morning.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ entered the Masjid one day wearing a shawl from Najraan that had thick edging. A Bedouin came from behind and pulled at a…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that a Bedouin pulled the Prophet's Najraan shawl so hard it marked his neck and demanded some of Allaah's wealth; the Prophet smiled and told the Sahabah to give him something.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) says, "We used to sit with Rasulullaah ﷺ in the Masjid in the mornings and when he stood up to leave, we would also stand and remain standing…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that a Bedouin demanding two camels pulled the Prophet's shawl until it marked his neck; the Prophet forgave him and ordered two camels given, one loaded with barley and one with dates.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Muqarrin (RA) narrates that they were four hundred people from the Muzaynah tribe who came to Rasulullaah ﷺ. After Rasulullaah had taught them aspects…
narrations.summary: Nu'maan bin Muqarrin reports that four hundred Muzaynah travellers with no provisions were fed by Umar from a room of dates that did not visibly diminish, as the Prophet had ordered.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dhukayn bin Sa'eed Khath'ami (RA) reports that they were four hundred and forty people who approached Rasulullaah ﷺ for food. Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Dhukayn bin Sa'eed reports that four hundred and forty people asked the Prophet for food; Umar objected that his dates would last only his family through the summer, then obeyed the Prophet's repeated order and fed them from a heap of dates that seemed undiminished.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dhukayn (RA) says, "We were four hundred people when we asked Rasulullaah ﷺ for food." The narration is then that same as the above narration but with the…
narrations.summary: Dhukayn reports the same dates incident, this time with four hundred people; Umar first objects, Abu Bakr tells him to listen and obey, and Umar replies that he hears and obeys.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aflah bin Katheer says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) never refused any beggar and even a leper with fingers dripping with blood could be seen eating with him…
narrations.summary: Aflah bin Katheer says Abdullaah bin Umar never refused a beggar, and that even a leper with blood-dripping fingers ate from the same plate as him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan Basri reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once brought his Sadaqah to Rasulullaah ﷺ, He secretly gave it to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ This is my…
narrations.summary: Hasan Basri reports that Abu Bakr gave his sadaqah secretly and Umar gave openly, and the Prophet said the difference between their gifts was like the difference between their words, Abu Bakr's intention being the purer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once announced, "Who will purchase the well of Roomah for us and donate it as Sadaqah for the Muslim public?…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the Prophet asked who would buy the well of Roomah for the Muslim public as a sadaqah, and Uthmaan bought it and donated it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Basheer Aslami (RA) narrates that when the Muhaajireen arrived in Madinah, the water did not agree with them. There was a well called Roomah which was owned by a…
narrations.summary: Basheer Aslami reports that the Muhaajireen disliked the water of Madinah, and that after a Ghifaari owner declined the Prophet's offer of a fountain in Jannah for his well, Uthmaan bought it, asked whether he too would receive that fountain, and donated the well.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Su'daa the wife of Hadhrat Talha (RA) reports that Hadhrat Talha gave away a hundred thousand Dirhams as Sadaqah on a single day and that he was delayed from…
narrations.summary: Su'daa, wife of Talha, reports that Talha gave away a hundred thousand Dirhams in one day, and that he was late to the Masjid because she had to stitch together his only garment.

narrations.excerpt: The narration has already passed in which it is mentioned that Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf donated half his wealth in the path of Allaah, which amounted to four…
narrations.summary: A cross-reference to an earlier narration: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf gave half his wealth (four thousand Dirhams), then forty thousand Dirhams and forty thousand Dinaars in the path of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saa'ib (RA) the son of Hadhrat Abu Lubaabah (RA) reports from his father that when Allaah forgave him, he approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ 1…
narrations.summary: Saa'ib reports from his father Abu Lubaabah that after Allaah forgave him, Abu Lubaabah offered to give all his wealth in charity, and the Prophet said a third would suffice, which he gave.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Humayd (RA) says, "I went with my uncle to visit Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) in Madaa'in (where he served as governor) as he was making something with the…
narrations.summary: Nu'maan bin Humayd, visiting Salmaan Faarsi, sees him earn his living by buying palm leaves and making goods to sell, putting one part back into more leaves, one on his family and one in charity, and vows to continue even if Umar stops him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Mas'ood (RA) narrates, "we were with Rasulullaah ﷺ on an expedition when we started experiencing extreme hardship. I could see the strains of hardship on the…
narrations.summary: Abu Mas'ood reports that during a hard expedition Uthmaan bought fourteen loaded camels and sent nine to the Prophet, who raised his hands in a long prayer for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) once stated, "For me to fulfil the necessities of a Muslim family for a month or for a week or for whatever period of time Allaah…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says that providing for a Muslim family's needs for a while is dearer to him than hajj after hajj, and that giving his brother a small utensil as a gift for Allaah's pleasure is dearer than spending a Dinaar in the path of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat All (RA) once mentioned, "To gather a few of my friends to share a Saa of food is more beloved to me than proceeding to the marketplace to purchase a slave and…
narrations.summary: Ali says that gathering a few friends to share a Saa of food is dearer to him than going to the market to buy a slave and free him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdul Waahid bin Ayman reports from his father that when some guests came to Hadhrat Jaabir (RA), he brought some bread and vinegar for them and said, "Eat this…
narrations.summary: Abdul Waahid bin Ayman reports from his father that Jaabir served his guests bread and vinegar, quoting the Prophet that vinegar is an excellent gravy and that those who look down on what is offered are destroyed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Humayd Taweel reports that when some people came to visit Hadhrat Anas when he fell ill, he said to his slave, "Bring something for our guests even though it be a…
narrations.summary: Humayd Taweel reports that when guests visited the ill Anas, he told his slave to bring something for them even if only bread, quoting the Prophet that good character leads to Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shaqeeq bin Salama (RA) reports that he once visited Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi with a friend. Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) said to them, "Had Rasulullaah ﷺ not forbidden us…
narrations.summary: Shaqeeq bin Salama reports that Salmaan Faarsi, with only bread and salt for his guests, pawned his jug to buy mint, and told a guest who had wished for mint that contentment with what Allaah provides would have saved the jug.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hamza bin Suhayb reports that Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) was in the habit of feeding a lot of people. Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said to him, "O Suhayb! You feed too many…
narrations.summary: Hamza bin Suhayb reports that Umar told Suhayb he fed too many people and was being extravagant, and Suhayb replied that the Prophet said the best people feed others and return greetings.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "I was once sitting at home when Rasulullaah passed by and motioned to me. I therefore stood up and went to him. Taking me by the hand,…
narrations.summary: Jaabir says the Prophet took him by the hand to one of his wives' rooms, where they shared three pieces of bread, and that the Prophet called the vinegar an excellent gravy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once saw Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) leading a camel laden with flour, butter and honey. Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Salaam reports that the Prophet had Uthmaan's camel-load of flour, butter and honey cooked in a stone pot and shared it with the Sahabah, calling it khabees.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ had a large plate that had to be carried by four men. it was called "Gharraa" and was brought out at…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Busr says the Prophet's large plate, carried by four men, was brought out after the Duha prayer; the Prophet sat squatting, calling himself a generous slave and not an arrogant tyrant, and told them to eat from the sides.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) the son of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) reports, "It was the practice of my father to engage in conversation with Rasulullaah ﷺ at nights. Therefore,…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan, son of Abu Bakr, reports that when guests came, Abu Bakr sent portions of camel meat to the Prophet's wives and then fed the rest to the Muhaajireen and Ansaar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam reports, "I once informed Hadhrat Umar (RA) that there was a blind camel amongst the pack animals. He said, 'Give it to some family who can derive some…
narrations.summary: Aslam relates that Umar ordered a blind Jizya camel slaughtered, sent portions of the meat to the Prophet's wives with Hafsah's share last, and then invited the Muhaajireen and Ansaar to eat the rest.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salama bin Akwa (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydullaah purchased a well at the foot of a mountain, he invited people for a meal. It was then that…
narrations.summary: Salama bin Akwa reports that when Talha bought a well at the foot of a mountain and invited people to a meal, the Prophet called him Fayyaadh, an extremely generous man.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) says, "The person who most benefited the poor was Ja'far bin Abu Taalib. He would take us home and feed us with whatever he had in his house. In…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah says Ja'far bin Abi Taalib did more for the poor than anyone, taking them home to feed them and breaking open his butter container so they could lick what remained.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) says, "I prepared some food for Rasulullaah ﷺ and went to (invite) him whilst he sat amongst a group of Sahabah (RA). I stood in front of him and…
narrations.summary: Suhayb reports that he prepared food for the Prophet and invited him; when the Prophet asked whether the others could come too, Suhayb agreed, and everyone ate and food was left over.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Qais reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) never ate without a poor person to join him. This eventually injured his health (because the poor…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Qais reports that Abdullaah bin Umar never ate without a poor person with him, until his health suffered and his wife gave him a date drink; a second report in the same entry says he ate only when an orphan was at the table.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that whenever Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) ate lunch or dinner (the Arabs never ate breakfast), he would invite an orphan from the vicinity. When…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Abdullaah bin Umar invited an orphan to every lunch or dinner and gave an orphan the cup from his hand; Maymoon bin Mahraan reports that Ibn Umar's wife, to keep the poor from waiting on the road, sent them food with instructions, so he had no dinner that night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ja'far Qaari says, "My master (Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ayaash bin Abu Rabee'ah Makhzoomi) instructed me to proceed with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar on a journey,…
narrations.summary: Abu Ja'far Qaari, serving Abdullaah bin Umar on a journey, describes how Ibn Umar invited local people to share each meal and made room for a poor black boy beside him at Juhfa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ja'far Qaari says, "I accompanied Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar on a journey from Makkah to Madinah. Around his large dish containing his sons, his companions…
narrations.summary: Abu Ja'far Qaari describes how Ibn Umar's travelling meals fed everyone who came to his large dish, and Ma'n reports that Ibn Umar invited the poor but not the well-off.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas Feeds People.
narrations.summary: Section title only, naming Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas as one who fed people; no narration follows.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Rabee'ah reports that he once performed Hajj during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA). With him was Hadhrat Muntasir bin Haarith and a group…
narrations.summary: Sulaymaan bin Rabee'ah reports that in Mu'aawiya's caliphate a group of Basrah Qurraa found Abdullaah bin Amr in Makkah with three hundred camels, one hundred to carry his brothers and two hundred loaded for his guests and travellers, and then met him at the Kabah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat. Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) narrates that he once went to Rasulullaah ﷺ with a large utensil full of camel's brains. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Abu Thaabit! What is this?"…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Ubaadah brings the Prophet a large dish of camel brains, saying he has slaughtered forty camels to feed him, and the Prophet eats and prays for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) once invited Rasulullaah ﷺ (for a meal). When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived (at Hadhrat Sa'd's house), Hadhrat Sa'd…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Sa'd bin Ubaadah served the Prophet dates, bread and milk, and that the Prophet then prayed for the righteous, fasting people and angels to bless Sa'd's household.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration also from Hadhrat Anas (RA) states that Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) served some sesame seeds and dates to Rasulullaah ﷺ.
narrations.summary: Anas gives a second, brief account in which Sa'd served sesame seeds and dates to the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa SSI reports that he once saw Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) announce from his house, "Whoever wishes to eat fat or meat should go to Sa'd bin Ubaadahf I then…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that Sa'd bin Ubaadah would announce from his house an open invitation to anyone wanting meat or fat, that his son did the same after him, and that Abdullaah bin Umar confirmed no one was as generous as that father and son.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Mas'ood Ansaari (RA) reports that there was a Sahabi from amongst the Ansaar who was called Abu Shu'ayb. He had a slave who was an expert in cooking meat. He…
narrations.summary: Abu Mas'ood Ansaari reports that Abu Shu'ayb invited the Prophet and four others to a meal, and when a fifth man came along, the Prophet let Abu Shu'ayb decide, and he welcomed him.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Abu Shu'ayb (RA) once saw Rasulullaah ﷺ , he noticed the sign of hunger on Rasulullaah ﷺ's face. He then said to his slave,…
narrations.summary: Another narration says Abu Shu'ayb noticed the Prophet's hunger and told his slave to cook for five people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates, "A tailor once invited Rasulullaah ﷺ to share a meal that he had prepared. I accompanied Rasulullaah ﷺ for the meal. He served barley bread to…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that a tailor served the Prophet barley bread and pumpkin gravy, that the Prophet searched the plate for the pumpkin pieces, and that Anas loved pumpkin from that day on.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates, "As we were busy digging (the trench) for the Battle of Khandaq, an extremely hard boulder became an obstacle. When the Sahabah (RA)…
narrations.summary: During the digging of the Trench, Jaabir's wife cooked one saa of barley and a kid goat, and at the Prophet's word the food and bread multiplied until all the Sahabah were fed with plenty left over.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "My mother cooked some food and asked me to invite Rasulullaah ﷺ for a meal. I went to Rasulullaah iffll and whispered to him, 'My mother has…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that when his mother cooked and asked him to invite the Prophet, the Prophet had about fifty men come in ten at a time, and all ate their fill while food remained.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Abu Talha (RA) once said to his wife (my mother) Ummu Sulaym, 'I have heard Rasulullaah fill's voice go very weak and I know that it is because…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Abu Talha and Ummu Sulaym fed the Prophet and some seventy or eighty men from a few loaves of barley bread and a little butter, in batches of ten.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that (after re-entering the fold of Islaam after leaving it) Hadhrat Ash'ath (RA) was brought as a prisoner to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (who…
narrations.summary: Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that after Ash'ath returned to Islaam, Abu Bakr released his shackles and married him to his sister, and Ash'ath then slaughtered camels in the market and told the people to eat them as his waleema.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan bin Hakeem reports from his mother that Hadhrat Abu Barzah Siigig kept a large dish of Thareed ready every morning and evening for the widows, orphans and…
narrations.summary: Hasan bin Hakeem reports, from his mother, that Abu Barzah kept a large dish of thareed ready each morning and evening for widows, orphans and the poor.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Talha bin Amr (RA) says, "Whenever a person came to meet Rasulullaah ﷺ in Madinah, he stayed with someone he knew, if he did not know anyone, he stayed with the…
narrations.summary: Talha bin Amr, one of the men of the Suffa, reports that after the men complained of hunger and dates burning their stomachs, the Prophet spoke of his own hardships, and that he once told a man sleeping face-down in the Masjid that this was Shaytaan's way of lying.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Fudaalah Laythi (RA) says, "Whenever a person came to meet Rasulullaah ﷺ in Madinah, he stayed with someone he knew. If he did not know anyone, he stayed on the…
narrations.summary: Fudaalah Laythi relates that visitors to Madinah stayed with acquaintances or on the Suffa, and that when Companions complained about eating dates, the Prophet told them a time would come when large platters of food would be served morning and evening.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salama bin Akwa (RA) narrates that after leading the salaah, Rasulullaah iffi? would turn to the Sahabah (RA) and say to them, "Each of you should take as many…
narrations.summary: Salama bin Akwa relates that after leading salaah the Prophet told the Companions each to take home as many guests as they could host, and that he himself took those who remained.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen reports that in the evenings Rasulullaah ﷺ used to distribute the men of Sulfa amongst the rest of the Sahabah (RA). Some would take one…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports that each evening the Prophet distributed the men of the Suffa among the Companions, and that Sa'd bin Ubaadah took eighty of them home every night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once called out, 'O Abu Hirr!' 'I am at your service, O Rasulullaah ﷺ ,' I responded. He said, 'Go to the men of Suffa…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that the Prophet sent him to invite all the men of the Suffa, who had neither wealth nor family, and that the Prophet gave them all the Sadaqah he received and shared any gifts with them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) says, "I was amongst the men of Sulfa, Every evening we would go to Rasulullaah fill's door and he would instruct someone who would take one of us…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr relates that each evening the men of the Suffa were taken in as guests in turn, and that when he was lying face down in the Masjid the Prophet nudged him with his foot and said that this is how Shaytaan lies.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tughfah bin Qais (RA) narrates, "in compliance with the instruction of Rasulullaah ﷺ, some Sahabah (RA) took one person (from the men of the Suffa as his guest)…
narrations.summary: Tughfah bin Qais recounts being taken with four other men to Aa'isha, who served them meat, dates and milk, and then being nudged awake in the Masjid by the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jahjaa Ghifaari US says, "I arrived (in Madinah) with a group from my tribe with the intention of accepting Islaam.. When we presented ourselves before…
narrations.summary: Jahjaa Ghifaari, who came to accept Islaam, recounts how the Prophet hosted him and his group, and the Prophet explained that a believer eats to fill one intestine while a disbeliever eats to fill seven.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) says, "We were amongst the men of Suffa when Ramadhaan arrived and we all fasted. Whenever the time came to end the fast, one of the Sahabah (RA) who had…
narrations.summary: An unnamed man of the Suffa reports that on two evenings of Ramadhaan no one came to take the group to eat, so the Prophet prayed for Allaah's grace and mercy, and a roasted goat and bread then arrived.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Bakr (RA) reports, "Because the men of Suffa were poor people, Rasulullaah iilf once said to the Sahabah (RA), 'whoever has food for two…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Bakr reports that his father's guests would not eat until Abu Bakr came home, that Abu Bakr scolded him and then ate with them, and that the food multiplied until all were full and more remained.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Abdul Azeez narrates, that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) would proceed in jihaad one year and his son Hadhrat Qais (RA) would proceed the following…
narrations.summary: Yahya bin Abdul Azeez reports that when Sa'd bin Ubaadah was away on jihaad and many guests came to the Prophet, Sa'd told his slave Nistaas that his son Qais would take provisions from the storehouse, and Qais did so, striking Nistaas and bringing a hundred wasaq.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maymoona bint Haarith (RA) (one of Rasulullaah ﷺ's wives) reports, "The Bedouins always came to Madinah and Rasulullaah ﷺ would instruct someone to take a Bedouin…
narrations.summary: Maymoona bint Haarith reports that during a drought a Bedouin ate all the Prophet's little food, and that after he accepted Islaam he ate only a little, so the Prophet said a Kaafir eats to fill seven intestines and a Mu'min only one.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam reports that during the "Year of Ashes (destruction)', Arabs from all over collected in Madinah. Hadhrat Umar Sins appointed certain persons to go to these…
narrations.summary: Aslam reports that in the Year of Ashes Umar appointed four men to distribute food to the Bedouins camped around Madinah, counted his nightly guests as they grew to fifty thousand, and had the Bedouins sent home with transport and provisions after the rains.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Firaas Daylami reports that from the camels that Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas sent from Egypt, Hadhrat Umar (RA) would have twenty slaughtered every day for his table…
narrations.summary: Firaas Daylami reports that Umar had twenty camels, sent by Amr bin Al Aas from Egypt, slaughtered each day for his table to feed those hit by the drought.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was going on his usual rounds one night when he came across a woman in a house surrounded by crying children. The woman had a…
narrations.summary: Aslam reports that Umar found a woman whose hungry children were crying over a pot of water, fetched flour, fat, dates, clothing and money from the treasury, carried it to her home himself, and cooked for the family until they were full.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Aslam said, "I accompanied Umar (RA) one night to Harrah and Aqim. When we came to Saraar, we noticed a fire burning. He said, 'O…
narrations.summary: Another report from Aslam says he went with Umar at night towards Saraar, found a woman with her children by a fire, and that the rest matches the account above.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Ukaydir (the ruler of Dowmatul Jandal) once sent a bag full of sweetmeats as a gift to Rasulullaah ﷺ. When Rasulullaah had performed the…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Ukaydir, ruler of Dowmatul Jandal, sent the Prophet a bag of sweetmeats, which he shared around, and that when Jaabir had already had a piece, the Prophet gave him another for his sisters.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan (RA) reports, "Ukaydir who was the ruler of Dowmatul Jandal once sent a bag full of sweetmeats as you may have already seen as a gift to Rasulullaah ﷺ. By…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that when Ukaydir's bag of sweets came, the Prophet's household had little food, so the Prophet had it passed around the Sahabah, and told Khaalid bin Waleed, who had taken from it twice, to eat and feed his family.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once distributed some dates amongst the Sahabah (RA). He gave each person seven dates. I also received seven dates, one…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet gave each Companion seven dates, and that one of his own seven had no seed and was the best of them, being firm and slow to chew.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Anas Si states that when some dates were once brought to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he shared it with the Sahabah (RA). Rasulullaah ﷺ was sitting in a…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that when dates were brought to the Prophet, he shared them with the Companions while eating quickly, apparently because he was about to leave.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Layth bin Sa'd reports that a severe drought afflicted the people of Madinah during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Umar (RA), in what was called the Year of Ashes.…
narrations.summary: Layth bin Sa'd reports that in the Year of Ashes Umar wrote to Amr bin Al Aas in Egypt for help, and Amr replied that a train of camels was on its way.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) then sent a train of camels so large that when the first camel reached Madinah, the last camel was still leaving Egypt. When the camels…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Al Aas sends so many camels that the first reaches Madinah as the last leaves Egypt, and Umar has Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf, Zubayr and Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas give every household a camel with its provisions.

narrations.excerpt: A narration from Hadhrat Aslam also mentions the letter that Hadhrat Umar SUM wrote to Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA). The narration also states that when the first camel…
narrations.summary: Aslam reports that Umar asked Zubayr to take the first camel to Najd and bring back families, and when Zubayr excused himself and another man did too, Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah took the task and accepted a thousand dinaars from Umar only after insistence.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) reports that he brought to Rasulullaah ﷺ a prisoner (of war that his people had captured). When Hadhrat Jaz (RA) accepted Islaam and Rasulullaah ﷺ intended…
narrations.summary: After a captive named Jaz accepted Islaam, the Prophet sent him to Aa'isha for two shawls, and she gave him two of her own, with the narrator noting that Arab women did not expose themselves because of hijaab.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ja'far bin Muhammad reports from his father that when some clothing came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) from Yemen, he distributed it amongst the people. As Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Ja'far bin Muhammad reports that Umar distributed new clothing, but was distressed when Hasan and Husayn came without any because the garments were too large for them, so he had two sets sent from Yemen for them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shafaa bint Abdullaah Adawiyyah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar once sent a message that she should come to see him the following morning. She says, "When I got…
narrations.summary: Shafaa bint Abdullaah reports that when Umar gave Aatika bint Usayd a better shawl than hers, she objected that she had come to Islaam first and was Umar's cousin, and Umar explained he preferred Aatika as closer kin to the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asbagh bin Nubaata reports that a man came to Hadhrat Ali (RA) saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! I have a need that I have already placed before Allaah before coming…
narrations.summary: Asbagh bin Nubaata reports that Ali, to spare a destitute man the humiliation of begging, had him write his request in the dirt, then gave him a set of clothing and a hundred gold coins, quoting the Prophet's saying to treat people according to their status.

narrations.excerpt: When a beggar once came to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA), he asked the man, "Do you testify that there is none, worthy of worship but Allaah and that Muhammad ﷺ is…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas asks a beggar whether he testifies to Allaah's oneness and fasts in Ramadhaan, then gives him a garment, quoting the Prophet that a Muslim who clothes another stays under Allaah's protection as long as a rag of it remains on him.

narrations.excerpt: The Practice of Hadhrat Qais bin Sa'd (RA) Hadhrat jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched an army under the command of Hadhrat Qais bin Sa'd…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that when Qais bin Sa'd's army went hungry on an expedition, Qais slaughtered nine riding animals to feed them, and the Prophet said generosity was the hallmark of that family.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Raafl bin Khudayj (RA) states that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah and Hadhrat Umar (RA) both approached Hadhrat Qais bin Sa'd and implored him not to…
narrations.summary: Raafi bin Khadeej relates that Abu Ubaydah and Umar pleaded with Qais bin Sa'd not to slaughter more camels, but he did so to feed the army during the Expedition of Leaves, and the Prophet praised him as being from the house of generosity.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat jaabir (RA) narrates, "Qais bin Sa'd bin Ubaadah IS once passed by us during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ when we were suffering severe hunger. He slaughtered seven…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that Qais bin Sa'd bin Ubaadah slaughtered seven camels to feed his hungry expedition, and that on the shore they then found a giant fish which fed them for three days.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) arrived in Shaam and was with the commanders of the various armies, Hadhrat Bilaal came calling, "Umar!…
narrations.summary: Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that when Umar reached Shaam, Bilaal rebuked him that the commanders ate well while the Muslims under them were ill fed, and Umar made each commander guarantee provision for every Muslim under his command.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah Howzini reports that he once met Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) the Mu'adhin of Rasulullaah ﷺ in Aleppo. When he asked Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) to explain to him how…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah Howzini relates Bilaal's account of the Prophet's finances: Bilaal borrowed on his behalf to help the destitute, a creditor pressed him, and four camels sent as a gift from Fidak let him settle every debt; the Prophet then gave away what remained rather than die with wealth in his possession.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Salama (RA) narrates, "I know of the most amount of wealth that came to Rasulullaah ﷺ during his entire lifetime, it was during the early hours of the night…
narrations.summary: Ummu Salama describes how a bag of eight hundred dirhams reached the Prophet at night, and how he kept breaking off his salaah to think about it until he had distributed all of it at dawn.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Alaa bin Hadhrami once sent eighty thousand to Rasulullaah ﷺ form Bahrain. Never before or afterwards had so much…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa relates that Alaa bin Hadhrami sent eighty thousand from Bahrain; the Prophet gave it out on a mat without counting, and when Abbaas, who had paid his own and Aqeel's ransom after Badr, asked for a share, the Prophet let him take as much as he could carry.

narrations.excerpt: as Khali fall Hadhrat Sahl bin Abi Hathma and others reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had the Baytul Maal (public treasury) in Sunh. It was known to all and no one…
narrations.summary: Sahl bin Abi Hathma reports that Abu Bakr kept the public treasury unguarded because it had a lock, distributed all of it, and after his death Umar's trusted men found only a single dirham in it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ismaa'eel bin Muhammad reports that whenever Hadhrat Abu Bakr distributed wealth amongst the people he always gave equally. Hadhrat Umar once objected saying, "O…
narrations.summary: Ismaa'eel bin Muhammad reports that Abu Bakr gave everyone equal shares; when Umar objected about the Badr veterans, Abu Bakr said worldly provision should be equal and the Badr veterans' superiority would show in their reward in the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when it was mentioned to Hadhrat Abu Bakr that he ought to give preference to some people in the distribution of wealth, he said, "Their…
narrations.summary: Three further reports show Abu Bakr refusing to favour any group in distribution: virtue is rewarded by Allaah in the Aakhirah and equality suits worldly life, and he asked whether he should buy the Muhaajireen's precedence from them, while Umar's objections are recorded.

narrations.excerpt: About Hadhrat Umar (RA), the freed slave of Ghafra reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, plenty of wealth arrived from Bahrain. Hadhrat Abu Bakr made an…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Abdullaah, freed slave of Ghafra, reports that after the Prophet's death wealth came from Bahrain; Abu Bakr paid Jaabir the handfuls the Prophet had promised him, then gave every person ten dirhams, and twenty the following year, refusing to favour the early Muhaajireen and Ansaar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) the freed slave of Ghafra reports the narration appearing above. The narration continues to state that after Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) passed away, Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Umar, as Khalifah, sets the allowances by precedence in Islaam and closeness to the Prophet, giving Badr veterans and their sons more, and answers the objections of Safiyya, Juwayriyya, Talha, Muhammad bin Abdullaah bin Jahash and his own son Abdullaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) and Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib both report that Hadhrat Umar (RA) stipulated five thousand for the Muhaajireen, four thousand for the Ansaar…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik and Sa'eed bin Musayyib report that Umar's allowances were five thousand for the Muhaajireen, four thousand for the Ansaar and four thousand for the sons of Muhaajireen who missed Badr, and that Abdullaah bin Umar refused a share he had no right to.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was stipulating allowances, he stipulated two thousand Dirhams for Hadhrat Abdullaah, the son of Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Aslam relates that Umar gave Abdullaah, son of Handhala, two thousand, more than Talha's Muhaajir cousin, because of his father Handhala's courage at Uhud; the report breaks off mid-sentence.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naashira bin Sumay Yazani reports, that on the day Hadhrat Umar was in Jaabiya, he heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) delivering a lecture in which he said, "Allaah has made…
narrations.summary: Naashira bin Sumay Yazani reports Umar's lecture at Jaabiya: he gave the Muhaajireen of Badr the most, the Ansaar of Badr less and the Uhud fighters three thousand, gave all the Prophet's wives an equal amount after Aa'isha pointed out the Prophet treated them equally, and defended removing Khaalid bin Waleed from command, which Abu Amr bin Hafs disputed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) says that he brought- to Umar bin Khattaab eight hundred thousand Dirhams from Abu Moosa Ash'ari. Hadhrat Umar asked, 'What have you come with?'…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports bringing Umar eight hundred thousand dirhams from Abu Moosa; Umar checked that it was lawful and stayed awake all night, then consulted the Sahabah and had a register drawn up, starting with the Prophet's family and the Banu Haashim.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jubayr bin Huwayrith (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) consulted with the people concerning the filing of a register. Hadhrat (RA) advisedhim to annually…
narrations.summary: Jubayr bin Huwayrith reports that Umar consulted on keeping a register; after Uthmaan and Waleed bin Hishaam urged it, Umar had Aqeel, Makhrama bin Naufal and Jubayr bin Mut'im record people by status, starting with the Prophet and his kin, and then Abu Bakr's tribe and his own.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam reports that (after Hadhrat Umar (RA) opposed the view to place him and his tribe after Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and his tribe) the Banu Adi (the tribe of…
narrations.summary: Aslam reports that when Umar put his own tribe after Abu Bakr's, the Banu Adi called him the successor of Rasulullaah; Umar corrected them that he succeeded Abu Bakr, and said honour comes only through the Prophet and reward only through deeds, not lineage.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar bin Abdullaah (RA) the- freed slave of Ghafra reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, plenty of wealth arrived from Bahrain. He then narrated the entire…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Abdullaah, freed slave of Ghafra, repeats the report of wealth from Bahrain after the Prophet's death, and Umar's Jumu'ah address answers rumours of a quick pledge after his death: he would switch to Abu Bakr's equal distribution if he lived.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that once after Hadhrat Umar (RA) had distributed money amongst the people, there was still some left over in the Baytul Maal. Hadhrat Abbaas (RA)…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that after Umar had distributed the money, some remained, and Abbaas argued that as the uncle of the Prophet he deserved it more than the uncle of Musa, so Umar gave the rest to Abbaas.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that when a perfume holder once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA), those around him looked at him to see whom he would give it to. He said, "Would…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha relates that Umar sent her a perfume container, asking permission because of the Prophet's love for her; she remarked on how many conquests Umar had made after the Prophet and prayed not to live to see his next gift.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) says that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had appointed him to collect the Zakaah. However, by the time he returned, Hadhrat Abu Bakr had already…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik relates that Abu Bakr had sent him to collect zakaah, Abu Bakr died before he returned, and Umar let him keep the four thousand collected, making him the richest person in Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr reports that while people were busy taking their gifts before Hadhrat umar (RA), he looked up and was surprised to see a man with a…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr relates that Umar gave a wounded man four thousand dirhams in four instalments; when the man left embarrassed, Umar said he would have kept giving until nothing was left, because of the scar from his wound in the path of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) distributed things amongst the people thrice in a year. When some wealth arrived from Isfahaan, he announced, "Come early in the morning for the fourth round…
narrations.summary: Ali distributes the wealth from Isfahaan three times a year and, announcing that he is not their treasurer, gives away everything, even the ropes that held the animals.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) instructed (the public treasurer) Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Arqam (RA) to distribute everything in the Baytul Maal every month.…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed narrates that Umar ordered the treasurer Abdullaah bin Arqam to distribute the Baytul Maal monthly, then weekly, then daily, and rejected a suggestion to keep a reserve as Shaytaan speaking, saying he would follow the Prophet's preparation of obedience to Allaah and His Rasool.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that some wealth once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) from Iraq. He was about to distribute it when someone stood up to say, "O Ameerul…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that when wealth from Iraq arrived, Umar refused a suggestion to hold a reserve for future emergencies, saying he would not disobey Allaah today for tomorrow's dangers and would prepare for the Muslims as the Prophet had.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salamah bin Sa'eed reports that when some wealth once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) approached him saying, "Why do you rather not…
narrations.summary: Salamah bin Sa'eed reports that when Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf urged keeping a reserve, Umar said the idea came from Shaytaan, quoted the verse promising a way out for the one who has taqwa, and warned that Shaytaan's words would become a test for later generations.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote the following letter to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) I wish that there comes a day in the year when here remains not…
narrations.summary: Hasan narrates that Umar wrote to Abu Moosa Ash'ari that he wished a day would come when the Baytul Maal was empty, so that Allaah would know he had given every person his right.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan also reports that Hadhrat umar (RA) wrote to Hadhrat Hudhayfah that he must give every person his dues and specified allowances. Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA)…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Umar wrote to Hudhayfah to pay everyone his dues; Hudhayfah replied that a large sum still remained, and Umar ordered it distributed, saying it was the people's property and belonged neither to him nor his family.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat All bin Rabee'ah waalibi reports that Ibn Nabbaaj once came to Hadhrat Ali and said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! The Baytul Maal of the Muslims is full of gold and…
narrations.summary: Ali bin Rabee'ah Waalibi reports that when Ibn Nabbaaj told Ali the Baytul Maal was full of gold and silver, Ali distributed all of it to the people of Kufa and then prayed two rakaahs in the emptied treasury; Mujamma Taymi adds that Ali swept it and prayed there, hoping it would testify for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Alaa reports from his grandfather that he heard Hadhrat Ali say, "I have received nothing from your spoils of war besides this date container that a…
