narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Alaa reports that Ali had received only one date container as his share and distributed the whole Baytul Maal; Antara Shaybaani reports Ali collecting from artisans and refusing to keep anything overnight; Abu Ubayd, through Antara, reports Qambar's hidden gold dish, which Ali weighed out and gave away.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam reports that he heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) say, "Gather around to consult and ponder about who should be the recipients of this wealth. (When the people…
narrations.summary: Aslam reports Umar's consultation on who should receive the wealth, quoting the Qur'anic verses on the booty of the villages and the rights of the Muhaajireen and Ansaar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "By Allaah! This wealth is not only for these people (there are others also as mentioned in the forthcoming verse). ftf should also be given to)…
narrations.summary: Umar says the wealth belongs to more than those first named, including those who come after, citing the verse of prayer for the brothers who preceded them in Imaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "By Allaah! There is not a single Muslim who does not have a right to this wealth, whether it is given to him or not, even though he may be a…
narrations.summary: Umar says there is no Muslim, even a shepherd in Aden, who has no right to the wealth.

narrations.excerpt: Narrating the same incident, Hadhrat Maalik bin Aws bin Hadathaan reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) also recited the following verses: Alms (zakaah) are only for the poor,…
narrations.summary: Maalik bin Aws bin Hadathaan reports that Umar recited the verses on the recipients of zakaah and on the one-fifth share of spoils, and concluded that zakaah is reserved for those groups.

narrations.excerpt: J Uf The booty that Allaah granted His Rasool ﷺ (without a battle being fought) from the people of the villages is for Allaah (to be distributed as Allaah pleases), for…
narrations.summary: Umar recites the verses on the booty of the villages and on the Muhaajireen and Ansaar, and says the verse covers every Muslim, so each will receive his right even if he is a shepherd in the upper reaches of Yemen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Su'da (RA) narrates, "I once went to (my husband) Talha bin Ubaydullaah and noticed that he was carrying a burden of grief, 'what is the matter?1 I asked, 'Did we…
narrations.summary: Su'da relates that Talha was distressed by wealth he did not know what to do with, so she advised him to give it to his family and tribe, and his treasurer later said the sum came to four hundred thousand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that Hadhrat Talha (RA) once sold a piece of land he owned for seven hundred thousand. Because the money stayed the night with him, he stayed awake…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Talha sold a piece of land for seven hundred thousand, stayed awake all night for fear of dying before giving it away, and distributed all of it at dawn.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Su'da (RA) the wife of Hadhrat Talha (RA) reports that she once came to Hadhrat Talha (RA) and found him to be extremely distressed. She asked, "Why are you so…
narrations.summary: Su'da reports again that Talha was distressed over the accumulated wealth, distributed four hundred thousand to his family and tribe on her advice, and was given the title Talha Fayyaadh, the Very Generous.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Abdul Azeez (RA) reports that Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awwaam had a thousand slaves who worked and gave their earnings to him. He then distributed the money…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Abdul Azeez reports that Zubayr had a thousand slaves who earned for him, and he gave the earnings away every night so that nothing was left when he returned home.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mugheeth bin Sumay reports that although Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awwaam had a thousand slaves who worked and gave their earnings to him, not a single Dirham of these…
narrations.summary: Mugheeth bin Sumay reports that although Zubayr's thousand slaves earned for him, not one dirham of their earnings entered his house, because he gave all of it to the needy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) says, "When (my father) Zubayr stood for the Battle of Jamal, he called for me. As I stood by his side, he -said, 'Dear son! None but an…
narrations.summary: Zubayr asked his son Abdullaah to sell his property to clear his debts, and Abdullaah repaid them by selling land at Ghaabah before distributing the inheritance after four Hajj seasons of announcements.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Bakr bint Miswar reports that Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf once sold a property of his for forty thousand Dinaars. He then distributed it amongst the Banu…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf sold a property for forty thousand Dinaars and gave the money away, and when Aa'isha heard of it she recalled the Prophet's words about his wives.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "After my demise, none but the truly righteous ones will show compassion towards you." Hadhrat Ja'far bin Burqaan says,…
narrations.summary: Ja'far bin Burqaan reports that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf freed thirty families of slaves, after an opening saying of the Prophet about who will show compassion to his people after his death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maalik Daar (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once placed four Bukhaari. hundred Dinaars in a bag and said to his slave, "Take this to Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah…
narrations.summary: Umar sent four hundred Dinaars first to Abu Ubaydah and then to Mu'aadh bin Jabal to see what they would do with it, and both gave the whole sum to the needy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked those around him to express their wishes. Someone said, "I wish that this room was filled with Dirhams that I…
narrations.summary: Umar wished for men like Abu Ubaydah, Mu'aadh and Hudhayfah to employ in Allaah's service, and when he tested them with money, each gave all of it away.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maymoon bin Mahraan reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once received twenty thousand Dinaars as he was sitting in a gathering. He then distributed all…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar gave away twenty thousand Dinaars during one gathering, and also spent a hundred thousand sent to him by Mu'aawiya within a single year.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ayyoob bin Waa'il Raasibi reports that when he went to Madinah, a neighbour offladhrat Abdullaah bin Umar told him, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar once received a…
narrations.summary: After receiving large sums, Abdullaah bin Umar had given it all away, and a visitor saw him buying fodder on credit for one Dirham, which his slave confirmed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once received, twenty odd thousand as he sat in a gathering. Before getting up from the gathering, he had…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar gave away about twenty thousand the moment he received it, borrowed to pay a latecomer, and was defended against the charge that he was a miser.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq reports, "A man from the Kindah tribe owed me some money and left to see him before dawn (to collect the money). However, I happened to be at the…
narrations.summary: After returning from Makkah, Ash'ath bin Qais gave every person at his mosque clothing, shoes and five hundred Dirhams, and a man from outside the locality also received a gift.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Durra says, "A hundred thousand was once brought to Hadhrat Aa'isha and she distributed it all even though she was fasting that day. I said to her, 'Could…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha gave away a hundred thousand that was brought to her while she was fasting, and when reminded she could have bought meat to break her fast, she said she would have if she had been told.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once sent a bag full of Dirhams to Hadhrat Sauda (RA) (one of the wives of Rasulullaah Sif). "What is this?"…
narrations.summary: Umar sent a bag of Dirhams to Sauda, who asked what they were and then gave the whole amount to the poor.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Barra bint Raafi narrates, "When some surplus wealth was being distributed, Hadhrat Umar (RA) sent to Hadhrat Zaynab bint Jahash (RA) her share. When it was…
narrations.summary: Umar sent Zaynab her share of surplus wealth, and after she objected that he gave allowances only to weaned children, he fixed an allowance for every Muslim child at birth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ka'b narrates that the share of Hadhrat Zaynab bint Jahash IS-lSsi from the surplus wealth amounted to twelve thousand. She however, only took it…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Ka'b relates that Zaynab bint Jahash, given a surplus share of twelve thousand, gave it all to her family and to the needy, and that Umar sent her another thousand, which she also gave away.

narrations.excerpt: An Incident of a Woman and Hadhrat Umar every Muslim baby Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that when a trade caravan arrived (in Madinah), they set up camp at the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar relates that Umar, on night watch with Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf, rebuked a mother whose crying baby kept him awake, learned the child was not yet weaned, and then ordered allowances for every Muslim child born so that mothers would not hurry weaning.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat umar (RA) once said, "I treat Allaah's money (public funds) as if it is the wealth of orphans. I stay away from it as long as I am able to do without it and use…
narrations.summary: Umar said he treated public funds as the wealth of orphans, taking from it only when he had to and only as much as he spent from his own earnings.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Imraan narrates that whenever Hadhrat Umar (RA) needed money, he would approach the public treasurer and take a loan from him. There were times when Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Umar borrowed from the public treasurer when short of money and repaid it from his share of the surplus, even when the treasurer had to press him for payment.

narrations.excerpt: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf . . Hadhrat tbraheem reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to engage in trade when he was Khalifah. When he once prepared a caravan to send to Shaam,…
narrations.summary: Umar, while trading as Khalifah, refused Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf's suggestion that he borrow from the public treasury and preferred a private loan, so that it could be repaid from his estate if he died.

narrations.excerpt: One of the sons of Hadhrat Baraa bin Ma'roor reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once fell ill and honey was prescribed to treat him. At that time there was a vial of honey in…
narrations.summary: When Umar was ill and prescribed honey kept in the public treasury, he asked the people's permission to use it, saying it would otherwise be forbidden to him, and they gave it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that some money once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA). When his daughter Hadhrat Hafsah (RA). heard about it, she approached him saying, "O Ameerul…
narrations.summary: Umar refused his daughter Hafsah's request that relatives receive a share of public money, saying his relatives had a right only in his own wealth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam reports that he once saw Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Arqam (RA) go to Hadhrat Umar (RA) and say, "0 Ameerul Mu'mineen! We have some jewels and silver utensils…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Arqam asked Umar to review jewels and silver from Jaloola, and Umar prayed against the pull of worldly wealth before refusing his young son Abdur Rahmaan's request for a ring.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ismaa'eel bin Muhammad bin Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that when some musk and ambergris perfume came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) from Bahrain, he said, "I wish that I…
narrations.summary: When musk and ambergris arrived from Bahrain, Umar declined his wife Aatika's offer to weigh it for distribution, fearing she might take a share for herself.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once saw a little girl dragging her feet as she walked because of weakness. "Who is this child?" he asked. "She is one of…
narrations.summary: Umar saw a weak little girl and, on learning she was Abdullaah's daughter, told him he must earn to provide for his children, since he did not spend on her.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aasim bin Umar (RA) (the son of Hadhrat Umar (RA)) says, "When Hadhrat Umar (RA) got me married, he provided for me from the Baytul Maal for a month. He then sent…
narrations.summary: After Umar had supported his newly married son Aasim from the public treasury for a month, he stopped and told him to sell produce from his orchard and go into partnership with a trader instead.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maalik bin Aws bin Hadathaan reports that when the envoy of the Roman Emperor came to Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s wife borrowed a Dinaar and bought…
narrations.summary: A Roman empress sent Umar's wife a bottle filled with gems in return for perfume, and Umar sold the gems, gave his wife one Dinaar and deposited the rest in the public treasury.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar Stelg says that he once purchased a camel and kept it in the grazing fields of the Baytul Once it grew fat, he brought it (to the marketplace…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar bought a camel and pastured it with public funds, and when Umar saw it fattened for sale he told him to return the profit to the Baytul Maal and keep only his capital.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen narrates that one of Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s in-laws once approached him and suggested that something be given to him from the Baytul Maal.…
narrations.summary: When an in-law of Umar asked for money from the public treasury, Umar rebuked him, and later gave him ten thousand Dirhams from his own money.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Antarah reports that he went to Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) in (a suburb of Kufa called) Khowrnaq. Hadhrat Ali (RA) was wearing a shawl and shivering from the…
narrations.summary: Ali, shivering in a shawl at Khowrnaq, refused to take anything from the state's wealth and said he had brought the shawl from his house in Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Allaah once sent to Rasulullaah ﷺ and angel with Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA). The angel said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, "Allaah has given…
narrations.summary: Allaah offered the Prophet the choice of being a prophet-king or a prophet-servant, and after Jibra'eel signalled humility he chose to be a servant and never ate reclining again until his death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) were once together on Mount Safa when Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Jibra'eel! I swear…
narrations.summary: On Mount Safa the Prophet said his family had had no food that evening, and when offered treasures and mountains of gold he again chose to be a servant-prophet out of humility.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "My Rabb had offered to transform the rocky plains of Makkah into gold for me. However, I submitted, 'No, my…
narrations.summary: The Prophet declined his Lord's offer to turn the rocky plains of Makkah into gold, preferring to eat one day and be hungry the next so that he could be humble, thankful and remember Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat All (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once informed them that an angel came to him and said, "O Muhammad ﷺ Your Rabb sends Salaams to you and offers to turn the…
narrations.summary: Ali reports that the Prophet declined an offer from his Lord to turn the plains of Makkah into gold, preferring to eat one day and be hungry the next so that he could thank and beg from Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that when a Mushrik was killed during the Battle of Ahzaab, the Mushrikeen sent a message to Rasulullaah ﷺ that they would give…
narrations.summary: After a Mushrik was killed at the Battle of Ahzaab, the Mushrikeen offered payment for his body, and the Prophet refused the money, saying both the body and the money were worthless.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Hakeem bin Hizaam S!3Sii once went to Yemen where he bought a suit of clothing that belonged to (the Yemeni ruler) Dhu Yazan. When…
narrations.summary: Hakeem bin Hizaam bought a suit of Dhu Yazan's clothing in Yemen and presented it to the Prophet, who refused it because he does not accept gifts from Mushrikeen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hakeem bin Hizaam (RA) says that even during the Period of Ignorance, Rasulullaah ﷺ was. the person he liked most. After Rasulullaah announced his Nabuwaat and…
narrations.summary: Hakeem bin Hizaam relates that he bought Dhu Yazan's clothing to give to the Prophet, who refused it as a gift but accepted to pay for it, and the Prophet then gave it to Usaama bin Zaid, who wore it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir bin Tufayl Aamiri (RA) reports that Aamir bin Maalik once gave Rasulullaah ﷺ a horse as a gift with a letter stating, "A sore has emerged on my stomach, so…
narrations.summary: Aamir bin Tufayl relates that Aamir bin Maalik, the Spear Juggler, sent the Prophet a horse with a request for a remedy; the Prophet declined the horse, sent him honey, and refused a gift from a mushrik who would not accept Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Another, narration from Hadhrat Ayaadh bin Himaar Mujaashi'ee (RA) states that when he once presented to Rasulullaah ﷺ a camel or something else as a gift, Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Ayaadh bin Himaar presented a camel to the Prophet as a gift, and when the Prophet found he was not a Muslim he refused it, saying he had been forbidden to accept gifts from Mushrikeen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once addressed the people. After praising Allaah, he said, "Verily the best of all intelligence is Taqwa." The narration…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr, who feared his Khilaafah allowance might not be permissible, accepted one fixed by consultation, and on his deathbed had the eight thousand Dirhams he used returned to the Baytul Maal.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Hafs bin Umar narrates that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) came to (her father) Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) when he was ill and about to breathe his last. She…
narrations.summary: On his deathbed Abu Bakr asked Aa'isha to return an orchard he had given her to his estate and to send his few belongings to Umar, and Umar refused to return them even when Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf advised it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa bin Yasaar reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent a gift to Hadhrat Umar (RA), he returned it. "Why have you returned it?" Rasulullaah asked. Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Ataa bin Yasaar reports that Umar returned a gift the Prophet had sent him, and the report breaks off as the Prophet asks why.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari once sent a fine silken mat as a gift for Hadhrat Aatika bint Zaid bin Amr bin Nufayl who was the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar relates that Abu Moosa sent a silk mat as a gift to Aatika bint Zaid, Umar's wife, and that Umar struck her over the head with it when she showed it to him, then had Abu Moosa brought and struck him with the mat, saying they had no need of gifts sent to his wives.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Layth bin Sa'd narrates that Maqoqis (the once king of Egypt) asked Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) (the governor of Egypt) to sell to him the foot of the Muqattam…
narrations.summary: Layth bin Sa'd relates that Maqoqis offered Amr bin Al Aas seventy thousand Dinaars for the foot of Muqattam hill, and that Umar forbade the sale because a tree of Jannah is reserved for the believers there, so Muslims should be buried there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam reports that during the "Year of Ashes" when the lands of the Arabs were stricken by drought, Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote a letter to Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas.…
narrations.summary: In the Year of Ashes Umar sent Abu Ubaydah a thousand Dinaars for his work, and when Abu Ubaydah refused, Umar cited the Prophet's instruction not to refuse such payment, and he accepted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin. Ziyaad narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once gave Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Aamir (RA) a thousand Dinaars. Hadhrat Sa'eed (RA) refused the money saying, "I…
narrations.summary: Umar offered Sa'eed bin Aamir a thousand Dinaars, which he refused, and Umar explained the Prophet's teaching to accept wealth that comes without asking or craving, so Sa'eed accepted it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said to Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Aamir bin Hudhaym (who was a governor in Shaam), "Why is it that the people of Shaam…
narrations.summary: Umar offered Sa'eed bin Aamir bin Hudhaym, a governor in Shaam, ten thousand Dirhams, which he refused because he had enough wealth and wanted to serve the Muslims freely.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Sa'di (RA) narrates that he once approached Hadhrat Umar during the period of his Khilaafah. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to him, "I have been told that…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Sa'di refused pay for his public services, and Umar explained that the Prophet had taught him to keep or give away what came without asking, so he urged Abdullaah to take payment.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ gave Hadhrat Hakeem bin Hizaam something after the Battle of Hunayn but because he regarded it to be to little,…
narrations.summary: After the Battle of Hunayn the Prophet told Hakeem bin Hizaam that wealth taken with a generous heart is blessed, and Hakeem then refused all payment from anyone, including Abu Bakr and Umar, until his death.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat urwa (RA) states that Hadhrat Hakeem did not accept anything from Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) until the Khalifah's death. Thereafter, he also…
narrations.summary: Hakeem bin Hizaam refused the money and gifts offered by Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthmaan and Mu'aawiya, each until that ruler's death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir bin Rabee'ah (RA) Refuses Land.
narrations.summary: Section heading only: Aamir bin Rabee'ah refuses land.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam reports that when an Arab man came to stay with Hadhrat Aamir bin Rabee'ah, he entertained his guest well and spoke to Rasulullaah about (addressing the…
narrations.summary: Aamir bin Rabee'ah refuses a valley of land offered by an Arab guest, citing the revealed verse about the Day of Qiyaamah drawing near.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Saamit the nephew of Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) says that he once accompanied his uncle (Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA)) to see (Ameerul Mu'mineen) Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr asks Uthmaan's leave to live in Rabdha and refuses the zakaah animals offered him, then rebukes Ka'b for praising a rich man's spending; a second report has him refuse money sent for his needs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Munkadir narrates that Hadhrat Habeeb bin Maslamah who was the Ameer of Shaam once sent three hundred Dinaars for Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) with the…
narrations.summary: Habeeb bin Maslamah sends Abu Dharr three hundred dinars, and Abu Dharr sends them back, saying he fears owning anything beyond his needs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen narrates that Hadhrat Haarith belonged to the Quraysh tribe and lived in Shaam. When the news reached him that Hadhrat Abu Dharr was living a…
narrations.summary: A Quraysh man living in Shaam sends Abu Dharr three hundred dinars, and Abu Dharr refuses, quoting the Prophet on begging.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Raafi (RA) the freed slave of Rasulullaah ﷺ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to him, "0 Abu Raafi! What will be your condition when you become a poor…
narrations.summary: The Prophet warns Abu Raafi not to give all his wealth away and to keep some for his son; later, poor, Abu Raafi refuses charity, and once wealthy he regrets his riches.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdul Azeez bin Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) once sent a hundred thousand Dirhams to Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Bakr…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya sends a hundred thousand dirhams to Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Bakr after he refused to pledge allegiance to Yazeed; he refuses the money and dies in Makkah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maymoon reports that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) thrust onto Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas the responsibility of determining what the intentions of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya asks Amr bin Al Aas to find out whether Abdullaah bin Umar would fight over the Khilaafah; Amr offers him land and wealth for his allegiance, and Abdullaah refuses, saying his Deen is not for worldly wealth.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Maymoon bin Mahraan states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar once entered into a contract of Kitaabah with his slave and fixed the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar, who had agreed a kitaabah contract with his slave, refuses money the slave had earned by begging and frees him for Allaah's pleasure, letting him keep the money.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen narrates that a chief of a rural area of Iraq once requested Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) to ask (Ameerul Mu'mineen) Hadhrat Ali (RA) to…
narrations.summary: A chief in Iraq asks Abdullaah bin Ja'far to intercede with Ali for a need; after Ali grants it, the chief sends forty thousand dirhams, which Abdullaah returns, saying they do not sell their good deeds.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Dinaar narrates that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) appointed Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Arqam (RA) as treasurer of the Baytul Maal. When Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) gave him…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan appoints Abdullaah bin Arqam treasurer of the Baytul Maal and pays him a large remuneration, which he refuses, saying he did the work for Allaah's pleasure.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Qurra reports that he was once staying with Hadhrat Amr bin Nu'maan bin Muqarrin. when Ramadhaan arrived, someone came with a bag of Dirhams saying,…
narrations.summary: During Ramadhaan, Amr bin Nu'maan bin Muqarrin refuses a bag of dirhams sent by Mus'ab bin Zubayr, saying he does not recite the Qur'aan for worldly profit, and sends it back.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) reports that Qutaylah bint Abdul Uzza bin Abd Sa'd from the Banu Maalik bin Hisl tribe was still a Mushrik when she brought some gifts…
narrations.summary: Asmaa bint Abi Bakr refuses gifts from her non-Muslim mother until Allaah revealed the verse permitting kind dealings with such relatives; the Prophet told her to accept the gifts and welcome her mother.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) relates, "A poor lady once came to me with a gift. I however refused to accept it out of pity for her (because she needed it more than 1 did).…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha refuses a poor woman's gift out of pity, and the Prophet tells her to accept it, return something in exchange, and humble herself.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports, "My family was suffering from extreme poverty when my wife told me to approach Rasulullaah ﷺ to ask for something. However, as I…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri, in poverty, is sent by his wife to ask the Prophet for help; the Prophet says Allaah grants independence to whoever asks Him for it, so he returns without asking, and the world later comes to them.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) once spent the morning with a stone tied to his belly to suppress his extreme hunger. It was then either his…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri, starving with a stone tied to his belly, goes to the Prophet on another's advice; the Prophet says he prefers those who do not depend on others, so Abu Sa'eed returns without asking and Allaah later provides abundantly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once promised me (some money). When the Banu Qurayzah were conquered, 1 approached him to fulfil the promise.…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf gives up asking the Prophet for a promised share; Thowbaan pledges to ask no one for anything, and Abu Umaamah reports how Thowbaan would not even ask for his fallen whip.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Abi Mulaykah reports that when the rein of his camel would sometimes fall from the hands of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), he would hit the front legs of the camel to…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr would strike his camel to make it kneel so he could pick up its fallen rein himself, because the Prophet had told him never to ask people for anything.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir (RA) reports that eight years after they had been martyred, Rasulullaah ﷺ again performed the Janaazah salaah for the martyrs of Uhud. Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Eight years after Uhud, the Prophet bade farewell to the living and the dead from the pulpit, said he could see the Fountain of Kowthar, and feared the Ummah would compete for worldly things rather than revert to shirk.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir (RA) states that Rasulullaah once came out of his home and performed the Janaazah salaah for the martyrs of Uhud. The rest…
narrations.summary: Uqba bin Aamir relates a second version: the Prophet prayed the janaazah for the Uhud martyrs, said he could see his fountain and had been given the keys to the treasures of the earth, and feared worldly competition more than shirk.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Al Auf Ansaari (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) to collect the Jizya from Bahrain. When he returned and the…
narrations.summary: The Prophet, pleased that Abu Ubaydah has returned from Bahrain with wealth, tells the Ansaar he fears the world will be spread before them and destroy them as it did earlier peoples.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates that while Rasulullaah ﷺ was sitting, an uncultured Bedouin stood up and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ The drought has consumed us!" Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr reports that when a Bedouin complained of drought, the Prophet said he feared the worldly wealth that would be poured on his Ummah, and wished they would not wear gold.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports that they were sitting around Rasulullaah ﷺ when he was on the pulpit. He said to them, "Amongst the things that 1 fear for you is…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports the Prophet, speaking from the pulpit, saying he feared the splendour and wealth the world would open up to them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "More than you being tested with difficulties, I fear more that you will be tested with prosperity.…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports the Prophet's saying that he feared prosperity for them more than hardship, because the world is sweet and tempting.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Auf bin Maalik (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once stood up amongst the Sahabah (RA) and said, "It is poverty and hard-living that you fear or are you concerned…
narrations.summary: Awf bin Maalik reports the Prophet's warning that conquests over Rome and Persia will bring worldly wealth that diverts from the straight path.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhrama llg narrates that when some of the bootywon at the Battle of Qaadisiyyah was brought to Hadhrat Umar (RA), he was inspecting it when he began…
narrations.summary: Umar weeps while inspecting the booty from Qaadisiyyah, saying such wealth brings enmity and hatred to a nation; Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf asks why, as it is a day of joy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf SI narrates that when the treasures of the Kisra (Persian Emperor) were brought to Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin…
narrations.summary: Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf reports that when the treasures of Kisra were brought to Umar, Umar wept, saying that Allaah sets enmity between a nation when it is given such wealth, while Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf tried to comfort him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that when the crown of the Kisra was brought before Hadhrat Umar (RA), he placed it before him (together with other crown jewels). Amongst the…
narrations.summary: Hasan Basri reports that Umar placed Kisra's crown and bracelets before the people, gave the bracelets to Suraaqa bin Maalik, and prayed that this wealth would not be a trap for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sinaan Duwali reports that he once went to see Hadhrat Umar at a time when a group of the earliest Muhaajireen were with him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) sent for a…
narrations.summary: Abu Sinaan Duwali finds Umar weeping over a ring his son had taken into his mouth, because he heard the Prophet say that worldly wealth opened to a nation brings enmity until the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports, "After leading the salaah, Umar would remain seated for awhile so that a person with any need may speak to him. He would stand up…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar, after finding the public money stacked before him, asked Uthmaan and him to share it out, and wept, wishing to leave the Khilaafah with a clean record. A second report has Umar giving him gold to distribute and weeping at the test it represents.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) states, "Umar once called for me and when I went to him, I found a leather tablecloth in " front of him on which…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that when Umar was given a gold-laden table cloth to distribute, he wept, fearing it was a test rather than a blessing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once sent for him. However, when he reached the door, he heard Hadhrat Umar crying loudly. He said,…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf finds Umar crying among stacked bags of money and consoles him; they agree to distribute the money, four thousand each to the Prophet's wives and two thousand to everyone else.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem reports that some food was once served to Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf after he had fasted. He said, "Mus'ab bin Umayr who was a better person than I…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, served food after fasting, weeps because Mus'ab bin Umayr and Hamza were martyred and shrouded in cloth too small for them, while worldly wealth has now been spread before him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naufal bin Ayaadh Hudhali says, "Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf was our companion and an excellent one indeed. He took us home one day and when he entered he first…
narrations.summary: Naufal bin Ayaadh reports that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, served bread and meat at his home, wept because the Prophet and his family never filled their bellies even with barley bread.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) once went to Hadhrat Ummu Salamah and asked, "Dear mother! I fear that my wealth will destroy me because I am the wealthiest of the…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf asks Umm Salama whether his great wealth will destroy him; she tells him to spend it in charity, and when Umar asks whether he is among the companions the Prophet mentioned, she refuses to say.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya. bin Ja'dah reports that some Sahabah (RA) once visited Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) during his illness. They said, "Good news for you, O Abu Abdullaah! You shall…
narrations.summary: Some Sahabah visit Khabbaab during his illness and tell him he will meet Muhammad at the pond; he points to his house and asks how that is possible, given the Prophet's words that a person needs only a traveller's provisions.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Taariq bin Shihaab reports that a group of Sahabah (RA) once visited Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) during his illness and said, "Good news for you, O Abu Abdullaah! You…
narrations.summary: Sahabah visit the ill Khabbaab and say he will soon meet his brothers; he weeps, fearing that their rewards were kept for the Aakhirah while he has received worldly wealth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haaritha bin Mudarrib reports that when they visited Hadhrat Khabbaab he had already taken seven brandings with a hot iron on his stomach (as treatment for his…
narrations.summary: During his illness, after seven brandings, Khabbaab says he would wish for death if the Prophet had not forbidden it, but fears the forty thousand dirhams in his house will keep him from meeting the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Another similar narration adds that Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) said, "I saw a time when I was with Rasulullaah ﷺ without a single Dirham to my name. I now have beside my room…
narrations.summary: Khabbaab recalls having no dirhams when he was with the Prophet and now having forty thousand beside his room; when his shroud is brought he weeps, noting that Hamza had only a small sheet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il Shaqeeq bin Salamah says that when they visited Hadhrat Khabbaab bin Aral during his final illness, he said, "There is eighty thousand Dlrhams in that…
narrations.summary: On his final illness Khabbaab weeps over eighty thousand dirhams, fearing his companions died poor while he has wealth, and says he wishes the world were like dung; other reports tell of Mus'ab's small shroud and the Prophet's instruction to cover the feet with idhkhir grass.

narrations.excerpt: A man from the Banu Abs tribe says, "I was once in the company of Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi when he spoke about the treasures of Kisra (the Persian Emperor) that Allaah…
narrations.summary: Salmaan Faarsi tells a man of the Banu Abs that the treasures now in Muslim hands are a worry, recalling that in the Prophet's time the Sahabah began their mornings with nothing and the Prophet never filled his belly for three days.

narrations.excerpt: Abu Sufyaan reports from his teachers that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) visited Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) during his final illness, when Hadhrat Salmaan started to weep,…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas visits the dying Salmaan Faarsi, who weeps and gives advice to fear Allaah in judgement, in distribution and in intentions.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Haakim states that all Hadhrat Salmaan Sfilis possessed at the time was a dish for washing clothes, a plate and a jug. Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that when…
narrations.summary: In Salmaan Faarsi's last illness Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas asks why he weeps; Salmaan says he fears he broke the Prophet's instruction to own only a traveller's provision, gives Sa'd advice, and leaves an estate of about twenty Dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir bin Abdullaah narrates that when Hadhrat Salmaan "al Khayr" was on his deathbed, the people noticed that he was somewhat uneasy. They asked " O Abu…
narrations.summary: On his deathbed Salmaan Faarsi is uneasy because he had more than a traveller's provision; his estate is valued at about fifteen Dirhams, and the reports on its value differ.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu waa'il narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) came to visit Hadhrat Abu Haashim bin Utba (RA) when he fell ill. Finding him in tears, Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA)…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya visits Abu Haashim bin Utba as he weeps on his deathbed; Abu Haashim says he failed to keep the Prophet's advice to own only a servant and a conveyance, and his estate is valued at thirty Dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hasanah Muslim bin Akyas the freed slave of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Aamir reports that when someone once went to Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jaraah he found him…
narrations.summary: Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah weeps, fearing that his house full of servants and animals means he cannot face the Prophet, who said the dearest person to him is the one who meets him in the state he left him.

narrations.excerpt: The Abstinence of Rasulullaah.
narrations.summary: Heading only: the section title on the abstinence of the Prophet and the Sahabah. No narration follows.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once told him about the time when he visited Rasulullaah ﷺ . Rasulullaah ﷺ was lying on a straw mat and…
narrations.summary: Umar tells Ibn Abbaas how he found the Prophet on a straw mat that had marked his side, with only a handful of barley and some leaves in the room; the Prophet consoles him that the others have the world and the Muslims have the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Umar Si states, "I once sought permission to see Rasulullaah ﷺ. When I entered an upper storey room he was occupying, Rasulullaah ﷺ was…
narrations.summary: Umar finds Rasulullah lying on a coarse mat that had marked his side, and Rasulullah says his luxuries are postponed to the Aakhirah while this world is like a traveller's brief shade.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "A woman from the Ansaar once visited me and noticed that the bedding of Rasulullaah ﷺ was merely a double-folded sheet. She then sent me a…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet returned a woollen bedding that an Ansaari woman sent, saying that if he wished, Allaah would make mountains of gold and silver travel with him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas SI reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ wore woollen clothing and patched shoes. He also said that Rasulullaah ﷺ ate Bashi and his clothing was made of coarse cloth.…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Rasulullah wore woollen clothing and patched shoes and ate coarse barley, and Hasan explains what Bashi was.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Ayman (RA) narrates that she once sifted some flour and made bread for Rasulullaah ﷺ (with the refined flour rather than with the coarse flour Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Ummu Ayman makes the Prophet bread from refined flour; he asks her to put it back and knead the coarse flour he was used to.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salma (RA) the wife of Hadhrat Abu Raafi (RA) reports that Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas once came to…
narrations.summary: Salma, wife of Abu Raafi, serves Hasan bin Ali, Abdullaah bin Ja'far and Abdullaah bin Abbaas coarse barley bread with olive oil and chillies, the food the Prophet liked.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that they once accompanied Rasulullaah ﷺ into an Ansaari's orchard, Rasulullaah ﷺ picked up some dates from the ground and ate…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the Prophet, four days without food, ate dates from the ground in an Ansaari orchard, and warns of a time when people will store provisions and their trust in Allaah will be weak; a verse about provision for animals is revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that when a cup containing milk and honey was given to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he commented, "A combination of two drinks as well two meals in one…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet refused a cup of milk mixed with honey as excess, saying he fears being questioned about worldly luxury on the Day of Qiyaamah and that he humbles himself before Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) narrates, "We were once with Hadhrat Abu Bakr when he asked for something to drink. When some water mixed with honey was brought and put in…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Arqam reports that Abu Bakr wept when offered honeyed water, because he had seen the Prophet repel the world, and feared that the world would take hold of him and that he might oppose the Prophet's way.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr once asked for a drink, he was given a cup with honey mixed in water. As he took it…
narrations.summary: A second version of the same incident: Abu Bakr weeps twice when offered honeyed water, and says the world told the Prophet that those after him would not escape it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Abu Bakr (RA) passed away without leaving behind a Dinaar or a Dirham. Just before his demise, he took all his money and deposited it in the…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says Abu Bakr left no dinar or dirham and gave all his money to the Baytul Maal; a second report says he deposited all his money on becoming Khalifah, since public affairs left him no time to trade.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa bin Saa'ib narrates that the morning after Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was appointed Khalifah, he had some shawls over his arm and was proceeding to the…
narrations.summary: When Abu Bakr became Khalifah and went to the market, Umar stopped him, and Abu Ubaydah set his allowance from the Baytul Maal: the average of a Muhaajir's, a set of clothing for each season, and half a goat a day.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Humayd bin Hilaal reports that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was appointed as Khalifah, some of the Sahabah (RA) suggested that he should receive an allowance from…
narrations.summary: Humayd bin Hilaal reports that the Sahabah agreed Abu Bakr should receive two shawls, a travelling animal and household expenses from the Baytul Maal as Khalifah, and he was happy with it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalim bin Abdullaah reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) became the Khalifah, he took the same allowance that was fixed for Hadhrat Abu Bakr Although he continued…
narrations.summary: Umar finds Abu Bakr's allowance hard to live on; Zubayr suggests raising it, Uthmaan advises first asking Hafsa, who reports Umar's anger, and Umar explains that the Prophet's and Abu Bakr's frugality is his model.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan Basri says that he once attended a gathering in the Jaami Masjid of Basrah where he found some Sahabah (RA) speaking about the abstinence of Hadhrat Abu…
narrations.summary: Hasan Basri reports a gathering in Basrah where Ahnaf bin Qais says Umar shunned them for wearing Persian cloth until they changed, then welcomed them and shared the booty; the Sahabah then asked Ali, Hafsa and Aa'isha to ask Umar to dress and eat better, and Umar answered with the Prophet's frugal life.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ikrama bin Khaalid narrates that Hadhrat Hafsah (RA), Hadhrat Ibn Mutee and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once addressed Hadhrat Umar saying, "If you eat good…
narrations.summary: Hafsa, Ibn Mutee and Abdullaah bin Umar urge Umar to eat good food for strength; he replies that he will keep to the route his two companions, the Prophet and Abu Bakr, took.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah bin Sahl bin Hunayf says that for a long period of time, Hadhrat Umar (RA) took nothing from the Baytul Maal. He eventually reached a stage where he…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah bin Sahl reports that Umar took nothing from the Baytul Maal until poverty set in; he consults the Sahabah, Uthmaan and Sa'eed bin Zaid advise a sum that lets him feed others, and Ali advises enough for morning and evening meals, which Umar accepts.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qataadah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to say, "Had I ( 1) lbn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab (Vol.4 Pg.408). so wished, I could be eating the best of…
narrations.summary: Qataadah reports Umar saying he could have the best food and clothing but prefers to keep his luxuries for the Aakhirah; on reaching Shaam and seeing rich food, Umar weeps for the poor Muslims who die hungry and are in Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) (the son of Hadhrat Umar (RA)) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once came to his house while he was eating, Hadhrat Umar made space for his…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports Umar refusing to eat meat with butter at his house, because the Prophet ate only one and gave the other away; Abu Haazim reports Umar refusing Hafsa's two gravies, saying he will not eat them until he meets Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "When he was Khalifah, I saw that when a Saa of dates was given to Hadhrat Umar (RA), he would even eat the dates that were of an inferior…
narrations.summary: Anas and Saa'ib bin Yazeed report that Umar as Khalifah ate inferior dates and dry bread and meat, wiping his hands on his feet; a report through Thaabit and Deenowri adds that Umar told Jaarood to wipe his hands on his sleeve.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla reports that when some people from Iraq once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA), he noticed that they ate very little (because they were used…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla reports that Umar, seeing Iraqis eat little of his plain food, rebuked them with the Ahqaaf verse about luxuries used up in worldly life; Umar also rebuked Hafs bin Abul Aas, who would not eat the plain food, saying he could have refined meals made if he wished.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Humayd bin Hilaal reports that Hadhrat Hafs bin Abul Aas often joined Hadhrat Umar (RA) for meals but ate nothing, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "What prevents you…
narrations.summary: Humayd bin Hilaal reports that Hafs bin Abul Aas would not eat Umar's plain food, and Umar explains that he avoids luxury out of fear it would reduce his good deeds on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalim bin Abdullaah narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to say, "By Allaah! We have no concern for the luxuries of this world. We could easily give instructions…
narrations.summary: Saalim bin Abdullaah reports Umar saying they could easily have refined food and drink but prefer to keep their luxuries for the Aakhirah, citing the Ahqaaf verse about good things used up in the world.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) narrates, "I came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) with a delegation from Basrah. Whenever we met him (and ate with him), we noticed that every day he…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports that Umar, when a Basrah delegation ate with him, rejected luxuries and quoted the Ahqaaf verse; when the delegates asked for food from the Baytul Maal, Umar granted two goats and two bags of flour a day, warning that a town which takes that daily will be ruined.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Utba bin Farqad reports, "I once brought to Hadhrat Umar SSi a few baskets full of sweetmeats. "What is this?' he asked. I replied, 'Because you spend the…
narrations.summary: Utba bin Farqad brings Umar a basket of sweetmeats, which Umar refuses after asking whether every Muslim has one, and then they share a plain meal of coarse bread and tough meat.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was thirsty when he once visited someone. When he asked the man for something to drink, some honey (mixed in water) was…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that when Umar was thirsty and offered honey mixed in water, he refused it, fearing he would be questioned about it on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked for a drink, he was served some water mixed with honey. He said, "This is most excellent, but I have heard…
narrations.summary: Another report: Umar, offered water mixed with honey, calls it excellent but refuses it, citing the Ahqaaf verse about good things used up in worldly life.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) says that Hadhrat Umar (RA) arrived in Eela with a group of Muhaajireen and Ansaar. Because the journey was long and arduous, the seat of his upper…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that when Umar's upper garment tore on a long journey, the priest mended it and made a new one; Umar gave the new one back and wore the mended garment, saying it better absorbs sweat.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qataadah (RA) reports that when he was Khalifah, Hadhrat Umar wore a patched woollen robe that had some patches of leather. He used to walk through the…
narrations.summary: Qataadah reports that Umar as Khalifah wore a patched woollen robe with leather patches, carried a whip to correct people in the marketplace, and picked up stray thread and date stones to throw into people's yards.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was Khalifah, he was once delivering a lecture wearing a lower garment that had twelve patches. Hadhrat Anas (RA) says,…
narrations.summary: Hasan and Anas report Umar's clothing: he gave a lecture wearing a lower garment with twelve patches, and Anas saw a garment with three patches between the shoulders.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports, "The food that Hadhrat Umar took (from the Baytul Maal) was only what was absolutely necessary for his family and for himself. He…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar took from the Baytul Maal only what his family needed, plus one set of summer clothing, and patched rather than replaced; Muhammad bin Ibraheem reports that Umar's daily allowance was two Dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdul Malik bin Shaddaad says that he once saw Hadhrat Uthmaan on the pulpit on a Friday wearing a thick lower garment sewn in Aden that was worth no more than…
narrations.summary: Abdul Malik bin Shaddaad saw Uthmaan on the pulpit in a plain garment; Hasan says Uthmaan slept in the Masjid and got up with the mark of a straw mat on his side; Shurahbeel bin Muslim says Uthmaan fed guests royally but ate only vinegar and oil at home.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shurahbeel bin Muslim says that although Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) used to feed people the sumptuous meals of a ruler, he would eat (simple) vinegar and olive oil at…
narrations.summary: Shurahbeel bin Muslim says that Uthmaan served rich meals to guests but ate only vinegar and olive oil at home.

narrations.excerpt: A man from the Thaqeef tribe says, "Hadhrat Ali (RA) appointed me as governor of a place called Ukbara. It was a place in rural Iraq where no Muslims lived. Hadhrat Ali…
narrations.summary: A man of the Thaqeef tribe reports that Ali, when he appointed him governor of Ukbara, ate barley flour mixed with water from a sealed bag; A'mash reports that Ali fed guests well but ate only food brought from Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Shareek reports form his grandfather that some Faalooda was once served to Hadhrat Ali (RA). Addressing the Faalooda, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "You…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Shareek reports from his grandfather that when Faalooda was served to Ali, Ali said he did not want to grow used to something he was not accustomed to.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once came before them wearing a shawl and lower garment tied (to his waist) with a strip of cloth. When someone…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Wahab reports that Ali (RA) wore a plain lower garment tied with a strip of cloth to keep away pride, and said he had bought a coarse garment for five dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujammi bin Sam'aan Taymi narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once took his sword to the marketplace and announced, "Who will buy this sword from me? I would never…
narrations.summary: Mujammi bin Sam'aan Taymi reports that Ali (RA) took his sword to the market to sell it, saying he would never sell it if he had four dirhams to buy a lower garment.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalih bin Abil Aswad reports from someone else that he once saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) riding a donkey with both his legs hanging on one side as he said, "It is I who…
narrations.summary: Ali (RA) is reported riding a donkey and saying he holds the world in contempt, and separately the Prophet ﷺ wept on seeing Mus'ab bin Umayr wearing a patched shawl.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Razeen reports that they once went to meet Hadhrat Ali on the occasion of Eidul Adha. Hadhrat Ali (RA) served them a dish prepared with cubes of…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Razeen relates that when they visited Ali on Eid al-Adha and Ali served them a dish of meat and bran, Ali said he heard the Prophet say a Khalifah may take only two dishes from public funds, one for himself and his family and one for guests.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once went to see Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA), he found him lying down on a saddle blanket, using the…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that Umar found Abu Ubaydah sleeping on a saddle blanket with his mount's satchel as a pillow, and Ma'mar reports that when Umar reached Shaam he embraced Abu Ubaydah and found nothing in his house but a sword, a shield and his mount.

narrations.excerpt: Umayr.
narrations.summary: The text is only the word 'Umayr' from a split section heading about Mus'ab bin Umayr's abstinence, and contains no narration.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "One winter morning I left home extremely hungry with the cold almost killing me. There was a piece of undyed leather at home which was still…
narrations.summary: Ali relates that, starving on a cold winter morning, he drew water from a Jew's well for dates, and that the Prophet wept on seeing Mus'ab bin Umayr in a patched shawl, telling the Companions they were better off than they would be in future times of plenty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once saw Hadhrat Mus'ab Bin Umayr approach wrapped in a sheepskin. Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "Look at that man whose heart…
narrations.summary: Umar (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ praised Mus'ab bin Umayr, who came in a sheepskin after giving up a pampered life for the love of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once sitting with a group of Sahabah (RA) in Quba when Hadhrat Mus'ab Bin Umayr (RA) arrived wearing a shawl that could…
narrations.summary: Zubayr (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ praised Mus'ab bin Umayr for leaving a wealthy upbringing for Allaah, foretold wealth from conquests over Persia and Rome, and warned against being at ease with this world.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Khabaab (RA) states that all that Hadhrat Mus'ab Bin Umayr left behind (after his death) was a sheet (so small) that (when it was used as a…
narrations.summary: Khabbaab (RA) reports that all Mus'ab bin Umayr left behind was a sheet too small to cover his whole body at burial, so the Prophet ﷺ had his head covered and his feet covered with Idhkhir grass.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat ibn Shihaab narrates that Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) once entered the Masjid wearing a striped shawl that he patched with a piece of leather because it…
narrations.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports that Uthmaan bin Madh'oon entered the Masjid in a shawl patched with leather, and the Prophet ﷺ wept and foretold a time of plenty, saying their present state was better.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that after Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon had passed away, Rasulullaah ﷺ came to him and bent over him as if advising him.…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ wept over the body of Uthmaan bin Madh'oon, told the Sahabah to stop weeping, and said he had left the world owning nothing from it.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "May Allaah shower His mercy on you, O Uthmaan! Neither have you taken from this world nor has it taken from you."
narrations.summary: The Prophet ﷺ prays for Uthmaan bin Madh'oon, saying that he neither took from this world nor did the world take from him.

narrations.excerpt: Faarsi.
narrations.summary: No narration: the text is only the word 'Faarsi', a fragment of a heading about Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Atiyya bin Aamir says that he once saw Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) being forced to eat more. He said, "That is enough for me. That is enough for me because I…
narrations.summary: Atiyya bin Aamir reports seeing Salmaan Faarsi (RA) refuse more food, quoting the Prophet ﷺ that the most full in this world will be the most hungry in the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that the allowance Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) received was five thousand Dirhams and he was governor of approximately thirty thousand Muslims.…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Salmaan Faarsi (RA), governor of about thirty thousand Muslims, gave away his whole allowance and earned his living by weaving palm-fibre baskets.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat A'mash reports that he heard the incident from people that Hadhrat Hudhayfah once said to Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA), "O Abu Abdullaah! Should I not build a room…
narrations.summary: A'mash reports that Hudhayfah offered to build Salmaan Faarsi a room just big enough to lie down and stand in, and Salmaan said it was as if Hudhayfah lived in his heart.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maalik bin Anas narrates that Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) had no room which to administer public affairs). He would sit in the shade (of a tree) and move wherever…
narrations.summary: Maalik bin Anas reports that Salmaan Faarsi (RA) sat in the shade, and when a man offered to build him a room, Salmaan approved the plan of a room the size of his body.

narrations.excerpt: Ghifaari.
narrations.summary: No narration: the text is only the word 'Ghifaari', a fragment of a heading about Abu Dharr Ghifaari.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Asmaa reports that he once visited Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) who was then staying in Rabdha. With Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) at the time was an unattractive black…
narrations.summary: Abu Asmaa reports that Abu Dharr (RA), living in Rabdha, refused advice to move to Iraq, because the Prophet ﷺ had said light loads cross the slippery Siraat bridge more easily.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Khiraash reports that he once saw Hadhrat Abu Dharr sitting in the shade in Rabdha. He was sitting on a piece of coarse sack cloth with his wife who…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Khiraash reports that Abu Dharr (RA), sitting on coarse sackcloth with his wife, thanked Allaah for taking his children to the Aakhirah and preferred a humbling wife to a proud one.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem Taymi reports from his father that someone once suggested to Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) that he should become a land owner like some other person was doing.…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr and Abu Dardaa (RA) both give up worldly comfort for the Aakhirah: Abu Dardaa gives his guests' bedding away as charity, and Umar (RA) finds him sleeping on sand with a flimsy shawl.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) says, "I had been a trader before Rasulullaah ﷺ announced his Nabuwaat. After Rasulullaah ﷺ announced that he was a Rasul, I tried combining my…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa relates that he was a trader before the Prophet announced his mission, and that after the announcement he gave up trade because he could not combine it with worship.

narrations.excerpt: A narration similar to the one above adds that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "I swear by the Being Who controls the life of Abu Dardaa! Even today I would not like to…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says he would not want a shop at the Masjid door that earns forty Dinaars, all of which he gives in charity, because he fears the intensity of the reckoning.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "It gives me no pleasure to stand on the step of the Masjid, buying and selling to earn a profit of three…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says he would take no pleasure in trading at the Masjid door for three hundred Dinaars of profit, and three further reports show him giving his bedding away and telling his guests that they are heading for a permanent abode in the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: The narration has already passed in the chapter entitled "Condemning Rulers who Live Lives Above the Standards of the Common People" that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) pushed…
narrations.summary: This entry is a cross-reference that repeats, in abridged and garbled form, the earlier account of Umar finding Abu Dardaa's unlocked, dark room bare and the two of them reminding each other of the Prophet's words.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aflah the freed slave of Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to have a set of exclusive clothing made for the veterans of Badr. When he…
narrations.summary: Aflah reports that Umar (RA) sent Mu'aadh bin Afraa (RA) fine clothing, which he sold to buy and free five slaves, and when Umar sent plainer clothing instead, Mu'aadh asked again for the best Umar gave others.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jalaaj (RA) says, "Since the time I accepted Islaam at the hands of Rasulullaah ﷺ , I have never filled my belly. I eat only what is sufficient to sustain me." A…
narrations.summary: Jalaaj (RA) says that since accepting Islaam at the Prophet's ﷺ hands he has never filled his belly and eats only enough to sustain him; a report from Bayhaqi gives his lifespan as 120 years.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hamza bin Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says that whenever Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar had plenty of food, he would never eat to his fill after he had found someone to…
narrations.summary: Hamza bin Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that Abdullaah bin Umar, though he had plenty of food, would not eat to his fill while anyone he had not yet invited was present, and told a visitor he had not eaten his fill for eighty years.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar bin Hamza bin Abdullaah bin umar reports that he was once sitting with his father when a man passed by. He (Hadhrat Hamza) asked, "Tell me what you were…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Hamza reports that his father Hamza asked about a conversation a man had with Abdullaah bin Umar, in which the man urged him to eat better and Abdullaah said he had not filled his belly for eighty years.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaydullaah bin Adi who was a freed slave of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar reports that he once returned from Iraq and went to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar. After…
narrations.summary: Ubaydullaah bin Adi, a freed slave of Abdullaah bin Umar, reports bringing him a digestive preparation called Jawaarish, which Abdullaah refused because he had not filled his belly for forty years.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen narrates that someone once said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar, "Should prepare some Jawaarish for you?" "What is this Jawaarish?" enquired…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports that when Abdullaah bin Umar was offered Jawaarish, he said he had not eaten his fill for four months, not for lack of food but because he lived as the Prophet ﷺ and the Sahabah did, sometimes eating and sometimes going hungry.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA) once said, "Since the time Rasulullaah ﷺ was taken away, I have never laid a brick upon a brick (never built anything) and never planted a…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says that since the Prophet ﷺ was taken away he has never laid a brick on a brick or planted a single date palm.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "Besides Abdullaah bin Umar, there was none amongst us who received worldly wealth without the world turning towards him and he being inclined…
narrations.summary: Jaabir (RA) and Suddi say that Abdullaah bin Umar alone kept the state the Prophet ﷺ left them in, and Hudhayfah (RA) says he would rather his family had no food than have worldly wealth, quoting the Prophet ﷺ that Allaah guards the believer from it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once saw that I had eaten (full meals) twice during a single day and said, 'O Aa'isha! Are you not interested in any activity…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ rebuked her for eating two full meals in one day, asking whether she cared for nothing but her stomach and calling it extravagance.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "I was sitting and weeping by the side of Rasulullaah ﷺ (at his deathbed) when he said, "What makes you weep? If you wish to meet with me (in…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha (RA) reports weeping at the Prophet's ﷺ deathbed, and he told her that to meet him in the Aakhirah she should live on a traveller's provisions and never mix with the affluent.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ added, "Never replace your clothing until you have patched them (and can wear them no more)." A narration from Hadhrat Urwa…
narrations.summary: Urwa (RA) reports that Aa'isha (RA) patched her clothes until the patches overlapped and gave away the eighty thousand dirhams Mu'aawiya (RA) sent her by evening, after the Prophet ﷺ had advised mending clothes before replacing them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Juhayfah (RA) says that he once ate Thareed prepared with fatty meat because of which he was belching as he went to Rasulullaah iil?. Rasulullaah ﷺ said,…
narrations.summary: Abu Juhayfah (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ told him not to belch in front of others after a heavy meal, warning that those who fill themselves most in this world will suffer most hunger on Qiyaamah, after which he never ate to fill again.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ja'da (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once saw a man with a large stomach. Sticking his finger into the man's stomach, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "It would have been…
narrations.summary: Ja'da reports that the Prophet pointed at a man with a large stomach and said the food would have been better in a poor person's stomach.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that Hadhrat Umar Si once saw Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah with a man who was carrying some meat for him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Does…
narrations.summary: Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that Umar rebuked Jaabir bin Abdullaah for buying meat for his family, quoting the verse about using up one's good things in worldly life, and a second report has Jaabir describing how Umar kept repeating his excuse.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once saw a Dirham in the hand of Hadhrat Jaabir (RA). "What is that Dirham for?" asked Hadhrat Umar (RA).…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar saw a dirham in Jaabir's hand, asked what it was for, and rebuked him for buying meat out of craving.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once went to his son Abdullaah's house at a time when he was eating some meat. "Why are you eating this meat?" Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Umar (RA) rebuked his son Abdullaah for eating meat merely because he craved it, saying that eating whatever one craves is enough to make a person extravagant.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Jubayr reports that the news reached Hadhrat Umar (RA) that Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan (RA) ate various types of meats. Hadhrat Umar then said to…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Jubayr reports that Umar (RA), told that Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan ate many kinds of meat, went to his evening meal, ate beside him, and warned that opposing the Prophet's ﷺ way leads away from the highest Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by a rubbish dump and stopped there. When his companions felt disgusted (at the sight and stench), Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Umar (RA), passing a rubbish dump while his companions recoiled from the smell, said this is the world people aspire to and rely upon.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salma bin Kulthoom reports that when Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) built a tall building in Damascus, the news reached Hadhrat Umar (RA) in Madinah. Hadhrat Umar SSi…
narrations.summary: Salma bin Kulthoom reports that when Abu Dardaa (RA) built a tall building in Damascus, Umar (RA) wrote from Madinah rebuking him for building like the Persians and Romans, because the Companions must set an example to others.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Raashid bin Sa'd states that when the news reached Hadhrat Umar (RA) that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) had built porches (at house entrances) in…
narrations.summary: Raashid bin Sa'd reports that when Umar (RA) heard Abu Dardaa (RA) had built porches at house entrances in Hims, he wrote calling him a little builder and asking whether the decorations of the Romans and Persians were not enough for him.

narrations.excerpt: "were the worldly decorations and renovations built by the Romans and Persians not sufficient for you? (How can you be doing this) When Allaah has announced that these…
narrations.summary: Umar (RA) adds to his letter that the decorations of the Romans and Persians should be enough and orders the recipient to move from Hims to Damascus at once, which Sufyaan says was a form of punishment.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abu Habeeb reports that Hadhrat Khaarija bin Hudhaafah was the first person to build a double storey building in Egypt, when he received news of this,…
narrations.summary: Yazeed bin Abi Habeeb reports that Umar (RA) ordered Amr bin Al Aas (RA) to demolish the double-storey house Khaarijah bin Hudhaafah built in Egypt, because it would let him spy on his neighbours.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah Roomi narrates that he once entered the house of Hadhrat Ummu Talq. Noticing that the roof of her house was extremely low, he asked, "O Ummu Talq! why…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah Roomi reports that Ummu Talq (RA) kept her roof low, citing Umar bin Khattaab's instruction to his governors not to build tall buildings, because the worst days come when people do.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sufyaan bin Uyayna reports that when Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas was governor of Kufa, he wrote to Hadhrat Umar (RA), seeking permission to build himself a…
narrations.summary: Sufyaan bin Uyayna reports that Umar (RA) told Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, governor of Kufa, to build only what shields him from sun and rain because this world is only a place to make do with, and the report is cut off as Umar writes to Amr bin Al Aas.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sufyan reports that the news reached Hadhrat Umar (RA) that a man used baked bricks to build. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "I had no idea that there will be people…
narrations.summary: Umar rebukes a man who built with baked bricks, warning that people like Fir'oun could appear in this Ummah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalim the son of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "I got married during the lifetime of my father. Amongst the people that my father invited was Abu Ayyoob.…
narrations.summary: Saalim bin Abdullaah bin Umar recounts how Abu Ayyoob rebuked his father Abdullaah for decorating the walls at Saalim's wedding, and refused to enter the house or eat there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) reports that he once went to Hadhrat Abu Bakr SI and asked for some advice, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Fear Allaah, O Salmaan! You should know that…
narrations.summary: Salmaan asks Abu Bakr for advice, and Abu Bakr tells him to fear Allaah, take from conquests only what he needs, and never break the protection given by Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Hasan states that Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi visited Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) on his deathbed and asked, "Do give me some advice, O Khalifah of…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Salmaan Faarsi visited Abu Bakr on his deathbed for advice, and Abu Bakr said Allaah will open the world, so no one should take more than he needs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) once visited Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) on his deathbed and greeted him with Salaam. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Although it has not yet…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf visits the dying Abu Bakr, who warns that worldly wealth is coming and that being executed is better for a person than drowning in the intoxication of this world.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) bin Rabaah narrates that he once heard Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas say, "You people spend the morning and the evenings hankering after that which Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Al Aas rebukes his companions for craving the world the Prophet avoided, saying the Prophet never had more than he owed.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) said, "Never did three days pass Rasulullaah ﷺ in his entire life without his debts exceeding his dues." Yet…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Al Aas says the Prophet never went three days without his debts exceeding his dues, and contrasts the Prophet's abstinence with the Companions' desire for the world.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maymoon reports that when one of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar sons asked him for new lower garment, claiming that his was torn, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: When his son asked for a new garment, Abdullaah bin Umar told him to cut off the torn part and wear the rest, and warned against living only for food and clothing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thaabit reports that Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) once passed by Hadhrat Abu Dardaa who was busy building a house for himself. Hadhrat Abu Dharr remarked, "You are…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr rebukes Abu Dardaa for building a house, saying he is loading boulders onto people's necks, and says he would have preferred to see him tending his family's waste.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "I once wore a new upper garment of mine and was very taken aback by it as I looked at it. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said to me, 'What are you…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha wore a new garment and Abu Bakr warned that Allaah dislikes a servant who admires himself for worldly beauty, so she gave the garment away as sadaqah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Habeeb bin Hamzah says that when death came to one of Hadhrat Abu Bakr's sons, the youngster kept looking at the pillow. After he has passed away, the people…
narrations.summary: Habeeb bin Hamzah reports that Abu Bakr's son kept looking at his pillow when dying, and that five or six dinars were found beneath it, which Abu Bakr said his skin could not withstand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood built his house, he said to Hadhrat Ammaar (RA), "Come and have a look at what I have…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood built a house, and Ammaar told him that a sturdy house with long hopes meant death was near.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa narrates that he was once with Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) when he was invited for a Waleema. When Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) saw a variety of dishes,…
narrations.summary: Ataa reports that Abu Sa'eed Khudri, invited to a waleema with many dishes, reminded the host that the Prophet did not combine a big morning meal with a big dinner.
