narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Showdhab reports that the father of Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) kept confronting him during the Battle of Badr as Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah S.1SSSS continued avoiding…
narrations.summary: Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah kills his father during the Battle of Badr after he kept confronting him, and Allaah reveals the verse that believers do not befriend those who oppose Allaah and His Rasool, even their fathers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maalik bin Umayr (RA) who had seen the Period of Ignorance reports that a man came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "Amongst the enemy I encountered my father. When he…
narrations.summary: Maalik bin Umayr reports two men who fought or left their fathers in battle, and the Prophet stayed silent; Abu Hurayrah reports that Abdullaah bin Ubay's son offered to bring his father's head, and the Prophet refused.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) the son of Abdullaah bin Ubay says that when he requested permission from Rasulullaah ﷺ to execute his father, Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah, son of Abdullaah bin Ubay, asks the Prophet for permission to execute his father, and the Prophet refuses, choosing to be lenient with him while he remains among the Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Usaama bin Zaid (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ returned from the military offensive against the Banu Mustaliq tribe, Hadhrat Abdullaah the son of Abdullaah…
narrations.summary: Usaama bin Zaid reports that Abdullaah, son of Abdullaah bin Ubay, drew his sword before his father and vowed not to sheathe it until his father called the Prophet honourable; the Prophet was pleased with his act.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that Hadhrat Handhala (RA) the son of Abu Aamir and Hadhrat Abdullaah SI the son of Abdullaah bin Ubay bin Salool both sought permission from…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that Handhala, son of Abu Aamir, and Abdullaah, son of Abdullaah bin Ubay, both asked the Prophet to let them execute their fathers, and he refused.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) the son of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once said to his father, "When I saw you during the Battle of Uhud, I avoided you." Hadhrat Abu Bakr responded…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Bakr tells his father he avoided him at Uhud, and Abu Bakr says he would have attacked him; later, when the still non-Muslim Abdur Rahmaan challenged for a duel, Abu Bakr stood up to accept and the Prophet held him back.

narrations.excerpt: It is reported by Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah and other scholars proficient in the knowledge of the various battles Rasulullaah ﷺ fought, state that Hadhrat Umar once passed by…
narrations.summary: Umar tells Sa'eed bin Al Aas that he did not kill Sa'eed's father, who was struck down by Ali after Umar turned away, and Sa'eed replies that his father was on falsehood; Umar is greatly pleased.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that according to the instructions of Rasulullaah Hlf , the bodies of the Mushrikeen killed during the Battle of Badr were dragged to a…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet spoke to the Mushrikeen dragged into a well after Badr, and Abu Hudhayfah grieved over his father Utba being dragged there; the Prophet made dua for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nubay bin Wahab (RA) from the Banu Abdud Daar tribe reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived with the captives from the Battle of Badr, they distributed them…
narrations.summary: Nubay bin Wahab reports the Prophet ordered Badr captives treated well; Abu Azeez, Mus'ab's captive brother, recounts that the Ansaar gave him bread, and that Mus'ab told his captor to bind him tightly because his mother would pay a ransom.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ayyoob bin Nu'maan narrates that during the Battle of Badr, Hadhrat Abu Azeez bin Umayr, the real brother of Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Umayr (RA) was also captured (by…
narrations.summary: Ayyoob bin Nu'maan reports the same episode: Mus'ab asked Muhriz to bind Abu Azeez tightly for ransom, Abu Azeez protested, and his mother then paid four thousand dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zuhri reports that Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) once came to Madinah (before accepting Islaam) to meet Rasulullaah ﷺ at a time when Rasulullaah had intended to go to…
narrations.summary: Zuhri reports that Abu Sufyaan, before accepting Islaam, asked the Prophet to extend the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and was refused; he then sat down on the Prophet's bedding, and his daughter Ummu Habeebah rolled it up.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Ummu Habeebah (RA) added, "I would not like you to sit on his bedding."
narrations.summary: Ummu Habeebah adds that she did not want her father to sit on the Prophet's bedding.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Ahwas narrates, "We once visited Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood as he was with his three sons, who appeared (radiant) like three gold coins. As we looked at…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says he would rather dust the sand from his sons' graves than see a sparrow's egg fall from its nest, and that he would rather his family die and he follow them than see the sparrow die.

narrations.excerpt: The narration has already passed'45 concerning the statement that Hadhrat Umar SI made about what should be done with the prisoners from the Battle of Badr. He said, "I…
narrations.summary: Umar, disagreeing with Abu Bakr about the Badr prisoners, asks that Aqeel be handed to Ali and Abbaas to Hamza for execution, so Allaah would know the Muslims have no love for the Mushrikeen; the passage ends with an author's note on the Ansaar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr (RA) narrates that (during the Battle of Badr) Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA) said, "O Nabi of Allaah Should we not build you a structure…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr reports that Sa'd bin Mu'aadh offered to build the Prophet a shelter at Badr so he could stay safe, and the Prophet praised him and prayed for him.

narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports a man who feared he would not see the Prophet in Jannah; Allaah revealed Nisaa verse 69, promising companionship with the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) states that a man once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I love you so much that whenever I think…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports a man who loved the Prophet and feared he would be on a lower level in Jannah; Allaah revealed Nisaa verse 69, and the Prophet recited it to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that a man once asked Rasulullaah ﷺ when Qiyaamah will take place. "What have you prepared for the Day of Qiyaamah?" asked Rasulullaah ﷺ. The…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that a man asked when Qiyaamah would come and said he had prepared only his love for Allaah and His Rasool; the Prophet told him he would be with those he loves, and Anas says he loves the Prophet, Abu Bakr and Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration of Bukhaari states that a man from the desert once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and asked, "When will Qiyaamah take place?" "What!" exclaimed Rasulullaah ﷺ,…
narrations.summary: A man from the desert asks when Qiyaamah will come and says he loves Allaah and His Rasool; the Prophet tells him he will be with those he loves, and Anas says the Companions were overjoyed. A Tirmidhi report adds a similar exchange.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates that he once said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, "o Rasulullaah ﷺ (What will be the outcome of) A man who loves a group of people but is unable to…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr asks the Prophet about a man who loves a people but cannot do their deeds; the Prophet tells Abu Dharr he will be with those he loves, and Abu Dharr says he loves Allaah and His Rasool.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that the news once reached Hadhrat Ali (RA) that Rasulullaah ﷺ was experiencing severe hunger. Hadhrat Ali (RA) therefore left…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Ali earned dates for the hungry Prophet by drawing water for a Jewish man; the Prophet told him that love for Allaah brings hardship. Talha then dies before the Prophet arrives, and the Prophet prays that he be smiling when he meets Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ka'b bin Ujrah (RA) narrates that he once went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and found that his face had become extremely pale, "May my parents be sacrificed for you! What is…
narrations.summary: Ka'b bin Ujrah, hungry and having earned dates by watering a Jew's camel, brings them to the Prophet, who tells him that poverty comes swiftly to one who loves him and that he should prepare patience for trials.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Husayn bin Wahwah Ansaari (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Talha bin Baraa met Rasulullaah iif , he embraced Rasulullaah ﷺ and kissed his feet. He said, "O…
narrations.summary: Husayn bin Wahwah reports that Talha bin Baraa's love for the Prophet was so great that he was ready to obey even an order to kill his father, and that the Prophet prayed for Talha after his death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Talha bin Miskeen narrates that Hadhrat Talha bin Baraa (RA) came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "Stretch out your hand so that I may pledge my allegiance to you."…
narrations.summary: Talha bin Miskeen reports that Talha bin Baraa pledged to the Prophet only after being told Islaam does not require severing ties with parents; Talha later fell ill and died, and the Prophet prayed for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zuhri reports that someone once complained to Rasulullaah ﷺ that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Hudhaafa (RA) joked a lot and spoke many useless things. Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Zuhri reports that someone complained to the Prophet about Abdullaah bin Hudhaafa's jokes and useless talk, and the Prophet told them to leave him because his heart loves Allaah and His Rasool.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Adra (RA) narrates that he was guarding Rasulullaah ﷺ one night when he heard someone reciting Qur'aan in a loud voice. When Rasulullaah ﷺ came out, he said "O…
narrations.summary: Adra reports that a man reciting Qur'aan loudly at night was called a show-off, and the Prophet said he was Abdullaah bin Dhul Bijaadayn; after his burial the Prophet widened the grave, and mourned him because of his love for Allaah and His Rasool.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Sa'd reports, "I was once with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar when his leg cramped. "What is wrong with your leg?' I asked. 'The muscles have…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Sa'd reports that Abdullaah bin Umar's cramp eased when he named the Prophet, and recalls Zaid bin Dathana and Khubayb bin Adi refusing to let the Prophet be harmed even to save their own lives.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Weeps when his Father Embraces Islaam because of his Keenness for Abu Taalib to Accept Islaam. In the narration discussing how Hadhrat Abu Quhaafah…
narrations.summary: Anas and Abdullaah bin Umar report that Abu Bakr wept when his father Abu Quhaafah came to pledge to the Prophet, having hoped Abu Taalib would accept Islaam instead; Abu Bakr told the Prophet that his happiness is all he wishes for.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that amongst the captives of the Battle of Badr was Hadhrat Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib (RA). A man from the Ansaar captured him…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports Umar offering to free the captive Abbaas from the Ansaar, who refused; the Prophet was troubled, so the Companions began informing him only after a death, and later carried biers to his house. Umar bin Muhammad explains the place Mowda'ul Janaa'iz is named after this practice.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said to Hadhrat Abbaas (RA), "Accept Islaam, O Abbaas. I swear by Allaah that your accepting Islaam…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Umar urged Abbaas to accept Islaam, because the Prophet would have liked him to be among the first to do so.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that when Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) was pressurising Hadhrat Umar (RA) for something, he said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Tell me. How would you treat the…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports an exchange in which Umar honours Abbaas as the Prophet's uncle and, in a dispute over Bahrain land, refuses to rule for Abbaas on the testimony of Mughiera bin Shu'ba, after which Abbaas speaks harshly and Umar reminds him that his acceptance of Islaam pleased the Prophet more.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ali narrates that Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) once approached Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, "Rasulullaah ﷺ had apportioned the land of Bahrain for me." "Who else…
narrations.summary: Abbaas claims land in Bahrain that Rasulullah granted him, Umar does not rule in his favour despite Mughiera's testimony, and Umar then says he was happier at Abbaas's acceptance of Islaam than he would have been at his own father's.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ just arrived in Madinah, it was our practice to inform him whenever a person was about to pass away. Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri describes how the Companions first informed the Prophet of deaths in Madinah, then changed the practice to spare him inconvenience by bringing the bier to his house; Umar bin Muhammad adds that the place became known as Mowda'ul Janaa'iz.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once went to Hadhrat Faatima the daughter of Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Faatimal I have never seen anyone that Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Aslam reports that Umar went to Faatima, the Prophet's daughter, and told her that after her father none was dearer to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ went to the Sahabah as they were sitting with Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar none of them besides Hadhrat Abu…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Companions did not raise their gaze before the Prophet, except Abu Bakr and Umar, who were close enough to smile and speak informally with him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Usaama bin Shareek (RA) says, "We were sitting around Rasulullaah as if there were birds perched on our backs with no one uttering a word. Some people then…
narrations.summary: Usaama bin Shareek describes the Companions sitting so still around the Prophet that it seemed birds were perched on their backs, and the Prophet said the most beloved servants of Allaah are those with the best character.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Usaama bin Shareek (RA) said, "I once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ while his companions sat around him (so still) as if there were birds…
narrations.summary: Usaama bin Shareek says that when he came to Rasulullah, his companions sat around him so still that it seemed birds were perched on their backs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib (RA) says, "I once wanted to ask Rasulullaah ﷺ about something but delayed asking for two years because of the awe I felt for him."
narrations.summary: Baraa bin Aazib says he delayed for two years before asking the Prophet a question, out of the awe he felt for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zuhri reports, "Someone whose dependability is unquestionable mentioned to me that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ made wudhu or spat, the Sahabah (RA) would race to get…
narrations.summary: Zuhri relays that the Sahabah raced to collect the Prophet's saliva and leftover wudhu water for blessing, and the Prophet told them that whoever loves to be loved by Allaah and His Messenger must speak the truth, return trusts and not harm his neighbour.

narrations.excerpt: The narration of Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhramah (RA) and Marwaan concerning the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah as reported in Bukhaari and other books has already passed(5). This…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Mas'ood, sent to negotiate at Hudaybiyyah, describes how closely the Sahabah honoured the Prophet, and tells his people he has never seen any ruler's followers so devoted to their leader.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Quraad Sulami (RA) says, "We were with Rasulullaah ﷺ when he asked for some water. (When it was brought) Rasulullaah ﷺ dipped his hand in the water and…
narrations.summary: Abu Quraad Sulami says the Sahabah drank the water dripping from the Prophet's wudhu, and the Prophet told them that loving Allaah and His Messenger means keeping trusts, speaking truth and being kind to neighbours.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir the son of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) reports from his father that he once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ as Rasulullaah ﷺ was having his blood cupped.…
narrations.summary: Aamir reports that Abdullaah bin Zubayr drank the blood the Prophet had cupped out, and the Prophet foretold strife for him and for the people because of it; a separate note says popular opinion linked his great strength to that blood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Kaysaan who was the freed slave of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr reports that when Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) once came to Rasulullaah , he noticed Hadhrat Abdullaah bin…
narrations.summary: Kaysaan reports that Salmaan saw Abdullaah bin Zubayr drinking from the Prophet's cupping blood, and the Prophet told him he would be spared the Fire except to pass over the Bridge, after foretelling strife for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Safeenah (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once had himself cupped and said (to me), 'Take this blood and bury it out of the reach of animals, birds and people.' As 1…
narrations.summary: Safeenah says the Prophet asked him to bury his cupping blood out of sight, but he drank it instead; when he told the Prophet, the Prophet only laughed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports that his father Hadhrat Maalik Bin Sinaan licked the blood off Rasulullaah ﷺ 's face and then swallowed it. This happened after…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that his father Maalik bin Sinaan licked the Prophet's blood from his face after Uhud, and the Prophet said that once his blood had mixed with Maalik's, the Fire would never touch him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hakeemah bint Umaymah narrates from her mother that Rasulullaah had a wooden cup in which he used to urinate. He kept this cup beneath his bed. When he looked for…
narrations.summary: Hakeemah bint Umaymah reports that the Prophet kept a wooden cup for urine under his bed, and when a maidservant drank from it, the Prophet said she had built a solid barrier against the Fire.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ stayed at his house when Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, While Rasulullaah ﷺ stayed in the lower storey of the house,…
narrations.summary: Abu Ayyoob reports that he hosted the Prophet on the lower storey and worried about standing above him, and that the Prophet taught him dhikr with great reward; a second part says the Prophet sent back food containing garlic or onion.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) said, "o Rasulullaah SSi It is not proper for me to be above you. You should therefore move to the upper storey."…
narrations.summary: Abu Ayyoob asks the Prophet to move to the upper storey, since it is not proper for him to be above the Prophet, and the Prophet has his small luggage moved.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that there was a gutter belonging to Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) that was on the road Hadhrat Umar (RA) used (to the Masjid). Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Umar had Abbaas's gutter removed after blood from it spoiled his clothes, and then told Abbaas to restore it exactly where the Prophet had placed it, even if he had to climb on Umar's back.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Abdul Qaari says that he saw Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar place his hand on the place where Rasulullaah ﷺ sat on his pulpit and then…
narrations.summary: Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that Abdullaah bin Umar touched the place where the Prophet sat on his pulpit and then his own face, and Yazeed bin Abdullaah reports Sahabah taking sand from beside the Prophet's grave to make du'aa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Layla (RA) says that Hadhrat Usayd bin Hudhayr (RA) was a good man who was always smiling and jovial. One day as he was busy speaking to some people in the…
narrations.summary: Abu Layla reports that Usayd bin Hudhayr, while joking with the Prophet, asked to be allowed retaliation for a poke, and when the Prophet lifted his garment, Usayd embraced him and kissed his sides.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Habbaan bin Waasi reports from senior scholars from his tribe that Rasulullaah ﷺ had the shaft of an arrow in his hand during the Battle of Badr as he was…
narrations.summary: Habbaan bin Waasi reports that at Badr the Prophet nudged Sawaad bin Ghuzayyah's belly with an arrow shaft, and when Sawaad asked for retaliation and kissed the Prophet's belly, the Prophet made du'aa for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Rasulullaah ill? was once carrying the branch of a date palm in his hand when he met a man who had dyed his clothing yellow. Nudging the man's…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that the Prophet jabbed a man wearing yellow dye with a date-palm branch, leaving a mark, and when the man asked for retaliation the Prophet bared his belly and the man kissed it, forgoing retribution on condition of the Prophet's intercession.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once saw that Hadhrat Sawaad bin Amr was wearing perfume. "Remove the. Remove the Waras!" Rasulullaah ﷺ exclaimed. Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that the Prophet prodded Sawaad bin Amr in the belly with a twig for wearing perfume, and the rest of the account is said to match the report above.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Hasan 'states that a man called Sawaadah bin Amr used to apply so much of Khalooq fragrance that he actually resembled the branch of a date…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Sawaadah bin Amr wore so much Khalooq perfume that the Prophet shook it off his clothes, and after the Prophet lightly struck him with a twig he asked for retaliation, then kissed the Prophet, forgoing it on condition of intercession.

narrations.excerpt: The narration of Hadhrat Husayn bin Wahwah has already passed describing how Hadhrat Talha bin Baraa (RA) embraced Rasulullaah ﷺ and kissed his feet when he met…
narrations.summary: This is a cross-reference saying that Talha bin Baraa embraced the Prophet and kissed his feet on meeting him, and that Abu Bakr's kiss on the Prophet's forehead at his death will be quoted later.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) reports that when the people of Madinah were being defeated during the Battle of uhud, the people started saying that Rasulullaah ﷺ had been…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that when Madinah heard the Prophet had been martyred at Uhud, an Ansaari woman who had lost her father, son, husband and brother went looking for him, and on finding him safe said she no longer cared about her losses.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) says that on the day the Battle of uhud was fought, none but he was with Rasulullaah ﷺ near Madinah. None of the Sahabah (RA) remained behind in…
narrations.summary: Zubayr reports that on the day of Uhud, when the women of Madinah heard that the Prophet had been martyred, one woman set out on foot to see for herself how he was.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ passed by a lady from the Banu Dinaar tribe whose husband, brother and father had been martyred while…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that a woman of Banu Dinaar, whose husband, brother and father had all died at Uhud, asked after the Prophet and said that after seeing him every calamity seemed trivial.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) was firing arrows in front of Rasulullaah ﷺ during the Battle of Uhud. He was a proficient archer and was shielding…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that during Uhud Abu Talha shielded the Prophet with his arrows and his own chest, asked him not to rise lest an arrow strike him, and offered to be sent on any task.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qataadah bin Nu'maan (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was given a bow as a gift, which he gave to me during the Battle of Uhud. I used it to fire arrows in front of…
narrations.summary: Qataadah bin Nu'maan says that after his bow broke during Uhud, he stood in front of the Prophet and turned his own face to take each arrow aimed at the Prophet's face.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once came out to us from his room during the illness in which he passed away. He had a bandage wrapped around his head…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that in the Prophet's final illness he said he was standing at his Kowthar and that a servant of Allaah had chosen the Aakhirah over this world, and that only Abu Bakr understood and wept.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent for Hadhrat Faatima (RA) after Allaah revealed the Surah: He said to her, "This tells me of my pending…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that after a revelation the Prophet told Faatima that his death was near, and she wept until he told her she would be the first of his family to join him, and then she laughed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "During his final illness, Rasulullaah ﷺ once called for his daughter Faatima When he whispered something to her, she wept. He then called…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that during his final illness the Prophet whispered to Faatima, first making her weep and then making her laugh when he told her she would be the first of his family to join him.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) states, "When I asked Faatima about her laughing and crying, she replied, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ first informed me that he was…
narrations.summary: Ummu Salamah reports that Faatima laughed because the Prophet had told her that she would lead the women of Jannah after Maryam, the daughter of Imraan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Alaa (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was about to leave this world, Hadhrat Faatima ISI started weeping. Rasulullaah ﷺ said to her, "Do not weep, dear…
narrations.summary: Alaa reports that as the Prophet was about to pass away, Faatima wept, and he told her to say Innaa Lillaahi wa Innaa Ilayhi Raaji'oon, since every calamity is rewarded, and she asked whether this applied even to losing him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ sent him (as governor) to Yemen, Rasulullaah ﷺ walked with him as he gave him advice. Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA)…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal reports that as the Prophet walked beside him on his way to Yemen, the Prophet told him he might not see him again and that those closest to him are the people of taqwa, wherever they are; Mu'aadh wept at the parting.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Do not weep, O Mu'aadh because this weeping is from Shaytaan."
narrations.summary: A short variant reports that the Prophet told Mu'aadh not to weep, because such weeping comes from Shaytaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas Si reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once informed that the Ansaar men and women were crying in the Masjid, "What makes them cry?" Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that when Rasulullah heard the Ansaar weeping for fear of his death, he spoke from the pulpit, foretelling that the Ansaar would dwindle to little more than salt in food and advising that their good be accepted and their faults overlooked.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummul Fadhl bint Haarith (RA) says that when she came to Rasulullaah ﷺ during his final illness; she started weeping. Rasulullaah ﷺ lifted his head and asked,…
narrations.summary: Ummul Fadhl bint Haarith reports that she wept during his final illness fearing how they would be treated after his death, and the Prophet replied that they would be in a weaker position once he had left.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) says, "May my father and I be sacrificed for our beloved Nabi ﷺ who gave us the news of his demise six days in advance. When his end…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports the Prophet's final instructions: he would be bathed by his closest family, shrouded in his own clothes, prayed over first by the angels, and placed in the grave by the men of his family.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed bin Baabnoos says, "A friend and I once went to Hadhrat Aa'isha and sought permission to enter. She threw us some cushions and then concealed herself…
narrations.summary: Yazeed bin Baabnoos reports Aa'isha's account of the Prophet's last illness and death, Abu Bakr's kisses on his forehead and his speech that Muhammad had died while Allaah lives forever, and Umar then urging the people to pledge allegiance to Abu Bakr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) narrates that when they (the family of Rasulullaah illi ) started the burial preparations for Rasulullaah ﷺ, they locked the door and did…
narrations.summary: Ali bin Abi Taalib reports the dispute over who would bury the Prophet, which Abu Bakr settled by saying that the family should decide who enters the room; a second report from Ali bin Husayn says the Ansaar also claimed the right.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) and Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) were with Rasulullaah ﷺ when his illness grew severe. When Rasulullaah ﷺ saw…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Ali stayed with the Prophet as he died, and that Ali then washed the body with Fadhl bin Abbaas and an Ansaari, guided by a voice from the house to bathe him in his clothes.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, groups of men were let into the room and they performed the Janaazah salaah individually…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that after the Prophet's death, groups of men entered the room and prayed the Janaazah salaah individually, with no one leading them, followed by the women, children and slaves.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sahl in Sa'd (RA) that after Rasulullaah ﷺ was shrouded in the burial shroud, he was placed on a bed, which was then placed in the corner of the room. The people…
narrations.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that once the Prophet was shrouded and placed on a bed in a corner of the room, people entered in groups to pray the Janaazah salaah, with no one leading them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Moosa bin Muhammad bin Ibraheem says that he found a book in which his father, had written that after Rasulullaah ﷺ was shrouded in the burial shroud, he was…
narrations.summary: Moosa bin Muhammad bin Ibraheem reports, from a book written by his father, that Abu Bakr and Umar greeted the Prophet and made du'aa at the front of the rows, with no one acting as imam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat All (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was placed on a bed, he said to the people, "None shall be the imaam (to lead the Janaazah salaah) because Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Ali (RA) narrates the janaazah salaah for the Prophet, which the people performed in groups without an imaam, and Ali's farewell supplication.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, the Sahabah (RA) were all whispering to each other, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) instructed his slave to listen to…
narrations.summary: Anas (RA) reports that Abu Bakr, on hearing of the Prophet's death, hurried in grief towards the Masjid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that on the day Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddeeq (RA) emerged (from Rasulullaah room) as Hadhrat umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports Abu Bakr's address on the Prophet's death, his recitation of Aal Imraan 144, and Umar's collapse on hearing it; Uthmaan's own account of his grief follows in the same text.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Sa'eed bin Yarboo narrates that Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib one day had his face covered and was extremely grieved, "I notice that you are deeply…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Sa'eed bin Yarboo reports that Ali was deeply grieved at the Prophet's death, and Abu Bakr replied that no one grieved more than he did.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) says, "When we (the wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ) gathered together and were weeping (over the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ), we did not have a wink of…
narrations.summary: Ummu Salamah describes the wives' grief at the Prophet's death, the sound of grave-digging before dawn, and Bilaal's weeping when he called the Fajr adhaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dhu'ayb Hudhali says, "When I arrived in Madinah, the wailing of the people of Madinah pulsated like the calls of 'Labbaik' from people performing Hajj…
narrations.summary: Abu Dhu'ayb Hudhali describes the wailing in Madinah when he arrived and learned that the Prophet had passed away.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, the governor of Makkah was Hadhrat Attaab bin Usayd (RA). When the news of Rasulullaah ﷺ's demise reached the…
narrations.summary: A narrator whose name is lost in the OCR reports that the governor of Makkah, Attaab bin Usayd, could not speak after the Prophet's death, so Suhayl bin Amr addressed the people in Makkah in his place.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ja'far says, "After the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ, l never saw Faatima laugh. All I saw was her mouth extend on one side (as she smiled)."
narrations.summary: Abu Ja'far reports that Faatima never laughed after the Prophet's death and only smiled slightly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Is'haaq reports that when Rasulullaah till passed away, Hadhrat Abu Bakr said, "Today we have lost revelation and speech from Allaah." (3!
narrations.summary: Is'haaq reports Abu Bakr's words on the Prophet's death that revelation and speech from Allaah had now been lost.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, Hadhrat Ummu Ayman wept bitterly. When asked what made her weep so bitterly about the demise of Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Ummu Ayman wept because revelation had ended; Abu Bakr and Umar visited her to console her, and their own tears followed hers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) also reports that after the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ , Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once said to Hadhrat umar (RA), "Come with me to visit ummu Ayman " When…
narrations.summary: After Rasulullah passed away, Abu Bakr and Umar visit Ummu Ayman, who weeps because revelation from the heavens has ended, and a second report says she wept bitterly for the same reason.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Hadhrat Moosa bin Uqba quotes Hadhrat Ummu Ayman (RA) as saying, "I am weeping because the news from the heavens used to come to us in large quantities and…
narrations.summary: Moosa bin Uqba quotes Ummu Ayman saying she wept because the news from the heavens, which had come to them daily, had ended.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, the people wept bitterly and said, "We wished that we would pass away before Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the people wept at the Prophet's death, and Ma'n bin Adi replied that he wished to believe in him after his death as he had in his life.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas ffi reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ fell seriously ill, Hadhrat Faatima (RA) bemoaned, "O! The pain my father is suffering!" Rasulullaah ﷺ then said to her,…
narrations.summary: Anas reports Faatima's grief when Rasulullah fell ill and after his death, including her words about Jibra'eel informing them and her question to Anas about throwing sand over him.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes that Hadhrat Faatima (RA) said, "O Anas! How did your hearts allow you to return after burying Rasulullaah ﷺ in the sand?" Hadhrat Hammaad says…
narrations.summary: Another narration gives Faatima's words to Anas after the Prophet was buried, and Hammaad reports that Thaabit wept as he related it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that Hadhrat Safiyya bint Abdul Muttalib (RA) recited a few couplets in memory of Rasulullaah ﷺ. (The meaning of these couplets are): "My heart…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports Safiyya's couplets in grief for the Prophet; a second set of her verses and a third narration from Muhammad bin Mi bin Husayn follow.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ghunaym bin Qais reports that he heard his father say some couplets after the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ. They were: "Behold! I have been destroyed by the departure…
narrations.summary: Ghunaym bin Qais reports the couplets his father recited after the Prophet's departure.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) left the house one night to keep watch. When he saw a lantern burning, he went closer and found an old…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports that Umar, on his night patrol, found an old woman grieving for the Prophet in her couplets, wept with her, and asked her to pray for him.

narrations.excerpt: Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Aasim bin Muhammad reports that his father said, "I have never seen Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) mention Rasulullaah ﷺ without his eyes quickly…
narrations.summary: Aasim bin Muhammad reports that his father said Abdullaah bin Umar's eyes always filled with tears whenever he mentioned the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muthanna bin Sa'eed Daari reports that he heard Hadhrat Anas (RA) say, "1 see my beloved (Rasulullaah ﷺ every night (in a dream). "He then started weeping.
narrations.summary: Muthanna bin Sa'eed Daari reports that Anas said he saw the Prophet in a dream every night, and wept as he said it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ka'bbinAlqama narrates that a Sahabi by the name of Hadhrat Gharfa bin Haarith Kindi once heard a Christian reviling Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Gharfa hit the…
narrations.summary: Ka'b bin Alqama reports that Gharfa bin Haarith Kindi struck a Christian who reviled the Prophet, and that Amr bin Al Aas replied that a treaty applied, which Gharfa rejected.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Gharfa bin Haarith (RA) was a Sahabi who fought with Hadhrat Ikrama bin Abu Jahal against the.apostates in Yemen. He narrates that he once passed by a Christian…
narrations.summary: Gharfa bin Haarith reports his own case: he struck a Christian called Mundaqoon in Egypt for reviling the Prophet, and Amr bin Al Aas said that a treaty protected him.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Gharfa bin Haarith Kindi (RA) was a Sahabi who once passed by a man with whom the Muslims had entered into a peace treaty. When…
narrations.summary: Another narration tells of Gharfa killing a man under a peace treaty after he reviled the Prophet, and Amr bin Al Aas objecting that the treaty protected him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Jahash (RA) on a expedition to a place called Nakhla. Rasulullaah iffif's…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports the expedition to Nakhla under Abdullaah bin Jahash, who followed the sealed instructions, the killing of Ibn Hadhrami in a sacred month and the verses revealed after it; Jundub bin Abdullaah gives a second report of Ubaydah bin Haarith's expedition, which Abdullaah bin Jahash took over.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that after the Battle of Ahzaab, Rasulullaah ﷺ issued instructions (to the Sahabah (RA)) saying, "None of you should perform Asr…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's order after the Battle of Ahzaab not to pray Asr until reaching Banu Qurayzah, and that he did not rebuke either group who differed on it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ka'b bin Maalik (RA) narrates that after the Battle of Ahzaab, Rasulullaah ﷺ returned home and wore his armour (for. a second time after taking it off) and…
narrations.summary: Ka'b bin Maalik reports the Prophet's order after the Battle of Ahzaab to march on Banu Qurayzah at once, and the two groups' different decisions on Asr; Duhaym adds a separate account of the same event.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that during the Battle of Hunayn when Rasulullaah ﷺ saw the Sahabah (RA) dispersing (when caught by surprise), he instructed Hadhrat Abbaas…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that at Hunayn the Prophet had Abbaas call the Ansaar and the Bay'ah companions, and that Abu Sufyaan's requests to Abu Bakr, Umar and Faatima were refused.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ikrama (RA) reports that after Rasulullaah ﷺ had entered into the treaty with the people of Makkah; the Banu Khuzaa'ah tribe who had been Rasulullaah ﷺ's allies…
narrations.summary: Ikrama reports that after the Quraysh breached the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, Abu Sufyaan went to Madinah to ask Abu Bakr, Umar and Faatima to renew it, and was refused by each, so he returned with nothing achieved.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Azeez bin Umayr (RA) who was the real brother of Hadhrat Mus'ab bin umayr says, "I was amongst the prisoners captured the Muslims) during the Battle of Badr.…
narrations.summary: Abu Azeez bin Umayr, a prisoner taken at Badr, recounts that the Ansaar gave him wheat bread and ate dates themselves, as the Prophet had commanded them to treat prisoners well.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ at a time when Rasulullaah . ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abi Layla reports that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha sat down at once when the Prophet told him to during a sermon, and Aa'isha gives a second report of the same incident.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once delivering a sermon when he told the people to be seated. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) heard this instruction…
narrations.summary: Ataa reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood sat down at the door at once when the Prophet told the people to be seated during a sermon.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ had just stood up on the pulpit when he told the people to be seated. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood heard this instruction…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports the same incident: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood sat at the Masjid door until the Prophet called him inside.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that they were once with Rasulullaah Oil when he stepped out. Seeing a large dome, Rasulullaah (icp asked, "What is this?" When the Sahabah…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet disliked an Ansaari's dome and turned away from its owner until he demolished it, and that the Prophet said every building is a curse on its owner except what is necessary.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas narrates that he was once wearing a red shawl when he was walking with Rasulullaah ﷺ in Aqaba Adhaakhir (a valley between Makkah and…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas reports that when the Prophet disliked his red shawl, he threw it into the oven, and the Prophet told him he could have given it to the women of his household.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sahl bin Hadhaliyyah Abshami (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to him, "Khuraym Asadi is an excellent man if it were not for his long hair and his…
narrations.summary: Sahl bin Handhaliyya reports that the Prophet praised Khuraym Asadi except for his long hair and low garment, and Khuraym immediately cut his hair and raised his garment.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat juthaama bin Musaahiq bin Rabee bin Qais Kanani was Hadhrat Umar's envoy to Heraclius (the emperor of Rome). He says, "I once sat on a throne (when visiting…
narrations.summary: Juthaama bin Musaahiq reports that as Umar's envoy to Heraclius he got off a gold throne he had been given, because he had heard the Prophet forbid such things.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Raafi bin Khadeej (RA) says, "My uncle came home one day and said to me, 'Today Rasulullaah ﷺ had forbidden us from something that has been very beneficial for…
narrations.summary: Raafi bin Khadeej relays his uncle's words that the Prophet had forbidden them something that had been beneficial, and that obedience to Allaah and His Rasool is even better.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Aslam bin Bujra (RA) belonged to the Banu Haarith bin Khazraj tribe and was a very old man. He reports about himself that he would often come to…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Aslam bin Bujra reports that, in his old age, he would go back to Madinah to pray two rakahs in the Prophet's Masjid, having forgotten to do so on each visit, as the Prophet had instructed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mughiera bin Shu'ba (RA) reports, "1 once proposed for the hand of a lady from the Ansaar. When I mentioned this to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he asked, 'Did you see her?'…
narrations.summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba reports that, on the Prophet's advice, he looked at a woman from the Ansaar before marrying her; she allowed it only because the Prophet had told him to.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ma'roor bin Suwayd reports that he once saw Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) in Rabdha. Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) was wearing a thick shawl and his slave was wearing exactly…
narrations.summary: Ma'roor bin Suwayd reports that Abu Dharr, who had insulted Bilaal over his mother, was rebuked by the Prophet, who told him that slaves are his brothers to be fed and clothed as he is.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Hadhrat Abu Dharr "They are your brothers whom Allaah has placed in your custody. When Allaah has placed someone's…
narrations.summary: Another narration gives the Prophet's words to Abu Dharr that his slaves are his brothers, whom Allaah has put in his care, and should be fed and clothed as he is.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Salamah bin Abdur Rahmaan narrates that Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf once complained to Rasulullaah ﷺ that he was getting too much of lice and therefore…
narrations.summary: Abu Salamah bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that Umar tore the silk garment worn by Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf's son Abu Salmah, saying the Prophet had allowed silk to Abdur Rahmaan only because of lice and not to others.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Abu Salamah states that Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf once went to Hadhrat Umar (RA) with his son Muhammad who was wearing a silk garment.…
narrations.summary: Umar tears the silk garment worn by the son of Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, and Abdur Rahmaan protests, pointing out that he himself wears silk.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Seereen reports that Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) once went to Hadhrat Umar (RA) wearing a silk garment. "What is this, O Khaalid?" enquired Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Umar challenges Khaalid bin Waleed for wearing a silk garment, and in a second report Umar orders the people to tear up the silk cloak of Khaalid bin Sa'eed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdah bin Abu Lubaabah reports that he was informed that Hadhrat Umar once passed a person in the Masjid. The man wa? performing salaah and wearing a green…
narrations.summary: Umar cuts the silk buttons off a man's green garment after the man finishes his salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Sufyaan Qaari says, "When my brother passed away, he made a bequest that a hundred Dinaars should be donated in the path of Allaah. I therefore went to…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed Qaari goes to Uthmaan about his brother's bequest wearing a silk-trimmed cloak, Ali pulls at the cloak to tear it, and Uthmaan gives a ruling on the bequest.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Aamir bin Rabee'ah narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) appointed Hadhrat Qudaamah bin Madh'oon (RA) as governor of Bahrain. Hadhrat Qudaamah (RA) also…
narrations.summary: Jaarood and Abu Hurayrah testify that Qudaamah bin Madh'oon, Umar's governor of Bahrain, drank wine, and Umar has him lashed, then later reconciles with him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed bin Ubaydullaah reports from some of his companions that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood Sffilsei once saw a man laughing at a funeral. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood tells a man laughing at a funeral that he will never speak to him again.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that on the day the Battle of Badr of was fought, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to the Sahabah (RA), "I know well that the men from the…
narrations.summary: Abu Hudhayfah says he would kill Abbaas at Badr against the Prophet's order to spare the Banu Haashim, Umar asks to behead him, and Abu Hudhayfah lives in fear of his words until he is martyred at Yamaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ma'bad bin Ka'b reports that the Muslims laid siege to the (Jewish) Banu Qurayzah tribe for fifteen days until the siege became too much for them to bear and…
narrations.summary: During the siege of Banu Qurayzah, Abu Lubaabah gestures to them that they will be killed if they surrender, and then regrets it deeply.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Moosa bin Uqba states that the Banu Qurayzah asked, "0 Abu Lubaabah! What is your opinion? What would you instruct us to do because we have…
narrations.summary: After his regret, Abu Lubaabah ties himself to a pillar of the Masjid, and the Prophet says he will not untie him until Allaah decides the matter.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ did not see Hadhrat Thaabit bin Qais (RA) for awhile, a Sahabi volunteered to make enquiries about him. When…
narrations.summary: Thaabit bin Qais fears that raising his voice above the Prophet's has destroyed his deeds, and the Prophet gives him glad tidings that he will be among the people of Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Thaabit Ansaari (RA) reports that Hadhrat Thaabit bin Qais once said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I fear that I have been destroyed." When…
narrations.summary: Thaabit bin Qais tells the Prophet he fears ruin because he loves praise, beauty and a loud voice, and the Prophet promises him a praiseworthy life, martyrdom and Jannah, which he later attains at the battle against Musaylama.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha Ip narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ had a mat that he made into a room at nights to perform salaah (during Ramadhaan) and which he spread out during the day to…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that Rasulullah prayed at night in a room made of mats during Ramadhaan, and told the Sahabah to take on only the deeds they can keep up, since the most beloved deeds to Allaah are the consistent ones.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik Shifts reports that it was for only a single day that he saw Rasulullaah ﷺ wearingasilverringwhenthe Sahabah (RA) started having rings made for…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet wore a silver ring for only one day, and when he discarded it the Sahabah also removed their rings.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ wore a gold ring but then discarded it saying, "I shall never wear it again!" The Sahabah…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the Prophet wore a gold ring, then discarded it saying he would never wear it again, and the Sahabah removed their rings.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salamah (RA) narrates that when the Quraysh sent Hadhrat Khaarijah bin Kurz to spy for them, he returned full of praise (for the Muslims). The Quraysh said to…
narrations.summary: Umar declines to carry the Prophet's message to the Muslim prisoners in Makkah, so Uthmaan goes instead, is escorted by his cousin Abaan, and the Sahabah pledge allegiance under the tree at Hudaybiyyah, with the Prophet pledging on Uthmaan's behalf.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Abaan said, "Dear cousin! I see that you are humbling yourself. Why do you not let your garment fall below your ankles as your tribe does?"…
narrations.summary: Abaan tells Uthmaan to let his garment fall and to perform Tawaaf, and Uthmaan replies that they follow the Prophet's example and do nothing before him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once sent for him after the Battle of Yamaamah. With Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) at the time was Hadhrat umar…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr and Umar persuade Zaid bin Thaabit to compile the Qur'aan into one manuscript, and Zaid finds the last verses of Surah Taubah with Khuzaymah bin Thaabit.

narrations.excerpt: The statement of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) has already passed in which he said, "I swear by the Being Who controls my lifel I prefer falling from the sky rather than…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr swears he would rather fall from the sky than leave unfought what the Prophet fought for, and then wages jihaad against the Arabs who renounced Islaam and refused zakaah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "By Allaah! I shall certainly fight those who differentiate between salaah and zakaah (by performing Salaat…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr vows to fight those who separate salaah from zakaah, even over a rope the Arabs once gave the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration has also passed in which Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "I swear by the Being besides Whom there js none worthy of worship! Even though wild dogs should…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr vows that he will not recall the army Rasulullah sent out under Usaama bin Zaid nor untie a flag Rasulullah tied, and in a second report says he would send it even if he were the only one left in Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Urwa (RA) quotes that Hadhrat Abu Bakr said, "I have dared to do something extremely perilous! I swear by the Being Who controls my life! I…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr tells Usaama to march as the Prophet commanded, saying he would rather have all the Arabs turn against him than hold back the army.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) caught hold of the beard of Hadhrat Umar (RA) as he said, "May your mother lose you, O son of Khattaab! You are asking me…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr seizes Umar's beard and rebukes him for asking that Usaama be relieved of the command the Prophet gave him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) once said to her father Hadhrat Umar (RA) "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Why don't you wear clothing of a better…
narrations.summary: Umar reminds his daughter Hafsah of the hard life the Prophet and Abu Bakr led, and says he will share their hardship so he may join them in ease in the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was once sitting amongst some friends when a cotton garment was brought. He started wearing it and had hardly…
narrations.summary: Umar recites the du'aa for a new garment, cites the Prophet's words on giving old clothes to the poor, and has the excess sleeves cut off without stitching the ends.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports, "(My father) Umar once wore a new upper garment and then asked me to bring a knife. He then said, 'Dear son! Stretch the sleeves…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar had the sleeves of a new garment cut to length, unevenly, because he had seen the Prophet do the same.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once addressed the Hajar Aswad (Black Stone) saying, "Behold! I swear by Allaah that I know well that you can neither cause…
narrations.summary: Umar kisses the Black Stone only because the Prophet did, Abu Bakr does the same on his Hajj, and the Prophet is reported to have kissed it while saying it neither benefits nor harms.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ya'la bin Umayyah (RA) says, "I was performing Tawaaf with Hadhrat Uthmaan. After kissing the Hajar Aswad, I was walking next to the Kabah. When we passed by the…
narrations.summary: Ya'la bin Umayyah asks Uthmaan to touch the western pillar of the Kabah, and Uthmaan reminds him that the Prophet did not touch it and that the Prophet is the perfect example.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Bakr bin Abdullaah narrates that a Bedouin once asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas, "Why is it that (on the occasion of Hajj) the family of Mu'aawiya gives people…
narrations.summary: Bakr bin Abdullaah reports that Abdullaah bin Abbaas told a Bedouin why his family serves nabeedh on Hajj, recalling that Rasulullah came to them with Usaama bin Zaid, drank it and praised it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ja'far bin Tammaam reports that a man once approached Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas and asked, "Tell me about this Nabeedh from raisins that you give people to…
narrations.summary: Ja'far bin Tammaam reports Ibn Abbaas explaining that the Prophet praised the Nabeedh that Abbaas served him, and that he prefers not to replace it with milk and honey.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Seereen narrates, "I was once with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar in Arafaat. When the people left, I left with him until we reached the Imaam and performed the…
narrations.summary: Ibn Seereen reports that Abdullaah bin Umar stopped his animal at a narrow place near Ma'zamain to relieve himself, because the Prophet had done so there.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) used to go to a certain tree between Makkah and Madinah beneath which he would have his afternoon nap. He…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar used to take his afternoon nap under a certain tree between Makkah and Madinah because the Prophet did the same.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) was extremely particular about following in the footsteps of Rasulullaah ﷺ. He would therefore note every spot…
narrations.summary: Naafi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar was very particular about following the Prophet's footsteps, marking every place he prayed on journeys and watering a tree under which the Prophet had dismounted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaahid says, "We once accompanied Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) on a journey. When he passed by a certain place, he turned to the side of the road. When we…
narrations.summary: Mujaahid reports that Abdullaah bin Umar turned aside on a journey to follow the Prophet's footsteps, and the Prophet then declared each of the Ansaar, Muhaajireen and Banu Haashim equally beloved to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi says, "If you had to see Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) following in the footsteps of Rasulullaah ﷺ, you would say that he is mad."
narrations.summary: Naafi says that Abdullaah bin Umar followed the Prophet's footsteps so closely that an observer would think him mad.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha Wa says, "There was none who followed so meticulously the footsteps of Rasulullaah ﷺ in all his stops (during his travels) as Abdullaah bin Umar did."
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says that no one followed the footsteps of Rasulullah on his journeys, at every stop, as closely as Abdullaah bin Umar did.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that if anyone had to see Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar follow In the footsteps of Rasulullaah ﷺ, they would think that his mind was affected.…
narrations.summary: Naafi says that Abdullaah bin Umar searched for the Prophet's footsteps as thoroughly as a camel searches for its lost young one.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Umayyah bin Abdullaah reports that he once asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA), "we find the salaah of fear and the salaah of a resident in…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Umayyah asks Abdullaah bin Umar why the salaah of fear and the salaah of a resident are in the Qur'aan but not the traveller's salaah, and Abdullaah replies that they follow what the Prophet did.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umayyah bin Abdullaah bin Khaalid bin Usayd reports that he once asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), "in the Qur'aan we find mention of shortening the salaah…
narrations.summary: Umayyah bin Abdullaah asks Abdullaah bin Umar why the Qur'aan mentions shortening the salaah of fear but not the traveller's salaah, and Abdullaah says the Prophet did it and they copy him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Waarid bin Abu Aasim reports that he once met Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar in Mina and asked him about the salaah performed on a journey. When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin…
narrations.summary: Waarid bin Abu Aasim asks Abdullaah bin Umar about the salaah on a journey while in Mina, and Abdullaah rebukes him by citing the Prophet's practice of praying two rakaahs; Abu Muneed Jurashi adds a question about shortening salaah in safety.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam reports that he once saw Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar perform salaah with his buttons open. When he asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar about it, he…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports seeing Abdullaah bin Umar pray with his buttons open, and Abdullaah says he saw the Prophet do this.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qurra (RA) says, "I went to Rasulullaah ﷺ in the company of a group from the Banu Muzayna tribe and we pledged our allegiance to him. Rasulullaah ﷺ's buttons were…
narrations.summary: Qurra reports that he and a delegation of Banu Muzayna pledged allegiance to the Prophet and felt the seal of prophethood on his back through his open collar, and Urwa bin Abdullaah reports that Mu'aawiya bin Qurra and his son always prayed with their buttons open.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ka'b bin Ujrah (RA) says, "We were all sitting before (the room of) Rasulullaah ﷺ in the Masjid. We were a group from the Ansaar and there was also a group from…
narrations.summary: Ka'b bin Ujrah reports a dispute among the Ansaar, Muhaajireen and Banu Haashim over who was closest to the Prophet, and the Prophet affirmed the claim of each group and said he was the brother of the Ansaar, one of the Muhaajireen, and from Banu Haashim.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Awfa (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf once complained to Rasulullaah ﷺ about Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf complains about Khaalid bin Waleed, and the Prophet forbids anyone from hurting the veterans of Badr or Khaalid himself.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that there once arose a dispute between Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf and Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA). Hadhrat Khaalid said to'Hadhrat Abdur…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed disputes superiority with Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf over the date of their acceptance of Islaam, and in a second report the Prophet's farewell words ask people to treat the Ansaar kindly and overlook their faults.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that there once arose between Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf and Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) a dispute of that nature that usually…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that a dispute arose between Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf and Khaalid bin Waleed, and the Prophet told them to leave his Companions alone because even spending Uhud's worth of gold cannot match the reward of a Badri's mudd.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Allaah has selected my companions from all in the universe apart from the prophets and messengers. He has then…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports the Prophet's saying that Allaah chose his Companions above all creation after the prophets, singling out Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthmaan and Ali, and that his Ummah's first four generations are chosen too.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was on his deathbed, the Sahabah (RA) asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Give us some advice." Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf reports the Prophet's final advice to be good to the early Muhaajireen and their children, warning that otherwise no deed will be accepted.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ advised, "I advise you to be good towards those Muhaajireen who were the earliest adherents to Islaam, towards their children…
narrations.summary: The Prophet advises goodness towards the early Muhaajireen and their children, and Zaid bin Sa'd reports the Prophet's last sermon in which he asked people to treat the Ansaar well, accepting the good among them and overlooking their faults.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when mention was made of Hadhrat Maalik bin Dukhshun before Rasulullaah ﷺ and some people started accusing him of being the head of the…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet stopped people from accusing Maalik bin Dukhshun of hypocrisy, and Ibn Abbaas reports the Prophet cursing anyone who reviles his Companions.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Never revile my Sahabah (RA). May Allaah curse the one- who reviles my Sahabah (RA).
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports the Prophet's command never to revile his Companions and his curse on anyone who does.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Zaid bin Amr -bin Nufayl once said, "Are you people telling me to revile the Sahabah (RA) May Allaah rather shower His mercy on them and forgive them…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Zaid asks whether people are telling him to revile the Sahabah, and prays that Allaah shower His mercy on them and forgive them all.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Jubayr reports that a man once asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas for some advice. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "I advise you to adopt Taqwa…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Jubayr reports that Ibn Abbaas advised a man to fear Allaah and not to speak ill of the Sahabah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that the final words that Rasulullaah ﷺ spoke were: "Be my successors over the members of my household them well and care for…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's final words about his household, and Ummu Salamah reports the Prophet covering Faatima, Ali, Hasan and Husayn with his shawl and praying for them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "O progeny of Abdul Muttalib! I have asked Allaah for three things for you. That He keeps…
narrations.summary: The Prophet ﷺ prayed that the progeny of Abdul Muttalib be kept steadfast, educated and guided, warned that bearing enmity towards them leads to Jahannam, and promised to repay anyone who is not repaid in this world for a kindness shown to them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that on the occasion of Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s marriage to the daughter of Hadhrat Ali (RA), he heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) say to the people, "Will…
narrations.summary: Jaabir (RA) reports Umar's remark, on marrying Ali's daughter, that this made him kin to the Prophet ﷺ; a second report has the Prophet warning against speaking ill of the Quraysh, whose status is high in Allaah's sight.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that to the best of his knowledge, Rasulullaah ﷺ stated, "Always put the Quraysh forwards and never step ahead of them. Had I no fear of the…
narrations.summary: Ali (RA) reports the Prophet's instruction to put the Quraysh first and never to go ahead of them, and his statement that he would otherwise have told them their high status in Allaah's sight.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came to her and said, "Had I no fear of the Quraysh becoming boastful, I would have informed them of their status in…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ told her he would have revealed the high status of the Quraysh had he not feared their pride.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ mentioned, "Look for trustworthiness amongst the Quraysh because a trustworthy person from the Quraysh is superior…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet's praise of the trustworthiness of the Quraysh; Rifaa'ah bin Raafi reports that Umar was sent to gather the people, and that the Prophet told them only those with taqwa are Allaah's friends and warned against searching out the faults of the Quraysh.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Harbouring enmity for the Banu Haashim and for the Ansaar lead to Kufr and harbouring enmity for Arabs…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports the Prophet's warning that enmity towards Banu Haashim and the Ansaar leads to kufr, and that enmity towards the Arabs is a sign of hypocrisy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once entered my room and said, 'O Aa'isha! Your people shall be first of my Ummah to meet me.' After Rasulullaah sat down, I…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha (RA) relates the Prophet's prophecy that the Quraysh would be the first of his Ummah to die and be envied, after which people would become like locusts devouring the weak until Qiyaamah; a second narration calls them the first to be destroyed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates that he was once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when Rasulullaah ﷺ asked (the Sahabah (RA)), "Tell me whose Imaan is best from all those with imaan." The…
narrations.summary: Umar (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ ranked the Imaan of those who believe in him without seeing him as the strongest of all, above the angels, the Ambiyaa and the martyrs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once asked, "Tell me which creation will hold the highest status in Allaah's sight on the Day of Qiyaamah," When the Sahabah…
narrations.summary: Amr (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ ranked those who believe in him unseen above the angels and the Ambiyaa; Abu Jumu'ah (RA) reports that when Abu Ubaydah asked whether anyone was superior to the Sahabah, the Prophet gave the same answer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu umaamah (RA) states that he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "Glad tiding for those who believe in me after having seen me and seven times glad tidings for those who…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah (RA) reports the Prophet's glad tidings: a reward for those who believe in him after seeing him, and seven times that reward for those who believe in him without seeing him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "There will be people coming after me who will wish that they could sacrifice their families and wealth just to…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports the Prophet's saying that people will come after him who would wish to sacrifice their families and wealth just to see him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "I wish that I could see my brothers who will believe in me without seeing me." ^ Another narration states that…
narrations.summary: Anas (RA) reports the Prophet's wish to see his brothers, who will believe in him without seeing him, and that when the Sahabah asked whether they were not his brothers, he said they were his companions and his brothers are those who believe unseen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "The example of my Ummah is like the rain. .It cannot be specified whether it is the first part that is…
narrations.summary: Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) reports the Prophet's comparison of his Ummah to rain, of which it cannot be said whether the first part or the last part is better.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Verily Allaah has angels who travel extensively. They convey to me the greetings that my Ummah give…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ said angels convey the greetings of his Ummah to him, that his life is good for them because they ask him about Deen, and his death is good for them because their deeds are shown to him; he praises Allaah for good deeds and asks forgiveness for their sins.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Burdah (RA) says, "I was sitting with Ibn Ziyaad and Abdullaah bin Yazeed as the heads of the Khawaarij were brought. Whenever a head was passed, I said, 'He…
narrations.summary: Abu Burdah (RA) reports that, while the heads of the Khawaarij were brought before Ibn Ziyaad and Abdullaah bin Yazeed, he declared each one headed for Jahannam, and Abdullaah rebuked him, quoting the Prophet that the punishment of this Ummah is in this world.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Allaah has made killing the punishment of this Ummah in this world."
narrations.summary: A narration with no named narrator quotes the Prophet ﷺ that Allaah has made killing the punishment of this Ummah in this world.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Abu Burdah (RA) says, "I left Ubaydullaah bin ziyaad when I saw him meting extremely harsh punishment (to the Khawaarij). I then sat with…
narrations.summary: Abu Burdah (RA) reports that he left Ubaydullaah bin Ziyaad because of the harsh punishment he was giving the Khawaarij, and that a Sahabi told him the Prophet ﷺ had said this Ummah's punishment would be by the sword.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that a person was mysteriously killed during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ mounted the pulpit and said, "O people!…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas (RA) reports that after a man was killed in mysterious circumstances, the Prophet ﷺ addressed the people from the pulpit: if all the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth conspired to kill one Muslim, Allaah would punish them all.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed (RA) narrates that when a person was killed during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, he mounted the pulpit to address the people. Rasulullaah ﷺ thrice asked,…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed (RA) reports that after an unknown person was killed, the Prophet ﷺ asked three times on the pulpit who had done it, then warned that conspiring to kill a Mu'min brings Jahannam, and that bearing enmity to his household does too.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Usaama bin Zaid SI narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ sent us on a military expedition against a branch of the Juhayna tribe called the Banu Hurqah. We launched a surprise…
narrations.summary: Usaama bin Zaid reports that on a raid he killed a man who had recited the Kalimah, and Rasulullah rebuked him until he wished he had only become Muslim that day.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Usaama (RA) says, "When we returned to Rasulullaah ﷺ and informed him of the event, he said, 'O Usaama! Who will defend you against 'Laa…
narrations.summary: Usaama bin Zaid (RA) gives further reports of the Prophet ﷺ repeatedly asking who would defend him against La ilaaha illallaah, and of Usaama's pledge never to kill anyone who professes it; a third report names Mirdaas bin Nuhayk, killed after he professed the Kalimah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Bakr bin Haaritha (RA) narrates, "I was once part of an expedition that Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched. When we clashed with the Mushrikeen, I attacked a man who sought…
narrations.summary: Bakr bin Haaritha (RA) reports that in battle he killed a man who had accepted Islaam to save himself; the Prophet ﷺ withdrew from him until Surah Nisaa verse 92 was revealed on the matter, after which he was pleased with him again and drew him close.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uqba bin Khaalid Laythi (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched an expedition that engaged the enemy in battle. When one of them started to flee, one of…
narrations.summary: Uqba bin Khaalid Laythi (RA) reports that a Muslim killed a fleeing man who had cried out that he was a Muslim; the Prophet ﷺ condemned it, and when the killer said the man had professed Islaam only to save himself, the Prophet kept turning away from him and rebuked him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched an expedition which included Hadhrat Miqdaad bin Aswad (RA). When the Sahabah (RA) found the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Miqdaad killed a man who had said the Kalimah, and the Prophet rebuked him, after which the verse about verifying before judging a claim to Islaam was revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Hadrad (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ sent us with a party of Muslims to Idham. Amongst us were Abu Qataadah Kaarith bin Rib'ee and Muhallim bin…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Hadrad (RA) reports that Muhallim bin Jathaamah killed Aamir bin Athbat on an old grudge after Aamir greeted them with salaam, and that Surah Nisaa verse 94 was then revealed on the matter.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent Hadhrat Muhallim bin Jathaamah (RA) as part of an expedition. When Aamir bin Athbat met them, he…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports the same incident: Muhallim bin Jathaamah shot and killed Aamir bin Athbat; Uyaynah and Aqra debated before the Prophet ﷺ, who refused to forgive Muhallim, who died within seven days; the earth twice returned his body, so the Sahabah buried him under rocks, and Surah Nisaa verse 94 was then revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qabeesah bin Dhuwayb (RA) narrates that a Sahabi once attacked a group of Mushrikeen who had already been defeated. He then overpowered one of the Mushrikeen who…
narrations.summary: Qabeesah bin Dhuwayb (RA) reports that a Sahabi killed a defeated Mushrik who had recited the Kalimah, was distressed by it, and after he died the earth twice refused his body, so the Prophet ﷺ ordered it thrown into a crevasse in the mountains.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ja'far Muhammad bin Ali reports that when Makkah was conquered, Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) to invite people to Islaam and not to fight…
narrations.summary: Abu Ja'far Muhammad bin Ali reports that after Makkah was conquered Khaalid bin Waleed, sent to invite people to Islaam, killed many of the Banu Jadheema after they had laid down their arms; the Prophet ﷺ raised his hands to disown the act, sent Ali to compensate every loss, and praised what Ali did.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) to the Banu Jadheema tribe. When he invited them towards Islaam,…
