narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that Khaalid bin Waleed had the Banu Jadheema prisoners executed and that the Prophet ﷺ disowned the act; Ibn Is'haaq adds the quarrel between Khaalid and Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf, and the Prophet told Khaalid to leave his Badri companions alone.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sakhar (RA) from the Ahmas tribe narrates that as soon as he heard that Rasulullaah ﷺ was fighting the Thaqeef tribe, he led a party of horsemen to reinforce…
narrations.summary: Sakhar (RA) reports that he held the Thaqeef under siege until they surrendered and sent them to the Prophet ﷺ; the Prophet then had him hand back the captured aunt of Mughiera bin Shu'ba, and return the oasis he had taken from the Banu Sulaym once they embraced Islaam again.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aws bin Aws Thaqafi (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once approached them as they sat in a tent in the Masjid of Madinah. Someone then came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and…
narrations.summary: Aws bin Aws Thaqafi (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ ordered a man executed after a whispered report, then recalled him, asked whether he had testified to Allaah's oneness and the Prophet's risaalah, and ordered his release, since blood and wealth are protected once people testify.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Adi Ansaari (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah fill was once sitting with some people when someone came and requested permission to speak to Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Adi Ansaari (RA) reports that when the Prophet ﷺ was told of a hypocrite who had been killed, he asked whether the man had testified to Allaah's oneness and to his risaalah and prayed salaah, and said that such people were the ones he was forbidden to kill.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, 'Call one of my companions.' I asked, "Abu Bakr?' 'No,' replied Rasulullaah ﷺ, 'Then Utrtar?' I asked. 'No,'…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ asked for one of his companions, and after Abu Bakr, Umar and Ali were named and declined, he called Uthmaan and whispered to him; when Uthmaan was besieged and his companions asked to fight, he refused, saying the Prophet had made him pledge to remain steadfast.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Uthmaan was besieged in his house, he looked out to the people (the rebels) and asked them, "For what reason do…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that Uthmaan, besieged in his house, asked the rebels why they wanted to kill him, quoted the three cases in which a person's blood is lawful, and denied that any of them applied to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah Sengs says, "I was with uthmaan SSI in his house when he was under siege. From the entrance we used, we could hear what the people were talking at the…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah reports that Uthmaan, while under siege, said he had been threatened with death although Rasulullah said blood is lawful to shed only for three reasons, none of which applied to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Layla Kindi reports that he was present when Hadhrat Uthmaan was besieged in his house and peeped through a vent in the wall and said, "O people! Do not kill…
narrations.summary: Abu Layla Kindi reports that Uthmaan, under siege, warned the rebels through a gap in the wall that killing him would divide the Muslims, quoting Shu'ayb's warning from Surah Hood, and that Uthmaan then asked Abdullaah bin Salaam, who advised restraint.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mughiera bin Shu'ba (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Uthmaan was under siege, he approached him and said, "You are the leader of the ' masses and are in the…
narrations.summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba (RA) relates the three options he offered Uthmaan under siege (fight, leave for Makkah, or go to Shaam), and Uthmaan refused all three, quoting the Prophet's warning about a Quraysh man who would spread irreligiousness in Makkah, and saying he would never leave the place of Hijrah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that he entered Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA)'s house when he was under siege and said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! It has now become permissible for…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that he told Uthmaan under siege that fighting the rebels was now lawful, and Uthmaan answered that killing even one person is like killing all of mankind; Abu Hurayrah then left without fighting.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) entered Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA)'s house and said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! in your house you have such a group of people who will attract the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) asks Uthmaan to let them fight the rebels, and Uthmaan refuses, pleading that no man should have his blood spilt for him or spill another's for him; a second narration gives the same request and refusal.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Aamir (RA) narrates that when he was under siege in his house, Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) "The one most useful to me is he who restrains his hand and his…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Aamir (RA) reports that Uthmaan, under siege, said the one most useful to him is the man who restrains his hand and his weapon.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit SSI approached Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and said, "The Ansaar are at your door saying, 'If you permit, we shall be the helpers of the cause of…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit tells Uthmaan that the Ansaar at his door offer to help him, and Uthmaan refuses them permission to fight if they intend to fight.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Seereen says, "With Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) in the house were seven hundred men. Had he left them (to fight), they would have crushed the rebels with the…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan forbade his men, who were ready to fight the rebels besieging him, from fighting, and Sa'eed bin Al Aas then went out to fight and was fatally wounded.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir the son of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi waqqaas (RA) approached his father and asked, "Dear father! People are fighting for the world and you are sitting here?"…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas refused his son Aamir's urging to join the fighting unless he was given a sword that spares believers, and quoted the Prophet on loving the inconspicuous person who has taqwa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat ibn Seereen narrates that someone once asked Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, "Why don't you take up arms because you are one of the consultative assembly and more…
narrations.summary: Asked why he did not take up arms though he was among the consultative assembly and more deserving of the Khilaafah, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas said he would fight only with a sword that could tell a believer from an unbeliever.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem Taymi reports from his father that after eating a full meal, Hadhrat Usaama bin Zaid (RA) said, "I shall never fight anyone who recites 'Laa Ilaaha…
narrations.summary: Usaama bin Zaid and Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas each said they would never fight anyone who recites the kalimah, and when challenged with the verse on fighting, they replied that they had fought until corruption ended.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi reports that two men approached Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar during the period of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) when fighting was raging. They asked,…
narrations.summary: Two men asked Abdullaah bin Umar why he did not join the fighting in Abdullaah bin Zubayr's time, and he answered that Allaah had made his brother's blood haraam to spill and that the fighters were spreading corruption.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that a man approached Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar and said, "o Abu Abdur What makes you perform Hajj one year, Umrah the following year but…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar explained to questioners why he did not fight, and gave his view of Uthmaan (forgiven by Allaah) and Ali (the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law).

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) asked the man, "Do you know what is meant by 'corruption'? Muhammad ﷺ used to fight against the Mushrikeen and…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar told a questioner that the 'corruption' in the verse means fighting the Mushrikeen, unlike the fighting of his own day over land.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Aaliya Baraa reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Safwaan (RA) were one day sitting in the Hateem when Hadhrat Abdullaah…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Safwaan asked Abdullaah bin Umar why he would not pledge allegiance to Abdullaah bin Zubayr, and Ibn Umar replied that he would not pledge while the people's swords dripped with Muslim blood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan says that when the Muslims were plunged in problems, they approached Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar US and said, "You are a leader, the son of a leader and the…
narrations.summary: Hasan says that when the Muslims were in turmoil and people urged Abdullaah bin Umar to take the pledge of allegiance, he refused, and he was never drawn into their aims until he died.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sumayr narrates that some people once said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar, "why don't you set matters right for the people (by taking the reins of…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Sumayr reports that Abdullaah bin Umar, asked to take up the Khilaafah, said he would not accept it at the cost of even one life, since the unity of the Ummah matters more.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qatan reports that a man once came to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar and said, "No person has done worse for the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ than you!" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin…
narrations.summary: Qatan reports that a man told Abdullaah bin Umar that no one had done more harm to the Ummah, and Abdullaah replied that he had not shed blood, divided unity or broken strength, and would not want the Khilaafah while people disagreed about him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that during the first period of strife (4), the people once approached Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) saying, "Are you not going…
narrations.summary: Qaasim bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that when people urged Abdullaah bin Umar to fight during the first period of strife, he refused to fight people who say La ilaaha illallaah, and said he wanted to stay united with the Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi narrates that during the time when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr was struggling for the Khi.laafah and when the Khawaarij and Khashabiyyah sects were on the…
narrations.summary: Asked why he prayed with factions who were killing one another, Abdullaah bin Umar said he answers the call to salaah and to success, but refuses a call to kill his Muslim brother.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Ghareef says, "Twelve thousand of us were part of the frontline forces of Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA). Abu Umrata was our commander 'and in our eagerness to…
narrations.summary: Abul Ghareef recounts that Hasan bin Ali's frontline forces were furious at his truce with Mu'aawiya, and that Hasan told a man who called him a humiliator of the Mu'mineen that he had only disliked killing them for land.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that when Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) and Hadhrat Mu'aawiya entered into a truce, Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) said to Hadhrat Hasan (RA), "Stand up and…
narrations.summary: Hasan bin Ali addressed the people after the truce with Mu'aawiya, saying he had given up his claim to rule to save the Ummah's lives, and Amr bin Al Aas remarked to Mu'aawiya that this was exactly what he wanted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jubayr bin Nufayr (RA) narrates that he once said to Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali, "The people say that you desire the Khilaafah." Hadhrat Hasan replied, "When I had all…
narrations.summary: Jubayr bin Nufayr asked Hasan bin Ali about the claim that he wanted the Khilaafah, and Hasan answered that he gave up the post for Allaah's pleasure to save the Ummah's blood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir Sha'bi reports that when Marwaan fought Dahhaak. bin Qais, he sent a message to Hadhrat Ayman bin Khuraym Asadi (RA), saying, "We would like you to fight by…
narrations.summary: When Marwaan asked Ayman bin Khuraym Asadi to fight beside him against Dahhaak bin Qais, Ayman refused unless given a guarantee of freedom from Jahannam, and recited verses saying he would gain nothing from fighting another Muslim for no reason.

narrations.excerpt: A messenger from Hadhrat Ali (RA) once came to Hadhrat Hakam bin Amr with a message saying, "Verily you are most worthy of assisting me in this matter of Khilaafah."…
narrations.summary: A messenger from Ali asked Hakam bin Amr to help him in the matter of the Khilaafah, and Hakam replied that a friend had advised that in such times it is best to take up a wooden sword, which he had done.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ash'ath San'aani narrates, "Yazeed bin Mu'aawiya once sent me to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Awfa (RA), With him were many Sahabah (RA) when I asked, 'What…
narrations.summary: Abu Ash'ath San'aani reports that Yazeed bin Mu'aawiya sent him to Abdullaah bin Abi Awfa, who said the Prophet told him to break his sword and submit to being killed rather than fight Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslamah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "When you see people fighting for worldly wealth, take your sword to the largest boulder in Harrah and…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Maslamah recounts the Prophet's command to break his sword and stay at home rather than fight when Muslims fight Muslims, and says he did so after Uthmaan was martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rib'ee reports that at the funeral of Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA), he overheard someone saying, "The person on this bier once said, 'I have no doubts about what I…
narrations.summary: At Hudhayfah's funeral a man recalled his words that if Muslims fought one another he would go home and let any attacker take his sins along with his own.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Waa'il bin Hujar (RA) says, "When we heard about the appearance of Rasulullaah ﷺ , I left with a delegation form my tribe, when we reached Madinah, I met the…
narrations.summary: Waa'il bin Hujar recounts being welcomed by the Prophet, and later refusing to fight in the strife after Mu'aawiya summoned him, citing the Prophet's warning about tribulations and declining governorship.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Minhaal reports, "When Ibn Ziyaad was expelled (from Basrah when Yazeed passed away), Marwaan seized power in Shaam, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr seized…
narrations.summary: Abul Minhaal recounts how his father asked Abu Barzah Aslami about the conflict between Marwaan, Ibn Zubayr and the Qurraa in Basrah, and Abu Barzah condemned all sides as fighting for worldly gain and advised withdrawal.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thamar bin Attiyya reports that Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) once said to someone, "Will it please you to kill someone who is the worst of sinners?" When the man…
narrations.summary: Thamar bin Attiyya reports that Hudhayfah told a man that if he killed the worst of sinners he would be an even worse sinner himself.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked him, "What do you do when you lay siege to any city?" Hadhrat Anas (RA) replied, "We first make a strong…
narrations.summary: Umar asked Anas how his men besieged cities, and when Anas said a shield-bearer would be killed by thrown rocks, Umar said he would never be pleased to take a city of four thousand warriors at the cost of one Muslim's life.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "More than having control over the entire Arabian peninsula, I prefer rescuing a single Muslim from the clutches of the Kuffaar."
narrations.summary: Umar said that rescuing a single Muslim from the unbelievers is more precious to him than control of the whole Arabian peninsula.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Hasan (RA) was a Sahabi who participated in the Pledge of Aqabah as well as in the Battle of Badr. He says, "We were sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ when a man…
narrations.summary: Abul Hasan, who fought at Badr, recounts that the Prophet asked how a Companion would answer for frightening a believer after another Companion hid the first one's shoes as a joke.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir bin Rabee'ah (RA) reports that a Sahabi once hid away the shoes of another Sahabi in jest. When the matter was reported to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he said, "Never…
narrations.summary: Aamir bin Rabee'ah reports that when a Companion hid another's shoes in jest, the Prophet said that frightening a Muslim is a great injustice.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Basheer (RA) narrates that they were once on a journey with Rasulullaah ﷺ when one of them fell asleep on his animal. When another Sahabi removed an…
narrations.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer and Layla each report that the Prophet rebuked Companions who startled a sleeping traveller on a journey, saying it is not permissible to frighten a Muslim.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Surad (RA) narrates that a Bedouin was once performing salaah with Rasulullaah ﷺ when someone took away the rope he had with him. After Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Sulaymaan bin Surad reports that the Prophet rebuked Companions who took away a Bedouin's rope during salaah, saying whoever believes in Allaah should never frighten a Muslim.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Usaama bin Zaid (RA) once tripped and fell over a doorstep, causing him to sustain a gash on his head. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that when Usaama bin Zaid fell and cut his head, the Prophet licked the blood from the wound himself, and said that had Usaama been a girl he would have adorned and married her off.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa bin Yasaar reports that as soon as he arrived in Madinah, Hadhrat Usaama bin Zaid was afflicted with smallpox. He was still a little boy and mucus often ran…
narrations.summary: Ataa bin Yasaar reports that the Prophet washed and kissed the smallpox-stricken Usaama bin Zaid, after which Aa'isha vowed never to distance him, while Urwa says the people of Yemen reverted to kufr because they looked down on Usaama.

narrations.excerpt: Another similar narration quotes Hadhrat Urwa (RA) as saying, "After the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ, the people of Yemen reverted to kufr because of (their looking down at)…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that after the Prophet's passing the people of Yemen reverted to kufr because they looked down on Usaama bin Zaid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that when a group of people once went to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari, he gave something to the Arabs amongst them while giving nothing to (non-Arab)…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Umar rebuked Abu Moosa Ash'ari for giving gifts to the Arab Muslims but none to the non-Arab slaves, saying it is enough evil for a man to look down on his Muslim brother.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'idh bin Umar narrates that Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) (who was not yet a Muslim) once approached a gathering that included Hadhrat Salmaan Hadhrat Suhayb SSi and…
narrations.summary: Aa'idh bin Umar reports that Salmaan, Suhayb and Bilaal made a remark about Abu Sufyaan that angered Abu Bakr, and the Prophet warned that angering them would anger Allaah, so Abu Bakr went back to ask whether he had angered them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was once passing by with a prisoner for whom he had sought amnesty from Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) who was…
narrations.summary: Suhayb reports that after he said a Mushrik prisoner's neck would make a perfect place for a sword, Abu Bakr was angry, and the Prophet told Abu Bakr that hurting Suhayb would have hurt Allaah and His Rasool.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates that during the time of Rasulullaah iiil there was a man called Abdullaah. He was nicknamed 'Himaar' and used to make Rasulullaah ﷺ laugh.…
narrations.summary: Umar reports that the Prophet forbade cursing a man called Abdullaah, nicknamed Himaar, who was lashed repeatedly for drinking wine, because he loves Allaah and His Rasool.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that a man nicknamed 'Himaar' once gave Rasulullaah a container of butter and another of honey as a gift. When the owner of the butter and honey…
narrations.summary: Another report says that Himaar gave the Prophet butter and honey, and when the seller came to collect unpaid, the Prophet smiled and ordered him paid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam narrates that Hadhrat Ibn Nu'maan (RA) was once brought to Rasulullaah ﷺ (for drinking wine), for which he was lashed. He was then brought four or…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports that when someone cursed Ibn Nu'maan for repeated drinking and lashing, the Prophet told them not to curse him, because he loves Allaah and His Rasool.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that when someone who had drunk wine was brought to Rasulullaah ﷺ, the Sahabah (RA) hit him according to the instructions of Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet stopped Companions from cursing a drinker they had lashed, and the same narration records Umar's vow to cut out his son Abdullaah's tongue for swearing Miqdaad.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that a man came and sat in front of Rasulullaah He said, "I have many slaves who lie to me, cheat me and disobey me. I (retaliate when I)…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that a man asked the Prophet how to deal with slaves who lie, cheat and disobey him, and the Prophet explained that they will be recompensed on the Day of Qiyaamah; the man then asked to be separated from them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that someone started swearing Hadhrat Abu Bakr while Rasulullaah ﷺ was also sitting there. Rasulullaah ﷺ was impressed and kept smiling…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when someone abused Abu Bakr and he replied to some of it, the Prophet left, and explained that Shaytaan had come in; the Prophet also affirmed that forgiving injustice brings strength. Separately, Umar vowed to cut off his son Abdullaah's tongue for swearing Miqdaad, and Bahiy reports the same dispute.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that someone once spoke ill of another in the presence of Rasulullaah ﷺ. "Stand up- (and leave)," said Rasulullaah ﷺ "for your shahaadah is…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that when someone spoke ill of another in the Prophet's presence, the Prophet told him to stand up and leave, because his testimony of faith was worthless and he had mocked the Qur'aan by doing what it forbids.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Taariq bin Shihaab reports that there was once a dispute between Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) and Hadhrat Sa'd (RA). When someone started speaking ill of Hadhrat Khaalid…
narrations.summary: Taariq bin Shihaab reports that when someone spoke ill of Khaalid bin Waleed to Sa'd, Sa'd told him to stop, saying their dispute should not spill into their Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that a Sahabi from the Banu Aslam tribe once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and four times (on different occasions) confessed that he had…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet likened backbiting a Muslim who had been stoned for adultery to eating a dead animal, and Ibnul Murtkadir reports that the Prophet told someone who said a stoned woman's deeds were destroyed that the punishment had cleansed her, while he would be called to account for his words.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that she once said to Rasulullaah ﷺ , "It will suffice you to know that Safiyya is like that!" Narrators of the report say that Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet rebuked her for remarking that Safiyya was short, saying such words would spoil the ocean, and also that he disliked her imitating someone even for great wealth.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Abu Dawood states that the camel of Hadhrat Safryya (RA) once fell ill. Because Hadhrat Zaynab (RA) had extra riding camels, Rasulullaah asked her to give…
narrations.summary: Safiyya's camel fell ill and the Prophet asked Zaynab to give her one, but Zaynab refused with an insult, so the Prophet stayed away from her for months.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration' states that Rasulullaah iiif kept away from her for the two months of Dhul Hijjah and Muharram or perhaps even three months. Hadhrat Zaynab says that…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that Rasulullah told her to spit out a piece of meat after she remarked on a woman's long hem, and Zaid bin Aslam reports that in his final illness Rasulullah rebuked his wives for winking at Safiyya's sincere wish to share his suffering.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that when a particular Sahabi once stood up (and left), some of the Sahabah (RA) remarked, "What a feeble person he is, O Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when some Sahabah called a companion who left a gathering feeble, the Prophet said they had backbitten him and eaten the flesh of their brother.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin jabal (RA) report a narration similar to the above with the addition that the Sahabah (RA) (who passed the remark) enquired, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ We have…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal reports the same incident, with the Prophet explaining that mentioning a fault a person really has is backbiting, while mentioning one he does not have is slander.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) reports that some of the Sahabah (RA) once passed a remark about a particular Sahabi saying, "He will never eat until he is fed and will…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that the Sahabah described a companion as lazy, and the Prophet said that mentioning a real fault in a brother is backbiting.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that they were once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when a Sahabi got up to leave. After he had left, someone then spoke ill of him.…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that after a companion left a gathering, someone spoke ill of him, and the Prophet told that man to repent for eating his brother's flesh.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed, "Pick your teeth". "What should I pick them for, O Rasulullaah ﷺ the person queried, "I have not eaten any meat?"
narrations.summary: In a terse report the Prophet tells a man to pick his teeth, and the man asks why, since he has eaten no meat.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once instructed them to fast, making it clear that none was to end the fast until he permitted them. The Sahabah (RA) then…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet told two young women who had fasted all day, while backbiting, to vomit, and said that their backbiting had broken their fast and would have burned them in Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when the man told one of the ladies to vomit, she vomited blood, puss and meat which half filled a cup. When he then told the other lady to…
narrations.summary: In another report the two women vomit blood and flesh, and the Prophet says they broke their lawful fast with the forbidden act of backbiting.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) reports that it was customary amongst the Arabs to serve each other during journeys. There was a man who used to serve Hadhrat Abu Bakr and…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that when Abu Bakr and Umar mocked their sleeping servant, the Prophet told them they had eaten his flesh and advised them to ask the servant to forgive them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf US reports that one night he stood guard over Madinah with Hadhrat Umar (RA). As they were walking along, they noticed a lantern in a house.…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf reports that on a night patrol he and Umar came to a house where people were drinking wine, and Umar, recalling the Quranic ban on spying, went away and turned a blind eye.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) did not see one of his companions for some time, he told Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) to accompany him to the…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that Umar and Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf spied on a companion of Umar who was drinking in his house, and Abdur Rahmaan advised that the repentance for spying is to keep what was learned private and think well of him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Taa'oos reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) left home one night to keep guard over some travellers who had set up camp on the outskirts of Madinah. It was late at…
narrations.summary: Taa'oos reports that Umar, on night patrol, called out to a house where people were drinking, and when one of them reminded him that spying was forbidden, Umar left them alone.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thowr Kindi narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was patrolling Madinah one night when he heard a man singing in his house. Hadhrat Umar (RA) scaled the wall of the…
narrations.summary: Thowr Kindi reports that Umar scaled a wall to confront a man singing in his house, and when the man rebuked him with the Qur'aanic prohibitions on spying and on entering without permission, Umar pardoned him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Suddi reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) was with Hadhrat umar (RA) when he saw the light of a fire during the dead of night. Following the light,…
narrations.summary: Suddi reports that after Umar caught an old man drinking and was rebuked for spying, Umar swore privately that he had told no one, and the old man said he had never repeated what he had done.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Qilaabah narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was once informed that Hadhrat Abu Mihjin Thaqafi (RA) and some of his friends were drinking wine at his house.…
narrations.summary: Abu Qilaabah reports that Umar found Abu Mihjin Thaqafi drinking at his house and left him alone when Abu Mihjin reminded him that spying was forbidden, with Zaid bin Thaabit and Abdur Rahmaan bin Arqam agreeing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that a man once came to Hadhrat Umar ii saying, "I had a daughter whom I had buried alive during the Period of ignorance. However, we then removed…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that a man asked Umar how to treat his daughter, who had been buried alive in ignorance, then rescued, converted and repented, and Umar told him to keep her past hidden and marry her as he would any chaste Muslim woman.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that a woman was once punished for a crime of immorality. However, after her tribe had arrived as immigrants in Madinah, she repented very…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that when a woman's uncle asked Umar whether he must disclose her repented past before her marriage, Umar told him to marry her off as he would any righteous girl.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi also reports that a woman once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! I have found a child (abandoned) together with an Egyptian cloth bag…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that when Umar tried to identify a foundling's mother, one of the women rebuked him for trying to expose a woman Allaah had concealed, and Umar admitted he was wrong and told the nurse not to question the visitors.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalih bin Karz narrates, "I once brought before Hakam bin Ayyoob a slave girl of mine who had fornicated. I was sitting there when Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik…
narrations.summary: Saalih bin Karz reports that Anas bin Maalik persuaded him to take back his slave girl, who had committed fornication, instead of having her punished, urging him to fear Allaah and conceal her sin.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dukhayn Abul Haytham was a scribe for Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir He says, "I once said to Hadhrat Uqba (RA), 'We have a few neighbours who drink wine. I am going to…
narrations.summary: Dukhayn, scribe to Uqba bin Aamir, reports Uqba's advice against reporting neighbours who drank wine; the text then runs into Haatib bin Abi Balta'ah's secret letter to Quraysh, which the Prophet forgave because Haatib had fought at Badr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Bilaal bin Sa'd Ash'ari narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) once wrote to Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) to submit to him the names of all the criminals of Damascus.…
narrations.summary: Bilaal bin Sa'd Ash'ari reports that Mu'aawiya asked Abu Dardaa for a list of the criminals of Damascus, and Abu Dardaa refused, telling his son to begin with his own name.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was once in a room with Hadhrat Jareer bin Abdullaah (RA) (and others) when he smelt an odour (from someone who had passed…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that Umar, smelling a fart in a room, ordered the person responsible to make wudhu, and Jareer bin Abdullaah suggested everyone should do so to spare him embarrassment, which Umar praised.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah gjii dispatched him, Hadhrat Zubayr and Hadhrat Miqdaad (RA) with instruction saying, "Ride until you reach Rawda There you…
narrations.summary: Ali reports that the Prophet sent him, Zubayr and Miqdaad to a woman carrying a letter from Haatib bin Abi Balta'ah to the Mushrikeen of Makkah, and Haatib, a Badri, explained he had acted to protect his family, so the Prophet forgave him despite Umar's demand to kill him as a hypocrite.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Matar reports that he once saw a person being brought to Hadhrat Ali. The people accused him of stealing a camel. Hadhrat Ali (RA) said to him, "I do not…
narrations.summary: Abu Matar reports that Ali released a man who had confessed to theft once he retracted, and cites the Prophet's teaching that people should pardon one another's wrongs rather than demand punishment.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Maajid Hanafi reports that a man once brought his drunk nephew to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) saying, "1 found him drunk." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin…
narrations.summary: Abu Maajid Hanafi reports that Ibn Mas'ood had a drunkard lightly flogged, and then quotes the Prophet's grief over a thief's hand being cut and his call to forgive rather than demand punishment.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that he was once with (his father) Hadhrat Umar (RA) for Hajj or Umrah when they spotted a rider arrive. "I think that he is…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that a man whom Abu Moosa Ash'ari had flogged and paraded for drinking came to Umar in despair, and Umar warned Abu Moosa that he would be disgraced the same way if he repeated it, and ordered the man to be accepted if he repents.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Own and others reports that Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) once claimed that Hadhrat Maalik bin Nuwayrah (RA) had left the fold of Islaam because of a…
narrations.summary: Abu Own reports that Khaalid bin Waleed had Maalik bin Nuwayrah executed for apostasy despite testimony in his favour and then married his widow, and that Abu Bakr refused Umar's demands to punish Khaalid, saying he had erred in judgement.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Qilaaba narrates that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once passed by a person whom people were insulting for committing a sin. Hadhrat Abu Dardaa said to them, "If…
narrations.summary: Abu Qilaabah reports Abu Dardaa's advice to hate a sinner's sin rather than the sinner, and Ibn Mas'ood's instruction not to help Shaytaan by cursing a brother who sins.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that they were once sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ when he said, "A man from amongst the people of Jannah shall now appear before you." A man from…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Abdullaah bin Amr followed a man the Prophet had named as one of the people of Jannah, and stayed with him three days, learning that the man's secret was harbouring no envy or ill-feeling towards any Muslim.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration names the Sahabi as Hadhrat Sa'd SI The end of this narration states that Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) said, "There is nothing besides what you have observed, dear…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr asks Sa'd how he has earned his reward, and Sa'd replies that he never sleeps with ill-feeling towards any Muslim, which Abdullaah says is beyond what he can manage.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration names the Sahabi as Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA). The end part of that narration states that Hadhrat Sa'd said, "There is nothing besides what you…
narrations.summary: A variant names the companion as Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, who says he harbours no ill-feeling towards any Muslim and never speaks ill of them, and Abdullaah bin Amr says he cannot match this.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam (RA) reports that when people went to visit Hadhrat Abu Dujaanah during his illness, his face was always shining and radiant. When he was asked the…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports that Abu Dujaanah's face shone during his illness, which he credited to speaking only when necessary and keeping a clear heart towards all Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Buraydah Aslami (RA) narrates that when someone once insulted Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA), he responded by saying, "You are insulting me when I have three…
narrations.summary: Buraydah Aslami reports that when someone insulted Abdullaah bin Abbaas, he listed three things that made him happy: wishing all people shared his knowledge of the Qur'aan, joy at a just Muslim ruler, and joy at rain falling on Muslim cities.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that when a man asked permission' to see Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "He is the worst of his tribe." However, when he entered,…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet received a man he had called the worst of his tribe warmly, and that he explained the worst people are those whose abuse others must guard against.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Safwaan bin Assaal (RA) narrates that they were once on a journey with Rasulullaah ﷺ when a man arrived. Seeing him arrive, Rasulullaah ﷺ commented, "He is the…
narrations.summary: Safwaan bin Assaal reports that the Prophet welcomed a man he had called the worst of his tribe, saying he was a hypocrite and that he treated him kindly so that the man would not spoil the Prophet's name among others.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) reports that they were once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when a man from the Quraysh arrived. Rasulullaah ﷺ allowed him to sit close by and treated him like a…
narrations.summary: Buraydah reports that the Prophet welcomed a wealthy Quraysh man as a close friend, then said that Allaah will not set up a scale of deeds for him on the Day of Qiyaamah because he has no good deeds.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once stated, "While we may be smiling in the faces of certain people, our hearts are actually cursing them."
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says that they may smile in the faces of some people while their hearts curse them.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "We also laugh with them."
narrations.summary: A variant adds Abu Dardaa's words that they also laugh with such people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) narrates that they were once sitting with Rasulullaah when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) came in (in a hurry) holding the edge of his clothing (and…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa reports that after Abu Bakr and Umar quarrelled, the Prophet asked the Companions to leave Abu Bakr alone, and Abdullaah bin Umar gives a parallel report that the Prophet urged Umar to forgive him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once used insulting words for Hadhrat Umar (RA) but then said, "Please forgive me, dear brother."…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Abu Bakr asked Umar's forgiveness after a heated exchange, Umar refused, and Rasulullah praised Abu Bakr and ordered every door to the Masjid sealed except his.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Ummu Habeebah the wife of Rasulullaah ﷺ called for me as she lay on her deathbed. She said, 'There had been incidents between us as occurs…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that Ummu Habeebah, on her deathbed, asked her forgiveness for the rivalries between co-wives, and then did the same with Ummu Salamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that when Hadhrat Faatima (RA) fell ill (just before her demise), Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) went to request permission to address her. (Her husband)…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that Abu Bakr asked Faatima's permission to visit her in her last illness, and calmed her by affirming his devotion to Allaah, His Rasool and her household until she was pleased.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) asks Forgiveness from a Man whom he Disliked Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once mentioned that he disliked a particular person. People…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that when Umar disliked Abdullaah bin Amr, Abdullaah explained that his unbroken fasts and night worship had been corrected by the Prophet, who told him to alternate fasting with sleep and to obey his father.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) Seeks Pardon from Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) Hadhrat Rajaa bin Rabee'ah narrates that he was once sitting in the Masjid of Rasulullaah ﷺ in…
narrations.summary: Rajaa bin Rabee'ah reports that Abdullaah bin Amr refused to greet Hasan bin Ali until after the Battle of Siffeen, when he sought his pardon, explaining he had fought only by following his father and had fasted and prayed through the nights, which the Prophet had told him to moderate.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) Seeks Pardon from Hadhrat Husayn bin (RA) Hadhrat Rajaa bin Rabee'ah narrates that he was once sitting in the Masjid of Rasulullaah ﷺ when…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) asks Husayn bin Ali (RA) for forgiveness after a long estrangement, and Husayn accepts once Abu Sa'eed (RA) has arranged the meeting.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "I cannot say which of the two favours of Allaah to me are greater. Whether it is a man coming to me with the sincere belief that I am able to…
narrations.summary: Ali (RA) says that fulfilling a Muslim's need is more beloved to him than a earth full of gold and silver.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat ibn Yazeed narrates that a lady called Khowlah met Hadhrat Umar (RA) as she was travelling with some people. When she bade Hadhrat Umar (RA) to stop, he obliged,…
narrations.summary: Umar (RA) stands still and listens to an old woman, Khowlah, until she has stated her need, and explains that Allaah heard her complaint from above the seven heavens.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thumaamah ibn Hazan (RA) reports that a lady once met Hadhrat Umar as he was riding his donkey. "Stop, O Umar!" she demanded. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) stopped, she…
narrations.summary: Thumaamah ibn Hazan reports that Umar stopped on his donkey to listen to a woman who spoke to him harshly, justifying this by the Quranic verse that Allaah heard a woman who complained to Him about her husband.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) was once observing I'tikaaf in the Masjid of Rasulullaah ﷺ when a man came to him. After the man had greeted with Salaam and sat down,…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas, while in I'tikaaf in the Prophet's Masjid, leaves it to help a man with a debt, recalling the Prophet's saying that walking to meet a Muslim's need is better than ten years of I'tikaaf.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Qais (RA) narrated that Rasulullaah ﷺ visited the Ansaar very often, both on an individual basis and on a collective basis. When he visited someone…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Qais reports that the Prophet often visited the Ansaar, both at home and in the Masjid; Anas reports that he once prayed on a mat at an Ansaari house and made du'aa for the household.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to forge a bond of brotherhood between every two Sahabah (RA). (The bond became so strong that) The night would seem…
narrations.summary: Anas (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ forged a bond of brotherhood between every two Sahabah, so that each missed his brother terribly until they met.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Own narrates that when the companions of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood came to see him, he said, "Do you people sit in each other's company?" "That we do not…
narrations.summary: Companions of Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) tell him they still visit each other, and he says they will remain in good stead as long as they keep doing so.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Dardaa (RA) says that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) once came walking all the way from Madaa'in to visit them (her husband Hadhrat Abu Dardaa in Shaam. He was then…
narrations.summary: Ummu Dardaa (RA) reports that Salmaan (RA) walked all the way from Madaa'in to visit her husband Abu Dardaa in Shaam, and that Abu Dardaa wore only a short shawl.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates, "When I once visited Rasulullaah he threw to me a pillow stuffed with bark. However, I did not sit on it (out of respect) and it…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ threw him a pillow stuffed with bark during a visit, which he did not sit on out of respect.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Sa'd (RA) who was the daughter of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Rabee reports that she once went to see Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) (for some need because he was Khalifah). He…
narrations.summary: Ummu Sa'd (RA), daughter of Sa'd bin Rabee (RA), is given a sheet to sit on by Abu Bakr (RA), who tells Umar (RA) that her father has already prepared his place in Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) reports that Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) once came of visit Hadhrat Umar (RA) who was reclining on a cushion. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) threw…
narrations.summary: Anas (RA) reports that Salmaan (RA) visited Umar (RA), who threw him a cushion, and Salmaan quoted the Prophet's words that a host who gives his guest a cushion has his sins forgiven.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) once came of visit Hadhrat Umar (RA) who was reclining on a cushion. Hadhrat umar threw the cushion to Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Anas (RA) reports that Umar (RA) threw a cushion to Salmaan (RA) and recited the hadith that a host who gives a cushion to his guest has his sins forgiven.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) also reports that when Hadhrat Umar SI5.8SS8) went to visit Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA). Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) threw a cushion to Hadhrat Umar (RA), who…
narrations.summary: Anas (RA) reports that Salmaan (RA) threw a cushion to Umar (RA), who asked what it meant, and Salmaan quoted the Prophet's hadith on the cushion of hospitality and honour.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Nasheet reports that when he once visited Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Haarith bin Jaz Zubaydi, the latter threw to him a cushion that he had been sitting…
narrations.summary: Ibraheem bin Nasheet reports that Abdullaah bin Haarith bin Jaz Zubaydi threw him the cushion he had been sitting on, and said that whoever is not hospitable to a visitor has no ties with Ahmad or Ibraheem.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sahl bin Sa'd (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Usayd Saa'idi (RA) invited Rasulullaah ﷺ for his wedding (Waleema). His wife who was the new bride was actually…
narrations.summary: Sahal bin Sa'd (RA) reports that Abu Usayd Saa'idi (RA) invited the Prophet ﷺ to his wedding feast, where his new bride served him dates soaked overnight in a vessel.

narrations.excerpt: When two persons went to visit Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Haarith bin Jaz Zubaydi he removed from beneath him a cushion that he had been sitting on and threw it to them. They…
narrations.summary: Two visitors decline a cushion from Abdullaah bin Haarith (RA), who warns that whoever is not hospitable to a visitor has no ties with the Prophet or Ibraheem.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jareer bin Abdullaah Bajali SIS!is reports that he once went to see Rasulullaah ﷺ in his room at a time when there was a large crowd present. As Hadhrat Jareer…
narrations.summary: The Prophet ﷺ throws his shawl to Jareer bin Abdullaah (RA) so he can sit, and tells the people to honour a prominent person of a tribe who comes to them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Jareer bin Abdullaah once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ's room, it was full of people and he could find nowhere to sit.…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when the room was full, Rasulullah threw his garment to Jareer bin Abdullaah to sit on, and told his Companions to honour a prominent person who comes to them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Uyaynah bin Hisn once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ whilst Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) were sitting there…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that when Uyaynah bin Hisn came to the Prophet, who was sitting with Abu Bakr and Umar on the bare ground, the Prophet had a duvet placed for him and said a prominent person of a tribe should be honoured.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Adi bin Haatim (RA) narrates that when he came to Rasulullaah ﷺ , Rasulullaah ﷺ gave him a cushion (to sit on) but he preferred to rather sit on the bare ground.…
narrations.summary: Adi bin Haatim reports that the Prophet gave him a cushion, which he declined in favour of sitting on the ground, and that after praising the Prophet's humility he accepted Islaam; the Prophet then said a prominent person of a tribe should be honoured.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Raashid bin Abdur Rahmaan (RA) says, "I went to Rasulullaah iS with a hundred men from my tribe. When we drew close to Rasulullaah we stopped and the others…
narrations.summary: Abu Raashid reports that he went to Rasulullah with a hundred men of his tribe, was taught the Muslim greeting, accepted Islaam, and was honoured with a seat beside Rasulullah and gifts of the Prophet's shawl, shoes and staff.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once asked him what he thought of Hadhrat Ju'ayl (RA). "I see him as just another poor man like many others," Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr (RA) judges Ju'ayl (RA) to be a poor man, but the Prophet ﷺ says Ju'ayl is better than a world full of leaders like him, and that he gives to Uyaynah and Aqra only to win their hearts to Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that someone said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, "O Rasulullaah You have given Uyaynah bin Hisn and a hundred camels each while you have left Ju'ayl out.…
narrations.summary: Someone asks why Rasulullah gave Uyaynah and Aqra a hundred camels each and not Ju'ayl, and Rasulullah replies that Ju'ayl is better but that he gives to win the hearts of the others, entrusting Ju'ayl to his Imaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed bin Hayyaan says, "Husayn bin Saburah, Amr bin Muslim and I once went to Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA). When we sat down with him, Husayn asked, 'You have…
narrations.summary: Husayn bin Saburah and Amr bin Muslim ask Zaid bin Arqam (RA) about the Prophet's household, and Ibn Abbaas (RA) reports that Abu Bakr (RA) gave his seat to Abbaas (RA), after which the Prophet ﷺ foretold the future of Abbaas's descendants.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Consider Muhammad ﷺ when dealing with the members of his household."
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr tells the Muslims to consider Muhammad ﷺ in how they treat the members of his household.

narrations.excerpt: Ummul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once sitting with his companions with Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar on his sides. When…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha relates that the Prophet lowered his voice when his uncle Abbaas came in, and Ibn Abbaas relates that Abu Bakr gave up his seat for Abbaas and the Prophet foretold Abbaas's descendants would be kings.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ja'far bin Muhammad narrates from his great grandfather that Hadhrat Abu Bakr always sat on the right of Rasulullaah ﷺ while Hadhrat Umar sat on his left. Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Ja'far bin Muhammad reports the seating order around the Prophet ﷺ, and that Abu Bakr (RA) always gave his place to Abbaas (RA) when he came.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muttalib bin Rabee'ah reports that Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ in a rage. "What is the matter?" Rasulullaah ﷺ enquired. "O Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abbaas (RA) comes to the Prophet ﷺ in anger at how the Quraysh treat the Banu Haashim, and the Prophet says that faith is incomplete without loving the Banu Haashim for the sake of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib (RA) reports that he once said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ While the Quraysh meet each other with open and smiling faces, whereas…
narrations.summary: Abbaas (RA) reports that he complained to the Prophet ﷺ that the Quraysh greet the Banu Haashim with strange faces, and the Prophet became very angry.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ismah narrates that when Hadhrat Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib (RA) entered the Masjid one day, he noticed resentment on the faces of some people. He then went to…
narrations.summary: Ismah narrates that Abbaas (RA) noticed resentment on people's faces in the Masjid, asked the Prophet ﷺ about it, and the Prophet told the people that they cannot be believers until they love Abbaas.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent Hadhrat Umar (RA) to collect zakaah. The first person Hadhrat Umar (RA) met was Hadhrat Abbaas…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ sent Umar (RA) to collect zakaah, that Umar and Abbaas (RA) quarrelled over it, and that the Prophet approved Umar's conduct after Ali (RA) brought the matter to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when someone spoke about the father of Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) and insulted him, Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) slapped the man. Some…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Abbaas (RA) slapped a man who insulted his father, and the Prophet ﷺ told the people that Abbaas is from him and that the dead should not be insulted to hurt the living.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that the people added, "0 Rasulullaah ﷺ We seek Allaah's protection from your anger! Do seek forgiveness from Allaah on our behalf." Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: In another report, the people ask the Prophet ﷺ to seek Allaah's forgiveness on their behalf after the incident with Abbaas, and he agrees.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat ibn Shihaab reports that during their terms as Khalifah, whenever Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) or Hadhrat Umar (RA) met Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) while they were riding, they…
narrations.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports that Abu Bakr (RA) and Umar (RA), during their caliphates, dismounted and led Abbaas's animal on foot whenever they met him riding.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) Lashes a man who Ridiculed Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad reports that amongst the rulings that Hadhrat Uthmaan initiated and which…
narrations.summary: Qaasim bin Muhammad reports that Uthmaan (RA) had a man lashed for ridiculing Abbaas (RA), reasoning that whoever allows such behaviour opposes the Prophet, and the Sahabah approved the ruling.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once sitting in the Masjid with the Sahabah is around him. Hadhrat Ali (RA) then arrived, greeted with Salaam and then…
narrations.summary: Anas (RA) reports that Abu Bakr (RA) gave his place beside the Prophet ﷺ to Ali (RA), and the Prophet said that only people of virtue recognise virtue in others.

narrations.excerpt: as "O Moulana" Hadhrat Rabaah bin Haarith reports that a group of the Ansaar once came to Hadhrat Ali (RA) in Rahbah (a place in Kufa) and greeted him with the words, "As…
narrations.summary: Rabaah bin Haarith reports that a group of Ansaar greeted Ali (RA) as their Moula, citing the Prophet's words at the pond of Khum, and that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA) was among them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched us on an expedition to which he appointed Hadhrat Ali (RA) as commander. After we returned, Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Buraydah (RA) reports that after an expedition under Ali (RA) he complained about Ali, and the Prophet ﷺ's face turned red with anger as he said: for whoever I am a friend to, Ali is also their friend.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Shaas Aslami (RA) who was with Rasulullaah ﷺ at Hudaybiyyah says, "I was with the group of horsemen under the command of Hadhrat Ali (RA) whom Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Shaas Aslami (RA) reports that he harboured anger against Ali (RA) for his harshness, and the Prophet ﷺ told him that whoever hurts Ali has hurt him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) says, "I was sitting in the Masjid with two other persons when we insulted Ali. When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived, we could see the anger on…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) reports that he and two others insulted Ali (RA) in the Masjid, and when the Prophet ﷺ came in angry, he said that whoever hurts Ali has hurt him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that someone once insulted Hadhrat Ali (RA) in the presence of Hadhrat Umar (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Do you know that occupant of this…
narrations.summary: Umar (RA) rebukes a man who insulted Ali (RA) in his presence, reminding him that the Prophet ﷺ is in the grave and that hurting Ali hurts him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Khaalid bin Urfuta narrates that he once went to Hadhrat Sa'd bin Maalik and asked, "The news has reached me that in Kufa you people are being forced…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr bin Khaalid bin Urfuta asks Sa'd bin Maalik whether he has reviled Ali, and Sa'd says he would never revile him even if a saw were placed on his head.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Abu Sufyaan once instructed him saying, "What prevents you from reviling Abu Turaab (Hadhrat Ali US…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Abi Sufyaan asks Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) why he does not revile Ali, and Sa'd lists the virtues the Prophet ﷺ gave Ali: the rank like Haaroon and Moosa, the flag at Khaybar, and being called with his family.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Nujayh narrates that when Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) performed Hajj, he took hold of the hand of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) and said, "O Abu Is'haaq! We…
narrations.summary: Abu Nujayh reports that Mu'aawiya bin Abi Sufyaan, during Hajj, spoke ill of Ali (RA) to Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA), who rebuked him and walked out, quoting the Prophet's words about Ali.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Abdullaah Jadali reports, "I once went to Hadhrat Ummu Salamah who asked, 'Do people amongst you revile Rasulullaah ﷺ 'Allaah forbid!' I exclaimed. I may also…
narrations.summary: Abu Abdullaah Jadali reports that Ummu Salamah (RA) asked whether people revile the Prophet, and then quoted the Prophet that whoever reviles Ali has reviled him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Abdullaah Jadali reports that Hadhrat Ummu Salamah IS once asked him, "Do people amongst you revile Rasulullaah ﷺ "How can Rasulullaah ﷺ be reviled?" he…
narrations.summary: Abu Abdullaah Jadali reports that Ummu Salamah rebuked those who reviled Ali, asking how Rasulullah could be reviled when Ali, whom he loved, was reviled.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Saadiq reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said to him, "My lineage is the same as that of Rasulullaah ﷺ and my Deen is also the same as that of Rasulullaah ﷺ.…
narrations.summary: Ali (RA) tells Abu Saadiq that his lineage and his deen are the same as the Prophet's, so whoever reviles him reviles the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Isbahaani narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was sitting on the pulpit of Rasulullaah ﷺ when Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) (who was still a child)…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Isbahaani reports that the young Hasan (RA) asked Abu Bakr (RA) to leave the Prophet's pulpit, that Abu Bakr lifted him onto his lap and wept, and that Ali (RA) said he had not instructed it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was once delivering a sermon when Hadhrat Hasan (RA) (who was still a child) arrived and also mounted the pulpit…
narrations.summary: Urwa (RA) reports that Hasan (RA) climbed the Prophet's pulpit during Abu Bakr's sermon, and Ali (RA) said it was done without his consultation.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was once delivering a sermon when Hadhrat Husayn (RA) (who was still a child stood up and said, "Do dismount my…
narrations.summary: Husayn tells Umar to step down from his grandfather's pulpit; Ali threatens Husayn, Umar intercedes, and Umar later welcomes Husayn into his home and blesses him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uqba bin Haarith narrates that it was after the demise of Rasulullaah that he left the Masjid with Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) after performing the Asr salaah. Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Uqba bin Haarith describes how the Prophet comforted Hasan and Husayn, who were crying of thirst, by giving them his tongue to suck until they were quiet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umayr bin Is'haaq reports that he saw Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) meet Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) and say, "Show me that part of your stomach where I saw…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah asks Hasan to show him the part of his belly the Prophet used to kiss, and then kisses that spot himself.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maqbari reports that they were once with Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) when Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) arrived and greeted them with Salaam. The people returned the…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah greets Hasan as 'my leader', explaining he heard the Prophet call him a leader.

narrations.excerpt: Marwaan once visited Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) during the illness that claimed his life. Marwaan said, "Since we have been living with you, nothing has angered us more…
narrations.summary: Marwaan objects to Abu Hurayrah's love for Hasan and Husayn; Abu Hurayrah answers with an account of the Prophet quieting the two thirsty children on a journey.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ammaar bin Abu Ammaar reports that when Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit was once about to mount his animal, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas held the stirrup (so that he may…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas holds the stirrup for Zaid bin Thaabit, who protests; Abdullaah says this is how scholars and elders are honoured, and Zaid kisses his hand in honour of the Prophet's family.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that as Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) was about to mount his animal one day, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) caught hold of the stirrup. "Go…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports the same stirrup incident: Zaid bin Thaabit is served by Abdullaah bin Abbaas, who says this is how scholars and elders are honoured.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) held the stirrup of Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit's animal, he said, "We have been commanded to hold on to the…
narrations.summary: Another report says Abdullaah bin Abbaas, holding Zaid bin Thaabit's stirrup, explained that they had been commanded to hold the stirrups of their teachers and seniors.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that a drink was once served when Rasulullaah ﷺ was in the company of some Sahabah (RA) such as Hadhrat Abu Bakr, Hadhrat Umar (RA) and…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah reports that when the Prophet passed a drink to Abu Ubaydah, the eldest, he insisted that Abu Ubaydah drink first, and said that blessings lie with elders.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Raafi bin Khadeej llilgi and Hadhrat Sahl bin Abi Hathmah (RA) both reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Sahl (RA) and Hadhrat Muhayyisah bin Mas'ood were separated…
narrations.summary: Two Ansaar reports: after Abdullaah bin Sahl was murdered at Khaybar, the Prophet let the eldest speak first, offered the case to the Jews by oath, and paid the blood money himself when the Ansaar refused the oath.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Waa'il bin Hujar (RA) says, "(In Hadhramaut) We heard about the appearance of Rasulullaah ﷺ at a time when we were in control of a large kingdom where people…
narrations.summary: Waa'il bin Hujar says that he left his kingdom in Hadhramaut to come to the Prophet, who welcomed him, seated him beside himself on the pulpit and praised his sincerity before the people.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Waa'il bin Hujar Sfiiigi says that when he came to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ilif announced, "This is Waa'il bin Hujar who has come…
narrations.summary: In a second report, the Prophet tells the people to be kind to Waa'il bin Hujar, who has just left his royal background, and promises to repay him double for what his family took from him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh's arm started bleeding profusely (from a wound), Rasulullaah stood by him and embraced him…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that the Prophet embraced the dying Sa'd bin Mu'aadh and prayed for him, and that the Prophet overruled criticism of Sa'd's mother reciting a lament, saying poets other than her lie.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaarijah bin Zaid narrates that supper was once served to Hadhrat Umar when he was dining with some people. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then left the house to call Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Khaarijah bin Zaid reports that Umar invited Mu'ayqeet, a leprosy-stricken Companion, close to sit and eat with him; a second report says Umar urged him to eat from the dish in front of him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdul waahid bin Aun Dowsi narrates that Hadhrat Tufayl bin Amr returned (from the region of his tribe the Dows) to Rasulullaah ﷺ and remained with Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abdul Waahid bin Aun Dowsi reports that Tufayl bin Amr was martyred at Yamaamah, that his son Amr, who had lost a hand there, was embarrassed to eat with others, and that Umar insisted he eat and would not eat until Amr did.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that Hadhrat Umar Hugs once wrote to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari saying, "The news has reached me that you allow a large group of people in all at…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Umar wrote to Abu Moosa Ash'ari instructing him to admit the people of virtue, status and character first, before the rest.

narrations.excerpt: On his deathbed, Hadhrat Qais bin Aasim (RA) gave the following advice to his sons: "Fear Allaah and give leadership to the seniors because when people hand over…
narrations.summary: On his deathbed, Qais bin Aasim advises his sons to fear Allaah, give leadership to their seniors, earn and invest wealth, avoid begging, not wail over him, and bury him where the Banu Bakr cannot find his grave.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed narrates from his uncle who says, "When we participated in the Battle of Jamal, Hadhrat Ali (RA) formed our rows (before engaging in battle) and…
narrations.summary: Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that Ali ordered his army at Jamal not to start the fighting; Abul Bakhtari reports that Ali called the opponents his brothers who had rebelled, neither polytheists nor hypocrites.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Umar bin Ali bin Abi Taalib reports that Hadhrat Ali did not engage the opposite army in battle until he had called them (to forsake the weapons) for…
narrations.summary: Before the Battle of Jamal, Ali prays and orders his men not to pursue fleeing enemies, not to kill the wounded, and not to take their possessions.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali bin Husayn reports that when he once went to Marwaan bin Hakam, the latter said to him, "I have never seen anyone so noble in victory as your (grand) father…
narrations.summary: Marwaan bin Hakam tells Ali bin Husayn that he never saw a man so noble in victory as Ali, who at Jamal ordered that no fleeing or wounded man be killed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abd Khayr reports that when Hadhrat Ali (RA) was questioned about those who fought him in the Battle of Jamal, he said, "They were simply our brothers whom we…
narrations.summary: Ali says the men who fought him at Jamal were his brothers who rebelled, that he pardoned them, and that they were neither mushrikeen nor munaafiqeen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) was once asked whether the people who fought him in the Battle of Jamal were Mushrikeen. He replied, "It is from…
narrations.summary: Abul Bakhtari reports that Ali was asked whether those who fought him at the Battle of Jamal were mushrikeen or munaafiqeen, and Ali replied that they were simply brothers who had rebelled against them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Habeebah the freed slave of Hadhrat Talha (RA) says that it was after the Battle of Jamal that he once went to Hadhrat Ali (RA) in the company of Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Abu Habeebah, freed slave of Talha, reports that after Jamal Ali welcomed Talha's son Imraan, spoke warmly of Talha, quoted the verse about brothers in Paradise, returned Talha's lands and rents, and rebuked two men who had criticised Talha and Zubayr.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Hadhrat Rib'ee bin Hiraash adds that (when the two men passed their comment), Hadhrat Ali (RA) screamed so loud that the scream could have brought a palace…
narrations.summary: Rib'ee bin Hiraash adds that Ali shouted that the critics could only mean Talha and himself; Ibraheem reports that Ali refused to see Ibn Jurmooz, the killer of Zubayr, and said that Talha, Zubayr and he were among those promised brotherhood in Paradise.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Ghaalib reports that when Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) overheard someone speak ill of Ummul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), he said, "Be quiet! May you…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Ghaalib reports that Ammaar bin Yaasir rebuked a man who spoke ill of Aa'isha, saying she is the Prophet's wife in Paradise; a second report adds that Ammaar called him an insulter of the Prophet's beloved.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) once said, "Our mother Aa'isha Sgiiffili had her own opinion. We know for sure that she is the wife of Rasulullaah ipif in this world as well as in…
narrations.summary: Ammaar bin Yaasir says that Aa'isha is the Prophet's wife in this world and the next, and that Allaah used her to test whether the believers obey Him or her.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Ali (RA) sent Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir and Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali. (RA) to Kufa to rally people to fight, Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Abu Waa'il reports that Ali sent Ammaar bin Yaasir and Hasan bin Ali to Kufa to rally people, and Ammaar told them that Aa'isha is the Prophet's wife in this world and the next, and that Allaah was testing whether they obeyed Him or her.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab reports, "I once went to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood to teach me a particular verse of the Qur'aan. When he taught it to me in a certain way,. I…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Wahab reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood told him that Allaah assisted the Prophet when the disbelievers drove him out, and quoted the verse of the cave, where Abu Bakr was with him, to show Abu Bakr's rank.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shurayh bin Ubayd reports that a man once said to Hadhrat Abu Dardaa "What is the matter with you learned men? You are more cowardly than us, most miserly when…
narrations.summary: Umar seizes a man who mocked Abu Dardaa, brings him to the Prophet, and the verse about 'only joking' is revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Abu Bakr Hadhrat Jubayr bin Nufayr reports that a group of people once came to Hadhrat Umar and said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineenl We swear by Allaah that we have never seen…
narrations.summary: Umar rebukes a group who said he was the best after the Prophet, insisting Abu Bakr was purer than musk and that Awf had told the truth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that Hadhrat Umar Ul had appointed informants amongst the masses who once informed him that a group of people had gathered and claimed that he…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Umar angrily summoned people who claimed Umar was better than Abu Bakr, and told them that he wished he could reach a place in Jannah from where he could see Abu Bakr at the furthest point of his sight.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Abu Bakr (RA) is the best of this Ummah after its Nabi ﷺ. Whoever claims otherwise after this proclamation of mine…
narrations.summary: Umar declares that Abu Bakr is the best of this Ummah after its Nabi and that anyone who claims otherwise is a slanderer to be punished.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Hadhrat Ziyaad bin Ilaaqah states that Hadhrat Umar once overheard someone saying (about him), "This man is the best of this Ummah after its Nabi fill."…
narrations.summary: Umar whips a man who said Umar was the best of this Ummah after its Nabi, insisting that Abu Bakr is better than him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Zinaad narrates that someone once asked Hadhrat Ali (RA), "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! What is the matter with the Muhaajireen and Ansaar? They regard Abu Bakr as…
narrations.summary: Ali rebukes a man who asked why the Muhaajireen and Ansaar ranked Abu Bakr above him, and lists four virtues of Abu Bakr, quoting the verse about the cave.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mughierah bin Shu'bah (RA) narrates, "I was with Abu Bakr when a horse was brought to him. When a man (from the Ansaar) asked for the horse to be given to him,…
narrations.summary: Mughierah bin Shu'bah reports that when a man from the Ansaar insulted Abu Bakr, the Khalifah, he struck him, and Abu Bakr refused to let the Ansaar take retribution, preferring exile to letting them harm a man who restrains others from evil.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once saw a man's garment hanging below his ankles, he told him to lift it up. The man retorted,…
narrations.summary: Abu Waa'il reports that Ibn Mas'ood told a man to lift his garment; when the man retorted that Ibn Mas'ood also wore his high, Ibn Mas'ood explained his thin calves. Umar then struck the man for insolence. Alaa reports that Umar threw a brick at a Quraysh man who suggested he hire someone to build for him, saying he did not want to dislike Ibn Mas'ood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il narrates that because Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) owed something to a certain man, the man took an oath against her. For this, Hadhrat Umar had the man…
narrations.summary: Abu Waa'il reports that Umar had a man who swore an oath against Ummu Salamah, who owed him money, lashed thirty stripes.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Moosa reports that when the news reached Hadhrat Ali (RA) that Ibn Saba claimed that he (Hadhrat Ali (RA)) was superior to Hadhrat Abu Bakr and Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Ummu Moosa reports that when Ibn Saba claimed Ali was superior to Abu Bakr and Umar, Ali wanted him executed, but accepted a ruling that he should simply not be allowed to live in Ali's town.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem reports that the news once reached Hadhrat Ali (RA) that Abdullaah bin Aswad degraded the status of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA). Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Ibraheem reports that Ali, on hearing that Abdullaah bin Aswad had belittled Abu Bakr and Umar, reached for a sword to execute him, but was persuaded to exile him to Shaam instead.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) Rebukes a Man for Regarding him to be Superior to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) Hadhrat Katheer narrates that a man once came to Hadhrat Ali…
narrations.summary: Katheer reports that a man praised Ali as the best of people; Ali asked whether he had seen the Prophet, Abu Bakr or Umar, and said that a claim to have seen the Prophet deserves execution and a claim to have seen Abu Bakr or Umar deserves lashing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Alqamah reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once delivered a lecture to them. After duly praising Allaah, he said, "The news has reached me that some people regard me…
narrations.summary: Alqamah reports Ali's lecture that the best after the Prophet is Abu Bakr, then Umar. A second report from Suwayd bin Ghaflah has Ali praising Abu Bakr and Umar, describing Abu Bakr's nomination to lead prayer and Umar's appointment by consultation, and warning against reviling them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq reports that a man once came to Hadhrat Ali (RA) and said, "Uthmaan is in Jahannam." "What makes you say this?" Hadhrat Ali enquired. The man replied,…
narrations.summary: Abu Is'haaq reports that a man called Uthmaan a sinner for introducing new practices, and Ali asked him whether Allaah had selected Uthmaan to marry the Prophet's daughters, then warned the man to say nothing else.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalim reports that his father once met one of the Sahabah (RA) who had a problem with his speech and could therefore not express himself clearly. When he…
narrations.summary: Saalim reports that his father, Abdullaah bin Umar, rebuked a companion who complained about Uthmaan, reminding them that during the Prophet's time they named Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan together, and that the complaint arose only when wealth became the priority.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir bin Sa'd narrates that Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) was once walking somewhere when he overheard a person speaking ill of Hadhrat Ali (RA), Hadhrat Talha (RA) and…
narrations.summary: Aamir bin Sa'd reports that Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas warned a man against reviling Ali, Talha and Zubayr, then prayed that Allaah would show the man His power; a camel then trampled him, and the people hailed Sa'd's prayer as accepted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Sa'd narrates that when someone reviled Hadhrat Ali (RA), Hadhrat Sa'd bin Maalik (RA) (Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas US cursed him. A camel then ran…
narrations.summary: Mus'ab bin Sa'd reports that when a man reviled Ali, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas cursed him, a camel killed the man, and Sa'd then freed a slave and vowed never to curse anyone again.
