narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that he was once walking about the marketplace in Madinah when he reached a place called Ahjaaruz Zayt. There he saw some people…
narrations.summary: Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, finding a man reviling Ali in the Madinah marketplace, listed Ali's virtues and prayed that the gathering be shown Allaah's power; the ground swallowed the man's mount and he died.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rabaah bin Haarith reports that Hadhrat Mughiera (RA) was sitting in the largest Masjid with the people of Kufa on his right and his left when someone called…
narrations.summary: Rabaah bin Haarith reports that Sa'eed bin Zaid objected to a Kufan who swore at Ali while sitting with Mughiera bin Shu'ba, and cited the Prophet's words that ten people, including Ali, would enter Paradise; a second report from Abdullaah bin Dhaalim says Sa'eed warned Mughiera's orators against reviling Ali.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Seereen reports that when a drink was brought to Hadhrat Umar after he has been stabbed, the drink came out from his wounds (as he drank). At this, Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Ibn Seereen reports that Suhayb wept aloud over Umar's stabbing, and Umar reminded him of the Prophet's words that the person over whom people wail is punished. Abu Burdah reports the same. Miqdaam bin Ma'dikarib reports that Hafsa wailed, and Umar forbade her to wail over him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdul Malik bin Zaid narrates from his father that as he was weeping, someone once asked Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Zaid (RA), "What makes you weep, O Abu Hadhrat Sa'eed…
narrations.summary: Abdul Malik bin Zaid reports that Sa'eed bin Zaid wept, saying Islaam had suffered a void at Umar's death that would never be filled. Abu Waa'il reports that Ibn Mas'ood wept more than ever at Umar's death and said even thorny trees were distressed by it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan says, "when the news of Nu'maan bin Muqarrin's death reached Umar, I saw him place his hands on his head and start to weep."
narrations.summary: Abu Uthmaan reports that when Umar heard of Nu'maan bin Muqarrin's death, he put his hands on his head and wept.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Ash'ath San'aani says, "The governor of San'aa was a Sahabl called Thumaamah bin Adi, when he heard of the death of Hadhrat Uthmaan he wept and said,…
narrations.summary: Abul Ash'ath San'aani reports that Thumaamah bin Adi, governor of San'aa, wept when he heard of Uthmaan's death, saying the caliphate on the pattern of prophethood had ended and that kingship and tyranny would follow.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Ali narrates that Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) wept over Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) the day he was martyred in his home. Hadhrat Abu Saalih reports, "Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Three reports on the death of Uthmaan: Zaid bin Thaabit wept for him on the day he was martyred in his home; Abu Hurayrah wept whenever it was mentioned; Abu Humayd Saa'idi, a Badr veteran, vowed never to laugh again until he met Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) once said, "We had hardly left from burying when we found a change within our hearts."
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri says that they had hardly left the burial when they found a change in their hearts.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) said, "When with, we were united but no sooner did he leave us and we divided left and right." Another narration states that he said, "We all…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b said that after the Prophet passed away, the Companions who had been united while with him began looking in different directions.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) said, "The day passed away, everything in Madinah became dark. We had hardly finished burying ( 1) Ibn Abi Dunya, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal.…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik said Madinah turned dark on the day the Prophet passed away, and recalled that the day he entered Madinah was the brightest day and the day of his death the darkest.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas Si reports that when the consultative assembly (appointed by Hadhrat Umar (RA) before his death) assembled, Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) saw what they were doing…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that when Umar's consultative assembly met after his death, Abu Talha warned that each of them seemed to want the Khilaafah for himself or to pass it on, and said that every Muslim home had suffered by Umar's death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) narrates that they were six Muslims with Rasulullaah ﷺ when the Mushrikeen said (to Rasulullaah ﷺ), "Drive these people away from you."…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas said that when the Mushrikeen asked the Prophet to drive away the poor Sahabah, among them Bilaal and Ibn Mas'ood, Allaah revealed the verse forbidding him to do so.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports that a group of the Quraysh once passed by Rasulullaah ﷺ when he was in the company of some poor Muslims such as Hadhrat Suhayb…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood reports that when a group of the Quraysh asked the Prophet to drive away poor Muslims such as Suhayb, Bilaal, Khabbaab and Ammaar, Allaah revealed Surah An'aam verses 51 and 52.

narrations.excerpt: Discussing the verse j, Hadhrat Anas (RA) says that Hadhrat Ibn Umm Maktoom (who was blind) once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ while Rasulullaah ﷺ was speaking to Ubay bin Khalaf…
narrations.summary: Anas and Aa'isha report that while the Prophet was inviting Ubay bin Khalaf to Islaam, the blind Ibn Umm Maktoom came to him, and that Surah Abasa was revealed; afterwards the Prophet always honoured Ibn Umm Maktoom.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khabbaab bin Arat (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once in the company of some poor Muslims, amongst whom were Hadhrat Ammaar Hadhrat Suhayb (RA), Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Khabbaab bin Arat relates that Aqra and Uyayna asked the Prophet to send away the poor Sahabah before the delegations saw them, and that Allaah revealed verses commanding him to stay with them, after which the Companions sat close to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) narrates that there came to Rasulullaah ﷺ some people (new Muslims) whose hearts Rasulullaah ﷺ was still winning over to Islaam. Amongst them was the…
narrations.summary: Salmaan reports that Uyayna and Aqra asked the Prophet to move the poor Muslims in woollen cloaks away from him so they could sit and learn with him, and that Allaah revealed Surah Kahf verses 27 and 28 forbidding him to obey such people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Salamah bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that Qais bin Mataatiyyah once came to a gathering that included Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA), Hadhrat Suhayb Roomi and…
narrations.summary: Abu Salma reports that Qais bin Mataatiyyah belittled Salmaan, Suhayb and Bilaal, and that Mu'aadh seized him and brought him to the Prophet, who told the people that all are of one Rabb, one father and one Deen, and that Arabic makes no one superior, and said to leave the man to the Fire.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) narrates that a man once came to- Rasulullaah ﷺ and asked, "O Rasulullaah ilil! I have carried my mother a distance of two on my neck over sands so…
narrations.summary: Buraydah reports that a man asked whether he had repaid his mother by carrying her on his neck across scorching sands, and the Prophet said it may have repaid only a single labour pain.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that someone once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ with an old man. "Who is this?" Rasulullaah ﷺ enquired. When he informed Rasulullaah ﷺ that the old…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that when a man came with his elderly father, the Prophet told him never to walk or sit before his father, never to call him by name, and never to make him the target of abuse.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ghassaan Dhabi says, "I was walking with my father on rocky ground (in Madinah) when Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) met me and asked me, "Who is this?' When I…
narrations.summary: Abu Ghassaan Dhabi says that Abu Hurayrah met him walking with his father and advised him to walk behind or beside his father, not to let anyone come between them, not to walk on an unrailed roof, and not to eat meat his father was eyeing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas narrates that a man once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ seeking permission to fight in Jihaad, Rasulullaah gpsgr asked, "Are your parents…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that when a man asked to join Jihaad, the Prophet asked whether his parents were alive and told him that his Jihaad was to be with them.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that a man came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "1 pledge at your hand my allegiance to migrate and to wage Jihaad seeking rewards from Allaah," "Are…
narrations.summary: Three reports say that men who wished to migrate or wage Jihaad were told to return to their parents and be good to them, and a man from Yemen was told he could fight only with his parents' permission.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that a man once said to Rasulullaah ii!?, "While I desire to march in Jihaad, I do not have the means." Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Are any of your…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that a man who wanted to march in Jihaad but lacked the means was told that serving his mother would bring him the reward of Hajj, Umrah and Jihaad.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that once Rasulullaah ﷺ announced, "Prepare to march on the town with oppressive inhabitants because if Allaah wills, He will allow you…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah reports that when the Prophet called the Muslims to march on Khaybar, Abu Hurayrah stayed behind to care for his mother, and the Prophet told him that being with his parents and fulfilling their rights is also in the path of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was in Siqaayah when a woman came to him with her son. She said, "This son of mine wants to march in Jihaad…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that a woman brought her son, who wanted to join Jihaad, to the Prophet at Siqaayah, and the Prophet told him to stay with his mother until she permitted him or died, as that would earn him greater reward.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that a man came with his mother to Rasulullaah ﷺ While he wanted to proceed in Jihaad, she was averse to the idea. Rasulullaah advised him…
narrations.summary: A narration states that a man wanting to fight in Jihaad, whose mother was against it, was told by the Prophet to stay close to her, as his reward with her would equal the reward of Jihaad.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Talha bin Mu'aawiya Sulami (RA) reports that he once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I wish to wage Jihaad in the path of Allaah." "Is your…
narrations.summary: Talha bin Mu'aawiya Sulami reports that he asked the Prophet's permission to wage Jihaad, and was told to stay at his mother's feet because Jannah lies there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaahimah (RA) reports that when he approached Rasulullaah ﷺ to seek advice about proceeding in Jihaad, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him whether his parents were alive.…
narrations.summary: Jaahimah reports that when he came to the Prophet for advice about Jihaad, he was asked whether his parents were alive, and was told to stay with them because Jannah lies beneath their feet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaahimah (RA) says, "I went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I intend fighting in Jihaad and have come to consult with you.' 'Do you have a mother?'…
narrations.summary: Jaahimah recounts asking the Prophet about Jihaad, being told to stay with his mother because Jannah lies beneath her feet, and receiving the same answer on repeated asking.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nu'aym the freed slave of Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) left for Hajj and was somewhere between Makkah and Madinah,…
narrations.summary: Nu'aym reports that Abdullaah bin Umar, sitting beneath a tree between Makkah and Madinah, recalled seeing a young man ask the Prophet to join Jihaad and being told to go back and be good to his parents.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) proposed for Hadhrat Ummu Kulthoom, (her father) Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "She is still too young for marriage." Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Hasan narrates that when Umar proposed for Ummu Kulthoom, Ali said she was too young; after Umar cited his kinship with the Prophet and Ali's sons objected, Ali told them to get the proposer married.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) bin Seereen reports that the price of a date palm reached a thousand Dirhams during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA). Hadhrat Usaama (RA)…
narrations.summary: Ibn Seereen reports that when a date palm's sap was prized at a thousand dirhams, Usaama bored into a palm and gave the sap to his mother because she had asked for it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) narrates that he once saw Rasulullaah ﷺ delivering a sermon from the pulpit when Hadhrat Husayn (RA) came out dragging a cloth around his…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that the Prophet came down from the pulpit to lift Husayn after the child tripped on his cloth during the sermon, saying that children are a trial.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Hasan (RA) once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ while he was in Sajdah and climbed on his back. Rasulullaah held him and stood up.…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed and Zubayr report that Hasan climbed onto the Prophet's back while he was in sajdah, and the Prophet did not rise or move him until the boy chose to get down.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) narrates that he once saw Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali climb on to Rasulullaah ilif's back when he was in Sajdah. Rasulullaah ﷺ did not make the boy get off…
narrations.summary: Zubayr reports that Rasulullah stayed in sajdah while Hasan bin Ali climbed on his back, did not make him get down until he got down himself, and sometimes parted his legs so the child could pass through.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Bahiy narrates that he once asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) who it was that most closely resembled Rasulullaah ﷺ . He replied, "Hasan bin Ali most closely…
narrations.summary: Bahiy reports that Ibn Zubayr described Hasan as the grandson most like the Prophet and most beloved to him, who would climb onto his back during salaah and be left there until he got down.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports that at times when Rasulullaah was in Sajdah, Hadhrat Hasan (RA) and Hadhrat Husayn (RA) would climb on his back. When the…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood and Anas report that Hasan and Husayn would climb onto the Prophet's back during sajdah, and that he prolonged the sajdah, saying he did not like to rise quickly while his grandsons were on him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Qataadah Si reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came out of his room with (his granddaughter) Hadhrat Umaamah bint Abil Aas (RA) on his shoulders. He then…
narrations.summary: Abu Qataadah reports that Rasulullah carried his granddaughter Umaamah bint Abil Aas on his shoulders while praying, setting her down for ruku and lifting her again when he stood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came out to them with Hadhrat Hasan (RA) on one shoulder and Hadhrat Husayn (RA) on the other. He was kissing…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet came out carrying Hasan on one shoulder and Husayn on the other, kissing each in turn, and said that whoever loves them loves him and whoever hates them hates him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) once said, "I have seen Rasulullaah ﷺ suck his tongue (the tongue of Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA)) and the tongue or lips that Rasulullaah ﷺ sucked…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya reports that he saw the Prophet suck Hasan's tongue and said that a tongue or lips the Prophet had sucked could never suffer punishment.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saa'ib bin Yazeed (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once kissed Hadhrat Hasan (RA), Hadhrat Aqra bin Haabis (RA) said, "Although I have ten children of my…
narrations.summary: Saa'ib bin Yazeed reports that when the Prophet kissed Hasan, Aqra said he had ten children and had never kissed one of them, and the Prophet replied that Allaah does not show mercy to those who do not show mercy to people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aswad bin Khalaf (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once picked up Hadhrat Hasan, kissed him and then turned to the Sahabah (RA) saying, "It is because of his child…
narrations.summary: Aswad bin Khalaf reports that the Prophet kissed Hasan and said that a child makes a man miserly, foolish and cowardly, because he fears for the child's welfare.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was most compassionate towards his family. He had a son (ibraheem) who was being suckled by the wife of a blacksmith at one end of…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet was the most compassionate towards his family and visited his son Ibraheem, who was nursed at a blacksmith's home, kissing and smelling the child.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a woman once came to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) with her two little daughters. When Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) gave her three dates, the woman gave one…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that after Aa'isha told the Prophet how a mother split her last date between her two daughters, he said she would surely enter Jannah for that deed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) reports that a woman once came to Rasulullaah to beg for food with her two sons. Rasulullaah iiif gave her three dates, one for each of them.…
narrations.summary: Hasan bin Ali reports that the Prophet gave a mother's two sons one date each and that she split her own date between them, and he said Allaah would show her mercy; Abu Hurayrah then reports the Prophet asking a father whether he is merciful to his child.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that a man was sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ when his son arrived. The man kissed the boy and seated him on his lap. When his daughter came, he…
narrations.summary: The Prophet rebukes a man who kissed his son and seated him on his lap but only seated his daughter in front of him, telling him to treat his children equally.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Haydah (RA) reports that he once asked Rasulullaah what the rights of his neighbours were. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "You should visit him when he…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Haydah asks the Prophet about the rights of neighbours and is told how to visit, help, congratulate and support a neighbour.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) says that he once complained to Rasulullaah ﷺ that his neighbour was causing him much trouble. Rasulullaah ﷺ encouraged him…
narrations.summary: A man complains to the Prophet about a troublesome neighbour; after advice to be patient, the Prophet tells him to put his belongings on the street and states the duties owed to neighbours and guests.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that as Rasulullaah ﷺ was once leaving for a battle, he announced, "None who has caused harm to his neighbour should accompany us…
narrations.summary: The Prophet bars a man who had urinated against his neighbour's wall from joining a military expedition.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Miqdaad bin Aswad (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once asked the Sahabah (RA), "What do you think of adultery?" They replied, "It is Haraam. Allaah and His…
narrations.summary: Miqdaad reports that the Prophet asked the Sahabah about adultery and theft, and said that both are more serious when committed against one's neighbour than against others.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mutarrif bin Abdullaah (RA) says, "I had always been hearing a Hadith narrated by Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) and desired to meet him (to hear the Hadith directly from…
narrations.summary: Mutarrif reports Abu Dharr's hadith that Allaah loves three kinds of people, beginning with one who fights with steadfastness in the path of Allaah; the passage then gives Aa'isha's account of the Prophet's teaching to treat people according to their status.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rabaah bin Rabee (RA) narrates, "We were on a military expedition with Rasulullaah ﷺ who had given every three of us a camel to ride. In the desert, two persons…
narrations.summary: Rabaah bin Rabee recounts that on the Prophet's advice two Companions let him ride their camel and took turns walking, because a righteous travel companion should be treated well.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Mikhraaq reports that when a man of prominent appearance passed by Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) as she was having a meal, she invited him (to share the meal with…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha explains that she invited a prominent man to eat with her but gave a passing beggar only bread, because the Prophet told them to treat people according to their status.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when a beggar came to beg from Hadhrat Aa'isha she had a piece of bread given to him. When a man of prominence then arrived, she allowed him…
narrations.summary: Variant accounts of Aa'isha's practice of treating a rich man and a beggar differently, based on the Prophet's instruction; the text cross-refers to Ali's earlier similar act.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Agharr (RA) from the Muzaynah tribe says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once gave instructions for me to have a Jareeb of dates that was with one of the Ansaar. However, when…
narrations.summary: Aghar reports that Abu Bakr greeted everyone he saw from afar with salaam before they could greet him, and Zuhrah bin Khameesa reports Abu Bakr saying people had outdone them in returning greetings.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) reports, "I was once riding behind Hadhrat Abu Bakr on the same animal. Whenever he passed by any people and greeted them with the words 'As Salaamu…
narrations.summary: Umar reports riding behind Abu Bakr, who greeted every group they passed, and that the replies were fuller than the greeting, prompting Abu Bakr to remark that people had surpassed them greatly that day.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) was once giving a lecture when he said, "Hold fast to patience because in markets that you like and those that you do not because patience is a…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah urged patience and recalled how the Companions greeted each other with Salaam even when a tree separated them, as Anas reports.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) once said, "When we were with Rasulullaah ﷺ and a tree came between us (causing us to separate), we would greet each other with Salaam as soon as we…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that when a tree came between them during a journey with Rasulullah, they would greet each other with Salaam as soon as they were back together.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tufayl bin Ubay bin Ka'b narrates, "I used to accompany Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar to the marketplace every morning. When we went there, he would not pass by any…
narrations.summary: Tufayl bin Ubay reports that Abdullaah bin Umar greeted everyone he met in the marketplace and went there only for the sake of Salaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah Baahili (RA) used to greet everyone he met with Salaam. There was none who ever beat him to making Salaam except a Jew who once hid behind a pillar…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah greets everyone with Salaam and tells a Jew who beat him to it that the Prophet said Salaam is a greeting for the Ummah and a security for non-Muslims under Muslim rule.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ziyaad reports, "I was holding the hand of Hadhrat Abu Umaamah as he proceeded to his house. He did not pass by any Muslim, Christian, youngster or…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Ziyaad reports that Abu Umaamah greeted every Muslim, Christian and child he passed and urged his nephew to spread Salaam among Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Basheer bin Yasaar says, "None could ever beat Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar to making Salaam."
narrations.summary: Basheer bin Yasaar says that no one ever beat Abdullaah bin Umar to making Salaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) reports that someone, once came to, Rasulullaah ﷺ and greeted with the words: "jui C ". Rasulullaah iii? replied with the words: oji iU-SS iilji ".…
narrations.summary: Salmaan reports that the Prophet answered a greeting in full and, when asked why he answered differently for later greeters, cited Surah Nisaa on returning a greeting in kind.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to her, "O Aa'isha! Jibra'eel is here and he conveys Salaams to you." Hadhrat Aa'isha replied by saying, ii She…
narrations.summary: The Prophet tells Aa'isha that Jibra'eel sends her Salaams, and Jibra'eel blesses the Ahlul Bayt.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) and other Sahabah (RA) narrate that when Rasulullaah once requested permission to enter the home of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah Rasulullaah ﷺ greeted with…
narrations.summary: Anas and other Companions report that the Prophet sought permission at the door of Sa'd bin Ubaadah, who answered each Salaam softly and then served him olive oil and received his du'aa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to visit the Ansaar and when he came to the locality of the Ansaar, the children of the Ansaar would gather around him.…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet greeted the children of the Ansaar and, at Sa'd bin Ubaadah's door, greeted three times before leaving, and Sa'd ran after him as in the previous narration.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Jubayr reports that Hadhrat umar (RA) once passed by Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and greeted him. Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) however did not reply to the…
narrations.summary: Umar complains to Abu Bakr that Uthmaan did not return his greeting, and Uthmaan explains he was lost in thought about Shaytaan's whisperings, so Abu Bakr relates the Prophet's teaching that the Kalimah is the salvation of this Ummah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) says, "I once passed by Uthmaan bin Affaan in the Masjid and greeted him. Although he could see me clearly, he still did not reply to my…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas says Uthmaan did not return his greeting; Uthmaan explains he was thinking of the Prophet's du'aa of Yunus, which the Prophet taught.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari narrates that Hadhrat Ash'ath bin Qais (RA) and Hadhrat Jareer bin Abdullaah Bajali (RA) once went to see Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi. when they came to…
narrations.summary: Ash'ath bin Qais and Jareer bin Abdullaah visit Salmaan Faarsi with a message from Abu Dardaa; Salmaan refuses their offer of wealth and accepts only the greeting Abu Dardaa sent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jundub (RA) says, "When meeting his companions, Rasulullaah ﷺ never shook their hands until he had first greeted them with Salaam." Someone once asked Hadhrat Abu…
narrations.summary: Jundub reports that the Prophet never shook hands before first greeting, Abu Dharr says the Prophet always shook his hand, and Hasan reports Umar embracing his companions after Fajr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once met Hadhrat Hudhayfah bin Yamaan (RA) and was going to shake his hand, Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) turned away…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah turns away from the Prophet's handshake because he is in a state of impurity, and the Prophet says that sins fall away when Muslims shake hands.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that the Sahabah (RA) once asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Can we bow to each other (when greeting)?" "No," came the reply. They then asked, "Can we…
narrations.summary: Anas reports the Companions asked whether they could bow, embrace or shake hands, and Aa'isha describes the Prophet rushing out to embrace Zaid bin Haaritha when he returned to Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that someone once asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ When any of us meets his brother or his friend, can he bow to him?" "No," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ. "Can…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet forbade bowing and embracing a brother, but allowed shaking his hand.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that when the Sahabi asked, "Can he then embrace him and kiss him?" Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "No, unless he shas returned from a journey."
narrations.summary: The Prophet allows embracing and kissing only after a journey, and Aa'isha describes him rushing to embrace Zaid bin Haaritha when Zaid arrived in Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was in my house when Zaid bin Haaritha arrived in Madinah. When Zaid came to meet Rasulullaah ﷺ and knocked at the door,…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that when Zaid bin Haaritha arrived in Madinah, Rasulullah rushed out in excitement, embraced him and kissed him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "It was the practice of the Sahabah (RA) to shake hands when meeting each other and embracing when returning from a journey."
narrations.summary: Anas says the Companions shook hands on meeting and embraced on returning from a journey, and Hasan relates how Umar hurried to embrace a companion after Fajr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) thought of one of his companions during the night, he would sigh, "Oh how long is the night!" Then after performing the…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Umar would sigh through the night when he thought of a companion, and after Fajr would hurry to embrace that companion as soon as he met him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) arrived in Shaam, the common people as well as the leaders came to meet him. "Where is my brother?" Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that when Umar reached Shaam he dismounted and embraced Abu Ubaydah on his arrival.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that Hadhrat Ja'far bin Abu Taalib (RA) met Rasulullaah as he was returning from Khaybar. Rasulullaah ﷺ embraced him and kissed him between the…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that the Prophet embraced Ja'far bin Abi Taalib and kissed him between the eyes on his return from Khaybar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Razeen reports that Hadhrat Salamah bin Akwa said, "It is with these hands of mine that I pledged allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Abdur…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Razeen reports that Salamah bin Akwa showed the hand he had pledged allegiance with, and the people kissed it without his stopping them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that he kissed Rasulullaah ﷺ's hands.
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that he kissed the Prophet's hands.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) also reports that he kissed Rasulullaah ﷺ's hands.
narrations.summary: Umar reports that he kissed the Prophet's hands.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ka'b bin Maalik SSi narrates that when the verses of the Qur'aan were revealed to confirm his forgiveness (for failing to participate in the expedition to…
narrations.summary: Ka'b bin Maalik reports that after the verses confirming his forgiveness for staying behind from the Tabook expedition were revealed, he went to Rasulullah and kissed his hands.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaari bin Aamir (RA) reports that when they arrived in Madinah and Rasulullaah iill was pointed out to them, they started kissing his hands and feet.(,) Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Zaari bin Aamir and Mazeedah Abdi report that visitors kissed the Prophet's hands, and that Ashaj kissed them too, and the Prophet told Ashaj that Allah and His Messenger love two of his qualities.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Rajaa Utaaridi says, "When I arrived in Madinah, I beheld a gathering at the centre of which a man was kissing the head of another man saying, We would have…
narrations.summary: Abu Rajaa saw Umar kissing Abu Bakr's head in Madinah for his stand against those who refused to pay zakaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tameem bin Salamah reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) arrived in Shaam, Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) welcomed him, shook his hand and kissed it. The two…
narrations.summary: Tameem bin Salamah reports that Abu Ubaydah welcomed Umar in Shaam, shook his hand and kissed it, and that kissing the hand of pious people is Sunnah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Haarith Dhimaari says, "When I met Hadhrat Waathilah bin Asqa, 1 asked, "Was it with these hands that you pledged allegiance to Rasulullaah ii!?' when…
narrations.summary: Yahya bin Haarith asks Waathilah bin Asqa whether he pledged allegiance to the Prophet with those hands, and then kisses his hand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yunus bin Maysarah narrates' that they once went to visit an ailing Yazeed bin Aswad when Hadhrat Waathilah bin Asqa (RA) also arrived there. When he saw him,…
narrations.summary: Yunus bin Maysarah reports that Yazeed bin Aswad, when ill, took Waathilah bin Asqa's hand and rubbed it on his face, and Waathilah told him the hadith that Allah treats His slaves according to their expectation of Him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Razeen says, "As we were passing Rabdha, Hadhrat Salamah bin Akwa was pointed out to us. I approached him and when we greeted him, he showed us…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Razeen reports that Salamah bin Akwa showed them his large hand, the one he pledged with, and they stood and kissed it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Jad'aan narrates that Hadhrat Thaabit once asked Hadhrat Anas "Did you ever touch Nabi ﷺ. with your hand?" When Hadhrat Anas said that he did, Hadhrat Thaabit…
narrations.summary: Abu Jad'aan reports that Thaabit Bunaani asked Anas whether he had touched the Prophet's hand, and when Anas said he had, Thaabit kissed his hand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) says that he saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) kiss the hand and feet of Hadhrat Abbaas (RA). Standing Out of Respect for a Muslim.
narrations.summary: Suhayb says he saw Ali kiss the hand and feet of Abbaas.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that she had not seen anyone who resembled Rasulullaah ﷺ more in his speech and mannerisms than (his daughter) Hadhrat Faatima (RA).…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha describes how Faatima most resembled the Prophet in speech and manner, how he welcomed and kissed her, and what passed between them during his final illness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hilaal (RA) (narrates from Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) who) says that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ left (their gathering), they stood up for him and would not sit until…
narrations.summary: Hilaal reports that whenever the Prophet left a gathering, the Companions stood up for him and did not sit until he had entered his room.

narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah says that when the Prophet came out leaning on his staff and the Companions stood for him, the Prophet told them not to stand as non-Arabs stand for one another.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once came out to them, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) (may Allaah shower His mercy upon him) said, "Stand up and…
narrations.summary: When Abu Bakr urged the Companions to stand up for the Prophet against a hypocrite, the Prophet said none should stand, since only Allaah deserves that.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "There was none whom the Sahabah (RA) loved to see more than Rasulullaah Si! . Despite this, they would not stand up for him when they saw him…
narrations.summary: Anas says the Companions loved seeing the Prophet more than anyone, yet did not stand up for him, because they knew he disliked it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi reports from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) that Rasulullaah forbade a person from making another stand up from his place and then sitting in the same…
narrations.summary: Naafi reports that the Prophet forbade a man from making another stand up and then sit in his place, so Abdullaah bin Umar would not sit where someone had stood for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Khaalid Waalibi says that when Hadhrat Ali (RA) once came out to them, they stood waiting for him to go ahead. Hadhrat Ali (RA) reprimanded them saying, "Why…
narrations.summary: Abu Khaalid Waalibi reports that Ali rebuked the Companions who stood waiting for him with their chests out like soldiers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Mijlaz reports that when Hadhrat Mu'aawiya SI once came out while Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Aamir (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr were seated. Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Abu Mijlaz reports that when Mu'aawiya came out while Abdullaah bin Zubayr stayed seated and Abdullaah bin Aamir stood, Mu'aawiya quoted Rasulullah that whoever likes people to stand for him should prepare a house in Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Waathila bin Khattaab Qurashi (RA) reports that a person once entered the Masjid when Rasulullaah ﷺ was there by himself, Rasulullaah shifted from his place for…
narrations.summary: Waathila bin Khattaab reports that the Prophet moved from his place in the Masjid for a man who entered, and Waathila bin Asqa reports the same and that Abu Bakr moved for Ali.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Katheer bin Murra says, "I once entered the Masjid on a Friday where I found Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik Ashja'ee (RA) sitting in a gathering with his legs stretched…
narrations.summary: Katheer bin Murra found Awf bin Maalik Ashja'ee folding in his outstretched legs in a gathering, saying he had stretched them out so that a pious person would come and sit there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Abbaad bin Ja'far narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas once said, "The person I have the most respect for is the one with whom I am sitting."…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas said that the person he respects most is the one sitting with him, and two chains report his words.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ja'far narrates that when two men went to see Hadhrat Ali (RA), he threw a cushion to each of them. While the one man sat on the cushion, the ( 1 ) Bukhaari…
narrations.summary: Ali gave two visitors cushions and told the man sitting on the ground to take the cushion, since only a donkey refuses hospitality.

narrations.summary: Umar reports that Abu Bakr gave him no reply when he proposed Hafsah to him, because he had heard the Prophet mention a proposal and kept the secret, and then Umar married Hafsah to the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) relates, "I was in Rasulullaah ﷺ's service one day and when I had completed, I thought to myself that since Nabi ﷺ is having his siesta, I may as well…
narrations.summary: Anas refuses to tell his mother the Prophet's secret errand and tells Thaabit Bunaani that he would trust no one else with it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that when a man once complained to Rasulullaah ﷺ about his hard heartedness, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Pass your hand over the head of an…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when a man complained of a hard heart, the Prophet told him to stroke an orphan's head and feed the poor.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) narrates that when a man once complained to Rasulullaah ﷺ about his hard heartedness, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Do you want your heart to be softened…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa reports the Prophet's advice to a man with a hard heart: show mercy to an orphan, stroke his head and feed him, which will soften the heart and fulfil needs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Basheer bin Aqrabah Juhani (RA) relates, "On the day the Battle of Uhud was fought, I asked Rasulullaah ﷺ , 'What has happened to my father?' Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Basheer bin Aqrabah reports that on the day of Uhud, after his father was martyred, the Prophet comforted him, stroked his head and offered to be his father and Aa'isha his mother.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) had a donkey that he took along with him when travelling to Makkah. He would use the donkey to rest or when the camels grew tired. He also…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar gives his donkey and his turban to a Bedouin whose father had been a friend of Umar, citing the Prophet's teaching to keep ties with a father's friends.

narrations.summary: Another narration adds that when someone asked whether two dirhams would not suffice, Abdullaah bin Umar cited the Prophet's command to care for a father's associates.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Usayd Saa'idi (RA) narrates that someone once asked, "Rasulullaah ﷺ Is there any good treatment that I may give to my parents after their demise?" Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Abu Usayd Saa'idi reports the Prophet's advice on how to treat parents after their death: make du'aa and seek forgiveness for them, fulfil their promises, keep their ties and honour their friends.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ziyaad bin An'am Afriqi reports that they were once at sea as soldiers during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) when their vessel joined up with that of…
narrations.summary: Ziyaad bin An'am reports that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari, while fasting, accepted an invitation to a meal because the Prophet said a Muslim owes six rights to his brother.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Humayd bin Nu'aym narrates that when Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab and Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) were once invited to a meal, they both accepted the invitation.…
narrations.summary: Umar and Uthmaan accepted a meal invitation, but Umar wished he had not gone, fearing it was hosted for show; later Uthmaan accepted Mughiera bin Shu'ba's wedding invitation while fasting, to pray for blessings.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi SE once said, "When your friend, neighbour or relative who works for the state gives you a gift or invites you for a meal, you should accept (even…
narrations.summary: Salmaan Faarsi advises that a gift or meal from a friend, neighbour or relative who works for the state should be accepted, since any sin in unlawful earnings falls on the giver.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Qurra (RA) says, "I was once with Ma'qal Muzani when he removed an obstacle from the road. When I later saw something else (on the road), I beat him…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Qurra says Ma'qal Muzani removed an obstacle from the road and told him, quoting the Prophet, that removing an obstacle from the Muslims' path earns a good deed and that whoever has a single good deed accepted enters Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that they were once sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ when he sneezed. When the Sahabah (RA) responded by saying: (Yar-Hamu Kallaah'),…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that when the Prophet sneezed while sitting with the Sahabah and they answered Yarhamukallah, he prayed that Allaah guide them and set their affairs right.

narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that a man who sneezed in the Prophet's presence asked what he should say, and the Prophet taught him the words for his own sneeze and for the reply to it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ taught us -to respond whenever someone sneezed."
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says the Prophet taught the Sahabah to respond whenever someone sneezed.

narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood describes the Prophet's teaching: the sneezer says Alhamdulillah, those present say Yarhamukallah, and the sneezer replies with a prayer for their guidance and the setting right of their affairs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) reports that a person once sneezed next to Rasulullaah ﷺ 's room and then said, ('Alhamdu Lillaah')". To this, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, iiii…
narrations.summary: Umm Salamah reports that the Prophet replied to a sneezer who said Alhamdulillah, and said that a second sneezer who gave a longer praise had surpassed the first by nineteen stages.

narrations.excerpt: "('Alhamdu Lillaah')" Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when two persons sneezed in the presence of Rasulullaah ﷺ, he replied to the one and not to the other. When he was…
narrations.summary: Anas and Abu Hurayrah report that the Prophet answered the sneeze of the one who said Alhamdu Lillaah and did not answer the one who did not, explaining that the first had remembered Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Burdah (RA) narrates, "I once went to (my father) Abu Moosa when he was at the home of Ummu Fadhl bin Abba as. ® When I happened to sneeze, he did not reply…
narrations.summary: Abu Burdah reports that his father Abu Moosa Ash'ari did not reply to his sneeze because he had not said Alhamdulillah, but did reply to a woman's sneeze that did, and his mother approved.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Makhool Azdi reports that he was once with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar in the Masjid when someone sneezed in the corner of the Masjid. To this, Hadhrat Abdullaah…
narrations.summary: Makhool Azdi reports that when someone sneezed in the Masjid, Abdullaah bin Umar said Yarhamukallah only if the sneezer had said Alhamdulillah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi narrates that whenever anyone replied to the sneeze of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar by saying ' ('Yar-Hamu Kallaah')', he would say: "May Allaah shower us and…
narrations.summary: Naafi reports that whenever someone answered Abdullaah bin Umar's sneeze with Yarhamukallah, Abdullaah bin Umar replied with a prayer for their mercy and forgiveness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi also reports that when a. man once sneezed in front of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar and said ('Alhamdu Lillaah'), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar remarked, "You…
narrations.summary: Naafi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar rebuked a man who said Alhamdulillah on sneezing for not sending salutations on the Prophet as well.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dahhaak bin Qais Yashkari says, "When a man once sneezed in front of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) and said ('Alhamdu Lillaah'), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar…
narrations.summary: Dahhaak bin Qais Yashkari reports that Abdullaah bin Umar asked a man who had said Alhamdulillah on sneezing why he had not completed it by sending salutations on the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Jamara narrates that he once heard Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas reply to someone's sneeze by saying: "May Allaah shower us and you with His mercy and may He…
narrations.summary: Abu Jamara reports hearing Abdullaah bin Abbaas reply to someone's sneeze with a prayer for their mercy and forgiveness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once visited me when I was suffering from an eye infection."
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Arqam says the Prophet visited him when he was suffering from an eye infection.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) says, "During the year in which the farewell Hajj was performed, Rasulullaah ﷺ visited me when I fell extremely ill. 1 then said to him,…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas says that when he fell gravely ill in the year of the Farewell Hajj and wished to give away most of his wealth, the Prophet advised a third, and told him that what he spends for Allaah's pleasure is rewarded, even a morsel placed in his wife's mouth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) says, "When I once fell ill, Rasulullaah ﷺ came with Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) to visit me. They both arrived on foot but found me…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Abdillaah says that when he was unconscious from illness, the Prophet and Abu Bakr visited him, and he asked how to dispose of his wealth but got no answer until the verses of inheritance were revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Usaama bin Zaid (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once mounted a donkey saddled with a carriage that was covered in shawl made in Fidak. Rasulullaah ﷺ then mounted…
narrations.summary: Usaama bin Zaid recounts the Prophet riding to visit Sa'd bin Ubaadah past a gathering that included Abdullaah bin Ubay, and Abu Faakhita relates Abu Moosa visiting Hasan and Ali's hadith on the reward for visiting the sick.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once visited a villager. Whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ visited a sick person, he would say: "Do not worry, this is a…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas relates that the Prophet visited a villager with fever and said it would cleanse his sins; the villager said it would kill him, and he died of it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, both Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) suffered extreme fever. She went to them both…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha describes the fever of Abu Bakr and Bilaal on arriving in Madinah, the couplets they recited, and the Prophet's du'aa that Madinah be made beloved and healthy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once asked which of them had started the day by fasting. When Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) replied that he had, Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet asked who had fasted, visited a sick person, followed a funeral and fed a poor person that day, and Abu Bakr had done all four, so the Prophet said such a person enters Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Naafi narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari once visited an ailing Hadhrat Hasan bin (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Take note that when a…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Naafi reports that Abu Moosa Ash'ari visited ailing Hasan bin Ali, and Ali relates the reward for visiting a sick Muslim morning or evening.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) visited Hadhrat Hasan (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked, "Have you come to visit him because he is ill or for…
narrations.summary: Abu Musa Ash'ari visits the ailing Hasan, and Ali confirms the Prophet's saying on the reward of visiting a sick Muslim brother.

narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Yasaar reports that Ali objected to Amr bin Hurayth visiting the ailing Hasan bin Ali when Amr's opinion opposed his, and then reminded Amr of the Prophet's hadith on the seventy thousand angels who pray for the one who visits the sick.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed reports that he was once with Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) when he visited a sick man in the Kindah district (of Kufa). When he entered the house, Hadhrat Salmaan…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed reports that he was with Salmaan when they visited a sick man in Kindah, and Salmaan said a believer's illness brings forgiveness, while a sinner's is like a camel tied and released without knowing why.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Wahab reports that he once accompanied Hadhrat Salmaan on a visit to a sick friend of his from the Kindah tribe, when they entered the house, Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Wahab reports the same visit with Salmaan to a sick Kindah man, with the same comparison of a believer's illness to forgiveness and a sinner's to a released camel.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi reports that whenever Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) came to a sick person, he would ask how the person was and whenever he left, he would say, "May Allaah…
narrations.summary: Naafi reports that whenever Abdullaah bin Umar visited a sick person he asked how they were, and on leaving he only prayed that Allaah give them the best.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Hudhayl reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood once visited a sick person along with several other men. There happened to be a lady in the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Hudhayl reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood rebuked a man who stared at a woman in the house of a sick person, saying it would be better for him if his eye burst.

narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that when the Prophet visited a sick person he sat by his head and recited a prayer seven times asking the Majestic Allaah to cure him, and the person recovered if his time had not yet come.

narrations.summary: Ali reports the prayer the Prophet said whenever he visited a sick person, asking the Lord of mankind to remove the difficulty and grant a cure that only He can give.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds the words: "There is no cure like Your cure. Grant a cure that does not leave out any illness."
narrations.summary: Another narration adds words to the Prophet's prayer for the sick, asking for a cure that leaves no illness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) also reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ visited a sick person, he would place his right hand on the person's right cheek and say: ■ "O Rabb of mankind,…
narrations.summary: Ali reports that when the Prophet visited a sick person he placed his right hand on the person's right cheek and prayed for a cure.

narrations.summary: Anas reports the prayer the Prophet said for a sick person, asking the Lord of mankind to remove the difficulty and grant a cure that leaves no illness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ visited a sick person, he would place his hand on the part of the person's body that was in pain and then say:
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that when the Prophet visited a sick person he placed his hand on the part of the body that was in pain before saying a prayer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) says that Rasulullaah ﷺ one visited him when he was ill. As Rasulullaah ﷺ prepared to leave, he addressed Hadhrat Salmaan saying: "May Allaah…
narrations.summary: Salmaan says the Prophet visited him when he was ill and prayed that Allaah ease his difficulty, forgive his sins and grant him well-being in his Deen and body until death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ went to see a sick person or whenever a sick person was brought to him, he would say: "O Rabb of mankind, remove…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that whenever the Prophet went to see a sick person, or a sick person was brought to him, he prayed for a cure in the same words.

narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that she passed the Prophet's hand over his body with protective words as he lay dying, and he drew his hand away and asked Allaah to forgive him and let him meet the Highest Friend.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ greeted with Salaam (to seek permission to enter a home), he did so thrice and when he spoke (something of great…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that when the Prophet gave Salaam to seek permission to enter a home he did so three times, and when he said something important he repeated it three times.

narrations.summary: Qais bin Sa'd narrates that when the Prophet visited his father's house and gave Salaam, his father Sa'd bin Ubaadah answered quietly so that he could hear more Salaams, then hosted him with food, a shawl and a donkey.

narrations.summary: Rib'ee bin Hiraash reports a man of Banu Aamir who asked permission to enter without first giving Salaam, and the Prophet had a slave girl teach him the greeting, after which he was admitted.

narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Umar asked permission with Salaam to enter the Prophet's upper room, and Abu Hurayrah reports that the Companions asked permission when they came after being summoned.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Safeenah (RA) narrates that he was once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when Hadhrat Ali (RA) arrived, wanting to enter the room. As he knocked very lightly at the door,…
narrations.summary: Safeenah reports that when Ali came to the Prophet's room and knocked very lightly, the Prophet had the door opened for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) reports that he once sought permission to enter while standing directly in front of the door. Rasulullaah ﷺ advised him saying, "Never seek…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Ubaadah reports that the Prophet told him not to seek permission while standing directly in front of the door, because asking permission is meant to protect the sight.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) reports, "A man was once peeping inside one of Rasulullaah ﷺ's rooms when (seeing him) Rasulullaah ﷺ stood up and headed towards him with an…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that when a man peeped into one of the Prophet's rooms, the Prophet stood up with an arrowhead in his hand as if looking for a chance to strike him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sahl bin Sa'd Saa'idi (RA) narrates that a man was once peeping through a hole in the door of Rasulullaah ﷺ's room while Rasulullaah ﷺ was scratching his head…
narrations.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that the Prophet rebuked a man who peeped through the door of his room, saying that seeking permission exists to protect the sight.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports, "I was once sitting in a gathering of the Ansaar when Abu Moosa came looking extremely flustered. He explained, 'I thrice sought…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri describes how Abu Moosa, refused entry three times by Umar, left, and how Umar demanded a witness before Ubay bin Ka'b and Abu Sa'eed confirmed the Prophet's ruling.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "This instruction of Rasulullaah ffilf was unknown to me. Trade in the marketplace had distracted me (from…
narrations.summary: Umar sent Abu Moosa away after three requests to enter went unanswered, and only when Abu Moosa brought Abu Sa'eed and the Ansaar as witnesses to the Prophet's rule on seeking permission did Umar accept it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir bin Abdullaah reports that a slave girl of his once accompanied the daughter of Hadhrat (RA) to see Hadhrat Umar (RA). "May I come in?" she asked (at the…
narrations.summary: Aamir bin Abdullaah reports that Umar refused a slave girl entry and sent after her, and that Hudhayfah warned a man who asked whether he must seek permission even from his mother.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once sought permission to see him at a time when his head happened to be in the hands of his slave girl who…
narrations.summary: Umar asks to see Zaid while a slave girl is combing Zaid's hair, and Zaid comes to him; separately Abdullaah bin Mas'ood veils his wife when people ask to see him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Moosa bin Talha (RA) says, "I once went with my father to my mother. When he entered the room and I followed him in, he struck me so forcefully. on the chest that…
narrations.summary: Musa bin Talha is struck by his father for entering without permission, and Hudhayfah warns a man who was peeping in before asking to enter.

narrations.summary: Suwayd Abdi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar questioned him about peeping into his room, and that when asked about Jihaad, Abdullaah answered that whoever wages Jihaad does so for his own benefit.

narrations.summary: Baraa bin Aazib reports that the Prophet named loving and hating for Allaah's sake as the strongest link of Imaan, and Abu Dharr reports the Prophet saying the same deed is the most beloved to Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ loved people who possessed Taqwa." Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Abil Aas (RA) says, "There were two men whom Rasulullaah ﷺ liked very…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha and Uthmaan bin Abil Aas report that the Prophet loved the people of taqwa, and that he held Abdullaah bin Mas'ood and Ammaar bin Yaasir dear until his death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched expeditions of Sahabah iS under the command of Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA). Someone therefore said to him,…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Al Aas says he cannot tell whether the Prophet appointed him out of real affection or only to ease his heart, and names Abdullaah bin Mas'ood and Ammaar bin Yaasir as the two men the Prophet loved most.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that the people then remarked, "By Allaah! That (Hadhrat Ammaar was the very man whom you people killed during the Battle of Siffeen!" "True,"…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Al Aas is told that Ammaar, whom the Prophet loved, was killed at Siffeen by their side, and he admits it.

narrations.summary: Usaamah bin Zaid reports the Prophet naming Usaamah and then Ali as the family members he loved most, and Amr bin Al Aas reports the Prophet naming Aa'isha, Abu Bakr and Abu Ubaydah as the people he loved most.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Whom do you love most?" "Aa'isha," came the reply. "And from amongst the men?" the…
narrations.summary: Amr bin al-Aas reports that when asked whom the Prophet loved most, he named Aa'isha, then Abu Bakr, then Abu Ubaydah.

narrations.summary: Anas reports that a Companion was told by the Prophet to tell a man he liked for Allaah's sake that he liked him, and that the man prayed for him in return.

narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar tells how, on the Prophet's instruction, he told a man he liked him for Allaah's sake.

narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Sarjas tells the Prophet he likes Abu Dharr, is told to tell him, does so, and the Prophet says that even mentioning it carries great reward.

narrations.summary: Mujaahid reports that Abdullaah bin Abbaas said a passing man liked him a lot, and explained that he liked the man in return.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaahid also reports that a Sahabi once held him by his shoulders from the back and said, 'You should know that I like you a lot." To this, Hadhrat Mujaahid…
narrations.summary: Mujaahid reports a Sahabi who told him he loved him for Allaah's sake and offered his daughter in marriage, and then reports Abdullaah bin Umar's saying that friendships and enmities must be for Allaah's sake.

narrations.summary: Auf bin Tufayl reports that Aa'isha vowed never to speak to Abdullaah bin Zubayr after he remarked on her charity, until Miswar and Abdur Rahmaan brought about reconciliation; Urwa bin Zubayr adds that she freed forty slaves as expiation.

narrations.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that the people of Quba fell into a dispute that led to stone-throwing, and that the Prophet went to settle it; another report says the same of the Banu Amr bin Auf.

narrations.summary: Anas reports that Abdullaah bin Ubay insulted the Prophet's donkey, the two sides quarrelled and fought, and the Prophet calmed them; Anas says this is the occasion of the revelation on reconciling believers.

narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Aws and the Khazraj, who had been enemies, fought over a quarrel of poetry, and that the Prophet stopped them by reciting the verses on unity and the fear of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haaroon bin Rabaab reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr was on his deathbed, he instructed the people to look for a certain man saying, "I had mentioned to…
narrations.summary: Haaroon bin Rabaab reports that Abdullaah bin Amr, on his deathbed, asked people to find a man to whom he had promised his daughter and married her to him, so as not to meet Allaah with a broken promise.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that a man once passed by a gathering during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ and greeted them. After they had greeted him and he had passed by, one…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that a Sahabi disliked a passing man, and after questioning the man's neighbour and the Sahabi, the Prophet said the man was the better of the two.

narrations.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit reports that a man from the Banu Layth asked the Prophet's permission three times, then recited a poem praising the Prophet, and the Prophet approved it.

narrations.summary: Another narration says Miqdaad threw sand on the face of a man who was heaping praise on one of the Khalifahs, citing the Prophet's command.

narrations.summary: Ataa bin Abi Rabaah reports that Abdullaah bin Umar threw sand at the mouth of a man who praised another in his presence, quoting the Prophet's instruction.

narrations.summary: Naafi reports that when someone called Abdullaah bin Umar the best of people, Abdullaah replied that he was only a servant of Allaah, and that people keep praising a man until they destroy him.

narrations.summary: Taariq bin Shihaab reports that Abdullaah bin Umar warned that a man can leave home with his Deen intact and return without it after swearing praise of a powerless man in the hope of gain.

narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that during a famine before the Prophet's mission, the Prophet and Abbaas took in Ali and Ja'far, while Abu Taalib kept Aqeel.

narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that when Juwayriyyah wanted to free one of her slaves, the Prophet advised giving the slave to an uncle among the Bedouin instead, for a greater reward.

narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that when the verse on giving the relative his due was revealed, the Prophet told Faatima she could have his land at Fidak.

narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports a man who complained that his relatives cut ties with him, and the Prophet told him that an angel stays with him as long as he keeps treating them well.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) narrates that a man came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I have relatives who severe ties, with me when I attempt to foster them,…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports a man who complained that his relatives cut ties with him, and the Prophet told him to take the better course and keep up the bonds of kinship.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat A'mash narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) was sitting in a gathering after the Fajr salaah when he said, "In the name of Allaah do I ask those who…
narrations.summary: A'mash reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood asked those who sever family ties to leave a gathering before he made du'aa, since the doors of heaven are closed to them.

narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Hishaam reports that when he asked Aa'isha about the Prophet's character, she replied that his character was the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration mentions that Hadhrat Qataadah (RA) said, "Indeed the Qur'aan brought every noble trait of good character."
narrations.summary: Qataadah says the Qur'aan brought every noble trait, and Abu Dardaa reports that Aa'isha described the Prophet's character as the Qur'aan, being pleased with what Allaah is pleased with.

narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa asked Aa'isha about the Prophet's character, and she said his character was the Qur'aan: he was pleased with what Allaah is pleased with and disliked what Allaah dislikes.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Zaid bin Baabnoos states that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) gave a similar reply when they asked her about the character of Rasulullaah ﷺ, This…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Baabnoos reports that when people asked Aa'isha about the Prophet's character, she told them to read from Surah Mu'minoon and said that was his character.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) reports that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) stated, "There was none with better character than Rasulullaah ﷺ. Whenever any of his companions or family called for him,…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says there was none with better character than the Prophet, and the report goes on to a garbled account of his dealings with the Jews of Khaybar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaarijah bin Zaid narrates that a group of people once came to his father Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) with the request, "Tell us something about the character…
narrations.summary: Khaarijah bin Zaid reports that Zaid bin Thaabit described how the Prophet joined in every kind of conversation with his companions, whether about worldly matters, the Aakhirah or food.

narrations.summary: Safiyya bint Huyay says she never saw anyone with better character than the Prophet, recalling how he gently woke her on the journey back from Khaybar and later explained what he had been forced to do to the Jews of Khaybar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was one of the most compassionate people. I swear by Allaah that he never refused even a slave or a child who brought water to him…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet was the most compassionate of people, never refusing a slave or child who brought him water, listening patiently to requests, and never withdrawing his hand before the other person did.

narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that the slaves of Madinah brought water to the Prophet after Fajr, and he dipped his hands into every vessel for blessing, even on very cold mornings.

narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet never withdrew his hand or turned away from a person until that person did, and never moved his head from one whispering to him until the person moved away.

narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah and Anas describe how the Prophet never withdrew his hand from anyone who took it, even a child of Madinah, and gave his full attention to whoever spoke to him.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that even the slaves girls of Madinah could take Rasulullaah ﷺ by the hand and take him wherever she needed him to go."
narrations.summary: Another narration says that even the slave girls of Madinah could take the Prophet by the hand and lead him wherever they needed him to go.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a lady who was mentally deranged once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ ! I need you to do something for me." Addressing her…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that a woman with a mental illness asked the Prophet for help, and he stepped aside with her into a street to hear her problem.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslamah (RA) says, "When I once returned from a journey, Rasulullaah ﷺ took me by the hand and did not leave if until I let go of his hand."
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Maslamah says that when he returned from a journey, the Prophet took him by the hand and did not let go until he did.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ was faced with two options, he always chose the easier of the two (so that it would be easy for the Ummah to emulate)…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet always chose the easier of two options when it involved no sin, and that he took revenge only for the sake of Allaah.

narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet never struck a servant or a woman, always took the easier option when it involved no sin, and punished only when Allaah's prohibitions were violated.

narrations.summary: Anas says the Prophet never cursed people or was rude, and that the strongest thing he said when scolding was 'May sand fall on his forehead'.

narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that the Prophet was never rude or vulgar, and said the best of people is the one with the best character.

narrations.summary: Saalim and Zuhri report that Abdullaah bin Umar never cursed a slave, and that he once stopped himself partway through a curse.

narrations.summary: After Hunayn the Prophet gave extra booty to Aqra bin Haabis and Uyaynah bin Hisn, and when Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reported a complaint about it, the Prophet pointed to Musa's patience under abuse and asked who would be just if Allaah and His Rasool were not.

narrations.summary: A narration says the Prophet had the body of Abdullaah bin Ubay taken out of the grave and shrouded it with his own garment.

narrations.summary: Zaid bin Arqam reports that the Prophet was ill for days from a Jew's spell, and that he never mentioned it to the Jew or showed anger.

narrations.summary: Aa'isha relates how the Prophet came to believe he had been with his wives when he had not, because of a spell, and how the location of the spell was revealed in a dream and he chose not to publicise it.

narrations.summary: Aa'isha adds that for six months the Prophet believed he had been with his wives when he had not, because of witchcraft, and that two angels then came to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a Jewish woman once gave Rasulullaah ﷺ a poisoned goat meat, which he ate from. When the woman was later bi ought before Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Anas and Abu Hurayrah report that a Jewish woman poisoned goat meat for the Prophet, and that he questioned her and did not punish her.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that a Jewish woman once presented some goat meat to Rasulullaah ﷺ which was poisoned. "Hang on," Rasulullaah cautioned the Sahabah…
narrations.summary: A Jewish woman served the Prophet poisoned goat meat to test whether he was a true Rasul; he warned the Companions, questioned her, and took no action against her.

narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that the Prophet had cupping done whenever he felt the effect of the poison, including once while about to enter ihraam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that a Jewish woman from Khaybar once poisoned some ruasted goat meat and presented it to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah took a foreleg of the…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports the poisoned roast goat, the woman's confession and the Prophet's forgiveness, and other reports say the Prophet had cupping done and that the woman was later executed.

narrations.summary: Marwaan bin Uthmaan reports that on his deathbed the Prophet told Ummu Bishr he could feel the poison from the meal he had eaten with her brother Bishr at Khaybar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ja'da bin Khaalid bin Simmah Jushami narrates that Rasulullaah once saw a man with a large belly and pointed towards the man's belly. Hadhrat Ja'da (RA) then…
narrations.summary: Ja'da bin Khaalid reports that the Prophet rebuked a large-bellied man for overeating, and that when told of an assassination plot he said nothing could harm him without Allaah's permission.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that during the time when the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was being concluded, eighty armed men from Makkah approached from Mount Tan'eem with the…
narrations.summary: Anas and Abdullaah bin Mughaffal report the Makkan ambush of eighty and then thirty men during the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, how the Prophet's prayer captured or blinded them, his forgiveness, and the revealed verse.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Tufayl bin Amr (RA) of the Daus tribe once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "The Daus tribe are disobedient and refuse to…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that Tufayl bin Amr asked the Prophet to curse the Daus tribe, and that the Prophet instead prayed for their guidance.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Za'raa (RA) reports that Hadhrat Ali bin Abu Taalib (RA) used to say, "My pure wives, pious progeny and myself have been the most tolerant people in youth and…
narrations.summary: Abu Za'raa reports Ali's statement that he, his pure wives and his pious progeny had been the most tolerant in youth and the most learned as adults, and Sa'd's praise of Ibn Abbaas for his knowledge and tolerance.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "I sometimes commence the salaah with the intention of lengthening it when I hear the cries of a child and then…

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that a man once asked Rasulullaah ﷺ, "where is my father (who died as a Mushrik)?" "In the fire (of Jahannam)," came the reply. When…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that when a man asked about his father, who died as a mushrik, the Prophet said he was in the fire and then consoled the man by saying his own father was there too.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that a Bedouin once came to Rasulullaah to seek assistance in paying some blood money. After giving him a handsome sum, Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when a Bedouin was rude about the gift he had received, the Prophet answered patiently and kindly, and told the Bedouin's story as a parable about a camel.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asma'ee reports that (when Hadhrat Umar (RA) became the Ameerul Mu'mineen) the people requested Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) to speak to Hadhrat Umar SSI to…
narrations.summary: Asma'ee reports that people asked Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf to ask Umar to be gentle with them, and Umar replied that his compassion for them would surprise them if they knew it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was more modest than a virgin in her own secluded quarters." Another narration adds that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri says the Prophet was more modest than a virgin in her private chamber, and that his dislike showed on his face.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas Hajggi reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Modesty is goodness through and through." Rasulullaah ﷺ Dislikes Telling People what would Displease them Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Anas reports the Prophet's saying that modesty is goodness, and his words to Aa'isha that he should be shy before one before whom even the angels are shy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Whenever the news reached Rasulullaah ﷺ that someone had said something, he would never say, "What is the matter with that person to say...?'…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says that when news reached the Prophet of something someone had said, he never named that person, but spoke of people in general.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "I have never seen the private parts of Rasulullaah iii." The Modesty of the Sahabah (RA).
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says she never saw the private parts of the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Al Aas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ's wife Hadhrat Aa'isha and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) both reported to him that Hadhrat Abu Bakr once sought…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Al Aas reports that the Prophet let Abu Bakr and Umar in as he lay covered, but sat up and covered himself for the bashful Uthmaan, and explains why when Aa'isha asks.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once sitting with Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) behind him when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) sought permission to enter and…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that while the Prophet sat with Aa'isha, Abu Bakr, Umar and others entered, and that he covered his knees when Uthmaan asked to enter because the angels are shy before Uthmaan.

narrations.excerpt: Abu Bakr Speaking about the extreme modesty of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), Hadhrat Hasan says, "Even though he was In a room behind a locked door, he would not remove his…
narrations.summary: Hasan describes the extreme modesty of Uthmaan, who would bathe seated and not stand up straight even behind a locked door.
