narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Be modest in front of All "ah. I cover my head out of modesty before Al'iah even when I enter the toilet."…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports Abu Bakr's saying that he covers his head out of modesty before Allaah, even when entering the toilet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mas'ood (RA) and Hadhrat Umaarah bin Ghuraab Yahsubi both narrate that Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) qnce came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Mas'ood and Umaarah report that Uthmaan bin Madh'oon did not want his wife to see his private parts, and that the Prophet told him the spouses are each other's garments.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Mijlaz reports that Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) said, "I bath in a dark room and do not stand up straight until I have picked up my clothes. This I do out…
narrations.summary: Abu Mijlaz, Abu Qataadah and Anas report Abu Moosa Ash'ari's extreme modesty, including bathing in a dark room, bending over to get his clothes, and sleeping in clothing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Nusay reports that Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) once saw some people standing in water without their lower garments. To this, he exclaimed, "I…
narrations.summary: Ubaadah bin Nusay reports that Abu Moosa Ash'ari said he would rather die and be raised again many times than do what people in the water were doing without their lower garments.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ashaj Abdul Qais (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to him, "You have two qualities that Allaah loves." When he asked what they were, Rasulullaah ﷺ said,…
narrations.summary: Ashaj Abdul Qais reports that the Prophet told him that tolerance and modesty are two qualities Allaah loves, and that these were naturally instilled in him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) was once sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ when he looked towards the sky. An angel suddenly descended to which…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that an angel came to the Prophet offering him the choice of being a king-prophet or a slave-messenger, and that the Prophet chose to be a humble slave-messenger.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) adds at the end, "After this, Rasulullaah ﷺ never ate in a reclining position and would say, 'I eat as a slave eats, and sit…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet never ate reclining and said he ate as a slave eats and sat as a slave sits.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ghaalib says that he once asked Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) to narrate to them a Hadith that he had heard from Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Abu Umaamah replied,…
narrations.summary: Abu Ghaalib asked Abu Umaamah for a Hadith, and Abu Umaamah described the Prophet's dhikr, brief talks, long salaah and humility.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ made Dhikr in abundance, never engaged in futilities, rode a camel, wore woollen clothing and even accepted the invitations of…
narrations.summary: Anas describes the Prophet's dhikr, plain clothing and riding, his acceptance of slaves' invitations, and his donkey at Khaybar.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ also visited the ill and attended funerals.
narrations.summary: An added narration says the Prophet also visited the sick and attended funerals.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to ride a donkey, wear woollen clothes, hold down a goat and milk it and personally serve guests."
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari says the Prophet rode a donkey, wore woollen clothes, milked a goat himself and served guests personally.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ would sit on the floor, eat on the floor, hold down a goat himself while milking it and even accept the invitation…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas says the Prophet sat and ate on the floor, milked a goat himself and accepted a slave's invitation to barley bread; another report adds that he accepted such an invitation in the middle of the night from a man of the upper part of Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ would accept an invitation even if it were to eat barley bread and foul-smelling fat. Rasulullaah ﷺ also had a suit of armour…
narrations.summary: Anas says the Prophet accepted even plain food, and pawned his armour to a Jew, dying without the money to redeem it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) says that when a man called for Rasulullaah ﷺ three times, Rasulullaah ﷺ replied with the word "Labbaik" ('At your service') each time.
narrations.summary: Umar says that each of the three times a man called the Prophet, he answered 'Labbaik'.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah Silg narrates that (during the time of Rasulullaah IS there was an immoral woman who was flirtatious with the men. She once passed by rasulullaah il…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah reports that when an immoral woman mocked the Prophet for eating like a slave, he gave her food from his own hand and mouth, and afterwards she never again flirted with a man.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jareer (RA) reports that when a man once came before Rasulullaah he started to shiver. Rasulullaah ﷺ put him at ease saying, "Take it easy. I am not a king but…
narrations.summary: Jareer says the Prophet calmed a man who was trembling before him, telling him he was no king but the son of a Quraysh woman who ate dried meat.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) states that it was on the day the Muslims conquered Makkah that a man started shivering while talking to…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood reports the same calming of a trembling man on the day Makkah was conquered, and Aamir bin Rabee'ah says the Prophet took his shoe and would not let him fix its strap, disliking preferential treatment.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Jubayr Khuzaa'ee (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once walking with his companions when someone shaded him with a sheet. When he saw the shadow,…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Jubayr says someone shaded the Prophet with a sheet, and he took it down, saying he was only a human being like them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) said, "I once said to myself, 'I wonder how long Rasulullaah ﷺ will still remain amongst us. (To…
narrations.summary: Abbaas wonders how long the Prophet will remain with them and asks why he has no raised platform; the Prophet says he prefers to stay among the people.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration from Hadhrat ikramah (RA), Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) says, "I shall definitely find out how long Rasulullaah ﷺ will still be staying amongst us. I then…
narrations.summary: Ikramah reports Abbaas asking about the platform again, and concluding from the reply that the Prophet would be with them only a short while.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aswad reports that he once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "What would Rasulullaah ﷺ do when he entered the house?" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) replied, "He would engage…
narrations.summary: Aswad asks Aa'isha what the Prophet did on entering the house, and she says he did household chores and went to salaah when the time came.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa SSI narrates that someone once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "Would Rasulullaah ﷺ carry out domestic chores at home?" "Certainly," she replied, "He would mend…
narrations.summary: Urwa and Amrah each report asking Aa'isha whether the Prophet did household chores, and she said he mended his shoes and clothes and milked his goat himself.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ never assigned to anyone the duty of making arrangements for his wudhu and also the duty of handing out the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says the Prophet never gave anyone the job of preparing his wudu or distributing his charity, and attended to both himself.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ came to visit me, he was neither riding a mule nor a thoroughbred horse."
narrations.summary: Jaabir says that when the Prophet came to visit him, he rode neither a mule nor a thoroughbred horse.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ performed on an old carriage (atop his camel) which was covered in a sheet that was hardly worth four Dirhams. Despite this, he…
narrations.summary: Anas says the Prophet performed Hajj on an old carriage under a sheet worth about four Dirhams, and prayed for a Hajj free of show and boasting.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ffli? entered Makkah (upon the Conquest of Makkah) and the people were crowding to have a look at him, he placed his head…
narrations.summary: Anas says that when the Prophet entered Makkah at the conquest, he lowered his head onto his carriage out of humility.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Rasulullaah ﷺ reached Dhu Tuwa, he stood on his carriage. He wore his reddish, striped Yemeni shawl around his head with its end…
narrations.summary: An unnamed narrator says that at Dhu Tuwa the Prophet stood on his carriage and lowered his head in gratitude to Allaah until his beard touched the middle of the carriage.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports, "I once entered the marketplace with Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ sat with some cloth merchants and bought a trouser for four Dirhams.…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah says the Prophet bought trousers in the market and carried them himself, told the measurer to give the buyer the benefit, and pulled his hand away from a man who tried to kiss it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) arrived in Shaam riding a camel, the people started talking amongst themselves (that he should have rather chosen a good…
narrations.summary: Aslam reports that when Umar rode a camel into Shaam, he rebuked people who looked at the mounts of unbelievers instead of those used by the Prophet and the Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hishaam narrates that he once saw Hadhrat Umar (RA) pass by a woman who was busy making Aseedah (a paste made from flour and clarified butter). "That is not how…
narrations.summary: Hishaam says he saw Umar stop a woman making aseedah and show her how to make it with a wooden spoon.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hishaam bin Khaalid says that he heard Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab say (as he taught some women to make Aseedah), "You should never add the flour until the water is…
narrations.summary: Hishaam bin Khaalid says he heard Umar teach women to add flour only once the water is hot, stirring gradually to avoid lumps.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat zirr says that he saw Hadhrat Umar (RA) proceed barefoot for the Eid salaah.
narrations.summary: Zirr says he saw Umar walk barefoot to the Eid salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar Makhzoomi reports that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) once made an announcement for the people to gather in the Masjid. The people got together and when a…
narrations.summary: Umar Makhzoomi reports Umar's sermon recalling how he herded for his Banu Makhzoom aunts for a few dates; Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf criticised it, and Umar said he had felt pride and wished to humble himself.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) added, "O people! 1 have seen the time when I had no source of livelihood apart from a few handfuls of raisins that my…
narrations.summary: Umar says he once had no source of livelihood apart from a few handfuls of raisins given to him for carrying water, and that he told this to humble himself after feeling pride.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) once left home on an extremely hot day with a shawl thrown over his head. When a young boy passed by riding a…
narrations.summary: Hasan says that Umar, walking out on a hot day, asked a boy on a donkey for a ride and then rode behind him into Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) says, "I once went out with some other boys to pick up dates (that had fallen to the ground). Hadhrat Umar (RA) suddenly appeared with a lash in his hand and…
narrations.summary: A boy recounts that Umar, with a lash, sent other boys scattering from the fallen dates, did not hit him when he saw the dates in his garment, and walked him home.

narrations.excerpt: The grandfather of Hadhrat Maalik say that he saw Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) when they arrived from Makkah and camped at a place called Mu'arras (Dhul…
narrations.summary: Maalik's grandfather says he saw Umar and Uthmaan each carry a youngster on the ride into Madinah; the narrator explains this as humility and benefit to others, and criticises rulers who make youths walk behind them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maymoon bin Mahraan reports from a man from Hamdaan that he saw Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) riding a mule with his slave Naa'il riding behind him on the same animal.…
narrations.summary: Maymoon bin Mahraan says he saw Uthmaan, while Khalifah, ride a mule with his slave Naa'il riding behind him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah Roomi says that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) himself fetched the water he needed for performing wudhu during the night. When someone suggested that he get one…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah Roomi says Uthmaan drew his own water for night wudu and never woke his household for Tahajjud; the grandmother of Zubayr bin Abdullaah, once his servant, adds that he fasted constantly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan says, "I saw Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) sleeping in the Masjid covered in a shawl. Although he was then the Ameerul Mu'mineen, there was none around him."
narrations.summary: Hasan says he saw Uthmaan sleeping in the Masjid under a shawl with no one around him, though he was then Ameerul Mu'mineen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Unaysa says, "The little girls of the locality would take their goats to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) (for milking). (Not only would he do it for them but) He would also…
narrations.summary: Unaysa says Abu Bakr milked goats for the girls of the locality, and kept doing so after he became Khalifah, asking them how they wanted the milk.

narrations.excerpt: The blanket merchant Hadhrat Saalih reports from his grandfather who says, "I saw (Ameerul Mu'mineen) Hadhrat Ali (RA) purchase dates for a Dirham and then carry them in…
narrations.summary: Saalih, a blanket merchant, reports that his grandfather saw Ali buy dates for a Dirham and refuse help to carry them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaadhaan reports that even as Ameerul Mu'mineen, Hadhrat Ali (RA) used to walk alone in the marketplace where he would guide lost people, announce lost items and…
narrations.summary: Zaadhaan reports that Ali walked the market guiding lost people, announcing lost items and helping the weak, and recited a verse about the Hereafter, saying it was revealed about just and humble rulers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jurmooz narrates that he saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) emerge from his house wearing two reddish cloths made in Qatar, a lower garment that reached halfway up his calves…
narrations.summary: Jurmooz saw Ali leave his house in two reddish cloths, walk the market with a lash, and urge traders to fear Allaah, deal amiably and give full weight and measure.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Matar says, "I was once leaving the Masjid when I suddenly heard someone behind me shouting, 'Lift your lower garment because it shows greater wariness of…
narrations.summary: Abu Matar recounts Ali's episodes in the market: he warned against oaths in trade, made a date seller take back dates sold to a servant, banned dead fish, and refused a refund a cloth merchant's father tried to give him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa reports that when Rasulullaah iffil's daughter Hadhrat Faatima kneaded dough, her plaits would hit against the bowl. Referring to Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA),…
narrations.summary: Ataa reports that Faatima's plaits hit the bowl as she kneaded dough, and Mutallib bin Abdullaah says Ummu Salamah, who had married the Prophet that evening, was grinding flour later that night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salaamah Ajali says, "One of my cousins from the countryside whose name was Qudaamah came to me with the request, 'I wish to meet Salmaan Faarsi and greet him. We…
narrations.summary: Salaamah Ajali says he and his cousin Qudaamah went to see Salmaan Faarsi, and found him weaving palm baskets while in command of twenty thousand men; Salmaan prayed that Allaah love the cousin.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haarith bin Umayrah reports, "I once went to Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) and found him in his tannery scraping off some hide with his hands. When I greeted him with…
narrations.summary: Haarith bin Umayrah recounts visiting Salmaan Faarsi, who was scraping hide in his tannery, and Salmaan says that souls who came together for Allaah's pleasure become friends.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Qilaabah narrates that someone once came to Hadhrat Salmaan as he was busy making dough. "What is this?" the man said in surprise. Hadhrat Salmaan (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abu Qilaabah reports that Salmaan Faarsi, while making dough himself, received a man who had come to pass on greetings from someone else, and told him that the greeting was a trust that would have been left unfulfilled.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr the son of Abu Qurra Kindi says that his father once offered his sister in marriage to Hadhrat Salmaan (RA). However, Hadhrat Salmaan refused the offer and…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Abu Qurra Kindi reports that his father offered his sister in marriage to Salmaan Faarsi, who refused and married a freed slave woman; when Abu Qurra went to Salmaan after an argument with Hudhayfah, Salmaan received him in very simple surroundings.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maymoon bin Mahraan reports that a man from the Abdul Qais tribe once saw Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) riding a donkey as commander of an army. He wore trousers, the legs…
narrations.summary: Three reports on Salmaan Faarsi's humility as a commander and governor: soldiers mocked him as he rode a donkey, the people of Madaa'in called him Gurg Aamad, and a witness saw him in short, shabby clothes; he said good and bad will be seen only in the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thaabit reports that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) was the governor of Madaa'in when a man arrived from Shaam carrying figs. Because Hadhrat Salmaan was wearing his simple…
narrations.summary: Thaabit reports that while Salmaan Faarsi was governor of Madaa'in he carried a stranger's load of figs to the man's house, saying he had intended to do it to please Allaah and could not put it down before he arrived.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Buraydah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) used to make things with his hands and when he earned some money by selling them, he would purchase…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Buraydah reports that Salmaan Faarsi made things with his hands, sold them, and used the money to buy meat or fish to share with lepers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen reports that whenever Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab appointed a governor, he would write in the letter of appointment (the following instruction…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports that whenever Umar bin Khattaab appointed a governor he would write that the governor should greet first, be content with a lower seat, and dislike ostentation and boasting.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Seereen narrates, "When Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) arrived in Madaa'in, he arrived riding atop a carriage mounted on his donkey. He was eating a piece of bread…
narrations.summary: Ibn Seereen reports that Hudhayfah arrived at Madaa'in riding on a carriage on his donkey and eating bread with meat, and Talha bin Musarrif adds that his legs hung down by the donkey's side.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sulaym bin Abu Hudhayl says, "1 mended clothes by the door of Hadhrat Jareer bin Abdullaah Siffisg, Whenever he came out of his house and mounted his mule, he…
narrations.summary: Sulaym bin Abu Hudhayl says that when Jareer bin Abdullaah left his house and mounted his mule, he took his slave up behind him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) was once passing through the marketplace carrying a bundle of wood when someone said to him, "What makes you do this when Allaah has…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Salaam carries a bundle of wood through the marketplace to guard against pride, quoting the Prophet that someone with even an atom of pride will not enter Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "Three factors form the core of humility. (These are:) That one is first to greet whoever one meets, that one is content with an inferior…
narrations.summary: Ali says the core of humility is to greet others first, to accept a lower place in a gathering, and to dislike ostentation and boasting.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that the Sahabah (RA) once asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ You manage to joke with us?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "However, I speak only the truth…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Sahabah asked the Prophet whether he joked with them, and he said he joked but spoke only the truth.

narrations.excerpt: A man once asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) whether Rasulullaah used to joke. When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas Wffigfe replied that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to joke,…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas describes a joke of the Prophet with one of his wives, whom he told to wear a large shawl and drag it along like a bride's.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ had the best of character. I had a brother called Abu Umayr who was just weaned off milk. Whenever Rasulullaah came and saw him,…
narrations.summary: Anas describes the Prophet's gentleness with Abu Umayr, a young brother of his, asking after the child's pet bird, and then recounts the Prophet leading prayer on a mat at their home.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Anas (RA) states, "Rasulullaah ﷺ would associate with us so much that he waiald even ask my little brother, 'O Abu Umayr! How is Nughayr?
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet would ask his young brother Abu Umayr how his little bird, Nughayr, was doing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA). narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once visited Hadhrat Abu Talha (Hadhrat Anas (RA)'s step-father) when he noticed, that Hadhrat Abu Talha's son Abu Umayrwas…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that at the home of Abu Talha, the Prophet noticed Abu Umayr looking sad, learned that his bird had died, and affectionately asked how Nughayr was.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a man once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ to ask for transport. Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "we shall give you the child of a camel to ride." "O…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that a man asked the Prophet for transport, and the Prophet offered him a camel's young to ride, then asked whether every camel is not the child of another.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once jokingly called Hadhrat Anas saying, "O two-eared one!"
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet affectionately teased him by calling him 'O two-eared one'.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a man from the countryside called Zaahir used to give Rasulullaah ﷺ things from the countryside and when he left, Rasulullaah ﷺ would give…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet loved Zaahir, a countryman who brought him gifts, joked with him in the market, and told him that he was precious in Allaah's sight.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Basheer (RA) -narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr was once about to ask permission to enter Rasulullaah fife's room, he heard (his daughter) Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer reports that Abu Bakr, finding his daughter Aa'isha raising her voice before the Prophet, moved to slap her and was stopped by the Prophet; when Abu Bakr later found them reconciled he joked that they should let him into their peace as they had let him into their war, and the Prophet agreed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports, "I once accompanied Rasulullaah ﷺ on one of his journeys when I was still a slim girl who had not put on much weight. Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha recounts how she beat the Prophet in a race when she was slim, and he beat her in a later race when she had gained weight, saying 'This is for that'; Anas and Abu Qilaabah report him telling the camel-driver Anjasha to go easy with the women.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Anas (RA) says that Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym was with the wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ (on a journey) when Rasulullaah came to them. (Noticing that the…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet, seeing the camel-driver Anjasha hurrying the camels while Umm Sulaym and the wives were travelling with him, told him to go easy with the crystals, and Abu Qilaabah gives a similar remark.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that an old woman once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ with the request, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Pray to Allaah to enter me into Jannah." Addressing her by her…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that an old woman asked the Prophet to pray that she enter Jannah; he told her old women will not enter it, and then sent word, citing the verse that Allaah created the women of Jannah especially.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat AwfbinMaalikAshja'ee (RA) reports, "I went to Rasulullaah ﷺ during the expedition to Tabook while he was in a (very small) leather tent. I greeted Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Awf bin Maalik Ashja'ee reports that during the Tabook expedition he jokingly asked the Prophet 'All of me?' when he was let into a very small tent, and Waleed explains the joke.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Abu Mulaykah (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) only cracked a few jokes with Rasulullaah ﷺ, her mother said, "O Rasulullaah Many of our tribe's…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha joked with the Prophet ﷺ, and her mother's remark about the Kinaana tribe drew his reply that they are the subject of many of the Muslims' jokes.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Haytham reports from someone that he heard Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan bin Harb joking with Rasulullaah ﷺ in the house of his daughter Hadhrat Ummu Habeebah (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abu Sufyaan joked with the Prophet ﷺ in the house of his daughter Ummu Habeebah, and the Prophet smiled at his remark.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Bakr bin Abdullaah says, "Although the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah used to (playfully) throw melons at each other, they were still the most resolute men when…
narrations.summary: Bakr bin Abdullaah says the Sahabah played together, throwing melons, yet were the most resolute men when matters were serious.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qurra narrates that he once said to Hadhrat ibn Seereen, "Did the Sahabah (RA) joke and play?" Hadhrat Ibn Seereen replied, "They were just like other people, in…
narrations.summary: Qurra asked Ibn Seereen whether the Sahabah joked, and Ibn Seereen said they did, quoting Abdullaah bin Umar's couplet said in jest.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once went on a trade journey to Busra. Accompanying him were Hadhrat Nu'aymaan and Hadhrat Suwaybit bin…
narrations.summary: Umm Salamah reports that Abu Bakr sent Nu'aymaan and Suwaybit bin Harmala on a trade journey, where Nu'aymaan tricked Suwaybit into being taken as a slave; Abu Bakr returned the ten camels paid for him and freed him, and the Prophet laughed about it for a year.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rabee'ah bin Uthmaan (RA) narrates that a Bedouin once came to see Rasulullaah ﷺ and put his camel to sit in the courtyard of the Masjid. Some of the Sahabah (RA)…
narrations.summary: Rabee'ah bin Uthmaan reports that Nu'aymaan bin Amr Ansaari, urged by some Sahabah, slaughtered a Bedouin's camel to eat it; when the Prophet found Nu'aymaan hiding in a house, Nu'aymaan blamed the Sahabah, and the Prophet compensated the Bedouin.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mus'ab (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Makhramah bin Naufal bin Uhayb Zuhri was an extremely old blind man in Madinah who had already reached the age of…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mus'ab reports that Makhramah bin Naufal, an old blind man, was led by Nu'aymaan to urinate in a corner of the Masjid; afterwards, on Nu'aymaan's word, Makhramah struck Uthmaan, who was praying, and Uthmaan forgave Nu'aymaan because he was a Badr veteran.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was the most generous of people. He was even more generous on Ramadhaan when he met Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) every…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says the Prophet was the most generous of people, most of all in Ramadhaan when he met Jibra'eel every night, and more generous than the blowing wind.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ never said 'No' to anything asked ofhim." In a lengthy Hadith from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr, Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed says,…
narrations.summary: Jaabir, and Abu Sa'eed citing a longer hadith from Abdullaah bin Abi Bakr, each say that the Prophet never refused anything he was asked for.

narrations.excerpt: In another lengthy narration, Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "When asked to do something, Rasulullaah ﷺ always said Yes' when he intended doing it and would remain silent when he…
narrations.summary: Ali reports that when asked for something, the Prophet said yes when he intended to do it and stayed silent when he did not, but never said no.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rubayyi bint Mu'awwidh bin Afraa (RA) says, "(My father) Hadhrat Mu'awwidh bin Afraa sent me to Rasulullaah ﷺ with a Saa of fresh dates topped with slices of…
narrations.summary: Rubayyi bint Mu'awwidh reports that her father sent a Saa of fresh dates with cucumber to the Prophet, who in return filled her hand with jewels that had just come from Bahrain.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA) reports that a woman once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "I want to give this garment to the most generous of all Arabs," Pointing to…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that a woman brought a garment for the most generous of the Arabs, and the Prophet directed it to Sa'eed bin Al Aas, after which such garments were called Sa'eediyyah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "There passed a time when (we had so much concern for each other that) none of us (Sahabah (RA) thought himself more than his fellow…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says there was a time when the Muslims thought of each other above themselves, but now people love dinars and dirhams more than their brothers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports that he once visited Rasulullaah ﷺ when Rasulullaah ﷺ was suffering extreme fever and was. covered in a blanket. Placing his hand…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports visiting the Prophet during a high fever and being told that the prophets suffer most, then the scholars, then the pious; Abu Ubaydah bin Hudhayfah reports, from his aunt Faatimah, that the Prophet lay under a dripping water bag in his fever and said the closest to the prophets suffer most.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was once overcome with pain, he was in great suffering and turned from side to side on his bed. Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet, in great pain, turned from side to side on his bed, and told her that every thorn or pain a believer suffers forgives a sin and raises his rank.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that fever (in the human form Allaah had granted it) once sought permission to see Rasulullaah ﷺ. "Who is it?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "Ummu…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that fever asked permission to visit the Prophet and was sent to the people of Quba; when they complained, he offered to pray it away or let it stay as a purification from sin, and they chose to keep it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) narrates that when fever once sought permission to see Rasulullaah ﷺ, '-he asked who it was. It replied, "I am fever. I peel at flesh and suck…
narrations.summary: Salmaan reports that the Prophet sent fever to the people of Quba, who chose to keep it as a means of forgiveness; Abu Hurayrah reports that fever went to the Ansaar, the Prophet prayed and they were cured, and a woman of the Ansaar chose patience and Jannah over a cure.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once did not notice someone who regularly attended his gatherings. When Rasulullaah ﷺ asked what the matter was that the…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that when a regular attendee at the Prophet's gatherings was struck down by a high fever, the Prophet visited him and told him that fever is his Ummah's share of Jahannam in this world.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Safar reports that when some people came to visit Hadhrat Abu Bakr during his illness, they said, "O Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ Should we not summon a…
narrations.summary: Abu Safar reports that when people visited Abu Bakr during his illness and asked whether they should summon a physician, Abu Bakr said the physician had already seen him and that Allaah does as He pleases.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Qurra Sfilg narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Dardaa fell ill, his friends came to visit him. "what is the problem?" they asked. "My sins," he replied.…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Qurra reports that when friends visited Abu Dardaa in illness, he said his sickness was for his sins and that he wished for Jannah, and when they offered to summon a physician he said that it was Allaah who had laid him there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Ghanam reports that when the plague struck Shaam, Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) announced, "This plague is a punishment, so flee from it to the…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Ghanam reports that when the plague struck Shaam, Amr bin Al Aas told people to flee it and Shurahbeel bin Hasanah rejected that; Mu'aadh bin Jabal prayed for his family's full share of the plague, lost two daughters and then his son Abdur Rahmaan, was himself struck, and advised a weeping man to seek knowledge from four men.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shahr bin Howshab reports from a man from his tribe called Raaba that when the plague started to spread, Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin jarraah (RA) addressed the people…
narrations.summary: Shahr bin Howshab, reporting from Raaba, says that when the plague spread Abu Ubaydah prayed for his family's share and then died of it; Mu'aadh bin Jabal, after taking command, also lost his son and was struck himself; Amr bin Al Aas then told people to flee to the mountains, Abu Waathilah rebuked him, and Umar, hearing the matter, said Amr had not condemned it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Qilaabah narrates that when the plague struck Shaam, Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas said, "This is a scourge that has come so flee from it to the mountains and…
narrations.summary: Abu Qilaabah reports Mu'aadh bin Jabal's reply to Amr bin Al Aas, that the plague is martyrdom, a mercy and the Prophet's du'aa, and explains the du'aa: the Prophet asked that his Ummah not perish by drought, be overrun by an enemy, or split into factions; the last was refused, so he said 'let it be fever or a plague'.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uxwa bin Zubayr (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah and his family were unaffected by the plague of Amwaas when he prayed to Allaah saying, "O…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports that Abu Ubaydah and his family were spared the plague until a sore appeared on his little finger, and that he hoped Allaah would bless it, since Allaah makes a little thing much.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haarith bin Abu Umayrah Haarithi narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal sent him to ask Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) how he was when the plague struck him. Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Haarith bin Abu Umayrah Haarithi reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal sent him to ask Abu Ubaydah how he was in the plague; Abu Ubaydah showed him a plague sore on his palm and swore he would not trade it even for red camels.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) says, "When I developed a cataract, Nabi ﷺ came to visit me. He asked, Zaid! What would you do if you lost your eye?' 'I shall exercise…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Arqam says that when he developed a cataract the Prophet visited him and told him that if he lost his eye and bore it patiently for Allaah's reward, his reward would be Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that he accompanied Rasululiaah to visit Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) when he was suffering from an eye ailment. Rasululiaah said to him, "O…
narrations.summary: Anas accompanies the Prophet to visit Zaid bin Arqam during an eye ailment, and the Prophet tells Zaid that losing his sight with patience and hope of reward will bring him to Allaah without sin.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) narrates that Rasululiaah once visited him when he was ill. Rasululiaah said, "No harm will come to you from this illness but what will you do…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Arqam relates that the Prophet visited him in illness and told him that if he lost his sight in old age and bore it patiently he would enter Jannah without reckoning.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that after the demise of Rasululiaah, Hadhrat Zaid (RA) did go blind but Allaah restored his eyesight before he passed away. May Allaah shower his…
narrations.summary: A variant report says Zaid bin Arqam went blind after the Prophet's death but Allaah restored his sight before Zaid died.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad narrates that when some people visited a Sahabi SI who had lost his eyesight, he said, "I wanted my sight only to see Rasululiaah SSI However,…
narrations.summary: Qaasim bin Muhammad reports that a blind Companion said he would not want his sight back now that the Prophet has passed away, since he wanted it only to see the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "1 saw (Rasulullaah ﷺ's son) Ibraheem JU) surrendering his soul in front of Rasulullaah ﷺ. With his eyes filled with tears, Rasulullaah said,…
narrations.summary: Anas saw the Prophet weep as his son Ibraheem died; Makhool reports Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf asking why he wept, and the Prophet explained that tears of mercy are natural but wailing and praising the dead are not.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Usaamah bin Zaid (RA) narrates that they were with Rasulullaah ﷺ one day when one of his daughters sent for him with the message that her son was dying.…
narrations.summary: Usaama bin Zaid relates that when the Prophet's grandson was dying, the Prophet went with several Companions, and seeing the child's last moments he wept and explained that Allaah places mercy in the hearts of His servants.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that as Rasulullaah ﷺ stood by the body of Hadhrat Hamzah bin Abdul Muttalib (RA) when he was martyred, the sight was more painful than…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah and Ibn Abbaas report the Prophet's grief at the mutilated body of his uncle Hamza after Uhud, his vow to mutilate in return, the revelation of Surah Nahl verse 126 counselling patience over revenge, and his funeral prayer for Hamza and the other martyrs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Usaamah bin Zaid (RA) says, "When my father (Hadhrat Zaid bin Haaritha was martyred, I went to see Rasulullaah ﷺ. When he saw me, Rasulullaah ﷺ started weeping.…
narrations.summary: Usaama bin Zaid relates that the Prophet wept when Usaama came to him after the martyrdom of Usaama's father Zaid bin Haaritha, and Khaalid bin Shumayr reports that the Prophet wept again when Zaid's daughter cried, calling it the longing a friend has for his friend.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ kissed Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon after his demise, his eyes were flowing with tears.
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet's eyes filled with tears when he kissed Uthmaan bin Madh'oon after his death, and said the reason was that he had been killed by the People of the Book.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Haaritha bin Suraaqa (RA) was killed during the Battle of Badr. Although he was a non-combatant, he was killed by a stray arrow.…
narrations.summary: Haaritha bin Suraaqa was killed by a stray arrow at Badr, and his mother vowed patience if he was in Jannah; the Prophet ﷺ told her of Firdous, the highest level.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that she said, "I shall exercise patience if he is Jannah. If not, I shall exert myself in oying." "O Ummu Haaritha!" Rasulullaah ﷺ consoled her,…
narrations.summary: Ummu Haaritha says she will be patient if her son is in Jannah, and the Prophet tells her there are many levels of Jannah and her son is in Firdous, the highest.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Anas (RA) states that Hadhrat Ummu Haaritha said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ if he is in Jannah, I shall not weep and will not be grieved. However,…
narrations.summary: In another narration from Anas, Ummu Haaritha says she will not grieve if her son is in Jannah, and the Prophet ﷺ tells her Haarith is in Firdous, so she rejoices.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Thaabit bin Qais bin Shammaas narrates that when the Muslims fought the (Jewish) Banu Qurayzah tribe, a man from the Ansaar called Khallaad was…
narrations.summary: When Khallaad was martyred at Banu Qurayzah, his mother went to receive his body in her veil, saying she had lost Khallaad but not her modesty, and the Prophet ﷺ said he has the reward of two martyrs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that (his mother) Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) once came to his father Abu Anas saying, "Today I have come with news that you will dislike." His…
narrations.summary: Anas relates that Ummu Sulaym refused Abu Talha's proposal until he accepted Islaam, which she made her dowry, the Prophet married them on that basis, and after their son died she bore it patiently, so the Prophet promised them another child.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA)'s son was ill and passed away one day when he was out. When he returned, Hadhrat Abu Talha asked, "How is my son?"…
narrations.summary: Anas relates that Ummu Sulaym did not tell Abu Talha of their son's death until after the night, that the Prophet prayed for a blessing on that night, and that the newborn received tahneek from the Prophet with a date.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) the son of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was struck by an arrow in the battle for Taa'if. (After healing) His…
narrations.summary: Qaasim bin Muhammad relates that Abdullaah, son of Abu Bakr, was struck by an arrow at Taa'if and died when the wound reopened forty days after the Prophet's death, that Abu Bakr bore it with patience, and that he thanked Allaah for his son's martyrdom when he showed the arrow to the Thaqeef delegation and learned who had shot it.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "The good that Allaah grants is indeed vast to both of you."
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr tells two grieving people that the good Allaah grants is vast for both of them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Sa'eed (RA) narrates that whenever a child was born to Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), he would ask for the child while it was still wrapped (after birth). He would…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Sa'eed relates that Uthmaan smelled each newborn while it was still wrapped so that he would feel more love and need more patience if it died, and that Abu Dharr thanked Allaah when told none of his children seemed to survive, since Allaah stores them as treasure for him in the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Zaid bin Khattaab narrates that whenever a calamity befell Hadhrat Umar (RA), he would console himself saying, "When I was struck with…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Abdur Rahmaan relates that Umar bin Khattaab consoled himself with patience after his brother Zaid bin Khattaab's death, and told the man who killed Zaid that he thought of him every time the wind blew.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Hamzah was martyred, (his sister) Hadhrat Safiyyah (RA), unaware of what had happened, came looking for him.…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates that Safiyyah came looking for Hamza after his death, that Ali and Zubayr did not tell her, that the Prophet calmed her with a hand on her chest and a du'aa, and that she accepted it saying 'To Allaah we belong'; the Prophet then prayed the funeral prayer for the martyrs one group at a time, leaving Hamza's body until last.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awaam (RA) narrates, "A woman came running during the Battle of Uhud and would have seen the dead bodies when Rasulullaah ﷺ called out, '(Stop) The…
narrations.summary: Zubayr relates how the Prophet forbade women to see the bodies at Uhud, how his mother Safiyyah insisted on bringing two sheets for Hamza, and how lots were drawn between Hamza and an unnamed Ansaari for the sheets; a second report has Safiyyah bearing the news with patience and the Prophet letting her go to Hamza's body.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) says, "(My husband) Abu Salamah once came to me from Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, 'I have heard from Rasulullaah ﷺ something that gives me great…
narrations.summary: Ummu Salamah relates that her husband Abu Salamah told her of the Prophet's promise that a Muslim who says 'To Allaah we belong' and the calamity du'aa will be given something better, that she recited it at his death, and that the Prophet later proposed marriage to her.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says that they were returning from Hajj or Umrah and were welcomed at Dhul Hulayfah where the children of the Ansaar normally met their families.…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha relates that Usayd bin Hudhayr wept on hearing of his wife's death, and when she asked why, he said the Prophet had said the Arsh shook at the death of Sa'd bin Mu'aadh.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Usayd bin Hudhayr (RA) said, "Have I no right to weep when I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, The pillars of the Arsh shook with the death…
narrations.summary: Usayd bin Hudhayr says he has every right to weep, since he heard the Prophet say that the pillars of the Arsh shook at the death of Sa'd bin Muaadh.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Awn reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) heard about the death of his brother, Hadhrat Utba (RA), he started to weep. When asked what made him…
narrations.summary: Awn relates that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood wept at the news of his brother Utba's death, saying he would rather be left to hope for reward for his patience than die first.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaythama (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood 'received the news of the death of his brother Hadhrat utba (RA), his eyes welled with tears as he…
narrations.summary: Khaytama relates that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood's eyes welled with tears at his brother Utba's death, and he said the weeping was a mercy Allaah placed in the heart.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Saleet (RA) narrates, "I saw Abu Ahmad bin Jahash carrying the funeral bier of (his sister) Zaynab bint Jahash. He was blind and in tears. As…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Saleet relates that Abu Ahmad bin Jahash, who was blind, carried the bier of his sister Zaynab bint Jahash in tears, and when Umar asked him to step aside he said carrying her bier cooled his grief, so Umar told him to hold on tight.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ahnaf bin Qais (RA) says, "I once heard Hadhrat umar (RA) say, 'The Quraysh are leaders and when any of them enter a door, an entire group of people enter with…
narrations.summary: Ahnaf bin Qais relates that after Umar was stabbed he asked Suhayb to lead prayer for three days and had food served, and that the grieving people refused to eat until Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib began, which showed Ahnaf what Umar meant when he said the Quraysh are leaders.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Uyaynah Sftgtg reports thatwhen Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) consoled a person, he said, "There is no calamity when there is patience and no benefit when there is…
narrations.summary: Abu Uyaynah relates that Abu Bakr consoled a bereaved person by saying there is no calamity where there is patience, and that thinking of the loss of the Prophet makes one's own loss seem light.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sufyaan reports that when consoling Hadhrat Ash'ath bin Qais HIS! upon the death of his son, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "It is the right of your family relationship…
narrations.summary: Sufyaan reports that Ali consoled Ash'ath bin Qais on the death of his son, saying that patience is rewarded and that impatience brings sin.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once in Makkah when a woman from the Ansaar came to him saying, "O Rasulullaah There is this wretch…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates that an Ansaari woman who suffered seizures chose to persevere for the reward of meeting Allaah without sin rather than be cured, and that after the Prophet prayed for her she would cling to the Kabah's shroud and the spirit would leave her.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) once said to him, "Should I not show you a woman who shall be amongst the inhabitants of Jannah?" "Please…
narrations.summary: Ataa relates Abdullaah bin Abbaas's account of a black woman with epilepsy who chose patience for Jannah over a cure, asking only that her body not be exposed, which the Prophet prayed for; Ataa adds that she was called Ummu Zufar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mughaffal (RA) narrates that a woman who had been a prostitute during the Period of Ignorance once passed by a man who stretched out his hand…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mughaffal relates that the Prophet told a man who struck his face on a wall after looking at a woman who had been a prostitute that Allaah intends good for him by hastening his punishment in this world; two further reports have Umar saying that anything a believer dislikes is a calamity, over a broken sandal strap and a broken shoe.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam reports that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) once wrote to Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab, informing him that the Romans were launching a massive military offensive and…
narrations.summary: Aslam relates that Abu Ubaydah wrote to Umar about the Romans' massive offensive, and Umar's reply urges steadfastness and patience, quoting the Qur'aanic command to persevere and fear Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) Mahdi says that Hadhrat Uthmaan Sftsfflgi possessed two virtues that neither Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) nor Hadhrat Umar (RA) had. One was his perseverance until…
narrations.summary: Mahdi says that Uthmaan had two virtues that Abu Bakr and Umar did not have: he persevered until his martyrdom, and he united the Muslims on one standard text of the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once left the Masjid and headed for his room on the upper storey. After entering, he faced towards the Qiblah…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf relates that the Prophet prolonged his sajdah in his room until he feared he had died, and told him that Jibra'eel had brought word that Allaah sends mercy on whoever invokes blessings upon the Prophet, so he prostrated in gratitude.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) says, "I once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and found him standing and performing salaah. He continued standing until dawn broke and made such a…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal relates that the Prophet stood in prayer until dawn and made a long sajdah, and explained that his Lord had asked about his Ummah and promised he would never be made to grieve over it, so he prostrated in thanks.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan Abu Bakr (RA) narrates that when he once went to visit Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ was busy receiving revelation. When the revelation stopped.…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Bakr relates that the Prophet recited Surah Sajdah and prostrated so long that people gathered, explaining he did so in gratitude that seventy thousand of his Ummah would enter Jannah without reckoning, and Abu Bakr and Umar remarked on how great a gift that was.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by a man suffering from a terminal disease, he dismounted from his animal and made Sajdah.…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar relates that the Prophet dismounted and prostrated when he passed a man with a terminal illness, and that Abu Bakr and then Umar did the same.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched an expedition comprising of his family members, he prayed, "O Allaah! If You return them to me safely, I…
narrations.summary: Ali relates that the Prophet prayed that if Allaah returned his family safely from an expedition he would thank Him as He deserves, and when they returned he thanked Allaah and told Ali that he had just done so.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when a beggar once came to Rasulullaah he gave instructions for a date to be given to the man. The beggar however (thinking it to be too…
narrations.summary: Anas relates that the Prophet gave a beggar a single date, which the beggar threw away, and that when a second beggar was delighted with a date he had the Prophet's instruction to have forty dirhams given to him through Ummu Salamah; a second report from Hasan has a beggar who was made wealthy after the Prophet told people to treat him well.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Yasaar narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by a place called Dajnaan, he said, "I once saw myself grazing animals in this place for (my…
narrations.summary: Sulaymaan bin Yasaar relates that passing Dajnaan, Umar recalled herding animals there for his stern father Khattaab, thanked Allaah for making him the guide of the Ummah of Muhammad, and recited verses that worldly wealth and children are temporary while Allaah remains.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "When I come to the conveyance of gratitude and the conveyance of patience, I care not which of the two I ride."
narrations.summary: Umar says that when he comes to the conveyance of gratitude or the conveyance of patience, he does not mind which of the two he rides.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ikramah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by a leper who was also blind, deaf and dumb. Addressing the people with him, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Do…
narrations.summary: Ikramah relates that Umar, passing a leper who was also blind, deaf and dumb, asked his companions whether they saw any bounty in him, and pointed out that the man could urinate with ease, which is a great bounty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat ibraheem reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once heard a man say, "O Allaah! I wish to spend my wealth and my life in Your path.". To this, Hadhrat Umar said, "why…
narrations.summary: Ibraheem relates that Umar heard a man say he wished to spend his wealth and his life in Allaah's path, and rebuked the people for not staying silent, advising patience in difficulty and gratitude in prosperity instead.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that after a man greeted Hadhrat Umar (RA) and he had replied to the greeting, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him, "How are you?" "I only have the…
narrations.summary: Umar asks a man who greeted him how he is, then writes to Abu Moosa Ash'ari urging him to be content with the provision Allaah gives and to be grateful for it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "The grateful ones always received more from Allaah so seek more from Allaah. This is because Allaah says: If you show gratitude (for the…
narrations.summary: Umar says the grateful always receive more from Allaah, so one should ask Allaah for more, citing Surah Ibraheem verse 7.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Moosa narrates that Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) was once called to deal with some people who were involved in some evil activity. However, when…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan praises Allaah for not meeting a group of wrongdoers he was sent to deal with, and frees a slave as a sign of gratitude.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali is once said, "Every bounty should be followed by gratitude and gratitude is followed by an increase (in the bounty). Gratitude and an increase in bounties…
narrations.summary: Ali says every bounty is followed by gratitude, which brings an increase, and Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi reports Ali's further teaching that the doors of du'aa, repentance and forgiveness are never closed while Allaah's Book is recited, citing verses.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "When a night or a day passes without people seeing me suffer any difficulty, I see this as an extremely great bounty from Allaah." Another…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa calls a day without hardship a great bounty from Allaah, and says those who see Allaah's bounties only in food and drink have limited understanding.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) once said, "Gratitude is binding on the person who drinks even plain water that enters his body without difficulty and then exits without…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says gratitude is due even for plain water drunk without difficulty, and Asmaa bint Abi Bakr falls into sajdah of gratitude after finding a keepsake from the Prophet that she had lost following Abdullaah bin Zubayr's martyrdom.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that when the Muslims went for the Battle of Badr, every three of them had to share a camel (to ride in turns because of a…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that at Badr, when the Prophet's turn came to walk, Abu Lubaabah and a second companion offered to walk instead, and the Prophet refused, saying they were no less in need of reward than he was.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muttalib bin Abu Wadaa'ah (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once saw a person performing salaah while sitting down, he said, "The salaah of a sitting person is…
narrations.summary: Muttalib bin Abu Wadaa'ah reports that the Prophet said the salaah of one who prays seated is half the reward of standing, and the Sahabah then strove to pray standing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, he was suffering with high fever and the other Muslims were also suffering of the same, when…
narrations.summary: When the Muslims in Madinah were ill with fever and could pray only seated, the Prophet said seated prayer is half the reward, and the Sahabah then struggled to stand in prayer despite their weakness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rabaa'ah bin Ka'b (RA) says, "I was Rasulullaah ﷺ's servant and served him all day until he performed the Isha salaah. I would then sit by his door when he…
narrations.summary: Rabaa'ah bin Ka'b, who served the Prophet, asks for companionship in Jannah, and the Prophet tells him to help himself by making much sajdah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdul jabbaar bin Haarith bin Maallk Hadasi Manaari narrates, "I was part of a delegation to Rasulullaah ﷺ from the land of Saraat. When I came to Rasulullaah ﷺ,…
narrations.summary: Abdul Jabbaar bin Haarith describes coming to the Prophet with a delegation, accepting Islaam and pledging allegiance, and refusing a worldly grant because he prefers to ask the Prophet for help in the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Taghlib (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ gave something to some people and not to others, it appeared as if they were upset. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said,…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Taghlib reports the Prophet praising him for trusting the independence Allaah placed in his heart when others were given gifts, and Amr says he would not trade those words for red camels.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Hammaad reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) and Hadhrat Umar were leaving from performing Tawaaf when they saw a Bedouin carrying his mother on his back…
narrations.summary: Ali and Umar see a Bedouin carrying his mother around the Tawaaf, and Ali urges Umar to go round again so that the mercy coming down on the Bedouin may reach them too, both reciting couplets.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maymoon bin Mahraan reports that people from Haroora who were associated with Najdah (one of the leaders of the Khawaarij) once passed by a camel belonging to…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar frees a shepherd who had escaped with him from the captors of his camel, declines to reclaim the camel so as to keep the reward, and is urged by his sister Hafsah to marry so that his children either earn reward for patience or pray for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abza (RA) reports that en route to Siffeen when he was on the bank of the Euphrates River, Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) said, "O Allaah! If I…
narrations.summary: Ammaar bin Yaasir, on the way to Siffeen, prays that he would gladly risk death for Allaah's pleasure and trusts that Allaah will never let him fail while he acts to please Him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas once said, "For me to do a good deed today is more beloved to me than two liked deeds done during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ because…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr says a good deed done now is dearer to him than two liked deeds done in the Prophet's time, because the world has now come to the Sahabah while they were then focused on the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Alqama narrates that he once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "was Rasulullaah ﷺ in the habit of specially setting aside certain days (for worship)?" "Not at all,"…
narrations.summary: Alqama asks Aa'isha whether the Prophet set aside particular days for worship, and she replies that his deeds were constant, and that no one can do what he did.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mughierah bin Shu'ba (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ stood in salaah until his feet cut open." When someone asked him, "Did Allaah not forgive all your past and…
narrations.summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba reports that the Prophet stood in salaah until his feet split, and when asked why, given that Allaah had forgiven his past and future errors, he said he should be a grateful servant.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zubayr bin Abdullaah reports from his grandmother whose name was Zuhaymah that Hadhrat Utnmaan (RA) fasted perpetually and stood in salaah throughout the night…
narrations.summary: Zubayr bin Abdullaah reports, through his grandmother Zuhaymah, that Uthmaan fasted continually and prayed through the night, sleeping only briefly at the start.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaahid narrates that the level of worship Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr reached was unmatched. In fact, when a flood prevented people from performing Tawaaf,…
narrations.summary: Mujaahid says Abdullaah bin Zubayr's worship was unmatched, and that during a flood, when people could not perform Tawaaf, he went round the Ka'bah several times by swimming.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qatan bin Abdullaah narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) would fast for seven days continuously to the extent that his intestines dried up. Another…
narrations.summary: Two chains report that Abdullaah bin Zubayr fasted seven days in a row until his insides dried, and that when very old he reduced it to three days.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was the most handsome of people, the most generous and the bravest, when a frightening sound scared the people of Madinah one…
narrations.summary: Anas describes the Prophet as the most handsome, generous and bravest of people, who rode Abu Talha's horse to investigate a night alarm in Madinah and reassured the people, and says the Sahabah sought refuge with him whenever battle grew fierce.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) says, "During the Battle of Badr, we sought refuge from the Mushrikeert by the side of Rasulullaah ﷺ because he was the most furious of fighters."
narrations.summary: An unnamed Companion says that at Badr they sheltered by the side of the Prophet, because he was the fiercest of fighters.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq reports that a man from the Qais tribe once asked Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib, "Did you people desert Rasulullaah ipi during the Battle of Hunayn?"…
narrations.summary: Baraa bin Aazib says the Prophet did not desert at Hunayn, describing the Hawaazin archers and the Prophet remaining on his white mule, with Abu Sufyaan holding its reins, while declaring he is a Nabi without a lie.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa (RA) also narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ then descended from his mule and prayed for assistance saying: "I am a Nabi without a lie. I am the son of Abdul…
narrations.summary: Baraa continues that the Prophet dismounted and prayed for help, and that in the battle only the bravest could fight beside him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas reports that one night Rasulullaah found a date lying by his side and ate it. When he was unable to sleep that night, one of his…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that the Prophet ate a date he found by his side, then stayed awake fearing it might have been one of the Sadaqah dates.

narrations.excerpt: Abu Bakr ■ Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen says that besides Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), he knows of no one who forcibly vomited out the food he had just eaten. Once after eating…
narrations.summary: Ibn Seereen says Abu Bakr alone forced himself to vomit food he had eaten, and Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla recounts that the food came from Ibn Nu'aymaan's paid incantation, which Abu Bakr then vomited out on learning its source.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had a slave who earned an income for him. When the slave brought some food one night and Hadhrat Abu Bakr…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Arqam reports that Abu Bakr's slave brought food from incantations he had performed for pay, and that Abu Bakr ate a morsel, then forced himself to vomit it out, fearing the Prophet's warning about a body fed by unlawful food.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once drank some milk and finding the taste queer, he asked the person who brought it, "Where did you get this milk…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports that Umar, finding the taste of some milk strange, learnt it came from zakaah camels and vomited it out.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhrama (RA) says, "We stuck close to Hadhrat Umar Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) was once out in Kufa when he stopped by a house and…
narrations.summary: Miswar bin Makhrama recounts sticking close to Umar, and Sha'bi reports that Ali, learning that a householder was a money-changer, refused to drink from his well and to take shade under a tax collector's property, citing the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) had two wives. (He was so particular about treating them equally that) When it was the turn of the…
narrations.summary: Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal, who had two wives, treated them equally, and that when both died in the Shaam plague he drew lots to decide which would be placed first in their shared grave.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tawoos says, "I testify that I heard Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) say, 'I testify that I heard Hadhrat Umar !s9SiK recite the Talbiya(3).' We were standing…
narrations.summary: Tawoos reports that Abdullaah bin Abbaas, asked when Umar left Arafaat, declined to say out of caution, which surprised the people.

narrations.excerpt: Rasulullaah ﷺ.
narrations.summary: Not a narration: the text is only the phrase 'Rasulullaah ﷺ' under a section heading.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that he accompanied Rasulullaah ﷺ on an expedition to Najd. On the way back, it was the time for their siesta when they came to a valley…
narrations.summary: Jaabir narrates that a Bedouin drew the Prophet's sword while he slept under a tree, and when the Prophet woke and asked who would save him, the Bedouin said Allaah, and the Prophet did not punish him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ had been fighting the Muhaarib and Ghatfaan tribes in Nakhlah (in Najd). It was at a time when the enemy found the Muslims…
narrations.summary: Jaabir narrates that at Nakhlah, Ghowrath bin Haarith stood over the sleeping Prophet with a sword, the sword fell from his hand, and the Prophet let him go after he pledged not to fight him or join those who did.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Murrah narrates, "When Hadhrat Mi (RA) used to go to the Masjid at night to perform Nafl salaah, we would also go with to guard him. After completing…
narrations.summary: Yahya bin Murrah narrates that Ali, when guarded at night, said that guarding does not help against what is decreed, that angels protect a person until his decreed time, and that no one tastes the sweetness of Imaan unless convinced of qadr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qataadah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) was extremely restless throughout the last night he spent in this world. This made his family very concerned and after…
narrations.summary: Qataadah reports that Ali was restless on his last night, that his family urged him not to go out, and that he said angels protect a person until destiny comes, then went to the Masjid and was assassinated.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Mijlaz narrates that a man from the Muraad tribe once came to see Hadhrat Ali (RA) when he was busy performing salaah in the Masjid. (After Hadhrat Ali (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abu Mijlaz reports that when a man warned Ali of a plot, Ali said a person's appointed term is his guard, and Yahya bin Katheer adds that Ali said the same when people offered to guard him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad ﷺ reports that two men presented their dispute to Hadhrat Ali (RA) for judgement. When he sat at the base of a wall, one of the men cautioned "O Ameerul…
narrations.summary: A narrator (name garbled in the OCR) reports that when Ali judged a dispute while sitting at the base of a wall, one man said the wall was about to fall, and Ali told him to continue because Allaah suffices, and the wall fell after Ali had left.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dhabiyya reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) was on his deathbed, Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) visited him. "What is the problem?" Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Abu Dhabiyya reports that Uthmaan visited Abdullaah bin Mas'ood on his deathbed and offered a stipend for his daughters, and that Abdullaah declined, telling them to recite Surah Waaqi'ah nightly because the Prophet said poverty would never afflict its reciter.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "I care not how my morning goes, whether it be in a manner that I like or in a manner that I dislike because I know not whether goodness is…
narrations.summary: Umar says he does not mind whether his morning brings what he likes or what he dislikes, since he does not know where the good lies.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that someone once said to Hadhrat Ali (RA), "Abu Dharr says that he prefers poverty to riches and illness to good health," To this, Hadhrat Ali (RA)…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Ali was told Abu Dharr prefers poverty and illness; Ali replies that whoever relies on Allaah's choice never wishes for another state, and separately says that whoever is content with Allaah's decision is rewarded.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "On the Day of Qiyaamah, each and every person will wish that in this world he had only that much of food which he could…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that on the Day of Qiyaamah people will wish they had only enough food to live on, that daily conditions harm only a heart full of anger, and that it is better to burn oneself than to say 'if only' about what Allaah has decreed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Kumayl bin Ziyaad says that he was once with Hadhrat Ali (RA) when they reached a graveyard. Turning towards the graves, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "O inhabitants of…
narrations.summary: Kumayl bin Ziyaad relates that at a graveyard Ali addressed the dead, told Kumayl that the best provision is taqwa, and wept, saying the grave is a box holding one's actions.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "Give more importance to having your aeeds accepted than to Taqwa because while a deed with Taqwa can…
narrations.summary: Qais bin Abu Haazim reports Ali's advice to value the acceptance of one's deeds above taqwa itself.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "When a deed with Taqwa can never be undermined, how can one that is accepted ever be undermined?"
narrations.summary: Another report gives Ali saying that a deed done with taqwa can never be undermined, so how can an accepted deed ever be undermined.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "The knowledge that Allaah has acceptedevenasingledeedofmineismore beloved to me than the earth full of gold."
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that knowing Allaah has accepted even one of his deeds is dearer to him than earth full of gold.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "How grand is the sleep of the intelligent ones (who prepare for the Aakhirah) and their days without fastingl How won't they object to the…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says the sleep of the intelligent and the little good done with taqwa and conviction are worth more than a mountain of worship by the negligent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) also said, "For me to know with certainty that Allaah has accepted even one salaah of mine is more beloved to me than the entire world and its…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says that knowing for certain that Allaah accepted one of his salaah is dearer to him than the whole world, citing the verse that Allaah accepts only from those with taqwa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) said, "Whenever a person leaves out something for the pleasure of Allaah, Allaah grants him something much better from sources he does not…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b says that whoever gives up something for Allaah's pleasure is given something better from unexpected sources, while the careless who take without knowing the lawful source are afflicted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once remarked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I see that your hair is getting white?" Rasulullaah replied, "Surahs…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Abu Bakr and then Umar each noticed the Prophet's greying hair, and the Prophet said Surah Hood and the surahs with it had whitened it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "How can I possibly enjoy life when the one with the horn (the angel Hadhrat israafeel already has it…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed reports the Prophet's concern about the angel ready to blow the Trumpet and the words he taught the Sahabah in reply; Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the Prophet fainted on hearing a verse about the chains of Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sahl bin Sa'd (RA) narrates that when the fear for Allaah gripped a young Ansaari, he wept so much every time he heard mention of Jahannam that this kept him…
narrations.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that a young Ansaari, overcome by fear of Jahannam, died in the Prophet's embrace, and the Prophet ordered him enshrouded because fear had ruptured his liver.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) has reported a similar narration with the addition that when the youngster saw Rasulullaah ﷺ, he stood up, embraced Rasulullaah ﷺ and then fell…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah reports the same incident: the youth stood to embrace the Prophet and fell dead, and the Prophet said Allaah had saved him from the Fire and that whoever fears something will flee from it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas- (RA) narrates that. after it was revealed to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he one day recited to the Sahabah (RA) the verse: O you who have imaan! Save…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that when the verse about saving yourselves from the Fire was recited, a young Sahabi fainted; the Prophet told him to say Laa Ilaaha illallaah and gave him glad tidings of Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once fell ill, Rasulullaah ﷺ went to visit him, "How are you feeling, O Umar?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "I…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports the Prophet's visit to the ill Umar, who said he had both hope and fear; Hasan reports Abu Bakr saying that Allaah pairs ease with hardship so the believer keeps both hope and fear.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Roomi reports that the news reached him that Hadhrat Uthmaan once said, "If I were between jannah and Jahannam, not knowing into which of the two I…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Roomi reports that Uthmaan said he would rather be turned to ashes than not know whether he is going to Jannah or Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qataadah narrates that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin jarraah Si once said, "I wish that I was a mere sheep whom my owners would slaughter and then eat my flesh and my…
narrations.summary: Qataadah reports that Abu Ubaydah bin Jarrah wished he were a sheep his owners would slaughter and eat, and that Imraan bin Husayn wished he were sand the wind would blow away.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir bin Masrooq narrates that someone once mentioned in the presence of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), "I do not want to be amongst the 'As'haabul Yameen'…
narrations.summary: Aamir bin Masrooq reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood, told that someone did not want to be among the As'haabul Yameen, said he himself wished not to be resurrected at all; Hasan reports Abdullaah saying he would rather be dust than be placed between Jannah and Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) said, "By Allaah! If you people knew what I know, you will neither make advances to your wives nor find rest on your beds. By Allaah! I wish that…
