narrations.summary: Abu Dharr says that if people knew what he knew they would neglect their wives and beds, and wishes Allaah had created him as a felled tree whose fruit is eaten.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hizaam bin Hakeem reports that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once stated, "If you people knew what you will see after death, you would neither derive pleasure out of…
narrations.summary: Hizaam bin Hakeem reports Abu Dardaa saying that if people knew what follows death they would take no pleasure in food or drink, and wishing to be a felled tree.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) also mentioned, "I wish that I were a sheep belonging to some people who have visitors passing by. They will then pass a knife over my jugular…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa wishes to be a sheep whose throat is cut to feed guests, and Abdullaah bin Umar wishes to be a pillar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tawoos reports, "When Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal SSI came to our land, our scholars said to him, 'If you just give the word, we shall take these rocks and trees…
narrations.summary: Tawoos reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal refused a masjid built from rocks and trees for fear of carrying it on his back on the Day of Qiyaamah; Naafi reports Abdullaah bin Umar weeping in sajdah in the Ka'bah; and Abu Haazim reports Abdullaah bin Umar's remark about a man who fell unconscious when the Qur'aan was recited.

narrations.excerpt: It is reported that whenever Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Aws Ansaari (RA) lay on the bed, he would turn from side to side without being able to fall asleep. He would then say,…
narrations.summary: Shaddaad bin Aws Ansaari, unable to sleep from fear of Jahannam, would cry out to Allaah and then stand in salaah until morning.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Salamah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "By Allaah! I Wish that I were a tree. By Allaah! I wish that I were .sand. By Allaah! I wish that…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Salamah reports Aa'isha wishing she were a tree or sand, or had never been created; another report has Abdullaah bin Abbaas praising Aa'isha before her death, and she replies that she wishes only to be forgotten.

narrations.excerpt: Rasulullaah Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to me, 'Recite (the Qur'aan) to me.' I replied, 'How can I recite to you when it was to…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that the Prophet asked him to recite the Qur'aan, and that when he reached the verse about a witness from every nation the Prophet's eyes filled with tears and he said that was enough.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that the men of Suffa wept excessively when Allaah revealed the verse; ("i. c-)l OjSs-H Oj Oj 1 Are you astonished about this speech…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the men of Suffa wept when a verse was revealed, the Prophet wept with them, and he said the one who weeps out of fear of Allaah will never enter Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once recited the verse; ...(The fire of Jaharmam) the fuel of which is people and stones,,. (Surah Tahreem, verse 6)…
narrations.summary: Anas reports the Prophet describing the fire of Jahannam and an Abyssinian man weeping loudly before him; the Prophet praised him, and Allaah's message brought through Jibra'eel is that tears shed in fear of Him will be rewarded with laughter in Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Abu Haazim (RA) says, "I once went to see Rasulullaah ﷺ and found that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had already taken his place become the Khalifah). (In his…
narrations.summary: Qais bin Abu Haazim says that when he went to visit the Prophet he found Abu Bakr had already taken his place as Khalifah, and that Abu Bakr praised Allaah at length in his address and wept greatly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan bin Muhammad bin (RA) bin Abi Taalib states that during the Friday sermon, Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to recite the Surah J-S-sJi is Takweer) until he reached…
narrations.summary: Hasan bin Muhammad bin Abi Taalib reports that Umar wept so much reciting Surah Takweer in the Friday sermon that his voice stopped, and that after reciting Surah Toor he fell ill and people visited him for twenty days.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubayd bin Umayr (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar iP once led them in the Fajr salaah and started reciting Surah Yusuf, However, he started weeping and had to stop…
narrations.summary: Ubayd bin Umayr reports that Umar wept while leading Fajr when he reached the verse about Ya'qoob's eyes turning white with grief, and then went into ruku.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Shaddaad bin Haad narrates that even while standing in the last rows of the congregation, he could hear the sobbing of Hadhrat Umar during the Fajr…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Shaddaad bin Haad says he could hear Umar sobbing in the Fajr prayer from the last rows, as Umar recited Surah Yusuf and stopped at the verse about complaining of sorrow to Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hishaam bin Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) would sometimes recite a verse of the Qur'aan that would choke him (with emotion). He would then weep so much…
narrations.summary: Hishaam bin Hasan narrates that a verse sometimes choked Umar with emotion, so that he would fall down weeping and stay indoors while people visited him thinking he was ill.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haani who was the freed slave of Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) says that whenever Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) stopped at a graveyard, he would weep so much that his…
narrations.summary: Haani, freed slave of Uthmaan, reports that Uthmaan wept at graveyards, quoting the Prophet that the grave is the first stage of the Aakhirah and the most frightening sight he had seen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) who was weeping. "What makes you weep?" Hadhrat Umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar asked the weeping Mu'aadh bin Jabal why he wept, and Mu'aadh quoted the Prophet that even slight ostentation is shirk and that the people most beloved to Allaah are the hidden God-fearing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) was once reciting the Surah (Surah Mutaffifeen). However, he started weeping when he reached the verse: ...the day when all of mankind…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar wept so much reciting Surah Mutaffifeen that he fell down; Naafi reports he always wept at certain verses of Baqarah and Hadeed; Yusuf bin Maahak reports walking with Abdullaah bin Umar to ask about Abu Dharr's worship, which was meditation in solitude.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubayd bin Umayr (RA) once recited the verse: How will it be (the condition of the Kuffaar on the Day of Qiyaamah) when We shall bring forth a witness from every…
narrations.summary: When Ubayd bin Umayr recited the verse about the witness from every nation, Abdullaah bin Umar wept so much that his beard and collar were wet with tears.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Mulaykah says, "I accompanied Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas from Makkah to Madinah and wherever he set up camp, he stood in salaah for half the…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abu Mulaykah reports that Abdullaah bin Abbaas stood in prayer half the night and wept while reciting Surah Qaaf, and Abu Rajaa describes the tear marks on his face.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat uthmaan bin Abu Saudah says that he once saw Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit on the wall of the Masjid that (Allaah showed Rasulullaah ﷺ a vantage point that)…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan bin Abu Saudah saw Ubaadah bin Saamit weeping on the wall of the Masjid over a valley of Jahannam, and Ubaadah said the Prophet ﷺ had shown them that place.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ya'la bin Ataa reports from his mother who made kohl for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr that he wept excessively, in fact, he would lock his door and weep so much that…
narrations.summary: Ya'la bin Ataa reports that Abdullaah bin Amr wept so much that his eyes were affected, and Muslim bin Bishr reports Abu Hurayrah weeping in his final illness over the journey to Jannah or Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dhamrah bin Habeeb reports from a freed slave of the Sahabi Hadhrat Abu Rayhaanah that when Hadhrat Abu Rayhaanah (RA) once returned from a military expedition,…
narrations.summary: Dhamrah bin Habeeb reports from a freed slave of Abu Rayhaanah that Abu Rayhaanah stood in prayer all night after a campaign, lost in thought about the descriptions of Jannah, and did not hear the Adhaan until Fajr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin waasi narrates that a man rode from Basrah to see Hadhrat Ummu Dharr (RA) after the demise of (her husband) Hadhrat Abu Dharr to ask her about the…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Waasi reports that a man came from Basrah to ask Ummu Dharr about Abu Dharr's worship, and she said he spent his whole days in solitary meditation.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aun bin Abdullaah bin utba reports that he once asked Hadhrat Ummu Dardaa. about the best deed of (her husband) Hadhrat Abu Dardaa She replied, "Meditation and…
narrations.summary: Aun bin Abdullaah bin Utba reports that Ummu Dardaa named meditation and heeding lessons as Abu Dardaa's best deed, and Abu Dardaa said meditation for a moment is better than standing in salaah all night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa S8ffl!8S also said, "Amongst people there are those who are the keys to good and the locks of evil. They shall have great rewards. There are then also…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says some people are keys to good and locks to evil, who will be richly rewarded, while others are keys to evil and locks to good, who will be severely punished, and repeats that meditation for a moment is better than a night of salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Habeeb bin Abdullaah narrates that a man intending to march in Jihaad came to Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) for advice. Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "Think of Allaah…
narrations.summary: Habeeb bin Abdullaah reports Abu Dardaa advising a man going to jihaad to remember Allaah in ease so that He remembers him in hardship; Saalim bin Abil Ja'd reports Abu Dardaa drawing a lesson from two bulls, one whipped for stopping and the other spared.

narrations.excerpt: One of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)'s freed slaves reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr once said, "whoever angers his carnal self for the sake of Allaah will be saved from Allaah's…
narrations.summary: A freed slave of Abu Bakr reports Abu Bakr saying that whoever opposes his own carnal self for Allaah's sake will be saved from Allaah's anger.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thaabit bin Hajjaaj narrates that Hadhrat umar (RA) once said, "Weigh yourselves up before you are weighed and assess yourselves before you are assessed because…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Khattaab urges people to weigh themselves before they are weighed, and Anas reports Umar's fear of Allaah while alone in an orchard.

narrations.excerpt: In a lengthy narration, Hadhrat Simaak says that he once asked Hadhrat Jaabir bin Samurah, "Did you associate often with Nabi ﷺ Hadhrat Jaabir replied, "Yes, He was a…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Samurah tells Simaak that the Prophet was a man who often remained silent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Maalik Ashja'ee (RA) reports that his father said, "We were little boys when we used to sit in the company of Rasulullaah ﷺ and have never seen anyone remain…
narrations.summary: Abu Maalik Ashja'ee reports that his father said the Companions never saw anyone as silent as the Prophet, who only smiled when others talked too much.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once out with his companions. As he rode, one of them stepped out ahead of him. Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal…
narrations.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal asked what deeds to do after the Prophet, and the Prophet taught that remaining silent except for good speech is the greatest restraint on the self.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that when someone was martyred, a lady was weeping over him saying, "Oh dear martyr!" Addressing her, Rasulullaah said, "Stop saying…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet telling a weeping woman not to call a slain man a martyr, and Anas reports the same about a Companion who died at Uhud.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Numayr says, "Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) often remained silent for prolonged periods of time and always seemed depressed. (When he did speak, he…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Numayr reports that Ammaar bin Yaasir often stayed silent for long periods and seemed depressed, and when he did speak it was mostly to seek Allaah's protection from trials.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Idress Khowlani says, "I once entered the Masjid of Damascus when my eyes caught sight of a man with sparkling front teeth. He was a very quiet man and…
narrations.summary: Abu Idress Khowlani recounts seeing a quiet, respected man in the Masjid of Damascus and learning from him a du'aa for steadfastness, gratitude, a pure heart and a truthful tongue.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once climbed Mount Safa, he caught hold of his tongue saying, "O tongue! Speak what is good and…
narrations.summary: Abu Waa'il reports that Ibn Mas'ood told a man to lift his garment; when the man retorted that Ibn Mas'ood also wore his high, Ibn Mas'ood explained his thin calves. Umar then struck the man for insolence. Alaa reports that Umar threw a brick at a Quraysh man who suggested he hire someone to build for him, saying he did not want to dislike Ibn Mas'ood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed Jareeri reports from a man who said, "I once saw Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas holding the point of his tongue as he said, 'Shame on you! Speakwhatisgood…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed Jareeri reports that he saw Abdullaah bin Abbaas holding his tongue and warning that on the Day of Qiyaamah a person will be angriest with his tongue.

narrations.excerpt: Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Thaabit Bunaani narrates that Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Aws (RA) once said to one of his companions, "Lay the tablecloth so that we may dig in to it!"…
narrations.summary: Shaddaad bin Aws, after pledging allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ, said that since then every word he spoke was measured, and taught a du'aa for steadfastness and a pure heart.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Shaddaad (RA) added, "Do not learn these words from me, but rather learn what I shall narrate to you that I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say,…
narrations.summary: Shaddaad relays the Prophet's du'aa for steadfastness and forgiveness, which the Prophet advised people to fill their treasures with instead of gold and silver hoarding.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Isa bin Uqba narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "I swear by the Being besides Whom there is none worthy of worship that nothing on earth…
narrations.summary: Isa bin Uqba reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood swore nothing on earth deserves a long prison sentence more than the tongue.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "Beware of futile speech. All you need to say it that which would get your needs fulfilled."
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood warns to beware of futile speech and to say only what will get one's needs fulfilled.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "The people guilty of the most sins on the Day of Qiyaamah shall be those who most engaged in idle…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says those guilty of the most sins on the Day of Qiyaamah will be those who engaged most in idle talk.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "The tongue is the basis of the body's well-being. When the tongue is upright, the other limbs are all upright. However, as soon as the tongue is…
narrations.summary: Ali bin Abi Taalib gives several sayings on the tongue and silence: the tongue governs the whole body, keep a low profile, silence leads to Jannah, and a couplet on keeping secrets.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once said, "Learn to remain silent just as you learn to speak because silence is a great source of self-control. You ought to be more interested…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa advises learning silence as one learns speech, listening more than speaking, and not speaking or laughing about things that do not concern you.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) also said, "There is no limb of a Mu'min that Allaah loves more than his tongue because it is by means of this that he will enter jannah. At the…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says the tongue is the limb a believer is loved for most, since it leads him to Jannah, and the limb a disbeliever is hated for most, since it leads him to Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "The limb that a person most needs to purify is his tongue." Hadhrat Anas (RA) said, "A person can never have Taqwa until he…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says a person most needs to purify his tongue, and Anas says no one attains Taqwa until he controls his tongue.

narrations.excerpt: The Speech of Rasulullaah ﷺ.
narrations.summary: Heading only, 'The Speech of Rasulullaah', with no narration under it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ's speech was such (so clear) that if anyone wished to count the words, they could have easily done so." She also mentioned,…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha describes how clearly the Prophet spoke, so that his words could be counted, and tells how she missed a chance to rebuke a man who spoke loudly beside her room.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ's speech was so clear that everyone could understand it. He would never speak continuously and quickly."…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet's speech was so clear that everyone understood it and he never spoke continuously and quickly, and a Companion said each of his letters was distinctly pronounced.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ spoke anything (of marked importance), he would repeat it thrice and whenever he approached a gathering, he would greet…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that when the Prophet said something important he repeated it three times, and that he greeted a gathering three times.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thumamah bin Anas narrates that whenever Hadhrat Anas (RA) spoke (something of importance), he repeated himself thrice and would say that when Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Thumamah bin Anas reports that Anas repeated important words three times, saying the Prophet did the same so that people would understand him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "I have been sent with concise yet comprehensive speech and have been assisted with awe. When I was…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet's words that he was given concise yet comprehensive speech and the keys to the treasures of the heavens and the earth, and Abdullaah bin Salaam reports that the Prophet looked to the sky when he sat to talk.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) says, "Even when speaking to the worst of people, Rasulullaah ﷺ would turn his full attention to the person so that (they would feel special…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Al Aas says the Prophet gave his full attention to whoever he spoke with, and recounts asking whether he, Abu Bakr, Umar or Uthmaan was best, then regretting the questions.

narrations.excerpt: The Smiling of Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Aa'isha Sglgieff.says, "I have never seen Rasulullaah ﷺ laugh so much in a manner that I could see his uvula. All he did was smile."
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says she never saw the Prophet laugh so much that his uvula showed, and that he only smiled.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Haarith bin Jaz (RA) says, "I have never seen anyone smile as much as Rasulullaah ﷺ ." In another narration, he says, "Rasulullaah never laughed but…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Haarith bin Jaz says he never saw anyone smile as much as the Prophet, and that the Prophet never laughed but only smiled.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Simaak bin Harb reports that he once asked Hadhrat Jaabir bin Samurah "Were you frequently in the company of Rasulullaah ﷺ ?" Hadhrat jaabir replied, 'Yes, I was…
narrations.summary: Simaak bin Harb reports asking Jaabir bin Samurah whether he was often with the Prophet, and Jaabir describes the Prophet smiling while the Companions laughed about pre-Islamic matters.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Simaak bin Harb reports that he once asked Hadhrat Jaabir bin Samurah (RA), "Were you frequently in the company of Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Simaak bin Harb reports that Jaabir bin Samurah described the Prophet as often silent and laughing very little, and only smiling when the Companions recited poetry and he said something that made them laugh.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Husayn bin Yazeed Kalbi (RA) says, "I have never seen Rasulullaah laugh. He would only smile. There were also times when he would have to tie a rock to his belly…
narrations.summary: Husayn bin Yazeed Kalbi says he never saw the Prophet laugh, only smile, and that at times he had to tie a rock to his belly from hunger.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amrah. reports that she once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) about Rasulullaah ﷺ's behaviour when he was alone with his wives. Hadhrat Aa'isha replied, "He was like…
narrations.summary: Amrah asks Aa'isha how the Prophet behaved at home, and Aa'isha replies that he was the noblest and most compassionate of men and often laughed and smiled.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "when revelation would come to Rasulullaah ﷺ or when he was delivering a lecture, he would appear like a person warning his people of an…
narrations.summary: Jaabir says that when revelation came or the Prophet was giving a lecture he looked like a warner, but otherwise he had the most smiling face, was the most jovial, and was the handsomest of men.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was one of the most jovial of people and the one with the best personality."
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah says the Prophet ﷺ was one of the most jovial and best-natured of people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir bin Sa'd reports that Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) said to him, "I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ smile so broadly during the Battle of Khandaq that his molar teeth actually became…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas told Aamir that during the Battle of Khandaq the Prophet ﷺ smiled broadly after Sa'd shot an enemy soldier who was taunting the archers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that a man once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "I am destroyed! I have engaged in sexual relations with my wife during Ramadhaan." "Then…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports a man who broke his fast in Ramadhaan by relations with his wife; the Prophet ﷺ told him to free a slave, fast, or feed the poor, and when he had nothing, gave him dates to spend on his family, and smiled.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah iiil once said, "I know the first person to enter Jannah and the last to emerge from Jahannam. A man will be summoned on…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet ﷺ describing a man whose minor sins are shown to him and whose major sins are hidden, and Abu Dharr saw the Prophet ﷺ smile widely.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I know who the last person to emerge from Jahannam will be. He will come out of Jahannam crawling…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports the Prophet's account of the last person to leave Jahannam, who is granted Jannah and ten times what the world had to offer, and says the Prophet then smiled so widely his molars showed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaarijah bin Zaid (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was the most dignified person in his gatherings and (as he sat) none of his limbs extended (towards the people)."
narrations.summary: Khaarijah bin Zaid says the Prophet was the most dignified person in his gatherings and never stretched his limbs out towards people while seated.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shahr bin Howshab says that whenever the Sahabah (RA) spoke in the presence of Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA), they kept looking at him out ofaweforhim. In…
narrations.summary: Shahr bin Howshab and Abu Muslim Khowlaani describe how the Companions turned to Mu'aadh bin Jabal, who was quiet and dignified, for verification of hadith, and Mu'aadh identifies himself as the youthful man in the second account.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Barzah (RA) narrates, "when a man spoke harshly to Hadhrat Abu Bakr, I said, 'Should I not execute him?' Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) rebuked me saying, 'Such…
narrations.summary: Abu Barzah says he wanted to execute a man who spoke harshly to Abu Bakr, but Abu Bakr rebuked him, and Umar says no sip is better than a sip of anger held back.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) narrates that a man once reported to Rasulullaah that a certain person frequently went to see his father's wife (with apparently sinister…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b says he would have killed a man seen visiting his father's wife, and the Prophet laughs and says he is more possessive than Ubay, and Allaah is more possessive than the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mughierah narrates that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) once said, "If I found any man with my wife, I would strike him with the sharp edge of my sword." When this…
narrations.summary: Mughierah reports that Sa'd bin Ubaadah said he would strike any man found with his wife, and the Prophet replied that he and Allaah are more possessive; Abu Hurayrah and Ibn Abbaas add the four-witness ruling and the Companions' plea for Sa'd.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ left her one night, she became extremely jealous, Rasulullaah ﷺ then returned to see what she was doing and…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha tells of her jealousy of Umm Salama, which she and Hafsah discussed, then the Qur'an verse on monasticism, and Mu'aadh bin Jabal's warning against forsaking enjoining good.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ married Ummu Salamah, I became extremely depressed because people always told us about her beauty. When I managed to…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha confesses her jealousy: after the Prophet married Ummu Salamah she thought her more beautiful than people said, Hafsah told her she was not, and on a second look Aa'isha agreed it had been her own possessiveness that made her see it that way.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once addressed the people saying, "The news has reached me that your women crowd the marketplaces with Kuffaar men. Have you people no sense of…
narrations.summary: Ali rebukes the people for letting their women crowd markets with unbelieving men, saying there is no good in one who has no sense of possessiveness, and that possessiveness is good only when it protects the family.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ came indoors one day and said, "O Ibn Mas'ood!" "At your service, O Rasulullaah ﷺ f Hadhrat Abdullaah bin…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Masood was told by the Prophet ﷺ that the best people do good deeds with deep understanding, and that the most learned see the truth in disputes; he then recounted the seventy-two groups and the tortured followers of Isa who opposed the kings.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "You people shall remain on the clear path of your Rabb as long as two intoxicants do not become manifest…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal narrates the Prophet ﷺ warning that love of the world and ignorance will lead people to stop enjoining good and forbidding evil.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed Raqaashi reports from Hadhrat Anas (RA) that Rasulullaah said, "Should I not inform you about a group of people who although not belonging to the Ambiyaa…
narrations.summary: Yazeed Raqaashi reports from Anas that the Prophet described people who travel to advise others, and who become beloved to Allaah by making His servants beloved to Him through enjoining good and forbidding evil.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) narrates that he once asked Nabi ﷺ, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ When will people forsake enjoining what is good and forbidding what is evil, whilst these two…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah asks the Prophet when people will abandon enjoining good and forbidding evil, and the Prophet answers that it will be when the affliction of the Bani Israa'eel befalls them: leniency towards sinners, knowledge given to the worst, and leadership to the young.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Abu Haazim narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had become Khalifah, he mounted the pulpit and after duly praising Allaah, he said, "O people! You…
narrations.summary: Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that when Abu Bakr became Khalifah he warned people against misreading the verse about looking after oneself, citing the Prophet's words that punishment reaches all when evil is seen and not changed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that on the day he was named Khalifah, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) sat on Rasulullaah ﷺ's pulpit. After duly praising Allaah and…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports Abu Bakr, on the day he became Khalifah, recounting the Prophet's explanation of the verse Take care of your own selves: when evil is tolerated in a community, Allaah will punish them all and their du'aas will not be accepted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "When people perpetrate evil in the midst of others who are more powerful than them but who do not prevent them, Allaah shall engulf them all…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr says that when people commit evil while stronger people who could stop them do not, Allaah will engulf them all in a calamity that will not be lifted.

narrations.excerpt: (Addressing the people) Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "When you people see a fool dishonouring people, what prevents you from opposing him?" When the people admitted that…
narrations.summary: Umar asks the people why they do not oppose a fool who dishonours others, and warns that if they stay silent out of fear they will be unable to bear witness for the Ambiyaa on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) once said, "Enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil before the worst amongst you are given authority over you and then when even the best of you…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan says to enjoin good and forbid evil before the worst among the people are given authority over them, since even the best will then have their du'aas rejected.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "You people must enjoin what is good, forbid what bin Mansoor and others, all reporting from reliable sources. is evil and defend the Deen of…
narrations.summary: Ali urges the people to enjoin good and forbid evil or the worst will rule them, and in a sermon warns that earlier nations were destroyed when their religious scholars failed to forbid their sins.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "Jihaad is of three categories; Jihaad with the hand, Jihaad with the tongue and Jihaad with the heart. The first of these to disappear will…
narrations.summary: Ali divides jihaad into three kinds, with the hand, the tongue and the heart, and says the jihaad of the hand will disappear first.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "The first Jihaad to disappear will be the Jihaad of your hands, followed by Jihaad of your tongue and then Jihaad of your heart. The heart…
narrations.summary: Ali says the jihaad of the hands, then the tongue, then the heart will vanish, and a heart that cannot recognise good or reject evil will be turned upside down.

narrations.excerpt: When Idrees bin Uroob Shaybaani once came to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood and said, "Destroyed is the person who does not enjoin good and forbid evil." Hadhrat Abdullaah…
narrations.summary: Idrees Shaybaani tells Abdullaah bin Mas'ood that whoever does not enjoin good and forbid evil is destroyed, and Ibn Mas'ood replies that one whose heart does not recognise good and reject evil is already destroyed, then describes three types of people who do good.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Wage Jihaad against the Munaaflqeen with your tongues and if you can do nothing else besides frowning at them (to express your…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says to wage jihaad against the hypocrites with the tongue, and if nothing else is possible, at least to frown at them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "When you see an evil and are unable to change it, it will suffice for Allaah to know that you hate it within your heart."…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that disliking an evil you cannot change is enough for Allaah, that approving of an evil done in your absence is like witnessing it, and that many evils will come in the future.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "The righteous ones shall leave this world first, leaving behind only doubtful people who will be unable to…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says the righteous will die first, leaving behind doubtful people who can neither recognise good nor reject evil.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abur Ruqaad says, "I was a youngster when I went out with my master one day. We were somehow led to (a gathering addressed by) Hadhrat Hudhayfah who was saying,…
narrations.summary: Abur Ruqaad recalls a gathering addressed by Hudhayfah, who warned that unless people enjoin good and forbid evil, Allaah will set the worst over them and their du'aas will go unanswered, and who said a time will come when the best people are those who do neither.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Adi bin Haatim (RA) once said, "The good you do today was considered an evil in times gone by and the evil of today will be considered something good in times to…
narrations.summary: Adi bin Haatim says that what is good today will be called evil in times to come and the reverse, and that people stay on the right path only while they do not call good evil and scholars keep speaking the truth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once said, "I enjoin on you to do something that I do not do in the hope that Allaah will grant me the reward for it."
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says he advises people to do something he does not practise himself, hoping to be rewarded by Allaah for the advice.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says that whenever Hadhrat Umar (RA) intended forbidding the people from anything, he first approached his family saying, "Should I come…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that whenever Umar meant to forbid the people something, he first warned his own family that anyone of them who did it would receive double the punishment.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Shihaab reports that Hadhrat Hishaam bin Hakeem bin Hizaam and few men with him together engaged in enjoining good and forbidding evil. Hadhrat Umar (RA) used…
narrations.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports that Hishaam bin Hakeem and some men enjoined good and forbade evil together, and Umar used to say that evil would not happen while he and Hishaam were alive.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ja'far Khatmi reports that his grandfather Hadhrat Umayr bin Habeeb bin Khumaasha was a Sahabi who had been in the company of Rasulullaah ﷺ since the time he…
narrations.summary: Abu Ja'far Khatmi reports that his grandfather, the Sahabi Umayr bin Habeeb, advised his son to avoid foolish company and to be patient with the harm that comes from enjoining good and forbidding evil.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdul Azeez bin Abu Bakrah narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakrah (RA) married a woman from the Banu Ghudaanah who later passed away. As he carried her to the…
narrations.summary: Abdul Azeez reports that Abu Bakrah led the funeral prayer for his wife over her brothers' objections, fell when people pushed him at the grave, and told his children he feared living in a time when he could not enjoin good and forbid evil.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali bin Zaid reports that he was once with Hajjaaj in a castle as Hajjaaj was busy interrogating people about their links with Ibnul Ash'ath. Hadhrat Anas arrived…
narrations.summary: Ali bin Zaid reports that Hajjaaj threatened Anas bin Maalik for supporting rival factions, and Anas answered calmly and left, saying he had held back only for the sake of his children.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "I once heard Hajjaaj say something in his lecture that I did not like. However, when I intended objecting to it, I recalled the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says he held back from objecting to a speech by Hajjaaj, recalling the Prophet's saying that a Mu'min should not humiliate himself by taking on what he cannot bear.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "In keeping to oneself, one finds an escape from mixing with bad company." in another narration, Hadhrat Umar (RA) stated, "Take your full…
narrations.summary: Umar says that keeping to oneself is a way to escape bad company, and another narration has him urging people to take their full share of keeping to themselves.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aafaa bin Imraan reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by some people who were following a man who had been arrested for committing a crime. Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Mu'aafaa bin Imraan reports that Umar, passing people who were following an arrested man, said there is no welcome for faces that appear only at times of evil.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Adasah Taa'ee reports, "I was in Sarif when Hadhrat Abdullaah (bin Mas'ood) arrived there and my family sent me to him with a few things (as gifts). It so…
narrations.summary: Adasah Taa'ee reports that when Abdullaah bin Mas'ood received a bird brought from a far-off place, he wished he could be somewhere he need not speak to anyone, and no one would speak to him, until he met Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaasim narrates that a man once came to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood asking for advice. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) advised him saying, "Let your home…
narrations.summary: Qaasim reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood advised a man who asked for counsel to stay indoors, guard his tongue and weep over his sins.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ismaa'eel bin Abu Khaalid narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood gave three advices to his son Abu ubaydah, when he said, "Dear son! I advise you to adopt…
narrations.summary: Ismaa'eel bin Abu Khaalid reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood advised his son Abu Ubaydah to keep taqwa, stay indoors and weep over his sins.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah li once said, "I wish I had someone to manage my finances so that I could lock my door and neither have anyone come to. meet me nor go out to meet…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah says he wishes he had someone to manage his affairs so he could lock his door and meet no one until he met Allaah, and Ibn Abbaas says that he would go where he had no friends if Shaytaan's whisperings did not hold him back, because people corrupt people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed says that Hadhrat Abu Jahm bin Haarith bin Simma was a person who did not associate with his fellow Ansaar. when this solitude was mentioned to…
narrations.summary: Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that Abu Jahm bin Haarith did not mix with his fellow Ansaar, and when this was mentioned to him he said people are worse than solitude.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "The best monastery for a Muslim is his home where he is able to keep his carnal self his eyes and his private organs under control. Beware…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says a Muslim's best place of seclusion is his home, where he keeps his self, eyes and private parts under control, and warns against marketplace gatherings that lead to negligence and idle talk.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) once passed by Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal who was standing by his door and pointing with his fingers as if speaking to himself. "What is the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr finds Mu'aadh bin Jabal talking to himself at his door, and Mu'aadh explains that Shaytaan urges him to leave home, while the Prophet said those who go out for good causes, or who stay home without backbiting, are under Allaah's protection.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ubayd narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once saw Hadhrat Ahnaf (RA) wearing a (new) upper garment, he asked, "O Ahnaf! What did you pay for this…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ubayd reports that Umar, seeing Ahnaf in a new garment bought for twelve dirhams, told him six would have been enough and the rest should go to a good cause.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan Basri reports that in a letter to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote, "Be content with whatever sustenance you receive in this world because…
narrations.summary: Hasan Basri reports that Umar wrote to Abu Moosa Ash'ari to be content with the provision he receives, since Allaah gives some people more and tests the wealthy by whether they are grateful.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ja'far narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once ate some dry dates, drank some water and then placed his hand on his belly saying, "May Allaah distance (from His…
narrations.summary: Abu Ja'far reports that Ali ate dry dates and drank water, then said that whoever's stomach leads them into the Fire is far from Allaah's mercy, and recited a couplet on the regret that follows indulging one's appetites.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that Hadhrat All bin Abi Taalib (RA) once said, "O son of Aadam. Never bring the worry of the approaching day before the worry of the present day…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that Ali advised not to worry about the next day's food, since sustenance is assured, and warned that wealth beyond one's needs is held in trust for someone else.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd (bin Abi Waqqaas) (RA) once advised, "Dear son! When you seek to be independent, do so with contentment because when a person is not content, his wealth will…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas advises his son that independence must be sought through contentment, because wealth without contentment never makes a person independent.

narrations.excerpt: It was Hadhrat Jaabir bin Samurah (RA) or another Sahabi who reported that (as a youngster before announcing his Nabuwaat) Nabi ﷺ grazed goats but later gave it up when…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Samurah, or another Sahabi, reports that the young Prophet gave up goat-herding for trade with camels, that Khadeeja's sister praised his modesty and character, and that Khadeeja then sought to marry him and afterwards sent gifts.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once mentioned how the father of Hadhrat Khadeeja ip was reluctant to marry her to Rasulullaah ﷺ. She however…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that the Prophet described how Khadeeja got her father drunk and then persuaded him to marry her to the Prophet, and that when he sobered up and objected to marrying the orphan of Abu Taalib, she talked him round.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nafeesah (RA) reports, "Hadhrat Khadeeja bint Khuwaylid (RA) was an extremely wise, strong and noble woman. She was all of this together with the honour and good…
narrations.summary: Nafeesah reports that Khadeeja, a wealthy and noble woman, sent her to ask the Prophet whether he would marry, and that Khadeeja's uncle Amr bin Asad arranged the marriage when the Prophet was twenty-five and Khadeeja forty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Khadeeja (RA) passed away, Rasulullaah ﷺ was still living in Makkah. it was then that Hadhrat Khowla bint Hakeem bin Awqas…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that after Khadeeja died, Khowla bint Hakeem proposed to the Prophet on behalf of Aa'isha and Sauda, that Abu Bakr at first doubted the match, and that the Prophet's answer of Islamic brotherhood settled it and the marriage was arranged.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states at the end that Rasulullaah ﷺ told Hadhrat Khowlah "Go back and tell him that I am his brother in Islaam (not by blood) and that he is my brother…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr withdraws his promise of Aa'isha to Mut'im bin Adi's son after Mut'im's wife objects, and then marries her to the Prophet; Khowla then proposes Sauda bint Zam'ah, whose brother Abd bin Zam'ah later regrets his grief, and Aa'isha describes her wedding in Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) became a widow when her husband Hadhrat Khunays bin Hudhaafah Sahmi who was a veteran of the Battle of…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that after Khunays bin Hudhaafah died, Umar offered Hafsah first to Uthmaan and then to Abu Bakr, both of whom held back, until the Prophet proposed to her himself and then gave his daughter to Uthmaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat ummu Salamah (RA) reports that when her iddah had expired, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) proposed for her hand in marriage but she did not marry him. when Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Ummu Salamah declines Abu Bakr's proposal, then accepts the Prophet's proposal after his replies to her objections, and her son Umar brings the marriage about.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ismaa'eel bin Amr reports that Hadhrat Ummu Habeebah bint Abu Sufyaan said, "What I remember well about the time I was in Abyssinia was the arrival of Najaashi's…
narrations.summary: Ummu Habeebah recounts that Najaashi's envoy Abraha brought the king's news that the Prophet wished to marry her, that Khaalid bin Sa'eed gave her in marriage, and that Najaashi paid the dowry and hosted a meal.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ismaa'eel bin Amr bin Saa'eed bin Al Aas reports that Hadhrat Ummu Habeebah bint Abu Sufyaan said, "I saw my husband Ubaydullaah bin Jahash in a dream looking…
narrations.summary: Ummu Habeebah tells how her dream of her husband Ubaydullaah bin Jahash foretold his turn to Christianity and his death in drink, how her later dream made her expect marriage to the Prophet, and how Abraha returned her gifts.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when the Iddah of Hadhrat Zaynab bint Jahash had expired, Rasulullaah ﷺ told Hadhrat Zaid (RA) to ask her if she would marry him. When…
narrations.summary: Anas relates how Zaid went to propose to Zaynab bint Jahash for the Prophet, how she referred the matter to her Lord and the marriage was then settled by revelation, and the walima and the Hijaab verses that followed.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Anas (RA) states, "To celebrate his marriage to Hadhrat Zaynab bint Jahash (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ hosted a meal of bread and meat. 1 was sent…
narrations.summary: Anas describes the wedding meal of Zaynab bint Jahash: after the guests left and three men stayed talking, the Prophet went to Aa'isha's room and then returned to Zaynab's, and the verse of hijaab was revealed as he dropped the curtain.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) also reports that after Rasulullaah ﷺ had consummated his marriage to one of his wives, Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) (Hadhrat Anas mother) cooked some…
narrations.summary: Anas relates that his mother Ummu Sulaym sent a dish after the Prophet's marriage to Zaynab, that the Prophet had about three hundred people fed from it, and that the Hijaab verses were revealed as the men left.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when the prisoners captured after the Battle of Khaybar were mustered together, Hadhrat Dihya (RA) approached Rasulullaah with a request.…
narrations.summary: Anas relates that after the Khaybar captives were gathered, Dihya asked for a slave woman and was sent to take another, and the Prophet freed Safiyya bint Huyay and married her.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that they marched to Khaybar and after conquering the fortress there, Rasulullaah ﷺ was informed about Saflyya bint Huyay bin Akhtab. She was…
narrations.summary: Anas relates the Prophet's marriage to Safiyya after Khaybar, the walima held near Sahbaa with food set on a leather cloth, and the Prophet's care in helping her onto his camel on the way back.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) states, "Rasulullaah ﷺ camped at a place between Khaybar and Madinah for three days. It was here that he consummated his marriage to Saflyya, after…
narrations.summary: Anas describes the walima for Safiyya, served on a leather cloth with dates, cheese and butter, and the Muslims' question about whether she was a wife or a slave woman; Jaabir reports the Prophet handing out dates after Safiyya entered his tent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that because there were bluish marks around the eyes of Hadhrat Saflyya bint Huyay (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ asked her the reason for…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the bluish marks around Safiyya's eyes came from her husband's slap after she told him of a dream, and Safiyya says her hatred for the Prophet left once he explained his position on her father and husband.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ entered (his tent) with Hadhrat Saflyya (RA), Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) spent the night guarding the entrance.…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that Abu Ayyoob guarded the Prophet's tent after his marriage to Safiyya, and Ataa bin Yasaar reports that Aa'isha went to see Safiyya and the Prophet corrected her for calling Safiyya a Jewess, since she had accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that when Hadhrat Safiyya bint Huyay arrived (in Madinah), she was wearing gold earrings in the shape of palm leaves. She however…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyab reports that on arriving in Madinah Safiyya gave her gold palm-leaf earrings to Faatima and some other ladies.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that when the captives of the Banu Mustaliq tribe were distributed (amongst the Muslim army), Hadhrat Juwayriyyah bint Haarith happened to…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that Juwayriyyah, a captive of the Banu Mustaliq under a kitaabah contract with Thaabit bin Qais, came to the Prophet for help, and that he paid her ransom and married her, after which the Muslims freed the tribe's captives.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that Hadhrat Juwayriyyah bint Haarith (RA) said, "Three days before the arrival of Rasulullaah ﷺ I dreamt that the moon came from Yathrib and…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports how a man asked the Prophet to marry Faatima to him, and was told to send back the armour, worth about four hundred dirhams, that the Prophet had given him, which became Faatima's dowry.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Shihaab narrates that it was the year after signing the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah that Rasulullaah ﷺ left to perform Umrah. This occurred seven years after the…
narrations.summary: After the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, the Prophet ﷺ went for Umrah and sent Ja'far to propose to Maymoonah bint Haarith, whose affairs Abbaas arranged, and the marriage was consummated at Sarif.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that after marrying Hadhrat Maymoonah bint Haarith Rasulullaah ﷺ stayed in Makkah for three days. On the third day, Huwaytib bin Abdul Uzza came…
narrations.summary: A second narration says that after the marriage the Prophet ﷺ stayed in Makkah three days, and when Huwaytib and the Quraysh told him to leave, he left for Madinah and consummated the marriage at Sarif.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates, "When a marriage proposal for Faatima was sent to Rasulullaah ﷺ, a slave of mine asked, you know that a marriage proposal for Faatima has been…
narrations.summary: Ali narrates how he asked the Prophet ﷺ for Faatima's hand; he had no dowry except an armour, which the Prophet ﷺ accepted as her dowry.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) narrates that a group of the Ansaar once suggested to Hadhrat (RA) that he propose for Hadhrat Faatima (RA) hand in marriage. (When he approached…
narrations.summary: Buraydah reports that some Ansaar urged Ali to propose for Faatima, that the Prophet welcomed the proposal, and that Sa'd provided a sheep for the walima, and the Prophet prayed for the couple on their wedding night.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration similar to the above, states that the du'aa Rasulullaah ﷺ made was: "O Allaah! Bless the two of them and bless them in their two lion like sons." A…
narrations.summary: A narration of the same wedding night adds that the Prophet called Ummu Ayman to fetch Ali, prayed for the couple, sprinkled water on Ali, and then sent for Faatima, who came flustered, and reassured her.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asmaa bint Umays (RA) narrates that after Hadhrat Faatima (RA) was married to Hadhrat Ali Stsifig, all that they saw in her house was a straw mat spread out on…
narrations.summary: Asmaa bint Umays describes Faatima's wedding night at Ali's house: the Prophet ﷺ made du'aa over Ali and Faatima, said Ali was his brother, and prayed for Asmaa.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Asmaa bint Umays (RA) says, "I was present the night Rasulullaah ﷺ's daughter Faatima became a new bride. That morning, Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: In another narration, Asmaa bint Umays describes the Prophet ﷺ coming the morning after the wedding, making du'aa for Ali and sprinkling water on him, and then telling Faatima he had married her to the family member he loved most.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ got him married to Hadhrat Faatima (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ sent for some water and then gargled with it. Rasulullaah ﷺ then…
narrations.summary: Ali narrates that after marrying him to Faatima the Prophet had water brought, gargled, and sprinkled it on Ali's chest and between his shoulders, and recited the protective surahs over him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Albaa bin Ahmar reports from Hadhrat Ali (RA) that when he proposed for Rasulullaah ﷺ's daughter Hadhrat Faatima (RA), he sold a suit of armour he owned as well…
narrations.summary: Albaa bin Ahmar reports from Ali that Ali sold his armour and other goods for 480 dirhams to pay the dowry, that the Prophet had the money spent on perfume and clothing, and that the Prophet put something in Hasan's mouth that made him more knowledgeable than his brother.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates, "We attended the marriage of Ali and Faatima and have not witnessed a better marriage. The matting (on which we sat) was stuffed with the…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports attending the wedding of Ali and Faatima, which was simple: a matting stuffed with date-palm bark, raisins and dates served, and a sheepskin for her first night's bedding.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Faatima (RA) got married, Rasulullaah ﷺ gave her a blanket, a water bag and a leather pillow stuffed with Idhkhfr grass.
narrations.summary: Ali reports that when Faatima married, the Prophet gave her a blanket, a water-skin and a leather pillow stuffed with idhkhir grass.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Faatima (RA) to (her husband) Hadhrat Ali (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ gave her a blanket, a water bag…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports the Prophet's gifts to Faatima and Ali, and a quarrel over a date palm between Abu Bakr and Rabee'ah, in which Rabee'ah refused to repeat Abu Bakr's words, and the Prophet told Rabee'ah to forgive Abu Bakr, so that Abu Bakr wept.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rabee'ah (RA) says, "I was Rasulullaah ﷺ's servant. One day he asked, 'O Rabee'ah! Are you not interested in getting married?' I replied, 'I have no intention of…
narrations.summary: Rabee'ah Aslami tells how the Prophet ﷺ sent him to marry into an Ansaar tribe, how he paid a dowry of gold, and how the Prophet ﷺ made a waleemah with a sheep, and then how the Prophet ﷺ settled a land dispute between him and Abu Bakr, who then wept.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Barzah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Julaybeeb (RA) a man who frequently visited women and joked with them. Hadhrat Abu Barzah (RA) himself instructed his wife…
narrations.summary: Abu Barzah reports the Prophet's request to an Ansaari for his daughter in marriage on Julaybeeb's behalf, and then an account of Salmaan Faarsi's wedding night, in which he rejects the luxuries of his house and advises his wife to obey Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) reports that he once married a woman from the Kindah tribe and consummated the marriage in her house. On the night of the marriage, his…
narrations.summary: Salmaan Faarsi tells how, on his wedding night, he refused to let his companions in, removed the excess drapes and goods and servants, and advised his wife on obedience to Allaah, citing the Prophet's ﷺ advice to keep only what a traveller needs.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) states that when Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) returned after a long absence, Hadhrat Umar (RA) met him and remarked, "You…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that Salmaan asked Umar to marry him to one of his daughters, and Umar's family asked him to drop it; Thaabit Bunaani reports that Abu Dardaa went with Salmaan to propose for a Banu Layth woman, then married her himself, and Salmaan regretted the mix-up.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thaabit Bunaani narrates that when Yazeed bin Mu'aawiya sent to Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) a proposal for his daughter Dardaa, he rejected the proposal. One of…
narrations.summary: Thaabit Bunaani reports that Abu Dardaa refused Yazeed bin Mu'aawiya's proposal for his daughter Dardaa, married her instead to a poor Muslim, and explained that he wanted to protect her faith from the pull of wealth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ja'far reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once sent a proposal to Hadhrat Ali (RA) for his daughter ummu Kulthoom's hand in marriage. When Hadhrat Ali (RA) sent a…
narrations.summary: Abu Ja'far reports that Umar proposed to Ali for Ummu Kulthoom, Ali first deferred because of his brother Ja'far's sons, then agreed, and Umar told the Muhaajireen he wished to be the Prophet's relative; Ataa Khuraasaani gives the dowry as forty thousand dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) proposed to Hadhrat Ali (RA) for his daughter Ummu Kulthoom's hand in marriage, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "I am…
narrations.summary: Umar asked Ali for Ummu Kulthoom in marriage; Ali said he had reserved his daughters for the sons of Ja'far, Umar pleaded and Ali agreed, and Umar told the Muhaajireen he now wished to be the Prophet's relative; Ataa Khuraasaani adds that Umar gave a dowry of forty thousand dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that Hadhrat Amr bin Hurayth (RA) once proposed for the daughter of Hadhrat Adi bin Haatim (RA). Hadhrat Adi (RA) said, "I shall marry her (to…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that Amr bin Hurayth proposed for Adi bin Haatim's daughter on condition that he pay the 480-dirham dowry the Prophet gave Aa'isha, which Adi called the Sunnah; a second report gives Adi's reply in the same terms.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that when Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) and his brother extended marriage proposals to family from Yemen, Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) said, "I am Bilaal and this is…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that Bilaal and his brother, both freed from slavery, proposed to families in Yemen and were accepted; Maymoon reports that when Bilaal's brother, who claimed Arab descent, proposed to an Arab family, they required Bilaal to be present, and Bilaal's speech won the match.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Ruwaym reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Qurt Thumaali who was a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ was appointed governor by Hadhrat Umar (RA). He was…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Ruwaym reports that Abdullaah bin Qurt Thumaali, appointed governor by Umar, whipped the people who lit fires at a wedding in Hims, then told them in a sermon that they had imitated the disbelievers, recalling how Abu Jandal had held his own wedding simply.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that that the dowry Rasulullaah ﷺ gave (her) was twelve Awqiya and a Nash, which totalled an amount of five hundred Dirhams. She then went on…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet's dowry to her was twelve awqiya and a nash, totalling five hundred dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once mounted the pulpit and said, "I do not know who increased dowries above four hundred Dirhams because the dowry that…
narrations.summary: Masrooq reports that Umar forbade dowries above four hundred dirhams from the pulpit, then accepted a Quraysh woman's correction from the Qur'aan and withdrew the prohibition, saying everyone knows more than Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "Allaah forgive me! Everyone has more understanding than Umar." He then returned to the pulpit and said, "O people! I had forbidden you from…
narrations.summary: Umar admits that everyone understands more than he does, returns to the pulpit, and withdraws his limit of four hundred dirhams on dowries, so people may give what they wish.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that Hadhrat umar bin Khattaab (RA) once delivered a sermon. After duly praising Allaah, he said, "Take note that you people should not make your…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that Umar bin Khattaab once delivered a sermon, and the text stops there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) twice or thrice repeated, "Everyone has more understanding than Umar." He then returned to the pulpit and said, "O people! I had forbidden you from…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Khattaab withdrew his earlier limit on dowries, saying a man may give what he likes from his wealth, and admitted that everyone has more understanding than he does.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "Had (exorbitant) dowries been a source of status and elevation in the Aakhirah, the daughters and wives of Rasulullaah would have been most…
narrations.summary: Umar said that if exorbitant dowries brought status in the Aakhirah, the Prophet's ﷺ daughters and wives would have deserved them most.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Seereen reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) allowed dowries of two thousand Dirhams while Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) allowed dowries of four thousand.
narrations.summary: Ibn Seereen reports that Umar allowed dowries of two thousand Dirhams and Uthmaan allowed dowries of four thousand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) married Hadhrat Safiyya for a dowry of four hundred Dirhams. She however returned it saying that it was…
narrations.summary: Naafi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar married Safiyya for four hundred Dirhams, she called it too little, and he added two hundred more without his father Umar knowing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Seereen narrates that when Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) married a woman, he sent a hundred slave women to her, each one of them carrying a thousand Dirhams.
narrations.summary: Ibn Seereen narrates that when Hasan bin Ali married a woman, he sent her a hundred slave women, each carrying a thousand Dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports, "I once brought Rasulullaah ﷺ some Hareerah that I had cooked. Sauda was sitting between between Rasulullaah ﷺ and I, so I told her to have…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha relates how Sauda smeared her face with hareerah at the Prophet's urging, how Umar's approach sent them to wash, and Abu Bakr adds that the Prophet lowered his knee to let Sauda get back at Aa'isha.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Razeenah (RA) who was a freed slave of Rasulullaah ﷺ reports that Hadhrat Sauda Yamaaniyyah (RA) once visited Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) at a time when Hadhrat Hafsah…
narrations.summary: Razeenah reports that Sauda Yamaaniyyah visited Aa'isha while Hafsah was there, dressed to impress, and Hafsah teased her that the Prophet was coming and that the one-eyed Dajjaal had appeared, which Sauda, who was hard of hearing, took as true.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sauda (RA). cried out. She was extremely shocked and started to shiver. "Where shall I hide?" she asked. 'You will have to go to the tent," Hadhrat Hafsah told…
narrations.summary: Hafsah sends Sauda to hide in the tent; the Prophet finds her shivering, tells her the Dajjaal has not yet appeared, and dusts the dirt and cobwebs off her.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) said to Hadhrat Aa'isha "Rasulullaah ilil is coming to see us and we are looking so unkempt while she is gleaming between…
narrations.summary: Hafsah complains to Aa'isha that they look unkempt before the Prophet's visit, and Aa'isha recounts watching the Abyssinians' display with the Prophet, who remarks that the human and jinn devils flee from Umar when he appears.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "By Allaah! I saw Rasulullaah standing at the door of my room as some Abyssinians amused the people with their spears in…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet stood at her door and screened her with his shawl while she watched Abyssinians perform with spears in the masjid, and he stayed standing until she tired.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to spend time at Zaynab bint jahash's place drinking honey, Hafsah and I therefore collaborated and that whichever of us…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha relates how she, Sauda bint Zam'ah and Safiyya agreed to tell the Prophet that the honey he had taken at Hafsah's smelled of Maghaafeer; Sauda reports how she did it, and the Prophet later declined honey when Hafsah offered it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports, "I had always been eager to ask Umar about the two wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ concerning whom Allaah says(intheQur'aan): 'If the…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports how he asked Umar which two wives the Tahreem verse meant, and Umar then recounts going to the Prophet, who was reclining on a straw mat, to ask whether he had divorced his wives; after that Umar advised Hafsah and Aa'isha, and the Prophet vowed to stay away from his wives for a month.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ separated from his wives, I entered the Masjid where I saw the people fondling…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports Umar's account of hearing that the Prophet had divorced his wives, going to the Prophet who said no, then calling out in the masjid that the wives were not divorced, and the verse on checking rumours being revealed about this.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was sitting in his house while the Sahabah (RA) were sitting by his door. When Hadhrat Abu Bakr arrived and sought…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that Abu Bakr and Umar, refused entry at first, were let in when the Prophet sat silent among his wives; Umar's joke made the Prophet laugh, Abu Bakr and Umar rebuked their daughters, and the choice verses of Surah Ahzaab were revealed, with the Prophet offering Aa'isha the choice first.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas Slifflg reports that Hadhrat Aa'isha HIS said, "When the verses giving (us) the choice were revealed, Rasulullaah ﷺ began with me before any…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports Aa'isha's account of the choice the Prophet offered his wives under the verses of Surah Ahzaab, that she and the others chose Allaah, His Rasool and the Aakhirah, and that this was not counted as a divorce.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to her, "I know exactly when you are happy with me and when you are angry." When she asked Rasulullaah ﷺ how he…
narrations.summary: The Prophet tells Aa'isha he can tell when she is pleased or angry by how she swears, and she answers that she only leaves out his name while her love stays the same.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "I was once on a journey with Rasulullaah ﷺ when I ran a race with him and beat him. After I had put on some weight, I again ran a race…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha tells of racing the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and Ibn Abbaas describes staying the night with Maymoonah and watching the Prophet ﷺ pray thirteen rakaahs of tahajjud before Bilaal called the adhaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) relates, "(As a young boy) I was once the guest of (my maternal aunt) Maymoona on a night when she was not performing salaah. She…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas describes staying the night at his aunt Maymoona's house, where the Prophet rose for night prayer, made wudu, prayed thirteen rakaahs, and at Bilaal's call prayed two rakaahs before the iqaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that when an old woman once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he asked her who she was. When she informed him that her name was Jathaamah Muzaniyyah.…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet ﷺ gave a warm welcome to an old woman, named Jathaamah Muzaniyyah, whom he called Hasaanah, because she used to visit when Khadeeja was alive, and maintaining old ties is part of Imaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, 'When a particular old woman used to visit Nabi he always became very happy and would honour her greatly. 'May my parents be sacrificed for…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports the Prophet ﷺ honouring an old woman who used to visit when Khadeeja was alive, and Abu Tufayl saw him spread his shawl for a woman who had nursed him as a baby.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) reports that when he once went to see Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ 's short Abyssinian slave was busy rubbing his back. "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Umar found the Prophet's short Abyssinian servant rubbing his back, asked whether he had been hurt, and the Prophet said his camel had thrown him the night before.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood used to put on Rasulullaah ﷺ 's shoes for him. He would then walk ahead with Rasulullaah ﷺ 's…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood carried the Prophet's shoes and staff, screened him when he bathed, woke him when he slept and walked with him when no one else was there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, I was a young boy of ten and when he passed away, I was only twenty. It was my mother and aunts who…
narrations.summary: Anas says he was ten when the Prophet reached Madinah and twenty when he died, and that his mother and aunts urged him to serve the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thumaamah narrates that when someone asked Hadhrat Anas (RA) whether he was present during the Battle of Badr, he replied, "Shame on you! How could I ever absent…
narrations.summary: Asked whether he was at Badr, Anas says he was there as a boy to serve the Prophet, and Jaabir reports the Prophet praising Hasan and Husayn as excellent riders when they climbed on his back.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that there were twenty youngsters from the Ansaar who always stuck close to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ would always dispatch them whenever he…
narrations.summary: Anas says twenty young Ansaar always stayed close to the Prophet ﷺ and were sent on errands, and Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf says four or five Sahabah never left his side on journeys or at his door.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri SI relates, "We used to take turns (to be at Rasulullaah ﷺ's service) so that we could fulfil any need he had or he could dispatch us for any…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri relates that the Companions took turns serving the Prophet, and that when they were discussing the Dajjaal the Prophet came out and asked why they were whispering, reminding them he had forbidden private whispered discussion.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Assim bin Sufyaan says that it was either Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) or Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) whom he heard say, "I once sought permission from Rasulullaah ﷺ to…
narrations.summary: Aasim bin Sufyaan reports that either Abu Dardaa or Abu Dharr told him the Prophet ﷺ allowed him to spend the night at the Prophet's door so that he could wake him for any need.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) reports, "I once performed salaah with Rasulullaah during the month of Ramadhaan. He then got up to take a bath and I screened him. When some water…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah reports that after praying with the Prophet in Ramadhaan, the Prophet offered him the leftover bathing water, and when Hudhayfah bathed the Prophet screened him in return.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "I have never seen anyone more compassionate towards his family than Rasulullaah ﷺ. His son Ibraheem was given to a woman in the upper reaches of…
narrations.summary: Anas describes the Prophet's tenderness toward his son Ibraheem, whom he would kiss and hold on visits to the wet nurse's house. Amr reports the Prophet's words when Ibraheem died while still being suckled, promising him two nursing mothers in Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Haarith (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to place Abdullaah, Ubaydullaah and Katheer, all the children of Hadhrat Abbaas in a line and would…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Haarith reports that the Prophet lined up the children of Abbaas, promised a prize to whichever reached him first, and they raced to him, jumping onto his back and chest as he hugged and kissed them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) reports, "Whenever Rasulullaah giif returned from a journey, the children of his family were brought to receive him. When he once…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ja'far reports that when the Prophet returned from a journey he set Ja'far's son in front of him on the animal, then one of Faatimah's sons, Hasan or Husayn, behind, so three rode into Madinah together.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) also narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by me as I was playing with some children. He then picked me up together with one of Abbaas's…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ja'far recounts that the Prophet lifted him and a son of Abbaas onto his animal while he was playing. In a second report, Ubaydullaah and Quthm, the sons of Abbaas, are taken up in turn, and the Prophet passes his hand over Ja'far's son's head and prays that Allaah be Ja'far's successor for his children.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) says, 'You should have seen the time when we were children and I would be playing with Ubaydullaah and Quthm, both…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ja'far recalls being a child on the Prophet's mount, where the Prophet took him first and then Quthm, sons of Abbaas being the other children, and prayed that Allaah be a successor to Ja'far for his children.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) says, "When I saw Hasan and Husayn riding on Rasulullaah ﷺ's shoulders, I remarked, "What a fine horse you two are riding?' Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Khattaab says he saw Hasan and Husayn riding on the Prophet's shoulders and remarked on what a fine mount they had. The Prophet replied that they were fine riders.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came out of the house carrying Hadhrat Hasan (RA) on his shoulders when someone commented, "Dear child!…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that the Prophet came out carrying Hasan on his shoulders, and when someone called the child a fine conveyance, the Prophet said he was also a mighty fine rider.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once performing salaah when Hadhrat Hasan (RA) and Hadhrat husayn (RA) or (1) Muslim (vol.2 Pg.254). Ahmad has…
narrations.summary: Baraa bin Aazib reports that while the Prophet was in salaah, Hasan and Husayn climbed onto his back, and he held them gently when he finished. Jaabir adds that he once found the Prophet on all fours with the two children riding on him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) reports that it was midday when they were sitting around Rasulullaah tflf and Hadhrat Ummu Ayman (RA) arrived saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Hasan and…
narrations.summary: Ummu Ayman reports that Hasan and Husayn were lost, and the Prophet finds them clinging together beside a snake, which slides away from him, then carries one on each shoulder while Salmaan praises the boys as excellent riders.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "We were with Rasulullaah ﷺ when we were invited for a meal. When we came across Husayn playing with other children in the street, Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Jaabir describes how, on the way to a meal, the Prophet ran to catch Husayn playing in the street, made him laugh, hugged and kissed him, and said Husayn is from him and he is from Husayn.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat ibn is'haaq Sabee'ee reports that the wife of Hadhrat uthmaan bin Madh'oon once came to the wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ dressed in unattractive and old clothes. When…
narrations.summary: The wife of Uthmaan bin Madh'oon complained that he worshipped all night and fasted all day, the Prophet rebuked him, and she then dressed well again; at his deathbed she mourned him in verse.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration names the wife of Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) as Hadhrat Khowla bint Hakeem (RA) and that it was Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) whom she visited. The…
narrations.summary: A variant names the wife as Khowla bint Hakeem and says she visited Aa'isha, and records the Prophet telling Uthmaan that monasticism is not prescribed for them and that he himself fears Allaah most.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas reports, "My father got me married to a woman from the Quraysh. However, when she first came to me, I paid no attention to her…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr neglected his new wife through his worship, his father Amr complained to the Prophet, and the Prophet had him reduce his fasting and Qur'aan recitation and fast on alternate days like Dawood.
