narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Juhayfah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ had made a bond of brotherhood between Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA). When Hadhrat Salmaan (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abu Juhayfah reports that the Prophet made a bond of brotherhood between Salmaan and Abu Dardaa. When Salmaan visited, he made Abu Dardaa break his fast, urged him to sleep at night, and told him that each person has rights owed to their Rabb, their body and their wife. The Prophet confirmed that Salmaan was right.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) the daughter of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) relates, "When Zubayr married me, he possessed neither any property, money, slaves nor anything else apart from…
narrations.summary: Asmaa bint Abi Bakr describes her hardships after marrying Zubayr, who owned only a horse. She carried date stones from land the Prophet had given him, felt too shy to ride with the Prophet when he offered her a ride, and was made to feel the weight of Zubayr's possessiveness, until her father sent a servant to take over the horse.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) the daughter of Hadhrat Abu Bakr was married to Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awwaam (RA). When she complained to her father about…
narrations.summary: Asmaa bint Abi Bakr complained to her father about Zubayr's strict nature, and Abu Bakr told her to be patient, since a woman with a pious husband who does not remarry after he dies will be reunited with him in Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Kahmas Hilaali reports that they were once sitting with Hadhrat Umar when a lady arrived. She sat down and said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! While the evil nature of my…
narrations.summary: A woman complains to Umar that her husband Abu Salamah has grown harsh while his goodness has faded; Umar hears both, strikes her, gives her three garments and warns the husband, then quotes the Prophet on the best generations of the Ummah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that a woman once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, "I have come to complain to you about a man who is the best of all men apart from a man whose…
narrations.summary: A woman complains to Umar that her husband worships all night and fasts all day; Umar excuses her, and Ka'b bin Soor, asked to judge, cites the Qur'aan on multiple wives and advises a balance of fasting, prayer and the wife's rights, so Umar appoints him judge of Basrah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to the lady, "Be honest with me and do not shy away from the truth." She then said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineenl I am a…
narrations.summary: Aatika, bound by her late husband's condition over an orchard, is freed by Ali's ruling to remarry Umar, and at the wedding feast Ali recites her grief verses to her, making her weep.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qataadah narrates that a woman once said to Hadhrat Umar (RA), "My husband stands in salaah all night and fasts all day." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to her, "Are you…
narrations.summary: Qataadah reports that a woman complained to Umar that her husband stood in prayer all night and fasted all day. Umar questioned her, then, on the advice of Ka'b bin Soor, ordered the husband to spend one night in four with his wife and to skip one fast in four, since she has a right to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Gharzah (RA) once led Hadhrat Ibn Arqam by the hand to his wife and asked her, "Do you hate me." "Yes I do," she replied. "What made you do this?" Hadhrat Ibn…
narrations.summary: Abu Gharzah led Ibn Arqam by the hand to his wife and asked her if she hated him, and she said yes. When Umar called them both, the wife said she had been made to swear and could not lie. Umar said that not every home is built on love, and that many are built on courtesy, social standing and Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Salamah bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf narrates that Hadhrat Aatika the daughter of Hadhrat Zaid bin Amr bin Nufayl (RA) was married to Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) the…
narrations.summary: Abu Salamah bin Abdur Rahmaan recounts that Aatika bint Zaid, married to Abdullaah bin Abi Bakr, was left an orchard on condition she did not remarry. After his death at Taa'if she mourned him in verse. Umar later proposed, and Ali advised that she could remarry if she returned the orchard. At the wedding feast Ali recited her verse to her, and she wept loudly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nadbah the freed slave of Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA) reports that her mistress, (Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA)) once sent her to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas. When she…
narrations.summary: Nadbah, sent by Maymoonah to Ibn Abbaas, sees two beds; Maymoonah finds his wife was menstruating and reproaches Ibn Abbaas, reminding him that the Prophet touched his wives during menstruation.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat ikrama says that he is not sure whether it was Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas who invited his cousin for a meal or whether it was his cousin who invited him.…
narrations.summary: Ikrimah reports that Ibn Abbaas rebuked a cousin who called a slave woman an adulteress, warning that such slander will be punished in the Aakhirah and that Allaah dislikes vulgar speech.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Imraan of Palestine reports that while the wife of Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas SIP was busy cleaning his hair of lice, she called for her slave woman. When the…
narrations.summary: Abu Imraan reports that Amr bin Al Aas rebuked his wife for falsely calling a slave woman an adulteress, warned her of the eighty lashes waiting on the Day of Judgement, and advised freeing the slave as compensation.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Mutawakkil narrates that Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) had a Negro slave who had caused grief to the entire household because of something she had done. Raising…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah raised his whip over his slave woman, held back for fear of retaliation on the Day of Judgement, and then set her free, saying she was Allaah's.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Qais or ibn Abul Qais says that he was with the delegation of Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin jarraah (RA) that received Hadhrat Umar (RA) when he arrived…
narrations.summary: On Umar's arrival in Shaam, Abu Ubaydah persuaded him not to stop the sword-bearing entertainers of Adhri'aat, since that would look like breaking the treaty, and Umar agreed, placing his family under Abu Ubaydah's command.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar Si reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat, Zubayr (RA) once had a race, Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) beat Hadhrat Umar and cried out, "I beat…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar and Zubayr raced twice; each won one race, and each called out that he had won by the Rabb of the Kabah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saleem bin Handhalah reports, "We once went to Hadhrat Ubay bin (RA) iliaiis to listen to Ahadeeth from him. (When he had completed) He stood up and we also stood…
narrations.summary: Saleem bin Handhalah says they walked with Ubay after a session of hadith, and Umar warned that being followed like that was a source of pride for the teacher and of shame for the students.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari narrates that a man once came to Hadhrat Salmaan and said, "How pleasant was the behaviour of people today! I had been travelling and I swear by…
narrations.summary: Abul Bakhtari reports a traveller telling Salmaan that every host had treated him like a son of his own father, and Salmaan said this shows Imaan is fresh, like a newly loaded beast that carries its load quickly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hayya bint Abu Hayya reports, "it was midday when a man came to my house. 'What is it you want, O servant of Allaah?' I asked. He explained, 'My friend and I have…
narrations.summary: Hayya bint Abu Hayya tells how a man came to her house at midday seeking shade and water, and when he named himself Abu Bakr she spoke of the old tribal wars and the love Islaam created, and he said the bond lasts while the leaders stay upright.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haarith bin Mu'aawiya narrates that when he came to Hadhrat Umar Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "In what condition did you leave the people of Shaam?" After he had…
narrations.summary: Haarith bin Mu'aawiya reports that Umar asked about the people of Shaam and warned that mixing with the mushrikeen leads to eating and drinking with them, which would spoil their good state.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ayaadh narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once instructed Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari to present to him all his earnings and expenditure (as governor) on a single…
narrations.summary: Ayaadh reports that Umar ordered Abu Moosa Ash'ari to present his accounts as governor on one piece of leather, and when Umar was impressed by Abu Moosa's Christian clerk he had Abu Moosa dismiss him, reciting the verse forbidding taking Jews and Christians as confidantes.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ never found fault with food ever. If he liked it, he ate and if he did not, he would leave it (without comment)."
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet never found fault with food, eating what he liked and leaving the rest without comment.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat All (RA) reports that the portion Rasulullaah ﷺ liked most of a goat was the foreleg.
narrations.summary: Ali reports that the part of a goat the Prophet liked most was the foreleg.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ liked the foreleg of an animal. When the foreleg was once poisoned, everyone suspected that it was the Jews who…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that the Prophet liked the foreleg and that, when it was once poisoned, people blamed the Jews. Jaabir says the Prophet remarked that the family seemed to know he liked meat when they slaughtered a goat for him, and Anas says the Prophet loved bottle gourd and he picked it out for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas giisig also narrates that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ ate food, he licked his three fingers (with which he ate).
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet licked his three fingers after eating.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ (was so humble that he) ate on the floor, tied the feet of goats when they were to be milked and even accepted the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says the Prophet was so humble that he ate on the floor, tied the legs of goats he was about to milk, and accepted slaves' invitations to plain barley bread.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahyaa bin Abu Katheer reports that a plate of Thareed came to Rasulullaah ﷺ every day from Hadhrat Sa'd bin ubaadah (RA). It went with him to the house of…
narrations.summary: Yahyaa bin Abu Katheer reports that Sa'd bin Ubaadah sent the Prophet a plate of thareed every day, and it went with him to whichever wife's house he was in.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when some goat's milk was milked for Rasulullaah ﷺ , he drank it and then gargled his mouth saying, "It has some stickiness (which needs to…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that after drinking goat's milk the Prophet rinsed his mouth, saying the milk left a sticky residue.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once stopped over at a certain place, a woman sent her son with a goat to Rasulullaah ﷺ . Rasulullaah ﷺ milked the…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr reports that when the Prophet stopped at a place, he milked the goats a boy brought, gave the first milk to the boy's mother, the second to Abu Bakr, and drank the third himself.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to keep his right hand free for acts such as eating, drinking and making wudhu. His left hand he would keep free for…
narrations.summary: Ibraheem reports that the Prophet kept his right hand for eating, drinking and wudhu, and his left for cleaning himself. Ja'far bin Abdullaah reports that his grandfather Hakam, seeing him eat from all over the plate, told him not to eat like Shaytaan does.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar bin Abu Salamah (RA) reports, "I was once eating with Rasulullaah ﷺ when I started taking meat from all over the plate. Rasulullaah said to me, 'Eat from…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Abu Salamah says that while eating with the Prophet he kept reaching all over the dish, and the Prophet told him to eat from what was in front of him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummayyah bin Makhshi (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once saw a man eating without first reciting Bismillaah, When there was only a single morsel left, he lifted…
narrations.summary: Ummayyah bin Makhshi reports the Prophet's remark that Shaytaan ate with a man who did not say Bismillaah until he named Allaah. Hudhayfah reports the Prophet stopping a Bedouin and a girl from grabbing food without Bismillaah, since food becomes lawful for Shaytaan when Allaah's name is not taken.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was eating with six others when a Bedouin came and ate all the food in two morsels. Rasulullaah remarked, "Had he recited…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that while the Prophet ate with six others, a Bedouin ate all the food in two morsels, and the Prophet said the food would have sufficed for them all had he said Bismillaah, and taught that one should say it before eating.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr (RA) relates, "Nabi ﷺ once stopped over by my father, who served him a meal of Saweeq W and Hais. After Rasulullaah ﷺ had eaten, my father…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Busr reports that the Prophet was served a meal and drink by his father, tossed the date stones behind him, and when he mounted, his father held the reins and asked for du'aa; the Prophet asked Allaah to bless them in their sustenance and to forgive and have mercy on them.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr (RA) says, "When my father once asked my mother to prepare some food for Rasulullaah ﷺ, she prepared some Thareed. My…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Busr reports that his father invited Rasulullaah ﷺ to a meal of thareed, and the Prophet ﷺ afterwards made du'aa for the household.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat ibn A'bad reports that Hadhrat (RA) once asked, "O Ibn A'bad! Do you know what is the right of food?" "What is the right of food?" Ibn A'bad asked. Hadhrat Ali…
narrations.summary: Ibn A'bad reports that Ali taught him the words to say before eating and the words of thanks to say after.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "Beware of excessive and drinking because it harms the body, is the cause of many diseases and leads to lethargy in salaah. Rather be…
narrations.summary: Umar warns against excessive eating and drinking, saying it harms the body, causes illness and dulls salaah, and that moderation is healthier.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Mah'dhoora (RA) reports that he was once sitting with Hadhrat Umar when Hadhrat Safwaan bin Umayyah (RA) brought a platter (of food). Hadhrat Umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abu Mah'dhoora reports that when Safwaan bin Umayyah brought a platter, Umar invited the poor and slaves to share it, and then rebuked those who will not let their slaves eat with them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maalik bin Anas reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) stopped over in Juhfah, Ibn Aamir bin Kurayz instructed his baker to take food to Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Maalik bin Anas reports that Ibn Umar had his baker pour every dish into one plate, and that Ibn Aamir corrected the baker who mocked him by calling Ibn Umar his leader.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat ja'farnarratesthatbecauseHadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) always ate the seeds of the pomegranate, someone asked, "O Ibn Abbaasl Why do you do that?" He…
narrations.summary: Ja'far reports that Ibn Abbaas always ate pomegranate seeds because he had heard that every pomegranate grows from a seed from Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalim says, "I was with my master Zaid bin Sowhaan when Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi passed by us after purchasing a wasaq of grain. 'O Abu Abdullaah!' Zaid called…
narrations.summary: Saalim reports that Zaid bin Sowhaan questioned Salmaan Faarsi for buying a large quantity of grain, and Salmaan said that securing one's sustenance frees the heart for worship; a second report has Salmaan saying he loves to eat from the work of his own hands.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi narrates that Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) said, "I love to eat from the efforts of my own hands."
narrations.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that Salmaan Faarsi said he loved to eat from the work of his own hands.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah SI once said, "I had fifteen dates so I broke my fast with five, ate Sehri with five and kept the other five to break my fast with."
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah says he had fifteen dates, broke his fast with five, ate Sehri with five and kept five to break his fast with later.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muslim who was the freed slave of Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) says, "When Hadhrat Ali (RA) once asked for a drink, I brought him a cup of water and blew into…
narrations.summary: Muslim, freed slave of Ali, reports that when Ali asked for a drink, Ali refused the cup he had brought him and told him to drink it first.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla says that he was once with Hadhrat Umar when he said, "I saw Abu Qaasim (Rasulullaah) ﷺ wearing a narrow-sleeved cloak made in Shaam."
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla reports that Umar said he saw the Prophet ﷺ wearing a narrow-sleeved cloak made in Shaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jundub bin Makeeth (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ wore his best clothing whenever he received a delegation and would instruct the senior Sahabah to do the same. On the…
narrations.summary: Jund bin Makeeth reports that the Prophet ﷺ wore his best clothing to receive delegations and that Abu Bakr and Umar dressed the same; Salamah bin Akwa reports that Uthmaan's loincloth reached halfway down his calves and that Uthmaan said it was the garment of the Prophet ﷺ.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ash'ath bin Sulaym reports from his aunt that her uncle said, "I was walking in Madinah one day when someone behind me said, 'Lift up your loincloth because it…
narrations.summary: Ash'ath bin Sulaym reports that the Prophet ﷺ told a man in Madinah to lift his loincloth, and Abu Burdah reports that Aa'isha showed a patched shawl and a coarse loincloth, saying the Prophet's soul was taken in those two garments.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urtimu salamah'ESSSSfc'says, "The garment Rasulullaah ﷺ loved most was his Qamees "
narrations.summary: Umm Salamah says the garment the Prophet ﷺ loved most was his qamees.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asmaa bint Yazeed (RA) reports that the sleeve of Rasulullaah ﷺ 's Qamees reached his wrists. Hadhrat jaabir (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah illjl was wearing a…
narrations.summary: Several short reports describe the Prophet's ﷺ clothing: sleeves reaching the wrists, a black turban on entering Makkah and when preaching, an oily bandage while ill, and turban tails hung between the shoulders, which Ibn Umar also did.

narrations.excerpt: when Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was once asked about Rasulullaah ﷺ's bedding, she replied, "it was made of leather and stuffed with the bark of a date palm."
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says that when asked about the Prophet's ﷺ bedding, it was leather stuffed with the bark of a date palm.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) relates, "A lady from the Ansaar once visited me and saw that Rasulullaah ﷺ's bedding comprised of cloak that was double-folded. She then left and…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha tells how a woman of the Ansaar saw the Prophet's ﷺ bedding, a double-folded cloak, and sent a wool-stuffed bedding; the Prophet ﷺ ordered it returned and said that had he willed, Allaah would have made mountains of gold and silver travel with him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad narrates that he once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "what was Rasulullaah ﷺ's bedding like in your home?" She replied, "it was made of leather and stuffed…
narrations.summary: Muhammad reports asking Aa'isha and then Hafsah about the Prophet's ﷺ bedding, and Hafsah's folded sheet was left as it was because its softness prevented the Prophet ﷺ from performing night salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Omar (RA) reports that he saw Rasulullaah ﷺ send for some new clothing. When it reached his collar-bone as he was putting it on, he recited: "All praise is for…
narrations.summary: Umar reports that when the Prophet ﷺ put on new clothing he recited the du'aa of thanks, and said that giving the old clothes to a poor person for Allaah's sake keeps the wearer under Allaah's protection.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat All (RA) reports that he was sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ near (the graveyard of) Baqee on a rainy day when a woman passed by on her donkey, carrying a heavy load.…
narrations.summary: Ali reports that when a woman fell from her donkey and her trousers kept her covered, the Prophet ﷺ prayed for forgiveness for the women of his Ummah who wear trousers and told the men always to wear trousers to protect their women.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dihya bin Khalifah Kalbi (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent him as envoy to Heraclius (the Byzantine Emperor), upon his return, Rasulullaah gave Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Dihya Kalbi reports that after he was sent as an envoy to Heraclius, the Prophet ﷺ gave him fine Egyptian cloth to make a qamees and a scarf for his wife, and then told him to have her wear something underneath so the scarf was not revealing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Usaamah bin Zaid (RA) relates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ gave me some of the thick but delicate white Egyptian cloth that he had given Dihya. I subsequently gave it to my…
narrations.summary: Usaama bin Zaid says the Prophet ﷺ gave him the same white Egyptian cloth he had given Dihya, and when he gave it to his wife, told him to have her wear something underneath because the cloth showed the shape of her bones.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that when she once wore some clothing, she kept looking down at it as she walked about in the room, turning about as she did so. (Her father)…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says that when she wore a new garment and kept admiring herself in it, her father Abu Bakr told her that Allaah was not looking at her with favour.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "I once wore a new upper garment of mine and was very taken aback by it as I looked at it. Hadhrat Abu Bakr said to me,…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha gives another account in which Abu Bakr told her that self-admiration over worldly beauty displeases Allaah, so she took the garment off and gave it away in charity.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdl Azeez bin Abu Jameelah Ansaari reports that the sleeves of Hadhrat Umar's Qamees never extended past his wrists. ® Hadhrat Badeel bin Maysara reports that…
narrations.summary: Several reports describe Umar's clothing: his qamees sleeves reached only his wrists, he went to Jumu'ah in a cloak from Sumbulaan and apologised for being late, he tied his loincloth above the navel, and Anas said that apart from Umar and his son, all the Sahabah wore khazz, which he disliked.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hishaam bin Khaalid reports that he saw Hadhrat Umar (RA) tie his loincloth above his navel. Hadhrat Aamir bin Ubaydah Baahili narrates that when he once asked…
narrations.summary: Hishaam bin Khaalid saw Umar tie his waist-wrap above his navel, and Aamir bin Ubaydah Baahili reports Anas saying he wished khazz had never been created, since all the Sahabah except Umar and his son wore it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once came out to them wearing cotton clothing. When the people stared at him, he recited a couplet (which meant): "The…
narrations.summary: Masrooq reports that Umar came out in cotton clothing, recited a couplet saying all wealth and children will perish, and said that compared with the Aakhirah this world is a fleeting thing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Abdullaah who was the freed slave of Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Haad says, "It was on a Friday that I once saw Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) standing on the…
narrations.summary: Abu Abdullaah, freed slave of Shaddaad bin Haad, says he saw Uthmaan on a Friday standing on the pulpit in a Kufa shawl and a coarse Aden loincloth worth four or five dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Moosa bin Talha says, "Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) used to lean on a staff (as he came to the Masjid) on Fridays. He was one of the most handsome men wearing his…
narrations.summary: Moosa bin Talha says that on Fridays Uthmaan leaned on a staff on his way to the Masjid and was one of the most handsome men, wearing a cream loincloth and shawl as he sat on the pulpit.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat SulaymAbuAamirsays,"lsaw Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) wearing a Yemeni shawl worth a hundred Dirhams."
narrations.summary: Sulaym Abu Aamir says he saw Uthmaan wearing a Yemeni shawl worth a hundred dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Rabee'ah bin Haarith says, "The Sahabah (RA) used to spend generously on such clothing for their wives that was both beautiful as well as concealing.…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Rabee'ah bin Haarith says the Sahabah spent generously on fine, modest clothing for their wives, and that Uthmaan wore a silk-edged shawl worth two hundred dirhams that he had given his wife Naa'ilah, wearing it only to please her.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab narrates that a delegation from Basrah once came to see Hadhrat Ali (RA). Amongst them was a man belonging to the whose name was Ja'd bin Na'Ja.…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Wahab reports that a delegation from Basrah criticised the clothing of Ali, and Ali replied that his clothing was far from pride and a fitting example for people to follow.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Qais reports that when someone asked Hadhrat Ali (RA) why he patched his Qamees, he replied, "The heart humbles with it and the Mu'min is able to follow…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Qais reports that when Ali was asked why he patched his qamees, he said the heart is humbled by it and the believer is able to follow the example.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa Abu Muhammad says, "I once saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) wearing an unwashed Qamees made of extremely coarse cloth,"
narrations.summary: Ataa Abu Muhammad says he once saw Ali wearing an unwashed qamees of extremely coarse cloth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Hudhayl reports, "I once saw on Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib a Qamees made in Ray which was such that when he stretched out his arms, the sleeves…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Hudhayl reports that Ali's qamees from Ray had sleeves reaching his fingertips, and that Ali trimmed off the excess, saying sleeves should never extend beyond the hands.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Azdi who was one of the Imaams of the Azd tribe reports that he once saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) come to the marketplace and say, "Who has a good Qamees for…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Azdi says he saw Ali at the market looking for a qamees for three dirhams, and that Ali paid the price the trader named, though he thought the trader had lowered it because he was the Ameerul Mu'mineen; Ali then had the extra sleeve cut off.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ibraheem says, "I saw Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) wearing a shawl or a suit of clothing worth four or five hundred Dirhams."
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Ibraheem saw Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf wearing a shawl or suit of clothing worth four or five hundred Dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qur'ah relates that when he saw Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) wearing coarse and stiff clothing, he approached him saying, "O Abu Abdur Rahmaan! I have brought…
narrations.summary: Qur'ah offered Abdullaah bin Umar soft cotton cloth from Khurasaan, since his own clothes were coarse. Ibn Umar checked that it was not silk and refused it, saying he feared becoming a boastful snob and that Allaah detests the boastful.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Hubaysh relates that he saw Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar wearing two cloths made by the Ma'aafir (a tribe in Yemen), which reached halfway down his…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Hubaysh saw Abdullaah bin Umar wearing two cloths made by the Ma'aafir, a tribe of Yemen, reaching halfway down his calves.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Waqdaan reports that he once heard a person asking Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar SSI "What clothing should I wear?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar replied, "Clothing…
narrations.summary: Waqdaan reports that a man asked Abdullaah bin Umar what clothing he should wear. Ibn Umar advised clothing that neither fools would mock nor sensible people criticise for extravagance, which costs between five and ten Dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq reports that he saw Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar illi wear his loincloth halfway down his calves. In another narration, he mentions that he saw several…
narrations.summary: Abu Is'haaq reports seeing Abdullaah bin Umar wear his waist-wrap halfway down his calves, and seeing Usaamah bin Zaid, Zaid bin Arqam and Baraa bin Aazib dressed the same way.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Abu Sulaymaan reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas once purchased and wore a garment worth a thousand Dirhams.
narrations.summary: Uthmaan bin Abu Sulaymaan reports that Abdullaah bin Abbaas once bought and wore a garment worth a thousand Dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Katheer bin Ubayd narrates that when he once went to Ummul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) she told him to wait until she completed stitching her old garment. As…
narrations.summary: Katheer bin Ubayd says that when he visited Aa'isha she was stitching an old garment, and she told him that a person who does not wear old clothes does not deserve new ones and may not have them in the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed reports that when someone entered Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)'s room as she was stitching her old garment, he remarked, "O Ummul Mu'mineen! Has Allaah not…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed reports Aa'isha mending an old garment and saying that one who will not wear old clothes does not deserve new ones; then Asmaa bint Abi Bakr, already blind, sent back fine garments from Marw and Quw that her son Mundhir had brought, and accepted only plain ones.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a woman once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! My upper garment is all tattered." "Have I not given you anything to…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that a woman came to Umar saying her upper garment was torn, and Umar gave her a fine garment and told her to wear the old one while baking and cooking.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Kharasha bin Hurr reports that he was once looking at Hadhrat Umar as a youngsten passed by, wearing his loincloth below his ankles and dragging it along as he…
narrations.summary: Kharasha bin Hurr reports that Umar saw a youth whose loincloth trailed below his ankles, asked him if he was menstruating, and then had the trailing end cut off with a knife.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that they were in Azerbaijan under the command of Hadhrat Utba bin Farqad (RA) when a letter from Hadhrat Umar arrived. The letter read:…
narrations.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports Umar's letter to the army under Utba bin Farqad in Azerbaijan, telling them to dress simply, avoid luxury and non-Arab attire, and not to wear silk, which the Prophet ﷺ forbade beyond the width indicated by his finger.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Muhammad ﷺ says that they were sitting in a gathering between the pulpit and the grave of Rasulullaah ﷺ . In the gathering was Hadhrat Imraan bin Abu…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Muhammad reports a gathering discussing the rooms of the Prophet's ﷺ wives, which Waleed bin Abdil Malik had ordered included in the Masjid; Ataa Khuraasaani and Imraan bin Abu Anas describe their simplicity, Sa'eed bin Musayyib wished they had been left standing, and Abu Umaamah said the same so people would see how little the Prophet ﷺ needed.

narrations.excerpt: with Conviction that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah isS-SaSs narrates, "We were a group of Sahabah (RA) including Abu Bakr and Umar…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah searches for the Prophet ﷺ, who had stepped away from a group of Companions, and finds him in an orchard; the Prophet sends him with his shoes to give glad tidings of Jannah to anyone who sincerely testifies that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah, and Umar, fearing people would rely on it, persuades the Prophet to let them keep doing good deeds.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates, "When I came outdoors one night, I happened to see Rasulullaah ﷺ walking all alone. Thinking to myself that perhaps Rasulullaah ﷺ did not…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr walks at night with the Prophet ﷺ, who tells him Jibra'eel brought the good news that whoever dies without shirk enters Jannah, even if he commits adultery or theft.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that an old Bedouin called Hadhrat Alqama'bin Ulaatha isI once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I am an old man who is unable to…
narrations.summary: An old Bedouin, Alqama bin Ulaatha, says he cannot learn the Qur'aan but testifies that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah and that Muhammad ﷺ is the servant and Rasool of Allaah, and the Prophet ﷺ praises his understanding.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) narrates that he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "I know a statement which if a person says sincerely from his heart, he will become forbidden to the fire…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan says he heard the Prophet ﷺ speak of a statement that keeps a sincere speaker from the Fire, and Umar explains that it is the testimony that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah, the statement the Prophet ﷺ urged his uncle Abu Taalib to recite at his death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ya'la bin Shaddaad reports that Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) was also present and confirming Hadhrat Abu Shaddaad (RA) when he said, "We were with Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Abu Shaddaad, reported by Ya'la bin Shaddaad with Ubaadah bin Saamit confirming, recounts how the Prophet ﷺ had the door shut and had the Companions raise their hands and say Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, then lowered his own hands praising Allaah and affirming the promise of Jannah for this Kalimah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rufaa'ah Juhani (RA) reports that they were once returning with Rasulullaah ﷺ (to Madinah) when we arrived in Kudayd. When some people started seeking permission…
narrations.summary: Rufaa'ah Juhani reports that at Kudayd the Prophet ﷺ told those who had asked leave to go home that whoever sincerely testifies and walks the right path will enter Jannah, and that 70,000 of his Ummah will enter without reckoning.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration clarifies that it was Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) who said, "Whoever seeks leave after this must be a fool!"
narrations.summary: A variant clause says it was Abu Bakr who called anyone who sought leave after this a fool.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ charged a particular person for doing something, the man denied it saying, "No. I swear by the Being besides Whom there…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that when the Prophet ﷺ charged a man for a deed the man denied with an oath, the Prophet told him to atone by testifying that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "When a man took a false oath using the words 'I swear by the Being besides Whom there is none worthy…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr reports that the Prophet ﷺ said a man who swore falsely using the words of the Kalimah was forgiven because of those words.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "When the people of Jahannam will get together, amongst them will also be those who faced the Qibla…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports the Prophet ﷺ saying that Muslims in Jahannam will be taken out after the unbelievers see them, and recites Surah Hijr verses 1-2; Anas reports that believers in Laa Ilaaha Illallaah will be removed from Jahannam by Allaah's mercy after idol-worshippers mock them.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration of Tabraani reports that because of the blackness on their faces, they will be called 'the people from Jahannam'. They will then plead to Allaah saying,…
narrations.summary: A narration reported via Tabraani adds that the believers will be called 'the people from Jahannam' because of blackness on their faces, until they bathe in a river in Jannah and the name is removed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Islaam shall fade away just as decorative work fades from a garment. People will have no idea what fasting,…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah reports the Prophet ﷺ saying Islaam will fade until only a few old people remain who recite Laa Ilaaha Illallaah from following their forefathers, and that this Kalimah will save them from Jahannam, as Hudhayfah tells Sila when Sila keeps asking.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "The people with the clearest record with Allaah 3,1853515 and who know Him best are those who have the most love for and who most honour the…
narrations.summary: Ali says the people closest to Allaah are those who most love and honour the believers in Laa Ilaaha Illallaah; Abu Dardaa, told that Abu Sa'd bin Munabbih freed a hundred slaves, says that keeping Imaan attached to the heart and the tongue moist with Dhikr is better.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalim bin Abul Ja'd reports that someone once informed Hadhrat Abu Dardaa that Abu Sa'd bin Munabbih had set a hundred slaves free. Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says that freeing a hundred slaves from one man's wealth is a great deed, but better is imaan that stays in the heart day and night, with the tongue kept moist with the dhikr of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Verily Allaah has distributed good character amongst you just as He has distributed your sustenance: Whereas Allaah has given…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says Allaah gives Imaan only to those He loves, and that whoever is too miserly to give Sadaqah, too afraid to fight in Jihaad, or too weak for night worship should recite Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, Allaahu Akbar, Al Hamdu Lillaah and Subhaanallaah abundantly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that whenever Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha met one of the Sahabah (RA), he say to him, "Come! Let us believe in our Rabb for a…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha would invite Companions to believe for a moment by talking about Allaah, and the Prophet ﷺ forgave him after a man complained; Ataa bin Yasaar adds that Abdullaah said this to increase Imaan when a companion asked whether they were not already believers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shurayh bin Abdullaah reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha would grab hold of the hand of one of the Sahabah (RA) and say, "Stand with me so that we may…
narrations.summary: Shurayh bin Abdullaah reports that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha would take hold of a Companion's hand and ask him to stand with him in a gathering of Dhikr to believe for a while.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) says, "Abdullaah bin Rawaaha once caught hold of my hand saying, 'Come! Let us believe for a moment because the heart overturns faster than a pot…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says Abdullaah bin Rawaaha took his hand and said to believe for a moment, because the heart overturns faster than a pot boiling at its pitch.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) says, "When Abdullaah bin Rawaaha would meet me, he would say, 'O Uwaymir! Sit down so that we may discuss (Imaan) for a while.' We would then sit…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says Abdullaah bin Rawaaha would call him to sit and discuss Imaan, likening it to a qamees that is taken off and put on again, and that the heart overturns faster than a boiling pot.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) would grab hold of the hands of one or two Sahabah (RA) and say, "Stand awhile with me so that we may renew our…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr reports that Umar would take one or two Companions by the hand and ask them to stand with him to renew their Imaan, and they would talk about Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aswad bin Hilaal reports that they were walking with Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal when he said to them, "Sit with us so that we may believe for a moment."
narrations.summary: Aswad bin Hilaal reports that while walking with them, Mu'aadh bin Jabal asked them to sit with him so they could believe for a moment.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "Renew your Imaan." "O Rasulullaah ﷺ someone asked, "How are we to renew our Imaan?" Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet ﷺ told people to renew their Imaan, and when asked how, said to recite Laa Ilaaha Illallaah abundantly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates that a man once came to Rasulullaah saying, "My brother is suffering from diarrhoea." "Give him honey to drink," Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that a man's brother had diarrhoea, honey made it worse twice, and the Prophet ﷺ told the man to try again, saying Allaah speaks the truth and the brother's belly is lying, until the brother was cured.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaynab (RA) who was the wife of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says, "Whenever (my husband) Abdullaah came home after relieving himself, he would clear his throat…
narrations.summary: Zaynab, wife of Abdullaah bin Mas'ood, reports that he cut a thread tied to her neck, calling incantations and amulets shirk, and told her to recite the Prophet's ﷺ supplication for cure instead.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ikramah reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha (RA) was once lying beside his wife when he got up and went to have intercourse with one of his slave women in…
narrations.summary: Ikrimah reports that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha was caught by his wife with a slave-woman; when she came with a knife he recited verses, and she said she believed in the Book of Allaah and rejected what her eyes had seen, and the Prophet ﷺ smiled broadly when told.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Habeeb bin Abu Thaabit narrates that when he went to pose some questions to Hadhrat Abu Waa'il (RA), the Sahabi related to them that when they were fighting at…
narrations.summary: Habeeb bin Abu Thaabit reports Abu Waa'il's account that at Siffeen Sahl bin Hunayf reminded them that at Hudaybiyyah they had accepted the treaty rather than fight, and that Umar questioned the treaty until the Prophet ﷺ and then Abu Bakr assured him.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Sahl bin Hunayf (RA) said, "O people! You have only your own opinions to blame! I have seen myself on the day of Abu Jandal (when…
narrations.summary: Sahl bin Hunayf and Umar recall the Hudaybiyyah treaty: Abu Jandal pleads not to be returned, the Prophet ﷺ says he cannot disobey Allaah, and both the Prophet and Abu Bakr assure Umar that he will perform Tawaaf at the Kabah, after which Umar makes amends.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that as Rasulullaah ﷺ was returning from Hudaybiyyah, Allaah revealed the verse: So that Allaah may forgive you (O Rasulullaah ﷺ) for your past…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that on the return from Hudaybiyyah the Prophet ﷺ received the verse of forgiveness and victory, which he said he loved more than everything on earth, and the Companions then received the verse promising Jannah to the believers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that after Rasulullaah ﷺ had been prevented from performing Umrah, he was returning from Hudaybiyyah when the following verse was revealed:…
narrations.summary: Anas and Mujammi bin Jaariya Ansaari report that after Hudaybiyyah the Prophet ﷺ recited the verses of clear victory, and when asked whether it was a victory he swore that it certainly was.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa (RA) once said, "You people regard the conquest of Makkah as the 'victory' (referred to in the first verse of Surah Fatah). Although that certainly was a…
narrations.summary: Baraa says the 'victory' of Surah Fath is the pledge of Ridwaan at Hudaybiyyah rather than the conquest of Makkah, and Jaabir says it is nothing other than the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Hajjaaj reports from his teacher that after Egypt was conquered (by the Muslims), the people approached the governor Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas when the…
narrations.summary: Qais bin Hajjaaj, reporting from his teacher, says Amr bin Al Aas stopped the Egyptian custom of throwing a virgin into the Nile, the river stopped flowing, and after Umar's note was thrown in it rose sixteen arm's lengths in a single night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sahm bin Minjaab reports, "We were on a military expedition with Alaa bin Hadhrami when we approached the island of Daarayn. The ocean however posed an obstacle…
narrations.summary: Sahm bin Minjaab reports that on an expedition Alaa bin Hadhrami prayed at the island of Daarayn and led the army through the sea, where the water did not reach their saddle-cloths.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) adds that when Ibn Muka'bir the Persian Emperor's governor saw the Muslims (travelling through the water), he said, "No!…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that Ibn Muka'bir, the Persian governor, seeing the Muslims cross the water, refused to fight such people and sailed back to Persia; the author then summarises a later account of Hujr bin Adi leading the crossing of the Tigris, with Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Harmal reports a narration that mentions a fire emerging from Harra (a rocky terrain near Madinah). Hadhrat Umar (RA) then came to Hadhrat Tameem…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Harmal reports that Umar sent Tameem Daari to deal with a fire rising from Harra, and Tameem drove it back into its crevice with his bare hands; Umar then said one who has witnessed such a sign cannot be like one who has not.

narrations.excerpt: A Sahabi reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ gave the command for the trench to be dug, a large boulder presented an obstacle to the digging. Rasulullaah ﷺ took up a spade,…
narrations.summary: A Sahabi reports that when the Prophet ﷺ struck a boulder at the Khandaq with a spade, each strike sparked and showed him the palaces of Persia, Rome and Abyssinia, and he asked Allaah to grant them to the Muslims; Salmaan Faarsi watched and confirmed it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Auf Muzani reports a similar narration. This narration states that when Nabi ﷺ arrived, he took a spade from Hadhrat Salmaan (RA). He then struck the…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Auf Muzani reports the same boulder event in which the spark lit up Madinah and the Prophet ﷺ promised Heera, Rome and San'aa; the Munaafiqeen mocked, and Surah Ahzaab verses were revealed; the author then previews Ibn Abbaas's fuller account.

narrations.excerpt: Also coming shortly in the chapter discussing the unseen assistance from Allaah is the incident of poison having no effect on Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed and his statement…
narrations.summary: The author previews later narrations: the incident of poison having no effect on Khaalid bin Waleed, and the words of a Christian named Amr praising the Arabs while the Sahabah are with them.

narrations.excerpt: Soon to appear in the chapter discussing the sources of assistance is the statement of Hadhrat Thaabit bin Aqram ig who said, "O Abu Hurayrah! Do you perhaps see a large…
narrations.summary: Thaabit bin Aqram tells Abu Hurayrah that numbers did not help at Badr; Khaalid says victory comes from Allaah and not numbers; Abu Bakr writes to Amr bin Al Aas that Allaah helped them with few, and refuses to hold back Usaamah's army; and Abdullaah bin Rawaaha urges the Muslims at Mu'ta to fight with trust in Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ entered the Masjid one day where he found Hadhrat Haarith bin Maalik (RA) asleep. Nudging him with his foot, Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet ﷺ found Haarith bin Maalik asleep in the Masjid and asked how he felt that morning; Haarith said he felt like a true Mu'min, describing how he turned from the world, fasted, prayed at night and seemed to see the Arsh and the people of Jannah and Jahannam, and the Prophet told him to remain steadfast.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration names the Sahabi as Hadhrat Haaritha bin Nu'maan and states that Rasulullaah gill said to him, "You have seen (the reality of Imaan), so remain…
narrations.summary: Another narration names the Sahabi as Haaritha bin Nu'maan, who asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray that he be martyred, and was the first to mount his horse when the call to Jihaad was made and the first to be martyred; Anas then reports a similar exchange with a young Ansaari, and another narration gives the same question about substantiating Imaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was walking somewhere when he met a young man from the Ansaar. "How do you feel this morning, O Haarith?" Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet met a young Ansaari, Haarith, and asked how he felt that morning; Haarith said he felt like a true believer, the Prophet advised him to weigh his words, and Haarith said he had turned his eyes away from this world.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Every statement requires substantiation, so how do you substantiate your Imaan?"
narrations.summary: The Prophet asks how a person substantiates his imaan, since every statement requires proof.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal arrived one day, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him, "How do you feel this morning, O Mu'aadh?" Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal said he felt like a true believer that morning; when the Prophet ﷺ asked for proof, he described fearing death each morning and evening, seeing all nations kneeling for the Day of Qiyaamah, and the punishments of Jahannam and rewards of Jannah, and the Prophet told him to remain steadfast.

narrations.excerpt: In the chapter discussing giving Da'wah towards Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ the narration of Hadhrat Suwayd bin Haarith (RA) passed. In the narration he states that he was…
narrations.summary: Suwayd bin Haarith (RA) relates how a delegation of seven met the Prophet, who asked them the reality of their Imaan, and they listed its fifteen attributes.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that they were sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ when Hadhrat Harmalah bin Zaid Ansaari (RA) of the Banu Haaritha tribe came and sat in…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar relates how Harmalah bin Zaid Ansaari confessed that his heart held hypocrisy, and the Prophet prayed for him and left the obstinate hypocrites to Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that a Sahabi whom Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched as commander of an expedition used to lead his companions in salaah but would always conclude…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha (RA) relates that an unnamed Sahabi who led prayers always ended with Surah Ikhlaas, and the Prophet said Allaah loves him for loving it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports that a (Jewish) scholar once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ using the address of "O Muhammad" or "O Rasulullaah he said, "Verily Allaah…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood relates the words of a Jewish scholar about Allaah's power over creation, which the Prophet confirmed with a smile and a verse of Surah Zumar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that someone once asked Rasulullaah "How will the Kaafir be resurrected on his face on the Day of Qiyaamah?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied,…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik relates the Prophet's answer about the disbelievers being raised on their faces, and Hudhayfah bin Usayd reports Abu Dharr's account of the three groups in which people will be resurrected and of the calamity that will destroy all riding animals.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah bin Usayd reports that Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) once said, "O tribe of Ghifaar! Talk (to each other) without taking oaths because the truthful one to whom…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr warns his people that on the Day of Qiyaamah mankind will be resurrected in three groups, and that a calamity will destroy all riding animals.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tufayl bin Abdullaah (RA) who was Hadhrat Aa'iSha (RA)'s uterine brother relates that he once saw a group of Christians in a dream. He said to them, "You people…
narrations.summary: Tufayl bin Abdullaah (RA) relates his dream about Christians and Jews, after which the Prophet told the Sahabah not to say what Allaah and Muhammad wills but to say that the One Allaah wills.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) narrates that one of the Muslims saw in a dream that he met a man from the Ahlul Kitaab who said to him, "You people are excellent people had it…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah relates a Muslim's dream about the Ahlul Kitaab and the Prophet's correction of the phrase what Allaah and Muhammad wills, and Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the Prophet rebuking a man who equated him with Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when a man came to discuss something with Rasulullaah ﷺ, the man said, "What Allaah wills and what you will." Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: A man told the Prophet ﷺ 'what Allaah wills and what you will', and the Prophet rebuked him for equating him with Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Imaam Awzaa'ee reports that a Jew once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ asking about volition. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Everything occurs by the will of Allaah." "What if I decide…
narrations.summary: Awzaa'ee reports that a Jew asked the Prophet about free will, and each action was affirmed as Allaah's will, after which Jibra'eel said the Prophet had been inspired with the correct facts as Ibraheem was.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was returning (with the Sahabah (RA)) from Hudaybiyyah, he set up camp at a particular place in the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood relates how the Prophet and the Sahabah overslept Fajr on the way back from Hudaybiyyah and the Prophet said Allaah had willed it as a lesson, and Abu Qataadah reports the Prophet saying Allaah takes souls in sleep when He wills.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Taariq bin Shihaab narrates that a Jew once asked Hadhrat Umar 'Tell me where is Jahannam when Allaah says: Jannah has the vastness of the heavens and the earth.…
narrations.summary: Taariq bin Shihaab relates that a Jew asked Umar where Jahannam is, given the verse about the vastness of Jannah, and Umar answered by comparing it to where the day goes at night, which the Jew said matched the Torah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) was once introduced to a man debating the issue of volition. "O servant of Allaah!" Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Has Allaah…
narrations.summary: Muhammad relates that Ali questioned a man who debated volition, asking whether Allaah creates, sickens, cures and moves people as He wills or as they will, and the narration breaks off mid-sentence.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that the Sahabah (RA) once said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ We experience a wonderful frame of mind when we are with you, but no sooner we leave your…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik relates that the Sahabah feared hypocrisy when they left the Prophet's company, and the Prophet said that Allaah being their Rabb in private and in public is not hypocrisy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that a Bedouin once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ with a question. "O Rasulullaah ﷺ he asked, "Who will ask the creation to render their…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates how a Bedouin asked who will call creation to account on the Day of Qiyaamah, and when told it is Allaah, the Bedouin said they were saved because the Magnanimous One forgives.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once sent Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) to collect zakaah from the Banu Kilaab tribe. Hadhrat Mu'aadh distributed…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib relates that Umar sent Mu'aadh bin Jabal to collect zakaah, and Mu'aadh gave it all to the poor and told his wife an inspector had gone with him, after which Umar laughed and gave her a gift.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "All praise belongs to Allaah Who hears everything. The Mujaadalah (the lady who debated) came to speak with Rasulullaah ﷺ and although I was…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha (RA) relates that Allaah hears everything, and that a verse was revealed about Khowla bint Tha'laba's debate with the Prophet over her husband, though Aa'isha could hear nothing from the corner of the room.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "Blessed is that Allaah Whose hearing captures everything. As I was listening to Khowla bint Tha'laba complain to Rasulullaah Wt about her…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha (RA) relates Khowla bint Tha'laba's complaint to the Prophet about her husband, and that Jibra'eel brought the verse before she had stood up.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) addressed the people saying, "O people! If Muhammad ﷺ was your deity…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the people wept at the Prophet's death, and Ma'n bin Adi replied that he wished to believe in him after his death as he had in his life.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Alqamah narrates from his mother that a woman once entered the room of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) (to visit the tomb of Rasulullaah ﷺ). She was perfectly healthy when…
narrations.summary: Alqamah reports from his mother that a woman who came to Aa'isha's room to pray near the Prophet's grave died while still in sajdah. Aa'isha took this as a lesson about death, and her doubt about the sudden death of her brother Abdur Rahmaan was removed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "Every drop of water passes through a measure in the hand of an angel (referred to as the Khazzaan whom Allaah has appointed to the task).…
narrations.summary: Ali (RA) explains that the water of the Flood and the wind that destroyed Aad were released by Allaah directly, without the angel who normally measures them, and cites the verses of Surah Haaqqah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Buqayrah (RA) who was the wife of Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) says, "When Salmaan was on his deathbed, he called for me to his upper story room that had four doors. He…
narrations.summary: Buqayrah (RA), the wife of Salmaan Faarsi, relates that on his deathbed Salmaan had the doors opened for expected visitors and musk sprinkled around his bed, and she found him dead as if asleep.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that when Hadhrat Salmaan ig was on his deathbed, he called for his wife and said, "Bring me the bag I asked you to keep away." When she brought…
narrations.summary: On his deathbed Salmaan asks for musk to be sprinkled around him, because angels who smell fragrance but do not eat are coming to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was, called to the funeral of a child from, she remarked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Glad tiding for him! a sparrow fronv…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha (RA) remarks on a child of the Ansaar who died young, and the Prophet explains that Allaah created the people of Jannah and Jahannam with their destinies set while they were still in their fathers' backs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Waleed bin Ubaadah narrates, "I once went to see (my father) Ubaadah bin Saamit when he was so ill that I anticipated he would soon pass away. 'Dear father,' I…
narrations.summary: Waleed bin Ubaadah relates his father Ubaadah bin Saamit's deathbed advice that one cannot taste Imaan without believing in predestination, quoting the Prophet that the pen was the first thing Allaah created.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Nadhrah narrates that a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ known as Abu Abdullaah was weeping when his companions came to visit him. "Why are you weeping?" they…
narrations.summary: Abu Nadhrah relates that Abu Abdullaah, a companion of the Prophet, wept on his deathbed because he did not know which of the two handfuls of souls Allaah had set aside for him.

narrations.excerpt: When death came to Hadhrat Muaa'dh bin Jabal (RA), he started weeping. "What makes you weep?" someone asked. Hadhrat Muaa'dh (RA) replied, "By Allaah! It is neither fear…
narrations.summary: Muaadh bin Jabal (RA) weeps on his deathbed, saying he does not know which of the two handfuls of souls he will be placed in, as the Prophet had said.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ubayd Makki reports that someone once said to Hadhrat (RA) bin Abbaas (RA), "A man who denies predestination has come to us." Hadhrat (RA) bin Abbaas…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Ubayd Makki relates that Ibn Abbaas, on hearing of a man who denied predestination, vowed to break his neck and bite off his nose, quoting the Prophet's warning that denying predestination would be the first Shirk in this Ummah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa bin Abu Rabaah relates, "I came to Hadhrat (RA) bin Abbaas at a time when he was drawing water from the Zamzam well and the bottom of his clothing had…
narrations.summary: Ataa bin Abu Rabaah relates Ibn Abbaas's words about people who objected to predestination, whom he called the worst of this Ummah and whose sick he would not visit or whose dead he would not bury.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) bin Abbaas (RA) once said, "I wish that there was a person who denied predestination with me so that I could trample his head." "Why would you do that?"…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas says he wishes he could trample the head of anyone who denied predestination, because the Lowhul Mahfoodh is written by Allaah's glances that create, give life, give death and honour as He pleases.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi reports that Hadhrat (RA) bin Umar (RA) had a friend in Shaam with whom he corresponded regularly. Hadhrat (RA) bin Umar wrote to him one day saying, "The…
narrations.summary: Naafi relates that Abdullaah bin Umar cut off a correspondent in Shaam who objected to predestination, quoting the Prophet's warning that people in his Ummah would deny it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nazzaal bin Sabrah narrates that someone once said to Hadhrat Ali "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! There are people here who believe that Allaah does not know about…
narrations.summary: Nazzaal bin Sabrah relates that Ali corrected a claim that Allaah does not know something until it happens, explaining the verse about testing, and quotes his earlier saying that nothing happens on earth until it is decided in the heavens.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood is reports that very often when delivering a sermon on the pulpit, Hadhrat Umar (RA) would recite the following couplets (which mean): "Go…
narrations.summary: Umar used to recite couplets from the pulpit saying that the outcome of all matters is in Allaah's hand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when the verse: When the trumpet is blown (to signal the arrival of Qiyaamah). . . (Surah Muddathir, verse 8) was…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas relates that when the verse about the trumpet was revealed, the Prophet said he could not live in ease with the trumpet-blower poised to blow, and taught the Sahabah to say that Allaah is sufficient for them.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when the Sahabah (RA) heard this from Rasulullaah ﷺ, they were troubled and asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ What should we do." Rasulullaah ﷺ then…
narrations.summary: Another narration of the trumpet incident says that when the Sahabah heard the warning they were troubled, and the Prophet told them to recite that Allaah is sufficient for them.

narrations.excerpt: The narration has already passed in the chapter discussing the relationships of women in which Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) said to Hadhrat Sauda Yamaaniyyah "The one-eyed…
narrations.summary: Hafsa (RA) tells Sauda Yamaaniyyah (RA) that the one-eyed Dajjaal has appeared, and Sauda hides in a tent until the Prophet comes, clarifies that he has not yet appeared, and dusts her off.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once asked, "Is there a place in Iraq called Khurasaan?" When he was informed that there was, he said,…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib relates that Abu Bakr asked whether there is a place in Iraq called Khurasaan, from which Dajjaal would emerge, and Abu Bakr also stated that Dajjaal would come from the Jews of Marw.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Mulaykah (RA) narrates, "When I went to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas early one morning, he said, 'I have not had a wink of sleep all night.'…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abi Mulaykah relates that Ibn Abbaas stayed awake fearing the smoke sign of the Last Day after a tailed star appeared, and another report has him fearing that Dajjaal would appear.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Nasi reports that when death came to Hadhrat Abu Bakr he said to (his daughter) Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "Wash these two garments of mine and bury me in…
narrations.summary: Ubaadah bin Nasi reports that Abu Bakr on his deathbed told Aa'isha to bury him in his two garments, since the dead will be either richly clothed or stripped in the grave.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was about to pass away, she recited a couplet (which means): "By your life! An abundance of wealth are…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha (RA) reports that when Abu Bakr was dying she recited a couplet on the uselessness of wealth, and he corrected her with a verse of Surah Qaaf and asked to be buried in his two garments, since the living need new clothing more than the dead.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) became extremely ill, she started weeping and when he fell unconscious, she recited a couplet (which means):…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha (RA) relates Abu Bakr's last days: he rebuked her weeping, asked which day the Prophet died, hoped to die that same night, and asked that his saffron-stained garment be washed and added to the Prophet's three-sheet shroud.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that he said, "...because it (the clothing of the dead) will only be given over to body fluids and decay."
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr said that the clothing of the dead will only be given over to body fluids and decay.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Abu Raashid Nasri narrates that when death approached Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA), he said to his son, "Dear son? When death is approaching (when I…
narrations.summary: Yahya bin Abu Raashid Nasri relates Umar's deathbed instructions to his son about washing, shrouding, the grave and the funeral, based on the hope of good with Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: In the chapter discussing the weeping of the Sahabah (RA), the narration of Hadhrat Haani has already passed stating that whenever Hadhrat Uthmaan stopped at a graveyard,…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan (RA) wept whenever he stood at a grave, and when asked, said the Prophet called the grave the first stage of the Aakhirah and had never seen a sight more frightening.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Rabee narrates that when his tribe and the Ansaar heard that Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) was gravely ill, they went to him sometime during the middle of…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah, gravely ill, asked for a plain shroud, saying a good end would be exchanged for something better and otherwise the shroud would be quickly removed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sila bin Zufar narrates, "Hudhayfah (RA) sent Abu Mas'ood and me to purchase a burial shroud for him, we bought a striped and decorated sheet for him for three…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah sent Sila and Abu Mas'ood to buy his shroud, rejected the striped sheet they bought, and asked for two plain white sheets instead.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said to them, "What will you do with that? If your companion (myself) is a righteous person, Allaah will exchange it…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah told the men who bought his shroud that a righteous man's shroud would be exchanged, but a wicked man's would be thrown into the grave or used to strike his face on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dahhaak bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that when death drew close to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA), he called his attendants and instructed them, "Go and dig me a…
narrations.summary: As death approached, Abu Moosa told his attendants to dig a wide grave, then described how the grave would either open onto Jannah or narrow onto Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Usayd bin Hudhayr (RA) was amongst the best of people. He would always say, "I have no doubts about being amongst the…
narrations.summary: Usayd bin Hudhayr said he would have no doubt of Jannah if he stayed in one of three states: reciting or hearing the Qur'aan, hearing the Prophet's sermon, or attending funerals.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that the Sahabah (RA) once said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Whenever we see you, out hearts are softened and we think only of the Aakhirah.…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when the Sahabah asked about Jannah, the Prophet described its buildings and the three whose du'aa is never rejected.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Suwayd bin Ghafalah (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Ali (RA) was suffering extreme hunger one day, he suggested to (his wife) Hadhrat Faatima to approach (her…
narrations.summary: Faatima went to the Prophet for food for her hungry household, chose the words of dhikr he offered over five goats, and returned to Ali saying she had gained something of benefit for the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) reports that they were on a journey with Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) when he heard people talking and having eloquent discussions. "O…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that Abu Moosa, hearing people talk eloquently, asked why people neglect the Aakhirah, and answered that the world is before them while the Aakhirah is still to come.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was on a journey when the verse was revealed: (T ijy ijj O people! Fear punishment of) your Rabb f/?y obeying…
narrations.summary: Imraan bin Husayn reports the Prophet explaining the verse about the earthquake of Qiyaamah, that nine hundred and ninety-nine in a thousand will go to Jahannam, and his hope that his Ummah will be a quarter, a third or half of Jannah's people.

narrations.excerpt: A narration from Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) also discussing the explanation of the above verse states that Nabi ﷺ said, "On the Day of Qiyaamah, Allaah will call for…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri relates the same teaching from the Prophet, in which Aadam is told to separate those for Jahannam, the Sahabah turn pale, and the Prophet again hopes his Ummah will be a quarter, a third or half of Jannah's people.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that what Rasulullaah ﷺ said (about nine hundred and ninety nine going to Jahannam), the impact was heavy on the Sahabah and they became very…
narrations.summary: Another report says the Sahabah were deeply grieved and worried when the Prophet said that nine hundred and ninety-nine in a thousand would enter Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) reports that when the verse: Then, on the Day of Qiyaamah, you will all bring cases (against each other) in the presence of your Rabb.…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr reports that when the verse about bringing cases before Allaah was revealed, Zubayr asked whether such cases would be brought against them, and on being told yes, called the matter a serious one.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that when the verse: Thereafter, on that day (of Qiyaamah) you will definitely be questioned about the bounties. (Surah Takaathur, verse 8) was…
narrations.summary: Zubayr asked what bounties people would be questioned about and whether disputes between people would be brought before Allaah, and the Prophet confirmed that every right will be repaid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha was once lying down in his wife's lap when he started to weep. His wife then also started to weep.…
narrations.summary: Qais bin Abi Haazim reports that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha wept in his wife's lap, fearing he would not be rescued when crossing over Jahannam, and she wept with him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Muhammad bin Ubaadah bin Saamit narrates that when death approached Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA), he requested that his slaves, servants,…
narrations.summary: As death approached, Ubaadah bin Saamit asked everyone he had dealings with to claim any wrong from him, then told them not to weep, to pray and to ask forgiveness for him, and gave burial instructions.

narrations.excerpt: In the chapter discussing cautiousness in spending, the narration has already passed in which Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf for a loan of four…
narrations.summary: Umar, who had asked Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf for a loan of four thousand dirhams, was troubled at the idea of taking it from the public treasury, fearing he would be held to account on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: In the chapter discussing being influenced by the knowledge of Allaah and of Rasulullaah ﷺ. the narration will Inshaa Allaah be narrated in which Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah…
narrations.summary: The author signposts two later narrations, one in which Abu Hurayrah collapsed and one in which Mu'aawiya wept, both on hearing a hadith about Allaah's accountability on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Auf bin Maalik (RA) reports, "We were once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when we set up camp towards the end of the night. Laying down our heads by the foot of our…
narrations.summary: Awf bin Maalik and his companions, searching for the Prophet at night, found him and learned he had chosen intercession over having half his Ummah enter Jannah, and he promised intercession for those who never commit Shirk.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Aqeel (RA) reports, "I went to Rasulullaah with a delegation from the Thaqeef tribe. When we made our animals sit at the door, there was not…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Aqeel reports that when a Thaqeef delegation asked the Prophet for a kingdom like Sulaymaan's, he said Allaah had kept for him a special prayer, to be used for interceding for his Ummah on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "I am an excellent man for the sinners of my Ummah." "O Rasulullaah ﷺ a man from the Muzaynah tribe…
narrations.summary: Ummu Salamah reports the Prophet saying that he is an excellent intercessor for the sinners of his Ummah, and that intercession will be denied to anyone who belittles his Companions.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "I shall continue interceding on behalf of my Ummah until my Rabb asks, 'Are you now satisfied, O…
narrations.summary: Ali bin Abi Taalib reports the Prophet's saying that he will keep interceding until his Rabb is satisfied, and then tells the people of Iraq that the verse giving the Prophet hope refers to the privilege of intercession.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Buraydah narrates that (his father) Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) once went to Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) where a man was busy talking (in praise of Hadhrat Mu'aawiya…
narrations.summary: Ibn Buraydah reports that his father Buraydah told Mu'aawiya, who was being praised, that the Prophet expected to intercede for as many people as there are trees and stones, so Mu'aawiya should place his hope in that while Ali need not.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Talq bin Habeeb says, "I was a person who most vehemently denied intercession until I met Hadhrat Jaabir (RA). After I recited to him all the verses of the…
narrations.summary: Talq bin Habeeb and Yazeed Faqeer, who both had denied that believers will be brought out of Jahannam, were convinced by Jaabir bin Abdillaah's explanation of the Qur'aan and of the Prophet's words.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Handhala Kaatib Usaydi (RA) who was one of Rasulullaah ﷺ's scribes narrates, "We were once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when we spoke of Jannah and Jahannam (with) so much…
narrations.summary: Handhala, one of the Prophet's scribes, feared he had become a hypocrite because he forgot the vivid talk of Jannah when with his family, and the Prophet told him there are times for each.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that one night they spent a long time speaking to Rasulullaah ﷺ. When they went to him early the following morning,…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood reports the Prophet's vision of the nations and the seventy thousand who enter Jannah without reckoning, described as those who do not brand themselves, use amulets or divine by birds, and trust only in their Rabb, and his hope that his Ummah will be a third or half of Jannah's people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sulaym bin Aamir reports that the Sahabah (RA) always used to say, "Verily Allaah gave us tremendous benefit from the Bedouins and their questions." A Bedouin…
narrations.summary: Sulaym bin Aamir reports that a Bedouin asked about the thorny lotus of Jannah, and the Prophet explained that Allaah will remove its thorns and make each one a fruit with seventy-two flavours.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Utba bin Abdus Sulami (RA) reports that he was sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ when a Bedouin arrived and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I hear you speak about a tree in…
