narrations.summary: Utba bin Abd as-Sulami reports that a Bedouin asked about the acacia tree in Jannah, and the Prophet said Allaah will replace its thorns with fruit, each with seventy-two flavours.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Utba bin Abdus Sulami (RA) reports that a Bedouin once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ to enquire about the pond (Kowthar) and to speak about Jannah. He asked, "Are there…
narrations.summary: Utba bin Abd as-Sulami reports a Bedouin's questions about Jannah, and the Prophet describes its pond, the tree Tooba, the walnut tree of Shaam, its grapes, and a grape as large as a waterskin bucket that could feed a whole family and tribe.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that an Abyssinian man once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ. "Ask what you wish," Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him. The man said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Ibn Umar reports that an Abyssinian man asked whether he would be with the Prophet in Jannah, heard of its rewards, asked whether he would see what the Prophet sees, then wept until he died, and the Prophet himself lowered him into the grave.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Wahab reports from Hadhrat Ibn Zaid (RA) that an Abyssinian man was with Rasulullaah ﷺ when Allaah revealed the Surah: Undoubtedly, a moment in time…
narrations.summary: Ibn Zaid reports that when the Prophet recited the verses about Jannah to the Sahabah, an Abyssinian man sighed deeply and died, and the Prophet said that longing for Jannah had taken his soul.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Matar reports that he heard Hadhrat Ali (RA) say, "When Umar is was stabbed by Abu Lu'lu, I went to him and found him weeping. 'What makes you weep, O Ameerul…
narrations.summary: Ali consoled Umar, who was weeping after being stabbed, with the glad tidings of Jannah that Ali had heard from the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: In the chapter discussing the abstinence of Hadhrat Umar (RA) the narration has already passed which mentions that when served a good meal, Hadhrat umar (RA) said, "While…
narrations.summary: After a good meal was served, Umar wept at the thought that poor Muslims who died without filling themselves had been given Jannah, which he felt far surpassed his own share.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Sa'd (the son of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA)) relates, "My father's head was in my lap as he was surrendering his soul (to death). When he saw my…
narrations.summary: Mus'ab bin Sa'd reports his dying father, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, telling him not to weep, since Allaah will never punish him and he will be among the people of Jannah, as the Prophet clearly stated.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Shamaasa Mahri reports that they went to see Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas when he was on his deathbed. Turning his face towards the wall, he wept for a long while…
narrations.summary: Several reports describe Amr bin Al Aas on his deathbed weeping over what follows death, recalling his past enmity, his conversion and his growing love for the Prophet, and giving instructions for his burial.

narrations.excerpt: In the chapter discussing the assistance rendered to Rasulullaah ﷺ, the words of the Ansaar have been quoted when Khaybar was conquered, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to the Ansaar,…
narrations.summary: The author cross-refers to earlier sayings in which Companions longed for Jannah in battle, at home, in illness and at the loss of a child, including Umayr bin Humaam, Anas bin Nadhr, Ammaar and Abu Dardaa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that she once started to weep at the thought of Jahannam. "What is the matter, O Aa'isha?" Rasulullaah (iiil asked. She replied, "I thought…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha wept at the thought of Jahannam and asked whether anyone would think of family on the Day of Qiyaamah, and the Prophet described three moments when no one thinks of another: at the scales, at the handing out of the records, and at the bridge of Siraat.

narrations.excerpt: Amongst the Sahabah (RA) was a very old man when Rasulullaah ﷺ recited to them the verse: O you who have Imaan! Save yourselves and your families from the Fire (of…
narrations.summary: An elderly Companion fainted when the Prophet recited the verse on the fuel of Jahannam and was given glad tidings after saying the Kalimah; a young Ansaari who wept at mention of Jahannam died in the Prophet's arms.

narrations.excerpt: The restlessness of Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Aws (RA) in his bed has already been quoted with his words, "O Allaah! The fire of Jahannam has dispelled my sleep." Thereafter,…
narrations.summary: The author recalls two sayings: Shaddaad bin Aws said the fire of Jahannam had banished his sleep, and Abdullaah bin Rawaaha wept at Mu'ta, fearing the crossing over Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nayyaar bin Mukram Aslami (RA) reports that the Persians were prevailing over the Romans at the time when Allaah revealed the verses: Alif Laam Meem (The people…
narrations.summary: Nayyaar bin Mukram Aslami reports that when the revelation that the Romans would again prevail over the Persians came, Abu Bakr proclaimed it against the Quraysh, took their wager, and when the Romans won after the six-year limit many accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa (RA) narrates that when the verses: Alif Laam Meem (The people of) Rome will be defeated (by the Persians) in the (land that is) nearer (to the Arabs than…
narrations.summary: Baraa reports that Abu Bakr renewed the wager with the Quraysh on the Prophet's advice, and when the winnings came he was told to give them away in charity because they were unlawful.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ka'b bin Adi (RA) says, "I came with a delegation from Heera to Nabi SiS-f. When Rasulullaah ﷺ presented Islaam to us, we accepted and then returned to Heera. It…
narrations.summary: Ka'b bin Adi, returning from a delegation to the Prophet, has his doubts about the Prophet's death settled by a vision, and later tells Maqoqis of Allaah's promise that His Deen would dominate.

narrations.excerpt: In the chapter discussing the Jihaad against the, the following words of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) are quoted: He said, "I swear by Allaah that I shall remain devoted to the…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr, Umar and Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas each urge the Muslims to wage Jihaad with trust in Allaah's promise, Sa'd reminding them of the army of Yazdgird they face.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umaarah bin Khuzaymah bin Thaabit narrates from his uncle who was a Sahabi that Rasulullaah ﷺ once purchased a horse from a Bedouin. Rasulullaah ﷺ asked the…
narrations.summary: Umaarah bin Khuzaymah narrates how Khuzaymah bin Thaabit testified that the Prophet had bought a horse from a Bedouin, and the Prophet then accepted his single testimony as equal to that of two men.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "O Khuzaymah! On what basis do you testify when you were not with us?" "O Rasulullaah ﷺ he replied, "When I believe the…
narrations.summary: Two further versions of the horse testimony report that the Prophet asked Khuzaymah on what basis he testified, and that Khuzaymah's testimony was accepted because he believed the Prophet's news from the heavens.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that after Rasulullaah ﷺ was taken on the historic night journey to Masjidul Aqsa (and then to the heavens), he narrated it to the people…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha narrates that when the Prophet told of his night journey to Masjidul Aqsa and the heavens, some who had professed Imaan left Islaam, and Abu Bakr affirmed the report and received the title Siddeeq.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that on this occasion, some people who had previously professed Imaan left the fold of Islaam, while cithers believed (without question). The…
narrations.summary: Variant reports of the night journey account describe the test it posed to the people, and Abu Bakr's reply to those who came to him saying the Prophet had travelled a month's journey in one night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) reports that during the year in which Hadhrat Umar (RA) became the Khalifah, the numbers of locusts declined drastically. When Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports that when locusts became scarce in Umar's caliphate and a rider brought a handful from Yemen, Umar recalled the Prophet's saying that locusts would be the first creatures to become extinct and the rest would follow.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Fudhaala bin Abu Fudhaala Ansaari relates, "I accompanied my father (Hadhrat Abu Fudhaala (RA)) to Yamba to visit Hadhrat Ali (RA) who had become extremely ill…
narrations.summary: Fudhaala bin Abu Fudhaala Ansaari reports that his father urged the ill Ali to return to Madinah from Yamba, but Ali said the Prophet had told him he would not die until he became Khalifah and his beard was dyed with the blood from his forehead.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) one day came to him as he placed his foot stirrup (of his animal, ready to ride off). "Where do you…
narrations.summary: Ali recounts that Abdullaah bin Salaam warned him, as he set out for Iraq, that a sword would strike him there, and Ali says he had already heard the same from the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Jareer narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) was once inspecting the cavalry when Ibn Muljim passed by. When Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked him his name, he gave a…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Jareer narrates that when Ali caught Ibn Muljim giving a false name, Ali let him go after he gave his father's name, because the Prophet had said Ali's assassin would be a man from the Jews.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaydah narrates that whenever Hadhrat Ali (RA) saw Ibn Muljim, he would recite the following couplet (which means): "While I wish him life, he wishes to kill me…
narrations.summary: Ubaydah reports the couplets Ali recited whenever he saw Ibn Muljim, and Abu Tufayl reports that Ali, after ordering his allowance paid, pointed to his beard and recited verses on facing death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Ammaar (RA) who brought Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) up reports that when Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) became very ill one day, he said, "I am not going to die from this…
narrations.summary: Ummu Ammaar reports that Ammaar knew he would be killed in a battle between Muslim armies, and that at Siffeen he drank the milk he had been told would be his last drink before fighting until he was killed, and Khaalid bin Waleed relays Mu'aawiya's fear of being blamed for Ammaar's death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Ashtar narrates from his father that when death approached Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA), his wife started to weep. "What makes you weep?" he asked. "I am…
narrations.summary: Ibraheem bin Ashtar reports that Abu Dharr, dying in the wilderness as the Prophet had foretold, had his wife watch the road until a group of travellers from Yemen, including a young Ansaari who gave his own shroud, came to bury him.

narrations.excerpt: Shaymaa bint Buqaylah Hadhrat Khuraym bin Aws (RA) relates, "I migrated to Rasulullaah ﷺ and met him upon his return from Tabook, when I accepted Islaam. I heard…
narrations.summary: Khuraym bin Aws reports that the Prophet foretold he would be given Shaymaa bint Buqaylah if Heera was conquered, and after the conquest he claimed her, as described, and sold her to her wealthy brother for a thousand Dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jubayr bin Hayya reports, "When the Kaafir leader Bandaarfaan sent a message that the Muslims send someone to him for negotiations, Hadhrat Mugheirah bin Shu'ba…
narrations.summary: Jubayr bin Hayya reports that Mughiera bin Shu'ba, sent to negotiate with the Persian commander Bandaarfaan, told him the Prophet had promised the Arabs victory and assistance, so they would never return to their former hardship.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jubayr bin Hayya also narrates a lengthy Hadith in which an army under the command of Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Muqarrin (RA) was sent to the people of Ahwaaz. When…
narrations.summary: Jubayr bin Hayya reports a longer account of Mughiera bin Shu'ba, sent with Nu'maan bin Muqarrin's army to the people of Ahwaaz, explaining that the Prophet had ordered them to fight until the people worshipped Allaah alone or paid jizyah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Talq narrates that a man once came to Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) saying, "O Abu Your house has burnt down!" "It could not have burnt," Hadhrat Abu Dardaa said.…
narrations.summary: Talq reports that Abu Dardaa stayed sure his house would not burn, because he recited the words the Prophet had taught him each morning for protection.

narrations.excerpt: In the chapter of Da'wah'2', the words of Hadhrat Adi (RA) have been quoted who said, "I swear by the Being in whose control is my life, the third prophesy shall also…
narrations.summary: The author gathers several remarks that confirm the Prophet's predictions: Adi's third prophecy, Hishaam bin Al Aas and others telling Jabala bin Ayham that they would take his kingdom, Ali assuring Abu Bakr the Deen would prevail, and a forward reference to Ibn Umar and a lion.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Asmaa narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was once having lunch with Rasulullaah ﷺ when the verse was revealed: (a •jilr O j-P Whoever (sincerely) does an…
narrations.summary: Abu Asmaa reports that when the verse on an atom's weight of good and evil was revealed, Abu Bakr asked whether every evil would be requited, and the Prophet said worldly hardship is retribution while good deeds are rewarded in the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) reports that he was once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when the verse was revealed: Uj Oji ij tj jiu I s-j-. Whoever commits an evil act will meet (receive)…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr reports that after the verse saying whoever does evil will be requited was revealed, the Prophet recited it to him, and when Abu Bakr asked who could be free of sin, the Prophet said believers are punished in this world so they meet Allaah without sin.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr JU once asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ When we will be punished for every sin, who can keep himself in good stead after the verse: Whoever commits an evil act…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr asks how anyone can be safe from punishment for every sin, and the Prophet says the hardships of this world are the retribution for sins.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Muntashir narrates that a man once came to Hadhrat Umar saying, "I know which is the harshest verse in Allaah's Book." (Because referring to a verse…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Muntashir reports that Umar struck a man who called a verse of the Qur'aan the harshest, then explained the next day that the verse had weighed on the Sahabah until Allaah revealed the verse promising forgiveness to those who seek it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tha'laba (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Amr bin Samurah bin Habeeb bin Abdush Shams once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Rasulullaah I have stolen a camel from a…
narrations.summary: Tha'laba reports that Amr bin Samurah confessed to theft and had his hand cut off, praising Allaah for cleansing him, and Hasan reports that the ill Imraan bin Husayn explained his suffering as the result of sins that Allaah had largely forgiven.

narrations.excerpt: The narration has already been quoted that when death came to one of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)'s sons, the youngster kept looking at the pillow. After he has passed away, the…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr, finding dinars under his dying son's pillow, says he doubts his skin could bear the punishment for not giving them in charity, and the Prophet tells a slave-owner that his slaves' wrongs will be weighed against his punishment of them, after which the man frees them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that the Sahabah (RA) felt a hard blow when Allah revealed the verse: (To Allaah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Sahabah were distressed by the verse on what is in the heart, and the Prophet taught them to say 'we hear and obey', after which Allaah abrogated the burden with the verse that He does not burden a soul beyond its capacity; Mujaahid reports Ibn Abbaas explaining this and Ibn Umar weeping over the verse.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that it was a hard blow to the Sahabah (RA) when Allaah revealed the verse: Those who do not mix their Imaan with Dhulm…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that the Sahabah were distressed by the verse on not mixing Imaan with dhulm and asked who had not done wrong, and the Prophet explained from Luqmaan's advice to his son that dhulm here means shirk.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when the verse: Those who do not mix their Imaan with Dhulm (wrong-doing). . . (Surah An'aam, verse 82) was revealed, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I…
narrations.summary: A variant report says that when the verse on not mixing Imaan with dhulm was revealed, the Prophet said he had been told that he was among such people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Safiyya bint Shaybah (RA) reports that they were once with Hadhrat Aa'isha discussing the women of the Quraysh and their virtues. Hadhrat Aa'isha remarked, "No…
narrations.summary: Safiyya bint Shaybah reports Aa'isha's praise of the women of the Ansaar, who, when the verse on drawing scarves over the chest was revealed, covered themselves at once and came to salaah behind the Prophet looking like crows perched on their heads.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Makhool narrates that an extremely old man whose eyebrows had actually fallen over his eyes once came and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ There is a man who had been…
narrations.summary: Makhool reports that an extremely old, sinful man asked the Prophet whether repentance was possible, and on accepting Islaam was told that Allaah would forgive all his treachery and sins and turn his evils into good deeds.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Farwah (RA) narrates that a man once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Tell me about a man who had committed every type of sin and has not left…
narrations.summary: Abu Farwah reports that a man who had committed every sin asked whether he could repent, and the Prophet told him that doing good and abstaining from evil would turn all his past sins into good deeds, after which the man went off repeatedly saying Allaahu Akbar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) relates, "A woman once came to me and asked, 'Is there any repentance for me when I have committed adultery, given birth to a child and then…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that a woman who had committed adultery and killed her child was told by him that she had no repentance, until the Prophet recited the verses of Surah Furqaan offering forgiveness, and another report says she freed her slave woman and repented sincerely.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Hasan the freed slave of Hadhrat Tameem Daari (RA) narrates that when the verse: (Tttu-il hy) Only deviant people follow the poets. (Surah shu'araa; verse…
narrations.summary: Abul Hasan, a freed slave of Tameem Daari, reports that when the verse saying only deviant people follow poets was revealed, Hassaan bin Thaabit, Abdullaah bin Rawaaha and Ka'b bin Maalik came weeping, and the Prophet recited the exception for believing poets who defend Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa bin Saa'ib narrates that the first time he saw Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla was when he saw an old man with white hair and a white beard following a…
narrations.summary: Ataa bin Saa'ib describes the old Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla explaining that a believer's longing to meet Allaah at death differs from the dread of the rejecter, quoting the Prophet's saying that whoever loves to meet Allaah, Allaah loves to meet him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddeeq was sitting somewhere and started weeping excessively when Allaah revealed the verse: When the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that Abu Bakr wept excessively when the Surah Zilzaal was revealed, and the Prophet told him that if people never erred, Allaah would create a nation that erred and sinned so that He could forgive them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar JiS-SsiSSei reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to him, "O Umar! What would be your condition when you are in a piece of ground measuring four arm's lengths…
narrations.summary: Umar reports that the Prophet asked him how he would fare in the grave when Munkar and Nakeer examined him, and Umar, told he would be in full command of his senses, said he would be able to handle them.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ then said to Hadhrat Umar (RA), "I swear by the Being Who has sent me with the truth that Jibra'eel has just informed me that…
narrations.summary: A variant of the grave examination account says the Prophet told Umar, on Jibra'eel's word, that he would answer the questioners with the articles of faith and that they would wonder whether they had been sent to question him or he to question them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Bahriyya Kindi narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once came out of his home and found a gathering in which Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) was present.…
narrations.summary: Abul Bahriyya Kindi reports that Umar, coming out to a gathering where Uthmaan was present, said that among them was a man whose Imaan would suffice an entire army if it were divided among them.

narrations.excerpt: In the chapter discussing the attributes of the Sahabah (RA) \ the narration has already passed in which it is stated that when someone once asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin…
narrations.summary: A set of cross-references gathers remarks already quoted elsewhere on the strength of Imaan: Ibn Umar on the Sahabah's hearts being firmer than mountains, Ammaar's contentment with Imaan, Abu Bakr and Umar's trust and taqwa, Ali's trust in Allaah over one's own hand, Aamir bin Rabee'ah's detachment from the world, and Aa'isha's account of Usayd bin Hudhayr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haarith who was the freed slave of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) narrates that they were once sitting with Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) when the Mu'adhin arrived (to call out the…
narrations.summary: Haarith, a freed slave of Uthmaan, reports Uthmaan's wudhu and the Prophet's saying that sins between the prayers are forgiven, with the lasting good deeds being the tasbeeh, and Abu Uthmaan reports Salmaan Faarsi shaking a tree to show how sins fall away with wudhu and the five prayers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir the son of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas narrates that he heard his father and other Sahabah (RA) narrate that two brothers lived during the time of…
narrations.summary: Aamir bin Sa'd reports, from his father Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, that when told one of two brothers was the better, the Prophet pointed to the surviving brother's prayers and compared salaah to a river at the door that washes away dirt five times a day.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that two men from the Baliy branch of the Qudhaa'a tribe accepted Islaam at the hands of Rasulullaah ﷺ. While the one was martyred, the…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah narrates that Talha dreamt that a man who died later entered Jannah before the martyr, and the Prophet explained it by the man's Ramadan fast and his extra salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates that they were once with Rasulullaah Wife in the Masjid when a man stood up and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I have committed a sin." Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Ali narrates that a man confessed a sin to the Prophet in the Masjid, and the Prophet told him that his salaah performed with proper wudhu was compensation for it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) narrates that a man once asked Rasulullaah what the best of all deeds was. "Salaah," Rasulullaah Wife replied. "What then?" the man asked.…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr narrates that the Prophet named salaah, then jihaad, then kindness to parents as the best deeds, and told a man who vowed to leave his parents for jihaad to judge whether they had others to care for them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Murra Juhani narrates that a man once said, "O Rasulullaah Tell me in which category of people I will belong if I testify that there is none worthy of…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Murrah Juhani narrates that the Prophet told a man who asked his rank that the five salaahs, zakaah, Ramadan fasting and Nafl salaah in Ramadan would place him among the Siddeeqeen and the martyrs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "What Rasulullaah ﷺ emphasised most on his deathbed was, '(Take good care of your) Salaah and your slaves.' In fact, he was saying these words…
narrations.summary: Anas says that the Prophet's last emphasis on his deathbed was salaah and the treatment of slaves, which he repeated even when he could no longer speak clearly.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that what Rasulullaah ﷺ emphasised most on his deathbed was, "(Take good care of your) Salaah and your slaves" until his breath was caught in his…
narrations.summary: On his deathbed the Prophet stressed salaah and the treatment of slaves more than anything else, until he could no longer speak.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) relates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed me to bring him a slate to write down something that his Ummah should never forget after his demise. Fearing that he…
narrations.summary: Ali narrates that the Prophet asked for a writing so that his Ummah would never forget salaah, zakaah and the treatment of slaves, and Ali offered to memorise the words instead.

narrations.excerpt: Another similar narration adds that Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ then emphasised the performing of salaah, the paying of zakaah and kind treatment of slaves…
narrations.summary: Ali relates that the Prophet's last words, up to the departure of his soul, stressed salaah, zakaah, kindness to slaves and the Shahaadah, and that the Fire is forbidden to one who testifies to it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once said, "It is by performing salaah that a person secures Allaah's protection on earth."
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr says that a person secures Allaah's protection on earth by performing salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Maleeh reports that he heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) say from the pulpit, "There can be no Islaam in the person who does not perform salaah."
narrations.summary: Abu Maleeh reports that Umar said from the pulpit that there can be no Islaam in a person who does not perform salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) said, "When a man performs (Nafl) salaah at home, it is a source of light (for the house). As a person stands in Salaah, his sins stand…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit, Hudhayfah, Abdullaah bin Umar and Abdullaah bin Amr each give a saying on salaah, including that the ground will testify for the one who prays on it on the day he meets Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) said, "Whenever a Muslim goes to an elevated location or to a Masjid built of stone and performs salaah there, the ground says, 'Salaah has…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr said that the ground on which a Muslim prays will testify for him on the day he meets Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) also narrates that when a cyst developed on Hadhrat Aadam (RA)'s neck, he performed salaah. This made the cyst fall to his chest. When he…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr narrates that a cyst on Aadam's neck moved down his body and finally left him each time he performed salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "You are knocking at the King's (Allaah's) door as long as you are performing salaah and the door of the King opens to whoever…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that while a person performs salaah he is knocking at the King's door, and the door opens to whoever knocks.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that he said, "Stack -your needs on the Fardh salaahs (pray after these salaahs for them to be fulfilled)." 'Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA)…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood and Salmaan Faarsi say that salaah compensates for sins committed between prayers, and Ibn Mas'ood tells how Aadam's cyst fell away with each salaah; Ibn Mas'ood also advises making du'aa after the Fardh salaahs.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) once said, "As a person stands in salaah, his sins are all gathered above his head. They then fall off each time he…
narrations.summary: Salmaan Faarsi says that a person's sins gather above his head while he stands in salaah and fall away at each prostration, like leaves falling from a tree.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Taariq bin Shihaab narrates that he once spent the night with Hadhrat Salmaan to observe how he exerted himself (in Ibaadah). Hadhrat Salmaan however woke up only…
narrations.summary: Taariq bin Shihaab spent a night with Salmaan Faarsi, who advised guarding the Fardh salaahs and moderation in worship, and Abu Moosa Ash'ari said that salaah compensates for the sins that burn a person up.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) said, "(By committing sins) We are constantly burning ourselves up but when we perform the Fardh salaah, our sins are compensated for. When…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari said that the Fardh salaah compensates for the sins a person commits between one prayer and the next.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "Perfume and women have been made beloved to me and the coolness of my eyes (my source of comfort and…
narrations.summary: Anas narrates that the Prophet said perfume and women were made beloved to him and the coolness of his eyes was placed in salaah, and Ibn Abbaas narrates that Jibra'eel told the Prophet to take from salaah as much as he pleased.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) once said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, "Salaah has been made beloved to you, so take from it as much as you…
narrations.summary: Jibra'eel told the Prophet that salaah had been made beloved to him, so he should take from it as much as he pleases.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates Nabi ﷺ was once sitting with the Sahabah (RA) around him when he said, "Allaah has given every Nabi a yearning for something…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates that the Prophet said every Nabi had a yearning, his being standing in Tahajjud salaah at night, and that his income is the Khums, which goes to the leaders after him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to stand so long in (Tahajjud) salaah that his feet would swell. Another narration states that his calves would swell.…
narrations.summary: Anas narrates that the Prophet stood so long in Tahajjud salaah that his feet swelled, and when asked why, he said he should not then be a grateful servant.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) also narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to stand so long in (Tahajjud) salaah that his feet would swell. ^ ' Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Mas'ood, Nu'maan bin Basheer, Aa'isha, Mughiera and Anas describe the Prophet's long Tahajjud standing until his feet swelled or cracked, and Anas, through Humayd, describes how his night prayer, sleep and fasting varied through the month.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to stand so long in (Tahajjud) salaah at night that his feet would rupture, l said to him, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ Why do you do…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha and Anas describe how the Prophet stood so long in night salaah that his feet ruptured, and said he should be a grateful servant.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Humayd narrates that when Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) was once questioned about the salaah Rasulullaah ﷺ performed at night, he replied, "The times we wanted to…
narrations.summary: Anas describes how the Prophet's night salaah, sleep and fasting varied, so that his Companions could not predict them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) relates, "I followed Rasulullaah ﷺ in salaah one night and he remained standing so long that I contemplated doing something terrible."…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says he followed the Prophet in salaah and nearly sat down out of the length of his standing, and Abu Dharr narrates that the Prophet stood all night reciting one verse about Allaah's punishment and forgiveness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was injured one day. The following morning, someone remarked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ The effect of the injury is still clearly…
narrations.summary: Anas narrates that after the Prophet was injured he still recited seven long Surahs in the night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) says, "I performed salaah behind Rasulullaah ﷺ one night and when he commenced with Surah Baqarah, I said to myself that he would proceed into Ruku…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah narrates praying behind the Prophet at night, when he recited Surah Baqarah, Nisaa and Aal Imraan unhurriedly, pausing to glorify, ask and seek refuge as he passed each relevant verse, with long ruku and sajdah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) relates, "I once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ as he was busy performing salaah and I joined him in salaah at the back without him knowing. When he started…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah narrates joining the Prophet's salaah from behind, when the Prophet prolonged four rakaahs, and that the Prophet said he would have shortened it had he known Hudhayfah was there.

narrations.excerpt: When it was reported to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) that some people completed a recitation of the Qur'aan once or twice in a single night, she remarked, "Although those people…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha describes the Prophet's long night prayer and his final illness, when he asked Abu Bakr to lead the people in salaah despite her objections, and Ubaydullaah bin Abdullaah reports that the Prophet bathed repeatedly and fell unconscious each time he tried to go out to the people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) relates, "Abu Bakr (RA) used to lead the people in salaah during Rasulullaah ﷺ's final illness. It was on Monday and the Sahabah were standing in their…
narrations.summary: Anas narrates that Abu Bakr led the people in salaah during the Prophet's final illness, and that when the Prophet lifted the curtain and looked at them, they almost broke their salaah with joy; the Prophet passed away that day.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ did not come out of his room for three days. (On Monday) When the Iqaamah was called out and Abu Bakr stepped…
narrations.summary: Anas narrates a second account of the Prophet lifting the curtain during Abu Bakr's leading of salaah on the Monday of his final illness, and indicating to them to complete the salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhramah (RA) reports, "I went to see Umar when he was covered in a sheet (and still in a coma after he had been attacked). 'How is he?' I asked.…
narrations.summary: Miswar bin Makhramah narrates going to see Umar, who lay in a coma after being stabbed, and that Umar roused when told salaah was due, saying he must perform it, and then prayed with blood still flowing from his wound.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Miswar (RA) states that after Hadhrat Umar was stabbed, he fell into a coma. Someone said, "If he is still alive, you will not be able to…
narrations.summary: Miswar narrates a second account in which Umar, after being stabbed, regained consciousness when told the time for salaah had set in, and said that there is no part in Islaam for one who does not perform it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Miskeen narrates that when the rebels surrounded the house of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), his wife said to them, "You wish to assassinate him?! Whether you…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Miskeen narrates that Uthmaan's wife told the rebels surrounding his house that he spent whole nights reciting the entire Qur'aan in a single rakaah of salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when the rebels assassinated Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan, his wife said, "You have killed him when he was a man who spent the whole night…
narrations.summary: Another narration reports that after Uthmaan bin Affaan was assassinated, his wife said he had spent whole nights reciting the entire Qur'aan in a single rakaah of salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Abdur Rahmaan Taymi reports that his father said, "I once told myself that I would ensure that I was the only one to stand in Ibaadah by the Maqaam…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan bin Abdur Rahmaan Taymi relates that his father once saw Uthmaan recite the entire Qur'aan in one rakaah by the Maqaam Ibraheem, and Ataa bin Abi Rabaah and Muhammad bin Seereen are also reported to have spent nights reciting the whole Qur'aan in one rakaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Abdur Rahmaan Taymi relates, "I saw Hadhrat Uthmaan step forward to the Maqaam Ibraheem one night where he recited the entire Qur'aan in a single…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan once stood by the Maqaam Ibraheem at night and recited the entire Qur'aan in a single rakaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa bin Abi Rabaah reports that after leading the people in salaah, Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) would stand behind the Maqaam Ibraheem where he would recite the entire…
narrations.summary: After leading the people in salaah, Uthmaan would stand behind the Maqaam Ibraheem and recite the entire Qur'aan in one rakaah of witr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen would stand in salaah all night in which he would complete the entire Qur'aan in a single Rakaah.
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen would stand in salaah all night, completing the entire Qur'aan in a single rakaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Musayyib bin Raafi narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas became blind, a man came to him saying, "If you are able to restrain yourself from (standing…
narrations.summary: Musayyib bin Raafi narrates that Ibn Abbaas refused a treatment for his blindness that would have stopped his salaah for seven days, after the Sahabah asked what he would do with his salaah if he died in that time.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) lost his eyesight, someone offered to treat him on condition that he does not perform salaah for few…
narrations.summary: Another narration says that when Ibn Abbaas lost his sight and was offered a treatment that required him to give up salaah for a few days, he refused, quoting the Prophet that whoever neglects salaah will meet Allaah in a state of His anger.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali bin Abu Jameelah reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) made Sajdah a thousand times every day.
narrations.summary: Ali bin Abu Jameelah reports that Ibn Abbaas made sajdah a thousand times every day.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) would not fast (optional fasts) very often because he would say, "I become too weak to perform salaah when I fast and I love salaah…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood fasted optional fasts rarely, saying he grew too weak to perform salaah when fasting and loved salaah more, so he fasted only three days a month; another report says he was irregular only in the Duhaa salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that it was only the midmorning (Duhaa) salaah that he was not very regular with. Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Yazeed narrates that when Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood was not very regular with Duha salaah, and he explained that he fasted less often because fasting weakened him for salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Yazeed says, "I have not seen a who fasted less (Nafl fasts) than Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA). When someone asked him why he did not fast…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Yazeed reports that Ibn Mas'ood fasted optional fasts less than anyone he had seen, preferring salaah because fasting made him too weak to perform it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports, "I was late in coming to Rasulullaah ﷺ one night after Isha. When I came to him and he asked where I had been, I replied, "We were listening…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha narrates that the Prophet praised Saalim, freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, for his beautiful night recitation of the Qur'aan in the Masjid, saying Allaah had made such people amongst his Ummah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Masrooq reports, "We were with Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari JjUS-siSSsi on a journey when the night gave us sanctuary in a plantation. When we set up camp there,…
narrations.summary: Masrooq describes Abu Moosa Ash'ari's night salaah and supplications on a journey, and Abu Uthmaan Nahdi says he was the guest of Abu Hurayrah for seven days, when the household took turns worshipping through a third of each night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi says, "I was the guest of Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah for seven days. His servant, his wife and he would take turns to each spend a third of the night…
narrations.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi stayed seven days with Abu Hurayrah, whose household took turns worshipping through a third of each night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Talha Ansaari was once performing salaah in his orchard when a little bird flew by and, unable to find an…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr narrates that Abu Talha lost his focus in salaah on seeing a bird in his orchard, so he gave the orchard to the Prophet in charity; an unnamed Ansaari did the same with his orchard, which Uthmaan sold for 50,000 Dirhams.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) reports that (her son) Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr passed the nights in salaah and the days fasting. He was therefore called the pigeon of the Masjid…
narrations.summary: Asmaa narrates that her son Abdullaah bin Zubayr prayed through the nights and fasted through the days, and was therefore called the pigeon of the Masjid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Adi bin Haatim (RA) says, "When the time for any salaah arrives, I have already prepared for it and am brimming with fervour for it."
narrations.summary: Adi bin Haatim says that whenever the time for any salaah came, he was already prepared and full of eagerness for it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was with us as we carried the bricks to the construction site of the Masjid (Nabawi. This incident took place after the…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah helped carry bricks for the Prophet's Masjid, and when he offered to take a brick the Prophet was carrying, the Prophet told him to take another, reminding him there is no life other than the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Talq bin Ali (RA) says, "When I assisted in the construction of the Masjid together with Rasulullaah ﷺ, he said (to the others), 'Let this Yamaami (Hadhrat Talq…
narrations.summary: Talq bin Ali says that while helping build the Masjid he was told by the Prophet to mix the mortar because he did it best, and the Prophet was pleased with the way he handled the spade.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Awfa (RA) narrates that when his wife passed away, he said to the people, "Carry her (bier) with great fervour because she and her slaves would…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Awfa says that when his wife died he asked the people to carry her bier with great fervour, because she and her slaves had carried rocks for the Masjid at night when the men could manage only two rocks at a time by day.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) narrates that the Ansaar once said to him, "For how long will Rasulullaah ﷺ perform salaah beneath (a roof made of) these palm branches?"…
narrations.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit relates that the Ansaar offered the Prophet money to renovate and beautify the Masjid, but he refused, wanting its ceiling to stay like the shelter of Moosa, and Hasan describes how high that shelter was.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Shihaab reports, "The pillars of the Masjidun Nabawi during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ were trunks of palm trees while the roof was made of palm branches and…
narrations.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports that in the Prophet's time the Masjid had palm-trunk pillars and a roof of palm branches without plaster, so it became full of mud whenever it rained.

narrations.excerpt: In the chapter discussing Laylatul Qadr, Imaam Bukhaari reports a narration (from Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA)) that states: "Rasulullaah (jiif said, '(In a vision…
narrations.summary: Imaam Bukhaari reports from Abu Sa'eed Khudri that the Prophet, in a vision about Laylatul Qadr, saw himself prostrating in mud, and mud traces were later seen on his forehead after rain leaked through the palm roof during salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Ma'daan narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) were once measuring the Masjid with a stick. Coming out of his room,…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Ma'daan narrates that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha and Abu Dardaa were measuring the Masjid with a stick to build it like the buildings of Shaam, and the Prophet threw the stick away and said it should be made of grass, sticks and a roof like the shelter of Moosa, because death is nearer than that.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi narrates, "Hadhrat Umar (RA) extended the Masjid from the pillars to the Maqsoorah (the room built for the Imaam). He said, 'Had I not heard Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Naafi narrates that Umar extended the Masjid from the pillars up to the Maqsoorah, saying that he would never have done so had he not heard the Prophet say that the Masjid ought to be extended.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi reports from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) that during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, the Masjid was built with unbaked bricks, the roof was made of palm…
narrations.summary: Naafi reports from Abdullaah bin Umar that the Masjid in the Prophet's time was built of unbaked bricks with palm pillars and a palm roof, that Umar rebuilt it the same way without extending it, and that Uthmaan made a large extension in decorative stone and teakwood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Atiyya narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "During the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, the pillars of the Masjid consisted of palm trunks with the top…
narrations.summary: Atiyya narrates that Abdullaah bin Umar said the Masjid's pillars were palm trunks in the Prophet's time, were rebuilt with palm trunks in Abu Bakr's Khilaafah, and were rebuilt by Uthmaan in baked brick, where they still stand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mahmood bin Labeed reports that when Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) expressed the intention to rebuild the Masjid, the people disliked the idea because they wanted him to…
narrations.summary: Mahmood bin Labeed reports that Uthmaan cited the Prophet's saying that whoever builds a Masjid for Allaah will have a house built for him in Jannah when he decided to rebuild the Masjid, and Muttalib bin Abdullaah reports that Uthmaan, after consulting the senior Sahabah, demolished and extended it over ten months, supervising the work himself.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Usaamah Juhani (RA) says, "When I once happened to run into Rasulullaah ﷺ and some of his companions in the marketplace, I asked them where Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Usaamah Juhani says he met the Prophet and his companions in the marketplace on their way to mark out a Masjid for his people, and by the time he arrived the Prophet had marked the site and fixed the Qibla with a stick.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Ataa narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) started conquering cities, he wrote to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) who was the governor of Basrah. He…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan bin Ataa narrates that when Umar was conquering cities he wrote to the governors of Basrah, Kufa and Egypt to build one central Masjid for Jumu'ah with small tribal Masaajid, and told army commanders to set up bases in cities and build only one Masjid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) reports that one of the Sahabah (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to instruct us to make places of salaah within our homes, to build them well…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports that one Sahabi said the Prophet instructed them to make places of salaah in their homes, build them well and keep them clean, and Aa'isha reports the same instruction.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when a woman who used to remove dirt from the Masjid passed away, the Sahabah (RA) did not inform Rasulullaah ﷺ about her…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas narrates that the Sahabah buried a woman who used to clean the Masjid without telling the Prophet, and when he learned of it he prayed the Janaazah for her and said he had seen her in Jannah picking up dirt from the Masjid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Urhar (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to burn incense in the Masjid of Rasulullaah ﷺ every Friday.
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Urhar (RA) reports that Umar used to burn incense in the Prophet's Masjid every Friday.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) says, "There was a person who in my knowledge lived furthest from the Masjid. He however never missed a single salaah. Someone once suggested…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b says that a man who lived furthest from the Masjid never missed salaah, and when told to buy a donkey he refused, wanting every step to be recorded for him, and the Prophet said Allaah has recorded it all for him.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) says, "There was a person from the Ansaar whose house was the furthest (from the Masjid) in Madinah. He however never…
narrations.summary: In another narration Ubay bin Ka'b says that a man from the Ansaar, whose house was furthest from the Masjid, refused a donkey because he hoped for reward in every step, and the Prophet told him he would have what he hoped for.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "His stages (in Jannah) are elevated with every step that he takes."
narrations.summary: Another narration states that the Prophet said the stages of the Ansaari man in Jannah are raised with every step he takes to the Masjid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) narrates that when he used to walk with Rasulullaah ﷺ when they went for salaah, Rasulullaah ﷺ took short steps. "Do you know why I shorten…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit narrates that when he walked with the Prophet to salaah the Prophet took short steps, explaining that a person keeps the reward of salaah while he is making the effort toward it and that he did so to increase his steps toward salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ's explanation was: "1 am doing this only so that my steps in the effort of (going for) salaah are increased."
narrations.summary: The Prophet explains that his reason for walking to the masjid with short steps is to increase the steps he takes for salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thaabit (RA) says, "I was once walking with Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik in Zaawiyah (a district of Basrah) when he heard the Adhaan. He then started to shorten his…
narrations.summary: Thaabit says he walked with Anas bin Maalik in Zaawiyah, and when Anas heard the Adhaan he shortened his steps until he entered the Masjid, explaining that this was so his steps in the effort of salaah would be increased.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once left home for the Masjid. When he started to hurry, someone asked, "Why are you doing this when you prevent others from it?"…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood hurried to the Masjid, and when someone objected he said he wanted to reach the first takbeer and that salaah is the most deserving thing to hurry toward, a reply Salamah bin Kuhayl also reports.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Qataadah narrates that as they were once performing salaah behind Rasulullaah ﷺ, he heard some clamouring from the people at the back. After completing the…
narrations.summary: Abu Qataadah narrates that while the Sahabah were praying behind the Prophet he heard noise from those at the back, and after salaah the Prophet forbade running to salaah and told them to pray what they caught and complete what they had missed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that they were once in a Masjid with Rasulullaah when a Bedouin stood in the Masjid and started urinating there. "Stop! Stop!" the Sahabah (RA)…
narrations.summary: Anas narrates that when a Bedouin began urinating in the Masjid and the Sahabah shouted at him, the Prophet told them to leave him alone, then had a bucket of water poured over the spot and explained that Masjids are for the remembrance of Allaah, salaah and the Qur'aan, not for filth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) once approached a group of people in the Masjid. "What makes you people sit here?" he asked. "We are…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri narrates that Mu'aawiya questioned a group sitting in the Masjid for dhikr and got their oath of sincerity, then related that the Prophet asked the same of his Sahabah and told them Jibra'eel had reported that Allaah boasts of them before the angels.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waaqid Haarith bin Auf (RA) narrates that they were once sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ when three persons arrived. While two of them came towards Rasulullaah ﷺ,…
narrations.summary: Abu Waaqid Laythi narrates that the Prophet described three people who came to a gathering, one of whom found a place and was granted it, one of whom was shy and was treated kindly, and one of whom turned away and was turned away from, and Abul Qamraa relates that the Prophet sat with those learning and teaching the Qur'aan, saying he had been commanded to sit with that gathering.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Kulayb bin Shihaab narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once heard a lot of sound from the Masjid as people were busy reciting the Qur'aan and teaching others to do so.…
narrations.summary: Kulayb bin Shihaab narrates that Ali, hearing loud Qur'aan recitation and teaching in the Masjid, said these were the people the Prophet loved most, and also reports Ali saying the same in the Masjid of Kufa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) once passed through the market place of Madinah when he stood there and called out, "O traders! What makes you so…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Abu Hurayrah called out in the Madinah marketplace that the traders were missing the Prophet's inheritance, which was only people praying, reciting the Qur'aan and discussing halaal and haraam in the Masjid, and he rebuked them for it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Mu'aawiya Kindi reports that when he once went to see Hadhrat Umar in Shaam, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him about the condition of the people and said further,…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mu'aawiya Kindi reports that when he visited Umar in Shaam, Umar asked whether men sat in the Masjid only with their own tribe or acquaintances, and he replied that their Masjid had gatherings for learning and sharing good, so Umar said they would remain in good stead as long as they continued so.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that they were sitting in the Masjid one day when Rasulullaah ﷺ came out of his room and said, "Let us go to the Jews." (When he…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah narrates that the Prophet came out with the Sahabah and called the Jews to accept Islaam, and after they refused three times he told them the earth belongs to Allaah and His Rasool and that he wished to banish them, allowing them to sell their belongings first.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA) was injured during the Battle of Khandaq when a person by the name of Hibbaan bin Ariqah shot an arrow…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha narrates that Sa'd bin Mu'aadh was wounded at Khandaq and lodged in a tent in the Masjid, that Jibra'eel then directed the Prophet to Banu Qurayzah, where Sa'd ruled that their fighters be killed and their women and children enslaved, and that Sa'd's wound burst open and he died after praying for death if no further war with Quraysh remained.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abdullaah bin Qusayt (RA) says that the men of the Suffa were men during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ who had no homes. They slept and took shelter in the…
narrations.summary: Yazeed bin Abdullaah bin Qusayt says that the men of the Suffa were homeless men of the Prophet's time who slept in the Masjid, and that the Prophet would call some of them at night to eat supper with him until Allaah made them independent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asmaa bint Yazeed (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) used to be in the service of Rasulullaah ﷺ and whenever he had finished, he took shelter in the…
narrations.summary: Asmaa bint Yazeed narrates that Abu Dharr served the Prophet and then lay down to sleep in the Masjid as his home, and when the Prophet found him lying there and nudged him with his foot, Abu Dharr sat up and asked where else he had to sleep.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) himself reports that after serving Rasulullaah ﷺ, he used to lie down in the Masjid. Several incidents describing how the Sahabah (RA) slept in the…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr says that after serving the Prophet he would lie down in the Masjid, Hasan says he saw Uthmaan take his siesta there during his Khilaafah, Abdullaah bin Umar says that as youths they spent nights in the Masjid and rested there after Jumu'ah, and Umar says lying on one's side is fine after sitting long in the Masjid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaleed bin Abu Is'haaq narrates that he once asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas about sleeping in the Masjid. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas replied, "There is no…
narrations.summary: Khaleed bin Abu Is'haaq asked Abdullaah bin Abbaas about sleeping in the Masjid, and Ibn Abbaas replied that there is no harm in it when one sleeps to gain strength for salaah or Tawaaf.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "Whenever the wind blew fiercely at night, Rasulullaah ﷺ hastened towards the Masjid and would remain there until the wind subsided. He would…
narrations.summary: Jaabir says that when the wind blew fiercely at night the Prophet hurried to the Masjid and stayed until it calmed, and that he also hurried to salaah at eclipses, and Ataa reports that the Sahabi Ya'la bin Umayyah would sit in the Masjid even briefly with the intention of I'tikaaf.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa reports that a Sahabi by the name of Hadhrat Ya'la bin Umayyah' used to sit for even a moment in the Masjid with the intention of performing I'tikaaf.
narrations.summary: Ataa reports that the Companion Ya'la bin Umayyah would sit in the masjid, even for a moment, with the intention of i'tikaaf.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Atiyya bin Sufyaan bin Abdullaah (RA) narrates, "When a delegation from the Thaqeef came to Rasulullaah ﷺ one Ramadhaan, Rasulullaah ﷺ pitched a tent for them in…
narrations.summary: Atiyya bin Sufyaan bin Abdullaah narrates that when a delegation from Thaqeef came to the Prophet during Ramadhaan he pitched a tent for them in the Masjid, and once they accepted Islaam they began fasting with him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Abil Aas (RA) narrates that when the Thaqeef delegation came to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he accommodated them in the Masjid so that it would soften their…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan bin Abil Aas narrates that when the Thaqeef delegation came the Prophet housed them in the Masjid so that it would soften their hearts.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) says, "We once ate roasted meat with Rasulullaah ﷺ in the Masjid. When the Iqaamah was called out for salaah, all we did was wipe our…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr says that they once ate roasted meat with the Prophet in the Masjid, and when the Iqaamah was called they only wiped their hands on pebbles.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that the Masjidul Fadeekh got its name from the fact that it was in this Masjid that some Fadeekh was served to Rasulullaah ﷺ and…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports why the Masjid was called Masjidul Fadeekh, since the Prophet drank Fadeekh there, and the author lists other events that took place in the Masjid.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah was in the Masjidul Fadeekh when he was brought a jug of Fadeekh made from half-ripe dates. Because Rasulullaah ﷺ drank the…
narrations.summary: The Prophet drank fadeekh in a masjid, which is why it was named Masjidul Fadeekh; the rest is the author's cross-reference to other narrations about the masjid.

narrations.excerpt: A freed slave of Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) says that he was once with Thaqeef Tribe Sends Abd Yaaleel bin Amr with a Delegation to Rasulullaah ﷺ, who is Informed of…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri is with the Prophet when they enter the Masjid and see a man sitting with his fingers interlaced, which the Prophet forbids as prompted by Shaytaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) narrates that after Rasulullaah ﷺ conquered Khaybar, the Sahabah (RA) became infatuated with garlic and started eating it often. It was then that…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr reports that the Prophet barred anyone who had eaten garlic or onions from coming near the Masaajid, and Umar repeats this in a Jumu'ah lecture, advising that the smell be cooked out first.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that as Rasulullaah ﷺ was once delivering a lecture, he noticed some phlegm on the wall in the direction of the Qibla.…
narrations.summary: The Prophet forbids spitting in front of or to the right of a person praying, and Umar rebukes two men from Taa'if for raising their voices in the Masjid after Saa'ib brings them to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that Hadhrat Banna Juhani (RA) informed him that Rasulullaah ﷺ once saw or passed by some people who were exchanging naked swords amongst…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports, through Banna Juhani, that the Prophet saw people passing naked swords to each other in the Masjid and cursed them, saying a sword must be sheathed before it is handed over. Sulaymaan bin Moosa reports that Jaabir said arrows carried through the Masjid must be held firmly by their heads.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sulaymaan-bin Moosa narrates that when Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) was asked about drawing swords in the Masjid, he said, "We have always disapproved of it. In fact, when…
narrations.summary: Jaabir said swords should not be drawn in the masjid, and the Prophet told a man carrying arrows through it to hold their heads firmly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Abdullaah narrates that they were once in the Masjid with Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) when a person turned an arrow around. Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Abdullaah was in the Masjid with Abu Sa'eed Khudri when a man turned an arrow round, and Abu Sa'eed reminded him that the Prophet forbade turning weapons around in the Masjid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) narrates that a man once made an announcement in the Masjid saying, "Who has called for (the owner of) a red camel (that he has found)?" Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Buraydah reports that the Prophet rebuked a man who announced a lost red camel in the Masjid, saying the Masaajid were built for their own purposes. Ibn Mas'ood silenced a similar announcer, and Ibn Seereen reports that Ubay bin Ka'b angrily rebuked a man for asking after a lost item in the Masjid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Seereen reports that when Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) heard a person asking after his lost item in the Masjid, he became angry (and rebuked the man). "O Abul…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b rebuked a man who called out for a lost item in the masjid, saying they had been commanded to do so.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saa'ib bin Yazeed (RA) narrates that he was once sleeping in the Masjid when someone threw a pebble at him. When he looked up, he saw that it was Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Saa'ib bin Yazeed was sleeping in the Masjid when Umar threw a pebble at him. Umar had two men from Taa'if brought to him and rebuked them for raising their voices in the Prophet's Masjid, saying he would have punished them had they been from Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Ibraheem reports from his father that when Hadhrat Umar heard someone speaking in the Masjid, he asked, "Do you know where you are? Do you know where…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Ibraheem reports from his father that Umar told someone talking loudly in the Masjid to remember where they were, since Umar disliked loud speech there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that whenever Hadhrat Umar went to the Masjid, he announced in the Masjid, "Dc refrain from making a noise." Another narration…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar, Saalim and others report that Umar forbade noise, raised voices and futile talk in the Masjid, and had a platform built beside it for anyone who wanted to make noise.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Taariq bin Shihaab narrates that it was in the Masjid that a person was brought before Hadhrat Umar (RA) for some crime. Hadhrat Umar (RA) gave instructions that…
narrations.summary: Taariq bin Shihaab reports that Umar had a man who was brought before him for a crime taken out of the Masjid before he was beaten.

narrations.excerpt: It was between the Adhaan and Iqaamah of Fajr that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood once saw some people reclining against the wall of the Masjid in the direction of the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood sees people leaning against the Masjid wall facing the Qibla between the Adhaan and Iqaamah of Fajr and tells them not to block the angels' salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Aamir Alhaani narrates that a Sahabi by the name of Hadhrat Haabis bin Sa'd Taa'ee (RA) once entered the Masjid before dawn and saw some people…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Aamir Alhaani reports that Haabis bin Sa'd Taa'ee, a Sahabi, told people praying at the front of the Masjid before dawn that they should be driven off because they were showing off.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Murrah Hamdaani says, "I told myself that I would perform two Rakaahs salaah behind every pillar of the Masjid in Kufa. As I was busy performing salaah, Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Murrah Hamdaani planned to pray behind every pillar in the Masjid of Kufa, and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood said that someone who knew Allaah was at the nearest pillar would not pass it without completing his salaah there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umayr bin Anas narrates that from his uncles who belonged to the Ansaar that when Rasulullaah ﷺ became concerned about how to gather the people for salaah,…
narrations.summary: Abu Umayr bin Anas reports from his Ansaar uncles that the Prophet, troubled about calling people to salaah, rejected a flag, the trumpet and the bell, and that Abdullaah bin Zaid was then shown the Adhaan in a dream.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sheikh narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zaid (RA) said, "Announcing the salaah was a great concern for Rasulullaah ﷺ (during the early days). Whenever the…
narrations.summary: Abu Sheikh reports Abdullaah bin Zaid's account of the Prophet's worry about calling people to salaah, the rejected bell and trumpet, and the Adhaan he saw in a dream, and Anas adds that someone once called out in the streets.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi bin Jubayr, Hadhrat Urwa bin Zaid bin Aslam and Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib all relate that before receiving the directive to call out the Adhaan, Nabi ﷺ's…
narrations.summary: Naafi bin Jubayr, Urwa bin Zaid bin Aslam and Sa'eed bin Musayyab report that before the Adhaan, the call 'As salaatu jaami'ah' was used to gather people for salaah and for important announcements.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd Qaradh (RA) reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Quba, Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) would call out the Adhaan to inform the people that Rasulullaah ﷺ had…
narrations.summary: Sa'd Qaradh reports that when the Prophet came to Quba without Bilaal, Sa'd climbed a date palm and called the Adhaan to bring Muslims quickly, and the Prophet approved, telling him to call it whenever Bilaal was not with him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) said, "The share (of rewards) of those who call out the Adhaan on the Day of Qiyaamah will be like the share of those who wage Jihaad.…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, Abdullaah bin Mas'ood and Umar each praise the reward of the Mu'adhin, Umar quotes the Prophet praying for them, and Aa'isha links a Qur'aanic verse to the Mu'adhin.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "Had I been a Mu'adhin, I care not if I neither perform Hajj or Umrah except for the Fardh Hajj. Had the angels descended on earth, none…
narrations.summary: Umar says that if he were a Mu'adhin he would not mind missing Hajj or Umrah apart from the Fardh Hajj, because the angels would call the Adhaan themselves if they came down to earth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Abu Haazim narrates that when they went to Hadhrat Umar he asked, "Who calls out the Adhaan amongst you people?" When they informed him that it was their…
narrations.summary: Qais bin Abi Haazim reports that when he went to Umar and was told their slaves called the Adhaan, Umar called this a grave deficiency and said he would rather be a Mu'adhin than Khalifah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "I regret not requesting Rasulullaah ﷺ to assign the duty of calling out the Adhaan to (my sons) Hasan and Husayn."
narrations.summary: Ali says he regrets not asking the Prophet to appoint Hasan and Husayn as Mu'adhins, and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says he does not approve of appointing blind men or Qur'aan scholars to call the Adhaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "I do not approve of you appointing blind people to call out the Adhaan (because they are unable to determine the correct times…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood disapproves of appointing blind men or Qur'aan teachers to call the adhaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya Bakkaa narrates that a man once said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar, "I love you for the sake of Allaah." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar responded by saying,…
narrations.summary: Yahya Bakkaa reports that Abdullaah bin Umar told a man who loved him for Allaah's sake that he disliked him for Allaah's sake, because the man sang the Adhaan and took payment for it.

narrations.excerpt: When Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sa'eed bin Al Aas to Yemen, he gave him instructions to take as prisoners the inhabitants of all the towns he passed in…
narrations.summary: The Prophet sends Khaalid bin Sa'eed to Yemen with orders to take prisoner the people of any town where the Adhaan is not called, Amr bin Ma'dikarib gets Khaalid to release the Banu Zubayd, and Talha reports Abu Bakr's order to his commanders against the apostates.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zuhri narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr 5S5.l2ffiSg dispatched his armies against the Murtaddeen, he instructed them saying, "Monitor them overnight and take no…
narrations.summary: Zuhri reports that Abu Bakr, sending armies against the apostates, told them to hold off if they heard the Adhaan, because the Adhaan is a sign of Imaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates that when the time for salaah arrived and Rasulullaah ﷺ saw that the people were few in number, he remain sitting and did not lead the salaah.…
narrations.summary: Ali reports that when the time for salaah came and the Prophet saw few people, he stayed seated and did not lead the salaah until a substantial gathering had come.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Awfa (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ would wait until he heard the sounds of people's shoes.
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abi Awfa reports that the Prophet would wait until he heard the sound of people's shoes before he began the salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was busy dispatching an army until half the night had already passed or was about to. He then came out for salaah and said…
narrations.summary: Umar reports that the Prophet, busy sending an army until about half the night had passed, came out to those still waiting for salaah and told them they were in salaah for as long as they were waiting.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) narrates that after Rasulullaah ﷺ had performed the Maghrib salaah, some people left while others remained seated. Rasulullaah ﷺ then went…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that the Prophet told those who stayed seated after Maghrib that their Rabb boasts of them to the angels, and Abu Umaamah Thaqafi reports Mu'aawiya telling people to stay seated after Zuhr, citing the same saying of the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once delayed the Isha salaah until midnight. After leading the salaah, he turned to face the Sahabah saying, "Whereas other…
narrations.summary: Anas and Abu Hurayrah report that the Prophet told people waiting for Isha that they are in salaah while they wait, and that the angels keep praying for them until they leave their place or break wudhu.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Rasool ﷺ said, "A person is in salaah for as long as it is salaah that keeps him waiting and (all the while) the angels keep…
narrations.summary: The Prophet says a person keeps receiving the angels' prayers for his forgiveness for as long as salaah keeps him waiting in his place.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that a person remains in salaah for as long as he remains on his place of salaah or as long as he does not break his wudhu." ^ Yet another…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that a person keeps receiving the angels' prayers while he waits in his place of salaah, and that wudhu breaks when wind is passed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Shall I not point you towards something that wipes out sins and is expiation for misdeeds?" "Why not,…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports that the Prophet said making wudhu in difficult conditions, walking often to the Masjid and waiting from one salaah to the next wipe out sins and count as guarding the borders.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dawood bin Saalih narrates that Hadhrat Abu Salamah once asked him if he knew why Allaah revealed the verse-. Exercise patience, compete in patience, guard the…
narrations.summary: Dawood bin Saalih reports Abu Salamah's explanation, citing Abu Hurayrah, that waiting for salaah one after another was how the Companions guarded the borders in the Prophet's time, when there was no war.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) said that it is waiting for the Isha salaah that is referred to in the verse: ij s-yycr Their sides part from their beds... (Surah Sajdah, verse 16)
narrations.summary: Anas says that the verse about the sides parting from the beds refers to waiting for the Isha salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Ummu Maktoom (RA) once said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I am a blind man who lives far (from the Masjid). While I have a guide, he is a person with whom I cannot…
narrations.summary: Ibn Ummu Maktoom asks the Prophet to let him pray at home because he is blind and far from the Masjid, and the Prophet tells him to come if he can hear the Adhaan or Iqaamah, and says he had considered burning the houses of those who do not come to salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "Whoever wishes to meet Allaah tomorrow as a Muslim should regularly perform these (Fardh) salaahs in the place where the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that a Muslim who wants to meet Allaah as a Muslim should pray the Fardh salaahs in congregation where the Adhaan is called, because missing them forsakes the Sunnah of the Prophet, and that in his time only hypocrites or the very sick missed congregational salaah.

narrations.excerpt: A narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) added, "And now 1 cannot find who does not have a place of salaah inside his house where he performs salaah. If…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says that people who pray at home and leave the masjids forsake the Sunnah of the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) said, "Whoever would like to go peacefully to Allaah should perform these five (Fardh) salaahs at a place where the Adhaan is called out…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal says that the five Fardh salaahs should be prayed where the Adhaan is called, following the Prophet's practice, and that one should not claim a place at home for salaah, and the text breaks off into a footnote.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "When we did not see a person for the Fajr and Isha salaahs, we became suspicious of him (because it is the Munaafiqeen who do not…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says that when a person was not seen at the Fajr and Isha salaahs, they became suspicious of him, because it is the hypocrites who skip those prayers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Sulaymaan bin Abu Hathma narrates that Hadhrat Umar once did not see Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Abu Hathma (RA) for the Fajr salaah. Hadhrat Umar (RA) was…
narrations.summary: Umar did not see Sulaymaan bin Abu Hathma at the Fajr salaah, and his mother Shifaa explained that he had spent the night in prayer and sleep overtook him. Umar said he preferred attending Fajr in congregation to standing in prayer all night. In another report, Shifaa bint Abdullaah tells Umar that her husband and son slept after praying Fajr at home, and Umar again said he preferred Fajr in congregation to a night of Nafl.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Dardaa (RA) says that when (her husband) Hadhrat Abu Dardaa once came home angry, she asked him what the matter was. He replied, "By Allaah! I know nothing…
narrations.summary: Ummu Dardaa reports that her husband Abu Dardaa came home angry because people were starting to pray apart from congregation, and Naafi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar, when he missed the Isha salaah in congregation, stayed in worship through the night.
