narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that whenever Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar missed any salaah in congregation, he would remain engaged in salaah until the next salaah.
narrations.summary: Ibn Umar, whenever he missed a congregational salaah, would keep praying until the next salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ambasah bin Azhar narrates that it was customary for a newly married man to remain indoors for a few days after getting married and not to leave for the Fajr…
narrations.summary: Ambasah bin Azhar reports that a newly married man usually stayed indoors for a few days and did not go out for Fajr, but when Haarith bin Hassaan went out for Fajr on his wedding night and was taunted, he said that a wife who kept him from congregational Fajr would be a terrible woman.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to go to the ends of the rows and straighten the chests and shoulders of the people saying, "Do not be in…
narrations.summary: Baraa bin Aazib narrates that the Prophet went along the rows straightening chests and shoulders, and warned that disorder in the rows brings disunity to the hearts, while Allaah shows special mercy to the first row.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to weave between the rows from one end to the other, touching our chests and shoulders (when straightening the…
narrations.summary: Baraa bin Aazib reports that the Prophet walked between the rows, touching chests and shoulders to straighten them, and said not to stand in disarray.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Samurah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came out to them and said, "Will you not form your rows as the angels form theirs in front of their…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Samurah narrates that the Prophet asked the Sahabah why they did not form rows as the angels do, the angels completing the front rows first and standing close together.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Samurah (RA) also narrates that they were once performing salaah with Rasulullaah ﷺ when he motioned them to sit down. When they sat down, Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Samurah narrates that the Prophet motioned them to sit during salaah and asked what prevented them from forming rows as the angels do.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Basheer (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to straighten our rows as meticulously as he would straighten an arrow. This he did until we had understood him…
narrations.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer says that the Prophet straightened the rows as meticulously as an arrow, and on seeing one man's chest standing out he warned that Allaah would cast disunity between them unless they straightened their rows.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Nu'maan (RA) added, "I then saw a man touching his shoulders with those of the person beside him, touching his knees with those of…
narrations.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer adds that he then saw each man touch his shoulder, knee and ankle against the man beside him when the rows were straightened.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to instruct the people to straighten their rows and it was only when they reported to him that the rows were…
narrations.summary: Umar had the people straighten their rows and would not call the takbeer until he was told the rows were straight.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi (RA) reports that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) used to instruct the people to straighten their rows and would actually call people by their names to…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan had the people straighten their rows, calling them by name, and Abu Uthmaan also saw that Umar, before leading, looked at the shoulders and feet of those behind him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Nadhar narrates that when salaah was about to begin, Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab would tell people to straighten their rows and would take people's names as he…
narrations.summary: Abu Nadhar reports that Umar took people's names to move them forward or back to straighten the rows, saying Allaah wants them to follow the way of the angels' rows.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maalik says, "I was with Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) when the people stood up for salaah. I was busy requesting him to grant me an allowance and continued…
narrations.summary: Maalik recounts how Uthmaan, while Maalik was asking him for an allowance, straightened pebbles with his shoe and only then had the rows made straight before calling the takbeer, and that Ali told worshippers straight rows bring straight hearts.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "I saw a time when salaah would not begin until we had completed the rows of salaah." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says the rows were always completed before salaah began and that those who advance to the first row earn Allaah's mercy, and a report of Aamir bin Mas'ood racing for the first row recalls the Prophet's saying about its value.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Ensure that you always stand in the first row and ensure that it is on the right of the first row. You should also refrain from…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas tells the people to always stand in the first row, on its right side, and not to form rows between pillars.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Ubaadah says, "I was present in Madinah when the people stood up for salaah. I then forged ahead and stood in the first row. Hadhrat Umar arrived and…
narrations.summary: Qais bin Ubaadah was pushed out of the first row in Madinah, by Umar in one account and by Ubay bin Ka'b in another, and each explained the Prophet's ruling that only the Muhaajireen and Ansaar should occupy it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Usaamah bin Umayr (RA) says, "People would have already stood up for salaah when a person would stand between Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Qibla, presenting his need to…
narrations.summary: Several reports describe the Prophet hearing people's needs even after the iqaamah had been called, and Anas says he was the most compassionate of people, staying with a Bedouin who held his clothes until the request was met.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was the most compassionate of people and whenever someone came to him (with a request), he would promise it to him (if he did not…
narrations.summary: Anas says the Prophet stood up with a Bedouin who held his clothing and demanded his due, and only then returned to lead salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi says, "Salaah would be about to commence when a person would come before Hadhrat Umar (RA) to discuss something. In fact, some of us would…
narrations.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi says people kept Umar talking about their needs even as salaah was about to begin, and Moosa bin Talha heard Uthmaan asking people about their conditions and market prices while the iqaamah was called.

narrations.excerpt: Detailed narrations have already appeared in the chapter discussing the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and the Conquest of Madinah in which it is stated that Rasulullaah said to…
narrations.summary: After accepting Islaam, Abu Sufyaan watched the Sahabah follow the Prophet in salaah with great discipline, and when he called it a kingdom, Abbaas replied that it was Nubuwwah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Maymoona (RA) quoted in the chapter discussing the Conquest of Makkah states that when Rasulullaah ﷺ got up to perform wudhu, the Muslims…
narrations.summary: Maymoona relates that the Muslims competed for the water the Prophet had used for wudhu, and Abu Sufyaan called it a kingdom, which Abbaas corrected to Nubuwwah.

narrations.excerpt: A narration from Hadhrat Urwa (RA) states that when Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan awoke the morning after he had spent the night with Hadhrat Abbaas he saw the Sahabah (RA)…
narrations.summary: Urwa relates that Abu Sufyaan saw the Sahabah hurrying to purify themselves and bowing and prostrating exactly as the Prophet did, and Abbaas said they would obey him even if told to give up food and drink.

narrations.excerpt: In the chapter discussing the enthusiasm Rasulullaah ﷺ had for salaah, a narration from Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) has already passed stating that (when he was critically ill)…
narrations.summary: Umar began leading the salaah during the Prophet's final illness while Abu Bakr was absent, and when the Prophet learned this he had Abu Bakr lead, saying that neither Allaah nor the Muslims could accept otherwise.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Rasulullaah ﷺ heard Hadhrat Umar voice, he came out and with his head out of the room, he said angrily, "No! No! None but the son of…
narrations.summary: When the Prophet heard Umar's voice in salaah he angrily declared that only Abu Bakr should lead, and Abu Ubaydah, Ali and Zubayr later cited this to support Abu Bakr's leadership.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, the Ansaar said, "There should be an Ameer from us and one from you (Muhaajireen)."…
narrations.summary: After the Prophet's death the Ansaar proposed one Ameer from them and one from the Muhaajireen, but Umar reminded them that the Prophet had placed Abu Bakr forward in salaah, and they said they would never put themselves ahead of him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ certainly instructed Abu Bakr to lead the salaah when 1 was present, neither unavailable nor ill. Therefore, to take charge of our…
narrations.summary: Ali says that because the Prophet chose Abu Bakr to lead the salaah while Ali was present and well, he is content to accept Abu Bakr as Khalifah for worldly affairs too.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Layla Kindi reports that Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) once arrived with a group of twelve or thirteen riders from amongst the companions of Rasulullaah ﷺ. When…
narrations.summary: Salmaan Faarsi refused to lead Arab companions in salaah, saying non-Arabs could not lead Arabs, and when a man led four rakaahs on a journey, Salmaan said two would have been enough.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed was a slave of the Banu Usayd tribe. He prepared a meal one day and invited Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA), Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed, a slave of the Banu Usayd, hosted a meal for Abu Dharr, Hudhayfah and Ibn Mas'ood, and when salaah began they confirmed the host's right to lead, so Abu Sa'eed, though a slave, led them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi reports, "People had stood up for salaah in a Masjid in a district of Madinah where Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) had a property. The Imaam of the Masjid…
narrations.summary: Naafi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar declined to lead in a Madinah masjid whose imam was a slave, and Abdullaah bin Handhala reports that Qais bin Sa'd had one of his slaves lead the salaah in his house, following the Prophet's ruling that the householder has the right to lead.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Alqama narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once visited Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) at his house. When the time for salaah arrived, Hadhrat Abu…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood and Abu Moosa each urged the other to lead the salaah at Abu Moosa's house, and Abu Moosa, who led, had taken off his shoes, which Ibn Mas'ood asked about.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA), "O Abu Moosa! You know well that the Sunnah practice is for the…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood reminds Abu Moosa that the Sunnah is for the owner of the house to lead, but Abu Moosa refused until one of their slaves went forward.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Zuhayr (RA) says, "I once walked with Handhala bin Rabee to the Masjid of Furaat bin Hayyaan. When the time for salaah arrived, Hadhrat Furaat (RA) told…
narrations.summary: Furaat bin Hayyaan asked Handhala bin Rabee to lead the salaah in his masjid, and when Handhala refused, Furaat said the Prophet had praised Handhala after sending him as a spy to Taa'if, so Handhala led.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla (RA) narrates that when he once accompanied Hadhrat Umar (RA) to Makkah, they were received by the Hadhrat Naafi bin Alqama (RA) who…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abi Layla reports that Umar objected when Naafi bin Alqama, governor of Makkah, appointed a man from among the slaves, Abdur Rahmaan bin Abzah, to lead the salaah, and was satisfied when Naafi explained he was the best reciter of the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubayd bin Umayr (RA) narrates that it was during the Hajj season when a large gathering of people amassed around a spring in Makkah. When the time for salaah…
narrations.summary: At a Hajj gathering in Makkah, Miswar bin Makhrama pulled back a non-Arabic-speaking man of the Makhzoom family who was leading the salaah, because his unclear recitation could be copied by pilgrims, and Umar, after questioning him in Madinah, approved.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydullaah (RA) once led some people in salaah. When he turned to them (after completing the salaah), he said, "1 had forgotten to consult with you…
narrations.summary: Talha bin Ubaydullaah asked the congregation after leading the salaah whether they were pleased with it, recalling the Prophet's warning that the salaah of a leader whom the people dislike does not even pass his ears, let alone reach the heavens.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar bin Abdul Azeez once asked Hadhrat Anas (RA) why he did not perform salaah behind him(4). Hadhrat Anas (RA) replied, "I had seen Rasulullaah ﷺ perform salaah…
narrations.summary: Anas refused to pray behind Umar bin Abdul Azeez, and Abu Ayyoob Ansaari refused to pray behind Marwaan bin Hakam, each saying he would only follow an imam whose salaah matched the Prophet's.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Jaabir Waalidi says, "I once asked Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) (after he had led the salaah), 'Was the salaah of Rasulullaah ﷺ like this?' 'What did you not…
narrations.summary: Abu Jaabir Waalidi asked Abu Hurayrah whether his salaah matched the Prophet's, and Abu Hurayrah said it did but was shorter, with the standing as brief as the time a muezzin takes to come down from the minaret.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) once said, "The salaah' we performed with Rasulullaah ﷺ was such that you people will criticise if anyone had to perform the same (because of its…
narrations.summary: Anas says the Prophet's salaah was so brief that people would criticise anyone who copied it, and Adi bin Haatim, after an imam prolonged his sitting, led a brief salaah in the Prophet's manner; Anas refused to follow imams who prolonged it until Umar bin Abdul Azeez stopped the practice.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Adi bin Haatim (RA) once attended a gathering and when the time for salaah arrived, the Imaam went forward and led the salaah. However, because he prolonged the…
narrations.summary: Adi bin Haatim criticised an imam who prolonged the salaah, then led briefly himself; Anas refused to follow such imams until Umar bin Abdul Azeez ended the practice.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "After spending the night, Rasulullaah ﷺ would be summoned (to salaah) by Bilaal calling out the Adhaan. He would then get up and take a bath.…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says that after bathing, the Prophet would leave for salaah when Bilaal called the adhaan, and she would hear him weeping in salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubayd bin Umayr (RA) once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "Tell me what the most remarkable incident that you saw with Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Aa'isha was silent for…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha describes a night when the Prophet wept in salaah until the ground around him was soaked, and when Bilaal asked why, he said he should be a grateful slave after a verse was revealed to him; Mutarraf's father heard the weeping like a grindstone in his chest.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Shaddaad bin Al Haad says, "I was standing in one of the last rows during the Fajr salaah and I could hear Hadhrat Umar (RA) cry aloud as he recited…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Shaddaad says he heard Umar weeping aloud in the Fajr salaah while reciting Surah Yusuf, when he reached the verse about complaining of sorrow to Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "When performing salaah behind Hadhrat Umar (RA), I could hear his weeping from three rows back."
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says that when he prayed behind Umar he could hear Umar's weeping from three rows back.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sahl bin Sa'd (RA) says that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) could not be distracted when performing salaah.
narrations.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd says that Abu Bakr could not be distracted while performing salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaahid says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) would stand (still) like a stick in salaah, which was exactly as Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) used to do. That is what…
narrations.summary: Mujaahid says that Abdullaah bin Zubayr stood as still as a stick in salaah, as Abu Bakr used to do, and that this is what devotion in salaah means.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaahid says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) would stand (still) like a stick in salaah. It is said that this was due to his devotion in salaah."
narrations.summary: Mujaahid says that Abdullaah bin Zubayr stood as still as a stick in salaah, as Abu Bakr used to do, and that this is what devotion in salaah means.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibnul Munkadir says, "Had you seen Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr performing salaah, you would surely say that he is a branch of a tree that the wind laps over. In…
narrations.summary: Several reports describe Abdullaah bin Zubayr standing motionless in salaah, and Abdullaah bin Umar walking to salaah so slowly, and facing the Qibla so carefully, that even his thumbs were turned towards it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tawoos says, "I have never seen anyone perform salaah like Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar. He was so particular about facing the Qibla that even his face, palms and…
narrations.summary: Taa'oos says he had never seen anyone as careful to face the Qibla in salaah as Abdullaah bin Umar, whose face, palms and feet all faced it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Burdah narrates, "1 once performed salaah next to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar iS When he was in Sajdah, I heard him say, 'O Allaah! Make Yourself the most…
narrations.summary: Abu Burdah prayed beside Abdullaah bin Umar and heard him ask Allaah in sajdah to make Himself the most beloved and most feared to him, and heard him say he hoped each salaah would atone for his sins.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat A'mash stated that whenever Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) performed salaah, he (was so still that he) appeared to be a discarded piece of cloth.
narrations.summary: A'mash says that when Abdullaah bin Mas'ood prayed he was so still that he looked like a discarded piece of cloth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Roomaan (RA) says, "When Abu Bakr • once saw me leaning while performing salaah, he reprimanded me so sternly that I almost terminated my salaah. He then…
narrations.summary: Ummu Roomaan says Abu Bakr sternly reprimanded her for leaning in salaah, quoting the Prophet that one should stand at ease and not lean as the Jews do, since being at ease completes the salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Shaqeeq reports that he once enquired from Hadhrat Aa'isha about the optional salaahs that Rasulullaah ﷺ performed. She replied, "Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha lists the optional salaahs the Prophet performed: four rakaahs before Zuhr at home, two after Zuhr, Maghrib and Isha, nine at night including Witr, and two before Fajr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah iSli.did not attach as much importance to any optional salaahs as much as he attached to the two Rakaahs of Fajr."
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet gave no optional salaah more importance than the two Rakaahs of Fajr.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) states, "I have not seen Rasulullaah ﷺ so eager to do any good deed as much as he was to perform the two Rakaahs before Fajr.…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet never omitted the Fajr and Zuhr sunnahs, and Bilaal reports that the Prophet came out late for Fajr because he was finishing the two Fajr Rakaahs and would not leave them even when the sky was bright.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) also mentioned that Rasulullaah ﷺ would never omit the four Rakaahs before Zuhr salaah and the two Rakaahs before Fajr. Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) reports…
narrations.summary: Bilaal reports that the Prophet came out late for Fajr because he was praying his two sunnah rakaahs, which he would perform properly even if the sky were brighter.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaaboos reports that his father once sent someone to ask Hadhrat Aa'isha which salaah (apart from the Faraa'idh) Rasulullaah ﷺ most loved to perform with…
narrations.summary: Qaaboos reports Aa'isha's answer that the optional salaah the Prophet kept most consistently was the four Rakaahs before Zuhr, and Abdullaah bin Saa'ib and Ali each report the Prophet's sunnah salaahs around Zuhr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to perform four Rakaahs before (the Fardh of) Zuhr and two Rakaahs after.
narrations.summary: Ali reports that the Prophet prayed four rakaahs before Zuhr and two after it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that if Rasulullaah ﷺ was unable to perform the four Rakaahs before (the Fardh of) Zuhr, he would perform them afterwards.' ' Hadhrat Abu…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says that if the Prophet could not pray the four Rakaahs before Zuhr he would make them up afterwards, and Abu Ayyoob reports the Prophet's regular practice of the four before Zuhr and his reason for it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Before the Asr salaah Rasulullaah ﷺ would perform four Rakaahs salaah, separating them with Salaam to the high-ranking angels and the Muslims and…
narrations.summary: Ali says the Prophet prayed four Rakaahs before Asr, giving salaam between each pair to the angels and the believers.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Ali (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ performed two Rakaahs before Asr.
narrations.summary: Ali reports, in another narration, that the Prophet prayed two Rakaahs before Asr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that after the Maghrib salaah Rasulullaah ﷺ used to perform two Rakaahs salaah in which he prolonged the recitation of the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that the Prophet prayed two Rakaahs after Maghrib, reciting for so long that the people in the masjid had dispersed by the time he finished.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said about the two Rakaahs before Fajr, "They are more beloved to me than red camels."
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports Umar saying that the two Rakaahs before Fajr are dearer to him than red camels.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abdullaah reports that he once went to Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab when the latter was performing salaah before Zuhr. "What salaah is this?"…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abdullaah reports finding Umar praying before Zuhr, and Umar says the prayer counts as part of the night prayer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Utba says, "I performed four Rakaahs salaah with Hadhrat Umar in his house before the Zuhr salaah."
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Utba says he prayed four Rakaahs with Umar in Umar's house before Zuhr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfa bin Usayd reports that he noticed Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib performing four long Rakaahs of salaah after the sun has crossed its meridian and asked…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfa bin Usayd reports seeing Ali pray four long Rakaahs after the sun passes its zenith, and Ali says he saw the Prophet pray the same salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Yazeed says, "Someone closest to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood informed me that after the sun had crossed its meridian, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Yazeed reports, from someone close to Ibn Mas'ood, that Ibn Mas'ood prayed four Rakaahs after noon reciting two long surahs, and then left for the masjid fully dressed when the adhaan was called.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aswad, Hadhrat Murra and Hadhrat Masrooq all narrate that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood said, "No salaah of the day equals the salaah of the night except for the…
narrations.summary: Aswad, Murra and Masrooq report Ibn Mas'ood saying that the four Rakaahs before Zuhr are the only daytime salaah equal to night prayer, because they have always been counted as equal to Tahajjud.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood is said, "No salaah of the day equals the salaah of the night except for the four Rakaahs before Zuhr because they have always been regarded…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says the four rakaahs before Zuhr are the only daytime salaah equal to night salaah, since they are regarded as on par with Tahajjud.

narrations.excerpt: It is reported that both Hadhrat Baraa (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar performed the four Rakaahs of Sunnah salaah. ' It is also narrated that whenever the sun passes…
narrations.summary: Baraa and Abdullaah bin Umar are both reported to have prayed the Sunnah Rakaahs, and Naafi reports that Ibn Umar prayed eight Rakaahs before Zuhr and four after, while another account gives twelve before Zuhr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) would perform eight Rakaahs salaah before the Zuhr salaah and then four Rakaahs afterwards.
narrations.summary: Naafi reports that Ibn Umar prayed eight rakaahs before Zuhr and four after it.

narrations.excerpt: and Isha Salaahs Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ emphatically advised me never to forsake three acts throughout my life. One of them is to perform four Rakaahs…
narrations.summary: Ali says the Prophet urged him never to give up the four Rakaahs before Asr, Abu Faakhtah reports Ali calling the time between Maghrib and Isha 'salaah of negligence', and Ibn Umar begins to say that whoever prays four Rakaahs after Maghrib is like someone fighting battle after battle.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Faakhtah narrates that when Hadhrat Ali (RA) once mentioned that the salaahs between the Maghrib and Isha salaahs are called Salaatul Chaflah ('salaah of…
narrations.summary: Ali called the salaahs between Maghrib and Isha 'Salaatul Chaflah' and warned people they had become negligent, and Ibn Umar said that whoever prays four rakaahs after Maghrib is like a fighter in battle after battle.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abul Qais narratesxthat Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "Never omit the Qiyaamul Layl because Rasulullaah ﷺ never left it out. Even when he was ill or…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abul Qais reports Aa'isha telling him never to leave the Qiyaamul Layl, because the Prophet never left it, even when he was ill or very tired and then prayed it sitting.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "Qiyaamul Layl became compulsory for us with the revelation of the verse: O you wrapped in a cloth! Stand up all night (in Tahajjud salaah)…
narrations.summary: Jaabir says Qiyaamul Layl first became compulsory for the Companions with the revelation of Surah Muzammil, so long that their feet swelled, until Allaah granted a concession.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Hishaam divorced his wife and then journeyed to Madinah to sell the property he had there. He intended to invest the money from the sale in horses and…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Hishaam, after taking his wife back, asks Ibn Abbaas and then Aa'isha about the Prophet's night prayer and Witr, and Aa'isha describes the Prophet's Witr of eleven and then nine Rakaahs and his habit of making up missed Qiyaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports, "When the beginning of Surah Muzammil was revealed, the Sahabah (RA) stood in salaah as long as they did during Ramadhaan. A…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that when the start of Surah Muzammil was revealed the Companions stood in prayer as long as they did in Ramadhaan, and a year passed between the first and last parts of the surah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) used to perform his Witr salaah at the beginning of the night and when he stood for (Tahajjud) salaah, he…
narrations.summary: Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that Abu Bakr prayed Witr at the start of the night and, when he rose for Tahajjud, prayed in units of two Rakaahs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam says, "Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) used to perform salaah for a long while at night and when half the night had passed, he would awaken his family for…
narrations.summary: Aslam reports that Umar prayed for a long time at night and, when half the night had passed, woke his family for prayer while reciting the verse that tells him to order his family to pray.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that when Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Abul Aas (RA) married one of Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s widows, he said, "By Allaah! I did not marry her simply for wealth…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that Uthmaan bin Abul Aas, who had married one of Umar's widows, asked her about Umar's night worship, and she described how Umar dipped his hand in water, made dhikr and dozed until it was time for Tahajjud.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) loved to perform salaah in the middle of the night.
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Umar loved to pray in the middle of the night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) used to perform salaah for a long while at night and then ask, "Naafi! Has the last portion of the night…
narrations.summary: Naafi reports that Ibn Umar prayed for a long time at night, repeatedly asking Naafi whether the last part of the night had come, and then sat making istighfaar and du'aa until dawn.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) would start performing salaah whenever he awoke during the night." Hadhrat Abu Ghaalib says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah…
narrations.summary: Muhammad reports that Ibn Umar began prayer whenever he woke in the night, and Abu Ghaalib reports Ibn Umar urging him to pray before dawn, saying that Surah Ikhlaas is equal to a third of the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Alqama bin Qais relates, "I once spent the night with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood. He got up during the early part of the night and started performing salaah.…
narrations.summary: Alqama bin Qais describes how Ibn Mas'ood prayed through the night, reciting steadily and finishing with Witr near dawn, and Taariq bin Shihaab reports Salmaan's advice to keep the five Fardh salaahs and to avoid haste in worship.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Haani (RA) whose name was Faakhtah and who was the daughter of Abu Taalib, reports that when Makkah was conquered, she went to see Rasulullaah ﷺ. When she…
narrations.summary: Ummu Haani reports that when Makkah was conquered the Prophet bathed and then prayed eight Rakaahs of Duhaa, and Aa'isha says he usually prayed four but sometimes more.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates, "I sav/ Rasulullaah ﷺ perform six Rakaahs of Salaatud Duhaa and I have never them thereafter."
narrations.summary: Anas reports seeing the Prophet pray six Rakaahs of Duhaa; the end of his sentence is garbled in the OCR.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrc.t H.aani SgH2i6!sgi states that when Rasulullaah ﷺ went to her house the dty Makkah was conquered, he performed six Rakaahs Salaatud Duh?2.…
narrations.summary: Ummu Haani states that the Prophet prayed six Rakaahs of Duhaa at her house when Makkah was conquered, and Abdullaah bin Abu Awfa says he prayed only two because the Prophet prayed two when he got news of a victory and when the head of Abu Jahal was brought to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) once said, "There is a verse of the Qur'aan that I used to recite without understanding what it referred to. The verse is: ...by evening…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says he came to understand the Qur'anic word 'Ishraaq' from Ummu Haani, who reported that the Prophet made wudhu and then prayed Duhaa, calling it the Ishraaq salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched an army, they returned very quickly with a large booty. Someone remarked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet saying that a person who makes wudhu well, goes to the masjid for Fajr and then prays Duhaa returns sooner and with more reward than a returning army with booty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa Abu Muhammad says that he saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) performing the Salaatud Duhaa in the Masjid.
narrations.summary: Ataa Abu Muhammad reports seeing Ali pray Duhaa in the masjid, Ikramah reports that Ibn Abbaas prayed Duhaa once every ten days, and Aa'isha bint Sa'd reports that her father Sa'd prayed eight Rakaahs of Duhaa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ikramah reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) would perform the Salaatud Duhaa once every ten days. The daughter of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA),…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas prayed Duha once every ten days, and Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas prayed eight rakaahs of Duha, as reported by his daughter.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that although Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) did not perform the Salaatud Duhaa, he performed Nawaafil salaahs between Zuhr and Asr together…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that Ibn Mas'ood did not pray Duhaa but prayed nawaafil between Zuhr and Asr alongside his long night worship.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) engaged himself in salaah between Zuhr and Asr.
narrations.summary: Naafi reports that Ibn Umar prayed nawaafil between Zuhr and Asr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) says, "I went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and performed the Maghrib salaah with him. Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ continued performing salaah until Isha.
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah says he prayed Maghrib with the Prophet, and after that the Prophet kept on praying until Isha.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ammaar bin Yaasir reports that he saw (his father) Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) perform six Rakaahs salaah after the Maghrib salaah. Hadhrat Ammaar…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Ammaar reports seeing his father Ammaar pray six Rakaahs after Maghrib, and Ammaar says the Prophet promised that whoever prays them will have all sins forgiven, even as many as the foam on the oceans.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Yazeed says, "There was a time when I would always find Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) engaged in salaah. The time was between Maghrib and…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Yazeed says he always found Ibn Mas'ood praying between Maghrib and Isha, and Ibn Mas'ood explains that it is a time of people's negligence of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aswad bin Yazeed reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "How excellent is the time of negligence i.e. the time between Maghrib and Isha."
narrations.summary: Aswad bin Yazeed reports that Ibn Mas'ood called the time between Maghrib and Isha an excellent time, the time of negligence.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Verily the angels surround the people who perform salaah between Maghrib and Isha, which is the Salaatul Awaabeen."
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas says that angels surround those who pray between Maghrib and Isha, which he calls Salaatul Awaabeen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla (RA) narrates that when someone married the widow of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha (RA) and asked her about some special deed that he…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla reports that the widow of Abdullaah bin Rawaaha said he prayed two Rakaahs whenever he left the house and whenever he came back into it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ encouraged standing in (Taraweeh) salaah during Ramadhaan without emphatically commanding it (so that it should not be…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet encouraged standing in Taraweeh during Ramadhaan without making it compulsory, promising forgiveness of past sins to whoever prays it in faith and hope of reward.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) also said, "After Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, matters remained the same during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah adds that the practice of Taraweeh stayed the same through the Khilaafah of Abu Bakr and the early part of Umar's Khilaafah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that it was during Ramadhaan that Rasulullaah ﷺ once saw some Sahabah (RA) performing salaah (in congregation) in the corner of the…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet saw Sahabah praying Taraweeh in congregation behind Ubay bin Ka'b in a corner of the Masjid, and approved of it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abdul Qaari says, "I entered the Masjid with Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab one night in Ramadhaan where we found people in various groups.…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan Al Qaari recounts how Umar gathered the people behind Ubay bin Ka'b for Taraweeh, calling it an excellent innovation while saying the latter part of the night is better for sleep.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naufal bin Iyaas Hudhali says, "In Ramadhaan during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA), we used to stand in various groups everywhere in the Masjid…
narrations.summary: Naufal bin Iyaas Hudhali reports that Umar disliked people choosing Taraweeh leaders for their voices, and within three days had Ubay bin Ka'b lead the people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq Hamdaani reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once entered the Masjid on the first night of Ramadhaan to find lanterns burning and the Book of Allaah being…
narrations.summary: Abu Is'haaq Hamdaani reports that Ali, on entering the Masjid on the first night of Ramadhaan and finding lanterns lit and the Qur'aan recited, prayed for Umar's grave to be illuminated.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) had all the people perform the (Taraweeh) salaah of Ramadhaan collectively, he gathered the men behind Hadhrat Ubay…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that when Umar had all the people pray Taraweeh together, he placed the men behind Ubay bin Ka'b and the women behind Sulaymaan bin Abu Hathma.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar bin Abdulaah Ansi reports that it was Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b and Hadhrat Tameem Daari (RA) who stood in the place of Rasulullaah to lead the men in Taraweeh…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Abdulaah Ansi reports that Ubay and Tameem Daari led the men and Sulaymaan led the women under Umar, and that under Uthmaan one Imaam led both, with the women leaving only after the men.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Arjafa says, "Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) used to instruct the people to perform the (Taraweeh) salaah of Ramadhaan and would appoint an Imaam for the men and…
narrations.summary: Arjafa says that Ali had Taraweeh performed with one Imaam for the men and another for the women, and that she was the Imaam of the women.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports, "Ubay bin Ka'b came to Rasulullaah ﷺ one night of Ramadhaan saying, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I have done something tonight (and wish to know if it…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that Ubay bin Ka'b led the women of his household in eight Rakaahs of Taraweeh and Witr, and the Prophet approved, so the practice is established as a Sunnah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ summoned Hadhrat Bilaal one morning and said, "O Bilaal! How did you beat me to Jannah? When I entered Jannah last…
narrations.summary: Buraydah reports that the Prophet asked Bilaal how he had reached Jannah before him, and Bilaal explained that he prays two Rakaahs after each sin and two Rakaahs of Tahiyyatul wudhu after each broken wudhu.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thumaamah bin Abdullaah narrates that during the summer months, the caretaker of Hadhrat Anas (RA)'s orchard came to him complaining about the drought. Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Thumaamah bin Abdullaah reports that in a drought Anas repeatedly prayed and made du'aa, sending the caretaker to look for clouds, until rain fell only on his own land.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) relates, "I was once suffering intense pain, so I went to Rasulullaah ﷺ. He_put-me where he was covered me with the end of his shawl and started…
narrations.summary: Ali relates that when he was in intense pain, the Prophet covered him with his shawl, prayed and made du'aa for him, and he was immediately cured.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that there was a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ called Hadhrat Abu Mu'liq (RA). He was a trader who traded both his own goods as well as those of…
narrations.summary: Anas narrates how Abu Mu'liq, threatened with death by a robber, prayed and made du'aa three times, and a rider with a spear, an angel from the fourth heaven, killed the robber.

narrations.excerpt: Rasulullaah ﷺ Welcomes Hadhrat Safwaan bin Assaal who had come to Seek Knowledge Hadhrat Safwaan bin Assaal Muraadi (RA) says, "I once came to Rasulullaah in the Masjid…
narrations.summary: Safwaan bin Assaal reports that the Prophet welcomed him as a seeker of knowledge, and the Prophet told Qabeesah bin Mukhaariq that certain du'aas recited after Fajr would protect him from blindness, leprosy and paralysis.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sakhbarah (RA) narrates that two men were passing by when Rasulullaah ﷺ was busy giving a talk. Rasulullaah ﷺ said to them, "Sit down because you two are upon…
narrations.summary: Sakhbarah reports that the Prophet told two men who were passing by that seeking knowledge atones for all of a person's past sins.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah Baahili (RA) says that someone once spoke to Rasulullaah ﷺ about two men, one being an Aalim and the other an ordinary worshipper. Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah reports the Prophet's words that the superiority of an Aalim over an ordinary worshipper is like his own superiority over the lowest of people, and that Allaah and all creation pray for the one who teaches good.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration does not mention the incident of the two men but continues to state that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "The superiority of an Aalim over an ordinary worshipper is…
narrations.summary: Another narration gives the Prophet's words on the Aalim's superiority with a verse on those closest to the Prophets, and then Kumayl bin Ziyaad reports Ali's speech on knowledge being better than wealth and on the scarcity of true bearers of knowledge.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir ig says that they were on the Suffa platform when Rasulullaah ﷺ came out of his room and said, "Which of you would like to every day to go to the…
narrations.summary: On the Suffa, the Prophet said that learning or teaching two verses of the Qur'aan in the masjid is better than two camels, and more verses are better than as many camels.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ there were two brothers, one of whom worked while the other was always with Rasulullaah to learn from him.…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that in the Prophet's time one of two brothers worked while the other stayed with the Prophet to learn. When the working brother complained about him, the Prophet said that he may be receiving his sustenance because of his brother.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Tufayl narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) used to say, "Indeed the people closest to the Ambiyaa are those who practise most on what they brought." He would then…
narrations.summary: Abu Tufayl reports Ali's saying that those closest to the prophets are those who act on what they brought, and he applies the verse about Ibraheem's followers to the Prophet's followers. Kumayl bin Ziyaad relates Ali's long discourse that knowledge is better than wealth, that scholars remain while the wealthy die, and that Ali longs to meet those few who can bear true knowledge.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) said, "Acquire (divine) knowledge because learning it is fear of Allaah, going out in search of it is Ibaadah, rehearsing it is Tasbeeh,…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal lists the rewards of acquiring, studying, rehearsing, discussing and teaching knowledge, and how knowledge guides people in the halaal and haraam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haaroon bin Rabaab narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood said, "Start your mornings as either an Aalim or one busy acquiring the knowledge of Deen but do…
narrations.summary: Haaroon bin Rabaab and Zaid report Ibn Mas'ood urging people to begin each morning as an Aalim or a student of Deen, to acquire knowledge before it is lost with the departure of its bearers, and to follow the traditions of the Sahabah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "Start your mornings as either an Aalim or one busy acquiring the knowledge of Deen but do not be…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood urges people to seek knowledge of the Deen before it is taken away, warns against hair-splitting, and tells them to follow the practice of the Sahabah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Ahwas narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "No person is born an Aalim. Knowledge is gained only through studies."
narrations.summary: Abul Ahwas narrates that Ibn Mas'ood said no person is born a scholar, and knowledge is gained only through study.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "Start your mornings as either an Aalim or one busy acquiring the knowledge of Deen but do not be something other than these…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says to begin each morning as an Aalim or student of Deen, and if that is not possible, at least to love the Ulema and never despise them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once said, "Either be an Aalim, a student acquiring the knowledge of Deen, one who loves such people or one who…
narrations.summary: Hasan narrates Abu Dardaa's warning to be a scholar, a student, a lover of them or a follower of them, and never the fifth kind, which Hasan explains to Humayd is the one who innovates Bid'ah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dahhaak narrates that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once addressed the people saying, "O people of Damascus! You people are our brothers in Deen, our neighbours in…
narrations.summary: Dahhaak reports Abu Dardaa's address to the people of Damascus, criticising neglect of learning and worldly building and hopes, and stating that teaching and learning bring equal reward.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hassaan reports that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) addressed the people of Damascus saying, "Are you people content to just filling yourselves with bread made of wheat…
narrations.summary: Hassaan reports Abu Dardaa rebuking the people of Damascus for neglecting remembrance of Allaah and for not seeking knowledge, and warning that earlier nations were destroyed by following their desires.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qurra narrates that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once said, "Acquire knowledge before it is taken away because its disappearance will be effected by the demise of the…
narrations.summary: Qurra reports Abu Dardaa saying to acquire knowledge before it is taken away, and Abdur Rahmaan bin Mas'ood Faraazi reports that going to the Masjid to learn or teach earns the reward of a Mujaahid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Abu Hudhayl narrates that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "A person is lacking in intelligence and good judgement if he thinks that spending mornings and…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abu Hudhayl reports Abu Dardaa saying that a person lacks intelligence if he thinks spending mornings and evenings in learning and teaching is not Jihaad.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rajaa bin Hayaat reports that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "Knowledge is derived from studies."
narrations.summary: Rajaa bin Hayaat reports Abu Dardaa saying that knowledge is derived from study.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) both said, "Learning even a single chapter of knowledge is more beloved to me than a thousand Rakaahs of Nafl…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr and Abu Hurayrah both say that learning one chapter of knowledge is more beloved to them than a thousand Nafl Rakaahs, and they narrate that the Prophet said whoever dies while studying the knowledge of Deen dies as a martyr.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that they stated, "Learning even a single chapter of knowledge is more beloved to me than a thousand Rakaahs of Nafl salaah, regardless of…
narrations.summary: Another narration has Abu Dharr and Abu Hurayrah saying that learning a chapter of knowledge is better than a thousand Nafl Rakaahs whether or not it is practised upon.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali Azdi reports that when he once asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas about Jihaad, the Sahabi replied by saying, "Should I not tell you about something that is…
narrations.summary: Ali Azdi reports that Ibn Abbaas said teaching the Qur'aan, Fiqh and the Sunnah in a Masjid is better than Jihaad.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Everything seeks forgiveness for the one who teaches people what is good, even the fish in the…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas says that everything, even the fish in the oceans, seeks forgiveness for the one who teaches people what is good.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zirr bin Hubaysh reports that when he went to Hadhrat Safwaan bin Assaal one morning, Hadhrat Safwaan (RA) asked, "What brings you here this morning, O Zirr?" "I…
narrations.summary: Zirr bin Hubaysh reports that Safwaan bin Assaal advised him to begin his mornings as an Aalim or student of Deen, and Safwaan also said the angels spread their wings for whoever leaves home seeking knowledge.

narrations.excerpt: When he was on his deathbed, Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) asked the people to see whether dawn had broken. When they reported that it had not yet come, he again sent…
narrations.summary: On his deathbed, Mu'aadh bin Jabal asks whether dawn has broken, seeks refuge from a morning that leads to Jahannam, welcomes death, and says he loved this world only for fasting thirst, hardship and sitting with the Ulema.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once said, "Had it not been for three things, 1 would have loved to be no longer in this world. When asked what the three things were, Hadhrat Abu…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says that three things would make him wish to leave this world: prostrating to his Creator through the day and night, enduring thirst while fasting, and sitting with people who choose their speech as carefully as fruit.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, I said to an Ansaari friend of mine, 'The Sahabah is are plenty in number. Come. Let us learn…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas recounts that after the Prophet's death he went to learn hadith from the Sahabah, waiting at their doors and asking them to let him come to them, despite the doubts of his Ansaari friend.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "When the various cities were being conquered (by the Muslims) and people started focussing their attention towards the things of…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas says that when the cities were being conquered and people turned to worldly affairs, he focused on learning from Umar, which is why most of his hadith come from Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to me. 'Are you not going to ask me for a share of the booty as your companions are asking me?' I replied,…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah recounts that when he asked the Prophet to teach him, the Prophet narrated to him and he never forgot anything afterwards; he then explains why he narrates more hadith than others, citing the Qur'aanic warning against concealing knowledge.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) once said, "People complain that Abu Hurayrah narrates too many Ahadeeth. I was a person who stuck with Rasulullaah ﷺ to have my belly filled…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah describes the hunger he endured while staying with the Prophet, and how Ja'far bin Abi Taalib would take him and others home and feed them everything he had.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "The example of the guidance and knowledge that Allaah has sent me with is like a drenching rain that…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa reports the Prophet's parable of the guidance and knowledge he was sent with as rain falling on different kinds of ground, showing the different ways people benefit from it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Every Nabi ﷺ that Allaah has sent before had close friends and companions who adopted his ways and…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood relays the Prophet's warning that after earlier Nabis came people who did not practise, and that whoever resists them by hand, tongue or heart is a Mu'min.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Knowledge is of three types; explicit verses of the Qur'aan, concrete Ahadeeth (with authenticity that is…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr relays the Prophet's saying that knowledge is of three kinds, the clear verses of the Qur'aan, authentic Ahadeeth and matching injunctions, and everything beyond these is extra.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Auf (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I have left with you two factors that you will never go astray as long as you hold fast to them. They are the…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Auf relays the Prophet's saying that he has left two things, the Book of Allaah and the Sunnah, and that holding fast to them keeps people from going astray.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once entered the Masjid where he found the people gathered around a man. "What is happening?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "O…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet called the learning of an Allaamah, a man who knows Arabic, poetry and the differences between Arab tribes, knowledge that does not benefit.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once said, "Knowledge is in three things; the talking book (the Qur'aan), the perpetual Sunnah and to say 'I do not know' (when one does…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says that knowledge rests on three things: the Qur'aan, the constant Sunnah, and saying 'I do not know' when one does not know.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Knowledge is really in the Book of Allaah and the Sunnah of Rasulullaah ﷺ. Based on personal opinion, if anyone says anything…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas insists that knowledge comes only from the Book and the Sunnah, and corrects his students, who had ruled from their own opinion on a man troubled by a fluid after urinating, saying that wudhu is enough for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Yahya bin Ja'dah (RA) narrates that when someone brought to Rasulullaah ﷺ a scripture written on the shoulder blade of an animal, Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked,…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Yahya bin Ja'dah reports that the Prophet rebuked a man who brought him a scripture written on an animal's shoulder blade, and that the verse saying the Qur'aan is sufficient was then revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Urfuta narrates that he was with Hadhrat Umar (RA) when a man from the Abdul Qais tribe was brought. The man lived in a place called Soos (where…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Urfuta says Umar beat a man from the Abd Qais who had copied the scripture of Daaniyaal and ordered it erased, and Umar recalls the Prophet's anger when he once brought him a scripture from the People of the Book; Jaabir reports a similar rebuke.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Thaabit (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "I was passing by a friend from the (Jewish) Banu Qurayzah…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Thaabit reports that Umar brought the Prophet some quotations from the Torah, the Prophet's face reddened with anger, and the Prophet said that even Moosa could not be followed instead of him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) Rebukes a man who told him That he Found a Scripture with wonderful Content Hadhrat Maymoon bin Mahraan narrates that a man came to Hadhrat Umar saying,…
narrations.summary: Maymoon bin Mahraan reports that Umar whipped a man who had brought a scripture found in Madaa'in that did not match the Qur'aan, and said earlier nations were destroyed by turning to the books of their scholars.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hurayth bin Zuhayr reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Never question the Ahlul Kitaab about anything because since they are misguided, they…
narrations.summary: Hurayth bin Zuhayr reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood told people never to question the People of the Book, since they are misguided and may give them truth to reject or falsehood to believe.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "If you have to ask them (the Ahlul Kitaab), then consider what they say. If it coincides with the teachings of Allaah's…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood and Abdullaah bin Abbaas each say that people should not ask the People of the Book, since they have Allaah's latest Book, which has not been altered.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) once said, "How can you people ask the Ahlul Kitaab about anything when you have with you the Book that Allaah has revealed to His Nabi…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas rebukes people for asking the Ahlul Kitaab, since the Qur'aan they have is unaltered and the Ahlul Kitaab altered their own scriptures for worldly gain.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, 'You ask the Ahlul Kitaab about their scriptures when you have Allaah's Book which is the latest of…
narrations.summary: A variant report has Abdullaah bin Abbaas asking why people question the People of the Book when they have Allaah's latest Book, which is new and which they can read.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shufay Asbahi narrates, "Upon entering Madinah one day, I saw many people gathered around a particular man. When I asked who the man was, I was informed that he…
narrations.summary: Shufay Asbahi reports Abu Hurayrah's hadith that the reciter of the Qur'aan, the martyr and the wealthy man will be the first fuel for Jahannam because they acted for show; Mu'aawiya wept on hearing it. The report also has Abdullaah bin Umar weeping after hearing from Abdullaah bin Amr a hadith about pride.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Salamah bin Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas met at Marwa, they…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar wept after hearing from Abdullaah bin Amr a hadith warning that anyone with pride the size of a mustard seed in his heart will be thrown headlong into the fire.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Hasan the freed slave of the Banu Naufal tribe reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha and Hadhrat Hassaan bin Thaabit (RA) ' (both acclaimed poets) came…
narrations.summary: Abul Hasan reports that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha and Hassaan bin Thaabit came weeping to the Prophet when Surah Shu'araa was revealed, and he told them that the exception for poets who believe applies to them. A separate report by Abu Saalih has the people of Yemen weeping at the Qur'aan in Abu Bakr's time.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abzah Abu Abdur Rahmaan (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once praised certain groups of the Muslims in his sermon. Thereafter, Rasulullaah said, "What is the…
narrations.summary: Abzah Abu Abdur Rahmaan reports the Prophet's sermon rebuking tribes who neither teach Deen to their neighbours nor learn it, and the Ash'ar people who asked for a year's grace to teach theirs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salamah narrates that a man came to (the bedside of) Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) and started to weep. "What makes you weep?" Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Salamah reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal told a weeping man at his bedside that whoever strives for knowledge and Imaan will be granted them, as Ibraheem was.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haarith bin Umayrah reports that when Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal was about to pass away, the people around him started to cry. "What makes you people cry?" he…
narrations.summary: Haarith bin Umayrah reports Mu'aadh bin Jabal's advice as he was dying: knowledge and Imaan remain until Qiyaamah, so seek them from Umar, Uthmaan, Ali and four men, and judge every claim by the Qur'aan and Sunnah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed bin Umayrah narrates, "During the illness that claimed his life, Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) would often fall unconscious and then regain consciousness.…
narrations.summary: Yazeed bin Umayrah reports Mu'aadh bin Jabal's advice as he was dying: take knowledge from four named men, beware the blunders of a wise man and the words of a hypocrite, and take sound knowledge from wherever it comes.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Maymoon narrates, "We were in Yemen when Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal came there and addressed us saying, 'O people of Yemen! Accept Islaam and live in…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Maymoon reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal, who had come to Yemen as the Prophet's envoy, consoled him when he wept at Mu'aadh's death by saying that knowledge and Imaan will remain until Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "During the greater portion of my life I have seen that a man (from the Sahabah (RA)) learns Imaan before the Qur'aan. Whenever a…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says that in the Prophet's time people learnt Imaan before the Qur'aan and then knew its commands; now people read the Qur'aan without knowing what it commands. Jundub bin Abdullaah says that learning Imaan first with the Prophet made their Imaan grow when they learnt the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "Whenever a Surah, a verse or a few verses were revealed during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, it would serve to strengthen the Imaan and…
narrations.summary: Ali says each revelation in the Prophet's time strengthened the Mu'mineen's Imaan and that they abstained at once from any prohibition. Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami says the Sahabah did not go on to the next ten verses until they had learnt to practise the ones before.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that the Sahabi also said, "We used to learn the Qur'aan as well as how to practise on it. There shall however come people who will inherit the…
narrations.summary: An unnamed Sahabi says the companions learnt the Qur'aan together with how to act on it. Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says they learnt ten verses from the Prophet before going on to the next ten, and Shareek confirms that this meant acting on them first.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Whenever we learnt ten verses of the Qur'aan from Rasulullaah ﷺ, we would not proceed to learn the next ten verses until we had…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood said they would not learn the next ten verses of the Qur'aan until they had put the first ten into practice; asked whether this meant practising first, Shareek confirmed it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hafs bin Umar Sa'di narrates from his uncle that Hadhrat Salmaan once said to Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA), "O member of the Banu Abs! While knowledge is abundant, life…
narrations.summary: Hafs bin Umar Sa'di reports that Salmaan told Hudhayfah to learn only the Deen he needs, since knowledge is abundant and life short. Abul Bakhtari relates Salmaan's lesson with the sip of water from the Tigris: knowledge never decreases.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Qayla reports that when a man wrote to ask Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar about knowledge, the Sahabi wrote back saying, "You have written to me asking about…
narrations.summary: Abu Qayla reports that when he asked Abdullaah bin Umar about knowledge, Ibn Umar replied in a letter that the most important thing is to meet Allaah with a tongue that did not dishonour a Muslim, with no Muslim's blood or wealth on one's hands, and united with the Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Rifaa'ah (RA) narrates, "I came to Rasulullaah ﷺ at a time when he was busy delivering a sermon. 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I said, 'A stranger has come to enquire…
narrations.summary: Abu Rifaa'ah reports that he interrupted the Prophet during a sermon to say a stranger had come to learn his Deen, and the Prophet came down from the pulpit and sat to teach him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jareer (RA) reports that a Bedouin once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "Teach me Islaam." Rasulullaah ﷺ explained, "(Islaam is) That you testify that there is none…
narrations.summary: Jareer reports that a Bedouin asked the Prophet to teach him Islaam, and the Prophet listed the Shahaadah, salaah, zakaah, Ramadhaan, Hajj and loving for others what one loves for oneself. Muhammad bin Umaarah then says Farwah bin Musayk gave up Kindah's royalty to join the Prophet and learnt the Qur'aan and Shari'ah from Sa'd bin Ubaadah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dubaa'ah bint Zubayr bin Abdul Muttalib reports that a delegation from Bahraa in Yemen once came to Madinah. They were thirteen men and when they arrived, they…
narrations.summary: Dubaa'ah bint Zubayr reports that a delegation of thirteen men from Bahraa came to Madinah, was hosted by Miqdaad bin Amr, accepted Islaam before the Prophet, learnt the Faraa'idh, and left with gifts after farewell.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Seereen reports that when teaching Islaam to the people, Hadhrat Abu Bakr and Hadhrat Umar (RA) would say, "Worship Allaah without ascribing any partners to…
narrations.summary: Ibn Seereen reports that Abu Bakr and Umar, when teaching Islaam, told people to worship Allaah alone, keep salaah on time, pay zakaah cheerfully, fast in Ramadhaan and obey their leaders.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that a Bedouin once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Teach me the Deen." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "(The Deen of Islaam is) To…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that a Bedouin asked Umar to teach him the Deen, and Umar listed the Shahaadah, salaah, zakaah, Hajj and fasting, and told him to judge only outward actions and not to probe people's private lives.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) added, "O servant of Allaah! Hold fast to this and when you meet Allaah, then tell Him whatever comes to mind."
narrations.summary: Another narration adds that Umar told the same Bedouin to hold fast to this advice, and that when he meets Allaah he may tell Him whatever comes to mind.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that a man approached Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! I am a man from the countryside and have many duties to tend to. Do advise me…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that a countryman asked Umar for a sure path to Jannah, and Umar advised him to worship Allaah alone, keep salaah, zakaah, Hajj, Umrah and obedience, and not to probe people's private lives; the man said he would tell his Rabb that Umar had instructed him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Maalik Ashja'ee reports from his father that salaah was the first thing Rasulullaah ﷺ taught anyone who accepted Islaam.
narrations.summary: Abu Maalik Ashja'ee reports from his father that the Prophet taught salaah first to anyone who accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hakam bin Umayr (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ taught them thus: "When you stand up for salaah, say 'Allaahu Akbar' and raise your hands without passing your…
narrations.summary: Hakam bin Umayr reports that the Prophet taught them that on standing for salaah they should say Allaahu Akbar, raise their hands without passing the ears, and recite the opening words of praise.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar is says, "Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) used to teach us the Tashahhud from the pulpit just as little children are taught at school."
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Abu Bakr used to teach the Tashahhud to the people from the pulpit, as children are taught at school.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says(5), "Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab once took hold of my hand and taught me the Tashahhud, informing me that Rasulullaah ﷺ has also…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Umar bin Khattaab took his hand and taught him the Tashahhud, which Umar had himself been taught by the Prophet; a second report from Abdur Rahmaan al-Qaari of Umar teaching it from the pulpit follows, and the text is cut off.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to teach us the Tashahhud just as he taught us a Surah of the Qur'aan."
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says the Prophet taught them the Tashahhud just as he taught them a Surah of the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Rasulullaah Wife taught me the Tashahhud with my hand in his just as he would teach me a Surah of the Qur'aan." The narration…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says the Prophet taught him the Tashahhud with his hand in the Prophet's hand, as he taught him a Surah. Aswad reports that Ibn Mas'ood taught them the Tashahhud the same way and corrected their small mistakes.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab reports that when Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) once entered the Masjid, he noticed a man who was performing salaah without carrying properly. When the…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Wahab reports that Hudhayfah saw a man pray for forty years without carrying out the salaah properly and told him he had not prayed at all, then taught him to perform ruku and sajdah correctly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to him, "Should I give you five thousand goats or teach you five phrases that contain the welfare of…
narrations.summary: Ali bin Abi Taalib reports that the Prophet offered him five phrases for his Deen and worldly life rather than five thousand goats, and taught him to ask for forgiveness, good character, lawful earnings, contentment and no craving for what is not decreed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) used to teach his daughters certain words (of du'aa) and instructed them to always recite them. He mentioned that it was Hadhrat Ali…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ja'far reports that Ali taught him words the Prophet used to recite in difficulty, and that Ali promised entry to Jannah for whoever recites them at death, with the Tasbeeh repeated three times each; the text breaks off in the middle of the list.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Junaadah (RA) says, "I was one of the first persons from the people of Taa'if to meet Rasulullaah ﷺ (to accept Islaam). I left early in the morning from…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Junaadah relates how he came from Taa'if to accept Islaam in Makkah and how the Prophet then taught him the words called the Baaqiyaatus Saalihaat.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ taught them to recite the following du'aa every morning: Ia "We begin the morning on the natural way of Islaam, the…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b relates the morning and evening du'aa the Prophet taught the Companions, affirming the natural way of Islaam and the creed of Ibraheem.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ taught them the following du'aa just as a teacher would teach children to write: "O Allaah! I beseech You to protect me from…
narrations.summary: Sa'd and Naufal each report a du'aa the Prophet taught: one for protection from harm and one for a person who has passed away.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salaamah Kindi narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) taught the people to send salutations to Rasulullaah ﷺ with the following words: Jptlu OJJ olvj Ji li "O Allaah The…
narrations.summary: Salaamah Kindi reports that Ali taught people a salutation to send to the Prophet, asking Allaah to bless Muhammad, the seal of the prophets, with the best of mercies, the highest house and the most complete light, and to accept his testimony.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shihaab bin Abbaad reports that he heard a Sahabi who had been part of the Abdul Qais delegation say, "When we came to Rasulullaah ﷺ, the Muslims were extremely…
narrations.summary: The Abdul Qais delegation arrives, and the Prophet welcomes their leader Mundhir bin Aa'idh (Ashaj), seats him beside himself and questions the delegation on what they have learnt.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports, "We were sitting with Rasulullaah when he said, 'A delegation from the Abdul Qais have come.' We could see no one, but after a…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri relates how the Abdul Qais delegation came, was hosted and taught, and afterwards asked the Prophet about their local drinks.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that after living in Madinah for nine years, Rasuluilaah WtO/Hi did not perform Hajj until the announcement was made one day that Rasuluilaah…
narrations.summary: Jaabir relates the Prophet's journey for the Farewell Hajj, including the ihram instructions given to Asmaa bint Umays when her son was born at Dhul Hulayfah, and the talbiya recited on the road.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Azraq Ghaadiri (RA) says, "I was riding my animal and carrying my provisions when I came to Rasulullaah ﷺ. I rode with him until we reached a waypoint.…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Azraq Ghaadiri recounts travelling from the far ends of Yemen to hear the Prophet at Mina, and the author then quotes Ibn Jareer's commentary on the verse about gaining understanding of Deen through jihaad.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) says, "When we marched to battles, we would leave behind one or two men to listen to Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ and when we returned from…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri says that the Sahabah left one or two men behind on campaigns to learn Hadith, who then reported the Prophet's words to the others on their return.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thaabit Bunaani reports that Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) mentioned seventy men from the Ansaar who would go to a specific place in Madinah as soon as night fell.…
narrations.summary: Thaabit Bunaani reports Anas bin Maalik describing the Ansaar who learnt and taught the Qur'aan at night, and the martyrdom of Anas's uncle Haraam bin Milhaan and of the Qurra sent by the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "I had an Ansaari neighbour from the upper reaches of Madinah who belonged to the Banu Umayyah bin…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates Umar's account of taking turns with an Ansaari neighbour to attend the Prophet's gatherings, and of his alarm when the neighbour brought word that the Prophet had divorced his wives, which proved untrue.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa (RA) says,"Allofus(Sahabah (RA)) were unable to (exclusively devote all our time to) listen to Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ because we had properties and…
narrations.summary: Baraa says the Sahabah could not all sit to hear Hadith because of their property and work, so those who were present passed it on to those who were absent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa (RA) also said, "We did not hear every Hadith directly from Rasulullaah ﷺ but our companions would narrate them to us when we were (unable to be with…
narrations.summary: Baraa adds that the Sahabah who were out grazing camels heard the Hadith from companions who had been with the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Anas Maalik bin Abu Aamir Asbahi says that he was with Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydullaah when a man came to him saying, "O Abu Muhammad! By Allaah! We do not know…
narrations.summary: Abu Anas Maalik bin Abu Aamir Asbahi relates that Talha bin Ubaydullaah defended Abu Hurayrah against a man who doubted his many Hadith, explaining that Abu Hurayrah had always been with the Prophet while the others had homes and families.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "None may trade in our marketplace unless he had developed an understanding of Deen (enabling him to trade in a manner that complies with the…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Khattaab rules that no one may trade in the marketplace without first understanding the Deen that governs trade.

narrations.excerpt: Allaah says in the Qur'aan.- ". . . Save yourselves and your families from the Fire ..." (Surah Tahreem, verse 6) In his commentary of the above verse, Hadhrat Ali (RA)…
narrations.summary: Ali bin Abi Taalib explains the verse 'Save yourselves and your families from the Fire' as meaning to educate yourselves and your families in all that is good.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes Hadhrat Ali (RA)'s interpretation as, "Teach them (your families) and educate them in good etiquette (manners)."
narrations.summary: Another narration gives Ali's explanation of the same verse as teaching one's family good manners.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maalik bin Huwayrith (RA) reports, "We were a few youngsters of similar ages when we came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and stayed with him for twenty days. When Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Maalik bin Huwayrith relates that after twenty days with the Prophet he and his companions were sent home to teach their families and to pray as they had seen the Prophet pray.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ just arrived in Madinah and I was brought before him, the people said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ This boy from the Banu…
