narrations.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit relates that the Prophet asked him to learn the Jewish language, or in other reports the Syriac or Hebrew, so that he could read and write the letters for him, and that he mastered it within about half a month or seventeen days depending on the report.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Zaid (RA) says, "Rasulullaah (assfe once asked me, 'Do you know the Syriac language well because letters written in that language come to…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit says the Prophet asked him to learn the Syriac (or Hebrew) language because letters were coming to him, and he learnt it in seventeen days.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar bin Qais says, "Although Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) had a hundred slaves, all of whom spoke a different language, he was capable of speaking to each…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Qais describes how Abdullaah bin Zubayr spoke to each of his hundred slaves in their own language, and balanced worldly affairs with remembrance of the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Study as much astronomy as will assist you to navigate over land and sea during the darkness. Thereafter you should stop."
narrations.summary: Umar tells people to study astronomy only as far as it helps them navigate by land and sea in the dark, and then to stop.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Study as much astronomy as will assist you in navigation and study as much genealogy as will assist you in…
narrations.summary: Another report has Umar telling people to study astronomy as far as it aids navigation and genealogy as far as it helps them keep family ties.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'sa'a bin Sowhaan narrates that a Bedouin once came to Hadhrat Ali and asked, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! How do you recite the ii) ('Only those who take steps shall…
narrations.summary: Sa'sa'a bin Sowhaan relates that after a Bedouin challenged Ali's reading of a verse, Ali recited it correctly and had Abul Aswad Duwali add the vowel marks to the Qur'aan for the many non-Arabs entering Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ left for Hunayn, he appointed Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) over the people of Makkah with instructions to teach the…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that when the Prophet left for Hunayn and later for Madinah, he appointed Mu'aadh bin Jabal over Makkah to teach the Qur'aan and develop understanding of Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaahid narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal over the people of Makkah when he left for Hunayn so that he should create an…
narrations.summary: Mujaahid reports that the Prophet appointed Mu'aadh bin Jabal over Makkah when he left for Hunayn, to teach the Qur'aan and develop understanding of Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaasim narrates that whenever Hadhrat Umar (RA) left on a journey, he would leave Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) as his deputy in Madinah. Whereas Hadhrat Umar…
narrations.summary: Qaasim relates that Umar kept Zaid bin Thaabit in Madinah as his deputy and sent him out only for vital tasks, because the people of Madinah needed him, not because Umar thought less of him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalim bin Abdullaah says, "We were with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar the day Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) passed away. 'A great Aalim has passed away today,' I…
narrations.summary: Saalim bin Abdullaah relates that when Zaid bin Thaabit died, Abdullaah bin Umar called him a great scholar who gave rulings in Madinah while Umar sent others to the cities and forbade them to judge by their own opinion.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami reports that he used to recite the Qur'aan to Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA). However, Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) once told, him, "If you continue to do…
narrations.summary: Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami relates that Uthmaan told him to recite the Qur'aan to Zaid bin Thaabit, and Ka'b bin Maalik reports Umar's regret that Mu'aadh bin Jabal left for Shaam after Abu Bakr refused to keep him in Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aasim bin Umar bin Qataadah' narrates that delegates from the Udhal and Qaara tribes, both branches of the Jadeelah clan, came to Rasulullaah ﷺ after the Battle…
narrations.summary: Aasim bin Umar bin Qataadah relates that after Uhud delegates from the Udhal and Qaara asked for teachers, and the Prophet sent six Sahabah under Marthad bin Abu Marthad.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates, "Some people from Yemen once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, 'Please send to us someone who will help us develop an understanding of the Deen,…
narrations.summary: Ali relates that the Prophet sent him to Yemen to teach and judge between people, and that the Prophet's prayer for his heart to be guided and his tongue steadied kept his judgements sound.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that some people from Yemen once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ with the request, "Do send with us someone who will teach us the Qur'aan."…
narrations.summary: Anas relates that when people from Yemen asked for a teacher of the Qur'aan, the Prophet sent Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah with them, calling him the most trustworthy person of this Ummah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that the people of Yemen requested Rasulullaah ﷺ for someone who would teach them the Sunnah and Islaam.'
narrations.summary: Another narration says that the people of Yemen asked the Prophet for someone to teach them the Sunnah, but the text breaks off there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazam said, "Here with us is the letter (of appointment) that Rasulullaah ﷺ had written for Hadhrat Amr bin Hazam when…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm quotes the letter the Prophet gave Amr bin Hazam on being sent to Yemen to teach, collect zakaah and urge taqwa, and Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports being sent there with Mu'aadh bin Jabal to teach the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) relates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent me to a clan belonging to the Qais tribe to teach them the Shari'ah of Islaam. However, I found them to…
narrations.summary: Ammaar bin Yaasir relates that he was sent to teach a Qais clan and found them indifferent, and the Prophet said there are people even stranger, who know what these ignorant people do not and are just as indifferent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haaritha bin Mudarrib narrates that he read the letter Hadhrat Umar wrote to the people of Kufa. The letter read: "I have sent Ammaar as your governor and…
narrations.summary: Haaritha bin Mudarrib reads Umar's letter to the people of Kufa, appointing Ammaar bin Yaasir as governor and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood as teacher and advisor, and praising them as among the choicest Companions.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Aswad Duwali says, "When I arrived in Basrah, Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn Abu Nujayd was there. Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) had sent him there to create an…
narrations.summary: Abul Aswad Duwali relates that when he reached Basrah he found Imraan bin Husayn there, sent by Umar to teach Deen to the people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi (RA) reports that only five persons (from amongst the Ansaar) had memorised the entire Qur'aan during the lifetime of Rasulullaah ﷺ.…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi relates that Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan asked Umar for teachers for Shaam, and Umar sent Mu'aadh bin Jabal, Ubaadah bin Saamit and Abu Dardaa to Hims, Damascus and Palestine.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Muhammad bin Aqeel reports that he once heard Hadhrat Jaabir say, "The news once reached me that there was a man who had heard a particular Hadith…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Muhammad bin Aqeel reports that Jaabir rode for a month to Shaam to hear from Abdullaah bin Unays a Hadith of the Prophet on retribution on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says,"IusedtohearaHadithfrom Rasulullaah ﷺ concerning retribution which was being narrated by someone in Egypt. I therefore purchased a camel and…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah relates travelling to Egypt to hear from Maslamah bin Mukhallad the Prophet's Hadith on concealing a Mu'min's faults, and Muneeb reports a similar journey by another Sahabi to hear the same Hadith.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Jurayj narrates that Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA) travelled all the way to Egypt to see Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir (RA). When he arrived there, he said, "I…
narrations.summary: Ibn Jurayj relates that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari travelled to Egypt to hear from Uqba bin Aamir the Prophet's saying on concealing a Muslim's faults, and then narrated it in Madinah before dismounting.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Makhool narrates that when Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir (RA) went to see Hadhrat Maslama bin Mukhallad (RA), an argument ensued between the usher and Hadhrat Uqba (RA).…
narrations.summary: Makhool relates that Uqba bin Aamir went to Maslamah bin Mukhallad to confirm the Prophet's saying that whoever conceals a brother's sin will have his own sin concealed on the Day of Qiyaamah; Abdullaah bin Buraydah adds a one-line report of a Sahabi travelling to Egypt to see Fudhala bin Ubayd about a Hadith.

narrations.excerpt: Another similar narration adds the Sahabi came to Hadhrat Fudhala at a time when he was feeding his camel. When Hadhrat Fudhala (RA) welcomed the Sahabi, he said, "I have…
narrations.summary: Fudhaala bin Ubayd welcomes a visiting Companion who has come to ask whether he still remembers a Hadith they both heard from the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaydullaah bin Adi (RA) says, "When I heard that Hadhrat Ali (RA) knew a particular Hadith, I feared that if he passed away, I would be unable to hear it from…
narrations.summary: Ubaydullaah bin Adi travels to Iraq to hear a Hadith from Ali, who narrates it but asks him to keep it private; Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says he would travel to anyone with more knowledge of the Book.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Ubaydullaah bin Adi (RA) said, "When I asked Hadhrat Ali (RA) about the Hadith, he narrated it to me but then made me promise that I…
narrations.summary: Ubaydullaah bin Adi says he asked Ali about a hadith and Ali related it on condition that he tell no one else; Ibn Mas'ood's saying about travelling far for knowledge of the Book is introduced.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "If a camel could take me to a person who has more knowledge of what has been revealed to Muhammad ﷺ than I have, I shall…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that if a camel could carry him to someone with more knowledge of what was revealed to Muhammad ﷺ than he has, he would go to them to increase his own knowledge.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Tha'laba (RA) says, "I once went to Rasulullaah ﷺ with the request to refer me to someone who could teach well. Rasulullaah ﷺ then referred to Hadhrat Abu…
narrations.summary: Abu Tha'laba asks the Prophet for a good teacher; the Prophet refers him to Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah and praises him, and a Hadith about Khilaafah following Nubuwwat is begun.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Tha'laba (RA) added, "When I came to Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA), he was busy talking with Hadhrat Basheer bin Sa'd Abu…
narrations.summary: Abu Tha'laba says he went to Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah, who was talking with Basheer bin Sa'd, and Abu Ubaydah then related the Prophet's words that after prophethood would come a khilaafah on its pattern, followed by monarchy and tyranny.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates, "I once asked Rasulullaah ﷺ when the time will come when people will stop enjoining good and forbidding evil. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'When…
narrations.summary: Anas asks the Prophet when people will stop enjoining good and forbidding evil, and the Prophet lists signs of the end including knowledge of Deen carried by the wretched.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umayyah Jumhi (RA) reports that when they once asked Rasulullaah ﷺ about the signs of Qiyaamah, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Amongst the signs of Qiyaamah is that…
narrations.summary: Abu Umayyah Jumhi reports that when the Companions asked the Prophet about the signs of Qiyaamah, he said knowledge would be sought from juniors.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ukaym narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to say, "Remember that the most truthful words are those of Allaah, the best way of life is that of…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ukaym reports Umar's saying that the truest words are Allaah's, the best way is that of Muhammad, the worst matters are fabrications in Deen, and people stay well only while they take knowledge from their seniors.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Bilaal bin Yahya reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "I know exactly when people will remain righteous and when they will start to degenerate. When the knowledge…
narrations.summary: Bilaal bin Yahya reports Umar's saying that people stay righteous while their knowledge comes from seniors, and degenerate when it comes from juniors.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "People will always remain righteous and steadfast as long as their knowledge of Deen comes to them from the Sahabah (RA) of…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says people stay steadfast while they take their knowledge of Deen from the Sahabah and their seniors, and are destroyed once it comes from juniors.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "People will always remain in good stead as long as they acquire their knowledge of Deen from their seniors. However, as soon…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says people do well while they take knowledge of Deen from their seniors, and that taking it from juniors and sinners will destroy them.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes Hadhrat (RA) bin Mas'ood (RA) as saying, "You people will remain in good stead as long as the knowledge of Deen remains in the custody of your…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says people are well guided while knowledge stays with their seniors, and that once it passes to juniors they will regard the seniors as fools.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) said, "Verily the most effective tool for leading people astray is a man who recites the Qur'aan without understanding it and then proceeds to…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya warns that the most effective way to mislead people is a man who recites the Qur'aan without understanding it and teaches it to children, slaves and women, who then argue with the scholars.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) said, "I do not fear for this Ummah a Mu'min whose Imaan restrains him nor a sinner whose sinful life is manifest. However, what I do fear…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Khattaab says he does not fear for the Ummah a believer restrained by Imaan or an open sinner, but fears a man who learns the Qur'aan and interprets it in a way it should not be interpreted.

narrations.excerpt: When Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir (RA) was on his deathbed, he advised his sons saying, "Dear sons! I forbid you from three things, so take note of what they are. Never accept…
narrations.summary: On his deathbed Uqba bin Aamir tells his sons to accept Ahadeeth only from reliable people, not to borrow, and not to write poetry, which distracts the heart from the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that it was at Jaabiya that Hadhrat Umar delivered a sermon to the people saying, "Whoever has any queries about the Qur'aan should…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports Umar's sermon at Jaabiya directing people with Qur'aan questions to Ubay bin Ka'b, inheritance questions to Zaid bin Thaabit, Fiqh questions to Mu'aadh bin Jabal, and sending those who need money to Umar.

narrations.excerpt: The narration has passed at the beginning of the chapter in which Hadhrat Safwaan bin Assaal Muraadi says, "I once came to Rasulullaah dcii in the Masjid as he was…
narrations.summary: Safwaan bin Assaal says he came to the Prophet in the Masjid to seek knowledge, and the Prophet welcomed him as a seeker of knowledge, describing how angels encircle him with their wings.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Haaroon narrates that whenever they went to Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri, he would say, "Welcome to the people about whom Rasulullaah gave us emphatic…
narrations.summary: Abu Haaroon reports that whenever they visited Abu Sa'eed Khudri he welcomed them, quoting the Prophet's emphatic instruction to treat well the people who come to learn Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) quoted Rasulullaah ﷺ as saying, "People will come from the East to learn from you. It is my emphatic…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri quotes the Prophet that people will come from the East to learn and must be treated well; Abu Haaroon reports Abu Sa'eed's welcome to them.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that part of Rasulullaah ﷺ's instruction was, "Teach them that which Allaah has taught you." Yet another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said,…
narrations.summary: Several variant narrations record the Prophet's instruction to welcome, teach and accommodate students who come from far away, and Abu Sa'eed's own welcome and offer to explain whatever they do not understand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ismaa'eel reports that so many of them once went to visit Hadhrat Hasan that they filled his house. Pulling his legs together, he said, "So many of us once went…
narrations.summary: Hasan relates Abu Hurayrah's account of a large visit by students and the Prophet's instruction to welcome, greet and teach future seekers of knowledge, followed by a complaint about later teachers who were harsh to students.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Dardaa (RA) says, "Whenever Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) narrated Ahadeeth to people, he would always smile. 1 once said to him, 'I fear that people would regard…
narrations.summary: Ummu Dardaa says Abu Dardaa always smiled when narrating Ahadeeth, and he explained that the Prophet also smiled when he narrated.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Which of our companions are best?" Rasulullaah replied, "The person who…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that when the Prophet was asked which companions are best, he described one who reminds you of Allaah, whose speech adds to your knowledge, and whose deeds remind you of the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qurra (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ sat in a gathering, the Sahabah (RA) would sit in groups around him (to learn and teach, asking Rasulullaah gfgi when…
narrations.summary: Qurra reports that when the Prophet sat in a gathering, the Companions sat in circles around him to learn and to ask him when they needed to.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed • Raqaashi says that after narrating Ahadeeth to them, Hadhrat Anas would say, "By Allaah! This Hadith has not been learnt as you people learn when people…
narrations.summary: Yazeed Raqaashi reports that Anas, after narrating Ahadeeth, said the Companions used to sit in groups after Fajr to recite the Qur'aan and learn the compulsory and optional parts of Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) relates, "I was sitting with a group of Muhaajireen amongst whom were people who (because of poverty) had so little clothing that they were…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri recounts sitting with poor Muhaajireen when the Prophet came and promised them perfect light on the Day of Qiyaamah and entry into Jannah half a day, five hundred years, before the rich.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaari bin Amr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by two gatherings in his Masjid. While the people in one gathering were making du'aa to Allaah and…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that the Prophet passed two gatherings in the Masjid, one making du'aa and one learning and teaching Fiqh, and that he sat with the learning group, saying he had been sent as a teacher.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Abu Moosa narrates that Hadhrat Abu Moosa (RA) once went to Hadhrat Umar (RA) after Isha. "What bringsyou here?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. "I have…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr bin Abu Moosa reports that Abu Moosa went to Umar after Isha to discuss a matter of Fiqh, and that Umar, who had been occupied in salaah when he arrived, sat up and talked with him at length.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jundub bin Abdullaah Bajali says, "When I arrived in Madinah to seek knowledge, I entered the Masjid of kasulullaah where I saw people engaged in discussions in…
narrations.summary: Jundub bin Abdullaah Bajali travels to Madinah to seek knowledge and is put off by Ubay bin Ka'b's remark about Iraqis; Ubay apologises and promises to relate what he heard from the Prophet, and dies before Friday. Abu Moosa Ash'ari sighs when told of it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hilaal bin Yasaaf says, "When I arrived in Basrah and entered the Masjid, I saw an old man with white hair and a white beard leaning against a pillar and…
narrations.summary: Hilaal bin Yasaaf says that on arriving in Basrah he saw Imraan bin Husayn narrating Ahadeeth to a group in the Masjid, and asked who he was.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Saalih says, "I have seen such a large gathering around Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas that if the entire tribe of the Quraysh boasted about such numbers, they…
narrations.summary: Abu Saalih describes the crowds at Abdullaah bin Abbaas's door and how Ibn Abbaas taught each group in turn about the Qur'aan and its Tafseer, Halaal and Haraam and Fiqh, inheritance, and Arabic poetry and rare words.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "The best of all gatherings is the one in which matters of wisdom are discussed." Another narration states that Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood praises gatherings where wisdom is discussed, and says that people of Taqwa are the chiefs and that attending the gatherings of the jurists increases Imaan and knowledge.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Juhayfah (RA) always used to say, "Sit in the company of the seniors, associate with the Ulema and mingle with the wise." ® Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "It…
narrations.summary: Abu Juhayfah tells people to sit with their seniors, associate with the Ulema and mingle with the wise, and Abu Dardaa says it is deep understanding that keeps a person in contact with men of knowledge.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) added sitting in their gatherings.
narrations.summary: In another narration, Abu Dardaa adds that sitting in the gatherings of scholars is part of this advice.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Haazim says, "Hadhrat Sahl bin Sa'd Saa'idi (RA) was narrating the Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ to a group of his people when some of them started turning to…
narrations.summary: Abu Haazim reports that Sahl bin Sa'd Saa'idi became angry when some people talked among themselves during his teaching, and said he would leave and go out to fight in Jihaad to seek martyrdom.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that a youngster from the Quraysh once approached Rasulullaah taMO- with the request, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Do permit me to fornicate." The…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah relates that a young man from Quraysh asked the Prophet for permission to commit fornication; the Prophet questioned him about his mother, daughter, sister and aunts, and then prayed for his forgiveness, purity and chastity.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ spoke (something of importance), he would repeat himself thrice so that he would be understood."
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah says that when the Prophet said something important he repeated it three times so that he would be understood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) once said to the lecturer of Madinah Hadhrat Ibn Abi Saa'ib, 'You must obey me in three factors, otherwise I shall…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that Aa'isha told Ibn Abi Saa'ib, the teacher at Madinah, to keep three conditions when teaching: not to rhyme his du'aas, as the Prophet and Sahabah did not; to lecture once a week (at most thrice) so people do not tire of the Qur'aan; and not to interrupt people's discussions.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shaqeeq bin Salamah narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood once came to them and said, "I know well that you people are sitting here but the only thing that…
narrations.summary: Shaqeeq bin Salamah reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood did not lecture them daily so as not to tire them, following the Prophet's practice; A'mash reports Ibn Mas'ood telling a lecturer not to make people despair of Allaah's mercy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "Should I not inform you who a true scholar is. He is one who neither makes people despondent of Allaah's mercy nor grants them the licence to…
narrations.summary: Ali describes a true scholar as one who neither makes people despair of Allaah's mercy nor licenses disobedience, nor lets them feel safe from Allaah's punishment, and says knowledge without understanding and worship without knowledge or contemplation have no value.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) to Yemen, he addressed them…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the Prophet sent Mu'aadh bin Jabal and Abu Moosa to Yemen and told them to help each other and speak well to people, not to put them off; Mu'aadh then taught Islaam and understanding, and said a person is destined for Jannah when people speak well of him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) said, "When the Sahabah (RA) of Nabi ﷺ sat together, their discussion always concerned Deen unless one of them was reciting a Surah or…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri says the Companions' gatherings were always about Deen, and Abdullaah bin Umar says a man is respected as a scholar only if he is not jealous of his superiors, does not look down on those below him, and does not sell his knowledge.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "A man can never occupy a respectable position as a scholar unless he is not jealous of those above him, does not look down on those…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says a man can only be a respected scholar if he is free of envy, does not look down on those beneath him, and does not sell his knowledge.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Acquire knowledge and teach the people. Learn also the respectability and composure that goes with it. Humble yourself before those you learn…
narrations.summary: Umar advises people to acquire knowledge and teach it, to stay humble before their teachers and students, and never to be arrogant.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Amongst the rights of an Aalim is that you should not pose too many questions to him, you should not press him to give answers and should not…
narrations.summary: Ali lists the rights a student owes a scholar, from not overburdening him with questions to honouring him in his absence.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jameela the slave woman of Hadhrat Anas (RA) who mothered some of his children says, "Whenever Thaabit came to Hadhrat Anas (RA), Hadhrat Anas would instruct me…
narrations.summary: Jameela, a slave woman of Anas, reports that Anas had perfume brought for the hands of Thaabit Bunaani, who would not be satisfied until he kissed them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "For many years I had wanted to ask Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) about an incident but it was my awe for him that prevented me…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas recounts how, having held back for years from asking Umar about an incident, he finally asked who the two wives were who acted together against the Prophet, and Umar named Aa'isha and Hafsa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib says, "I once said to Hadhrat Sa'd bin Maalik (Abi Waqqaas), '1 wish to pose certain questions to you, but I stand in too much awe of you.'…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib asks Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas what the Prophet said to Ali when he appointed him deputy at Tabook, and Sa'd quotes the Prophet comparing Ali's status to that of Haaroon with Moosa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Abdullaah bin Mowhab narrates that Hadhrat Jubayr bin Mut'im was passing through an oasis when the people questioned him about a matter of…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan bin Abdullaah bin Mowhab reports that when Jubayr bin Mut'im was asked about inheritance, he said he had no knowledge and sent someone to ask Umar, who praised him for saying Allaah knows best.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaahid reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) was once questioned about an aspect of children's inheritance, he replied, "I do not know." "What…
narrations.summary: Mujaahid and Urwa each report that Abdullaah bin Umar, when asked about matters he did not know, simply said that he did not know.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uqba bin Muslim says, "1 stayed with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar for thirty four months and on many occasions when he was questioned about something, he would…
narrations.summary: Uqba bin Muslim says he stayed with Abdullaah bin Umar for thirty-four months and that Ibn Umar often answered 'I do not know', warning that such questions would make their backs a bridge to Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi narrates that a man once posed a question to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) lowered his head and did not respond for such a…
narrations.summary: Naafi reports that when a man asked Abdullaah bin Umar a question, Ibn Umar stayed silent for a long time, then rebuked him for thinking Allaah will not hold people to account for what they ask, and said he would answer only what he knew.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "O people! When a person is questioned about something he has knowledge about, he should give the reply and if he does not…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says a scholar should answer what he knows and otherwise say 'Allaah knows best', which is itself part of knowledge, and quotes the verse in which the Prophet is told to say he asks no payment and does not pretend.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Basheer states that when Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib was once asked a question, he replied by saying, "I have no knowledge on the subject." He then…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Basheer reports that when Ali was asked a question he said he had no knowledge of it, and then said it was a comfort that he had once admitted not knowing something he did know.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "When an Aalim forsakes the statement 'I do -not know', then he has reached his point of destruction." Another narration also…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says that when an Aalim gives up saying 'I do not know', he has reached his ruin, and the same saying is given again in a second narration.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Makhool reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) noticed that the people were getting tired as he narrated Ahadeeth to them, he would occupy them with planting trees.
narrations.summary: Makhool reports that Umar gave people tree-planting to rest them from lessons; Abdullaah bin Mus'ab reports that Umar set a limit on dowries and conceded to a woman who quoted the Qur'aan against him; Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi reports that Ali conceded to a man who corrected him; and Sa'eed bin Musayyib says Umar and Uthmaan debated sharply but always parted amicably.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mus'ab narrates that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) said, "Do not pay more than forty Awqiya as dowry, even though the bride may be the daughter of…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Khattaab said dowries should not exceed forty awqiya; a woman stood up and corrected him from Surah Nisaa verse 20, and Umar accepted that she was right.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi (RA) narrates that a man once posed a question to Hadhrat Ali (RA), to which he gave a reply. "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" the man said, "That…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi reports that a man corrected Ali's answer to a question; Ali admitted he was wrong and recited the verse that above every knowledgeable person is one more knowledgeable.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib says, "Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) used to debate a question so vehemently that an onlooker would be…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib says Umar and Uthmaan would debate a question so fiercely that onlookers thought they could never be reconciled, yet they always parted most amicably.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir (RA) relates, "I arrived riding with twelve members of my tribe to see Rasulullaah ﷺ. When we had tied our camels, Mustahab companions said, 'Who…
narrations.summary: Uqba bin Aamir tells how he took turns minding his tribe's camels so the others could hear the Prophet, and how Umar relayed the Prophet's words on wudhu and on dying without shirk, after which the Prophet asked whether he preferred one or twelve.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Abul Aas (RA) reports, "I arrived with the delegation of the Thaqeef tribe when they came to see Rasulullaah ﷺ. We were changing our clothes at…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan bin Abul Aas, the youngest of a Thaqeef delegation, asked the Prophet to pray that he understand the Deen, and was made Ameer over his tribe; a second narration adds that the Prophet had a copy of the Qur'aan and gave it to him when he asked.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "When we used to sit with Rasulullaah ﷺ as he narrated Ahadeeth to us, we would sometimes number as many as sixty. Then when Rasulullaah ﷺ needed…
narrations.summary: Anas says that when the Prophet narrated Ahadeeth, as many as sixty Companions would sit with him, and when he left they rehearsed what they had heard among themselves.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) says, "After Rasulullaah ﷺ performed the Fajr salaah, we would turn towards him. Some of us would then ask him about the Qur'aan, others…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari says that after the Fajr salaah the Companions turned to the Prophet, and some asked him about the Qur'aan, others about inheritance and others about dreams.

narrations.excerpt: When his companions used to come to him, Hadhrat Fudhaala bin Ubayd (RA) would say to them, "Learn and teach each other, convey glad tidings and increase (your…
narrations.summary: Fudhaala bin Ubayd tells his companions to learn and teach each other, rehearse what they have learnt, and add istighfaar to their discussions.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Nadhra says that when they once requested Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri Ji to write down Ahadeeth for them, he said, "I shall never write it for you and never…
narrations.summary: Abu Nadhra says that when people asked Abu Sa'eed Khudri to write hadiths down, he refused, telling them to learn by memory as he had from the Prophet, and told them to rehearse hadiths among themselves because that reinforces memory.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) as saying, "Rehearse the Ahadeeth amongst yourselves because this rejuvenates the memory."
narrations.summary: In another narration, Abu Sa'eed Khudri urges rehearsing hadiths, Ali says that without rehearsal they will be forgotten, and Ali adds that people should keep visiting one another.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Rehearse the Ahadeeth amongst yourselves because if you do not do this, you will forget them." Another narration states that Hadhrat Ali iS also…
narrations.summary: Ali tells people to rehearse the ahadith among themselves so they do not forget them, and adds that they should keep visiting each other.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Rehearse the Ahadeeth amongst yourselves because this keeps it alive." ^ Another narration quotes Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that rehearsing hadiths keeps them alive, and in another narration that rehearsing knowledge of the Deen earns the reward of nafl salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "I prefer rehearsing the knowledge of Deen for a part of the night to engaging in Ibaadah throughout the night."
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says he prefers rehearsing the knowledge of Deen for part of the night to spending the night in worship.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once addressed Hadhrat Ali (RA) saying, "O Abul Hasan! There were times when you were present with…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar put three questions to Ali, and Ali answered each with a saying of the Prophet about souls that either recognise or stay apart from one another, about clouds that pass over the heart so that a person forgets, and about true and false dreams; Umar said he was glad to have these answers before his death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraaheem Taymi narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was alone one day when he started thinking to himself. He then sent for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas and asked…
narrations.summary: Ibraheem Taymi reports that Umar, troubled that the Ummah differs although it has one Book, one Nabi and one Qiblah, asked Ibn Abbaas, who answered that differences arise when people recite the Qur'aan without knowing why its verses were revealed; Umar first rebuked him, then called him back and asked him to repeat it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates, "Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, 'I recited a verse last night that kept me awake. (The verse is): Would any of you like to own a…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that when Umar asked what the orchard verse of Surah Baqarah meant and no one could say, Ibn Abbaas said it refers to deeds, and Umar agreed, explaining that a man most needs his deeds on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "Because Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to allow me in with the veterans of Badr, Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) objected saying, 'Why…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas recounts that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf objected to Umar letting him sit with the Badr veterans, and that when Umar asked about Surah Nasr Ibn Abbaas explained it as a sign of the Prophet's approaching death, which Umar confirmed.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Because Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to consult with me together with the senior Sahabah (RA) of…
narrations.summary: In another, abbreviated narration, Ibn Abbaas says Umar consulted him alongside the senior Companions and that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf objected in the same way.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that he once asked Hadhrat Umar about the verse: O you who have Imaan! Do not ask questions concerning those things that you…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that Umar explained the Maa'idah verse against troublesome questions as relating to Muhaajireen doubts about lineage, then voiced fear that Ali might be carried away by conceit if he became Khaleefah, which Ibn Abbaas rejected by defending Ali and citing Aadam's lapse.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) reports that he was once sitting with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) when Hadhrat Khabbaab came there saying, "O Abdullaah bin Umar…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas says Khabbaab told Ibn Umar that Abu Hurayrah reported a reward for attending funerals, so Ibn Umar sent Khabbaab to Aa'isha to verify it, and when she confirmed it Ibn Umar said they had lost many qiraats.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) said, "We (the poor men of Suffa) had neither plantations nor trade in the marketplaces to distract us frpm being…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah says the poor men of Suffa had no trade or farms to keep them from the Prophet, so he sought words to learn from him, and Ibn Umar tells him he knows more hadiths than they do because he stayed closer to the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "I have never seen people better than the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ . Until he passed away, they did not ask him more than…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas says the Companions asked the Prophet no more than thirteen questions, all of them matters of benefit that appear in the Qur'aan, and then adds that the angels were the first to circle the Ka'bah and that several prophets are buried between the Black Stone and the Yamani corner.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "The women of the Ansaar were the best of women. Modesty did not prevent them from asking questions about Deen and attaining a deep…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says the Ansaari women were the best because modesty did not stop them asking about the Deen, and Ummu Sulaym asks the Prophet whether a woman must bathe after a dream of intercourse, to which he says yes if she finds semen, adding that women are offshoots of men.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) narrates that she was sitting next to Rasulullaah wife Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) when she asked, "O Rasulullaah Should a woman have a bath if she…
narrations.summary: Ummu Sulaym asks the Prophet whether a woman must bathe after dreaming of intercourse; he says yes if she finds semen, and tells Ummu Salamah, who objected, that women are offshoots of men.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd (RA), "People used to question each other about certain matters that Rasulullaah ﷺ mentioned and would then question Rasulullaah ﷺ so much about it that…
narrations.summary: Sa'd (RA) says people used to question each other about things the Prophet mentioned, then questioned him so much that a matter which had been lawful became unlawful.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "The verses of Li'aan were revealed only because of the many questions that were asked." When people were posing too many questions to Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Jaabir says the verses of Li'aan were revealed only because of the many questions asked; Ibn Mas'ood asks Haarith bin Qais why people ask so much, and Haarith says they want answers only to forget them, which Ibn Mas'ood affirms.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once said, "O people! Never ask about things that have not happened because Hadhrat Umar (RA) use to curse people who asked about things…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar tells people never to ask about things that have not happened, because Umar used to curse those who did.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "It is not permissible to ask about things that have not happened because Allaah has already decreed everything that is still to happen."
narrations.summary: Umar says it is not permissible to ask about things that have not yet happened, because Allaah has already decreed everything that is still to happen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaarijah bin Zaid bin Thaabit narrates that his father (Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit would never voice his opinion concerning anything he was asked about until he…
narrations.summary: Khaarijah bin Zaid reports that his father Zaid bin Thaabit would not give an opinion on a question until he had checked whether the matter had happened, and would answer only once it had.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Masrooq relates, "When I once questioned Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b about something, he asked, 'Has this actually occurred?' When 1 informed him that it did not, he…
narrations.summary: Masrooq says that when he asked Ubay bin Ka'b about a matter, Ubay asked whether it had happened, and on hearing it had not said they should rest until it did; a second narration adds that they would then find a solution.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir narrates that when Hadhrat Ammaar iS was once questioned about something, he asked, "Has this actually occurred?" When informed that it did not, he…
narrations.summary: Aamir reports that when Ammaar was asked about a matter, he asked whether it had actually happened, and when told it had not, said to leave it until it does.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that a man once came to Rasulullaah and explained how much profit he had earned by buying (and selling) the shares of a particular…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaama says that when a man who had profited from trading a tribe's shares came to the Prophet, the Prophet told him that learning ten verses of the Qur'aan was more profitable, and the man went to learn them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to me, 'Should I not inform you of a Surah, the like of which has not been revealed in the Torah, the…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b narrates that the Prophet taught him the virtue of Surah Faatiha as the seven often-repeated verses.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Abu Talha is once arrived (at the Masjid) to find Rasulullaah ﷺ teaching the men of Suffa with a portion of a rock tied to his belly in order to…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Abu Talha came to the Masjid and found the Prophet teaching the men of Suffa, with a stone tied to his belly against hunger.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) was once sitting at home and when some people gathered there, he started reciting the Qur'aan to them. A…
narrations.summary: Anas relates that Abu Moosa recited the Qur'aan at home, and that the Prophet, having heard him unseen, praised his recitation as one of the tunes of the family of Dawood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas ig relates, "Hadhrat (Abu Moosa) Ash'ari (RA) once sent me to Hadhrat Urnar (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, 'How was Ash'ari when you left?' I replied, 'He…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Umar asked about Abu Moosa Ash'ari, who was teaching the Qur'aan in Basrah; Abu Rajaa then says Abu Moosa taught him Surah Alaq, the first surah revealed to the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ left this world, I vowed never to remove my shawl from my back (would not rest) until I had memorised what was contained…
narrations.summary: Ali says that after the Prophet passed away he vowed not to take off his shawl until he had memorised the whole Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maymoon (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) learnt Surah Baqara in four years.
narrations.summary: Maymoon reports that Abdullaah bin Umar took four years to learn Surah Baqara.

narrations.excerpt: A man from the Ashja tribe narrates that when the people of Madaa'in heard that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) was in the Masjid, they continued arriving there until almost a…
narrations.summary: Salmaan recites Surah Yusuf to a crowd in the Madaa'in masjid, and when most of them leave he rebukes those who prefer a lecture to the Book of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Whenever Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) taught a verse of the Qur'aan to someone, he would say, "This (verse) is better than everything upon which the sun rises and…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood teaches each verse of the Qur'aan to the people who come to his house each morning and tells them it is better than everything the sun rises upon.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abduilaah bin Mas'ood (RA) used to say to the people, "Ensure that you stick to this Qur'aan because it is Allaah's tablecloth (laden with food). Whoever is…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood tells the people to hold fast to the Qur'aan as Allaah's laden tablecloth, since knowledge is acquired only through study.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abduilaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Verily this Qur'aan is Allaah's tablecloth (laden with food). Whoever is capable of learning…
narrations.summary: Another narration has Abdullaah bin Mas'ood say that a house without the Book of Allaah is like a deserted house and that Shaytaan leaves a house where Surah Baqarah is recited.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said to a man who very often came to his door, "Go and study the Book of Allaah." The man left and Hadhrat Umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: Umar tells a man who often came to his door to go and study the Book of Allaah, and the man later says the Book has made him independent of Umar's door.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "It is necessary for every Muslim man to learn six Surahs, two Surahs for the Fajr salaah, two Surahs for the Maghrib salaah and two Surahs for…
narrations.summary: Umar says every Muslim man should learn six Surahs, two each for the Fajr, Maghrib and Isha salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhrama (RA) Sgi says that he heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) say, "Learn Surah Baqarah, Surah Nisaa, Surah Maa'idah, Surah Hajj and Surah Noor because they…
narrations.summary: Umar names the Surahs that should be learnt, citing Miswar bin Makhrama, a letter to governors reported by Haaritha bin Mudarrib, and a further narration on teaching Surah Noor to women.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Rayhaana (RA) reports that he once complained to Rasulullaah ticS-f that it was difficult for him to learn the Qur'aan and that what he learnt escaped his…
narrations.summary: Abu Rayhaana complains that he finds the Qur'aan hard to learn, and the Prophet advises him not to take on more than he can manage and to pray much nafl salaah; Umayrah reports that he used to make much sajdah at Asqalaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaradha bin Ka'b (RA) reports that when they were leaving for Iraq, Hadhrat Umar (RA) accompanied them to a place called Siraar. There Hadhrat Umar performed…
narrations.summary: Qaradha bin Ka'b reports that Umar, on the journey to Iraq, asked the Sahabah to keep the people occupied with the Qur'aan and narrate few Ahadeeth, and Qaradha repeated that prohibition when asked to narrate in Iraq.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar Ji said, "Do not preoccupy them with Ahadeeth for it will prevent them from mastering the Qur'aan." Yet another narration…
narrations.summary: Umar tells the Sahabah not to occupy people with ahadith in a way that stops them mastering the Qur'aan; a second report has Umar explaining why he walked with them, and that report is abridged.

narrations.excerpt: A freed slave of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that an Iraqi called Sabeegh in the Muslim army was questioning certain (Mutashaabih) verses of the Qur'aan and…
narrations.summary: A freed slave of Abdullaah bin Umar relates how Umar had Sabeegh, who questioned the mutashaabih verses, beaten with date-palm branches and ordered the people to shun him until Abu Moosa reported he had reformed; a second narration, from Sulaymaan bin Yasaar, gives an account of Sabeegh being beaten by Umar in Madinah until he said his doubts had gone.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Yasaar states that a man from the Banu Tameem called Sabeegh bin Isl once arrived in Madinah. He had many books and always…
narrations.summary: Sulaymaan bin Yasaar relates that Sabeegh bin Isl kept questioning the mutashaabih verses of the Qur'aan, so Umar beat him with date-palm branches until his head bled; Sabeegh then said that his doubt had gone.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan said, "Hadhrat Umar (RA) then wrote to instruct us not to associate with Sabeegh. Therefore, if he ever arrived, we would…
narrations.summary: Abu Uthmaan says Umar wrote ordering the Muslims not to associate with Sabeegh, and another narration says Sabeegh was despised by his people after once being their leader.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that when some people met Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar in Egypt, they said, "We have come across some matters in the Qur'aan that we have been…
narrations.summary: Some men from Egypt, who had questioned Abdullaah bin Umar about difficult Qur'aanic matters, are examined by Umar on what they have memorised and practised, and Umar says he would have made an example of them if the people of Madinah had known.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) says, "Because Rasulullaah ﷺ was very occupied, he would hand over to one of us any person who migrated so that we may teach him the…
narrations.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit says that a migrant he had taught the Qur'aan gave him a bow as a gift, and the Prophet called it a burning ember hung between his shoulders.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) once taught a Surah to a man who gave him a garment or a shawl as a gift. When he informed Rasulullaah ﷺ about this, Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked,…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b, having taught a Surah to a man who gave him a garment, is told by the Prophet that wearing it would be wearing a garment of fire.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Ubay (RA) taught the Qur'aan to a man, he gave him a bow as a gift.
narrations.summary: Another narration says that when Ubay bin Ka'b taught the Qur'aan to a man, he received a bow as a gift.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tufayl bin Amr (RA) says, "When Hadhrat Ubay ig! taught me the Qur'aan, I gave him a bow as a gift. When he went to Rasulullaah ﷺ the next morning with the bow…
narrations.summary: Tufayl bin Amr gave Ubay bin Ka'b a bow after Ubay taught him the Qur'aan; the Prophet asked Ubay why he wore it, called it a spark from Jahannam, and explained that food prepared for others may be eaten but food prepared specially for the teacher eats from his share in the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik (RA) reports that there was a man with him to whom • (1) Ibnjareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaai '(Vol.1 Pg.228). he had taught the Qur'aan. When the…
narrations.summary: Awf bin Maalik reports that a man he had taught the Qur'aan gave him a bow, and the Prophet asked whether he wanted to meet Allaah carrying an ember of Jahannam on his back.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muthanna bin Waa'il says, "When I went to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr one day, he passed his hand over my head and I held him by the forearm. Just then someone…
narrations.summary: Muthanna bin Waa'il recounts Abdullaah bin Busr's report of a man who was given a bow for teaching a child the Qur'aan, and the Prophet told him to return it, asking whether he wanted a bow of fire around his neck.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Usayr bin Amr narrates that the news once reached Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab that Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) said, "I shall include those who teach the Qur'aan amongst the…
narrations.summary: Umar objects when he hears that Sa'd plans to pay Qur'aan teachers an allowance, later tells a governor to give allowances by merit of family and companionship with the Prophet instead, and warns that those who take pay for teaching will see even adulterers enter Jannah before them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates, "1 was sitting with Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab when a letter came to him from Kufa, informing him how much Qur'aan the people…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas warns Umar that the spread of the Qur'aan among the people will lead to disputes, and after Umar's anger he recites verses to explain his view, and Umar agrees that he is right.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas said, "1 was with Hadhrat Umar (RA) when he caught hold of my hand and said, 'I think that…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr relates that Ibn Abbaas warned Umar that the spread of the Qur'aan would cause disputes and then killing, and that Umar admitted he had understood the same but had been concealing it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Kinaanah Adawi narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote to the commanders of his armies to send him a list of all the men who were Huffaadh of the Qur'aan so that he…
narrations.summary: Kinaanah Adawi relates that Umar asked his commanders for lists of the Huffaadh so he could send them out to teach, that Abu Moosa replied there were just over three hundred, and that Umar wrote to them on honouring and following the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Kinaanah reports that when Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) gathered together the Huffaadh (of the army he commanded), they numbered close t. three hundred.…
narrations.summary: Abu Kinaanah and Abul Aswad Daly each relate Abu Moosa's addresses to his Huffaadh and Qurraa, urging them to follow the Qur'aan and not let time harden their hearts, and reminding them they will be questioned about what they do.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once addressed the people of Kufa. After greeting them with Salaam and instructing them to observe Taqwa, he said, "Never dispute about…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood tells the people of Kufa not to dispute about the Qur'aan, since it contains no contradictions, and recalls that the Prophet approved his recitation; other reports add his advice on the qualities of a man of the Qur'aan and on listening carefully.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "It is only befitting that a man of the Qur'aan be recognised by his nights (when he is engaged in Ibaadah) when others are…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood advises that a man of the Qur'aan should be known by his night prayers, fasting, sorrow, weeping and humility, and should be a good listener; another report gives further advice to listen and heed Allah's commands.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was busy narrating Ahadeeth when a Bedouin arrived and asked, "When will Qiyaamah take place?" When Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that when a Bedouin asked the Prophet, in the middle of his narrating, when the Qiyaamah would come, the Prophet said it would come when trusts are misappropriated and authority is given to unworthy people.

narrations.excerpt: Standing before the people in the largest Masjid of Riqqa during the days of Eidul Fitr and Eidul Adhaa, Hadhrat Waabisah (RA) used to say, "I was present with…
narrations.summary: Waabisah recalls the Prophet's address on the Farewell Hajj, that the month, city, and the blood, wealth and honour of the Muslims are sacred until the Day they meet their Rabb, and that those present must convey it to those absent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Makhool says, "Ibn Abu Zakariyyah, Sulaymaan bin Habeeb and 1 once went to Hadhrat Abu Umaamah SE in Hims. After we had greeted him with the words of Salaam, he…
narrations.summary: Makhool relates that Abu Umaamah told him and his companions that their sitting was a means for the Deen to reach them and that they must propagate it, and Saleem bin Aamir relates that Abu Ubaadah asked his listeners after each session to pass on what they had heard.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once prayed, "O Allaah! Shower Your mercy on my successors." "O Rasulullaah (illli?!" the Sahabah (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates the Prophet's du'aa for mercy on his successors, those who will narrate his Ahadeeth and teach them to the people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aasim bin Muhammad narrates from his father that he saw Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah come to the Masjid of Rasulullaah ﷺ on the day of Jumu'ah. Standing and holding the…
narrations.summary: Aasim bin Muhammad relates from his father that he saw Abu Hurayrah on a Jumu'ah standing at the pulpit narrating Ahadeeth until the Imaam emerged, and then sit down.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aslam reports that when they used to ask Hadhrat Umar (RA) to narrate Ahadeeth to them, he would say, "I fear that I may add a word or omit a word because…
narrations.summary: Aslam relates that Umar refused to narrate Ahadeeth when asked for fear of adding or omitting a word, and Abdur Rahmaan bin Haatib says that Uthmaan narrated more thoroughly than any Sahabi but was very reluctant to do so.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Haatib says, "I have not seen any of the Sahabah narrate Ahadeeth as well and as thoroughly as Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA). However, he was a man who…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Haatib says he has not seen any Companion narrate hadith as well and thoroughly as Uthmaan, though Uthmaan was very reluctant to narrate.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) used to say, "What prevents me from narrating Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ is not the fact that I was not one of those Sahabah (RA) with the best…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan explains that his reluctance to narrate Ahadeeth is not weak memory but fear of the Prophet's warning against those who attribute falsehoods to him, and another narration gives that warning in different words.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "When narrating Ahadeeth to you, I prefer falling from the sky rather than stating something that Rasulullaah Wife never said. However, when…
narrations.summary: Ali says that when narrating Ahadeeth he would rather fall from the sky than say what the Prophet did not say, but that in matters of war strategy such strictness need not apply.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Maymoon reports that sometimes an entire year would pass by without Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrating a single Hadith. When he narrated a…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Maymoon and Masrooq each relate that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood sometimes went a whole year without narrating a Hadith, and that when he did he trembled and sweated, adding a qualification to what he attributed to the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Masrooq reports, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) started to narrate a Hadith one day, but as soon as he said, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said,' he started to shiver so…
narrations.summary: Masrooq reports that when Ibn Mas'ood began a hadith with 'The Prophet said', he shook so much that his clothes trembled, and then added that the Prophet said something to that effect.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Idrees Khowlaani says, "I noticed that whenever Hadhrat Abu Dardaa completed narrating Ahadeeth, he would add, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said that, something similar to…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa and Anas bin Maalik closed their hadith reports with a qualifying phrase, so as not to claim more than the Prophet's exact words.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrated few Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ, but when he did, he would end with the words, "It was…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik narrated few hadith and always added the qualifying phrase. Abu Ja'far Muhammad bin Ali says no Companion was more careful in narrating than Abdullaah bin Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ja'far Muhammad bin Ali says, "There was no companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ more cautious of adding anything to or omitting anything from the Ahadeeth of…
narrations.summary: Abu Ja'far Muhammad bin Ali says that no Companion of the Prophet was more careful than Abdullaah bin Umar about adding to or omitting anything from the Prophet's ahadith.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi says, "I sat in the company of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) for an entire year without hearing him narrate anything from Rasulullaah.
narrations.summary: Sha'bi says he sat with Abdullaah bin Umar for a full year and never heard him narrate a hadith from the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) said, "I have heard many Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ which I have memorised. All that prevents me from narrating them is that some of my…
narrations.summary: Imraan bin Husayn says he has memorised many hadith but holds back from narrating them, because some of his companions may differ with him over the wording.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mutarraf reports that Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) said to him, "O Mutarraf! By Allaah! I am certain that if I chose to do so, I could narrate Ahadeeth from…
narrations.summary: Mutarraf reports that Imraan bin Husayn could narrate hadith for two days without repeating one, but refrained because companions confuse the sequence of words. He was exact when quoting the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Abu Abdullaah reports that he heard Hadhrat Suhayb say, "By Allaah! I shall never intentionally narrate Ahadeeth to you saying that it is what…
narrations.summary: Suhayb tells Sulaymaan bin Abu Abdullaah that he will never say 'Rasulullaah said' for a hadith, though he will relate what he experienced on the expeditions.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Makhool relates, "Abul Azhar and I once went to Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa and said, 'O Abu Asqa! Narrate to us a Hadith that you heard from Rasulullaah ﷺ without…
narrations.summary: Makhool and Abul Azhar asked Waathila bin Asqa for a hadith in exact words. He replied that they had not mastered the Qur'aan, and that narrators should relate only the meaning.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf relates, "By Allaah! Before he passed away, Hadhrat Umar (RA) sent messengers to various distant places to summon Sahabah (RA)…
narrations.summary: Before his death Umar summoned Companions from distant lands, asked what hadith they were spreading, and kept them in Madinah. He also confined Abdullaah bin Mas'ood, Abu Mas'ood and Abu Dardaa there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Abu Awfa (RA) reports that when they used to request Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam to narrate the Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ to them, he would say, "We have aged and…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abu Awfa reports that when asked to narrate hadith, Zaid bin Arqam said he had grown old and forgetful, and that narrating the Prophet's hadith was a serious matter.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) both said, "Learn as much as you wish to learn but Allaah will place no benefit in your knowledge until you practise what…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal and Abu Dardaa both said that knowledge brings no benefit until it is practised. Anas bin Maalik said the same, that there is no reward for knowledge until it is put into practice.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Ghanam says, "Ten Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah informed me that they were learning in the Masjid of Quba when Rasulullaah ﷺ came to them and…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Ghanam reports that ten Companions were learning in the Masjid of Quba when the Prophet came and told them to learn.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that a man came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ What will satisfy the evidence that ignorance will hold against me?" "Knowledge,"…
narrations.summary: Ali reports that a man asked the Prophet what would be the proof against him for ignorance and what would be the proof against him for knowledge. The Prophet answered knowledge, and then action.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Study the Book of Allaah and you will be known for it. Practise on its teachings and you will be amongst its worthy bearers." Pg.153) has…
narrations.summary: Umar tells people to study the Book of Allaah and practise its teachings, so that they become among its worthy bearers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Study and you will be known for it. Practise on your knowledge and you will be amongst its worthy bearers because soon a time will come when…
narrations.summary: Ali tells people to study and practise, warning that a time will come when most of the truth is rejected. Only the anonymous, aloof people who are the lanterns of knowledge will be saved, and they are not hasty and do not spread immoral behaviour or speech.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "O men of knowledge! Practise on your knowledge because only that person is an Aalim whose knowledge is followed by practise and whose…
narrations.summary: Ali warns of people of knowledge whose private lives contradict their public teaching, who boast in their gatherings, and whose actions will not rise to Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "O people! Study, but whoever studies should practise what he learns."
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood urges people to practise what they learn. Abdullaah bin Ukaym and Adi bin Adi relate his warnings that Allaah will question each person about whether they practised their knowledge.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ukaym says, "It was in this very Masjid that I heard Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) begin his speech with an oath as he said, 'Your Rabb shall…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ukaym quotes Ibn Mas'ood that on the Day of Judgement each person will be asked whether he acted on his knowledge; Adi bin Adi relates Ibn Mas'ood's warning that the one who has knowledge but does not practise is destroyed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood is said, "Everyone has fantastic words to say but only those will be successful whose deeds are consistent with their words. The one whose…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says everyone has fine words but only those whose deeds match their words will succeed, and that people need the scholar who acts on his knowledge and the one absorbed in Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Luqmaan bin Aamir narrates that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) used to say, "What I fear most about Allaah on the Day of Qiyaamah is that he would call me in front of…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa said he feared being asked on the Day of Judgement whether he practised his knowledge. He also said that the worst person before Allaah is one whose knowledge does not benefit him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) said, "No person will be able to move his feet on the Day of Qiyaamah until he is questioned about four things; (1) about how he used his…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal said that no one will be able to move on the Day of Judgement until he is questioned about four things, including how he practised his knowledge.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) also said, "Learn as much as you want but Allaah shall not reward you for it until you practise on your knowledge."
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal says no reward is given for knowledge until it is practised. Anas bin Maalik adds that true scholars aim to remember and practise, while foolish people aim only to pass knowledge on.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) said, "Learn as much as you want to learn but Allaah shall not reward you for it until you practise on your knowledge. While the objective of true Ulema…
narrations.summary: Anas says that knowledge brings no reward until it is practised, and that true scholars seek to remember and act on it while foolish people seek only to relate it to others.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) said, "Hold fast to the straight path and the Sunnah because Allaah shall never punish a person who is steadfast on the straight path and the…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b urges holding fast to the straight path and the Sunnah. He says that moderate deeds done for Allaah's pleasure are better than exertion that goes against the Sunnah, and that deeds should be checked against the way of the Prophets.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) arrived back in Madinah, he addressed the people saying, "O peoplel The Sunan have been demonstrated to…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports Umar's address after returning to Madinah, that the Sunan have been shown and the Faraa'idh ordained. Ibn Mas'ood then taught that every new introduction in the Deen is a bid'ah, and warned against distant hopes that make one forget the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Moderation in the Sunnah is better than exerting oneself in Bid'ah."
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says that moderation in the Sunnah is better than striving in bid'ah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) said, "The Qur'aan was revealed and Rasulullaah ﷺ demonstrated his way of life (which we emulated). You people must follow us because if…
narrations.summary: Imraan bin Husayn says the Qur'aan was revealed and the Prophet showed how to live by it, and that people must follow the Companions or they will go astray.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) once said to someone (who insisted on following only the Qur'aan), "You are a fool! Do you find any verse of the Qur'aan telling you that…
narrations.summary: Imraan bin Husayn rebukes a man who would follow only the Qur'aan. He shows that the details of prayer, zakaah and other rules come from the Sunnah, which explains what the Qur'aan states only briefly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Whoever wishes to follow anyone, should follow the companions of Muhammad ﷺ because from amongst the entire Ummah, their hearts…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood urges people to follow the Companions of the Prophet, who had the most righteous hearts, the deepest knowledge and the most upright example in the Ummah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) used to say, "O assembly of Qurraa! Fear Allaah and follow the path of those before you. I swear by my life that if you follow them, you will go…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah urges the Qurraa to fear Allaah and follow those who came before them, warning that whoever turns from their path goes far astray.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Sa'd reports that whenever his father (Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas led the salaah (in congregation), he would make it brief together with performing…
narrations.summary: Mus'ab bin Sa'd reports that his father, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, kept congregational prayer brief but prolonged it when praying alone. He told his son that the Companions are the leaders to be followed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Follow and do not introduce" and his Statement about Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says to follow and not introduce new ways, because the Prophet and the Companions have already laid the path.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "An integral part of the Sunnah is to love Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) and to acknowledge their worth."
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says that loving Abu Bakr and Umar and acknowledging their worth is an integral part of the Sunnah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Be careful not to emulate people because while a man can be doing the deeds of the people of Jannah, he can change according to the knowledge of…
narrations.summary: Ali warns against imitating living people, since a person may change course for better or worse and die in that state. He says that if one must follow someone, it should be those who died as practising believers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari says that someone once informed Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood about a group of people who sat in the Masjid after Maghrib when one of them would…
narrations.summary: When Ibn Mas'ood learned that a group in the Masjid was performing dhikr in set counts led by one man, he confronted them, called it a wrong bid'ah, and had them disperse.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) saw two groups in the Masjid of Kufa, he stood between the two and asked, "Which of you two was…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood confronts groups in the Masjid of Kufa and between Maghrib and Isha, saying they have strayed very quickly while the Companions are still alive. Abu Moosa Ash'ari brings him word of the dhikr group.

narrations.excerpt: that he once came to his father, who asked him, "Where have you been?" The son replied, "I found a group of people better than whom I have not seen. When they engage in…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr finds his son Aamir sitting with people who fall unconscious in dhikr, and tells him never to sit with them again, since the Companions did not behave like this.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Saalih Sa'eed bin Abdur Rahmaan narrates that Anz Nujaybi was once standing and relating stories in the Masjid when a Sahabi by the name of Hadhrat Sila bin…
narrations.summary: Sila bin Haarith Ghifaari rebukes Anz Nujaybi, who was telling stories in the Masjid, saying the Companions had scarcely left the Prophet's time and that such innovations should not appear among them yet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Zuraarah says, "I was relating stories in the Masjid when Hadhrat Abdullaah (bin Mas'ood) (RA) stood up and said, 'O Amr! You have started a misleading…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Zuraarah says that while he was relating stories in the Masjid, Ibn Mas'ood called it a misleading bid'ah, and everyone around him dispersed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Shihaab reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was standing on the pulpit and addressed the people saying, "O people! Accurate opinions came only from Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports Umar's sermon that accurate opinions came only from the Prophet, whom Allaah guided. Sadaqah bin Abu Abdullaah reports Umar's warning that those who follow personal opinion are enemies of the Sunnah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) also said, "The Sunnah is that which Allaah and His Rasool (ic have determined. You should never make your mistaken opinion a Another narration from…
narrations.summary: Umar says the Sunnah is what Allaah and His Rasool have determined, and that one should not let one's own opinion take its place; Amr bin Dinaar reports Umar disclaiming that Allaah guided his judgements, as that was a speciality of the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Beware of asking, "What is your opinion? What is your opinion?' because those before you were…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi relates Ibn Mas'ood's warning against asking for opinions and judging one matter by another, and his saying that 'Allaah knows best' is a third of knowledge. Ibn Mas'ood also foresaw that after the Ulema die, people would destroy Islaam by personal opinion.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "The basis (of Islaam and the Shari'ah) is Allaah's Book and the Sunnah of Rasulullaah ﷺ. Whoever says anything else based on his…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas says the basis of Islaam is the Book of Allaah and the Sunnah. A Companion, reported through Ataa from his father, says he is too shy before his Rabb to give a personal opinion on matters affecting the Ummah.
