narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ sent him to Yemen, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him, "How will you pass judgement when a case comes beforeyou?" "I…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal tells how the Prophet, sending him to Yemen, asked how he would judge. He answered by the Book of Allaah, then the Sunnah, then ijtihaad without neglecting diligence, and the Prophet approved.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen says, "After Rasulullaah ﷺ there was none more concerned about not knowing something than Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and after Hadhrat Abu Bakr…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports that Abu Bakr was the most careful of all not to pass a verdict without knowledge, and that when no verse or Hadith applied he practised ijtihaad, asking Allaah's forgiveness if he was wrong.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shurayh narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once wrote to him saying, "When a matter presents itself before you, pass your verdict according to the Book of Allaah. If…
narrations.summary: Shurayh reports Umar's letter to him: judge by the Book of Allaah, then by the Prophet's directives, then by the unanimous view of the scholars, and if none of these applies, either practise ijtihaad or refrain, with Umar advising refraining.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "When any of you has to pass a verdict, he should pass his verdict according to the Book of Allaah. If the matter is not…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says a judge should rule by the Qur'aan, then by the Prophet's practice, then by the verdicts of the righteous scholars, and otherwise practise ijtihaad firmly, never speaking in doubt, since the clearly lawful and the clearly unlawful are plain and doubtful matters should be avoided.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Yazeed reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas was questioned about anything and the reply was to be found in the Qur'aan, he would state…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Yazeed reports that Ibn Abbaas gave his answers in order: from the Qur'aan first, then from the Prophet's sayings, then from the statements of Abu Bakr or Umar, and only then by ijtihaad.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, '"When we receive corroboration (to an injunction), we would not equate anything else to it (and…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas says that when a command was confirmed by corroborating evidence they would not place anything else on a par with it and would readily practise it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that when he once questioned Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b about something, Hadhrat Ubay (RA) asked, "Has it already happened?" When he was informed that…
narrations.summary: Masrooq reports that when he asked Ubay bin Ka'b about a matter that had not yet happened, Ubay asked for respite until it happened so that they could then practise ijtihaad.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla says, "I met a hundred and twenty Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ in the Masjid. When any of them narrated a Hadith, he wished that his…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla says he met 120 Sahabah in the Masjid, and each one, whether narrating a Hadith or giving a Fatwa, wished that a fellow Sahabi had done it instead.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "It is only a madman who will immediately issue a Fatwa for everything he is asked." The same statement has been reported from…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood and Ibn Abbaas say that only a madman would issue a Fatwa on everything he is asked, and Hudhayfah says only three kinds of people should issue Fataawaa: one who knows which verses abrogate and which are abrogated, a leader with no alternative, and a pretentious fool.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Seereen narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to Hadhrat Abu Mas'ood Uqba bin Umar, "I was informed that you issue Fataawaa to people! The person blessed with…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports that Umar told Abu Mas'ood Uqba that he had heard he was issuing Fataawaa to people, and warned him of the burden that goes with it.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration staites that Hadhrat Umar also added, "And you are not a governor (so you need not issue Fataawaa). "
narrations.summary: Umar adds that Abu Mas'ood is not a governor, so he need not issue Fataawaa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Minhaal says, "When I questioned Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) and Hadhrat Baraa (RA) about selling gold and silver, each one of them told me to ask the other,…
narrations.summary: Abu Minhaal reports that Zaid bin Arqam and Baraa each sent him to ask the other about selling gold and silver, and Abu Husayn says that people now issue Fataawaa on matters which, had they been put to Umar, he would have taken to the veterans of Badr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Husayn says, "Everyone now issues Fataawaa on matters that had they been posed to Hadhrat Umar (RA), he would have gathered all the veterans of Badr (to…
narrations.summary: Abu Husayn says that people now issue fatwas on matters which, had they been put to Umar, he would have referred to the veterans of Badr before answering.

narrations.excerpt: When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) was asked who used to issue Fataawaa during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, he replied, "Abu Bakr and Umar. I do not know of anyone else."…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar names Abu Bakr and Umar as the only ones who issued Fataawaa in the Prophet's time, while Qaasim bin Muhammad names Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthmaan and Ali, and Fudhayl bin Abu Abdullaah bin Dinaar names Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Attiyya Hamdaani reports that he was once sitting with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood when a person came to ask him a question. "Have you asked anyone else?"…
narrations.summary: Abu Attiyya Hamdaani reports that when a man had already asked Abu Moosa, Ibn Mas'ood gave a contrary answer and left, and Abu Moosa then told people not to ask him anything while this great scholar was present.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sahl bin Abu Khaythamah reports that during the time of Rasulullaah three Sahabah (RA) from the Muhaajireen and three Sahabah (RA) from the Ansaar were authorised…
narrations.summary: Sahl bin Abu Khaythamah reports that in the Prophet's time three Muhaajir Sahabah (Umar, Uthmaan and Ali) and three Ansaar Sahabah (Ubay bin Ka'b, Mu'aadh bin Jabal and Zaid bin Thaabit) were authorised to issue Fataawaa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Masrooq reports that from amongst the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah those who issued Fataawaa were Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Ali Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood…
narrations.summary: Masrooq reports that the Sahabah who issued Fataawaa were Umar, Ali, Ibn Mas'ood, Zaid bin Thaabit, Ubay bin Ka'b and Abu Moosa Ash'ari.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qabeesah bin Duayb bin Halhala reports, "During the time of Hadhrat Umar, Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) remained the chief authority of the judiciary of Madinah,…
narrations.summary: Qabeesah reports that Zaid bin Thaabit held the posts of judge, Fatwa, Qiraa'ah and inheritance in Madinah under Umar, Uthmaan and Ali, and after them until his death in 45 AH; Ataa bin Yasaar reports that Umar and Uthmaan consulted Ibn Abbaas, who issued Fataawaa until he died; Ziyaad bin Meenaa lists the Madinah Fatwa-givers; and Qaasim reports that his aunt Aa'isha issued Fataawaa after Abu Bakr's time.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ left us with so much knowledge that even when a bird fluttered its wings in the sky, it would remind us of something he had…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr says the Prophet left the Sahabah with so much knowledge that even the flutter of a bird's wings in the sky would remind them of something he had taught.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Everything that draws one closer to Jannah and that takes one further from Jahannam has been explained to you (Sahabah…
narrations.summary: Another narration quotes the Prophet saying that everything which brings a person closer to Jannah and further from Jahannam has been explained to the Sahabah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) says, "I have learnt a thousand similitudes from Rasulullaah ﷺ In a lengthy narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Whenever they (the Sahabah…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Al Aas says he learnt a thousand similitudes from the Prophet, and Aa'isha reports that when the Sahabah disagreed her father Abu Bakr settled the matter with Hadiths on where a Nabi is buried and on the inheritance of the Prophets.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "If the knowledge of Umar was placed on one pan of a scale and the knowledge of all on earth was…
narrations.summary: Abu Waa'il reports that Ibn Mas'ood said Umar's knowledge would outweigh all the knowledge on earth, and Ibraheem reports Ibn Mas'ood saying that nine-tenths of knowledge left the world with Umar's death, and Ibn Mas'ood described Umar as the one who knew Allaah best and understood the Deen most deeply.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said, "In comparison to the knowledge of Umar the knowledge of all other people seems like it could be buried in a little hole." A man from Madinah…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah says the knowledge of everyone else is, compared with Umar's, like what could be buried in a small hole, and a man from Madinah says that learned scholars seemed like children before Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ got Hadhrat Ali (RA) married to Hadhrat Faatima (RA), she said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, "You have married me to a man whose…
narrations.summary: Abu Is'haaq reports that when the Prophet married Faatima to Ali, she objected that he had weak eyesight and a large stomach, and the Prophet replied that Ali was the first of his companions to accept Islaam, the most knowledgeable and the most tolerant.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Hadhrat Faatima (RA), "Are you not pleased that 1 have married you to the person who was the first of my Ummah to…
narrations.summary: The Prophet tells Faatima that he has married her to the first of his Ummah to accept Islaam, the most knowledgeable and most tolerant man.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "By Allaah! 1 know precisely about what every verse of the Qur'aan was revealed, where it was revealed and concerning whom it was revealed. My…
narrations.summary: Ali says he knows precisely about which occasion, place and person every verse of the Qur'aan was revealed for, because his Rabb gave him a perceptive heart and an eloquent tongue.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to seek Allaah's protection against any intricate problem which had to be resolved without the help of…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyab reports that Umar used to seek Allaah's protection against any intricate problem that had to be resolved without Ali's help.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "I know the precise circumstances surrounding the revelation of every chapter of the Qur'aan. If I…
narrations.summary: Masrooq reports Ibn Mas'ood's claim to know the occasion of revelation of every chapter of the Qur'aan and Masrooq's own comparison of the Sahabah to dams and Ibn Mas'ood to an ocean; Zaid bin Wahab and Asad bin Wadaa'ah report that Umar called Ibn Mas'ood a coffer filled with knowledge of the Deen and preferred sending him to the people of Qaadisiyyah over keeping him in Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari narrates that they once approached Hadhrat Ali (RA) with the request to inform them about the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ. "Which of them would…
narrations.summary: Abul Bakhtari reports that some men asked Ali about the Sahabah, and Ali described the knowledge of Ibn Mas'ood, Abu Moosa, Ammaar, Hudhayfah, Abu Dharr and Salmaan, and then described his own: whenever he asked the Prophet he received an answer, and when he was silent the Prophet informed him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Mu'aadh bin Jabal is certainly an Ummah who was Qaanit and Haneef (one inclined towards the truth and averse to all false…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says Mu'aadh bin Jabal was an Ummah, Qaanit and Haneef, and not one of the Mushrikeen; when the narrator doubted this against the Qur'aan's description of Ibraheem, Ibn Mas'ood explained that Ummah means one who teaches good and Qaanit one who obeys Allaah and His Rasool, and that this described Mu'aadh.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Masrooq says, "I examined the Sahabah (RA) carefully and found that all their knowledge could be found in six of them; namely Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA),…
narrations.summary: Masrooq says that after examining the Sahabah he found all their knowledge in six of them, and then found that all of it could be found in Ali and Ibn Mas'ood alone.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Masrooq also said, "When I arrived in Madinah and enquired about the Sahabah (RA), I discovered that amongst those with the most profound knowledge was Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Masrooq says that on arriving in Madinah and asking about the Sahabah, he found that Zaid bin Thaabit was among those with the most profound knowledge.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Masrooq reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "If Abdullaah bin Abbaas were our age, none of us would be able to equal even a tenth of his…
narrations.summary: Masrooq reports that Ibn Mas'ood said that if Ibn Abbaas were their age none of them could equal a tenth of his knowledge, and Mujaahid reports that Ibn Abbaas was called an ocean because of how much he knew.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Layth bin Abu Sulaym says that he once said to Hadhrat Tawoos, "Why have you attached yourself to this youngster (Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas instead of the…
narrations.summary: Layth bin Abu Sulaym asks Tawoos why he follows Ibn Abbaas, and Tawoos says seventy Sahabah preferred Ibn Abbaas's opinion; Aamir reports his father Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas praising Ibn Abbaas and Umar deferring to him; Abu Zinaad reports Umar's visit during Ibn Abbaas's fever; Talha praises his understanding; and Ubay bin Ka'b predicts he will become the most learned of the Ummah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir the son of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) reports that his father said, "I have never seen as quick-witted, as intelligent, as knowledgeable and as…
narrations.summary: Aamir, son of Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, reports his father's praise of Abdullaah bin Abbaas for his wit and knowledge, and that Umar would call him for complicated problems and accept his opinion even in front of the Badr veterans.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Zinaad narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) was suffering from high fever when Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) came to visit him. Hadhrat Umar (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abu Zinaad reports that Umar visited the ill Abdullaah bin Abbaas and that Talha praised his understanding; Muhammad bin Ubay bin Ka'b reports that Ubay foretold Ibn Abbaas would become the most learned scholar of the Ummah, since the Prophet had prayed for his understanding of Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tawoos says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) towered above others in knowledge just as a tall palm tree towers above shorter ones."
narrations.summary: Tawoos says Ibn Abbaas towered above others in knowledge as a tall palm tree towers above shorter ones.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il says, "A friend and I performed Hajj at a time when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas was the Ameer of Hajj. When he started reciting Surah Noor and…
narrations.summary: Abu Waa'il reports that when Ibn Abbaas was Ameer of Hajj and recited and commented on Surah Noor, his companion said even the Turks would accept Islaam; Umar praised Ibn Abbaas's answer to a question sent by Ya'la bin Umayyah from Yemen; and Ataa reports that Ibn Abbaas gave each group of questioners - on poetry, ancestry, Arab battles and history - a full answer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) relates, "When I went to Umar bin Khattaab one day, he asked me a question that Ya'la bin Umayyah had written to him about from Yemen.…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas relates that Umar asked him a question that Ya'la bin Umayyah had sent from Yemen; after the answer, Umar testified that Ibn Abbaas was the most eligible to speak on behalf of the Prophet's household.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa says, "While some people used to approach Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas to ask about poetry, others went to him to ask about ancestry and there were still…
narrations.summary: Ataa says people came to Ibn Abbaas to ask about poetry, lineage and the battles and history of the Arabs, and he gave each group a full answer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubadullaah bin Abdullaah bin Utba says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas surpassed all other people in his qualities. He excelled others in his knowledge of past…
narrations.summary: Ubaydullaah bin Abdullaah bin Utba describes the breadth of Ibn Abbaas's knowledge, including the verdicts of Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan, and Ibn Abbaas himself says he questioned senior Muhaajir and Ansaar Sahabah about the Prophet's battles, and that Ubay bin Ka'b told him which Surahs were revealed in Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "I used to remain close to the senior Muhaajireen and Ansaar Sahabah (RA) and ask them about the battles Rasulullaah ﷺ fought and…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas says he stayed close to the senior Muhaajireen and Ansaar to learn about the battles and the revelations concerning them; Ubay bin Ka'b told him that twenty-seven Surahs were revealed at Madinah and the rest at Makkah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ikrama says, "I heard Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) say, 'From all of us, it is Abdullaah bin Abbaas who has the most knowledge of the previous scriptures and also…
narrations.summary: Ikrimah reports that Amr bin Al Aas said Ibn Abbaas had the most knowledge of the earlier scriptures and of what the Qur'aan and Hadith left unclear, and Ibn Abbaas replied that he had that knowledge because he used to ask the Prophet about what was Halaal and Haraam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was once looking at a group of people gathered around Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) during the days of Hajj, asking him about the rites of Hajj.…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says Ibn Abbaas knew the rites of Hajj best of the Sahabah still living, and Jaabir, Raafi bin Khudayj and Ibn Hanafiyyah each lament his death, Ibn Hanafiyyah calling him the sage of this Ummah; Abu Kulthoom reports the last remark.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Dinaar says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) was regarded as one of the young Fuqahaa."
narrations.summary: Amr bin Dinaar says Abdullaah bin Umar was regarded as one of the young Fuqahaa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Ma'daan says, "From amongst the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ, there are none left in Shaam whose knowledge is more dependable, who have a deeper…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Ma'daan says that in Shaam there remained no Sahabi whose knowledge was more reliable, whose understanding was deeper and who was more beloved to the people than Ubaadah bin Saamit and Shaddaad bin Aws.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Handhla bin Sufyaan reports from his teachers that none had a better understanding of the Deen than Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri Sip.
narrations.summary: Handhla bin Sufyaan reports from his teachers that none had a better understanding of the Deen than Abu Sa'eed Khudri.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Za'eeza'a who was Marwaan bin Hakam's scribe reports, "Marwaan once summoned Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) and, seating me behind his chair, he started…
narrations.summary: Abu Za'eeza'a, Marwaan bin Hakam's scribe, reports that Marwaan questioned Abu Hurayrah on the same matters a year apart, seating him behind a screen the second time, and that Abu Hurayrah repeated his answers word for word both times.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) says, "Whenever the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ had doubts about anything, they referred it to Hadhrat Aa'isha and always found the…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports that whenever the Sahabah had doubts they referred them to Aa'isha and always found the answer with her, and Qabeesah bin Dhuwayb says she was among the most knowledgeable.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Salamah says, "I have not seen anyone with more knowledge of the Sunnah practices of Rasulullaah ﷺ than Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) I have also not seen anyone offer…
narrations.summary: Abu Salamah says no one knew the Sunnah better than Aa'isha or gave better opinions, and Masrooq affirms she knew the laws of inheritance, as senior Sahabah consulted her on it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mahmood bin Labeed says, "Although all the pure wives of Rasulullaah knew many Ahadeeth, none knew as much as Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) and Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA).…
narrations.summary: Mahmood bin Labeed says that Aa'isha and Umm Salamah knew the most Ahadeeth of the Prophet's wives, that Aa'isha issued fatwas through the caliphates of Umar and Uthmaan, and that they sent to her to ask about Sunnah practices.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) said, "I have never seen a speaker as well-spoken, as eloquent and as intelligent as Aa'isha.
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya praises Aa'isha's eloquence, and Urwa says she was the most proficient in jurisprudence, poetry, Arab history and medicine, having learnt medicine while treating the Prophet in his illness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) says, "I have not seen a woman as knowledgeable in medicine, Fiqh and poetry as Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA).
narrations.summary: Urwa says he has not seen a woman as knowledgeable in medicine, fiqh and poetry as Aa'isha.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) once said to (his aunt) Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "I am more astonished about you the more I think about you! When I find you to be one of those most…
narrations.summary: Urwa asks his aunt Aa'isha how she came to know fiqh, Arab history, lineage, poetry and medicine; she says she learnt medicine from the remedies that physicians sent when the Prophet's illness worsened.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that she said, "When I used these to treat Rasulullaah ﷺ, I learnt all about it."
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says that by using these remedies to treat the Prophet she learnt all about them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said to his students, "Be people who are the fountainheads of knowledge, who are beacons of guidance, who spend most of the time…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood tells his students to be fountainheads of knowledge and lanterns of the night who stay unknown on earth but known in the heavens, and a similar report from Ali is given.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Wahab bin Munabbih narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas was informed that some people were debating about predestination at Baab Bani Sahm, he quickly…
narrations.summary: Wahab bin Munabbih reports that Ibn Abbaas, on hearing a group debating predestination, went to them and described the scholars who are devoted to Allaah and fear Him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood ig said, "If the men of knowledge would safeguard their knowledge and give it only to those who are worthy, they would lead the people of…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says that scholars who hand their knowledge to worldly people for a share of the world fall in the eyes of the people, and quotes the Prophet that whoever makes the Aakhirah his only worry, Allaah will take care of his other worries.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sufyaan bin Uyaynah reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "if the bearers of knowledge uphold it as it ought to be upheld and in a befitting…
narrations.summary: Sufyaan bin Uyaynah reports Ibn Abbaas saying that scholars who uphold knowledge properly are loved by Allaah, His angels and the pious and held in awe by people, while those who seek worldly wealth with it are detested by Allaah and lose their standing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "What will happen to you when such a calamity overtakes you because of which your youngsters start to age, your elders grow older…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood warns of a time when fabricated Sunnahs become the norm and resisting change is treated as heresy, when the trustworthy and the Fuqahaa become few, and when knowledge is sought for worldly motives.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) said, "You should understand well that these Ahadeeth ought to be learnt solely for the pleasure of Allaah. When a person learns them solely for…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr says Ahadeeth must be learnt only for Allaah's pleasure; Ka'b says greed and begging remove knowledge from scholars' hearts, and Ali names seeking the Deen for worldly motives as a sign of the end of time, in answer to Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once addressed the people saying, "I fear two people for you, the person who misinterprets the Qur'aan and a person who is vying with his brother for…
narrations.summary: Umar tells the people he fears two kinds of person for the Ummah: one who misinterprets the Qur'aan, and one who vies with his brother for kingship.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that when a delegation from Basrah that included Hadhrat Ahnaf bin Qais (RA) came to Hadhrat Umar (RA), he granted them all leave, except for…
narrations.summary: Hasan narrates that Umar kept Ahnaf bin Qais back for a year when a delegation from Basrah came to him, then explained that he had feared the eloquent hypocrite and was now confident Ahnaf was not one.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that he heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) say from the pulpit, "Beware of the hypocritical Aalim." "How will a hypocrite become an Aalim?" the…
narrations.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that Umar warned from the pulpit against the hypocritical Aalim, defined as one who speaks what is right but does what is wrong.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) also said, "We always maintained that the one to destroy this Ummah will be a hypocrite with an educated tongue."
narrations.summary: Umar says he always maintained that the one who will destroy this Ummah is a hypocrite with an educated tongue.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that he heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) say from the pulpit, "What I fear most for this Ummah is the hypocritical Aalim." "How will a hypocrite…
narrations.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports Umar's sermon that what he fears most for the Ummah is the hypocritical Aalim, whose tongue is educated but whose heart and actions are ignorant.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said, "Beware of the places of tribulation!" "O Abu Abdullaah!" someone asked, "What are the places of tribulation?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah warns against the places of tribulation, and Ibn Mas'ood identifies them as the doors of rulers, where a scholar confirms the rulers' lies and praises them, losing his Deen for their wealth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "At the doors of the rulers lie tribulations just as certainly as there are camels at the place where camels rest. I swear by the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood warns that frequenting the doors of rulers brings tribulation and that the Deen is lost in exchange for their wealth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik Ashja'ee (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ looked to the sky one day and said, "(There shall come) A time when Deeni knowledge will be lifted (off…
narrations.summary: Awf bin Maalik reports that the Prophet said Deeni knowledge will be lifted, and when Labeed and Ziyaad bin Labeed ask how, Shaddaad bin Aws explains that devotion will be the first thing to go.

narrations.excerpt: A similar narration from Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Of what benefit was the Torah and the Injeel that were with the Jews and the…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa reports the Prophet asking what benefit the Torah and Injeel were to the Jews and Christians.

narrations.excerpt: A narration from Hadhrat Wahshi (RA) mentions that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "They (the Jews and Christians) did not pay any attention to it (their scriptures)." (S) Yet…
narrations.summary: Wahshi reports the Prophet saying the Jews and Christians paid no attention to their scriptures, and Ibn Labeed reports him saying they gained no benefit from them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once asked, "Do you know how islaam will dwindle?" The people replied, "Just as the dye on clothing fades or as an animal loses its fat…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says that the most serious cause of Islaam dwindling will be the death of the Ulema.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib says, "I attended the funeral of Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit. After he had been buried, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "O you people!…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that after Zaid bin Thaabit was buried, Ibn Abbaas said that a great deal of knowledge had just left them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ammaar bin Abu Ammaar says, "When Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) passed away, we sat with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) in the shade of a building. He said,…
narrations.summary: Ammaar bin Abu Ammaar reports that Ibn Abbaas, sitting by Zaid bin Thaabit's grave, pointed to it and said knowledge leaves when its bearers die, and gives variant wordings of this.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "I strongly believe that it is by committing sins that a man forgets the knowledge he once learnt."
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says that a man forgets the knowledge he once learnt because of the sins he commits.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaasim reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "The problem with knowledge is forgetting." (S)
narrations.summary: Qaasim reports that Ibn Mas'ood said the problem with knowledge is forgetting it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said to them, "We have been given this knowledge to bear and we therefore pass it on to you even…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports Hudhayfah saying that they were given this knowledge to bear and pass on, even though they do not practise it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa, he said, "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from four things; from knowledge that is not beneficial,…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet's du'aa seeking refuge from knowledge that does not benefit, a heart that does not submit, a soul never satiated, and a du'aa that is not answered.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thowbaan (RA) narrates that they were once on a journey with Rasulullaah ﷺ when some of the Muhaajireen said, "If only we knew what type of wealth is good now…
narrations.summary: Thowbaan reports that when the Muhaajireen asked which wealth is best, Umar offered to ask the Prophet, who said the best is a tongue that engages in dhikr, a grateful heart and a believing wife.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ thrice repeated the words, "Destruction to gold! Destruction to silver!" This he said after Allaah had revealed narration. the…
narrations.summary: Ali reports the Prophet repeating a warning against hoarding gold and silver after the verse on them was revealed, which prompted the Sahabah to ask what wealth to keep and led Umar to offer to ask.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was travelling on the road to Makkah when he passed by a mountain called Humdaan. Rasulullaah then said, "This is…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet, passing Humdaan on the road to Makkah, said the Mufarriddoon are in the lead, and explained that they are those who engage abundantly in dhikr.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when the Sahabah (RA) asked who the Mufarridoon were, Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Those who are intoxicated by the Dhikr of Allaah. Dhikr then…
narrations.summary: Another narration has the Prophet describing the Mufarriddoon as those intoxicated with Allaah's dhikr, which unburdens them of sins so they meet Allaah without a burden on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) reports that as they were once travelling with Rasulullaah ﷺ, he asked, "Where are those in the lead?" The Sahabah (RA) replied, "While…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal reports that the Prophet asked where those in the lead are, and said they are those intoxicated with Allaah's dhikr, and that whoever wishes to eat from the gardens of Jannah should engage in dhikr abundantly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once asked, "Which of Allaah's servants shall have the highest status with Allaah on the Day of Qiyaamah?"…
narrations.summary: Several reports say the Prophet named those who engage most in dhikr as the highest in rank, the most rewarded and the most saved from Jahannam, above jihaad, and Abu Bakr told Umar that the people of dhikr had taken all the good, which the Prophet confirmed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Anas (RA) narrates that someone once asked Rasulullaah ﷺ which form of Jihaad carried the most reward. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "(The Jihaad of) Those…
narrations.summary: Asked which jihaad carries most reward, the Prophet said it is the jihaad of those who engage most in dhikr, and a man is told to keep his tongue moist with the dhikr of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maalik bin Makhaamir reports that Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) once said to them, "The last words with which I parted from Rasulullaah glUH- (as I left for…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal recounts that the last advice the Prophet gave him when he left for Yemen was that the most beloved deed to Allaah is to die with the tongue moist with dhikr.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) asked, "Tell me which deed is best and which takes one closest to Allaah."
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh asks the Prophet which deed is best and closest to Allaah, and the narration is cut off before the answer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Do not preoccupy yourself with discussing people because it is a cause of misfortune. You had rather engage constantly in the Dhikr of Allaah."
narrations.summary: Umar advises against discussing people and urges constant dhikr of Allaah as a cure, and Uthmaan says that if their hearts were pure they would never tire of dhikr.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Engage assiduously in the Dhikr of Allaah because it is a cure. At the same time, avoid discussing people because…
narrations.summary: Umar says to engage in the dhikr of Allaah because it is a cure, and to avoid discussing people because it is a disease.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) said, "Had our hearts been pure, we would never tire with the Dhikr of Allaah."
narrations.summary: Uthmaan says that had their hearts been pure they would never tire of the dhikr of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Engage abundantly in the Dhikr of Allaah and it matters not if you do not associate with anyone apart from those who can assist…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood urges abundant dhikr of Allaah, saying it does not matter if one keeps company only with those who can help in dhikr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) once said that if a man spends an entire night giving away slave women with fair complexions and another man spends the night reciting the Book of…
narrations.summary: Salmaan says that a man who spends the night reciting the Book of Allaah and engaging in dhikr is better than one who spends it giving away fair-complexioned slave women.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ahmad bin Habeeb bin Ubayd narrates that a man approached Hadhrat Abu Dardaa and asked for some advice. Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "Remember Allaah during…
narrations.summary: Ahmad bin Habeeb reports that Abu Dardaa advised a man to remember Allaah in ease so that Allaah remembers him in hardship, and to consider how soon worldly things pass.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once said, "Shall I not inform you of the best of all deeds, which is most beloved to your Master and will elevate your rank the most? It is…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says the best deed is the dhikr of Allaah, better than jihaad or giving gold and silver in charity, and that those whose tongues are moist with dhikr will enter Jannah laughing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) said, "A person can do no action more effective in saving himself from Allaah's punishment than engaging in Allaah's Dhikr." "O Abu Abdur…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal says dhikr saves a person from Allaah's punishment more than any deed, even jihaad unless the sword breaks, and Abdullaah bin Amr says dhikr morning and evening is better than breaking swords or giving large sums in charity.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I prefer sitting with a group of people engaged in Allaah's Dhikr between Fajr and sunrise to setting free four…
narrations.summary: Anas reports the Prophet preferring to sit with people engaged in Allaah's dhikr between Fajr and sunrise, and between Asr and sunset, over freeing four slaves each time.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) also narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "The person who performs his Asr salaah and then remains sitting to dictate words of worth until the evening is…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet said sitting in dhikr from Asr until evening is better than freeing eight slaves from the progeny of Ismaa'eel.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I prefer sitting with a group of people engaged in Allaah's Dhikr between Fajr and sunrise to everything upon which the…
narrations.summary: The Prophet said he prefers sitting with people engaged in Allaah's dhikr between Fajr and sunrise to everything the sun rises upon.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sahl bin Sa'd Saa'idi (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "More than providing thoroughbred horses to be used in the path of Allaah, I would love to rather…
narrations.summary: Sahal bin Sa'd reports that the Prophet said he would rather attend Fajr and then sit in dhikr until sunrise than provide thoroughbred horses for the path of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I prefer sitting (to engage in Allaah's Dhikr) from the time of the Fajr salaah until sunrise to…
narrations.summary: Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib reports that the Prophet said sitting in dhikr from Fajr until sunrise is preferred to freeing four slaves.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I prefer performing the Fajr salaah and then sitting to engage in Allaah's Dhikr until sunrise'rather than racing a…
narrations.summary: The Prophet said he prefers praying Fajr and then sitting in Allaah's dhikr until sunrise over racing a horse in the path of Allaah until sunrise.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Rather than having everything over which the sun rises, I prefer reciting 'Subhaanallaah', 'Al Hamdulillaah',…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet said he prefers reciting Subhaanallaah, Al Hamdulillaah, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah and Allaahu Akbar over everything the sun rises upon.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I prefer sitting and reciting 'Allaahu Akbar', 'Al Hamdulillaah', 'Subhaanallaah', and 'Laa Ilaaha Illallaah'…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah reports two versions of the Prophet preferring the reciting of the four phrases of dhikr to freeing slaves from the progeny of Ismaa'eel, one version counting two slaves and the other four.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Rather than providing thoroughbred horses (for Jihaad) from morning to night, I prefer engaging in the Dhikr of Aliaah from…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says he prefers engaging in Allaah's dhikr from morning to night over providing thoroughbred horses for jihaad from morning to night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says, "It was difficult for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) to say anything that was not the Dhikr of Aliaah."
narrations.summary: Abu Ubaydah bin Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says it was difficult for Abdullaah bin Mas'ood to say anything other than the dhikr of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that it would upset Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood to hear anyone talking between dawn and the Fajr salaah. Yet another narration states that it…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood disliked talk between dawn and Fajr and, after Fajr, told people chatting in the masjid either to pray or to stay silent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "I love more to recite 'Allaahu Akbar' a hundred times than spending a hundred gold coins in Sadaqah."
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says he loves saying Allaahu Akbar a hundred times more than giving a hundred gold coins in charity, and Mu'aadh bin Jabal says he prefers dhikr from morning to night over providing horses for jihaad.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) said, "Rather than providing thoroughbred horses (for Jihaad) in the path of Aliaah from morning to night, I prefer engaging in the Dhikr…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal says he prefers the dhikr of Allaah from morning to night over providing thoroughbred horses for jihaad.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) reports that they were on a journey with Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) when he heard people talking and having eloquent discussions. "O…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that Abu Moosa, hearing people talk eloquently, asked why people neglect the Aakhirah, and answered that the world is before them while the Aakhirah is still to come.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Abdullaah bin Raafi reports that he was once present in a gathering with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far and Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Abdullaah bin Raafi reports a gathering where Abdullaah bin Abu Umayrah relayed Mu'aadh bin Jabal's report that the Prophet said one of two phrases rises to the Throne and the other fills the space between heaven and earth, and Abdullaah bin Umar wept on hearing it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jareeri reports, "When Hadhrat Anas (RA) entered into the state of Ihraam from Dhaatul Irq, we heard him say nothing other than the Dhikr of Allaah until he came…
narrations.summary: Jareeri reports that when Anas entered Ihraam from Dhaatul Irq he spoke nothing but the dhikr of Allaah until he came out of Ihraam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates from Rasulullaah (Mi that on the Day of Qiyaamah, Allaah will say, "The people of this assembly will soon learn who the people of…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri narrates that on the Day of Qiyaamah Allaah will say the people of this assembly will soon learn who the people of honour are, and the Prophet said they are those who take part in gatherings of dhikr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched an expedition to Najd that won a large booty and returned very quickly. Someone who was not part of the…
narrations.summary: Umar narrates that the Prophet said people who attend Fajr and then stay in dhikr until sunrise return sooner, with greater reward, than an expedition that had just come back from Najd with booty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Sahl bin Hunayf narrates that Rasulullaah was in one of his rooms when Allaah revealed the verse-. Rasulullaah ﷺ Restrain yourself with (in the…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Sahl bin Hunayf narrates that when the verse of Surah Kahf 28 was revealed the Prophet went out to find people engaged in dhikr, sat with them, and praised Allaah for placing such people among his Ummah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha (RA) as he was busy advising some of his companions.…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas narrates that the Prophet passed Abdullaah bin Rawaaha while he was advising companions, recited Surah Kahf 28 to them, and said that angels say the same dhikr as those gathered and that Allaah forgives them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thaabit Bunaani narrates that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) was part of a group engaged in Dhikr when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed by. When they stopped, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked them…
narrations.summary: Thaabit Bunaani narrates that when the Prophet passed a group engaged in dhikr that included Salmaan, he told them to continue and said Allaah's mercy was descending on them so he wished to join them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came to them and said, "O people! Verily Allaah has many groups of angels who descend and remain with the gatherings…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that the Prophet said angels attend gatherings of dhikr, that such gatherings are the gardens of Jannah, and that Allaah treats a servant according to the esteem in which the servant holds Him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Samurah (RA) reports that after performing the Fajr salaah, Rasulullaah ﷺ used to sit and remain engaged in Dhikr until sunrise.
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Samurah reports that after the Fajr salaah the Prophet used to sit engaged in dhikr until sunrise.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) narrates that he once asked Rasulullaah ﷺ what the rewards would be for the gatherings of Dhikr. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "The rewards for…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr asked the Prophet what the reward for gatherings of dhikr would be, and he replied that it is Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "The gatherings of Dhikr are the life of knowledge and create humility in the heart."
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says gatherings of dhikr are the life of knowledge and create humility in the heart.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that after every gathering and salaah, Rasulullaah ﷺ used to say something. When I asked him about it, he said, 'If what you spoke was good,…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha asked the Prophet what he said after every gathering and salaah, and he explained that the words seal the good that was said and expiate the bad; Abu Barzah reports that the Prophet recited them at the end of every gathering.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Barzah (RA) reports that at the end of every gathering just before he stood up, Rasulullaah ﷺ would recite: 'You are Pure, O Allaah and it is Your praises…
narrations.summary: Abu Barzah reports the words the Prophet recited at the end of every gathering, which he said are an expiation for the sins of that gathering.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes the du'aa with additional words: 'You are Pure, O Allaah and it is Your praises that we sing. . I .testify there is none worthy of worship but…
narrations.summary: A longer version of the du'aa said at the end of a gathering, adding a request for forgiveness for having sinned and wronged oneself, because none but Allaah forgives sins.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awwa'am (RA) reports that they once said, "O Rasulullaah When we leave your gatherings, we find that we start discussing matters of the Period of…
narrations.summary: Zubayr bin Awwaam reports that the Companions said they fall into talk of the Period of Ignorance after gatherings, and the Prophet advised reciting the du'aa at the end of a gathering to atone for what was said in it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas said, "There are certain words that, if recited thrice after a gathering, will atone for anything wrong said in the gathering,…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr says that certain words, recited three times after any gathering, atone for wrong said in it and seal it, as a letter is sealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates that when he once asked Rasulullaah ﷺ for advice, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Hold fast to Taqwa because it is the basis of every act." "When…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr asked the Prophet for advice and was told to hold fast to taqwa, and then to be particular about reciting the Qur'aan, which is a light for him on earth and a treasure in the heavens.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aws bun Hudhayfah Thaqafi (RA) says, "When we came to Rasulullaah as a delegation from the Thaqeef, those of us who belonged to the Ahlaaf stayed with Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Aws bin Hudhayfah describes the Thaqeef delegation's stay in Madinah, when the Prophet came to them late one night because he had not finished his daily portion of the Qur'aan, and his companions explained how he divided the Qur'aan into seven portions.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mughiera bin Shu'ba (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once at a place between Makkah and Madinah when a man sought permission to see him. Rasulullaah ﷺ (did…
narrations.summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba narrates that when a man asked to see the Prophet between Makkah and Madinah, the Prophet delayed granting permission because he had not finished his daily portion of the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Salamah reports that when Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) used to say to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA), "Remind us about our Rabb", he would start reciting…
narrations.summary: Abu Salamah reports that when Umar asked Abu Moosa Ash'ari to remind them of their Rabb, Abu Moosa would begin reciting the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Habeeb bin Abu Marzooq says, "The report reached us that Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari used to recite the Qur'aan in a most excellent voice and would do so when…
narrations.summary: Reports of Umar's love for Qur'aan recitation: Abu Moosa Ash'ari recited beautifully when Umar asked him to remind them of their Rabb, and when told it was time for salaah Umar said they were already in salaah; Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Umar would open the Qur'aan and recite when he entered his house.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) used to say, "I notlike a single day or night to pass without looking into the of Allaah i,e. to recite the Qur'aan by looking into it."
narrations.summary: Uthmaan says he does not like a single day or night to pass without looking into the Qur'aan and reciting it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) also said, "Had your hearts been pure, you would never get enough of the speech of Allaah.
narrations.summary: Uthmaan says that had our hearts been pure we would never get enough of the speech of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan says, "Ameerul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) said, 'Had our hearts been pure, we would never get enough of the speech of Allaah and I would not…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports Uthmaan's saying that had hearts been pure they would never tire of Allaah's speech, that he never let a day pass without looking into the Qur'aan, and that the pages of his Qur'aan were worn out by the time of his death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Always look into the Qur'aan (when reciting because it facilitates easier contemplation)."
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says to always look into the Qur'aan while reciting, because it makes contemplation easier.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Habeeb bin Shaheed narrates that when Hadhrat Naafi was asked about what Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) used to do at home, he replied, "Something that others…
narrations.summary: Habeeb bin Shaheed narrates, through Naafi, that Abdullaah bin Umar made wudu for every salaah and recited Qur'aan between salaahs; Ibn Abu Mulaykah reports that Ikrama bin Abu Jahal placed the Qur'aan on his face and wept.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "The reward of ten good deeds are recorded every time'a person sends salutations to Nabi ﷺ. Now, when any of you returns home from…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says that each letter of the Qur'aan recited brings ten good deeds, and that each salutation sent upon the Prophet also brings ten rewards; a second version explains that Alif, Laam and Meem each count for ten rather than the three letters together.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir Juhani (RA) narrates that he once met Rasulullaah who said to him, "O Uqba bin Aamir! Maintain ties of kinship with those who sever them, give to…
narrations.summary: Uqba bin Aamir narrates that the Prophet advised him to keep ties with those who sever them, give to those who deprive him and forgive those who wrong him, and then taught him to recite Surahs Ikhlaas, Falaq and Naas every night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ lay down to sleep, he would place his palms next to each other, recite Surah Ikhlaas and Surah Falaq and then…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that when the Prophet lay down to sleep he blew into his palms after reciting Surahs Ikhlaas and Falaq, then wiped over his body, and that when his illness intensified he asked her to do this for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ would not go to sleep until he had recited Surah Alif Laam Meem Sajdah and Surah Mulk. Hadhrat Tawoos mentioned that these…
narrations.summary: Jaabir, Irbaadh and Aa'isha report that the Prophet did not sleep until he had recited particular Surahs, and Tawoos comments on the virtue of those Surahs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ would not go to sleep until he had recited Surah Zumar and Surah Bani Israa'eel.
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet would not sleep until he had recited Surah Zumar and Surah Bani Israa'eel.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Farwah bin Naufal (RA) reports that he once approached Rasulullaah with the request, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Teach me something to recite when I lie down to sleep."…
narrations.summary: Farwah bin Naufal asks the Prophet for something to recite on going to sleep, and the Prophet names Surah Kaafiroon as an exoneration from Shirk.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "When the angels of punishment approach a person in the grave from his feet, the feet will say, You have no approach from our…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that Surah Mulk protects its reciter from punishment in the grave and that reciting it at night is a great virtue.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration briefly states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Allaah will protect from the punishment in the grave every person who recites Surah Mulk…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood repeats that Surah Mulk protects from the punishment of the grave, and Umar says that whoever recites Baqarah, Aal Imraan and Nisaa in one night is counted among the obedient.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "The person who recites Surah Baqarah, Surah Aal Imraan and Surah Nisaa in a single night shall be recorded as one of the obedient ones."
narrations.summary: Umar says that whoever recites Surah Baqarah, Aal Imraan and Nisaa in a single night is recorded among the obedient.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jubayr bin Mut'im ii narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to him, "O Jubayr! When you travel on a journey, would you like your position to be the best from all…
narrations.summary: Jubayr bin Mut'im reports that the Prophet taught him to recite the last five surahs on journeys, after which he always had the best position and the most provisions.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Khubayb (RA) narrates, "It was an extremely dark and rainy night when we went out in search of Rasulullaah ﷺ to lead us in salaah. When we met him,…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Khubayb says that on a dark rainy night, when the Companions went out to find the Prophet to lead salaah, the Prophet told him to recite Surah Ikhlaas and the Mu'awwadhatayn three times each morning and evening for protection.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "When a person recites Ikhlaas) ten times after the Fajr salaah, he will commit no sin all of that day even though Shaytaan may try his utmost (to…
narrations.summary: Ali says that whoever recites Surah Ikhlaas ten times after Fajr salaah will commit no sin that day, even if Shaytaan tries hard to make him sin.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was on the wooden step of that pulpit when I heard him say, "When a person recites Aayatul Kursi after every salaah, there is…
narrations.summary: Ali reports the Prophet saying that reciting Aayatul Kursi after every salaah leaves nothing but death between a person and Jannah, and that reciting it at bedtime protects his house and those around it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) also said, "I do not think that, a person born as a Muslim or who has any intelligence would ever spend the night without reciting the verse (Aayatul…
narrations.summary: Ali says that no person with understanding should spend the night without reciting Aayatul Kursi, which was given to the Prophet from the treasures beneath the Throne, and that he himself recites it three times each night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "I do not think that a person who has any intelligence would ever spend the night without reciting the concluding verses of Surah Baqarah because…
narrations.summary: Ali says that no person with understanding should spend the night without reciting the final verses of Surah Baqarah, which come from the treasures beneath the Throne.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) said, "Whoever recites the concluding verses of Surah Aal Imraan at night shall receive the reward of spending the night in Ibaadah."
narrations.summary: Uthmaan says that whoever recites the final verses of Surah Aal Imraan at night receives the reward of spending the night in worship.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "If a person recites ten verses of Surah Baqarah in his home, no Shaytaan shall ever enter that home all night. The verses are…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says that reciting ten verses of Surah Baqarah at home keeps Shaytaan from entering that home all night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) had two silos of dates and in keeping check on them, he discovered that the dates were decreasing. When he stood on guard one night, he…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b catches a jinn stealing from his dates, and the jinn tells him that Aayatul Kursi protects people from jinn from evening until morning and from morning until evening; Ubay reports this to the Prophet, who confirms the jinn spoke the truth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr (RA) says, "When I left Hims, the night gave me shelter on a piece of ground where the Jinn of the area came to me. I however recited the verse…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Busr says that when jinn came to him at night near Hims, he recited a verse of Surah A'raaf, and they kept watch over him until morning.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Alaa bin Jalaaj once said to his sons, "When you place me to rest in my grave, please say.- 'In the name of Allaah and upon the creed of Rasulullaah ﷺ Thereafter,…
narrations.summary: Alaa bin Jalaaj asks his sons to recite the beginning and end of Surah Baqarah at his grave, as he saw Abdullaah bin Umar do; and Ali says that reciting Surah Saaffaat verses 180 to 182 three times weighs one's deeds on a large scale.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr narrates that whenever Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf entered his house, he would recite Aayatul Kursi in all the corners of the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr reports that whenever Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf entered his house, he recited Aayatul Kursi in every corner of it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that he once asked Rasulullaah ﷺ, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Who will be most fortunate to receive your intercession on the Day of Qiyaamah?" "O…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah asks the Prophet who will be most fortunate to receive his intercession, and the Prophet answers whoever says Laa Ilaaha Illallaah with complete sincerity; Zaid bin Arqam and Abu Sa'eed Khudri add reports on the same Kalimah, and Abu Sa'eed also reports Moosa's request to Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zadi bin Arqam (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Whoever recites Ilaaha Illallaah') with sincerity shall enter Jannah." Someone asked, "What is meant by…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Arqam reports that whoever recites the Kalimah with sincerity enters Jannah, and Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports Allaah's answer to Musa that the Kalimah outweighs the seven heavens and earths.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Allaah said, "If all the seven heavens and their inhabitants apart from Myself together with the seven earths are placed on one pan of the…
narrations.summary: Another narration quotes Allaah saying that Laa Ilaaha Illallaah placed on one side of a scale would outweigh the seven heavens, their inhabitants and the seven earths on the other.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "Should I not inform you of the advice that Hadhrat Nooh (RA) gave to his sons?" When the Sahabah…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's account of the advice Nooh gave his sons, to affirm Laa Ilaaha Illallaah and the tasbeeh of Azeem wa Bihamdihi and to avoid Shirk and pride, and the Prophet explains that pride is looking down on others.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "If the heavens and the earth and everything they contain were made into a ring and (iiil Ilaaha placed on top of it, it…
narrations.summary: The Prophet says that if the heavens, the earth and everything in them were made into a ring with the Kalimah placed on top, it would shatter them all.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ya'la bin Shaddaad reports, "Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) was also present to confirm the report of my father Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Aws when he said, "We were…
narrations.summary: Ya'la bin Shaddaad reports, confirmed by Ubaadah bin Saamit, that his father Shaddaad bin Aws reported the Prophet having the Companions raise their hands and recite Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, and then giving them glad tidings that Allaah had forgiven them all.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates that when he once requested Rasulullaah for advice, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "When you commit a sin, follow it up with a good deed to erase…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr asks the Prophet for advice and is told to follow a sin with a good deed to erase it; when Abu Dharr asks whether a particular recitation is a good deed, the Prophet calls it the best of all good deeds.

narrations.excerpt: When Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) once saw some people reciting •sliJiiV) (jliiijui)('Allaahu Akbar'), he exclaimed, "That's it! I swear by the Rabb of the Kabah!…
narrations.summary: Umar says that when he saw people reciting Allaahu Akbar, it was the word of Taqwa that the Sahabah deserved most.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) also stated that it was the Kalimah i!ijv)that Allaah refers to in the verse: ...and Allaah stuck the word of Taqwa onto them... (Surah Fatah, verse 26)
narrations.summary: Ali says that the word of Taqwa mentioned in Surah Fath verse 26 is the Kalimah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that the words ('Allaahu Akbar') are also part of the 'word of Taqwa'. Dhikr of, ('Al HamduMlaah)/lijito) (Laa Ilaaha Illallaah), Jjbi) Akbar) and…
narrations.summary: A further narration says that Allaahu Akbar is also part of the word of Taqwa, and lists other formulas of dhikr that go with it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to them, "Carry out the everlasting good deeds in abundance." When someone asked Rasulullaah ﷺ what…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that the Prophet called Allaahu Akbar, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, Al Hamdulillaah and Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Ilia Billaah the everlasting good deeds.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Take up your shields." "O Rasulullaah ﷺ the Sahabah (RA) asked, "Has the enemy come?" "No," Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet told the Companions to take up their shields, meaning Al Hamdulillaah and Allaahu Akbar, which protect against Jahannam and go before and behind them on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ mentioned, "They are the saviours." Yet another narration adds the words (Jju-iuy %) ('Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Ilia…
narrations.summary: Another narration quotes the Prophet calling the same formulas the saviours, and adds Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Ilia Billaah.

narrations.excerpt: A narration from Hadhrat Anas (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Verily they shall be ahead of you, they are the saviours, they shall be behind and they are the…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet described the same formulas as going before and behind people, as saviours, and as everlasting good deeds.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "Does any of you have the ability to do actions as huge as Mount Uhud every day?" "O Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Imraan bin Husayn reports that the Prophet asked whether anyone could do deeds as large as Mount Uhud every day, and then said that Subhaanallaah, Al Hamdulillaah, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah and Allaahu Akbar each weigh more than Mount Uhud.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that he was busy planting something when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed by. "O Abu Hurayrah!" Rasulullaah ﷺ called out, "What are you planting?"…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah says that when the Prophet passed him while he was planting, the Prophet told him that Al Hamdulillaah, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah and Allaahu Akbar are better plants, and that a tree is planted in Jannah for each one said.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "When you pass through the gardens of Jannah, eat to your fill there." "O Rasulullaah the Sahabah (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet saying that the gardens of Jannah are the masjids, and that one eats one's fill there by reciting Al Hamdulillaah, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah and Allaahu Akbar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once caught hold of a branch and shook it, but the leaves did not fall off. When he shook it again, the leaves still did not…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet shook a branch three times, its leaves falling only on the third, and then said that Al Hamdulillaah, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah and Allaahu Akbar shake off sins as leaves fall from a tree.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) narrates that a Bedouin once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ with the request, "Do teach me something that I may recite." Rasulullaah ﷺ told him…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that a Bedouin asked the Prophet to teach him something to recite, and the Prophet taught him a prayer for forgiveness, mercy, guidance, provision and safety, and said that the Bedouin left with his hands full of good.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to him, "Should I not inform you of those words that Allaah loves most?" "O Rasulullaah (Sep!" Hadhrat Abu…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr reports that the Prophet named Subhaanallaahi wa Bihamdihi as the words most loved by Allaah, and other narrations give variant wordings of the same answer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Whoever says illjv) (iili VJ('Laa Ilaaha Illallaah') shall enter Jannah or (Rasulullaah ﷺ said) Jannah shall…
narrations.summary: Abu Talha reports that the Prophet said whoever says Laa Ilaaha Illallaah enters Jannah, and that reciting Subhaanallaahi wa Bihamdihi a hundred times earns a great number of good deeds, though the Companions' deeds still need Allaah's mercy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once asked, "Is any of you unable to earn the reward of a thousand good deeds every day?" One of the Sahabah (RA) sitting…
narrations.summary: Sa'd (RA) reports that the Prophet asked whether anyone could not earn a thousand good deeds each day, and said that reciting a formula a hundred times earns a thousand good deeds or erases a thousand sins.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) relates, "My father placed me in the care of Rasulullaah ﷺ to be of service to him. One day after I had performed two Rakaahs…
narrations.summary: Qais bin Sa'd bin Ubaadah says that after he had prayed two rakaahs, the Prophet nudged him with his foot and told him that reciting Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Ilia Billaah is a door of Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates, "I had been walking behind Rasulullaah when he said to me, 'Should I not inform you of a treasure from amongst the treasures of Jannah?'…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr reports that while he was walking behind the Prophet, the Prophet told him that reciting Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Ilia Billaah is a treasure of Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas narrates that Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob Ansaari once said to him, "Should I not teach you some words that Rasulullaah ﷺ taught me?"…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari told him the Prophet had named abundant recitation of Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Ilia Billaah as a treasure of Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was taken on the journey of Mi'raaj, he passed by Hadhrat Ibraheem (RA), who asked, "Who is "this with…
narrations.summary: Abu Ayyoob Ansaari reports that on the Mi'raaj the Prophet passed Ibraheem, who told him to urge his Ummah to plant plenty of the plants of Jannah, which are the words Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Ilia Billaah.

narrations.excerpt: Another adds that before addressing Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat ibraheem (RA) first greeted Rasulullaah ﷺ and welcomed him.
narrations.summary: Hadhrat Ibraheem (RA) greeted the Prophet before addressing him and welcomed him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Whoever says has thought of Allaah, whoever says ('Al Hamdulillaah') has thanked Allaah, whoever ('Allaahu Akbar') has revered…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas explains the reward of saying Subhaanallaah, Al Hamdulillaah, Allaahu Akbar, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah and Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Illa Billaah, which become an adornment and treasure for the speaker in Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mutarraf reports that Hadhrat Imraan (RA) once said to him, "Should I not inform you of a Hadith today which Allaah will make a source of benefit for you even…
narrations.summary: Mutarraf reports that Imraan bin Husayn told him that the best of Allaah's bondsmen on the Day of Qiyaamah will be those who praised Him most excessively.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked, "While we know what is meant by (jjbi) ('Subhaanallaah') andvjiljv) (illi ('Laa Ilaaha…
narrations.summary: Umar asked what is meant by the phrases Subhaanallaah, Al Hamdulillaah and Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, and Ali replied that Allaah chose them for Himself and loves them to be said; a second report has Ibn Kawwaa asking Ali about Subhaanallaah, and Ali said it proclaims Allaah's purity from all evil.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dhabyaan narrates that Ibn Kawwaa once asked Hadhrat Ali (RA) about the phrase (Uii) ('Subhaanallaah'), to which Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied, "It is a phrase…
narrations.summary: Ibn Kawwaa asks Ali about the phrase Subhaanallaah, and Ali explains it is a phrase Allaah chose for Himself to proclaim His purity from all evil.

narrations.excerpt: When Hadhrat Umar ig) once had two men lashed, one of them said, "jJ-j) wbi ('Bismillaah')" while the other said " ('Subhaanallaah')". Hadhrat Umar exclaimed, "Shame on…
narrations.summary: Umar eases the lashing of one of two men he had flogged, because that man was saying tasbeeh, which can only find a place in the heart of a believer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) Interprets the verse "The Pure Word climbs up to Him" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "Whenever I relate a Hadith to you,…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood explains that when a person recites the tasbeeh and dhikr words an angel carries them up to the heavens, and he cites the verse that the pure word rises to Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat juwayriyyah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once left. her room and when he returned after midmorning, he found her still sitting where she was. Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: The Prophet told Juwayriyyah that four phrases he recited three times after leaving her would outweigh all the dhikr she had done since morning, and gave the wording of the dhikr in its variant forms.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) reports that when he once accompanied Rasulullaah ﷺ to see a particular lady, they found her reciting Tasbeeh, using some date seeds or…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that when he went with the Prophet to see a woman, they found her counting tasbeeh on date seeds or pebbles, and the Prophet taught her easier phrases to say instead.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ saw him moving his lips one day, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "O Abu Umaamah! What are you reciting causing your lips to…
narrations.summary: The Prophet taught Abu Umaamah a long dhikr praising and glorifying Allaah in measures covering all He has created, all that fills the earth and heavens, and all that His Book counts, and told him to teach it to everyone.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ saw him moving his lips one day, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "O Abu Dardaa! What are you reciting?" "I am engaged in the…
narrations.summary: The Prophet taught Abu Dardaa a comprehensive dhikr of glorifying and praising Allaah in measures covering all He has created, all that is on earth and all that His Book counts.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that he was sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ in a gathering when a Sahabi arrived and greeted Rasool ﷺ saying, ili-ij ('As Salaamu Alaykum wa…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that a Sahabi greeted the Prophet and praised Allaah in a gathering, and the Prophet said ten angels raced to record the words, and Allaah ordered them to be recorded exactly as His servant said them.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration records the words of the Dhikr as: Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once heard someone recite: "Who said those words?"…
narrations.summary: Abu Ayyoob Ansaari reports that the Prophet praised a man's words of praise; the man said he had spoken them hoping for reward, and the Prophet said thirteen angels raced to present them to Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Jubayr reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once saw a man reciting Tasbeeh on a rosary, he remarked, "It would suffice him to rather say: 'I express…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Jubayr reports that Umar saw a man counting tasbeeh on a rosary and advised him to say instead that he glorifies and praises Allaah and magnifies Him as much as fills the heavens, the earth and all that Allaah wills.

narrations.excerpt: narrates that the poor Muhaajireen once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "The wealthy ones have taken the elevated positions and everlasting bounties!" "Why do you say…
narrations.summary: The poor Muhaajireen complained that the wealthy had taken the rewards through charity and freeing slaves, and the Prophet taught them to glorify, praise and magnify Allaah after every salaah; Sumay recounts a dispute with his family about the counts, and Abu Hurayrah reports a similar account from Abu Dharr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Dardaa (RA) narrates that when a man once came to Hadhrat Abu Dardaa, he asked the man, "Will you be staying over so that we may send your animal for grazing…
narrations.summary: Ummu Dardaa reports that Abu Dardaa told a traveller of his own conversation with the Prophet about the wealthy taking the rewards, and that the Prophet taught him to glorify, praise and magnify Allaah thirty-three, thirty-three and thirty-four times after every salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qataadah reports that some poor Mu'mineen once said, "O Rasulullaah The wealthy ones have taken all the rewards. They are able to donate in Sadaqah, while we…
narrations.summary: Qataadah reports that some poor believers complained that the wealthy had all the rewards, and the Prophet taught them a dhikr whose roots are on earth and whose branches are in heaven, to be recited ten times after every salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that when he married Hadhrat Faatima (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ sent with her a blanket, a leather pillow filled with the bark of a date palm, two…
narrations.summary: Ali says that he and Faatima asked the Prophet for a servant because of their hardships, and the Prophet taught them to recite three phrases ten times after every salaah and thirty-three, thirty-three and thirty-four times at bedtime, as better than a servant.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Hadhrat Ali (RA) and Hadhrat Faatima (RA), "Should I not tell you of something that is better for you than a servant?…
narrations.summary: In another narration the Prophet tells Ali and Faatima that the dhikr to be recited after every salaah and at bedtime is better for them than a servant.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Faatima (RA) once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ to tell him about the difficulty she was having with her domestic chores. "O…
