narrations.summary: Ummu Salamah reports that Faatima complained to the Prophet about the callouses on her hands from grinding and making dough, and he taught her the dhikr to say at bedtime and after Fajr and Maghrib, which he said is better for her than a servant and brings protection.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) narrates that after performing salaah, Rasulullaah ﷺ used to recite; jsr jij juiji £ ti Iiiy. h fej iiii r "There is none worthy of worship but the One…
narrations.summary: The Prophet used to recite after salaah that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah, to Him belong all kingdom and praise, and that none can prevent what He gives or give what He prevents.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdul Hameed whose mother served one of the daughters of Rasulullaah ﷺ narrates from Rasulullaah ﷺ's daughter that Rasulullaah taught her to recite the following…
narrations.summary: Abdul Hameed reports a morning du'aa that the Prophet taught a daughter of his, which protects until evening; Abu Dardaa reports that a dhikr said seven times morning and evening relieves all worries, though the dhikr itself is not legible in the text.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ismah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "The action Allaah loves most is is Tahreef." "O Rasulullaah the Sahabah (RA) asked, "What is Subhatul Hadith?"…
narrations.summary: Ismah reports that the Prophet called dhikr in the marketplace, when people are negligent of Allaah, the action Allaah loves most, and explained the two terms used for it, Subhatul Hadith and Tahreef.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Idrees Khowlaani reports that Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) once said to them, "When you associate with people, it is inevitable that they would engage in (worldly)…
narrations.summary: Abu Idrees Khowlaani reports Mu'aadh's advice to give full attention to Allaah when people are negligent of Him, which the chain says is the sign of an accepted du'aa; Abu Qilaabah reports that two men in a marketplace asked Allaah's forgiveness together, and one later saw the other forgiven in a dream.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Qilaabah narrates that when two men met in the marketplace, one said to the other, "Come, let us seek forgiveness from Allaah while the rest of the people are…
narrations.summary: Abu Qilaabah reports that two men who met in the marketplace sought Allaah's forgiveness together, and one later saw the other in a dream and learned that they had been forgiven.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Laas Khuzaa'ee (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once provided us with a Zakaah camel to go for Hajj. 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ we said, We do not think that this camel will…
narrations.summary: Abu Laas Khuzaa'ee says the Prophet gave them a Zakaah camel to use for Hajj and told them to mention Allaah whenever they mount, because a shaytaan sits in the hump of every camel, and that they could ride them as Allaah permits.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once let him ride behind him on his animal. When he was seated on the animal, Rasulullaah ﷺ recited Akbar')…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says the Prophet let him ride behind him and recited a set of glorifying phrases while mounting, then leaned on him and smiled, saying that Allaah smiles on a person who mounts and does the same.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Usaamah (RA) narrates that he was sitting behind Rasulullaah ﷺ on a camel when the camel tripped. "May Shaytaan be destroyed!" Hadhrat Usaamah exclaimed.…
narrations.summary: Usaamah reports that when the camel tripped with him behind the Prophet, he said may Shaytaan be destroyed, and the Prophet told him to say Bismillaah instead, since Shaytaan then shrinks to the size of a fly; Abu Tameemah Hujaymi relays a similar incident with another rider.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Tameemah Hujaymi narrates that someone who was once sitting behind Rasulullaah ﷺ on the same animal said, "I was sitting behind Rasulullaah ﷺ on his donkey…
narrations.summary: Abu Tameemah Hujaymi reports that the Prophet taught a rider behind him on a stumbling animal to say Bismillaah, which humiliates Shaytaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ mounted an elevated place (when travelling), he would say: "O Allaah! All prominence belongs to You on every…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that when the Prophet mounted a high place while travelling, he said a du'aa that all prominence belongs to Allaah on every high place and all praise belongs to Him in every condition.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that whenever they reached a destination, they recited ('Subhaanallaah') until they had untied their carriages. Several incidents have passed…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that whenever the Sahabah reached a destination they recited Subhaanallaah until they had unloaded their carriages.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Awf reports that whenever Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) left the house, he used to recite: "-dub If "I leave in the name of Allaah. I trust only in Allaah…
narrations.summary: Awf reports the du'aa Ibn Mas'ood recited when leaving home, trusting only in Allaah and affirming that there is no power or might except with Allaah; Ka'b Qurazi cites the travel du'aa in the Qur'aan from Surah Hood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) narrates that after two thirds of the night had passed, Rasulullaah ﷺ stood up and addressed the people saying, "O people! Engage in the Dhikr…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b tells the Prophet that he wants to give all his time to sending salutations on him, after the Prophet warned the people to remember Allaah as the great events of the Last Day were near; the Prophet said his worries would be taken care of and he would be forgiven.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) says, "Four or five of us would remain with Rasulullaah ﷺ day and night so that we could be of assistance to him when he needed us. It…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf reports that the Prophet prostrated for so long in a date orchard that he feared the Prophet had died, and the Prophet said he prostrated in gratitude that whoever sends one salutation on him earns ten good deeds and has ten sins removed.

narrations.excerpt: Another similar narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Jibra'eel has just come to me saying, 'Should I not convey to you the good news that Allaah says, "Whoever…
narrations.summary: The Prophet tells his Companions that Jibra'eel brought the good news that Allaah sends salutations on whoever sends salutations on the Prophet and greets of peace whoever greets him, and that this was why he prostrated.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Talha Ansaari (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was in an extremely good mood one morning and his happiness could actually be seen on his face. "O Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abu Talha Ansaari reports that the Prophet was joyful because a messenger from his Lord said that whoever sends one salutation on him earns ten good deeds, has ten sins removed and ten stages raised; Ka'b bin Ujrah reports that on three steps of the pulpit the Prophet said Aameen after Jibra'eel named three people who are far from Allaah's mercy: one who does not get forgiven in Ramadhaan, one who does not send salutations when the Prophet is mentioned, and one whose parents grow old and do not get him into Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ka'b bin Ujrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once instructed them to present themselves at the pulpit. When they did so and Rasulullaah ﷺ ascended the first…
narrations.summary: Ka'b bin Ujrah reports that the Prophet said Aameen on each step of the pulpit after Jibra'eel's curses on the person who misses forgiveness in Ramadhaan, who fails to send salutations on him, and who fails his aged parents.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates that when he went out one day to Rasulullaah Rasulullaah ﷺ was saying, "Should I not inform you of the most miserly person?" "Please' do,…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr reports that the Prophet asked whether he should tell them who the most miserly person is, and said it is the one in whose presence his name is mentioned and who does not send salutations on him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Mas'ood (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came to sit with them as they sat with Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA). It was then that Hadhrat Basheer bin Sa'd…
narrations.summary: Abu Mas'ood reports that Basheer bin Sa'd asked the Prophet how the Companions should send salutations on him, and the Prophet taught them a salutation asking Allaah to shower mercies on Muhammad and his family as He did on Ibraheem, then said that the greeting of peace is already taught in the Tashahhud.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said'2', "When you send salutations to Rasulullaah ﷺ, do so properly because you do not know that your salutations will be presented to…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood tells the people to send salutations on the Prophet properly, since they do not know whether their salutations will be presented to him, and teaches them a form of salutation.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Sending salutations to Rasulullaah ﷺ eradicates sins more effectively than water extinguishes fire and sending greetings of peace (Salaams)…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr said that sending salutations on the Prophet removes sins more effectively than water extinguishes fire, that greeting him is more rewarding than freeing slaves, and that love for him is more rewarding than both freeing slaves and wielding a sword in Allaah's path.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) said, "Du'aas remain suspended between the heaven and the earth and no part of it ascends until you send salutations to Nabi ﷺ.
narrations.summary: Umar bin Khattaab said that du'aas remain suspended between heaven and earth and do not rise until salutations are sent on the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "All du'aas are stopped just short of the heavens until salutations are sent to Nabi ﷺ. It is only when salutations are sent to Nabi that the…
narrations.summary: Umar said that all du'aas stop just short of the heavens until salutations are sent on the Prophet, and only then is the du'aa raised.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Every du'aa is held back until salutations are sent to Muhammad ﷺ.
narrations.summary: Ali said that every du'aa is held back until salutations are sent on the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "The person who sends salutations to Nabi ﷺ a hundred times on a Friday will have so much celestial light on his face on the Day of Qiyaamah that…
narrations.summary: Ali said that whoever sends a hundred salutations on the Prophet on a Friday will have so much light on his face on the Day of Qiyaamah that people will wonder what great deed he did; Abdullaah bin Abbaas said it is not appropriate to send salutations on anyone other than the Prophets.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "It is not appropriate to send salutations to anyone other than the Ambiyaa."
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas says that it is not appropriate to send salutations upon anyone other than the Ambiyaa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) also said, "For anyone to send salutations to anyone else is inappropriate unless it be to one of the Ambiyaa."
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas states that sending salutations to anyone else is inappropriate, and the text breaks off in the middle of his exception.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says that in a single sitting, they would count Rasulullaah ﷺ recite the following Istighfaar a hundred times: "O my Rabbi Forgive me and…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that in a single sitting the Prophet recited a hundred times the istighfaar, 'O my Rabbi, forgive me and accept my repentance.'

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) narrates that when he once complained to Rasulullaah ﷺ about his sharp tongue, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "How far you are from Istighfaar? I seek…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah complains to the Prophet that his sharp tongue towards his family may lead him to Jahannam, and the Prophet tells him to seek forgiveness a hundred times daily.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was on a journey when he said, 'Seek forgiveness from Aiiaah.' We then all engaged in Istighfaar. Rasulullaah then instructed us…
narrations.summary: Anas says that on a journey the Prophet had them all seek forgiveness seventy times, and taught that Allaah forgives seven hundred sins of a servant who does so each day; the text breaks off mid-sentence.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali bin Rabee'ah narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) allowed him to ride behind him on his animal as he went to'the outskirts of Harra. Hadhrat Ali then raised his…
narrations.summary: Ali bin Rabee'ah relates that while he rode behind Ali he saw him ask Allaah for forgiveness and then smile, and that the Prophet had done the same and explained that Allaah laughs at a servant who knows none but Him forgives sins; the text breaks off.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) says, "I have never seen anyone after Rasulullaah (ie who more excessively recited: 'I Seek forgiveness from Allaah and repent to Him.
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah says he has never seen anyone after the Prophet recite istighfaar more often than him; the quotation breaks off.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) narrates that a man once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "Alas! How many are my sins! Alas! How many are my sins!" When he repeated…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Abdillaah reports that a man with many sins came to the Prophet, who taught him a du'aa asking for forgiveness greater than his sins, and then told him Allaah had forgiven him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hannaad narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) overheard someone saying, " ('I seek forgiveness from Allaah and repent to Him')", Hadhrat Umar (RA) addressed him…
narrations.summary: Hannaad reports that Umar corrected a man who said only 'I seek forgiveness from Allaah and repent to Him', telling him to add the words asking Allaah to forgive him and accept his repentance.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "I am surprised at the person who destroys himself when salvation is at hand." "What is the salvation?" someone asked.…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that Ali said he is surprised at someone who destroys himself when salvation is at hand, and that the salvation is istighfaar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "Glad tidings for the person who finds in his record of deeds even a little bit of Istighfaar."
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says there are glad tidings for the person who finds even a little istighfaar in his record of deeds.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) mentioned that a person will be forgiven even for the sin of fleeing from the battlefield if he recites the following thrice: "I seek…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that a person who recites a particular istighfaar three times will be forgiven even for fleeing from the battlefield.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "If you people knew my sins, not even two of you would walk behind me and you would rather throw sand on my head. I would be…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that if people knew his sins not even two of them would walk behind him, and he would be glad if Allaah forgave even one of them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) once said, "Every day I seek Allaah's forgiveness and repent to him twelve thousand times and this is in proportion to the debt I owe Allaah."
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah says that every day he seeks Allaah's forgiveness and repents twelve thousand times, in proportion to the debt he owes Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes him as saying, "This is in proportion to my sins." A man once asked Hadhrat Baraa (RA) about the verse: "And do not throw yourselves into…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah is quoted in another version as saying the figure is in proportion to his sins, and Baraa bin Aazib explains that the verse 'do not throw yourselves into destruction' refers to one who sins and then despairs of Allaah's forgiveness, not to one who dies fighting.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Allaah shall raise some people on the Day of Qiyaamah whose faces will be shining with resplendence. They will…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa relates that the Prophet described people whom Allaah will raise on the Day of Qiyaamah on thrones of pearls, neither prophets nor martyrs, who love one another for Allaah's pleasure and gather to remember Him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Abasa (RA) reports that he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "There shall be people on the right hand side of Ar Rahmaan (Allaah) - and both His sides are the…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Abasa reports the Prophet said there are people on the right of Ar-Rahmaan who are neither prophets nor martyrs, whose faces shine, who gather for Allaah's dhikr and choose the best words as one chooses the best dates.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came to some Sahabah (RA) who were engaged in a discussion. They said, "We were busy discussing the…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that the Prophet came upon Companions discussing their former ignorance and how Allaah guided them, and praised them, telling them to continue as they were.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Speak often about Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab because speaking about him is speaking about justice, and speaking about justice is…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says to speak often of Umar bin Khattaab, since speaking of him is speaking of justice and speaking of justice is speaking of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "Adorn your gatherings with sending salutations to Rasulullaah ﷺ and speaking of Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA).
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says to adorn gatherings with sending salutations upon the Prophet and with speaking of Umar bin Khattaab.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when someone asked Rasulullaah ﷺ who the friends of Allaah (the Awliyaa) are, Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Those people who…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates that when asked who the friends of Allaah are, the Prophet said they are the people whose sight reminds you of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Handhala Usayyidi (RA) who was one of Rasulullaah ﷺ's scribes narrates, "We were once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when we spoke of Jannah and Jahannam (with) so much…
narrations.summary: Handhala, a scribe of the Prophet, reports that he felt himself a hypocrite when his heart's state from the Prophet's gatherings faded at home with his family, and the Prophet told him that if he stayed as he was in his company the angels would shake hands with him, with a second version adding Abu Hurayrah's similar complaint.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) says, "We were performing Tawaaf when I extended to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) my proposal to marry his daughter, he remained silent and…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr relates that when he proposed to Abdullaah bin Umar's daughter during Tawaaf, Ibn Umar stayed silent because they were remembering Allaah, and later in Madinah accepted the proposal and married him to her.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates from Rasulullaah ﷺ that the salaah performed after brushing the teeth with a Miswaak is seventy times superior to the salaah performed…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha relates that the Prophet said prayer after brushing the teeth with a miswaak is seventy times better than without it, and that silent dhikr is seventy times better than audible dhikr and will be rewarded by Allaah on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates, "We once saw a fire in Baqee (the graveyard of Madinah) and we got to the grave, Rasulullaah ﷺ was already there. 'Hand over the body to…
narrations.summary: Jaabir relates that at Baqee the Prophet asked for a body to be lifted from its grave and handed to him, and they found it was the man who used to raise his voice in dhikr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ibraaheem Taymi narrates that Dhul Bijadaayn ('the one with two striped blankets') was a Sahabi by the name of Abdullaah. He belonged to the Muzaynah…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Ibraaheem Taymi relates the story of Abdullaah Dhul Bijaadayn, an orphan who after accepting Islaam was stripped of his uncle's goods, was told by the Prophet to stay at his door, and was buried at Tabook by Abu Bakr and Umar while the Prophet prayed for his pleasure.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir (RA) states, "It was with regard to a person called Abdullaah Dhul Bijaadayn that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Indeed, he is one who…
narrations.summary: Uqba bin Aamir reports that the Prophet said of Abdullaah Dhul Bijaadayn that he is one who sighs deeply, because he remembered Allaah aloud through Qur'aan and du'aa.

narrations.excerpt: What Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Hadhrat Safiyya when he saw her Using Date Seeds to Count her Tasbeehaat Hadhrat Safiyya (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came to her when…
narrations.summary: Safiyya relates that the Prophet came to her while she was counting her tasbeehaat with four thousand date seeds and taught her to glorify Allaah as much as all of His creation.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes the Dhikr in the following words: "I glorify Allaah as much as everything that He has created" Several similar narrations have already-passed in…
narrations.summary: Another narration gives the dhikr as 'as much as everything He has created', and reports that Abu Safiyya, Abu Hurayrah and Sa'd counted their tasbeeh with stones or a knotted string.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Nadhrah narrates that an old man from the Banu Tufaawah tribe related, "I was the guest of Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) in Madinah and have never seen any of the…
narrations.summary: Abu Nadhra relays an old man's account of being Abu Hurayrah's guest in Madinah, where he saw him count his tasbeeh with stones or date seeds while his slave woman refilled the bag for him, and was struck by his care for guests.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hakeem bin Daylami reports that Hadhrat Sa'd (bin Abi Waqqaas) (RA) used stones to count his Tasbeehaat.
narrations.summary: Hakeem bin Daylami reports that Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas used stones to count his tasbeeh.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "If possible, you should engage in Dhikr only when you are in a state of purity." ' ' Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar advises making dhikr only in a state of purity, and Abu Hurayrah relates that the Prophet said Allaah multiplies the reward of a good deed to a very great number, citing Qur'aan 4:40.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by a person who was making du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Grant me patience." Rasulullaah ﷺ addressed the…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal relates that the Prophet corrected several people's du'aas: he told one who asked for patience to ask for safety, explained that the perfect bounty is Jannah and rescue from Jahannam, and said that the du'aa of one who called on Dhul Jalaali wal Ikraam had been accepted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once went to visit a man who was suffering so much that he (had lost a lot of weight and) looked like a…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik relates that the Prophet visited a very weak man who had asked Allaah to bring his punishment forward, taught him the Qur'aanic du'aa for good in this world and the Hereafter, and the man was cured.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Basheer bin Khasaasiyah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to him, "Trunk Allaah for bringing you from the Rabee'ah Khath'am tribe and allowing you to…
narrations.summary: Basheer bin Khasaasiyah relates that the Prophet thanked Allaah for guiding him to Islaam, and that when Basheer asked him to pray that he die before him, the Prophet refused to make that du'aa for anyone.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) says, "Whenever making du'aa for anyone, Rasulullaah ﷺ always began with (asking for) himself. When speaking of Hadhrat Moosa (RA) one day,…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b says the Prophet always began his du'aa for anyone with himself, and remarked that Moosa would have seen stranger things had he been more patient with his companion.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA) also reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa, he began with himself. ' ' Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) once said to Ibn Abu Saa'ib who was…
narrations.summary: Abu Ayyoob Ansaari reports that the Prophet always began his du'aa with himself, and Aa'isha told Ibn Abu Saa'ib, a lecturer in Madinah, not to contrive rhymed du'aas since the Prophet and Companions did not.

narrations.excerpt: When Hadhrat Umar (RA) overheard a man making du'aa to be protected from tests, he remarked, "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from his words." He then addressed the man…
narrations.summary: Umar corrects a man who prays for protection from trials by asking whether he wants his Lord to withhold family and wealth from him, and Muhaarib bin Dithaar reports his uncle's account of Ibn Mas'ood's pre-dawn du'aa for forgiveness, which Ibn Mas'ood linked to Ya'qoob's pre-dawn du'aa for his sons.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) says, "Whenever he made du'aa, Rasulullaah ﷺ raised his hands and after completing, he would pass them over his face."
narrations.summary: Umar relates that whenever the Prophet made du'aa he raised his hands and passed them over his face on finishing.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when raising his hands to make du'aa, Rasulullaah SPS-? would not drop them until he passed them over his face (upon completing the du'aa).
narrations.summary: Another narration says the Prophet would not lower his hands from a du'aa until he had passed them over his face on completing it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) also said, "I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ making du'aa at Ahjaaruz Zayt with his palms (towards his face) and when he completed, he passed them over his face."
narrations.summary: Umar says he saw the Prophet make du'aa at Ahjaaruz Zayt with his palms towards his face and pass them over his face afterwards, and Aa'isha says he raised his hands for so long in du'aa that she grew tired.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to raise his hands for so long when making du'aa that I would get tired."
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet raised his hands in du'aa for so long that she would grow tired watching.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! I am but a human. Please do not punish me for verbally abusing or hurting anyone." Yet another…
narrations.summary: Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa asking Allaah not to punish him for any verbal abuse or hurt he had caused a Mu'min, saying he is only a human.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by a tribe of Bedouins who had accepted Islaam and whose settlement the coalition of Kuffaar armies had…
narrations.summary: Rasulullaah ﷺ raised his hands and cursed the coalition of armies that had destroyed a Bedouin tribe's settlement, and Abdullaah bin Umar and Abdullaah bin Zubayr were seen wiping their faces after du'aa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais Madani narrates that when a man came to ask Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit something, he said to the man, "Go to Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah because it once happened that…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit tells a man to go to Abu Hurayrah, because Rasulullaah ﷺ said Aameen to his du'aa and Abu Hurayrah's, and Abu Hurayrah's request for knowledge he would never forget was granted first.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaami bin Shaddaad narrates from a relative that he once heard Hadhrat Umar say, "I want you people to say 'Aameen' to three du'aas that I am going to make." He…
narrations.summary: Umar asked the people to say Aameen to three du'aas he made, asking Allaah to strengthen his weakness, soften his sternness and make him generous.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saa'ib bin Yazeed reports that it was early one morning during the Year of Ashes (the year, in which Madinah experienced a crippling drought) that he saw Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: In the Year of Ashes, Saa'ib bin Yazeed saw Umar weeping and seeking forgiveness in du'aa, then asking Allaah to accept the intercession of the Prophet's uncle Abbaas, who wept as he prayed beside him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed who was the freed slave of Hadhrat Usayd reports, "Hadhrat Umar used to patrol the Masjid at night and remove from there everyone besides the person…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed, a freed slave of Usayd, recounts how Umar patrolled the masjid at night, sat with a group making Dhikr and du'aa, and asked each to pray in turn, weeping himself when it came to Abu Sa'eed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Habeeb bin Maslamah Fahri was a person whose du'aas were always accepted. When he was once appointed commander of an army…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that Habeeb bin Maslamah, whose du'aas were always accepted, asked his army to say Aameen and prayed for protection of their blood and the reward of martyrs while facing the Roman army.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir (RA) states, "It was with regard to a person called Abdullaah Dhul Bijaadayn that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Indeed, he is one who sighs very deeply.'…
narrations.summary: Uqba bin Aamir reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said Abdullaah Dhul Bijaadayn sighs very deeply, because he made Dhikr and du'aa aloud, reciting the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates that when he once requested Rasulullaah ﷺ for permission to perform Umrah, Rasulullaah ﷺ granted him permission and said, "Dear brother! Do not…
narrations.summary: Umar asked Rasulullaah ﷺ for permission to perform Umrah and was asked not to forget them in his du'aas; Abu Umaama reports the comprehensive du'aa Rasulullaah ﷺ made for the people when they wished for more.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaama Baahili (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ came to us once, we wished that he would make du'aa for us. He then said, 'O Allaah forgive us, have mercy on…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah Baahili reports that when the Prophet was asked for du'aa he prayed for forgiveness, mercy, acceptance, Jannah and protection from Jahannam for them, and said he had included all their affairs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydullaah (RA) narrates that a Sahabi once removed his excess clothing and then started to roll in the hot sand, saying to himself, "Taste the fire of…
narrations.summary: Talha reports a Companion who, while rolling in hot sand and chiding his nafs, was told by Rasulullaah ﷺ to ask his brothers to include them in their du'aas; Buraydah reports the same incident and the du'aa that followed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aseer bin Jaabir narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) requested Hadhrat Uwais Qarni to seek forgiveness on his behalf, Hadhrat Uwais asked, "How can I seek…
narrations.summary: Aseer bin Jaabir reports that Umar asked Uwais Qarni to pray for his forgiveness, citing the Prophet's words that the best of the Taabi'een is a man called Uwais, and that whoever meets him should ask for his du'aa.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ also added, "Whoever meets him (Hadhrat Uwais), must request him to seek forgiveness on your behalf."
narrations.summary: The Prophet tells people who meet Uwais Qarni to ask him to seek forgiveness on their behalf.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Roomi narrates that Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) was in Zaawiya (close to Basrah) when someone said to him, "Some of your brothers from Basrah have…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Roomi reports that when people from Basrah asked Anas bin Maalik for du'aa, he prayed for forgiveness, mercy, the best of this world and the Aakhirah, and salvation from Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed bin Asam reports that a man from Shaam was a fierce warrior and would often be in the company of Hadhrat Umar (RA). When Hadhrat Umar did not see him for a…
narrations.summary: Yazeed bin Asam reports that when a fierce warrior from Shaam took to drink, Umar wrote him a letter reminding him of Allaah's forgiveness and punishment, and asked the people to pray that the man's heart turn to Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that after repeating the words to himself several times, the man started to weep and then gave up drinking most admirably. When this news reached…
narrations.summary: The man stopped drinking after reading Umar's letter, and Umar told the people to correct a brother who slips, encourage him, pray for his forgiveness, and not help Shaytaan against him.

narrations.summary: A fragment in which someone is said to have called on Allaah by His Ismul A'zam, too damaged by OCR to say more.

narrations.summary: Buraydah reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ overheard a Companion's du'aa that called on Allaah's Oneness and His Ismul A'zam, and told him he had asked by the name through which requests are granted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once overheard a Sahabi making du'aa saying:" ". Rasulullaah ﷺ addressed him saying, "Your du'aa has been…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ overheard a Companion making du'aa and told him that his du'aa had been accepted, so he should ask for what he wants.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that Rasulqllaah once passed by Hadhrat Abu Ayaash Zaid bin Saamit Zuraqi 'while he was performing salaah and making the du'aa: "O…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ passed Abu Ayaash Zaid bin Saamit Zuraqi while he prayed, praising Allaah and calling on Him by His Ismul A'zam, and told him that with this name any du'aa is accepted.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Ayaash. (RA) also added the words: Ij £ ". Yet another narration states that he added, "I ask You for Jannah and seek Your…
narrations.summary: Abu Ayaash adds that the Prophet's du'aa also asked Allaah for Jannah and for protection from Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by a Bedouin who was making the following du'aa in his salaah: du'aa a person makes will definitely be accepted.…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ gave gold to a Bedouin who praised Allaah beautifully in salaah, and explained that he gave it for the manner of his praise rather than for family ties.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "I once heard Rasulullaah ﷺ make du'aa saying, 'O Allaah! I beg from You using that pure and blessed name of Yours which You love best and…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa using Allaah's most beloved name, refused to teach her the Ismul A'zam, and she then made du'aa calling on Allaah by His names.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salamah bin (RA) narrates. that every du'aa he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ make started with the words: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Even if Rasulullaah ﷺ had to make a…
narrations.summary: Salamah and Anas report that the Prophet began every du'aa with a praise and always included the request for the best of this world and the Aakhirah and protection from the Fire.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Fudhaala bin Ubayd (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was sitting (in the Masjid) one day when a man entered, performed salaah and then made du'aa saying, "O…
narrations.summary: Fudhaala bin Ubayd reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ told a man who prayed and made du'aa too hastily to first praise Allaah and send salutations on him, and a later Companion who did so had his du'aa accepted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "When any of you intends making du'aa, he should commence by praising Allaah as. He deserves to be praised. Thereafter, he should…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood advises that anyone making du'aa should begin by praising Allaah and sending salutations on the Prophet before asking for his need.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abbaas bin Mirdaas (RA) reports that during the evening Rasulullaah spent at Arafaat, he made du'aa that Allaah forgive and have mercy on his Ummah. After making…
narrations.summary: Abbaas bin Mirdaas reports that at Arafaat Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed at length for his Ummah, and Allaah forgave all but wrongs between people, forgave those too at Muzdalifah, and Iblees fell to the ground in grief.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once recited the words of Hadhrat Ibraheem (RA) when he said: "O my Rabb? Indeed these idols have misled many…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ recited the words of Ibraheem and Isa, then wept calling for his Ummah, and Allaah sent Jibraeel to tell him that his Ummah would please him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made the following du'aa for his Ummah, "O Allaah! Turn their hearts to your obedience and engulf them from the back…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports the Prophet's du'aa that Allaah turn the hearts of his Ummah to obedience, and Aa'isha reports that when she asked for du'aa he prayed for forgiveness of all her sins, which he said he prays for his Ummah in every salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Include Abu Bakr in my rank on the Day of Qiyaamah."
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ asked Allaah to include Abu Bakr in his own rank on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Strengthen Islaam with the one whom You love more between Umar bin Khattaab and Abu Jahal…
narrations.summary: Khabbaab reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed that Islaam be strengthened through whichever of Umar bin Khattaab and Abu Jahal bin Hishaam Allaah loves more.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Grant Islaam strength with Umar bin Khattaab especially."
narrations.summary: Aa'isha and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood each report that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed for Islaam to be strengthened through Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said in his du'aa, "O Allaah! Assist Islaam through Umar."
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood reports the Prophet's du'aa, 'O Allaah! Assist Islaam through Umar.'

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) sent a reddish coloured camel to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed to Allaah saying, "O Allaah!…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ asked Allaah to let Uthmaan pass speedily over the Siraat, Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports the Prophet's thrice-repeated words that he is pleased with Uthmaan, and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports a du'aa for the forgiveness of Uthmaan's sins.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ thrice said, "O Allaah! I am pleased with Uthmaan, You also be pleased with him."
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that the Prophet three times said he was pleased with Uthmaan and asked Allaah to be pleased with him too.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Forgive, Uthmaan's past and future sins, those that he committed secretly and…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood reports the Prophet's du'aa asking Allaah to forgive all of Uthmaan's past and future sins, public and private.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "I was once experiencing severe pain, so I went to Rasulullaah ﷺ. He put me where he stood, threw a portion of his shawl over me and then started…
narrations.summary: Ali reports that when he had severe pain Rasulullaah ﷺ covered him with his shawl and prayed, and he was cured, and the Prophet said that whatever he asked for himself he had asked for Ali, and that there would be no prophet after him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Yuthay, Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Wahab and Hadhrat Amr bin Dhi Murr all report that they heard Hadhrat Ali (RA) say, "It is in the name of Allaah that I ask…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Yuthay, Sa'eed bin Wahab and Amr bin Dhi Murr report that Ali called on those who heard the Prophet at Ghadeer Khum to stand, thirteen Companions testified that they heard him say he is closer to the believers than they are to themselves, and the Prophet then prayed for whoever befriends Ali.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa for Hadhrat Ali (RA) saying, "O Allaah! Assist him and assist others through…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed for Ali to be helped, for others to be helped through him, for mercy on him, and for Allaah to befriend Ali's friends and oppose his enemies.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali 5S83sS!sa reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa for him saying, "O Allaah! Keep his tongue firm (on the truth) and guide his heart."
narrations.summary: Ali reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed that Allaah keep his tongue firm on the truth and guide his heart, and Ibn Abbaas reports a du'aa asking Allaah to guide Ali in passing judgement.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ's du'aa for Hadhrat Ali (RA) was, "O Allaah! Guide him in passing judgement."
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports the Prophet's du'aa for Ali: 'O Allaah! Guide him in passing judgement.'

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) narrates that the du'aa Rasulullaah ﷺ made for Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) was, "O Allaah! Make his arrows travel straight, accept his du'aas…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed for Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas that his arrows travel straight, that his du'aas be accepted, and that Allaah love him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) himself narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa for him saying, "O Allaah! Accept the du'aa of Sa'd whenever he makes du'aa to You." ™ Hadhrat Zubayr bin…
narrations.summary: Sa'd reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed that his du'aas be accepted, and Zubayr bin Awwaam reports that the Prophet made du'aa for him, his children and his progeny.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) who was the wife of Rasulullaah ﷺ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once told Hadhrat Faatima (RA) to come to him with her husband and her two sons.…
narrations.summary: Umm Salamah reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ gathered Faatima, her husband and her two sons under a blanket and prayed that Allaah send mercy and blessings on the family of Muhammad as He did on the family of Ibraheem.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ammaar narrates that he was once sitting with Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa when some people started to revile Hadhrat Ali (RA). When they had left, Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Abu Ammaar reports that Waathila bin Asqa told him how Rasulullaah ﷺ covered Ali, Faatima, Hasan and Husayn with a blanket and prayed for their purity, and Ali reports the Prophet tying a shawl over them and praying that Allaah be pleased with them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates that he once went to Rasulullaah ﷺ, who had already spread out a shawl on the ground. When Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Ali Hadhrat Faatima (RA),…
narrations.summary: Ali reports that the Prophet drew a shawl over himself, Faatimah, Hasan and Husayn and prayed that Allaah be pleased with them as he was.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa for Hadhrat Hasan (RA) and Hadhrat Husayn (RA) saying, "O Allaah! IloveJhem,soYou love them…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed for Hasan and Husayn, saying that whoever loves them loves him too.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) also reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa for Hadhrat Hasan (RA) and Hadhrat Husayn (RA) saying, "O Allaah! I love them, so You love them…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah and other narrators report that the Prophet ﷺ made du'aa for Hasan and Husayn, asking Allaah to love them and those who love them.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Usaama states that Rasulullaah ﷺ added, "...and love those who love them." The beginning of this narration adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ said,…
narrations.summary: Usaama reports the Prophet added that he loves whoever loves Hasan and Husayn, and Abu Hurayrah reports that he added that he detests whoever detests them; the Prophet called them his children.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA), Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Zaid (RA) and Hadhrat Aa'isha all narrate that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! I love Hasan, so You love…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah, Sa'eed bin Zaid and Aa'isha report the Prophet's du'aa 'I love Hasan, so love him too', and Muhammad bin Seereen reports his du'aa that Hasan be kept safe and keep others safe through him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa (RA) says, "I once saw Rasulullaah ﷺ carrying Husayn on his shoulders saying, 'O Allaah! I love him, so You love him too.
narrations.summary: Baraa reports seeing the Prophet carry Husayn on his shoulders and pray, 'O Allaah! I love him, so You love him too.'

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat.Abdullaah bin Abbaas narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Forgive the open and secret sins of Abbaas and his children. O Allaah! You be…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed for forgiveness of the open and secret sins of Abbaas and his children, and that Allaah be their guardian after his death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Forgive the open and secret, the public and the private sins of Abbaas and any…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed for forgiveness of Abbaas's sins, both public and private, and of any sins he or his descendants might commit until the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aasim narrates from his father that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "Abbaas is my father's brother and therefore just like my father and what is left of my forefathers.…
narrations.summary: Aasim reports the Prophet ﷺ's words about Abbaas, Abu Usayd Saa'idi describes the Prophet gathering Abbaas and his household under his shawl to pray for them, and Ibn Abbaas is prayed for deep understanding of the Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Usayd Saa'idi (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to Hadhrat Abbaas (RA), "You and your children should not leave the house in the morning until I come…
narrations.summary: Abu Usayd Saa'idi reports the Prophet gathering Abbaas and his household under a shawl and praying that Allaah shelter them from Jahannam; Ibn Abbaas reports the Prophet's du'aa for his understanding of the Deen and the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes the du'aa as, "O Allaah! Teach him the Qur'aan and grant him deep understanding of the Deen." Yet another narration quotes the words as, "O…
narrations.summary: A variant wording of the Prophet's du'aa asks Allaah to teach him the Qur'aan and grant him deep understanding of the Deen, and another wording asks for wisdom and the interpretation of the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: A narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar 'ig states that Rasulullaah words were, "O Allaah! Bless him and spread the Deen through him."
narrations.summary: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet's du'aa, 'O Allaah! Bless him and spread the Deen through him.'

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) reports that Rasulullaah (icil once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! You be Ja'far's successor in (caring for) his children."
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ja'far reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed that Allaah be the successor to Ja'far in caring for his children.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that the du'aa Rasulullaah ﷺ made was, "O Allaah! You be Ja'far's successor in (caring for) his family and bless (his son) Abdullaah in trade."…
narrations.summary: Another report gives the Prophet ﷺ's du'aa that Allaah care for Ja'far's family and bless his son Abdullaah in trade, repeated three times.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi states that after Hadhrat Ja'far (RA) was martyred at Balqaa during the Battle of Mu'ta, Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! You be Ja'far's…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that after Ja'far was martyred at Balqaa in the Battle of Mu'ta, the Prophet ﷺ prayed that Allaah be a better successor to Ja'far's family than to any of His righteous servants.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Maysara narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ received the news of the martyrdom of Hadhrat Zaid bin Haaritha (RA), Hadhrat Ja'far (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin…
narrations.summary: Abu Maysara reports that on hearing of the martyrdom of Zaid bin Haaritha, Ja'far and Abdullaah bin Rawaaha, the Prophet ﷺ spoke of them and prayed for their forgiveness.

narrations.excerpt: . Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Forgive the family of Yaasir although you have already forgiven them."
narrations.summary: Uthmaan bin Affaan reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed that Allaah forgive the family of Yaasir.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Bless Ammaar (the son of Hadhrat Yaasir (RA) The Hadith still continues further.…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports a du'aa for Ammaar bin Yaasir, and Umm Salamah reports the Prophet ﷺ's du'aa for the forgiveness of Abu Salamah, the raising of his rank, Allaah being his successor among those left behind, and his grave being filled with light.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Usaamah bin Zaid (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to put me on his thigh and then put Hasan bin Ali on his left thigh. Rasulullaah ﷺ would then hug us and say, "O…
narrations.summary: Usaama bin Zaid says the Prophet ﷺ placed him and Hasan bin Ali on his thighs, embraced them, and prayed that Allaah show mercy and love to both of them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Usaamah (RA) relates, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ's illness became severe, I returned to Madinah (after camping with the Muslim army in nearby Juruf) and those with me…
narrations.summary: Usaama bin Zaid relates that when the Prophet's illness grew severe and he could no longer speak, the Prophet repeatedly placed his hand on him and lifted it, and Usaama understood that the Prophet was making du'aa for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ thrice made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Forgive Amr bin Al Aas because whenever I request him for charity, he always brings it…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports the Prophet ﷺ prayed for Amr bin al-Aas's forgiveness because he always gave charity when asked; Hakeem bin Hizaam reports a du'aa for blessing in his trade; Jareer reports the Prophet ﷺ prayed that he would sit steady on a horse, and he never fell off again.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jareer ii says, "When I once mentioned to Rasulullaah ﷺ that I could never remain steady on horseback, he placed his hand on my chest until I could actually see…
narrations.summary: Jareer reports that after the Prophet placed his hand on Jareer's chest and prayed that he be steady and rightly guided, he never fell from a horse again.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Jareer Si! says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to me, Wry do you not relieve me of Dhu Khalasa?' Dhu Khalsa was a building of the Khath'am tribe…
narrations.summary: Jareer reports the Prophet asking him to relieve him of Dhu Khalasa, the Khath'am idol-house, and Jareer repeats that he cannot stay steady on a horse.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr (RA) relates, "My father and I were sitting by the door of our house when Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived on his mule. 'O Rasulullaah my father said,…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Busr reports that the Prophet ate at his family's door and prayed for blessings on them, after which they always saw abundant sustenance.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nadhla bin Amr Ghifaari (RA) reports, "When a man from the Ghifaar tribe came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him what his name was, he replied that it…
narrations.summary: Nadhla bin Amr al-Ghifaari reports that the Prophet ﷺ renamed a man of the Ghifaar tribe from 'Muhaan' to 'Mukrim', and that when he led the janazah of Baraa bin Ma'roor he prayed for Allaah's special mercy and for Baraa's entry into Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Abu Qataadah (RA) reports that the person for whom Rasulullaah led the Janaazah salaah when he arrived in Madinah was Hadhrat Baraa bin Ma'roor. Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abu Qataadah reports that when the Prophet ﷺ led the janazah of Baraa bin Ma'roor on arrival in Madinah, he prayed for Allaah's forgiveness, mercy and pleasure with him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Sa'd (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Shower Your special mercy on the family of Sa'd bin Ubaadah and forgive them."
narrations.summary: Qais bin Sa'd reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed that Allaah shower His special mercy on the family of Sa'd bin Ubaadah and forgive them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Qataadah (RA) relates, "We were with Rasulullaah ﷺ on a journey when (because of exhaustion) he started to lean to one side of his animal. I then held him up…
narrations.summary: Abu Qataadah relates that on a journey he held up the Prophet ﷺ when he leaned from exhaustion on his animal, and the Prophet prayed that Allaah look after Abu Qataadah as he had looked after him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) once requested Rasulullaah ﷺ to make du'aa for him, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Allaah! Grant him plenty of wealth…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that when Umm Sulaym asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray for him, the Prophet prayed that Allaah grant him plenty of wealth and children and bless him in them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) narrates that a man called Harmala once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Pointing to his tongue, he said, "O Rasulullaah (Mi! Imaan is still here while…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa reports that a man named Harmala said his faith was on his tongue while hypocrisy lurked in his heart, and the Prophet ﷺ prayed for him to have a tongue that makes dhikr, a grateful heart and a good ending to his affairs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Talib (RA) narrates that when he once requested Rasulullaah ﷺ to make du'aa for him, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "(I will do so) When permission is granted (by Allaah)."…
narrations.summary: Talib reports that when he asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray for him, the Prophet waited for permission and then prayed three times for Allaah's forgiveness and mercy on him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Elevate your little servant Abu Aamir above the majority of people on the…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed that Allaah elevate his little servant Abu Aamir above most people on the Day of Qiyaamah; Hassaan bin Shaddaad reports that his mother brought him to the Prophet for a du'aa that he become big and good, and the Prophet prayed for her and the child.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that after making the Salaam, Rasulullaah ﷺ was still facing the Qibla when he raised his head and made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Free…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed in salaah for Salamah bin Hishaam, Ayaash bin Abu Rabee'ah, Waleed bin Waleed and other oppressed Muslims in Makkah to be rescued, and cursed the Mudhar tribe with drought.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that it was after raising his head from a Rakaah of the Fajr salaah that Rasulullaah ijcll made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Rescue Waleed bin…
narrations.summary: The Prophet prays after rising from a Fajr rakah for the release of Waleed bin Waleed, Salamah bin Hishaam, Ayaash bin Abu Rabee'ah and the other oppressed Muslims in Makkah, and against Mudhar; the text then breaks into a farewell du'aa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qaz'ah narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once said to him, "Come. Let me bid you farewell as Rasulullaah ﷺ bid me farewell. (Rasulullaah ﷺ said:)…
narrations.summary: Qaz'ah reports that Abdullaah bin Umar, bidding him farewell, recited the Prophet ﷺ's words placing his Deen, his trustworthiness and the results of his deeds in Allaah's custody.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) would always say to a person embarking on a journey, "Come close to me so that I may bid you farewell as…
narrations.summary: Another narration says that Abdullaah bin Umar would call anyone setting out on a journey close to him and recite that same farewell du'aa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a Sahabi once came to Rasulullaah saying, "O Rasulullaah iiS-?! I intend embarking on a journey, so do give me some provision (du'aas).…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that a Companion asked the Prophet ﷺ for a provision of du'aa before a journey, and the Prophet prayed that Allaah make Taqwa his provision, forgive his sins and make good easy for him wherever he went.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qataadah Rahaawi (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed me as leader of my people, I held his hand as he bade me farewell. Rasulullaah ﷺ said: "May Allaah make…
narrations.summary: Qataadah Rahaawi says that the Prophet ﷺ appointed him leader of his people and bade him farewell; Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet ﷺ advised a man to keep Taqwa and say Allaahu Akbar when climbing a slope, and prayed that his journey be shortened and made easy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) reports that when Nabi ﷺ lifted the tablecloth off the ground (after eating), he would recite: "Lij .up Fiy JU "All praise that is most abundant,…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah reports that when the Prophet ﷺ finished eating and lifted the tablecloth, he would praise Allaah with abundant, pure and blessed praise.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ ate or drank, he would recite: ^ Uuerj Uli-ij ij "All praise belongs to Allaah Who has given us food…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that whenever the Prophet ﷺ ate or drank, he praised Allaah for providing food and drink and for making him one of the Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ wore a new garment, he would take the name of the garment - either a Qamees, a turban, a shawl (etc.) -…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that whenever the Prophet ﷺ wore a new garment he named it and recited a du'aa praising Allaah and asking for the good of the garment and protection from its evil.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Talha (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ sighted the new moon, he would recite: "O Allaah! Let this new moon rise over us with good fortune, Imaan, safety and…
narrations.summary: Talha reports that when the Prophet ﷺ sighted the new moon he asked Allaah to let it rise over them with good fortune, Imaan, safety and Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: A narration of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) quotes the words of the du'aa as follows: "Allaah is the Greatest! O Allaah! Let this moon rise over us with peace,…
narrations.summary: Ibn Umar quotes a different wording of the new moon du'aa, asking Allaah to let the moon rise over them with peace, security, serenity and Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Raafi bin Khadeej (RA) reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ saw the new moon, he would remark, "The moon of good and virtue." He would then recite the following…
narrations.summary: Raafi bin Khadeej reports that when the Prophet ﷺ saw the new moon he called it the moon of good and virtue, and recited a du'aa three times for the good of that month and protection from its evil.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ heard thunderclaps, he recited: "O Allaah! Let not Your wrath kill us, let not Your punishment destroy us…
narrations.summary: Ibn Umar reports that when the Prophet ﷺ heard thunderclaps he asked Allaah not to let His wrath kill them or His punishment destroy them, but to grant them safety before that.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that whenever the wind blew violently, Rasulullaah ﷺ would say: "O Allaah! I ask You for its good, the good in it and the good it has been…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that whenever the wind blew violently the Prophet ﷺ asked Allaah for its good, the good in it and the good it was sent for, and sought protection from its evil.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) also reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ noticed a cloud forming on the horizon, he would leave what he was doing. In fact, if he was performing…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that when the Prophet ﷺ noticed a cloud forming on the horizon he would leave what he was doing, even shorten his salaah, seek protection from its evil, and ask Allaah for a pleasant downpour if it rained.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ noticed a dense cloud in the sky, he /Would forsake everything he was doing, even salaah. He would then turn to the…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that when the Prophet ﷺ noticed a dense cloud he would leave what he was doing, even salaah, seek Allaah's protection from the punishment it was sent with, and ask for a beneficial downpour if it rained.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salamah bin Akwa (RA) reports that when the wind blew fiercely, Rasulullaah ﷺ would say: "O Allaah! Make it a wind that is fruitful and not one that is…
narrations.summary: Salama bin Akwa reports that when the wind blew fiercely the Prophet ﷺ asked Allaah to make it a fruitful wind and not a destructive one.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make du'aa saying: ij is iulii "O Allaah! I ask you for guidance, Taqwa, chastity and independence"
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that the Prophet ﷺ used to ask Allaah for guidance, Taqwa, chastity and independence.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) reports that one of the du'aas Rasulullaah often recited was: "O Allaah! Forgive my sins, my acts of ignorance, the excesses I commit in my…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports one of the Prophet's ﷺ frequent du'aas asking Allaah to forgive his sins, known and unknown.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make the following du'aa: "O Allaah! Set right the affairs of my Deen in which lies the safety of all my…
narrations.summary: Three Companions each report a du'aa the Prophet ﷺ made: Abu Hurayrah on setting right the affairs of the Deen and the Aakhirah, Ibn Abbaas on submission and trust in Allaah, and Umm Salamah on steadfastness in the Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that another of the du'aas that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make was: Oj Co JU "O Allaah! Grant me well-being in my body and well-being in my…
narrations.summary: Two Companions report du'aas of the Prophet ﷺ: Aa'isha on well-being in body and sight, and Ibn Abbaas asking for help, guidance and a steadfast heart.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that amongst the du'aas that Rasulullaah ﷺ made was: "O Allaah! We beg You for everything that attracts Your mercy and…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports a du'aa of the Prophet ﷺ asking for Allaah's mercy, forgiveness, safety from sin, Jannah and protection from Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make du'aa saying: "b fa blrj Qifc "O Allaah! Forgive the sins and wrong we do in jest, in earnestness…
narrations.summary: Three narrators report du'aas of the Prophet ﷺ asking forgiveness for sins committed in jest, earnestness, error or intent, and asking Allaah to make his character beautiful.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to say: "O my Rabb! Forgive me, have mercy on me and guide me to the most upright path"
narrations.summary: Umm Salamah reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah to forgive him, have mercy on him and guide him to the most upright path.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make du'aa saying: "O Defender of Islaam and the Muslims! Keep me steadfast on Islaam until the day I…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah to keep him steadfast on Islaam until he meets Him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Busr bin Abu Artaat Qurashi (RA) reports that he heard Rasulullaah make the following du'aa: oi oiji jy j "O Allaah! Conclude all our affairs in a most beautiful…
narrations.summary: Busr bin Abi Artaat reports hearing the Prophet ﷺ ask Allaah to conclude all affairs well and to save from disgrace in this world and punishment in the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Whoever recites this du'aa will die before being put through tribulations."
narrations.summary: The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever recites the preceding du'aa will die before being put through tribulations.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sirma (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to say: "O Allaah! I ask You to grant independence to me and to all those associated with me"
narrations.summary: Abu Sirma reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah to grant independence to him and to those associated with him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thowbaan (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make du'aa saying: "O Allaah! I ask You for all that is lawful, for the resolve to stay away from evil, for the…
narrations.summary: Thowbaan reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah for what is lawful, for resolve to avoid evil, for love of the poor, for acceptance of repentance, and to be taken before any trial.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that one of the du'aas Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make was: "O Allaah! Allocate the greatest quantity of the sustenance you give me to my old age…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports a du'aa of the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah to give the greatest share of provision in his old age and in the period just before death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ loved making comprehensive du'aas and would make them rather than any other."
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet ﷺ loved comprehensive du'aas and preferred them to any other kind.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) also reports that she was busy performing salaah when (her father) Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) came to tell Rasulullaah ﷺ something that she was unable to…
narrations.summary: While Aa'isha was praying, the Prophet ﷺ told her to make comprehensive du'aas, and afterwards taught her a du'aa asking for all good and protection from all evil in this world and the next.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "I was busy performing salaah when Nabi ﷺ entered the room. He needed something and because I was delaying him, he said,…
narrations.summary: In another narration of the same event, Aa'isha describes how the Prophet ﷺ asked her to make a concise and comprehensive du'aa and then taught her one.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) says that because Rasulullaah ﷺ made so many du'aas, they were unable to remember them. They therefore said to him one day, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ You…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaama reports that the Prophet ﷺ taught the Companions one comprehensive du'aa that covers all the du'aas he had been making, asking for all good he asked for and protection from all he sought protection from.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make du'aa saying: "O Allaahl 1 seek Your protection from helplessness, laziness, cowardice, extreme old age and…
narrations.summary: Anas reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah for protection from helplessness, laziness, cowardice, old age, miserliness, punishment in the grave and the trials of life and death, and another narration adds protection from debt and oppression.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to include the following words in his du'aa: "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from the evil of what 1 do and from…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet ﷺ included in his du'aa a request for protection from the evil of what he did and of what he did not do.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that amongst the du'aas that Rasulullaah ﷺ made was: "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from losing Your bounties, from a reverse…
narrations.summary: Three narrators report du'aas of the Prophet ﷺ: Abdullaah bin Umar on protection from losing blessings and from Allaah's wrath; Zaid bin Arqam teaching a du'aa for protection from helplessness, grave punishment and useless knowledge, asking Allaah to grant taqwa to the self; and Aa'isha on protection from the trial of Jahannam and the evils of wealth and poverty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qutba bin Maalik (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make the following du'aa: "O Allaah! 1 seek Your protection from character, actions and desires that are…
narrations.summary: Qutba bin Maalik reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah for protection from evil character, actions and desires.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make du'aa saying: "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from leprosy, insanity and all debilitating diseases"
narrations.summary: Anas reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah for protection from leprosy, insanity and all debilitating diseases.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Yasar (RA) who was also a Sahabi reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make du'aa saying: "O Allaah! 1 seek Your protection from being crushed, from falling,…
narrations.summary: Abu Yasar reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah for protection from being crushed, falling, drowning, burning, extreme old age, Shaytaan's madness at death, dying while fleeing a battle, and dying from a poisonous bite.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make the following du'aa: "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from starvation because it is the worst of…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah for protection from starvation, the worst companion, and from treachery, the worst confidant.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ used say in his du'aas: "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from disputes, hypocrisy and bad character"
narrations.summary: The Prophet ﷺ used to ask Allaah for protection from disputes, hypocrisy and bad character.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) -reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to recite the following du'aa: ,-4-j Uj O Allaah! 1 seek Your protection from helplessness, laziness, hard-heartedness,…
narrations.summary: Several narrations of the Prophet's ﷺ du'aas: Anas on protection from helplessness, poverty, sinfulness, hypocrisy, deafness, insanity and leprosy; Uqba bin Aamir on protection from a terrible day, night, companion and neighbour; Umar on protection from miserliness, cowardice and punishment in the grave; and Umar on a protective du'aa for Hasan and Husayn.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used the following words to secure Allaah's protection for (his grandsons) Hadhrat Hasan (RA) and Hadhrat Husayn "In the…
narrations.summary: Umar reports the Prophet's words seeking Allaah's complete protection for Hasan and Husayn from every Shaytaan, harmful creature and evil eye.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Tayyaah narrates that he once asked Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Khambash Taymi - who was an old man by then - "Did you meet Rasulullaah ﷺ When the Sahabi…
narrations.summary: Abu Tayyaah asks Abdur Rahmaan, who met the Prophet ﷺ, what happened the night the jinn plotted against him; he describes how Jibra'eel taught the Prophet ﷺ a protective du'aa and the jinn's flame was put out.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) reports that he was once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when a Bedouin came and said, "O Nabi of Allaah ! I have a brother who is suffering." "What is it…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b reports that a Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ about his brother afflicted by jinn, and the Prophet ﷺ recited protective verses and surahs over him, after which the man was cured.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) once told Rasulullaah (iei!? about the frightening dreams that he saw, which prevented him from…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaama reports that Khaalid bin Waleed told the Prophet ﷺ about frightening dreams that kept him from night prayer, and the Prophet ﷺ taught him a du'aa to recite to dispel them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) mentioned that the above du'aa should be recited whenever a dream scares a person. He therefore used to teach the du'aa to those children…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr taught the du'aa for dreams that frighten a person to children old enough to learn it, and wrote it on paper tied around the necks of younger ones. Khaalid bin Waleed, who often woke frightened, was told by the Prophet to recite Bismillaah and the du'aa on waking. Waleed bin Waleed, who often felt fearful, was told to recite it on going to bed.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) often woke up frightened from his sleep. When he mentioned this to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ advised him…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed often woke frightened from sleep, and the Prophet taught him to say Bismillaah on waking and then the du'aa to dispel what he saw in his dreams.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Waleed bin Waleed (RA) told Rasulullaah ﷺ that he often felt fearful, Rasulullaah ﷺ advised him to recite the above du'aa when…
narrations.summary: Waleed bin Waleed told Rasulullaah that he often felt fearful, and Rasulullaah advised him to recite the du'aa when going to bed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed me to recite the following du'aa whenever I faced any difficulty: tA iiji t "There is none worthy of worship but Allaah…
narrations.summary: Ali says the Prophet instructed him to recite a du'aa whenever he faced difficulty, praising Allaah as the Most Forbearing and Most Magnanimous, the Lord of the Glorious Throne and the Lord of the universe.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ was faced with any difficulty, he used to recite: "O The Ever Living and Controller, it is by Your mercy that I seek…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that whenever the Prophet ﷺ faced difficulty he would say that he sought help through Allaah's mercy, the Ever Living and Controller.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asmaa bint Umays (RA) narrates that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ was perturbed about something or when he was faced with some difficulty, he would recite: "Allaah!…
narrations.summary: Asmaa bint Umays reports that whenever the Prophet ﷺ was troubled or faced difficulty he would say that Allaah is his Rabb and he would not associate any partner with Him.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) says that Rasulullaah ﷺ taught her to the above du'aa when in difficulty.
narrations.summary: In another narration, Asmaa says the Prophet ﷺ taught her the above du'aa to say when in difficulty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that they were inside a room when Rasulullaah ﷺ held on to the door-frame and told them, "O family of Abdul Muttalib! When you…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that the Prophet ﷺ, holding the door-frame, told those in the room, the family of Abdul Muttalib, to say that Allaah is their Rabb and they would not associate any partner with Him when they face difficulties.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes the same narration with the words: "Allaah! Allaah has no partner"
narrations.summary: A variant of the previous narration gives the words as 'Allaah! Allaah has no partner'.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to recite the following du'aa during times of difficulty: ij ill Ij iill ilj ijbl 2)J T "There is none…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the du'aa the Prophet ﷺ recited in times of difficulty, affirming that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah, the Rabb of the Throne, the heavens and the earth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thowbaan (RA) reports that whenever something alarmed Rasulullaah ﷺ, he would say: "Allaah! Allaah is my Rabb and I shall not ascribe any as partner to Him"
narrations.summary: Thowbaan reports that whenever something alarmed the Prophet ﷺ he would say that Allaah is his Rabb and he would not associate any partner with Him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once mentioned that whether with sincerity or not, when a person recites the following du'aa seven times, Allaah will alleviate all his worries:…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says that reciting a particular du'aa seven times will relieve all worries, and Ibn Abbaas recited another du'aa for any anxiety or fear of a ruler, asking Allaah on the strength of his belief in Him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ taught him to recite the following du'aa before a (tyrannical) ruler and whenever one feels apprehensive: unfljjl JU ^ "5"…
narrations.summary: Ali reports that the Prophet ﷺ taught him a du'aa to recite before a tyrannical ruler; Abu Raafi reports that Abdullaah bin Ja'far advised his daughter to recite a du'aa when Hajjaaj came to her, and she was protected from him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Raafi narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) (under duress) married his daughter to (the notorious governor) Hajjaaj bin Yusuf, he advised her…
