narrations.summary: Abu Raafi reports that Abdullaah bin Ja'far, under duress, married his daughter to Hajjaaj bin Yusuf and taught her a du'aa from Rasulullaah that kept Hajjaaj from getting close to her.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "When you appear before a fearsome ruler and you fear that he may tyrannise you, then recite the following du'aa three times: Jul…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas teaches that when a person faces a fearsome ruler who may oppress him, he should recite a du'aa three times seeking Allaah's protection from the ruler, his army and his partisans among jinn and mankind.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said that if a person has a ruler whom he fears for his arrogance and oppression, he should recite: "O Allaah Rabb of the seven heavens…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood teaches that a person who fears a tyrannical ruler should recite a du'aa seeking protection from him, his armies and partisans among jinn and mankind; in another version the tyrant's name is said as well, and Ibn Mas'ood says the tyrant will then be unable to harm him.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "If you fear a tyrannical ruler, say..." The words of the du'aa are as quoted above, but with the words: "…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood teaches a du'aa to say when fearing a tyrannical ruler, asking Allaah for protection from him, from the jinn and from mankind.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Salamah bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ stood up to deliver a sermon in Madinah for the first time, he began by duly praising…
narrations.summary: The Prophet ﷺ's first sermon in Madinah urged people to send good deeds ahead for the Aakhirah, and he gave a second sermon praising the Qur'aan and calling to the worship of Allah alone.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Abdur Rahmaan Jumhi narrates that from the narrations he received, the sermon that Rasulullaah ﷺ delivered in the locality of the Banu Saalim bin Auf…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Abdur Rahmaan Jumhi reports the Prophet's sermon at the first Jumu'ah in Madinah, calling people to taqwa, the Aakhirah and the worship of Allah alone.

narrations.excerpt: A Sahabi by the name of Hadhrat Hiraar (RA) reports that they were with Rasulullaah ﷺ in a battle and it was when they were about to engage the enemy in combat that…
narrations.summary: Hiraar reports the Prophet's address before a battle, reminding the Sahabah of the reward of the one who is martyred in the path of Allah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that when on the expedition to Tabook, Rasulullaah ﷺ stopped at Hijr (the place where the nation of Hadhrat Saalih were destroyed) and…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that at Hijr on the Tabook expedition the Prophet warned the Sahabah not to ask for miracles, recounting how the people of Saalih were destroyed, and named the one man who was saved.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) reports that during the expedition to Tabook, Rasulullaah ﷺ mounted the pulpit and after praising Allaah. he said, "O people! I instruct you to…
narrations.summary: Hasan bin Ali reports the Prophet's sermon on the Tabook expedition, telling people to seek a moderate livelihood and to look for sustenance through obedience to Allah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) says, "When Makkah was conquered, Rasulullaah ﷺ announced that everyone should lay down their arms except for the people of the Banu…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports the Prophet's address after the conquest of Makkah, condemning unlawful killing, rejecting claims to a child that is not one's own, and giving rulings on adultery, prayer times and marrying an aunt and niece together.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was standing on the steps leading to the Kabah when he praised Allaah and said, "All praise belongs to Allaah…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's address at the conquest of Makkah, setting the blood money for manslaughter and abolishing the killings and pride of the Period of Ignorance.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was riding his camel Qaswaa as he performed Tawaaf of the Kabah. He was using the opposite end of his stick to…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's address from his camel during the conquest of Makkah, teaching that taqwa, not lineage or pride, is what makes a person honoured before Allah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) reports that on the last day of Sha'baan, Rasulullaah ijcji addressed the Sahabah (RA) saying, "O people! A great and blessed month is dawning upon…
narrations.summary: Salmaan reports the Prophet's sermon on the last day of Sha'baan about the coming of Ramadhaan, its virtues, the reward for feeding a fasting person, and the four things to be done abundantly in it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when Ramadhaan drew close, Rasulullaah addressed them briefly at the time of Maghrib. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Ramadhaan is arriving, so…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that as Ramadhaan drew near, the Prophet ﷺ told people that on its first night every believer of the Qiblah is forgiven.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that on the first night of Ramadhaan, Rasulullaah stood up to address the Sahabah (RA). After duly praising Allaah, he said, "Allaah has seen to…
narrations.summary: Ali reports the Prophet's first-night Ramadhaan sermon that the Shayaateen are restrained and du'aas are accepted, and then reports that the Prophet ﷺ devoted the last ten nights of Ramadhaan to worship and seclusion.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir iS reports that once Rasulullaah ﷺ addressed them saying, "O people! Repent to Allaah before you die and hasten to do good deeds before you become too busy…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports Rasulullaah's sermon urging repentance, dhikr and sadaqah, and stating that the Jumu'ah salaah is compulsory until the Day of Qiyaamah, with a warning against neglecting it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) narrates that it was on a Friday that Rasulullaah ﷺ stood up and addressed them saying, "When a person lives a mile away from Madinah…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports the Prophet's warning that whoever lives one, two or three miles from Madinah and misses Jumu'ah will have his heart sealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that on the occasion of the Farewell Hajj, Rasulullaah ﷺ addressed the Sahabah (RA) saying, "Shaytaan has lost hope in being…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the Prophet's Farewell Hajj address: Shaytaan has despaired of being worshipped in the land but still works through lesser sins, the Book and Sunnah are left behind, Muslims are brothers, and they must not kill one another.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that it was in Masjidul Khayf (in Mina) that Rasulullaah ﷺ addressed them. After praising Allaah as he deserves to be praised,…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the Prophet's sermon at Masjidul Khayf in Mina: whoever makes the Aakhirah his main concern will have his affairs set right and be made self-sufficient, while whoever makes this world his main concern will be scattered and poor.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that it was in Masjidul Khayf (in Mina) that Rasulullaah ﷺ addressed them saying, "May Allaah always keep fresh the person who…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's Mina sermon on three things a Muslim's heart never betrays, and Jaabir reports the Prophet's Farewell Hajj address on the sanctity of life and wealth, the abolition of Period of Ignorance debts and blood money, and the rights of women.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that it was on the day of Nahr of Dhul Hijjah) that Rasulullaah Wife delivered a sermon to the people. "O people!" Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the Prophet's sermon on the day of Nahr, establishing the sanctity of the day, city and month, and charging those present to convey it to the absent and not to kill one another after him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jareer (RA) narrates that after asking him to keep the people quiet (on the occasion of the Farewell Hajj), Rasulullaah ﷺ addressed them saying, "After I have…
narrations.summary: Jareer reports that at the Farewell Hajj, after asking for silence, the Prophet warned the people not to become disbelievers after him by killing one another.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummul Husayn (RA) reports that when she performed the Farewell Hajj with Rasulullaah ﷺ she saw Hadhrat Usaamah (RA) and Hadhrat Bilaal with Rasulullaah ﷺ. One of…
narrations.summary: Ummul Husayn reports seeing Usaamah and Bilaal with the Prophet ﷺ at the Farewell Hajj and hearing him tell the people to obey a leader who rules by the Book of Allaah; Abu Umaamah reports his further rulings on bequests, adultery, lending, debts, guarantees and a wife's spending.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) also reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was on a camel called Jad'aa with his feet in the stirrups and standing high so that people could hear him.…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah reports the Prophet's call from his camel to worship the Rabb, offer the five daily salaahs, fast Ramadhaan, obey the leader and so enter the Jannah of the Rabb.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Mu'aadh Taymi (RA) relates, "We were at Mina when Rasulullaah ﷺ addressed us. We listened attentively and could therefore hear him clearly even…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan Taymi reports the Prophet teaching the rites of Hajj at Mina and placing the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar in separate camps, and Raafi bin Amr Muzani reports seeing him preach on a mule while Ali repeated his words.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Raafi bin Amr Muzani (RA) narrates that it was in Mina during midmorning when he saw Rasulullaah ﷺ deliver a sermon on a brown mule. Hadhrat Ali (RA) was…
narrations.summary: Raafi bin Amr Muzani saw Rasulullaah deliver a sermon at Mina on a brown mule, with Ali repeating his words for the crowd.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurra Raqaashi reports from his uncle JI) who was holding the reins of Rasulullaah ﷺ's camel during the middle days of the days of Tashreeq. As he was busy…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurra Raqaashi reports Rasulullaah's sermon on the days of Tashreeq during Hajj: the sanctity of life, property and honour, the waiving of interest and of Jahiliyyah blood-feuds, the rights of husbands and wives, and the command to convey the message. Humayd and Abdullaah bin Umar add further reports.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) narrates that it was during the days of Tashreeq that Rasulullaah ﷺ delivered his farewell sermon to the Sahabah saying, "O people!…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports the Prophet's farewell sermon in the days of Tashreeq, saying no Arab is superior to a non-Arab, nor a white person to a black person, except by taqwa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was standing on (the carriage of) a camel with cut ears in Arafaat when he addressed the people saying, "Do…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports the Prophet's address at Arafaat on the sanctity of the day, month and city, his going ahead to the pond, and his warning about innovations introduced after him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "We were discussing during the Farewell Hajj whether it was really to be Rasulullaah ﷺ's farewell or not. It was during this…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that during the Farewell Hajj the Prophet ﷺ spoke at length about Maseeh Dajjaal, noting that every Prophet including Nooh warned his people of him, and that the Rabb is not one-eyed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Safeenah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ijeji delivered a sermon to them in which he said, "There has not been a single Nabi before me who has not warned his…
narrations.summary: Safeenah reports the Prophet's description of Maseeh Dajjaal: his missing left eye, the word Kaafir between his eyes, his deceptive Jannah and Jahannam, and his destruction at Afeeq in Shaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Junaadah bin Abu Umayyah Azdi narrates that he went with a companion to one of the Sahabah (RA) and asked, "Tell us a Hadith that you heard from Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Junaadah bin Abu Umayyah Azdi reports a Companion's narration of the Prophet's warning about Maseeh Dajjaal, describing his signs, his power to bring rain and his inability to enter the four Masaajid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah Baahili (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once delivered a lengthy sermon, most of which concerned Dajjaal. Rasulullaah ﷺ spoke about him until the end…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah Baahili reports the Prophet's long sermon on Maseeh Dajjaal: his trials, his forty days on earth, and how believers should estimate the prayer times in those short days.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ stood on the pulpit one day and said, "O people! I have not gathered you for some news coming from the heavens..." The…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports the Prophet's sermon on the spy sent to investigate Maseeh Dajjaal and his statement that Maseeh Dajjaal cannot enter Madinah or Makkah, which are guarded by angels.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tha'laba bin Abbaad Abdi from Basrah reports that he was once present for a lecture that Hadhrat Samurah bin Jundub (RA) delivered. Hadhrat Samurah narrated a…
narrations.summary: Tha'laba bin Abbaad reports Samurah bin Jundub's account of the eclipse sermon, in which the Prophet ﷺ said eclipses are signs for people to repent, and warned that Qiyaamah comes after thirty liars and the one-eyed Maseeh Dajjaal.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Whoever holds fast to Allaah and says, 'Allaah is my Rabb Who is Ever Living and will never die', he will suffer no…
narrations.summary: Another report has the Prophet say that whoever holds fast to Allaah, saying 'Allaah is my Rabb, Ever Living, who never dies', will suffer no punishment, while whoever tells the Dajjaal 'You are my Rabb' will be punished.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakrah (RA) says, "People had been saying a lot about Musaylama before Rasulullaah ﷺ made a statement about him. Rasulullaah stood up to deliver a lecture…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakrah says that people had been talking a lot about Musaylama before the Prophet spoke about him. The Prophet said Musaylama was one of thirty great liars who would appear before the Last Day, and that the awe of the Dajjaal would sweep up every town.

narrations.excerpt: Another states that Rasulullaah ﷺ added, "...except, for the city of Madinah that will have two angels at each of its entrances who will be repelling this awe from the…
narrations.summary: Another report adds that the Prophet said the awe would not enter Madinah, which has two angels at each of its entrances repelling it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Abdullaah bin Harmala reports from his aunt that Rasulullaah ﷺ once delivered a lecture when he had a bandage tied around his head because of a…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Abdullaah bin Harmala reports from his aunt that the Prophet, with his head bandaged after a scorpion bite, said that fighting would continue until Ya'jooj and Ma'jooj emerge, with broad faces, tiny eyes, reddish hair, scrambling down every hill.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baqeera (RA) who was the wife of Hadhrat Qa'qaa (RA) says, "I was sitting in the rows of the women when I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ deliver a lecture. Pointing with his…
narrations.summary: Baqeera, wife of Qa'qaa, reports the Prophet's warning that when the earth is heard to sink in the west, Qiyaamah has arrived.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once delivered a lecture (in such a high pitch) that even the young ladies sitting in seclusion in the inner rooms of their…
narrations.summary: Baraa reports the Prophet's loud lecture condemning backbiting and the searching out of Muslims' faults, warning that Allah exposes the faults of one who searches for them.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ added, "Never harm the Mu'mineen, and never search for their faults because Allaah will expose the faults of the person who…
narrations.summary: Another narration adds the Prophet's words that one should not harm the Mu'mineen or search out their faults, because Allah exposes the faults of one who searches for his brother's faults.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ came to my room one day and I could see from his face that something had happened. He proceeded to make wudhu and without…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha reports the Prophet's sermon on enjoining good and forbidding evil, warning that prayers and requests will go unanswered if this duty is neglected.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once delivered a lecture to them saying, "Stay away from oppression because oppression will assume the form of…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's warning against oppression, lewdness and greed, followed by his answers on the best act of Islaam and the best Hijrah, and a further command about keeping trusts.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ayman bin Khuraym (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once delivered a lecture saying, "O people! False testimony has been equated to ascribing partners to Allaah."…
narrations.summary: Ayman bin Khuraym reports the Prophet's warning that false testimony is equated with shirk, Anas bin Maalik reports his warning against interest, and Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports his warning against the subtle shirk.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that when delivering a sermon one day, Rasulullaah ﷺ spoke about interest and emphasising its evil, he said, "A Dirham that a person…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports Rasulullaah warning in a sermon that interest is a grave sin, and Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports his warning against Shirk together with the du'aa for protection from it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Basheer (RA) reports that it was while standing on the pulpit that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Whoever is ungrateful for a little will be ungrateful for a…
narrations.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer reports the Prophet's saying that ingratitude for little leads to ingratitude for much and that unity is a mercy while disunity is a punishment; Abu Umaamah Baahili then advises sticking to the larger group.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) reports that he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ recite the following in his sermon: "O family of Dawoodf Express your thanks (to Me for the favours I have…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet's recitation of the Surah Saba verse about Dawood's thankfulness, and his teaching that fearing Allah in private and public, being just in anger and contentment, and spending moderately in poverty and wealth are gifts given to Dawood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said in a lecture, "There is no good in life except for the one who listens and remembers and for the Aalim who speaks…
narrations.summary: Ali reports the Prophet's lecture that the only good in life lies with the listener and the truthful scholar, and his praise of the Qur'aan in reply to Miqdaad bin Amr's question about the period of truce.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Husayn bin Ali (RA) narrates that he once saw Rasulullaah ﷺ stand up to deliver a lecture to the Sahabah (RA). Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O people! (By the way we lead…
narrations.summary: Husayn bin Ali reports the Prophet's lecture on abstinence from the world, reminding people of death and giving glad tidings to those who avoid searching for faults, earn purely, give Sadaqah from their excess and keep to the Sunnah.

narrations.excerpt: In another similar narration'3', Hadhrat Anas (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ was on his camel Adbaa and that he added, "We eat their legacy while their corpses are still…
narrations.summary: Anas and Aaisha report the Prophet's counsel to follow the Sunnah without innovation, to be shy before Allaah, and to remember death and leave the pleasures of this world.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that he heard Rasylullaah deliver the following lecture from the pulpit: "You will meet your Rabb barefooted, naked,…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the Prophet's lecture that people will be resurrected barefoot and uncircumcised, with Ibraheem clothed first and some of his Ummah taken to the left for their innovations.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once mounted the pulpit and after duly praising Allaah, he said, "Allaah has written a register with the names and lineages of…
narrations.summary: Ali reports the Prophet's lecture that the register of who is destined for Jannah or Jahannam is already fixed, and that actions are judged by how they end.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ saying from the pulpit, "What is the matter with some people who say that being related to me will be of no…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports the Prophet saying that his kin are attached to him in both worlds, but that people who introduced innovations and turned back will be turned away from his pond of Kowthar on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ mentioned the following in one of his lectures: "Take note that I shall soon be called (to Allaah) and will…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri and Abu Humayd Saa'idi report the Prophet's warnings to rulers and collectors: obey what is good, and do not keep gifts from office, since embezzled property will be carried on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Qataadah (RA) reports that he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say the following about the Ansaar from the pulpit: "Listen well! While all other people are like my outer…
narrations.summary: Abu Qataadah and Ka'b bin Maalik report the Prophet's words that the Ansaar are his inner garments and must be honoured, and his instruction to the Muhaajireen to honour the righteous Ansaar and overlook the sinful among them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ka'b bin Maalik (RA) who was one of the three men whose repentance was accepted'3', was informed by one of the Sahabah (RA) that Rasulullaah once came out of his…
narrations.summary: Ka'b bin Maalik reports the Prophet's last sermon, in which he asked forgiveness for the martyrs of Uhud and advised the Muhaajireen to honour the honourable Ansaar and overlook the sinful among them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was on the wooden pulpit when he said, "Save yourselves from Jahannam even if it be with a piece of a date (that you give…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr reports the Prophet urging people to save themselves from Jahannam even with a piece of a date given in charity, because sadaqah straightens crookedness and repels a bad death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir bin Rabee'ah reports from his father that he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say the following in his sermon, "For as long as a person continues sending salutations to…
narrations.summary: Aamir bin Rabee'ah reports the Prophet saying that the angels keep praying for forgiveness for as long as a person keeps sending salutations on him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once delivered a lecture to them saying, "Whoever wishes to be saved from Jahannam and to be allowed entry into…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr, Anas, Abu Sa'eed Khudri and Abu Hurayrah report the Prophet's lectures on Jannah and Jahannam, including his wish that people would weep more if they knew what he knew, and his counsel to think well of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once delivered a lecture saying, "O peoplel Entertain good thoughts about the Rabb of the universe because Allaah…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports Rasulullaah urging people to think well of the Lord of the universe, because Allaah treats His servants according to their expectation of Him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Zuhayr Thaqafi (RA) narrates that he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say in a lecture, "O people! Soon you will be able to distinguish the people of Jannah from the…
narrations.summary: Abu Zuhayr Thaqafi reports the Prophet saying that people will be told apart by the praise and criticism they receive after death, and Tha'laba reports his instruction to give a saa of dates or barley as Sadaqatul Fitr for every person.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tha'laba (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once stood up to deliver a lecture in which he instructed the payment of Sadaqatul Fitr. He detailed that it should be a…
narrations.summary: Tha'laba reports Rasulullaah ordering Sadaqatul Fitr of a saa of dates or a saa of barley for every person, whether minor or adult, free or slave.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir Juhani (RA) reports that when they left with Rasulullaah ﷺ for Tabook, they were -a day away from their destination when Rasulullaah ﷺ (and the…
narrations.summary: Uqba bin Aamir reports that after the Muslims slept past Fajr near Tabook, the Prophet led the qadhaa salaah and gave a long lecture on the best speech, guidance and dangers of sin, while Bilaal said the same sleep had overtaken him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ayaadh bin Himaar Mujaashi'ee (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once delivered a lecture saying, "From the knowledge I have today, my Rabb has instructed me to…
narrations.summary: Ayaadh bin Himaar reports the Prophet's lecture quoting Allaah: the Shayaateen led people into shirk, the Prophet was commissioned to call the Quraysh, and the traits of the people of Jannah and Jahannam are described.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates, "It was after he had led the Asr salaah that Rasulullaah ﷺ stood up to deliver a lecture. There is nothing to occur until the Day…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports the Prophet's comprehensive lecture after Asr, warning against the world and women, describing how people's faith at birth and at death differs, urging control of anger, honest settlement of debts, and speaking the truth to a tyrant.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saa'ib bin Mahjaan was from Shaam and had met many Sahabah He reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) arrived in Shaam, he (in his address to the people) praised…
narrations.summary: Saa'ib bin Mahjaan reports that Umar, while in Shaam, repeated a lecture of the Prophet on staying united, avoiding seclusion with a non-mahram woman, the signs of a believer and a hypocrite, moderation in seeking livelihood, and qadr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Abu Sufyaan (RA) reports that (during his final illness,) Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed the Sahabah (RA) saying, "Pour over me seven water bags of waters…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Abu Sufyaan reports the Prophet's final sermon, in which a servant was given the choice between this world and what is with Allaah, and that Abu Bakr alone understood and wept, so the Prophet praised him and asked that only his door stay open to the Masjid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ayyoob bin Basheer (RA) narrates that during his illness, Rasulullaah requested for water to be poured over him. The narration then proceeds like the one above,…
narrations.summary: Ayyoob bin Basheer reports the same final sermon, beginning with prayers for the martyrs of Uhud, and that only Abu Bakr understood it and wept.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ delivered a lecture saying, 'Allaah has asked a servant from amongst His servants to choose between this world and…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that Abu Bakr alone wept at the Prophet's final sermon and was praised as the one who did him the most favours, and Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the Prophet's advice about the Ansaar from the same sermon.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that during the illness with which he passed away, Rasulullaah ﷺ came out of his room with his head wrapped in an oily bandage.…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that during his final illness Rasulullaah came out with his head bound and gave his last sermon, which also included advice about the Ansaar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ka'b bin Maalik (RA) who was one of the three men whose repentance was accepted relates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came out of his room and after duly praising Allah…
narrations.summary: Ka'b bin Maalik reports the Prophet's last sermon, in which he asked forgiveness for the martyrs of Uhud and advised the Muhaajireen to honour the honourable Ansaar and overlook the sinful among them.

narrations.excerpt: Another similar narration states that this was the last sermon that Rasulullaah ﷺ ever delivered.
narrations.summary: Another narration confirms that this was the last sermon Rasulullaah ever delivered.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Salmah bin Abdur Rahmaan narrates that he heard from both Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) that the last sermon they heard…
narrations.summary: Abu Salmah bin Abdur Rahmaan reports, from Abu Hurayrah and Abdullaah bin Abbaas, the Prophet's final sermon: whoever guards the five fardh salaahs in congregation will cross the Siraat first and receive the reward of a thousand martyrs for each day and night he guarded them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Zaid Ansaari (RA) relates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ led us in the Fajr salaah and then delivered a lecture to us until Zuhr. He then dismounted the pulpit and led the…
narrations.summary: Abu Zaid Ansaari reports that the Prophet led them in prayer and then lectured them from Fajr until Maghrib, telling them everything that was still to happen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ delivered a lecture, his eyes would redden, his voice would get louder and (when necessary) his anger would be intense…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports the Prophet's manner while lecturing, his eyes reddening and voice rising, his words that the Hour is as near as his two fingers, that the best guidance is Muhammad's and every bid'ah misleads, and that the debts and children left behind are his responsibility.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) assumed the office of Khilaafah, he delivered a lecture to the people. After duly praising Allaah, he said, "O…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports Abu Bakr's first address as Khalifah: he is not the best of them, the Qur'aan and the Prophet's ways are settled, the strong and the weak must each have their rights restored, and he asks to be assisted when right and corrected when wrong.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ukaym (RA) narrates that when the Muslims pledged allegiance to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), he ascended the pulpit and, sitting a step beneath the step…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ukaym reports Abu Bakr's first address as Khalifah, with variant versions recorded by Hasan, in which he says he is not the best of them, asks to be watched over, and says a Shaytaan comes to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates a narration similar to the one above, but with the addition that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "The most foolish of all foolishness is sin. Take note…
narrations.summary: Hasan (al-Basri) reports Abu Bakr's speech on taking up the khilaafah: he is not the best of them, he dislikes the post, and he asks to be watched and corrected if he strays.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) also added, "I am but a human being who does right and makes mistakes as well. When I do right, I want you to praise…
narrations.summary: Qais bin Abi Haazim and Aasim bin Adi report Abu Bakr's later addresses, in which he asks to be corrected if he strays, sends Usaamah's army forward, and urges people to do good before their lives end.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Abu Maryam says that he was informed that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr became the Khalifah, he mounted the pulpit. After duly praising Allaah, he said, "By…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Abu Maryam reports Abu Bakr's address on becoming Khalifah: he would rather the burden had fallen on someone he detested, kings are the most ill-fated, and only the poor will be forgiven.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ukaym reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once delivered a lecture to them saying, "I emphatically advise you to adopt Taqwa, to praise Allaah as He deserves…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Ukaym reports the Prophet's lecture urging taqwa, hope and fear of Allaah, quoting the praise of Zakariyya's family in the Qur'aan, and telling people to compete in good deeds before their lives end.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Dinaar reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once said the following in one of his lectures: "My advice to you in your conditions of poverty and hunger is to…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Dinaar reports Abu Bakr's counsel in hardship: fear Allaah, be sincere, send good deeds ahead, and reflect on those who have passed and on the kings whose cities are now in ruins.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nu'aym bin Namha narrates that a lecture of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) included the following: "Do you not know that you spend mornings and evenings within the…
narrations.summary: Nu'aym bin Namha reports a variant of Abu Bakr's address with additions: speech is good only when it pleases Allaah, wealth is good only when spent in His path, and a person should not fear a critic when carrying out Allaah's command.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aasim bin Adi reports a lecture that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) delivered. While the first part is like the one already narrated, this narration states that Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Aasim bin Adi reports Abu Bakr's address on sincerity and on learning from the dead, including that the sins of earlier kings remain theirs while their possessions pass to others.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Moosa bin Uqba reports that when he delivered a lecture, Hadhrat Abu Bakr would say, "All praise belongs to Allaah the Rabb of the universe. I praise Him, seek…
narrations.summary: Moosa bin Uqba reports the comprehensive address Abu Bakr gave: testimony of faith, taqwa, obedience to leaders who enjoin good, guarding against desires and pride, and sincerity for the sake of the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed bin Haaroon reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once delivered a lecture saying, "(On the Day of Qiyaamah) A person will be brought forward upon whom Allaah…
narrations.summary: Yazeed bin Haaroon reports Abu Bakr's warning about the ungrateful person who is humiliated on the Day of Qiyaamah for having sent no good deeds ahead, quoting Surah Taubah verse 63.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ibraheem bin Haarith narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr once delivered a lecture to the people saying, "I swear by the Being Who controls my life that if…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Ibraheem bin Haarith reports Abu Bakr's promise that if people have taqwa and do good, the time will come when they eat bread and butter until they are full.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zubayr SKSi!!ss narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once delivered a lecture saying, "O people! Have shame before Allaah. I swear by the Being Who controls my…
narrations.summary: Zubayr reports Abu Bakr telling people to be modest before Allaah, saying he always covers his head when he goes out to relieve himself, out of shame before his Rabb.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Shihaab reports that during one of his sermons, Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddeeq said, "Have shame before Allaah. I swear by Allaah that out of shame before my Rabb,…
narrations.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports Abu Bakr's sermon on shame before Allaah, and Abu Bakr himself reports that the Prophet once wept on the pulpit and asked for forgiveness and well-being, the best gift after conviction.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aws (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once delivered a sermon saying, "It was during the first year that Rasulullaah ﷺ stood where I am standing and said,…
narrations.summary: Aws reports Abu Bakr's sermon quoting the Prophet's advice to ask Allaah for forgiveness and well-being, to hold to truthfulness and avoid lying, to avoid envy and hatred, and to be brothers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddeeq once delivered a lecture to them saying, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once told us to seek Allaah's…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm reports that Abu Bakr told people the Prophet taught them to seek refuge from hypocritical humility, which is humility of the body with hypocrisy in the heart.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Aaliya narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once delivered a lecture to them saying, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "The traveller will perform two Rakaahs salaah…
narrations.summary: Abul Aaliya reports Abu Bakr quoting the Prophet: a traveller prays two rak'ahs while a resident prays four, and on his own journey from Dhul Hulayfah towards Makkah he would pray two rak'ahs until he returned to Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dhamra narrates that in one of his lectures to the people, Hadhrat Abu Bakr praised Allaah and then said, "You people will soon be conquering Shaam. You will…
narrations.summary: Abu Dhamra reports Abu Bakr's warning that the Muslims will conquer Shaam and that the masjids there must be built for Allaah's remembrance alone, and Anas reports Abu Bakr explaining how man is created, to remove pride.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Humayd bin Hilaal reports from someone who was present for the burial of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) that after Hadhrat Umar (RA) had finished with the burial, he…
narrations.summary: Humayd bin Hilaal reports, from someone present, that after Abu Bakr's burial Umar vowed to settle matters with integrity, to treat well those who behave well, and to punish those who do evil.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) became the Khalifah, he ascended the pulpit and said, "Allaah should never see me considering myself worthy of sitting…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports Umar's first address as Khalifah, in which he says he will not presume to sit where Abu Bakr sat, urges reciting and practising the Qur'aan, and regards himself as a guardian of public funds in the way a guardian of an orphan is.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said the following in his sermon: "Take reckoning of yourselves before your reckoning is taken (on the Day of Qiyaamah),…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Khattaab tells the people in his first sermon as Khalifah to take account of themselves before Allaah takes account of them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Firaas reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once delivered a lecture saying, "O people! We knew you people well when Rasulullaah ﷺ was in our midst because it was…
narrations.summary: Abul Firaas reports that Umar told the people he now judges them only by their outward conduct, warned against reciting the Qur'aan for worldly show, and instructed his governors to teach rather than oppress.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibnul Ajfaa reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said the following in his lecture: "Take note that you should not inflate the dowries of your women because had…
narrations.summary: Ibnul Ajfaa reports that Umar warned against inflated dowries and against calling every slain man a martyr, since he may have carried trade goods.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once mounted the pulpit and said, "O people! What is this inflation of dowries for your women when the dowries common…
narrations.summary: Masrooq reports that Umar, from the pulpit, asked why dowries were inflated when those of the Prophet and his Companions were modest.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) was in Jaabiya when he delivered a lecture. After duly praising Allaah, he said, "There can be none to mislead the one whom Allaah guides and none can…
narrations.summary: At Jaabiya, Umar rebukes a priest who denied that Allaah misleads anyone, and explains that the dispute about predestination arose after the people were created and their destinies recorded.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abzah narrates that when someone reported to Hadhrat Umar (RA) that some people were disputing about predestination, he stood up to deliver a…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abzah reports that Umar threatened to execute any two people he heard disputing predestination, and the dispute only resurfaced in Shaam under Hajjaaj.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baahili narrates that when he arrived in Shaam, Hadhrat Umar (RA) stood up to deliver a lecture in Jaabiya. He said, "Learn the Qur'aan and you will be noted for…
narrations.summary: Baahili reports Umar's long lecture at Jaabiya urging people to learn and act on the Qur'aan, to be patient in seeking sustenance, to avoid wine, tyrants and prohibited dealings, and to refrain from abusing or cutting off fellow Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Moosa bin Uqba reports that the following is the lecture that Hadhrat Umar delivered at Jaabiya: "After praising Allaah and sending salutations to Rasulullaah ﷺ,…
narrations.summary: Moosa bin Uqba reports Umar's comprehensive Jaabiya lecture on fearing Allaah, the times of salaah, fasting, zakaah, true jihaad and hijrah, and the duties of rulers to their subjects.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) appointed Hadhrat Ali as his deputy and then left Madinah by horseback so that he could travel faster. When he reached…
narrations.summary: Umar, at Jaabiya, urges people to put their private lives in order, stay with the united body of Muslims, and never be alone with a non-Mahram woman.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that in his lecture to the people at Jaabiya, Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) said, "Just as I am standing before you here,…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports Umar's Jaabiya lecture quoting the Prophet on honouring the Sahabah and on unity, and Suwayd bin Ghafala reports Umar's ban on men wearing silk beyond a trivial amount.

narrations.excerpt: In his report detailing Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s arrival (in Shaam) after the outbreak of the plague in Amwaas at the end of the year 17 A. H., Hadhrat Sayf reports that it…
narrations.summary: Sayf reports that just before returning to Madinah, Umar told the people in Shaam that he had been just in sharing the booty, camps and borders, and invited them to point out anything else worth doing.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) and others have reported after duly praising Allaah, Hadhrat Umar (RA) reminded the people about (the greatness of) Allaah and about the Day…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports Umar's first address as Khalifah on accountability, Taqwa and fair treatment of the people; a second address, from an anonymous transmitter, covers the same ground.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said the following in his lecture: "Allaah has appointed me to be in charge of your affairs. Although I know what is most…
narrations.summary: Umar bin Khattaab tells the people in his first sermon as Khalifah to take account of themselves before Allaah takes account of them.

narrations.excerpt: After praising Allaah and sending salutations to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Umar once said the following in his lecture, "O people! Some instances of greed lead to poverty…
narrations.summary: Umar warns against greed and miserliness, urges generous sadaqah and earning only halaal wealth, forbids women from wearing sheer Egyptian cloth, and gives advice on buying a camel.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) and others have narrated that in one of his lectures, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Indeed Allaah is Pure and free from all blemishes and it is necessary for…
narrations.summary: Urwa and others report Umar's sermon on Allaah's countless bounties to the Ummah and the duty to be grateful, quoting the Qur'aan on how Allaah addressed Musa and the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Kulayb narrates that it was on a Friday that Hadhrat Umar (RA) addressed the people. He recited a portion of Surah Aal Imraan until he reached the verse:…
narrations.summary: Ibn Kulayb reports that Umar, reciting Surah Aal Imraan from the pulpit on a Friday, recounted how he ran up Uhud and threatened to kill anyone who said the Prophet had been martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Ibn Kulayb states that as he recited Surah Aal Imraan on the pulpit, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "This Surah discusses the Battle of Uhud. When we…
narrations.summary: Ibn Kulayb reports Umar's account, given while reciting Surah Aal Imraan, of seeing the Prophet alive after the rumour of his death at Uhud and of the verse revealed then.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Adi bin Khiyaar reports that he heard Hadhrat Umar deliver the following lecture from the pulpit: "When a servant humbles himself for the pleasure…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Adi bin Khiyaar reports Umar's lecture that Allaah raises the one who humbles himself for Him and humbles the one who is proud.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once delivered a lecture saying, "It may happen that I forbid you from things that are of benefit to you and…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports Umar telling people to avoid any transaction that raises doubt about interest, since the Prophet died before explaining its details.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aswad bin Yazeed narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once delivered a lecture saying, "Whoever intends performing Hajj should enter into the state of Ihraam only from…
narrations.summary: Aswad bin Yazeed reports Umar's list of the Miqaat places for Hajj, and Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports Umar's lecture that the Prophet had adulterers stoned and that this penalty must not be doubted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that while discussing Rajm (stoning an adulterer) in his lecture, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Never be deceived about it because…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports Umar's lecture defending stoning (Rajm) as a penalty ordained by Allaah, carried out by Rasulullaah and afterwards, and warning of people who will deny Rajm, Dajjaal, intercession, punishment in the grave and release from Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) left Mina (after his stay in Makkah), he sat his camel down at Abtah, where he made a mound with the…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports Umar's du'aa at Abtah, his Madinah speech on the ordained duties and on stoning for adultery, and that he was stabbed within the month of Dhul Hijjah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ma'daan bin Abu Talha Ya'muri reports that it was on a Friday that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once stood on the pulpit and praised Allaah. He then spoke of Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Ma'daan bin Abu Talha reports Umar's last Friday sermon: his dream of his death, the six-man consultation to choose a successor, his concern about the law of kalaalah inheritance, and the rule that garlic and onions must be cooked before entering the Masjid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yasaar bin Maroor narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once addressed them saying, "O people! Rasulullaah ﷺ built this Masjid when we the Muhaajireen and Ansaar were…
narrations.summary: Yasaar bin Maroor reports Umar saying that the Prophet built the Masjid for the Muhaajireen and Ansaar, so that when crowds grew, people should make sajdah on each other's backs and pray inside rather than in the streets.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that when he was appointed Khalifah, Hadhrat Umar (RA) addressed the people saying, "Rasulullaah ﷺ permitted Mut'ah for us for…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports Umar's statement that the Prophet permitted Mut'ah for three days before it was forbidden, and Abdullaah bin Sa'eed reports Umar's warning about children born to non-Arab slave women.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ma'roor or Ibn Ma'roor Tameemi reports, "Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab was on the pulpit, sitting on a step beneath that on which Rasulullaah sat when I heard him…
narrations.summary: Ma'roor Tameemi reports hearing Umar urge people from the pulpit to adopt Taqwa and to obey those entrusted with their affairs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) used to say the following in his lectures: "The most successful of you all is he who is safeguarded…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah, Qabeesah, Urwa and Abdullaah bin Khiraash each report short sayings of Umar on truthfulness, mercy, greed and independence, and a du'aa asking Allaah to keep them on His Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qabeesah narrates that he heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) say from the pulpit, "Whoever has no mercy will not be shown any, whoever does not forgive will not be forgiven,…
narrations.summary: Qabeesah reports that Umar said from the pulpit that whoever shows no mercy will receive none, and whoever does not forgive, repent or abstain from sin will not be forgiven, accepted or saved.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said in his lecture, "Know well that greed leads to poverty and that losing hope leads to independence because when…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports Umar's saying that greed leads to poverty and losing hope leads to independence; Abdullaah bin Khiraash reports Umar's du'aa asking Allaah to hold them with His rope and keep them steadfast on the Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) also added, "...and provide for us from Your grace."
narrations.summary: Another narration adds Umar's du'aa phrase 'and provide for us from Your grace'.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once delivered a lecture saying, "Verily Allaah had granted certain concessions to His Nabi ﷺ as He pleased (because of…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed, Abdullaah bin Zubayr, Abu Ubayd, Alqama and Sulaymaan bin Yasaar each report Umar's sayings on Hajj and Umrah, silk, the prohibition of fasting on the two Eids, intention, and his du'aa for rain during a drought.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) says that he heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) say in his lecture that he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "Whoever (from amongst the males) wears silk in…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr reports Umar's warning that men who wear silk in this world will not be given silk in the Aakhirah; Abu Ubayd, freed slave of Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, reports Umar leading the Eid salaah without adhaan or iqaamah, then forbidding fasting on the two Eid days.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Alqama bin Waqqaas Laythi (RA) narrates that he heard Hadhrat Umar say the following in his lecture to the people: "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Actions are…
narrations.summary: Alqama bin Waqqaas Laythi reports Umar's lecture quoting Rasulullaah that actions are judged by intention; Sulaymaan bin Yasaar reports Umar's address in a drought, calling the people to pray with him for relief.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi says, "I was sitting beneath Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s pulpit as he said in his lecture, 'I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "What I fear most from this Ummah…
narrations.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi heard Umar say in a sermon that the Prophet had said what he feared most for this Ummah was the hypocrite with an eloquent tongue.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan Makhzoomi reports that when the people had pledged allegiance to Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA), he stood up to deliver a lecture.…
narrations.summary: Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan Makhzoomi reports that after the people pledged allegiance to Uthmaan, Uthmaan gave a sermon saying the first rung of the ladder is the hardest and promising more carefully prepared lectures in future.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Badr bin Uthmaan reports from his uncle that when the other members of the consultative assembly pledged allegiance to Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA). he left for the…
narrations.summary: Badr bin Uthmaan reports from his uncle that after the consultative assembly pledged allegiance, the uncle went to the Prophet's pulpit and warned that the world is deception and death comes without warning, quoting Surah Luqmaan and Surah Kahf on the passing nature of this world and the lasting value of good deeds. The people then pledged allegiance.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Utba narrates that after he became the Khalifah, Hadhrat Uthmaan addressed the people saying, "I have been made responsible for this task and have accepted it.…
narrations.summary: Utba reports Uthmaan's first address as Khalifah: he will follow the Book, the Sunnah and what the people agree on, and he warns against being drawn to the world.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaahid reports that Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) once delivered a lecture saying, "O son of Aadam You must know that the angel of death who has been…
narrations.summary: Mujaahid reports Uthmaan's address warning that the angel of death is closing in and that each person must prepare for death and take charge of his own soul.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that in an address to the people, Hadhrat Uthmaan started by praising Allaah and then said, "O people! Adopt Taqwa because Taqwa is a great asset.…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports Uthmaan's address urging Taqwa, control of the soul for the life after death, and trust in Allaah above all else.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that he saw Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) delivering the following lecture from the pulpit: "O people! Fear Allaah in your private affairs because I heard…
narrations.summary: Several reports are strung together: Uthmaan's advice to fear Allaah in private, his account of serving the Prophet on journeys and at home, his orders against child labour, slave-girl earning and backgammon, his full prayer at Mina, and a Hajjaaj report on the grave.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qutaybah bin Muslim narrates, "Hajjaaj bin Yusuf once addressed us and spoke of the grave. He then said, 'It is a place of solitude and a place of loneliness.' He…
narrations.summary: Qutaybah bin Muslim reports Hajjaaj's sermon on the grave, which he backs with a chain: Abdul Malik and Marwaan report that Uthmaan said Rasulullaah always wept whenever he saw a grave or spoke of one.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that he heard Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) say the following in an address from the pulpit: "I used to buy dates from a tribe of the Jews…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports Uthmaan's account of buying dates from the Banu Qaynuqaa and the Prophet's advice to weigh them when buying and again when selling; Hasan reports Uthmaan ordering that dangerous dogs be killed and sporting pigeons slaughtered.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that he was present when Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) instructed from the pulpit that all (dangerous) dogs should be killed and pigeons (used for sport)…
narrations.summary: Hasan (al-Basri) reports that Uthmaan instructed from the pulpit that dangerous dogs should be killed and pigeons kept for sport should be slaughtered.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Badr bin Uthmaan reports from his uncle that in the final lecture that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) delivered in public was when he said, "Verily Allaah has granted you…
narrations.summary: Badr bin Uthmaan reports Uthmaan's final public address: the world is given to be used for the Aakhirah, not to be clung to; people should fear Allaah, avoid splintering, and stay united.

narrations.excerpt: A narration has already passed in the chapter discussing Jihaad in which Hadhrat Uthmaan is extols the virtues of keeping guard in the path of Allaah.
narrations.summary: A cross-reference: Uthmaan's praise of guarding in the path of Allaah was already narrated earlier in the chapter on Jihaad.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali bin Husayn narrates that when he was appointed Khalifah, Hadhrat Ali started his first lecture by praising Allaah. Thereafter, he said, "Verily Allaah has…
narrations.summary: Ali bin Husayn reports that when Ali became Khalifah, his first address urged obedience to Allaah, avoiding harm to Muslims, and readiness for death and the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once delivered a lecture saying, "A man's tribe is more valuable to him than he is to his tribe. If he restrains his hand from (assisting) them, he will…
narrations.summary: Ali says that a man's tribe is more valuable to him than he is to them, citing the Qur'aanic accounts of Loot and Shu'ayb and their tribes.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that whenever Ramadhaan arrived, Hadhrat Ali (RA) would deliver a lecture and say, "This is that blessed month in which fasting has been made…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that at the start of each Ramadhaan, Ali reminded people that fasting means abstaining from lies and falsehood as well as food, and that the month must be fixed by sighting the moon.

narrations.excerpt: After commencing with the praises of Allaah in one of his lectures, Hadhrat Ali proceeded to speak about death. He said, "O servants of Allaah! By Allaah! There is no…
narrations.summary: Ali speaks about death and the grave, warning that the grave is either a pit of Jahannam or a garden of Jannah, and describes the coming Day of Resurrection; Asbagh bin Nabaatah reports the same sermon with additions, and Ali weeps.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Asbagh bin Nabaatah reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) one day ascended the pulpit and after duly praising Allaah, he spoke about death. The rest of the narration is…
narrations.summary: Asbagh bin Nabaatah reports Ali's sermon on death and the coming day, when even the young will turn white and people will look intoxicated from the severity of Allaah's punishment; Ali and those around him wept.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalih Ijli reports that Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) once addressed the people. After praising Allaah and conveying salutations to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he said, "O…
narrations.summary: Saalih Ijli reports Ali's address on the transience of the world, the lonely graves of those who have passed away, and the Day of Judgement when every deed is laid open.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states at the beginning that Hadhrat Ali (RA) commenced his lecture saying, "All praise belongs to Allaah. I praise Allaah, seek His assistance, believe…
narrations.summary: Ali (RA) opens a lecture praising Allaah, reminding people of death, resurrection and accountability, and warning them not to be deceived by this world.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ja'far bin Muhammad reports from his grandfather that Hadhrat Ali once accompanied a funeral procession. When the deceased was lowered into the grave, the family…
narrations.summary: At a funeral, Ali (RA) tells the mourners what the dead man has witnessed and urges them to fear Allaah and prepare for the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: After duly praising Allaah in one of his lectures, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Verily this world is turning its back around and bidding farewell while the Aakhirah is…
narrations.summary: Ali (RA) urges people to act for the Aakhirah, warning that this world is departing and the Aakhirah is arriving, and that they should be neither deceived nor heedless.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ziyaad A'raabi narrates that Ameerul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib once ascended the pulpit in Kufa after the scourge (of the Khawaarij) and after the…
narrations.summary: Ziyaad A'raabi reports that Ali (RA) wept in the pulpit at Kufa after the battle of Nahrwaan and then warned against people who speak like the righteous but act like lovers of the world.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Yamur narrates that in a lecture to the people, Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib started by praising Allaah. Thereafter, he said, "O people! Those who came…
narrations.summary: Yahya bin Yamur reports Ali (RA) teaching that Allaah's decisions come down like rain, so adversity should be met with humility and du'aa, and that enjoining good neither cuts off sustenance nor brings death closer.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Allaah's decisions descend from the heavens..." The narration continues like the one above, but adds that he also…
narrations.summary: A variant of the same lecture on Allaah's decisions adds that a believer who makes du'aa gets either what he asks or a reward in the Aakhirah, and that the harvest of this world is wealth and Taqwa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il reports that in a lecture delivered in Kufa, he heard Hadhrat Ali say, "O people! The person who portrays himself as a pauper will soon suffer poverty,…
narrations.summary: Abu Waa'il reports Ali's warnings in Kufa about pretending to poverty, long life, authority and consultation, and Ali's answer that Qiyaamah is near when the knowledge of Deen rests with the downtrodden.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once stood up to deliver a lecture saying, "All praise belongs to Allaah Who has created creation, Who breaks the dawn, Who will resurrect the dead and…
narrations.summary: In a long sermon Ali (RA) advises taqwa, the Qur'aan, following the Sunnah and sincerity, and reminds people that this world is ending while the Aakhirah is arriving.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Khayrah reports that he accompanied Hadhrat Ali (RA) to Kufa, where he ascended the pulpit and duly praised Allaah. Thereafter, addressed the people saying,…
narrations.summary: Abu Khayrah reports Ali (RA) warning the people of Kufa that they would attack the Prophet's descendants among them, and reciting verses about Husayn being brought to Kufa by deception and pressed to pledge to Yazeed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem Taymi reports from his father that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once addressed them saying, "Whoever claims that we (the family of Rasulullaah have with us something…
narrations.summary: Ibraheem Taymi reports that Ali (RA) denied the family had any secret writings beyond the Qur'aan and a note with camel ages for zakaah, injury laws and the Prophet's ruling that Madinah is sacred, with curses for fabrication and false claims of parentage.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem Nakha'ee reports that Hadhrat Alqama bin Qais once mounted the pulpit and said, "It was on this very pulpit that Hadhrat Ali (RA) delivered a lecture to…
narrations.summary: Ibraheem Nakha'ee reports Alqama bin Qais repeating from the same pulpit Ali's words that the best after the Prophet were Abu Bakr and Umar, and that later innovations are for Allaah to judge.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Juhayfah also reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once mounted the pulpit where he commenced by praising Allaah and sending salutations to Rasulullaah ﷺ.…
narrations.summary: Abu Juhayfah reports Ali (RA) saying from the pulpit that the best person of this Ummah after the Prophet was Abu Bakr, and then Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration is similar to the first one quoted above, but without the words "After them, we had initiated many new things...". This narration however adds that…
narrations.summary: A variant report in which Ali (RA) says it never seemed far-fetched that an angel spoke through the tongue of Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Alqama reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once addressed them. After duly praising Allaah, he said, "The news has reached me that some people regard me to be better…
narrations.summary: Alqama bin Qais reports Ali (RA) rebuking those who rank him above Abu Bakr and Umar, announcing that anyone who says so after this will be punished as a slanderer, and stating the order of the best after the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab reports that Hadhrat Suwayd bin Ghafalah once went to Hadhrat Ali (RA) when he was the Khalifah. "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" Hadhrat Suwayd said, "I…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Wahab reports that Suwayd bin Ghafalah, visiting Ali, led the salaah without adhaan or iqaamah and then gave the Prophet's ruling on eating sacrificial meat after three days, noting that the prohibition was later lifted.

narrations.excerpt: A scholar from the Banu Tameem tribe reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once addressed them saying, "There shall come a time when people will bite into each other and the…
narrations.summary: A scholar of Banu Tameem reports Ali warning that a time will come when people hold on to their wealth and the wicked are honoured, and that the Prophet forbade buying from the desperate and sales involving deception. Abu Ubayd, freed slave of Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, reports Ali leading the Eid salaah without adhaan or iqaamah and telling people not to eat their sacrifice after three days, a ruling since lifted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rib'ee bin Hiraash reports that he heard Hadhrat Ali (RA) say in a lecture, "Do not lie about me because whoever lies about me shall enter Jahannam."
narrations.summary: Ribee bin Hiraash reports Ali (RA) saying in a lecture not to lie about him, because whoever lies about him will enter Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) said the following in his lecture: "O people! Enforce the penalties of the Shari'ah on your slaves,…
narrations.summary: Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami reports Ali (RA) saying that the Shari'ah penalties must be enforced on slaves and recounting the Prophet's approval of his delayed sentence on a slave woman; Abdullaah bin Sabt reports Ali foretelling his own assassination and forbidding the people to kill anyone but the killer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Sabt narrates that Hadhrat Mi. (RA) once addressed them saying, "I swear by the Being Who splits the seed and creates the soul that this beard will…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Sabt reports that Ali foretold his own death at the hand of an assassin, forbade his followers from killing anyone but the assassin, and refused to name a successor, preferring to leave the Ummah as Rasulullaah had left it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Maa reports that Hadhrat Mi (RA) once addressed the people saying, "O people! I swear by the Being besides Whom there is not deity that I have not…
narrations.summary: Umayr bin Abdul Malik reports Ali (RA) telling the people he had taken nothing from their wealth except a perfume vial given to him as a gift, and then relaying the Prophet's report of Allaah's mercy and wrath towards those who obey or disobey.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umayr bin Abdul Malik reports that Hadhrat Mi (RA) once addressed them from the pulpit in Kufa saying, "Rasulullaah ﷺ would be first to notify me if I did not ask…
narrations.summary: Umayr bin Abdul Malik reports Ali's sermon from Kufa, in which Ali says Rasulullaah told him, quoting Allaah, that Allaah turns His punishment away from those who turn from disobedience to obedience and turns His wrath towards those who turn from obedience to disobedience.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hubayrah narrates that when Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) passed away, his son Hadhrat Hasan (RA) stood up, mounted the pulpit and addressed the people saying,…
narrations.summary: Hubayrah reports Hasan bin Ali (RA) addressing the people after his father Ali's death, praising Ali's merits and the night of his martyrdom, and Abu Tufayl reports Hasan reciting his lineage to the Prophet's household.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Tufayl reports a narration similar to the one above, but with the addition that Hadhrat Hasan (RA) also said, "Whoever knows me knows and whoever does not…
narrations.summary: Abu Tufayl reports Hasan bin Ali's address after his father's death: he names his lineage, recites Qur'anic verses on the Prophet's family, and says Rasulullaah handed the flag to Ali while Jibra'eel fought beside him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Jameela narrates that after Hadhrat Ali (RA) was assassinated, (his son) Hadhrat Hasan (RA) became the Khalifah. However, when he was once leading the salaah,…
narrations.summary: Abu Jameela reports that after Ali's death and after Hasan was stabbed in the buttock, Hasan addressed the people of Iraq about fearing Allaah and about the Prophet's household, until everyone in the Masjid was weeping.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that he was present at Nakheelah when Hadhrat Hasan made peace with Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA). Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) then said to him, "Now that the…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that at Nakheelah, after making peace with Mu'aawiya, Hasan told the people he had relinquished the Khilaafah to Mu'aawiya to save the blood of the Ummah.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Sha'bi says, "Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) addressed us at Nakheelah when he made peace with Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA). He stood up and after…
narrations.summary: In a second report from Sha'bi, Hasan at Nakheelah says the Khilaafah is temporary, that the Prophet's family guided the people while his own peace saved their blood, and concludes by asking Allaah's forgiveness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Abu Sufyaan delivered a lecture in Madinah saying, "O people! There is none to prevent that which…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi reports Mu'aawiya's sermon in Madinah that Allaah grants understanding of the Deen to whoever He wishes good, and that Mu'aawiya heard this from the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that he heard Hadhrat Mu'aawiya deliver a lecture saying, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "When Allaah wishes well for a…
narrations.summary: Several chains report Mu'aawiya's sermon: the Prophet said that Allaah grants understanding of the Deen to whoever He wishes good, and that a group of this Ummah will stay upon the truth until Qiyaamah; Maalik bin Yakhaamir adds that Mu'aadh bin Jabal identified them as the people of Shaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umayr bin Haani narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Abu Sufyaan once addressed them saying, "I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Until the Day of Qiyaamah, this Ummah…
narrations.summary: Umayr bin Haani reports Mu'aawiya bin Abi Sufyaan quoting Rasulullaah that this Ummah will stay steadfast on the Deen until the Day of Qiyaamah and will dominate others; Maalik bin Yakhaamir says he heard Mu'aadh bin Jabal identify these people as the people of Shaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yunus bin Halbas Janadi reports a similar narration with the addition that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) recited the following verse (in substantiation): (Allaah said,)…
narrations.summary: Yunus bin Halbas Janadi reports Mu'aawiya's sermon, in which he recites a verse about Isa's elevation and the Ummah prevailing until Qiyaamah, and Makhool reports the Prophet's words that a group of the Ummah will prevail until Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Abdullaah reports, "I was present when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr delivered a lecture during the occasion of Hajj. We had no idea of his presence…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Abdullaah reports Ibn Zubayr's Hajj lecture in Makkah just before the Day of Tarwiyah, covering the verses on the months of Hajj, Arafaat, Muzdalifah, the Talbiyah, the miqaats and Tamattu, with much dhikr and du'aa.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hishaam bin Urwa narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) said the following in his lecture: "You need to know that one (performing Hajj) may stay at every…
narrations.summary: Hishaam bin Urwa reports Ibn Zubayr teaching that pilgrims may stay at any part of Arafah except Batn Urna, and at any part of Muzdalifah except Batn Muhassar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abbaas bin Sahl bin Sa'd Saa'idi Ansaari reports that he heard Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr iS deliver a lecture on the pulpit in Makkah. He said, "O people!…
narrations.summary: Abbaas bin Sahl reports Ibn Zubayr quoting the Prophet that a person given a valley of gold would want a second, and that only the grave's sand fills the belly; Ataa bin Abi Rabaah reports Ibn Zubayr relating the Prophet's ruling on the reward of salaah in Madinah's Masjid and the Masjidul Haraam, and that the whole Haram is a Masjid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ataa bin Abi Rabaah narrates that in one of his lectures, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'A single salaah in this Masjid of mine (in…
narrations.summary: Ataa bin Abi Rabaah reports Abdullaah bin Zubayr quoting Rasulullaah that one salaah in the Masjid of Madinah is better than a thousand elsewhere, except the Masjidul Haraam; Ibn Zubayr explained that the whole Haram counts as a Masjid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Wahab bin Kaysaan a freed slave of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr reports that he heard Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) deliver a lecture on the day of Eid. On…
narrations.summary: Wahab bin Kaysaan, a freed slave of Ibn Zubayr, reports that Ibn Zubayr led the Eid salaah before the lecture, saying this is the way shown by Allaah and His Rasool.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thaabit reports that he heard Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) say the following in a lecture: "Muhammad ﷺ said, 'Whoever (from amongst the males) wears silk in…
narrations.summary: Thaabit reports Ibn Zubayr relating the Prophet's ruling against men wearing silk in this world, and the Prophet's dhikr after salaah; Abu Zubayr reports Ibn Zubayr narrating the same from the same pulpit.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thuwayr narrates that he heard Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) say from the pulpit: "This is the day of Aashura of Muharram) so fast because Rasulullaah ﷺ gave…
narrations.summary: Thuwayr reports Ibn Zubayr telling the people from the pulpit to fast on the Day of Aashura because the Prophet gave the instruction to fast.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Kulthoom bin Hibr narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) once addressed the people saying, "O people of Makkah! 1 have been informed that some of you…
narrations.summary: Kulthoom bin Hibr reports Ibn Zubayr warning the people of Makkah about a gambling game called Nardsheer, quoting Surah Maa'idah verse 90, and vowing severe punishment for anyone caught playing it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) narrates that after once delivering a short lecture, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "o Abu Bakr Stand up and deliver a lecture." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa reports that the Prophet asked Abu Bakr, Umar and then Ibn Mas'ood to speak, and praised Ibn Mas'ood's short address on Allaah as Rabb, Islaam as Deen, the Qur'aan as Imaam and the Prophet as the one they follow, while warning against bombastic speech.

narrations.excerpt: Another similar narration states that after Rasulullaah ﷺ asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood to speak, he began by praising Allaah, invoking peace and blessings on…
narrations.summary: A similar report of the Prophet asking Ibn Mas'ood to speak, in which Ibn Mas'ood says he is pleased with Allaah as Rabb and Islaam as his religion, and the Prophet says he is pleased with what Ibn Ummi Abd likes for them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Ahwas Jushami reports that while Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood was delivering a lecture, he noticed a snake slithering along a wall. He immediately stopped…
narrations.summary: Abul Ahwas Jushami reports Ibn Mas'ood killing a snake during his lecture on the Prophet's ruling that killing a snake is like killing a mushrik; Abu Waa'il reports Ibn Mas'ood's address in Kufa after Uthmaan became Khalifah, urging the people to pledge allegiance to him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il narrates that when Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) became the Khalifah, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) travelled for eight days from Madinah to Kufa. He then…
narrations.summary: Abu Waa'il reports that after Umar's death Abdullaah bin Mas'ood travelled from Madinah to Kufa and told the people to pledge allegiance to Uthmaan, as the Companions had done.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Umayr Adawi reports that Hadhrat Utba bin Ghazwaan was the governor of Basrah when he addressed them. After duly praising Allaah, he said, "Verily…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Umayr Adawi reports Utba bin Ghazwaan's sermon as governor of Basrah, on the world's ending, the stones of Jahannam, the gates of Jannah, his memory of living on tree leaves with the Prophet, and his fear of being esteemed by himself while humbled before Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Utba (RA) concluded with the words, "There has never been a (succession of leaders starting from the period of) Nabuwwaat that does…
narrations.summary: A variant of Utba bin Ghazwaan's address in which leadership after the Prophethood degenerates into kingship and many leaders and governors will test the people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami reports, "I once accompanied my father for the Jumu'ah salaah in Madaa'in. We lived a Farsakh away from the Masjid and it was during the…
narrations.summary: Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami reports Hudhayfah bin Yamaan's Jumu'ah lectures at Madaa'in on Qiyaamah drawing near and the race towards Jannah through good deeds.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Kurdoos narrates that in a lecture in Madaa'in, Hadhrat Hudhayfah said, "O people! Closely monitor what your slaves earn. If it is Halaal, you may utilise it,…
narrations.summary: Kurdoos reports Hudhayfah bin Yamaan at Madaa'in telling the people to check what their slaves earn, because the Prophet said no flesh nourished with haraam will enter Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that in a lecture he delivered in Madaa'in, Hadhrat Hudhayfah said, "O people! Be vigilant over your slaves and ensure that you know their…
narrations.summary: A variant of Hudhayfah bin Yamaan's Madaa'in lecture, warning the people to watch their slaves' sources of income and saying the seller, buyer and maker of wine are like the one who drinks it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qasaama bin Zuhayr narrates that Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) once addressed the people of Basrah saying, "O people! Do weep (over your sins and for fear of…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari told the people of Basrah to weep over their sins and fear of Jahannam, since the people of Jahannam will weep until they cry blood.
