narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shaqeeq says, "When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) was the Ameer of Hajj, he delivered a lecture. He started reciting Surah Baqarah and he commented on each…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas, as Ameer of Hajj, lectured on Surah Baqarah verse by verse, and Shaqeeq said it was so impressive that the Romans and Persians would accept Islaam if they heard it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Yazeed Madeeni reports that Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) once ascended Rasulullaah ﷺ's pulpit and stood on a step lower than that on which Rasulullaah ﷺ stood.…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah praised Allaah from the Prophet's pulpit, foretelling the ruin of the Arabs at the hands of child rulers and that a group from the non-Arabs would reach the Deen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Habeebah narrates that he entered the house of Hadhrat Uthmaan during the period when he was besieged in it. It was then he heard Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA)…
narrations.summary: During the siege of Uthmaan, Abu Hurayrah quoted the Prophet's advice to stay with the Ameer during tribulation and pointed to Uthmaan as that Ameer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Yusuf bin Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam reports that he once sought permission to see Hajjaaj bin Yusuf and when permission was granted, he entered…
narrations.summary: Hajjaaj asks Muhammad bin Yusuf about the narration of Abdullaah bin Salaam, who went to the besieged Uthmaan and addressed the rebels, and the item then passes to lectures of Husayn bin Ali.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uqba bin Abul Ayraaz narrates that it was at a place called Bayda that Hadhrat Husayn (RA) addressed his companions together with the army of Hurr bin Yazeed…
narrations.summary: Uqba bin Abul Ayraaz reports Husayn bin Ali's address at Bayda to the army of Hurr bin Yazeed, quoting Rasulullaah on the tyrant, rebuking the ruling party, and calling on the people of Kufa to keep their pledge, reminding them how they had treated his father, brother and cousin Muslim bin Aqeel.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaahid says, "Hadhrat Yazeed bin Shajarah (RA) was one of those people whose' words always materialised into action. He once addressed us saying, 'O people!…
narrations.summary: Mujaahid reports Yazeed bin Shajarah urging the people to engage the enemy in full combat and describing the rewards of martyrdom in Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaahid reports, "Hadhrat Yazeed bin Shajarah Rahaawi (RA) was one of the governors of Shaam whom Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) had placed in command of the armed…
narrations.summary: Mujaahid reports Yazeed bin Shajarah Rahaawi, a governor of Shaam, exhorting the people to combat and describing the recording of deeds, the shore of Jahannam and the punishment there.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Suwayd reports that a Sahabi by the name of Hadhrat Umayr bin Sa'd was the governor of Hims and would say from the pulpit, "Listen well! Islaam has a…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Suwayd reports that Umayr bin Sa'd, governor of Hims, taught from the pulpit that justice is the wall and truth the door that protect Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubayd (RA) once addressed the people saying, "We shall be meeting the enemy tomorrow and will be martyred. You should therefore not wash off any blood…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Ubayd told the people they would meet the enemy and be martyred the next day, and instructed that they not be washed or shrouded in anything other than the clothes they wore.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salamah bin Sabarah reports that it was in Shaam that Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal addressed them saying, 'You are the Mu'mineen and the people of Jannah. By Allaah!…
narrations.summary: Salamah bin Sabarah reports that in Shaam Mu'aadh bin Jabal told the Muslims that Allaah would admit into Jannah the prisoners from Rome and Persia who serve them, because the Muslims thank them for their service.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Howshab Fazaari reports that he heard Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) deliver a lecture from the pulpit saying, "1 fear the day when my Rabb will summon me saying, 'O…
narrations.summary: Howshab Fazaari reports that Abu Dardaa feared being asked on the Day of Judgement how he acted on his knowledge, when the verses of Allaah's Book would testify against him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) reports that he once asked Rasulullaah ﷺ what the scriptures revealed to Hadhrat Ibraheem (RA) contained. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "They were full of…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr asked the Prophet what the scriptures of Ibraheem and Moosa contained, and received lessons and advice on taqwa, the Qur'aan and dhikr, truthfulness, silence and good character.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to the Sahabah "Do you know the example of each one of you and his family, wealth and actions?" "Allaah and His…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha narrates the Prophet's parable of a dying man's three brothers, representing his family, his wealth and his deeds, and Abdullaah bin Kurz then recited verses on the same theme.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once advised a man saying, "Never allow people to distract you from yourself because you are ultimately responsible for yourself and not for them. Never…
narrations.summary: Umar advised a man not to let others distract him from himself, not to waste his days, and to follow each sin with a good deed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) also said, "Stay away from that which causes you harm, ensure that you have righteous friends even though such people are scarce and consult those who…
narrations.summary: Umar advised staying away from what harms you, keeping righteous friends even though they are scarce, and consulting those who fear Allaah in all matters.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that there were eighteen guidelines that Hadhrat Umar (RA) formulated for the people, every one of which is replete with wisdom. He…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Umar gave eighteen guidelines, of which only a fragment survives: a principle on responding to someone who disobeys Allaah in matters affecting you, and a verse that only the knowledgeable fear Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Shihaab reports that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) said, "Never delve into matters that do not concern you, keep your distance from your enemy and…
narrations.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports Umar's advice to avoid meddling in others' affairs, to be wary of enemies and of friends who are not trustworthy, to avoid sinners, and to consult those who fear Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Samurah bin Jundub (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "Men are of three categories and women are also of three categories. As for women, there is the…
narrations.summary: Samurah bin Jundub reports Umar's description of three categories of women and three categories of men, contrasting the chaste, gentle and wise with the demanding and the bewildered.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ahnaf bin Qais narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said to him, "O Ahnaf! The person who laughs too much loses respect and the one who jokes too much is not…
narrations.summary: Umar told Ahnaf bin Qais that laughing, joking and talking too much cost a person respect, make him prone to error, and erode modesty, piety and eventually the heart.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "The person who laughs too much loses respect, the one who jokes too much is not taken seriously and the one who…
narrations.summary: Another narration gives Umar's similar advice on laughing, joking and talking too much, and refers back to the previous narration for the rest.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "There are some servants of Allaah who annihilate falsehood by staying away from it and revive the truth by speaking of it. When given…
narrations.summary: Umar described servants of Allaah who shun falsehood, speak the truth, fear Allaah, and prefer the rewards of the Aakhirah to the pleasures of this world.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "Become coffers of the Qur'aan, fountains of knowledge and ask Allaah for your sustenance on a day-to-day basis." Another narration states…
narrations.summary: Umar advised becoming storehouses of the Qur'aan and fountains of knowledge, asking Allaah for daily sustenance, and keeping company with those who repent often.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) also said, "The person who fears Allaah will never vent his anger and will never do as he pleases. Had it not been for the Day of Qiyaamah, matters…
narrations.summary: Umar said that one who fears Allaah does not vent anger or follow his whims, that justice to people brings success, and that humility in obedience is nearer to righteousness than seeking honour.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maalik reports that the report reached him that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "A man's respect lies in his Taqwa, his honour in his Deen and his manhood in his…
narrations.summary: Maalik reports Umar's teaching that a man's respect lies in taqwa, his honour in his Deen and his manhood in his character, and Sufyaan Thowri reports Umar's letter to Abu Moosa that wisdom is a gift and that one should avoid shameful acts.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sufyaan Thowri reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once wrote to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) saying, "Wisdom is not something that comes with age but it is a gift…
narrations.summary: Sufyaan Thowri reports that Umar wrote to Abu Moosa Ash'ari that wisdom is a gift from Allaah rather than something that comes with age, and told him to stay away from shameful acts and evil character.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once wrote to his son Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) saying, "I advise you to always adopt Taqwa because Allaah will always protect the one who has Taqwa.…
narrations.summary: Umar wrote to his son Abdullaah advising him to hold to taqwa, which Allaah protects, and warned that deeds without intention and wealth without compassion carry no benefit.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ja'far bin Zabrqaan reports that in a letter to one of his governors, Hadhrat Umar (RA) concluded with the words, "Take stock of yourself during times of…
narrations.summary: Ja'far bin Zabrqaan reports Umar's letters to a governor and to Mu'aawiya bin Abi Sufyaan urging self-reckoning and judgement by the truth, and Ibn Abbaas reports Ali's advice to Umar to curb his hopes and live simply.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said to Hadhrat Umar (RA), "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! If you wish to meet up with your two companions (Rasulullaah iffiw and Hadhrat Abu Bakr, then…
narrations.summary: Ali tells Umar that to meet his two companions, Rasulullaah and Abu Bakr, he should curb his hopes, eat less than his fill, shorten his loincloth, and patch and mend his garments and shoes.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "Goodness is not when your wealth or your children increase, but when your knowledge increases, when your tolerance grows and when you excel…
narrations.summary: Ali said that true goodness is not in wealth or children but in growing knowledge and forbearance and in excelling in worship, and that a deed done with taqwa is never small.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uqba bin Abu Sahbaa narrates that after Hadhrat Ali (RA) was stabbed by Ibn Muljim, (his son) Hadhrat Hasan (RA) came to him weeping. "What makes you weep, dear…
narrations.summary: Uqba bin Abu Sahbaa reports that after Ali was stabbed by Ibn Muljim, he advised his son Hasan that intelligence is the greatest wealth and foolishness the worst poverty, and to avoid fools, liars, misers and sinners.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "Inspiration (from Allaah) is the best guide, good character is the best companion, intelligence is the best friend, sound (Deeni) education…
narrations.summary: Ali said that inspiration is the best guide, good character the best companion, intelligence the best friend and sound education the best legacy, and that only friendship not built on greed endures.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nimraan bin Makhmar narrates that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah was walking amongst his troops as he said to them, "Listen well! There are many who keep their…
narrations.summary: Nimraan bin Makhmar reports that Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah warned his troops against outward show without sincere Deen and urged them to erase old sins with fresh good deeds.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Abu Sa'eed Maqbari (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah was struck by the plague in Jordan and this is where his grave is situated. When…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Abu Sa'eed Maqbari reports that Abu Ubaydah, struck by plague in Shaam, advised the Muslims on salaah, zakaah and death, and Mu'aadh bin Jabal then urged sincere repentance and reconciliation with brothers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) once said, "The heart of a Mu'min is like that of a sparrow, which changes so many times every day (because of which a person needs…
narrations.summary: Abu Ubaydah said that the heart of a believer changes many times a day, which is why a person should consult others.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen reports that Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) was once with his companions, who were greeting him and seeing him off. When a man then…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports Mu'aadh bin Jabal's advice to give precedence to the share of the Aakhirah over the share of this world, and Amr bin Maymoon Awdi reports Mu'aadh's warning to Banu Awd that all return to Allaah and remain forever in Jannah or Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Maymoon Awdi says, "Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) once stood up amongst us and said, 'O Banu Awd! I am the messenger of Allaah's messenger. Remember well…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Maymoon Awdi reports Mu'aadh bin Jabal telling the Banu Awd that everyone will return to Allaah and go to Jannah or Jahannam, to live there forever.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Qurra narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) once said to his son, "Dear son! Whenever you perform salaah, perform the salaah of a person who…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Qurra reports Mu'aadh bin Jabal's advice to his son to pray as one bidding farewell, and Abdullaah bin Salamah reports Mu'aadh's advice to a man to balance fasting and night prayer, earn without sin, die as a Muslim and beware the curse of the oppressed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salamah narrates that when someone once asked Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) to teach him, Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) asked him, "Will you then obey me?"…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Salamah reports Mu'aadh bin Jabal's advice to a man who asked to be taught: fast only at times, pray at night and also sleep, earn without sinning, die as a Muslim, and beware the curse of the oppressed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) once said, "The person who does three things exposes himself to resentment. (The three things are:) Laughing without being amused, sleeping…
narrations.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal said that laughing without amusement, sleeping through the night without salaah and eating without hunger expose a person to resentment, and warned that prosperity and women's gold, silver and finery would test the believers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "It angers me to see a man idle without doing anything for this world or for the Aakhirah."
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood said it angers him to see a man idle, doing nothing for this world or for the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Let me not find any of you lying like a corpse at night (without waking for salaah) and behaving…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood said he would not find anyone lying like a corpse at night and restless all day like the Qutrub insect, and that the cream of this world has passed, making death a gift for every Muslim; Ibn Uyaynah explains the Qutrub image.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "The cream of this world has passed on, leaving only waste behind. Death today is therefore a gift for every Muslim."
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that the best of this world has passed on, leaving only waste, so death is a gift for every Muslim.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that he said, "This world is like a lake at the top of a mountain, the best waters of which have departed, leaving behind only muddy remains." '…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood compared the world to a drying lake, called death and poverty things people dislike but which a believer can benefit from, and taught that perfect Imaan means preferring halaal poverty and submission to Allaah over worldly honour.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "I swear by the Being besides Whom there is none worthy of worship that when a person passes his mornings and evenings as a…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood swore that a person who passes his mornings and evenings as a Muslim will not be harmed by the adversities of this world.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Hujayrah reports from his father that when he took a seat, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) would say, "Days and nights are passing you people…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Hujayrah reports that Ibn Mas'ood reminded those sitting with him that lives are shortening, deeds are recorded and death is near, and that each person is a guest whose wealth is borrowed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once stated, "Each one of you is a guest and his wealth is borrowed. While the guest has to leave sometime, a borrowed item has to be…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that each person is a guest and his wealth is borrowed: the guest must leave one day, and the borrowed item must be returned to its owner.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan the son of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports that a man once approached his father saying, "O Abu Abdur Rahmaan! Teach me some words that…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood advised a man to worship Allaah alone and to accept what is true from anyone, while rejecting falsehood even when it comes from someone close.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) stated, "The truth is heavy and bitter while falsehood is light and pleasant. So many pleasures there are that give rise to nothing but…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood gave several sayings: the truth is hard and falsehood pleasant, the heart can be zealous or lethargic, outward health means little if the heart is sick, and one should not follow others blindly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mundhir (RA) that when some non-Arab chiefs came to see Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood, the people were impressed by their muscular necks and glowing health.…
narrations.summary: Mundhir reports that when non-Arab chiefs visited Abdullaah bin Mas'ood, he told the people that a healthy-bodied kaafir may have a sick heart and a sick-bodied Muslim a healthy heart; he also taught that comfort lies only in meeting Allaah, that no one should follow others blindly in faith, and that Allaah conceals a person's faults in this world and will do so in the Aakhirah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "Whoever desires this world will do harm to his Aakhirah and whoever desires the Aakhirah will do harm to his world. O…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood gave a long series of sayings on the Aakhirah, the Qur'aan, the Sunnah and the harm of worldly desire.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood Sit once said, "When a person does things for show in this world, Allaah will show his faults to people on the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that whoever does things to be seen in this world will have his faults shown on the Day of Qiyaamah, that whoever seeks to be heard will have his faults made known, and that Allaah humiliates the proud and raises the humble.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ja'far bin Burqaan reports that the report reached him that Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi used to say, "Three persons make me laugh and three things make me cry. I laugh…
narrations.summary: Salmaan Faarsi said that three things make him laugh and three make him weep: the one who hopes at length while death searches for him, separation from the Prophet and his party, the scene of death's pangs, and standing before Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) also said, "When Allaah intends destruction to come to a person, Allaah strips him of modesty and you find that he becomes a person who hates people…
narrations.summary: Salmaan said that when Allaah intends a person's ruin, He removes modesty, then mercy, then trustworthiness, and finally the bond of Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) is also reported to have said, "The example of a Mu'min in this world is like a sick person who has with him his physician who knows every illness…
narrations.summary: Salmaan compared the believer in this world to a sick person whose physician forbids harmful things, showing that Allaah withholds many comforts from the believer until Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once wrote to Hadhrat Salmaan (RA), inviting him to come and stay in the blessed land (of Shaam). Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa invited Salmaan to Shaam, and Salmaan replied that knowledge, not land, makes a person blessed, and warned Abu Dardaa as a judge not to be a quack who wrongly condemns people.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hassaan bin Atiyya reports that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) used to say, "You people will always remain in good stead as long as you love the righteous ones amongst…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa said the people stay in good standing while they love their righteous ones and recognise the truth when it is spoken.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "Never compel people to do what they have not been compelled to do (by Allaah) and never take them to task for what their Rabb would not. O…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa gave several pieces of advice: do not compel or blame people beyond what Allaah requires, worship as if you can see Allaah, goodness lies in knowledge and patience rather than wealth, and seek forgiveness after sin.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) also said, "Worship Allaah as if you can see Him and count yourselves amongst the dead. Remember that a little that is sufficient for you is…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa advises worshipping Allaah as if seeing Him, counting oneself among the dead, being content with little, and remembering that good deeds never age and sins are never forgotten; he adds that goodness lies in knowledge, forbearance and excelling in worship, and that one should praise Allaah when doing well and seek His forgiveness when doing wrong.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalim bin Abul Ja'd narrates that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "One should beware that he is not hated in the hearts of the Mu'mineen without him knowing it. Do…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa warned that secret disobedience brings hatred in the hearts of believers, described the apex of Imaan, warned against greed for wealth, and rebuked the people of Damascus for hoarding and building.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) also said, "The apex of Imaan is to steadfastly fulfil the orders of Allaah, to be satisfied with what Allaah decrees, to be sincere in pinning…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says the apex of Imaan is steadfastly fulfilling Allaah's orders, being content with His decree, trusting Him and surrendering to Him; he warns against being consumed by wealth, and addresses the people of Damascus about storing and building beyond their needs and the ruin of earlier nations.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) noticed how much the Muslims were absorbing themselves in building and planting trees, he stood up in their…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa called the people of Damascus to the Masjid and began to rebuke them for their building and planting, but the text gives only the opening and refers back to the previous narration.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Safwaan bin Amr narrates that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) used to say, "O assembly of the wealthy! Cool off your skins (save it from Jahannam) with your wealth (by…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa urged the wealthy to give in sadaqah before death, warned against seeking bounty while starving oneself of knowledge, praised those who fast, and spoke to builders and to ruins about the transience of the world.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "There are three things that I love and which people generally hate; poverty, illness and death." He also said, "I love death because of my…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa said he loved death, poverty and illness for the reasons they bring him closer to his Rabb and cleanse his sins, and Shurahbeel reports his reflection at every funeral.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shurahbeel narrates that whenever Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) saw a funeral, he would say, "You are leaving in the morning and we shall be leaving in the evening. You…
narrations.summary: Shurahbeel reports that whenever Abu Dardaa saw a funeral he would say that the living follow the dead, that death is a powerful advice, and that only the senseless remain unheedful.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aun bin Abdullaah reports that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "The person who searches very hard (for the faults of others) will lose sight of himself (of his own…
narrations.summary: Aun bin Abdullaah reports Abu Dardaa's advice that searching hard for others' faults makes a person lose sight of his own, and that one should lend to the one who will repay on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa ffi also said, "The person who often thinks of death will show off less and will also be less jealous."
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says that a person who often thinks of death will show off less and be less jealous.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) is also reported to have said, "Why is it that I see you greedy for that (sustenance) for which Allaah has already assumed responsibility on your…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa rebuked those who are greedy for provision already guaranteed while neglecting their duties, advised pure sustenance and remembrance of death, and urged seeking Allaah's mercy and forgiveness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Jubayr bin Nufayr reports that a man once said to Hadhrat Abu Dardaa, "Teach me something by which Allaah may grant me benefit." Hadhrat Abu Dardaa…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Jubayr bin Nufayr reports that a man asked Abu Dardaa for something that would benefit him, and Abu Dardaa advised eating, earning and bringing home only what is pure, seeking daily sustenance from Allaah, counting oneself among the dead, entrusting one's honour to Allaah, and seeking forgiveness after sin.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) also said, "A person remains youthful in his love for this world even though his collar bones may be meeting because of old age. This applies to…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa says a person stays youthful in his love for this world even in old age, and gives three rules: never complain of calamities, never speak of your illness, never claim spiritual purity.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "Beware of the curse of the oppressed and the curse of the orphan because both travel (to Allaah) at night when people are fast asleep." He…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa warned against the curse of the oppressed and of the orphan, and said the person he most hates to oppress is one who has none but Allaah to turn to for help.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ma'mar reports from a companion that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once wrote to Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) saying, "Dear brother! Make the most of your health and free time…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa wrote letters to Salmaan, an unnamed companion and Maslamah bin Mukhallad, passing on the Prophet's counsel about the Masjid, orphans, wealth, servants and pleasing Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Muhammad ﷺ reports that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa once wrote to a companion of his saying, "Everything you have in this world belonged to someone else…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa writes to a companion that only what one sends ahead for the Aakhirah is truly one's own, so one should spend for oneself rather than hoard for heirs; he also writes to Maslamah that Allaah makes all creation love the person whose actions conform to His commands.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) also said, "There is no Islaarn without obedience to Allaah and no good without affiliating with the broader Muslim community and without wishing…
narrations.summary: Abu Dardaa said there is no Islaam without obedience to Allaah, no good without staying with the Muslim community, and sincere goodwill toward Allaah's Deen, His Khalifah and the believers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sufyaan Thowri narrates that Hadhrat Abu Dharr Ghifaari (RA) once stood up near the Kabah and said, "O people! I am Jundub Ghifaari. Come to this well-wishing and…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr Ghifaari stood by the Kabah and advised the people to prepare provisions for the journey to Qiyaamah through Hajj, fasting, night prayer, sadaqah and good speech, and to avoid greed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Muhammad reports that he heard a reliable scholar say, "The news has reached me that Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) once said, 'O people! I am a well-wisher…
narrations.summary: Two reports give advice from Abu Dharr on the Aakhirah, night prayer, fasting, sadaqah, and the dislike people have for death and poverty, and in the second report Abu Dardaa joins him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) also said, "People are born to die and buildings are built to fall into ruins. That which shall come to an end is sought with greed while that…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr says people are born to die and buildings are built to fall, that people chase what ends while neglecting what lasts, and that death and poverty are the two things people dislike.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hibbaan bin Abi Jabalah reports that both Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "You are born to die, you build buildings to fall into ruins,…
narrations.summary: Hibbaan bin Abi Jabalah reports that Abu Dharr and Abu Dardaa both said people are born to die and build to ruin, chase what ends while neglecting what lasts, and dislike three things: death, illness and poverty.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Tufayl narrates that he heard Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) say, "O people! Do you have no questions to ask me? While others used to ask Rasulullaah ﷺ about the good…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah told the people to ask him about the living dead, who are those who oppose despotic rule neither with heart, tongue nor hand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) once said, "Hearts are of four types; (1) the veiled heart, which is the heart of the Kaafir, the two-faced heart, which is the heart . of the…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah said hearts come in four kinds: the veiled heart of the disbeliever, the two-faced heart of the hypocrite, the clear heart of the believer, and the heart that holds both hypocrisy and Imaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) is also reported to have said. "The trial of temptation (to do evil) presents itself to the hearts of people. When the heart accepts it, a black…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah warned that trials of temptation sweep away anyone who faces them alone, that each accepted temptation leaves a black spot on the heart, and advised staying at home and dying in times of peace if given the choice.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) also said, "Beware of the trials of temptation which none can stand up to by himself because I swear by Allaah that whenever someone tries to stand…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah warns against the trials of temptation, which sweep away anyone who tries to stand against them alone, and says that when such trials come one should stay at home, break one's swords and cut one's bowstrings.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said, "Verily, the trials of life have periods of repose and periods of upheaval. If you ever have the option to die when it is in repose, ensure…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah says the trials of life have periods of calm and periods of upheaval, and that if one can choose to die during the calm, one should do so.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) also said, "Verily, corruption stems from three persons; from the powerful and proficient scholar who uses the sword to annihilate everything that…
narrations.summary: Hudhayfah listed three sources of corruption, said trials wear down the senses more than wine, said a time will come when only one who makes du'aa like a drowning person is safe, and said the best person takes from both worlds.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) once said, "Even pure wine is not more effective than the trial of life in eliminating (causing to faulter) the…
narrations.summary: Several sayings of Hudhayfah: trials wear a person down more than pure wine does; in the time of trial only one who calls on Allaah like a drowning man is safe; and the best person takes from both this world and the Aakhirah, as reported by A'mash.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Aaliya reports that when a man once asked Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b for some advice, Hadhrat Ubay (RA) said, "Make the Qur'aan your guide and be satisfied to…
narrations.summary: Abul Aaliya reports that Ubay bin Ka'b advised a man to make the Qur'aan his guide, his judge and his intercessor.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) said, "Whenever a servant forsakes anything for the pleasure of Allaah, Allaah replaces it with something better from sources he never…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b said that whoever gives something up for Allaah's pleasure is given something better from unexpected sources, and whoever wrongly takes what he looks down on will meet something worse.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) also said, "A Mu'min is in one of four conditions; when afflicted with difficulties, he exercises patience, when given something, he is…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b said a believer has four qualities of patience, gratitude, truthfulness and justice, and that the believer and the disbeliever each pass through five places of light or darkness.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Basrah reports that a companion of his named Jabar or Juwaybir once said, "When I went to request a slave-girl from Hadhrat Umar (RA) during his Khilaafah, I…
narrations.summary: Jabar or Juwaybir reports that when he belittled the world before Umar, Ubay bin Ka'b, who was sitting beside Umar, corrected him that the world is the means to the Aakhirah, and Ubay later gave advice about minding one's own affairs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dinaar Bahraani narrates that Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) once wrote to Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) saying, "Verily Allaah has made the tongue an interpreter for…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit wrote to Ubay bin Ka'b that the tongue should follow the heart, that speech without matching action is empty, and that one should not look at others' faults while ignoring one's own.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) once said, "O sinner! Never feel that you are safe from an evil end. There are several things that are worse than the sin that you…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas warned a sinner that several things are worse than the sin itself, such as feeling safe, laughing at it or being pleased with it, and related how Ayyoob was tested for failing to help a poor man against an oppressor.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Ensure that you fulftf the Faraa'idh. Fulfil the rights owing to Him that Allaah has prescribed and seek His assistance in doing…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas advised fulfilling the obligations Allaah has set with sincere intention, and taught that every person's lawful provision is decreed, that patience brings it, and that taking the unlawful reduces it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "Whenever a servant receives anything of this world, it reduces his status in Allaah's sight even though the person may be enjoying…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar said that receiving anything of this world lowers a servant's status before Allaah, even for someone who is honoured by Him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) also said, "A man cannot reach the apex of Imaan until he regards people as being foolish in Deen (because of them preferring this world…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar said a man cannot reach the apex of Imaan until he counts people foolish for preferring this world, and then with Mujaahid he spoke to some ruins, saying that only their deeds remain.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Wahab bin Kaysaan narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr Ja once wrote to advise him saying, "The people of Taqwa have certain traits by which they are…
narrations.summary: Wahab bin Kaysaan reports Abdullaah bin Zubayr's letter of advice: the people of taqwa show patience in adversity, contentment with Allaah's decree, gratitude for blessings and submission to the Qur'aan; and a ruler attracts whatever is popular with him, truth or falsehood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) once said, "When a person hankers after this world, it makes him sit down (makes him subservient to it), whereas the person who exercises…
narrations.summary: Hasan bin Ali said that craving the world makes a person its slave, that one who does not aspire to it has enough, and that a person who makes no spiritual progress is deceived.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) also said, "You should know that tolerance is a source of beauty (in character) and fulfilling ones promises is a sign of manliness. Haste is…
narrations.summary: Hasan bin Ali said that tolerance adds beauty to character, keeping promises shows manliness, and haste, excessive travel, wicked company and sinful company are faults.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) is also reported to have said, "People are of four types. Some are those who have a great share of goodness but no good character. Then there…
narrations.summary: Hasan bin Ali divided people into four kinds: those with goodness but no good character, those with good character but no goodness, those with neither, and the best, who have both.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ziyaad bin Maahak narrates that Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Aws (RA) used to say, "Verily you people have seen no good apart from its causes and seen no evil apart from…
narrations.summary: Ziyaad bin Maahak reports Shaddaad bin Aws saying that goodness and evil lie in Jannah and Jahannam and that people should belong to the Aakhirah rather than this world, and Abu Dardaa then praised Shaddaad for combining knowledge with forbearance.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jundub Bajali (RA) once said, "Fear Allaah and recite the Qur'aan because it is light for a dark night and adornment for the day despite difficulties and poverty.…
narrations.summary: Jundub Bajali advises fearing Allaah, reciting the Qur'aan, valuing the Deen above wealth and health, and avoiding the shedding of a Muslim's blood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sulaym bin Aamir reports that they were in the company of Hadhrat Abu Umaamah Baahili when they once left the gates of Damascus to accompany a funeral procession.…
narrations.summary: At a funeral near Damascus, Abu Umaamah Baahili warns that the grave is a house of loneliness and darkness and describes how the hypocrites will be left without light on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Habeeb says, "I was with a group of people that went to see Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA). I found him to be a frail and old man whose wit and speech…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah Baahili tells a group that Allaah guarantees Jannah or reward for three kinds of people, warns of the debts settled on the bridge of Jahannam, and urges truthfulness and spending in the path of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr JU! once said, "People with Taqwa are simple, Ulema are leaders and being in their company is not only an act of Ibaadah, but something more.…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Busr says the people of taqwa are simple, the scholars are leaders, sitting in their company is worship, time shortens life while deeds are recorded, so one should prepare provisions for the return to Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sahl bin Sa'd (RA) reports that after he had lost his eyesight, Hadhrat Abu Usayd said, "O son of my brother! By Allaah! If you and I were at Badr and Allaah…
narrations.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that Abu Usayd, after losing his eyesight, said he had seen the angels come down into the valley at Badr to assist the Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) says, "Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) descended during the Battle of Badr in the form of Zubayr and wearing a yellow turban with a part of it hanging over his…
narrations.summary: Several reports describe angels taking the form of Companions at Badr, the angels wearing turbans, and Abu Raafi's account of Abu Lahab, Ummu Fadhl and the news of the Quraysh defeat at Badr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "The striking feature of (many of) the angels during the Battle of Badr was their white turbans (while others wore yellow…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas says the angels at Badr wore white turbans and only added to the Muslims' strength; Abu Raafi, freed slave of the Prophet, tells how Abu Lahab, who sent a substitute to Badr, struck him when news of the defeat arrived, how Ummu Fadhl hit Abu Lahab with a tent pole, and how Abu Lahab died of a plague within seven days.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Auf bin Abdur Rahmaan the freed slave of Ummu Burthun reports that a Sahabi who participated in the Battle of Hunayn on the side of the Kuffaar said, "When we…
narrations.summary: An unnamed Sahabi who fought against the Muslims at Hunayn says the enemy could not stand before the Muslims until strikingly handsome men appeared to the Prophet's side and told them to turn back, which led to their defeat.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Auf A'raabi reports from Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan the freed slave of Abu Burthun that a Sahabi who participated in the Battle of Hunayn said, "When we clashed with…
narrations.summary: Auf A'raabi reports from Abdur Rahmaan that a fighter at Hunayn saw the Prophet with strikingly handsome men who told them to turn back, which led to their defeat.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jubayr bin Mut'im (RA) says, "We were with Rasulullaah ﷺ during the Battle of Hunayn as the battle was raging. I then happened to look up and saw something like a…
narrations.summary: Jubayr bin Mut'im says that during Hunayn he saw what looked like a black blanket of ants come down between the two armies, and he was sure these were angels that decided the defeat.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Fadhl reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ gave the flag to Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Umayr (RA) during the Battle of Uhud. When Hadhrat Mus'ab was martyred, an…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Fadhl reports that at Uhud an angel in the form of Mus'ab bin Umayr took the flag after Mus'ab was martyred, and the Prophet realised it was an angel sent to help him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "It is as if I am actually looking at the dust rising from the Banu Ghanam street as Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) rode by at the time when Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Anas says he could see the dust rising from the street of Banu Ghanam as Jibra'eel rode past while the Prophet marched against Banu Quraizah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration recounts this incident of the battle against the Banu Quraizah tribe in detail. It states that after Rasulullaah ﷺ had downed his weapons (after…
narrations.summary: Another narration says that after the Battle of Khandaq Jibra'eel came to the Prophet and ordered the march against Banu Qurayzah, and the angels left in clouds of dust.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Suhayl bin Amr (RA) says, "Without doubt, it was during the Battle of Badr that I saw brilliant men riding spotted horses that glided between the ground and the…
narrations.summary: Suhayl bin Amr says that at Badr he saw brilliant men on spotted horses killing the Mushrikeen and taking them prisoner.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa (RA) and several other Sahabah (RA) report that when an Ansaari Sahabi brought Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) as a prisoner (during the Battle of Badr), Hadhrat Abbaas…
narrations.summary: Baraa and other Companions report that when an Ansaari took Abbaas prisoner at Badr, Abbaas said that man had not captured him, and the Prophet told the Ansaari that Allaah had sent a noble angel to help him.

narrations.excerpt: A similar narration from Hadhrat Ali (RA) states that when an Ansaari Sahabi brought Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) as a prisoner, Hadhrat Abbaas bin, Abdul Muttalib said, "O…
narrations.summary: A similar report from Ali says Abbaas described his captor as a handsome, bald-at-the-temples man on a spotted horse, and the Prophet told the Ansaari that a noble angel had helped him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that the person who took Hadhrat Abbaas Wa prisoner was Hadhrat Abu Yasr Ka'b bin Amr, who belonged to the Banu Salimah tribe.…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that Abbaas's captor at Badr was Abu Yasar Ka'b bin Amr, who said a man he had never seen helped him, and the Prophet said it was one of the noble angels.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that as a Muslim was pursuing a Mushrik soldier (during the Battle of Badr), he heard a whiplash from above and the voice of a…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that a Muslim pursuing a Mushrik heard a whiplash and a horseman calling his horse Hayzoom, and the Prophet confirmed it was an angel; a Sahabi of Banu Ghifaar adds how his cousin died of fear while watching Badr from a mountain.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) relates, "We were with Rasulullaah ﷺ in a battle and when we engaged the enemy in battle, I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'O Master of the Day of…
narrations.summary: Abu Talha says that in a battle, when the Prophet recited 'Only You do we worship and only from You do we seek help', he saw the angels strike the enemy from front and back.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah reports that his father Hadhrat Sahl (RA) once said to him, "Dear son! During the Battle of Badr, I saw that when any of us merely pointed (our…
narrations.summary: Abu Umaamah reports that his father Sahl bin Hunayf said that at Badr a Mushrik's head fell from his body as soon as a Muslim pointed a sword at it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waaqid Laythi (RA) says, "I would be following a man from the Mushrikeen to strike him a blow with my sword, only to find his head rolling even before my…
narrations.summary: Abu Waaqid Laythi says that at Badr a Mushrik's head rolled off before his sword could reach him, so he realised an angel had killed him, and Abu Dawood Maazini reports the same.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sahl bin Abu Hathma (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Barzah brought three heads of the Mushrikeen to Rasulullaah ﷺ during the Battle of Badr. Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Sahl bin Abu Hathma reports that Abu Barzah brought three Mushrik heads to the Prophet at Badr and said an angel killed one of them, and Haarith bin Simma reports that the Prophet said angels fought beside Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf, who had killed seven Mushrikeen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haarith bin Simma (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was in a gorge when he asked me whether I had seen Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf. 'Yes, O Rasulullaah ﷺ I replied, 'I saw him…
narrations.summary: Haarith bin Simma says the Prophet told him the angels were fighting beside Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf at Badr; Abdur Rahmaan, standing among seven fallen enemies, said he had killed only two of them himself.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was with Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) when he passed by a group of people who started jeering at Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that Jibra'eel pointed at those who ridiculed the Prophet, and the Prophet named them, after which each of them met a painful end.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that there was a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ called Hadhrat Abu Mu'liq (RA). He was a trader who traded both his own goods as well as those of…
narrations.summary: Anas narrates how Abu Mu'liq, threatened with death by a robber, prayed and made du'aa three times, and a rider with a spear, an angel from the fourth heaven, killed the robber.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Layth bin Sa'd reports that Hadhrat Zaid bin Haaritha (RA) once rented a mule from a man from Taa'if. The man however made a condition with him that Hadhrat Zaid…
narrations.summary: Layth bin Sa'd reports that Zaid bin Haaritha, led to ruins by a Taa'if man who meant to kill him, called out 'Yaa Arhamar Raahimeen' and a horseman sent from above killed the attacker.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ once heard a man's voice, he jumped up very fast and went outside to meet the man. I followed him out to see (who the…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet went out to a man on a Turkish horse whom she took to be Dihya Kalbi and told her it was Jibra'eel sent to order the march against Banu Qurayzah; Sa'eed bin Musayyib adds that the Prophet said the rider others saw was Jibra'eel shaking that fortress.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once went to visit a man from the Ansaar. When Rasulullaah ﷺ drew near to the house, he overheard the Ansaari…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that when the Prophet visited a sick Ansaari, he heard the Ansaari speaking to someone unseen, and the Prophet said it was Jibra'eel.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates, "1 was with my father when we went to. There was a man whispering something to because of which seemed to ignore my father. We…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas says he was with his father Abbaas when a man whispered to the Prophet, and the Prophet later said it was Jibra'eel, whom he had been too busy with to attend to them.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) once sent his son Hadhrat Abdullaah to for something. However, when Hadhrat Abdullaah found someone with, he returned…
narrations.summary: Another narration says Abbaas sent his son Abdullaah to the Prophet, that the man with him was Jibra'eel, and that the Prophet foretold Abdullaah would have great knowledge but go blind before he died.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa bin Ruwaym reports that a Sahabi by the name of Hadhrat Irbaadh bin Saariyah had become extremely old and was wishing that his soul could be taken. He would…
narrations.summary: Urwa bin Ruwaym reports that the very old Irbaadh bin Saariyah, who prayed to die, met a young man in the Damascus Masjid who taught him a du'aa and said he was the angel Roobaa'eel.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mutarrif bin Abdullaah reports that Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) once said to him, "Listen, O Mutarrif! (During the course of my illness) The angels used to…
narrations.summary: Mutarrif bin Abdullaah reports that Imraan bin Husayn said the angels had greeted him during his illness until he had himself branded, and Qataadah adds that the angels used to shake his hand until then.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salam bin Atiyya Asadi reports that when Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) was in the throes of death, a man came to see him. "Dear angel," Hadhrat Salmaan said, "Please be…
narrations.summary: Salam bin Atiyya Asadi reports that when Salmaan was dying he asked an angel to be gentle with him, and the angel replied that it is gentle with every Mu'min.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b is once made a resolve saying, "I shall go to the Masjid, perform salaah and then praise Allaah in such terms that…
narrations.summary: Anas says Ubay bin Ka'b resolved to praise Allaah in the Masjid, then heard an unseen voice behind him saying words of praise and repentance, and reported it to the Prophet, who said it was Jibra'eel.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "Whoever dislikes Umar dislikes me and whoever loves Umar loves me. Verily, Allaah boasts about…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that the Prophet said whoever dislikes Umar dislikes him, that Allaah boasts of Umar, and that a Muhaddath, one on whose tongue the angels speak, would be Umar if there is one in this Ummah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Hulays reports, "After defeating the Persians (in battle), we had laid siege to their fortress of Buharseer when one of their emissaries approached us…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Hulays reports that after the siege of Buharseer, Aswad bin Qutba (Abu Mufazzir) answered the Persian emissary with words he did not know he was saying, and the enemy fled, which the Persians took as the speech of angels.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports that one night when Hadhrat Usayd bin Hudhayr was reciting Qur'aan in his silo, his horse started to skip about. When he again…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that Usayd bin Hudhayr saw a cloud of lights while reciting in his silo and the Prophet said they were listening angels; a second report says an angel announced the death of Sa'd bin Muaadh, and the Prophet hurried to his funeral.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Usayd (RA) said, "When I turned, I saw something like lanterns suspended between the sky and the ground. I said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Usayd (RA) reports seeing lantern-like lights between the sky and the ground while reciting the Qur'aan; the Prophet ﷺ explains they were angels who had come down to listen, and a second report says they had drawn close because of his voice.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mahmood bin Labeed reports that Hadhrat Handhala bin Abu Aamir who belonged to the Banu Amr bin Auf tribe met Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan bin Harb in combat during the…
narrations.summary: Mahmood bin Labeed reports that Handhala bin Abu Aamir was struck down by Shaddaad bin Aswad at Uhud, and the Prophet ﷺ told the Companions that the angels were bathing him because he had left for battle without taking his ritual bath.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mahmood bin Labeed also reports that when Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh was struck (by an arrow) in his radial artery during the Battle of Khandaq, he fell seriously…
narrations.summary: Mahmood bin Labeed and Aasim bin Umar bin Qataadah report that the angels washed the body of Sa'd bin Mu'aadh after his death from an arrow wound at Khandaq, and the Prophet ﷺ hurried to the funeral, saying he feared the angels would reach Sa'd first as they had reached Handhala.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that when his father passed away, he lifted the cloth covering his father's face and started weeping. When the people forbade him from doing…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that when his father died he uncovered his face and wept, and the Prophet remarked that the angels would keep shading his father with their wings until the body was carried.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salamah bin Aslam (RA) says, "We were standing at the door of the room waiting to enter after Rasulullaah ﷺ. Although there was none in the room besides the…
narrations.summary: Salamah bin Aslam says the room where Sa'd bin Muaadh's body lay was full of angels, and other reports say seventy thousand angels attended his funeral while hypocrites mocked how light the bier was.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "For (the funeral of) Sa'd bin Mu'aadh, seventy thousand angels came down who had never tread upon earth…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet saying that seventy thousand angels came down for the funeral of Sa'd bin Muaadh, and that if anyone could be saved from the squeezing of the grave it would have been Sa'd.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ibraheem narrates that when the funeral bier of Hadhrat Sa'd was being carried, some of the Munaafiqeen mocked, "How light is this bier of Sa'd!"…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Ibraheem reports that some hypocrites mocked how light Sa'd bin Muaadh's bier was, and the Prophet said seventy thousand angels had come down for his funeral.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA) was a large and well-built man. Therefore, when he passed away, the Munaafiqeen walking behind his funeral bier…
narrations.summary: Hasan reports that hypocrites mocked how light Sa'd bin Mu'aadh's bier was, and the Prophet said it was light because angels were carrying it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Hayda Qashayri (RA) reports that he went to see Rasulullaah ﷺ and when he was brought into Rasulullaah ﷺ's presence, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Listen…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Hayda reports that after the Prophet had prayed for drought or fear to be sent on his people, the drought kept uprooting him and fear of the Muslims filled his heart, so he came to accept Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saa'ib bin Yasaar reports that they asked Hadhrat Yazeed bin Aamir Suwaa'ee what the fear was like that Allaah cast into the hearts of the Mushrikeen during the…
narrations.summary: Saa'ib bin Yasaar reports that he asked Yazeed bin Aamir Suwaa'ee, who had fought with the Mushrikeen at Hunayn, to describe the fear Allaah cast into their hearts, and Yazeed imitated it by rattling pebbles on a platter.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam and others reports that Hadhrat Suraaqa bin Maalik (who was then not a Muslim) thrice cast arrows to decide whether or not to pursue Rasulullaah ﷺ.…
narrations.summary: Suraaqa bin Maalik, still a non-Muslim at the time, pursued the Prophet during the Hijrah, and his horse's legs sank into the sand after the Prophet made du'aa.

narrations.excerpt: A narration from Hadhrat Umayr bin Is'haaq states that Hadhrat Suraaqa (RA) pleaded, "O you two men! If you pray to Allaah on my behalf, I shall give you an undertaking…
narrations.summary: Suraaqa pleads for his horse to be freed, the Prophet and Abu Bakr make du'aa, and Suraaqa then turns back the pursuers and becomes a defender of the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Arbad bin Qais and Aamir bin Tufayl once arrived in Madinah and came to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ was seated at the…
narrations.summary: Arbad bin Qais and Aamir bin Tufayl plot to kill the Prophet, Arbad is struck by lightning, and Aamir dies after developing a swelling on his throat.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Haarith bin Badal (RA) says, "I participated against Rasulullaah ﷺ in the Battle of Hunayn. (During the beginning) When all the Sahabah (RA) apart from Abbaas bin…
narrations.summary: At the Battle of Hunayn the Prophet threw earth or pebbles at the enemy, and they were defeated as if every tree and stone were chasing them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hakeem bin Hizaam (RA) says, "(While fighting on the side of the Mushrikeen during the Battle of Badr) We heard a sound booming from the heavens to the earth that…
narrations.summary: Hakeem bin Hizaam relates that at Badr, after hearing a sound like stones falling on a platter, the Mushrikeen were defeated when the Prophet threw pebbles at them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hakeem bin Hizaam (RA) also says, "During the Battle of Badr, Rasulullaah ﷺ was instructed to take a handful of pebbles, face us and throw it saying, 'May your…
narrations.summary: Hakeem bin Hizaam relates that the Prophet was instructed to throw a handful of pebbles at the Mushrikeen at Badr, and that Allaah then revealed Surah Anfaal verse 17.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ asked Hadhrat Ali (RA) to hand him a handful of pebbles. When Hadhrat Ali (RA) handed them over, Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that at Badr the Prophet took pebbles from Ali and threw them into the enemy's faces, and that Allaah then revealed Surah Anfaal verse 17.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yazeed bin Aamir Suwaa'ee (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ took, a handful of soil, faced the enemy and then threw it saying, "Get back! May your faces be…
narrations.summary: Yazeed bin Aamir Suwaa'ee reports that the Prophet threw a handful of soil at the enemy at Badr, after which the Mushrikeen complained of dust in their eyes.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) says, "The enemy appeared so few in our eyes during the Battle of Badr that my companion standing beside me said, 'Do you think that…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood recalls that the enemy looked very few in number at Badr, until a captured man revealed they were a thousand strong.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Jubayr reports that on the occasion of the Battle of Khandaq, those who marched to Madinah were Abu Sufyaan bin Harb and the Quraysh and Kinaanah whom…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Jubayr describes the combined forces that marched on Madinah at Khandaq, and how Allaah sent a wind and angels against them so that they fled.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Humayd bin Hilaal narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ had an unratified pact with the Banu Qurayzah tribe. They however broke the pact by assisting the Mushrikeen when they…
narrations.summary: Humayd bin Hilaal reports that Banu Qurayzah broke their pact by joining the Mushrikeen, and that Allaah sent an army and wind that routed the Mushrikeen while Qurayzah stayed in their fortress.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that the easterly wind approached the northerly wind during the night of the Battle of Ahzaab and said, "Go and assist…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that during the Battle of Ahzaab the east wind was sent to assist the Prophet, because the north wind refused to travel by night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) reports that a man (from the Mushrikeen) said during the Battle of Uhud, "O Allaah! If Muhammad is upon the truth, let me sink into the ground." He…
narrations.summary: Buraydah reports that a Mushrik who prayed for Muhammad's falsehood to be shown sank into the ground at Uhud, and Naafi bin Aasim reports that the man who wounded the Prophet's face was gored to death by a ram.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naafi bin Aasim says that the man who injured Rasulullaah ﷺ's face was Abdullaah bin Qami'ah who belonged to the Hudhayl tribe. Allaah made a ram attack him and…
narrations.summary: Naafi bin Aasim says that the man who injured the Prophet's face was Abdullaah bin Qami'ah, and Allaah sent a ram that gored him to death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mughaffal Muzani (RA) narrates, "We were with Rasulullaah ﷺ at Hudaybiyyah..." He then proceeds to recount the incident of the Treaty of…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mughaffal recounts that at Hudaybiyyah thirty armed Quraysh youths were blinded by the Prophet's curse, were then released, and Surah Fath verse 24 was revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaadhaan narrates that when Hadhrat Ali (RA) once narrated a Hadith, someone accused him of lying. "May 1 curse you if it is you who are lying?" Hadhrat Ali (RA)…
narrations.summary: Zaadhaan reports that when Ali was accused of lying, he challenged the accuser to a curse, and the man lost his sight before leaving the gathering.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Ali (RA) once narrated a Hadith, someone accused him of lying. The man had hardly stood up from the gathering and he was…
narrations.summary: Ammaar reports the same incident, in which the man who accused Ali of lying was blinded by Ali's curse, and a second Zaadhaan account is included.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Marwaan once sent some people to Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Zaid (RA) to discuss a claim that a woman named Arwa bint Uwais had made…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Zaid prays that Arwa bint Uwais, who falsely claimed his land, be blinded if she is lying, and she falls into her well and dies; a flood then proves his claim.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazam narrates that a woman named Arwa once sought judgement from Marwaan bin Hakam against Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Zaid. Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazam reports that Sa'eed bin Zaid called on Allaah against a woman named Arwa who falsely claimed he had wronged her; a flood then showed the boundary in his favour, and within a month Arwa went blind and fell into her well.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Utaaridi said, "Never revile Hadhrat Ali (RA) or any member of Rasulullaah ﷺ's family because a neighbour of ours from Balhujaym once scoffed, 'Can you not…
narrations.summary: Abu Utaaridi warns against reviling Ali or the Prophet's family, reporting that a man from Balhujaym who scoffed at Husayn bin Ali lost his sight.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to recite the Qur'aan in the Masjidul Haraam. One day, he was reciting Qur'aan loudly, which irritated…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas recounts that Quraysh men who tried to seize the Prophet in the Masjidul Haraam were blinded, then had their sight restored by his du'aa after pleading by family ties, and that Surah Yaaseen verses were revealed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qataadah bin Nu'maan (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ received a bow as a gift, which he gave to me during the Battle of Uhud. I then continued firing arrows standing in…
narrations.summary: Qataadah bin Nu'maan recounts losing his eye while shielding the Prophet at Uhud, and the Prophet restored it so that it became the better and sharper of his two eyes.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mahmood bin Labeed reports from Hadhrat Qataadah (RA) that when his eye was struck (by an arrow) during the Battle of Uhud, it fell out on to his cheek.…
narrations.summary: Mahmood bin Labeed reports from Qataadah that his eye was knocked out at Uhud and fell onto his cheek, and the Prophet put it back in its socket, after which it became the better of his two eyes.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that that eye turned out to be the better of the two and the one with sharper vision.
narrations.summary: Another narration confirms that the eye became the better and sharper of the two.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aasim bin Umar bin Qataadah reports that when Hadhrat Qataadah bin Nu'maan's eye was struck during the Battle of Uhud and it fell on to his cheek, the other…
narrations.summary: Aasim bin Umar bin Qataadah reports that the Companions wanted to cut off Qataadah's dislodged eye, and the Prophet reset it with his palm so that Qataadah could no longer tell which eye had been wounded.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaydah narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA)'s eye was injured during the Battle of Uhud, Rasulullaah ﷺ merely applied his saliva to it and it became the…
narrations.summary: Ubaydah reports that the Prophet applied his saliva to Abu Dharr's injured eye at Uhud, and it became the better of his two eyes.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rifaa'ah bin Raafl (RA) reports, "During the Battle of Badr, an arrow pierced my eye. Rasulullaah ﷺ applied some of his saliva to it and made du'aa, because of…
narrations.summary: Rifaa'ah bin Raafi reports that the Prophet's saliva and du'aa removed the pain of an arrow in his eye at Badr, and Habeeb bin Fuwayk reports that the Prophet restored his father's sight with saliva.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Habeeb bin Fuwayk narrates, "My father was taken to Rasulullaah ﷺ because his eyes had become completely white and he was unable to see anything. When Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Habeeb bin Fuwayk reports that his father's eyes turned completely white after his leg fell on a snake's egg, and that when the Prophet applied saliva to the eyes his father could see at once.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Ibraheem narrates that Hadhrat Zinneera (RA) was a Roman lady who accepted Islaam. When she became blind, the Mushrikeen told her that it was (their…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Ibraheem reports that the freed Roman woman Zinneera regained her sight after she rejected Laat and Uzza, and Anas reports from Ummu Haani that Abu Bakr had freed her and that her sight was restored.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hishaam bin Aas Umawi (RA) reports, "Another person and I were sent (by the Khalifah Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)) to invite Heraclius the Emperor of Rome to Islaam. We…
narrations.summary: Hishaam bin Aas recounts his mission, sent by Abu Bakr, to invite Heraclius to Islaam, the palace shaking at the takbeer, and Heraclius showing them pictures of the prophets and then of the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jubayr bin Mut'im (RA) says, "(When I was taken by some Christians to a church) they (pointed to some pictures and) asked, 'Do you see him?' When I looked, I saw…
narrations.summary: Jubayr bin Mut'im recounts that Christians in a church showed him pictures of the Prophet and of Abu Bakr, and said that Abu Bakr would be the Khalifah after him.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Jubayr (RA) asked, "And who is this person following him." The Christian replied, "There was a Nabi after every Nabi that came,…
narrations.summary: Jubayr bin Mut'im relates that a Christian told him there is no Nabi after the Prophet, and that the man following the Prophet in the picture is his Khalifah, which Jubayr confirmed was Abu Bakr.

narrations.excerpt: Some scholars from the Ghassaan and Banu Qayn tribes reports that as a reward for their patience during the battle for Hims, Allaah caused an earthquake to shake the…
narrations.summary: Scholars from the Ghassaan and Banu Qayn report that, as a reward for patience at Hims, Allaah shook the city with an earthquake when the Muslims called out Allaahu Akbar, and the Romans were humbled.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once dispatched an army, he appointed someone by the name of Hadhrat Saariyah as its commander.…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar called out 'The mountain, O Saariyah, the mountain!' during a sermon, and Saariyah's army heard it, turned to the mountain and were granted victory.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that while Hadhrat Umar (RA) was delivering a sermon, he suddenly called out, "The mountain, O Saariyah, the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar gives further accounts of Umar's call to Saariyah, including Umar's explanation of the vision behind it and Ali's defence of Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that the people asked Hadhrat Ali (RA), "Did you hear Umar say, 'O Saariyah!' while he was delivering the lecture on the pulpit?" "Shame on you…
narrations.summary: Ali tells people not to question Umar for calling out 'O Saariyah' in his sermon, since Umar always has a valid reason; Umar says the idea of using the mountain for defence came to his heart and he spoke hoping one of Allaah's servants would convey it to the army.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Haarith reports that because Hadhrat Umar (RA) was comfortable with Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA), it was Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf who…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Haarith reports that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf asked Umar why he made the call, Umar explained the danger his army faced near a mountain, and Saariyah's letter confirmed the Muslims' victory after they turned to it.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was asked why he made the statement, he replied, "By Allaah! I said only what was placed on my tongue (by Allaah). "
narrations.summary: Asked why he made the call, Umar replied that he said only what Allaah placed on his tongue.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Izzah bint Aas bin Abu Qirsaafah reports that the Romans once took one of Hadhrat Abu Qirsaafah (RA)'s sons prisoner. When the time arrived for every salaah,…
narrations.summary: Izzah bint Aas reports that Abu Qirsaafah, whose son had been taken captive by the Romans, would climb a wall at each prayer time and call 'Salaah', and his son heard him from Roman territory.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that after Rasulullaah ﷺ had passed away, the people bathing his body fell into a dispute. They then heard a voice, the source…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas and Aa'isha report that after the Prophet's death, an unidentified voice told the people to bathe his body in his garments, and they did so.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Nabi ﷺ once appointed Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) to command a naval expedition. As his vessei was travelling one night,…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that during a naval expedition led by Abu Moosa Ash'ari, under the Prophet's appointment, a voice from above promised that whoever stays thirsty for Allaah on a hot day will be given drink on the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Burda reports that Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) said, "We were once out on a naval expedition when the wind was pleasant and the sails were filled. We then…
narrations.summary: Abu Burdah reports Abu Moosa Ash'ari's account of hearing a voice at sea promise that whoever fasts on a hot day solely for Allaah's pleasure will be given drink on Qiyaamah, and that Abu Moosa afterwards sought out the hottest days to fast.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Jubayr reports, "I was present for the funeral of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas when he passed away in Taa'if. A (white) bird, the likes of which had…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Jubayr reports that at the funeral of Ibn Abbaas in Taa'if a white bird entered his shroud, and that unseen voices recited Surah Fajr beside the grave.

narrations.excerpt: A similar narration from Hadhrat Maymoon bin Mahraan states, "After the sand was levelled over his grave, we heard a voice but could not identify whom it was coming…
narrations.summary: Maymoon bin Mahraan reports that after the sand was levelled over the grave, an unidentified voice was heard.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds, "When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) passed away and his body was shrouded, a white bird arrived speedily and entered between the shroud. The…
narrations.summary: Another account adds that a white bird entered Ibn Abbaas's shroud, and Ikrimah explained it as the eyesight the Prophet had promised would return to him at death, and that the verses recited at the grave were heard by all present.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Khuraym bin Faatik (RA) once said to Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA), "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Should I relate to you how I…
narrations.summary: Khuraym bin Faatik tells Umar how a Jinn called him to Islaam and guided him to Madinah, where Umar accepted Uthmaan's testimony to a hadith Khuraym had quoted.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Khuraym (RA) recited the following couplets (which mean): "Guide me along, guide you May you never suffer any hunger, O person, nor…
narrations.summary: Khuraym bin Faatik recites the Jinn's verses of guidance again, and Ibn Abbaas later tells Umar the story.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "Whenever I heard Hadhrat Umar say, 'I think that this is like this,' it would always be exactly as he thought. However, we were…
narrations.summary: Umar questions the former fortune-teller Sawaad bin Qaarib, who relates how his Jinn told him of a Nabi from Luway bin Ghaalib, and how he came to the Prophet and accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: A narration from Hadhrat Baraa (RA) states that Hadhrat Sawaad (RA) was staying in India when the Jinn came to him that night. The rest of the narration is like the one…
narrations.summary: A narration from Baraa says that Sawaad bin Qaarib was in India when a Jinn came to him; Muhammad bin Ka'b reports that Sawaad, having heard the call of Islaam, went to Madinah after the Prophet had migrated, recited verses to the Prophet, who smiled and called him successful.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abbaas bin Mirdaas Sulami (RA) relates, "My becoming a Muslim began when my father was on his deathbed and he made a bequest that I take care of his idol called…
narrations.summary: Abbaas bin Mirdaas hears a voice from his idol Dimaad announcing the Prophet's coming, destroys the idol, and with his tribe goes to the Prophet and accepts Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) reports that the first news of Rasulullaah (Jill's Nabuwwaat reached Madinah because of a Jinn that a particular woman from Madinah had…
narrations.summary: Jaabir and Ali bin Husayn report that a Jinn serving a woman in Madinah brought news of the Prophet's coming and his prohibition of adultery.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) reports, "We once left with a caravan to Shaam before Rasulullaah ﷺ announced his Nabuwwaat. We had just entered the borders of Shaam when…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan recounts that a fortune-teller in Shaam said his Jinn could not enter because Ahmed had appeared, and that when he returned to Makkah the Prophet had already announced his Nabuwwaat.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaahid reports, "It was during the Battle of Rhodes when an old man called Ibn Isa who had lived during the Period of Ignorance related to me, "I was busy…
narrations.summary: Mujaahid reports an old man's account of hearing a voice from a cow's belly call people to say that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah, during the Period of Ignorance.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that a caller from the Jinn once announced from the Abu Qubays mountain in Makkah (the following couplets which mean): "May…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports how a Shaytaan named Mis'ar stirred the Quraysh against the Muslims through an idol, and how a Jinn named Samhaj, whom the Prophet named Abdullaah after he believed, killed him; Ali then prayed for the Jinn.
