narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mahmood reports that several men from the Khath'am tribe said, "We were idol worshippers and amongst the factors that called us towards Islaam was…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mahmood reports that men of the Khath'am tribe accepted Islaam after a Jinn's call, heard while they stood by their idol, announced the Prophet's Nabuwwaat.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tameem Daari (RA) says, "I was in Shaam at the time when Rasulullaah ﷺ started to announce his Nabuwwaat. I was out to do some work- once when night caught up…
narrations.summary: Tameem Daari recounts hearing a Jinn in Shaam announce the Prophet's coming, then consulting a monk who confirmed it, and then accepting Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa (RA) reports that Hadhrat Hajjaaj bin Alaat Bahzi Sulami was introduced to Islaam when he once left for Makkah with a group of riders from his…
narrations.summary: Waathila bin Asqa reports that Hajaaj bin Ilaat, frightened in a valley at night, heard a Jinn recite a verse of Surah Rahmaan, then went to the Prophet and accepted Islaam, while Aas bin Waail dismissed the story among the Quraysh.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) reports that a group of people once left for Makkah but got lost on the way. When they were close to death, they donned their burial shrouds…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b reports that a Jinn who had heard the Prophet guided a group of lost travellers, who were close to death, to water and the road.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Shuyaym who belonged to the Banu Saham bin Murrah tribe reports that his father was with the army of Uyaynah bin Hisn when they arrived to assist the…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Shuyaym reports that his father heard an unseen voice in Uyaynah's army warning that their families were under attack, so they all turned back during the Battle of Khaybar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I was asleep one night when a Shaytaan came to interfere with me. I grabbed him by the throat and could…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet's account of seizing a Shaytaan at night and releasing him after recalling the du'aa of Sulaymaan, and Abu Dardaa gives a similar account.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) reports that when he heard that Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal had captured a Shaytaan during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, he approached him and asked, "I…
narrations.summary: Buraydah reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal caught a Shaytaan stealing Sadaqah dates, and the Shaytaan taught him Aayatul Kursi and the end of Surah Baqarah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once appointed me to look after the zakaah of Ramadhaan. However, someone came and started helping himself to the food.…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah catches a Shaytaan taking from the zakaah of Ramadhaan, who teaches him Aayatul Kursi, and Abu Ayyoob Ansaari tells of a Jinn stealing his dates.

narrations.excerpt: A similar narration has already been quoted about Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) in the chapter concerning Dhikr.
narrations.summary: Cross-reference only: it notes that a similar narration about Ubay bin Ka'b has already been quoted in the chapter on Dhikr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "When a Shaytaan once met a Sahabi and wrestled him, the Sahabi floored him and even bit his…
narrations.summary: Abu Waa'il reports Ibn Mas'ood's account of a Companion who wrestled a Shaytaan three times and learned a verse of Surah Baqarah from him, and Ibn Mas'ood names that Companion as Umar.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "When a man from the companions of Rasulullaah ﷺ met a man from the Jinn and they wrestled, the human…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood tells of a Companion who floored a Jinn three times, learned Aayatul Kursi from him, and whom he identifies as Umar.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mujaahid says, "We were always told that the Shayaateen were chained up during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Umar (RA). It was only after his martyrdom that they were…
narrations.summary: Mujaahid says the Shaytaans were chained during Umar's khilaafah and were released only after his martyrdom.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aamir bin Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr was returning from Umrah with a group of people belonging to the Quraysh. They were…
narrations.summary: Aamir bin Abdullaah reports that Abdullaah bin Zubayr rebuked a Jinn he met at Yanaasib, and that his companions then fell from their animals.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sulaymaan Daaraani reports that it was a moonlit night when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) went out on his animal and camped at Tabook. As he turned around…
narrations.summary: Abu Sulaymaan Daaraani reports that Abdullaah bin Zubayr, camped at Tabook, lunged at an old man on his animal, who then warned him, and Ibn Zubayr rebuked him in return.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Suwayd bin Zaid reports, "When I once saw Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) sitting alone in the Masjid, I took advantage of the opportunity and went to sit beside him. When…
narrations.summary: Suwayd bin Zaid reports Abu Dharr's account of pebbles in the Prophet's hands glorifying Allaah in the hands of Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan, and the Prophet said this denotes the successors of Nubuwwah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ also gave the pebbles to Hadhrat Ali and (after engaging in Tasbeeh) they stopped only after he had put them down. Yet another…
narrations.summary: Abu Dharr adds that the pebbles also glorified Allaah in Ali's hand, and in the hands of the other Companions they stayed silent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "We viewed the miracles of Rasulullaah ﷺ as a source of blessings, while you people only see them as threats (to the…
narrations.summary: Ibn Mas'ood recounts the Prophet's miracles: water gushing from between his fingers, and food glorifying Allaah as it was eaten.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to lean on a date palm when standing (to deliver the sermon) on Fridays. Someone from the Ansaar made a…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that the palm trunk the Prophet used to lean on wept like a child when he left it for the new pulpit.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when the pulpit was built and Rasulullaah ﷺ was standing upon it, the Sahabah (RA) heard the trunk of the palm make a sound like that of a…
narrations.summary: Further reports describe the palm trunk moaning like a camel until the Prophet came back and embraced it, and Hasan used to tell this to remind people of their longing for the Prophet.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari reports that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) was with Hadhrat Abu Dardaa when the latter was busy lighting a fire beneath his pot. Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA)…
narrations.summary: Abul Bakhtari reports that Salmaan and Abu Dardaa saw a plate and the food on it glorify Allaah while they ate, and Qais adds that they often reminded each other of it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ja'far bin Abu Imraan reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas once heard the fire say, "Me as well." When someone asked him what this meant, he…
narrations.summary: Ja'far bin Abu Imraan reports that Abdullaah bin Amr heard a fire say it too seeks Allaah's protection from the immense Fire.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Umar (RA) Hears the Words of a Devout Youngster Hadhrat Yahya bin Ayyoob Khuzaa'ee narrates that he heard from someone that there lived a youngster during the…
narrations.summary: Yahya bin Ayyoob reports that a devoted youth who fell unconscious on remembering Allaah when tempted by a woman later died, and that when Umar recited a verse at his grave, the youth answered that he had been given both gardens of Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that the youngster said, "Dear under Go to Umar, convey my Salaams to him and ask him what the reward will be for the person who fears standing…
narrations.summary: A variant says the youth asked Umar to pass on his greetings and to ask about the reward for fearing standing before one's Rabb, and Umar then told the grave it would have two gardens.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Himyar reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by Baqee Gharqad (the graveyard of Madinah), he said, "As Salaamu Alaykum, O people of the…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Himyar reports that Umar greeted the dead at Baqee Gharqad, and a voice replied that the deeds sent ahead were found and the wealth left behind was lost.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates, "I was passing by the fringe of the plain of Badr when I was surprised to see a man emerge from a hole. He had a chain tied…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports seeing Abu Jahal in a pit near Badr being punished, which the Prophet confirmed would last until the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that the Ansaari Hadhrat Zaid bin Khaarija who belonged to the Banu Haarith bin Khazraj tribe passed away during the Khilaafah of…
narrations.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Zaid bin Khaarija spoke after death, naming the Prophet and the first three Khalifas and foretelling the trials to come, and that a man of Banu Khatmah did the same.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Basheer (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Zaid bin Khaarija was walking in one of the alleyways of Madinah some time between the Zuhr and Asr salaahs when he…
narrations.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer reports that Zaid bin Khaarija spoke from beneath his covering, affirming the Prophet's prophethood and praising Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan, and foretelling trials.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration, Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Basheer (RA) says, "When Zaid bin Khaarija passed away, I was waiting for Uthmaan to come, thinking that he would perform two…
narrations.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer says that while waiting for Uthmaan to lead the prayer, Zaid bin Khaarija raised his shroud, greeted them and spoke, asking about Abdullaah bin Rawaaha and his fathers; a variant adds more of his speech and a verse about Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Zaid (RA)'s corpse said, " The one in the middle is the strongest of the three. He never feared the reproach of those who reproach…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Khaarija's corpse speaks after death: it praises the one in the middle of three rulers as one who never feared blame, says Uthmaan will be Ameer and that strife will follow, urges obedience to the ruler, calls for Abdullaah bin Rawaaha, asks after his father Khaarija, and recites a verse on Jahannam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Basheer (RA) says, "When a man from amongst us (Ansaar) called Zaid bin Khaarija passed away, we shrouded him and I stood up to perform salaah. Just…
narrations.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer reports Zaid bin Khaarija's corpse speaking about the strength of the Khulafaa, Uthmaan's forgiveness and the coming trials, and greeting the Prophet and Abdullaah bin Rawaaha while asking after his father Khaarija bin Zaid.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) says, "When we once went to visit an ailing youngster of the Ansaar, he happened to pass away very quickly. We closed his eyes and drew a…
narrations.summary: Anas bin Maalik recounts how a Muhaajir mother's du'aa over her dead son brought him back to life, and he ate with them; a variant identifies her as Ummu Saa'ib.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that the lady was Hadhrat Ummu Saa'ib and that she was extremely old and blind.
narrations.summary: Another narration identifies the old, blind woman in the story as Ummu Saa'ib.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abduilaah bin Aun narrates that Hadhrat Anas (RA) once said, "I have witnessed three occurrences in this Ummah that would have been unmatched by any other nation…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Aun reports Anas bin Maalik's account that when the Prophet sent him to tell a Muhaajir woman her son had died, her du'aa brought the boy back to life, and he lived until the Prophet died.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Nadhrah reports that Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) said, "The night before the Battle of Uhud was fought, my father called for me and said, 'I feel that I…
narrations.summary: Abu Nadhra reports Jaabir bin Abdullaah's account that his father, the first to be martyred at Uhud, asked him to settle his debts and treat his sisters well, and that his body was found unchanged six months later.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Zubayr reports that Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) said, "When Mu'aawiya intended digging a canal, we were told to move the bodies of our martyrs who had been martyred…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports that the Uhud martyrs, exhumed about forty years later during Mu'aawiya's canal digging, were still fresh, including his father Abdullaah bin Amr and Amr bin Jamooh who shared one grave.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "When Mu'aawiya (RA) started to dig the canal near the martyrs of Uhud forty years after the battle, we were summoned to (move) them (from their…
narrations.summary: Jaabir reports that when the canal was dug near the Uhud martyrs, a spade struck Hamzah's foot and it bled after forty years.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Shurahbeel narrates that one of the Sahabah (RA) took a handful of sand from the grave of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA) and when he opened his fist,…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Shurahbeel narrates that a Companion took sand from the grave of Sa'd bin Mu'aadh, found it to be musk, and the Prophet exclaimed Subhaanallaah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states, "Someone took a handful of sand from the grave of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA) and then left. When he looked at it afterwards, he discovered…
narrations.summary: Another report says that someone took sand from the grave of Sa'd bin Mu'aadh and found it had become musk.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) says, "I was amongst those who dug the grave of Sa'd bin Mu'aadh. Each time we shovelled out some sand, the fragrance of musk wafted on to…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri says that while digging Sa'd bin Mu'aadh's grave, the fragrance of musk rose with each shovelful of sand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that after many Sahabah (RA) were martyred at Bir Ma'oonah and Hadhrat Amr bin Umayyah (RA) was taken prisoner, Aamir bin Tufayl pointed to one…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that after the Bir Ma'oonah massacre, Aamir bin Tufayl saw the martyr Aamir bin Fuhayrah lifted to the sky, and the Prophet told the Sahabah the martyrs were pleased with their Rabb.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that the person who killed Hadhrat Aamir bin Fuhayrah was a man named Jabbaar bin Sulma Kalbi. When he stabbed Hadhrat Aamir with his spear,…
narrations.summary: Another report says that the man who killed Aamir bin Fuhayrah, Jabbaar bin Sulma, asked what success Aamir had meant and then accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa reports that because the body of Hadhrat Aamir bin Fuhayrah could not be found afterwards, the Sahabah (RA) were convinced that the angels had buried him.
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that because Aamir bin Fuhayrah's body could not be found, the Sahabah believed the angels had buried him.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'The angels buried him and his soul was taken to the lttiyyeen (the /dace where the souls of the righteous are taken)."…
narrations.summary: The Prophet says the angels buried Aamir bin Fuhayrah and his soul was taken to 'Illiyyeen, and Aamir bin Tufayl describes seeing that Sahabi lifted between earth and sky.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Umayyah (RA) relates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ sent me alone as a spy to the Quraysh. I came to the pole where Khubayb was crucified and, keeping a lookout for…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Umayyah reports untying Khubayb's body from the cross and finding it gone into the earth, and Dahhaak reports the Prophet sending Miqdaad and Zubayr who found the body fresh and the ground then took it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dahhaak narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched Hadhrat Miqdaad and Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) to remove the body of Hadhrat Khubayb from the pole upon which he was…
narrations.summary: Dahhaak reports that the Prophet sent Miqdaad and Zubayr to take Khubayb bin Adi's body down from the pole; the body was still fresh, Zubayr had to leave it when the Mushrikeen closed in, and the ground took it in, which is why Khubayb was called the one the ground took in.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) once said, "I have witnessed three occurrences in this Ummah that would have been unmatched by any other nation had they occurred amongst the Bani…
narrations.summary: Anas and Abu Hurayrah report that the grave of Alaa bin Hadhrami was found empty after burial, filled with light, or could not be located again.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah JU states, "When he passed away, we/buried him in soft sand but we had not gone far when it occurred to us that wilcf animals…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Companions buried Alaa bin Hadhrami in soft sand, went back to protect the body from wild animals and could not find it, then dug a grave without a recess and could not find that grave again.

narrations.excerpt: The incident of Hadhrat Khubayb bin Adi (RA) has been quoted in detail'1'. The narration from Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent an expedition…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet sent Aasim bin Thaabit on an expedition, and Allaah protected his body from the Quraysh with a swarm of wasps.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Urwa (RA) states that when the Mushrikeen were about to cut off his head to send to the other Mushrikeen in Makkah, Allaah sent a swarm of…
narrations.summary: Urwa reports that when the Mushrikeen tried to cut off Aasim bin Thaabit's head, Allaah sent wasps that stung them and stopped them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hamzah bin Abu Usayd (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once went to the graveyard of Baqee for the funeral of an Ansaari. There however lay in the path, a wolf with…
narrations.summary: Hamzah bin Abu Usayd reports that the Prophet, going to a funeral at Baqee, told a wolf blocking the path to take its share, and advised a fixed one goat per year from each flock of forty or more.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mutallib bin Abdullaah bin Hantab reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was in Madinah one day when a wolf arrived and stood before him. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "This is the…
narrations.summary: Mutallib bin Abdullaah reports a wolf coming to the Prophet in Madinah with a proposal for a share of the flocks, and a Juhaynah man reports a delegation of about a hundred wolves that the Prophet sent away.

narrations.excerpt: Rasulullaah Slip's freed slave Hadhrat Safeenah (RA) says, "I was once on board a ship when it shipwrecked. 1 managed to cling on to one of its planks, which carried me…
narrations.summary: Safeenah, the Prophet's freed slave, reports that a lion guided him out of the forest after a shipwreck, and in another account the lion led him when he lost his way.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Safeenah (RA) says, "We were once at sea when we were shipwrecked. (When we managed to make our way to land) We were lost and did not know…
narrations.summary: Safeenah says that after a shipwreck he and his companions lost their way, and a lion walked ahead of him to the main road, then nudged him as if to bid them farewell.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Munkadir reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ's freed slave Hadhrat Safeenah was once in Roman territory when he either became separated from the rest of the army or…
narrations.summary: Ibn Munkadir reports that Safeenah, lost in Roman territory, met a lion that accepted his claim to be the Prophet's freed slave, then walked beside him and led him to the army.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Wahab bin Abaan Qurashi that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) was travelling on a journeywhentheysawacrowd of people standing by the road. "What is the matter with…
narrations.summary: Wahab bin Abaan reports that Abdullaah bin Umar moved a lion off the road, and then quoted the Prophet that whoever fears and hopes in none but Allaah will not be overpowered by anything else.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Auf bin Maalik (RA) reports, "I was sleeping in a church in Areeha, which was then already a Masjid in which salaah was performed. When I awoke, 1 was shocked to…
narrations.summary: Auf bin Maalik reports that a lion in a church in Areeha told him that Mu'aawiya, son of Abu Sufyaan, would be among the people of Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports that a wolf once attacked a goat and took it away. The shepherd however went after it and wrestled it from the wolf. The wolf then…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that a wolf spoke to a shepherd about the Prophet, and the Prophet confirmed it; a similar wolf spoke to Abu Sufyaan and Safwaan bin Umayyah about the Prophet's call.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais bin Hajjaaj reports from his teacher that after Egypt was conquered (by the Muslims), the people approached the governor Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas when the…
narrations.summary: Qais bin Hajjaaj reports that Amr bin al-Aas refused the Egyptians' ritual of throwing a girl into the Nile, Umar's letter had a note cast into the river, and the Nile then rose.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa A'ma who was a freed slave of the Banu Sa'd tribe reports that Hadhrat Abu Rayhaana (RA) was once travelling by sea. He was busy mending a few notebooks of…
narrations.summary: Urwa A'ma reports that Abu Rayhaana's needle fell into the sea and, after he prayed for it, surfaced in his hand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports, "I followed Alaa bin Hadhrami when Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched him to Bahrain. I witnessed three incidents with him and I cannot tell…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that Alaa bin Hadhrami, sent by the Prophet to Bahrain, crossed the sea by reciting Bismillaah, brought rain after a prayer and du'aa, and that his grave was later found empty.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) added, "When Ibn Muka'bir the Persian governor saw us, he exclaimed, 'Never! By Allaah! We can never fight such…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah adds that the Persian governor Ibn Muka'bir, on seeing the Muslims, said they could never be fought and sailed back to Persia.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) once said, "I have witnessed three occurrences in this Ummah that would have been unmatched by any other nation had they occurred amongst the Bani…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Umar appointed Alaa bin Hadhrami to lead an army, and that Alaa's du'aa brought rain and a crossing of the gulf without the animals' hooves getting wet.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes the du'aa of Hadhrat Alaa (RA) in the following words: lil li /Jj Ul. ,JIp £ £ £" 'O The All Knowing! O Most Forbearing! O The Most Exalted! O…
narrations.summary: Several accounts describe Alaa bin Hadhrami's du'aa for rain, his crossing of the sea with his men at Daareen, and Abu Bakr's dispatch of him to fight the Murtaddeen in Bahrain.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) dispatched Hadhrat Alaa bin Hadhrami iS to fight the Murtaddeen in Bahrain. The narration also describes how the…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr sent Alaa bin Hadhrami to fight the apostates in Bahrain; the lost camels came back with their loads, Allaah provided a pond of water, and Alaa led the army on foot across the gulf to defeat the enemy and return, all within a single day.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Rufayl reports that the town of Bahurseer was on the nearer bank of the Tigris River. When Hadhrat S'ad (RA) set up camp there, he searched for boats to take…
narrations.summary: Ibn Rufayl reports that Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, unable to find boats, led the army across the Tigris after Aasim bin Amr and sixty men went ahead, and the Persians fled the town of Bahurseer.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Hafs bin Umar reports that the person travelling with Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) over the water was Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA). As their horses swam across,…
narrations.summary: Several narrators describe the Muslim army crossing the Tigris at Madaa'in: Sa'd and Salmaan were assured the waters were subject, the rising mounds were seen, and the Persians fled, calling them madmen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi says, "Everyone of the Muslims crossed over safely, except for a man from Baariq who was called Gharqadah. He happened to slip off his brown…
narrations.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi tells how Gharqadah slipped from his horse while the Muslims crossed the Tigris and was pulled out by Qa'qaa bin Amr, and how a lost cup was returned; Umayr Saa'idi reports that Sa'd led the army across in pairs with mounds appearing to rest on; and Qais bin Abu Haazim says the deepest part reached only a horseman's reins.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Habeeb bin Suhbaan reports that one of the Muslims by the name of Hadhrat Hujr bin Adi said to the others, "What prevents you from crossing over to the enemy? Is…
narrations.summary: Habeeb bin Suhbaan reports that Hujr bin Adi asked what kept the Muslims from crossing the Tigris, recited a verse on the fixed time of death, plunged in on his horse, and the others followed until the enemy fled calling them madmen.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Habeeb bin Suhbaan Abu Maalik narrates that when the Persians saw the Muslims crossing the Tigris the day they conquered Madaa'in, they called out in Persian,…
narrations.summary: Habeeb bin Suhbaan reports that when the Persians saw the Muslims crossing the Tigris on the day Madaa'in was conquered, they called them mad devils and said they were fighting Jinn, and so they were defeated.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat A'mash reports from a companion of his that when they reached the Tigris River, the water level was very high and the Kuffaar had already crossed over. One of the…
narrations.summary: A'mash reports that a Muslim plunged into the Tigris saying Bismillaah, his horse rode over the water, and the other Muslims followed, which made the Persians flee.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Harmal reports, "When I arrived in Madinah, Hadhrat Tameem Daari took me home to eat. Although I ate voraciously, I did not seem to get enough…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Harmal reports that Tameem Daari, when Umar sent him, pushed back a fire that came from Harra with his bare hands, and Umar said such a witness cannot be like one who has not seen it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Harmal says, "I once went to Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, 'O Ameerul Mu'mineen! I have come to repent before being caught (for fighting by the side of…
narrations.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Harmal reports that after repenting of fighting for Musaylama, Umar sent him to Tameem Daari, who pushed a fire from Harra back through its door and came out unharmed.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to Hadhrat Tameem "It is for emergencies like this that we keep you hidden, O Abu Ruqayya."
narrations.summary: Another narration has Umar telling Tameem Daari that they keep him hidden for emergencies like this, but the text breaks off.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports, "We were once performing the Isha salaah behind Rasulullaah ﷺ when Hasan SUM and Husayn jumped on Rasulullaah ﷺ's back as he prostrated…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that during Isha, Hasan and Husayn climbed on the Prophet's back in sajdah, and a flash of lightning lit their way home; another account has Hasan walking home by lightning.

narrations.excerpt: In a narration discussing the special moment of the day of Jumu'ah, Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that there was a heavy storm that night and when Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that on a stormy night the Prophet saw Qataadah bin Nu'maan in lightning and gave him a date-palm branch that lit the way and was to be used against a Shaytaan.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Qataadah (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ gave me the branch of a date palm and said, 'Verily a Shaytaan went to your family after you left. You…
narrations.summary: Qataadah bin Nu'maan says that the Prophet's branch lit his way home and he struck a hedgehog in his house, which he took for a Shaytaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when two companions of Rasulullaah ﷺ left his company one night, lights appeared in front of them like two lanterns. When their paths…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that two Companions leaving the Prophet at night had lights shine before them, and each kept a light until they reached home.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Usayd bin Hudhayr (RA) and another Sahabi from amongst the Ansaar once happened to be discussing a need of theirs with Rasulullaah…
narrations.summary: Anas reports that Usayd bin Hudhayr and another Ansaari, leaving the Prophet on a dark night, each had their staff light up, and the second report names the other man as Abbaad bin Bishr.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hamzah bin Amr Aslami (RA) says, "We were with Rasulullaah ﷺ during one extremely dark night. When we left, my fingers started to shine so brightly and for so…
narrations.summary: Hamzah bin Amr Aslami reports that his fingers shone on a dark night so the Companions could gather their mounts, and at Tabook his fingers gave light to recover the Prophet's fallen luggage.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Hamzah bin Amr (RA) says, "We were in Tabook when some of the Munaafiqeen made Rasulullaah ﷺ's camel bolt. As a result of this; some of his…
narrations.summary: Hamzah bin Amr says that when hypocrites made the Prophet's camel bolt at Tabook and his luggage fell, all five of his fingers lit up so he could pick up the whip, rope and other items.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Abu Abs narrates that his father Hadhrat Abu Abs (RA) used to return to the (locality of the) Banu Haaritha tribe after every salaah that he performed…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Abu Abs reports that his father, Abu Abs, after praying behind the Prophet, had his staff light up on a dark rainy night so he could reach his locality.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ gave Hadhrat Abu Abs bin Jabr a staff after his eyesight had become very weak. Rasulullaah ﷺ told him to use the light from it…
narrations.summary: Another account says that the Prophet gave Abu Abs bin Jabr a staff when his eyesight became weak, and it lit up a wide area for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi (RA) was a Sahabi for whom Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa so that his whip would shine brightly. He used to use the light of the whip to see in the…
narrations.summary: Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi's whip shone with light after a du'aa of the Prophet, Abbaas advised treating people well, and a cloud shaded Amr bin Abasa.

narrations.excerpt: and the Sahabah ^'
narrations.summary: This is a broken fragment ('and the Sahabah') from the section on rain sent through the Prophet's du'aa, and it does not say who did what.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was delivering a sermon from the pulpit on a Friday when a man entered the Masjid from a door that was directly in front of…
narrations.summary: The Prophet ﷺ asked for rain during a Friday sermon, then asked for it to stop, and rain fell until Abu Lubaabah plugged his granary gutter with his loincloth.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr bin Ayaash bin Sahal reports that on one morning when the Sahabah (RA) had no water with them, they took the matter to Rasulullaah ﷺ.…
narrations.summary: When the Sahabah had no water, the Prophet ﷺ made du'aa and Allaah sent a cloud that rained enough for all their needs.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khawwaat bin Jubayr narrates that when a severe drought afflicted the people during the time of Hadhrat Umar (RA), he took them out of the town and led them in…
narrations.summary: Khawwaat bin Jubayr prayed for rain during Umar's caliphate and rain fell at once, and in a dream the Prophet ﷺ sent Umar word that rain was coming.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maalik Daar narrates that when a drought afflicted the people during the time of Hadhrat Umar (RA), someone went to Rasulullaah iieil's grave and said, "O…
narrations.summary: Maalik Daar reports that in Umar's time of drought a man went to the Prophet's grave, saw him in a dream saying rain would soon come and Umar should keep using his judgement; when told, Umar wept and said he was doing all he could.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Ka'b bin Maalik reports that the Year of Ashes (of drought) brought starvation to the people of Madinah and its surroundings, causing much…
narrations.summary: In the Year of Ashes Umar asked other provinces for food, led prayer for rain, and a Bedouin was told in a dream that rain would come and Umar should keep applying his intelligence.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Aamir Khabaa'iri narrated that when a drought struck, Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Abu Sufyaan (RA) went out of the town with the people of Damascus to…
narrations.summary: During a drought Mu'aawiya had Yazeed bin Aswad raise his hands in du'aa, and a cloud came with rain straight after.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Thumaamah bin Abdullaah reports that the keeper of one of Hadhrat Anas's orchards once came to him during the summer months, complaining of a scarcity of water.…
narrations.summary: Anas's orchard keeper asked for rain in summer and rain fell only on Anas's land after Anas prayed, and Hujr bin Adi asked for water while held by Mu'aawiya's forces and a cloud rained on him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan reports that a particular tribe of the Ansaar were blessed with a du'aa that Rasulullaah ﷺ had made for them, as a result a cloud would rain upon the grave…
narrations.summary: A tribe of the Ansaar had rain fall on the grave of each member through an earlier du'aa of the Prophet, including on a freed slave who was counted as one of them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Qaasim narrates that when Hadhrat Ummu Ayman (RA) migrated to Madinah, she reached a place called Munsarif by the evening, which was just before…
narrations.summary: Ummu Ayman, thirsty while fasting on her migration to Madinah, was given water from a bucket let down from the sky, and after that she never felt thirst on hot fasting days.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) says, "The time for Asr had arrived and I saw people looking for water to make wudhu, but were unable to find any. When some water was…
narrations.summary: At Asr time with no water for wudhu, the Prophet ﷺ placed his hand in a vessel and water gushed from under his fingers so that everyone could make wudhu.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "When the Adhaan was called out for salaah, everyone who lived close to the Masjid got up (to go home to make wudhu), while…
narrations.summary: Water flowed from the Prophet's fingers at a basin and at Zowraa, and at Hudaybiyyah he made du'aa and spat into the well, which then gave enough water for everyone.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib (RA) says, "We were fourteen hundred people at Hudaybiyyah and although Hudaybiyyah is itself a well, we drew so much water from it that not a…
narrations.summary: Baraa bin Aazib says that the fourteen hundred people at Hudaybiyyah drew all the water from its well, then the Prophet sat on the rim, made du'aa, gargled and spat into the well, and soon there was enough water for all of them and their animals.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) reports that the Sahabah isi suffered a shortage of water during their stay at Hudaybiyyah and only Rasulullaah ﷺ had a leather bag of…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports that during Hudaybiyyah the Companions had no water except what was in the Prophet's leather bag; when he put his hand in it, water flowed between his fingers, and Baraa said it would have been enough for a hundred thousand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) says, "We were with Rasulullaah ﷺ on a journey when the time for salaah arrived. We had only a little water with us and Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: On a journey, when there was little water for salaah, the Prophet ﷺ poured it into a dish and water gushed from his fingers, and Ibn Mas'ood drank some of it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) says, "We were with Rasulullaah ﷺ on a journey when he asked whether we had any water with us. 'Yes,' I replied, 'I have some water in…
narrations.summary: On a journey the Prophet ﷺ made wudhu from a small container of water, and once the container was opened it gave seven hundred people enough to drink with some left over.

narrations.excerpt: In a narration discussing combining salaahs during the expedition to Tabook, Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) reports, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said to us, You will Inshaa Allaah…
narrations.summary: On the way to Tabook the Prophet ﷺ washed his hands and face in a thin spring, after which the water gushed out for everyone, and he told Mu'aadh that the area would one day be full of gardens.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) reports, "We were on a journey with Rasulullaah ﷺ ..." The narration continues to the point where he says, "It then reached a stage when we…
narrations.summary: On a journey with no water, the Prophet ﷺ passed his hand over a woman's two waterskins so that forty thirsty men drank and filled their vessels, and her tribe then became Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ziyaad bin Haarith Sudaa'ee (RA) relates, "1 was with Rasulullaah ﷺ on a journey when he asked me whether I had any water with me. 'I do have a little,' I…
narrations.summary: Ziyaad bin Haarith Sudaa'ee saw water gush from the Prophet's fingers, and after his tribe became Muslims the Prophet ﷺ had seven stones thrown into their well so that it gave abundant water.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Awn reports that when Hadhrat Husayn bin Ali (RA) went from Madinah to Makkah, he passed by Ibn Mutee who was digging a well... The narration later mentions…
narrations.summary: Husayn bin Ali gargled with water from Ibn Mutee's well and returned it to the well, and afterwards the water increased and became sweeter.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Amrah Ansaari (RA) reports that they were with Rasulullaah ﷺ on a military expedition when they started to feel extreme hunger. The Sahabah itS. then sought…
narrations.summary: On an expedition the army was starving until Umar suggested pooling the remaining food, the Prophet ﷺ made du'aa over it, and everyone ate their fill with food still left over.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Abu Khunays Ghifaari (RA) reports that they were with Rasulullaah ﷺ on an expedition to Tihaamah and it was at a place called Usfaan that…
narrations.summary: At Usfaan the army drank rainwater after the Prophet ﷺ ordered them to leave, and on the Tabook expedition the Sahabah asked to slaughter their water camels for food until Umar intervened.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) both report that when the Sahabah (RA) suffered extreme hunger during the expedition to Tabook, they…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'eed Khudri report that during the hunger of Tabook the Companions asked to slaughter their water camels for food and oil; the Prophet permitted it, Umar intervened, and the narration then breaks off.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salamah (RA) reports, "We were with Rasulullaah ﷺ in the Battle of Khaybar when he instructed us to gather all our provisions of dates together. Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: At Khaybar the Prophet ﷺ had the Sahabah's dates gathered on a leather cloth, and after about 1,400 people had eaten, the pile was still the size of a sitting goat.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Salamah (RA) says, "We then ate to our fill and also filled our satchels.
narrations.summary: Salamah says that after they had eaten to their fill they also filled their satchels.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was busy with the digging of the trench, the Sahabah (RA) (as well as Rasulullaah Wfflife) had rocks…
narrations.summary: While the trench was being dug, the Prophet ﷺ made one goat and a little bread enough for the whole group, and at a boulder he promised the palaces of Shaam and Persia while the hypocrites scoffed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Samurah bin Jundub (RA) narrates that they were once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when a plate of Thareed was served. Rasulullaah ﷺ and all the Sahabah (RA) there ate and…
narrations.summary: A plate of Thareed was served to the Prophet ﷺ and the Sahabah, and they kept eating until near Zuhr, and Samurah said the extra food came from the heavens.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa (RA) says, "1 was one of the men of Suffa when Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent for some bread, which he broke into a dish. He then added some boiling…
narrations.summary: Waathila bin Asqa and the men of Suffa were fed bread and Thareed that the Prophet ﷺ made with his own hands, which kept increasing until the plate was full and each group had eaten its fill.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa (RA) says, "1 was one of the men of Suffa and when my other companions once complained to me about their severe hunger, they requested, 'O…
narrations.summary: Waathila bin Asqa tells how, when the men of Suffa were hungry, the Prophet asked Aa'isha for her bread, made thareed with his own hands so that it multiplied, and fed groups of ten until all were full with the plate still full; a second narration gives twenty men and says bread and milk were served.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ had once not had anything to eat for several days. When the hunger became unbearable, he went around to the rooms of his…
narrations.summary: Faatima kept the bread and meat a neighbour gave her for the Prophet ﷺ, and when he had eaten it with his household the platter stayed full and he told her to give it to the neighbours.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that a lady from the Dows tribe called Hadhrat Ummu Shareek (RA) became a Muslim in Ramadhaan... The narration then goes on to describe…
narrations.summary: Ummu Shareek Dowsiyyah was given a drink in a dream when thirsty on her migration, the Prophet ﷺ married her to Zaid with thirty Saa of barley, and her butter kept coming until the bag was tied shut.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that when Hadhrat Ummu Shareek Dowsiyyah migrated, she met up with a Jew (and his wife) on the road. She had been fasting but the Jew…
narrations.summary: Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that Ummu Shareek Dowsiyyah, fasting and thirsty on her migration after a Jewish couple refused her a drink, found a bucket of water in the night and drank from it; she had a small container of butter, and the narration goes on to describe its blessings.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that a man once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ to ask for some food. Rasulullaah ﷺ gave him half a Wasaq of barley from which the man, his wife and…
narrations.summary: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ for food and received half a Wasaq of barley, which lasted until they weighed it, after which it ran out.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naufal bin Haarith bin Abdul Muttalib narrates, "When I requested Rasulullaah ﷺ for assistance in getting married, Rasulullaah ﷺ got me married but when he looked…
narrations.summary: Naufal bin Haarith asked the Prophet ﷺ for help with marriage, and barley pawned for thirty Saa lasted half a year without decreasing until they weighed it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, I had nothing to eat apart from some barley stored on a shelf of mine. I continued eating from it for a very…
narrations.summary: After the Prophet ﷺ passed away, Aa'isha had barley on a shelf that lasted for a very long time until she weighed it.

narrations.excerpt: made Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) states, "Because my father had many debts when he passed away, 1 approached Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, 'My father had left some debts for me to…
narrations.summary: Jaabir's father left debts, and when the Prophet ﷺ walked around the heaps of dates and made du'aa, Jaabir's creditors were paid in full with dates left over.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ sat on the heap and told me to call the creditors. Rasulullaah ﷺ then continued weighing (and…
narrations.summary: Jaabir says the Prophet ﷺ sat on the heap of dates and had the creditors called, and although the debts were paid, the heap looked untouched.

narrations.excerpt: The daughter of HadhraU-Basheer bin Sa'd who was also the sister of Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Basheer (RA) reports, "(My mother) Amrah bint Rawaaha once called for me and…
narrations.summary: A girl carrying her mother's dates to her father was stopped by the Prophet ﷺ, who spread them on a cloth and called the trench-diggers to eat, and the dates kept multiplying.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Irbaadh (RA) relates, "Whether at home or on journey, I always stood guard at Rasulullaah ﷺ's door. We were at Tabook one night when we had to leave on some…
narrations.summary: On the Tabook expedition seven dates fed three hungry men and then ten people without ever decreasing, and the Prophet ﷺ later gave the dates to a child in Madinah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) says, "There were three such calamities that afflicted me as a Muslim, the magnitude of which I had never experienced before. (The first is) The…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah's bag of dates was blessed by the Prophet ﷺ's du'aa to feed the whole army, and it stayed full through the lifetimes of Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan until it was stolen after Uthmaan's martyrdom.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "My mother once took me before Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ Please make du'aa for this little servant of yours: Rasulullaah ﷺ made…
narrations.summary: Anas's mother asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray for her son, and Anas reports that his wealth, children and orchards were blessed, so that his orchards bear fruit twice a year.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "(My mother) Ummu Sulaym once said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ Make du'aa for Anas.' Rasulullaah ﷺ therefore prayed, 'O Allaah!…
narrations.summary: Anas says his mother Ummu Sulaym asked the Prophet to pray for him; the Prophet prayed for his wealth and children and for blessing in them, and Anas says he has buried a hundred and twenty-five children and his orchards bear fruit twice a year.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that Hadhrat Ummu Maalik Bahziyyah (RA) used to give Rasulullaah ﷺ butter in a little bag that she had. When her sons once asked her for some…
narrations.summary: Ummu Maalik Bahziyyah's bag of butter kept giving butter after she gave it to the Prophet ﷺ, and when she brought him a gift the bag stayed full, after which he taught her tasbeeh to recite after each salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Aws Bahziyyah (RA) narrates that she once made some butter, poured it into a little bag and then gave the butter as a gift to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ…
narrations.summary: Ummu Aws Bahziyyah's gift of butter stayed full after the Prophet ﷺ took some from it, and she went on eating from the bag until the dispute between Ali and Mu'aawiya.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that his mother (Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA)) had a goat (which she milked) and she collected all the butter from the goat's milk in a little bag.…
narrations.summary: Ummu Sulaym's bag of butter stayed full after the Prophet ﷺ took from it, he told her to eat from it and feed others, and it lasted her household a month or two.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Shareek (RA) reports that she had with her a little bag in which she gave Rasulullaah ﷺ some butter as a gift. One day when her children asked her for some…
narrations.summary: Ummu Shareek reports that the butter in her small bag kept replenishing until she emptied it out, and the Prophet remarked that it would have lasted much longer had she left it alone.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration from Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed states that Hadhrat Ummu Shareek used to lend her little bag to whoever came to her. When a man once approached here to…
narrations.summary: Ummu Shareek lent her bag out to people, and it refilled with butter even after it seemed empty, which people took as one of the signs of Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hamzah bin Amr (RA) relates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ's companions took turns in preparing food for his other companions and someone different would bring the food each…
narrations.summary: Hamzah bin Amr relates that when the butter bag spilled while he was preparing the Prophet's food, it later filled to its chest, and the Prophet said it would have filled to its mouth had he left it alone.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration has already passed concerning the expedition to Tabook in which Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "Had you left it as is, the entire valley would have been…
narrations.summary: Hamzah bin Amr relates that while the Prophet was away on the Tabook expedition, the butter bag refilled after he dozed beside it, and the Prophet said the whole valley would have flowed with butter had he left it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khabbaab bin Arat (RA)'s daughter reports, "When my father left on an expedition, he left us nothing apart from a goat. His instruction was that whenever we…
narrations.summary: Khabbaab bin Arat's daughter relates that the Prophet milked their goat into the family's largest vessel until it overflowed, and her father then said the Prophet's hands were far more blessed than his own.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mas'ood bin Khaalid (RA) says, "I once sent a goat to Rasulullaah and then had to leave to do something. Rasulullaah ﷺ sent a portion of the meat back to my…
narrations.summary: Mas'ood bin Khaalid relates that the meat the Prophet sent back from the goat he had given him was still left over after his family had eaten, which surprised him since one or two goats were usually not enough for them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Abdul Uzza (RA) once slaughtered a goat and sent it to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) with him ate it and then sent what was left…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Abdul Uzza sends a goat to the Prophet, who and his Companions eat it and return the leftovers, which still feed Khaalid's very large family with some to spare.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Salamah bin Nufayl (RA) reports that he once asked Rasulullaah ﷺ whether he received food from the heavens. When Rasulullaah ﷺ replied that he did, Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Salamah bin Nufayl reports that food is brought to the Prophet from the heavens and lifted back after it is left over, and the Prophet foretells a time of strife and many deaths before Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that someone asked Rasulullaah ﷺ whether he received food from Jannah.
narrations.summary: A narration says that someone asked the Prophet whether he received food from Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: In a lengthy narration reported by Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA), he says, "When the men complained of their extreme hunger to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he said, 'Allaah shall…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah relates that when the men were starving, the sea cast up a huge creature which fed them, and five of them went into its eye socket and then stood one of its ribs up like a bow.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) also reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched a regiment of three hundred men under the command of Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah I was amongst the men and we…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah relates that when Abu Ubaydah's army ran out of provisions, the sea washed up a fish the size of a hill that fed them for eighteen days, and a camel and carriage passed under its ribs without touching them.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) states, "Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched three hundred of us under the command of Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah to ambush one of the…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah gives several accounts of Abu Ubaydah's army, which ate a fish the sea threw up for a month, and reports that the Prophet called it the sustenance Allaah had brought out for them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that a Sahabi once came home but when he saw the great hunger his family was experiencing, he (was unable to bear it and) left and went…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when a Sahabi's wife prayed for provision in her family's hunger, the grindstone and oven kept producing until the husband lifted the grindstone, and the Prophet said it would have continued until the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that his wife's du'aa was: "O Allaah! Provide for us what we can grind, knead and make into bread. The bowl then suddenly filled with bread, the…
narrations.summary: A narration of a Sahabi and his wife: she prays for provision for what they can grind, knead and bake, the bowl fills with bread and the grindstone grinds by itself; when her husband stops it, the Prophet says had he left it, it would have gone on grinding until the Day of Qiyaamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) also reports that when a very poor man from the Ansaar once left home, his wife said, "If I start to turn my grindstone and place some palm…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that a poor Ansaari's wife, with no food in the house, ground grain and lit the oven so the neighbours would think they had food; on the husband's return they found the grindstone turning, flour everywhere and the oven full of bread, and the Prophet said had the husband left it, it would have gone on grinding for his whole life.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) says, "I once left Makkah with Rasulullaah ﷺ and we travelled until we reached the locality of an Arab tribe. Rasulullaah ﷺ saw a house that was…
narrations.summary: Abu Bakr relates how a Bedouin woman hosted the Prophet and himself, how the Prophet milked her goat for them and her flock grew, and how she accepted Islaam when she recognised him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports, "I was grazing goats for Uqba bin Abu Mu'eet when Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) passed by me. 'Dear boy!'…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood relates that the Prophet drew milk from a goat that had not yet mated, then told her teat to contract and it did, and afterwards Ibn Mas'ood asked to be taught and the Prophet prayed that he be well taught.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood brought Rasulullaah ﷺ a goat that was under a year old. Rasulullaah ﷺ tied her legs and made du'aa as he…
narrations.summary: Another account says Abdullaah bin Mas'ood brought the Prophet a young goat, who prayed over her and milked her into a dish that Abu Bakr brought, then gave Abu Bakr to drink before drinking himself.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) says, "It was during one of the expeditions on which Rasulullaah ﷺ sent us that we became extremely thirsty because we had no water with us. All of…
narrations.summary: Khabbaab bin Arat relates that on a campaign sent out by the Prophet the Muslims became very thirsty, and a companion's camel sat down with udders so full of milk that they all drank from her.

narrations.excerpt: After she had accepted Islaam, Hadhrat Maawiyya (RA) slave of Hujayr bin Abu Ihaab reports, "When Khubayb was held prisoner in our house (in Makkah), I once peeped at him…
narrations.summary: Maawiyya, a slave of Hujayr bin Abi Ihaab, reports that while Khubayb was held prisoner in their house in Makkah she peeped in and saw him eating a huge bunch of grapes, when grapes could not be had anywhere.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saalim bin Abul J a'd (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched two men for some task, they said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ We have nothing to take with as…
narrations.summary: Saalim bin Abul Ja'd relates that when the Prophet sent two men out with no provisions, he told them to fill a water bag and go to a place where Allaah would provide, and there they found goat's milk and cream inside it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) narrates, "I went to Uthmaan when he was imprisoned in his house. 'A warm welcome to my brother,' he said. He then said, 'Last night I…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Salaam relates that while Uthmaan was besieged, the Prophet appeared to him in a dream, offered him water, and then offered to help him against his attackers or to break his fast with the Prophet, and Uthmaan chose the latter and was martyred that day.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dubaa'ah bint Zubayr (RA) who was married to Hadhrat Miqdaad bin Aswad says, "People used to relieve themselves only every two or three days and would then pass…
narrations.summary: Dubaa'ah bint Zubayr relates that her husband Miqdaad found seventeen dinars that a rat had carried out of a hole, and when he told the Prophet, the Prophet said no khumus was due from him and prayed for blessing, after which their wealth grew greatly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Saa'ib bin Aqra (RA) reports, "When Hadhrat Umar (RA) appointed me governor of Madaa'in, I was once sitting in the throne room of the Persian Emperor when I…
narrations.summary: Saa'ib bin Aqra relates that while governor of Madaa'in he found a huge treasure under a figurine that pointed to the spot, and Umar wrote back instructing him to distribute it among the Muslims.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that Hadhrat Saa'ib (RA) participated in the Conquest of Mihrijaan and when he entered the chambers of Hurmuzaan, he saw a lime figurine of a deer…
narrations.summary: Sha'bi reports that during the Conquest of Mihrijaan Saa'ib bin Aqra noticed a lime figurine of a deer pointing its foreleg, investigated, and discovered the treasure of Hurmuzaan, which included several bags of gems.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Yazeed bin Jaabir reports that a slave woman of Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) (who was a Christian) once related to him, "Abu Umaamah loved to spend…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Yazeed bin Jaabir relays how Abu Umaamah gave away his last dinars in charity and then found three hundred gold coins left in his bed, after which his Christian slave woman accepted Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: In a lengthy narration discussing how he accepted Islaam, Hadhrat Salmaan says, "When I was still left owing something, a gold nugget resembling a fowl's eggs came to…
narrations.summary: Salmaan relates that when he still owed money for his freedom, the Prophet gave him a gold nugget that weighed forty awqiya, enough to pay off the debt in full.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa Baariqi (RA) reports, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ met a trade caravan, he gave me a Dinaar to purchase a goat. I managed to purchase two goats for the Dinaar and…
narrations.summary: Urwa Baariqi relates that the Prophet prayed for blessing in his trade after he bought two goats for one dinar and sold one, and he later made large profits in the Kunaasah marketplace.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Aqeel reports that his grandfather Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Hishaam would take him out to the marketplace, where he would buy some grains (to resell). Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Abu Aqeel relates that his grandfather Abdullaah bin Hishaam bought grain to resell and earned a camel's worth of profit, because the Prophet had prayed for blessing on him, and Abdullaah bin Zubayr and Abdullaah bin Umar asked to be partners.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Unays (RA) says, "The Jew Mustaneer bin Rizaam struck my face with his bent staff made from the Showhat tree. The wound was so severe that it…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Unays relates that after the Jew Mustaneer bin Rizaam struck him with a staff and fractured his skull, the Prophet opened the wound, applied his saliva to it, and it healed without a trace.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Mukhallad bin Uqba (RA) reports, "1 went to Rasulullaah ﷺ at a time when I had a boil on my palm. 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I said, 'This boil has developed on my palm…
narrations.summary: Mukhallad bin Uqba relates that a boil on his palm hindered him from holding his sword and reins, so the Prophet opened his palm, applied his saliva, and rubbed the boil until no trace of it remained.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abyadh bin Hammaal Maaribi (RA) reports that he once had a ringworm infection on his face, which covered his entire nose. Rasulullaah ﷺ sent for him and passed…
narrations.summary: Abyadh bin Hammaal relates that he had a ringworm infection covering his face and nose, and after the Prophet passed his blessed hand over it, no trace of it remained.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Raafi bin Khudayj (RA) relates, "I once went to Rasulullaah ﷺ at a time when a large pot of meat was being cooked. A delicious piece of fat caught my eye, so I…
narrations.summary: Raafi bin Khudayj relates that after he ate a piece of fat from a pot of meat and was ill for a year, the Prophet passed his hand over his stomach, he vomited a green lump, and he never had stomach pain again.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports, "I was ill one day when I happened to pass by Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, 'O Allaah! If my death is near, do grant me relief (from this illness by…
narrations.summary: Ali relates that the Prophet prayed for him when he was ill and then cured him, and Abdullaah bin Ateek describes how the Prophet healed his broken leg by passing his hand over it after he was injured going to kill Abu Raafi.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Handhala bin Hadheem (RA) says, "1 accompanied my grandfather with a delegation to Rasulullaah ﷺ. My grandfather said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ 1 have several sons (and…
narrations.summary: Handhala bin Hadheem relates that the Prophet passed his hand over his head and prayed for blessing when he came with his grandfather's delegation, and Dhayyaal relates that Handhala cured a swollen face and inflamed teats by touching them with the blessing of the Prophet's palm.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes that Hadhrat Dhayyaal said, "I saw that when a man with an inflamed face was brought to Hadhrat Handhala (RA), he applied some saliva on his…
narrations.summary: Dhayyaal relates that a man with a swollen face was brought to Handhala, who applied saliva to his hand, recited Bismillaah, touched the swelling and said it was done with the blessing of the place where the Prophet placed his palm, and it disappeared instantly.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Qurt (RA) reports, "Because my camel started to walk extremely slowly and sat down (because of exhaustion) as I rode with Khaalid bin Waleed, I…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Qurt relates that when his camel grew exhausted while he rode with Khaalid bin Waleed, he made du'aa to Allaah, and the camel stood up straight so he could ride it again.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Safar reports that when Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) arrived in Heera, he stayed with the Persian governor. Some people however warned him saying, "Be…
narrations.summary: Abu Safar, Dhul Jowshan and others relate that Khaalid bin Waleed swallowed poison in the name of Allaah without harm, and that Amr bin Buqayla, who carried poison, said the Arabs would conquer any land while the Sahabah lived among them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Dhul Jowshan Dhibaabi (RA) and others report that Amr bin Buqayla had his servant with him, who carried a little bag around his waist. Hadhrat Khaalid took the…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed drank poison that Amr bin Buqayla carried, after reciting a du'aa, and it did him no harm.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla reports, "Hadhrat Ali (RA) used to walk about during winter wearing only his loincloth and an upper garment, both made from thin…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abi Layla relates that his father asked Ali why he wore light clothes in winter and heavy ones in summer, and Ali explained that the Prophet's saliva and du'aa for protection against heat and cold had kept him from feeling either.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) says, "When we once met Ali wearing two (light) garments during winter, we said to him, 'Do not be deceived by our land because it is extremely cold, unlike…
narrations.summary: Ali says that after the Prophet applied his saliva to Ali's painful eyes before Khaybar, he never again felt heat or cold.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) reports, "I called out the Fajr Adhaan one icy winter morning but no one came for salaah. I then called out the Adhaan again, but still no one…
narrations.summary: Bilaal relates that on an icy winter morning the people did not come out for Fajr after the Adhaan, so the Prophet prayed that Allaah remove the cold from them, and then they came for Fajr and Duha with ease.

narrations.excerpt: A narration from Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) discussing the Battle of Khandaq also highlights the same point.
narrations.summary: A one-line cross-reference notes that a narration from Hudhayfah about the Battle of the Trench makes the same point about cold.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) reports, "I was sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ when Faatima arrived and stood facing towards him. 'Come closer, O Faatima,' Rasulullaah ﷺ said.…
narrations.summary: Imraan bin Husayn relates that the Prophet placed his hand on Faatima's chest and prayed that she not suffer hunger, after which the paleness from her hunger left her face and she never went hungry again.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Zaid Ansaari (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once told him to draw closer and when he did, Rasulullaah ﷺ passed his hand over his head saying, "O Allaah!…
narrations.summary: Abu Zaid Ansaari relates that the Prophet prayed for his good looks and that he lived past a hundred with only a few white hairs, and a second report says he had none at ninety-four.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abul A'laa says, "I was with Hadhrat Qataadah bin Milhaan (RA) at the place where he passed away. When someone passed by at the back of the room, 1 saw his…
narrations.summary: Abul A'laa reports that after the Prophet passed his hand over Qataadah bin Milhaan's face, the signs of age were removed from it, so that his face kept looking oiled and reflected passers-by.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hayyaan bin Umayr reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ passed his hand over the face of Hadhrat Qataadah bin Milhaan (RA), because of which every part of his body showed signs…
narrations.summary: Hayyaan bin Umayr reports that the Prophet's touch on Qataadah bin Milhaan's face kept every part of his body ageing except his face, which still reflected a woman passing behind him when he died.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Naabigha Ja'di (RA) reports that he once recited the following couplet before Rasulullaah ﷺ "While our honour and status have reached the skies we still aspire to…
narrations.summary: Naabigha Ja'di recites couplets before the Prophet, who asks where the greater heights lead and is told Jannah, and the Prophet then prays that Naabigha's teeth never fall out, and they stayed intact even past a hundred years of age.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds, "Throughout his life, he always had the best set of teeth. Whenever a tooth fell out, it was replaced by another and he lived to very old age."
narrations.summary: A further narration reports that Naabigha Ja'di always had a perfect set of teeth, and each one that fell out was replaced by another so that he lived to a very old age.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Is'haaq (RA) relates, "I was migrating to Rasulullaah ﷺ in Madinah with my brother when he said, 'Sit here, O Ummu Is'haaq because I have forgotten my money…
narrations.summary: Ummu Is'haaq relates that, after arriving in Madinah and learning her brother Is'haaq had been killed, the Prophet sprinkled water from his wudhu on her face, and her tears never ran down her cheeks in calamity afterwards.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Ummu Is'haaq (RA) said, "I said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I keep weeping about the murder of (my brother) Is'haaq.' Rasulullaah ﷺ then took…
narrations.summary: Ummu Is'haaq says she kept weeping over her brother's murder until the Prophet sprinkled water on her face, and Ummu Hakeem testifies that even in great tragedy her tears welled up but never fell.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports, "Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab Ji once instructed us to ride with him to the countryside where his tribe resided. We then left and…
narrations.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b made du'aa during a thunderstorm and the rain was averted from him and Ibn Abbaas, while the others on the journey were soaked.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam (RA) and others have narrated that when Hadhrat Ukaasha bin Mihsin's sword broke during the Battle of Badr, Rasulullaah gave him a branch, which…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Aslam and others narrate that when Ukaasha bin Mihsin's sword broke at Badr, the Prophet gave him a branch which became a sturdy, sparkling sword in his hand.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Khaythama reports that a man once came to Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed with a casket of wine. Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Transform it into…
narrations.summary: Khaythama reports several versions of Khaalid bin Waleed's du'aa turning a casket of wine into honey or vinegar after its bearer lied about what it was.

narrations.excerpt: Muhammad bin Is'haaq reports that Hadhrat Maalik Ashja'ee (RA) ofice came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "My son Awf has been taken captive." Rasulullaah then sent a message…
narrations.summary: Muhammad bin Is'haaq reports that Maalik Ashja'ee told the Prophet his son Awf had been taken captive, the Prophet told Awf to recite 'Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata illaa Billaah', and Awf escaped and brought back his captors' camels.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that whenever Hadhrat Awf (RA)'s father went to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he lamented about the situation his son was in and the difficulty he was…
narrations.summary: Awf's father complained to the Prophet about his captive son's suffering, and the Prophet advised him to be patient, saying Allaah would soon create an escape for him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abbaas bin Sahl bin Sa'd Saa'idi reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was passing by the area of Hijr (where the Thamud tribe were destroyed), he dismounted and the…
narrations.summary: Abbaas bin Sahl reports that when the Prophet forbade drinking the water at Hijr or leaving camp alone at night, two men who disobeyed were punished, one by a jinn and the other by a tempest, and the Prophet prayed for the one who was throttled and he was cured.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) was delivering a sermon from the pulpit when Hadhrat Jahjaa Ghifaari (RA) stood up, grabbed Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Jahjaa Ghifaari struck Uthmaan's knee with his staff during a sermon, and within the year Jahjaa was afflicted with a disease that ate his arm and killed him.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Jahjaa bin Sa'eed Ghifaari (RA) once confronted Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), snatched his stick from his hand and struck him so hard on his…
narrations.summary: Another narration says Jahjaa snatched Uthmaan's stick and struck his knee so that it broke, Uthmaan went home without retaliating, and Jahjaa died of a disease in his knee before the year was out.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdul Malik bin Umayr reports that a Muslim man once came up to Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) and directed the following couplets at him (which mean): "We…
narrations.summary: Abdul Malik bin Umayr reports that after a man mocked Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas in verse at Qaadisiyyah, Sa'd prayed against him, and the man was struck by an arrow, lost his tongue and hand, and was killed.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration quotes the same two couplets, but the first line of the couplets read: "Do you not see that Allaah has sent His assistance?" It states further that when…
narrations.summary: Another narration says that Sa'd's curse left the man's tongue and hand paralysed, an arrow struck his mouth and his hand was cut off in the battle, and when Sa'd was carried to the city gate with his wounds visible, people knew he was truly excused from fighting.

narrations.excerpt: In the chapter entitled "Getting Annoyed for the Sake of One's Elders", the narration of Hadhrat Aamir bin Sa'd has passed which states that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas…
narrations.summary: Several narrations describe how Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas cursed a man who reviled Ali, Talha and Zubayr, and the curse was fulfilled when a camel or the ground killed him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Showdhab reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) heard that Ziyaad wanted governorship over Hijaaz, he disapproved of his being governor. He…
narrations.summary: Ibn Showdhab reports that when Abdullaah bin Umar heard Ziyaad son of Sumayya wanted the governorship of Hijaaz, he prayed that Ziyaad be granted death without being killed, and a painful infection on his thumb killed him before the next Friday.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Waa'il or Hadhrat Abu Waa'il who was present at Karbala reports, "A man then stood up and said, 'Is Husayn amongst you?' When the people replied that he was,…
narrations.summary: Abu Waa'il, present at Karbala, reports that a man threatened Husayn with Jahannam, and Husayn prayed that he be taken in pieces to Jahannam, after which the man's animal threw him, his foot caught in the stirrup, and only his leg was left.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Kalbi reports that Hadhrat Husayn (RA) was drinking water when a man shot an arrow at him, which paralysed his jaw. "May Allaah never quench your thirst!" Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Kalbi reports that Husayn cursed the man who shot an arrow that paralysed his jaw so that he could not quench his thirst, and the man drank until his stomach burst; other reports describe punishments on the men who killed Husayn and on a man who defiled his grave.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sufyaan reports from his grandmother that there were two men from the Ju'fi tribe who participated in the martyrdom of Hadhrat Husayn (RA). The private organ of…
narrations.summary: Two reports say that the men who took part in the killing of Husayn, and the man who defecated on his grave, were struck with misfortune in this world.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Rabee'ah bin Qusayt reports, "I was with Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) during the "Year of Jamaa'ah" (the year in which the armies of Hadhrat Ali (RA) and Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Rabee'ah bin Qusayt reports that during the Year of Jamaa'ah, when Ali's and Mu'aawiya's armies had clashed, a downpour of blood fell on the returning army, and Amr bin Al-Aas warned the people to mend their relationship with Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zuhri reports, " Abdul Malik once said to me, 'If you can tell me what was the sign of Hadhrat Husayn (RA)'s martyrdom, you can truly be called a great scholar.'…
narrations.summary: Zuhri reports that Abdul Malik asked him for the sign of Husayn's martyrdom, and he answered that fresh blood was found beneath every stone lifted in Baytul Maqdas.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration, he says, "The day Hadhrat Husayn (RA) was martyred, every stone lifted in Shaam gave way to blood."
narrations.summary: Zuhri reports that on the day Husayn was martyred, every stone lifted in Shaam gave way to blood.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ummu Hakeem (RA) says, "I was still a little girl when Hadhrat Husayn was martyred. For a few days afterwards, the sky remained the colour of a blood clot."
narrations.summary: Ummu Hakeem says that for a few days after Husayn was martyred, the sky stayed the colour of a blood clot.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Qubayl says, "When Hadhrat Husayn (RA) was martyred, the sun eclipsed so extraordinarily that stars were visible at noon and we really thought that Qiyaamah…
narrations.summary: Abu Qubayl reports that when Husayn was martyred the sun eclipsed so much that stars were visible at noon, and people thought the Last Day had come.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Maalik bin Dinaar reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was martyred, a voice (of a Jinn) was heard coming from the Tabaalah mountains (in Yemen). It recited the…
narrations.summary: Maalik bin Dinaar, Ma'roof Mowsili and Aa'isha report that when Umar was martyred, an unseen voice of a jinn lamented him in couplets, and Aa'isha heard one lament recited at night.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ma'roof Mowsili narrates that he heard a voice reciting some couplets when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was martyred. The narration then proceeds to quote the above two…
narrations.summary: Ma'roof Mowsili heard a voice reciting couplets lamenting the death of Umar when he was martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Although I could see no one, I heard someone lamenting the death of Hadhrat Umar (RA) one night as he recited the following couplets (which…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha heard an unseen voice lamenting Umar at night, reciting couplets in his praise and grief.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Yasaar reports that the Jinn mourned the death of Hadhrat Umar' by reciting the following couplets (which mean): "Peace be on the Ameerul Mu'mineen…
narrations.summary: Sulaymaan bin Yasaar reports that the jinn mourned Umar's death with a set of couplets, which he quotes in full.

narrations.excerpt: In another narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) quotes the above four couplets in a different sequence, but then adds another couplet (which means) : "(O Ameerul Mu'mineen)…
narrations.summary: Aa'isha quotes the couplets of the jinn mourning Umar in a different order and adds a final couplet wishing Umar a meeting with his Rabb in Jannah.

narrations.excerpt: (Ummul Mu'mineen) Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) says, "The Jinn were heard bewailing the death of Husayn bin Ali.
