narrations.summary: Ummu Salamah says the jinn were heard bewailing the death of Husayn bin Ali.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) once said, "Since the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ, I have never heard the Jinn lament the death of anyone as I hear…
narrations.summary: Ummu Salamah says that after hearing the jinn lamenting one night, her maid learnt that Husayn had been martyred and a jinn woman recited couplets of mourning, and Maymoona reports that the jinn were also heard lamenting Husayn bin Ali.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) says, "1 saw myself at place where there were many roads. All the roads started to vanish until there was only one left. I then took the…
narrations.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari dreamt that the Prophet beckoned Umar up a mountain, which he took to mean Umar would die, and when Anas advised him to write to Umar, Abu Moosa said he could not inform Umar of his own death.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Katheer bin Silt narrates, "On the day Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) was martyred, he happened to fall asleep (during the day). He then woke up an said, 'I would inform…
narrations.summary: Katheer bin Silt reports that Uthmaan, after a nap on the day he was martyred, said he had dreamt the Prophet told him, 'You will be with us this Friday'.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration adds that that very day was Friday.
narrations.summary: Another narration adds that the day on which Uthmaan was martyred was a Friday.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat (RA) reports that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) related to them one morning that he saw Nabi ﷺ telling him in a dream, "O Uthmaan! Terminate your fast with us." Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Uthmaan told his companions one morning that the Prophet had told him in a dream to break his fast with them, so he fasted that day and was martyred on it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muslim Abu Sa'eed who was a freed slave of Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan says, "Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) set twenty slaves free and then asked for a pair of trousers,…
narrations.summary: Muslim Abu Sa'eed, a freed slave of Uthmaan, reports that Uthmaan freed twenty slaves and put on trousers for the first time, then said he had dreamt of the Prophet, Abu Bakr and Umar promising he would break his fast with them the next evening, and he was martyred while reading the Qur'aan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan (RA) or Hadhrat Husayn (RA), reports that (their father) Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "I met my beloved friend (Nabi ﷺ) in a dream and when I complained of…
narrations.summary: Hasan or Husayn, the sons of Ali, report that their father Ali said he had complained in a dream to the Prophet about the people of Iraq, and the Prophet promised deliverance soon, and Ali passed away barely three days later.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Saalih says, "Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, '1 saw Nabi ﷺ in a dream and complained to him about the way in which his Ummah are falsifying me and harming me.…
narrations.summary: Abu Saalih reports that Ali dreamt the Prophet told him to turn round and see two men in fetters whose heads were crushed by boulders and restored each time, and the next day Ali was assassinated.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Filfila Ju'fi reports that he heard Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) say, "1 saw in a dream that Nabi ﷺ was holding on to the Arsh. I then saw that Abu Bakr was holding…
narrations.summary: Filfila Ju'fi reports that Hasan bin Ali said he saw in a dream the Prophet holding the Arsh, with Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan each holding the one before him and blood flowing from the sky to the earth, and that when Shia present asked about Ali, Hasan said he would have loved Ali to be in that position.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Hasan (RA) once said, "O people! I saw a most remarkable thing in my dream last night. I saw the Rabb the Most High upon the Arsh. Rasulullaah ﷺ then arrived and…
narrations.summary: Hasan bin Ali relates a dream in which the Rabb was on the Arsh, the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan stood in order, and blood poured from the sky, and when told of it Ali replied that Hasan was only relating what he saw.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports, "In my afternoon sleep, I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ with dishevelled hair and with a glass in his hand. 'What is this glass for?' I…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that in a dream the Prophet appeared dishevelled with a glass, saying it held the blood of Husayn and his companions which he had been collecting all day, and Ibn Abbaas found that day was the day Husayn was martyred.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib (RA) says, "I was the neighbour of Umar bin Khattaab and have never seen anyone better than him. His nights were spent in salaah and his…
narrations.summary: Abbaas (RA) reports that Umar (RA) appeared to him in a dream after his death and said his reckoning was over and that only Allaah's mercy saved him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) relates, "Umar bin Khattaab was my very good friend. After he passed away, I made du'aa to Allaah for a complete year to show me Umar in a dream. The…
narrations.summary: Abbaas (RA) reports that after a year of du'aa he saw Umar (RA) in a dream, and Umar said his reckoning was over and that he was saved by a Forgiving and Merciful Rabb.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "I made du'aa to Allaah for a year to show me Umar bin Khattaab in a dream. When I saw him in a dream, I asked, 'How was your…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that after a year of du'aa he saw Umar (RA) in a dream, and Umar said he had found a Most Forgiving and Merciful Rabb.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "There was nothing I wanted more than to know what had happened to Umar (in the next life). I then saw a palace in a dream and when…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that in a dream he saw a palace belonging to his father Umar (RA), who said he had been saved by a Forgiving Rabb and had just come back from his reckoning.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat saalim bin Abdullaah reports that he once heard an Ansaari say, "I had always prayed to Allaah to show me Umar bin Khattaab in a dream. It was after ten years…
narrations.summary: Saalim bin Abdullaah reports an Ansaari's account of seeing Umar (RA) in a dream after ten years, when Umar said his reckoning was complete and he was saved only by his Rabb's mercy.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) was returning from Hajj when he (set up camp and) fell asleep at a place called Suqya. When he woke up, he said, "I just saw Umar (in a…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) reports that in a dream Umar (RA) nudged his sleeping wife awake, and that he chased Umar and caught up only after exhausting himself, which Umar said was not due to his speed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam Si reports that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) once said to him, "Dear brother! Whichever of us dies first should make an attempt to see his brother."…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Salaam says that Salmaan appeared to him in a dream after his death and advised him to hold fast to Tawakkul.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) saw Hadhrat Salmaan in a dream, he asked, "How are you faring, O Abu Abdullaah?" "I am well," came the reply.…
narrations.summary: A second report has Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) asking Salmaan (RA) in a dream which deed he found most virtuous, and Salmaan answering Tawakkul.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Auf bin Maalik (RA) relates, "I saw a leather tent and a green pasture in a dream. Around the tent there sat goats that ruminated and excreted Ajwa dates. When I…
narrations.summary: Auf bin Maalik (RA) reports seeing in a dream a tent belonging to Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, who said it was given for the Qur'aan and that Allaah had prepared a reward for Abu Dardaa because he pushed the world away.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Haraam (RA) says, "Before the Battle of Uhud I saw Mubashir bin Abdul Mundhir in a dream. He said to me, 'You will be coming to us in a few…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr bin Haraam (RA) reports that Mubashir bin Abdul Mundhir told him in a dream that the martyrs of Badr live in Jannah, and the Prophet ﷺ remarked that this is the reality of martyrdom.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) says, "Islaam came with many hardships and difficulties, but we always found the best of the good in things that seem unpleasant. When…
narrations.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) says that the Sahabah found good in hardships, such as leaving Makkah with the Prophet ﷺ and the march to Badr, and cites the Qur'aan's account of Badr.

narrations.excerpt: In his narration discussing the time when Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) was finished with the Battle of Yamaamah, Hadhrat Muhammad bin Is'haaq bin Yasaar continues to…
narrations.summary: Ibn Ishaq narrates Abu Bakr's letter to Khaalid bin Waleed after Yamaamah, ordering him to march to Iraq and urging the Muslims to fight in Allaah's path with patience and sincerity.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Utba bin Abd Sulami (RA) reports thatwhen Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed the Sahabah (RA) to stand up and fight in battle, they responded by saying, "Certainly, O…
narrations.summary: Utba bin Abd (RA) reports that the Sahabah pledged to fight with the Prophet ﷺ, and Ali (RA) rebuked an astrologer (Musaafir) for claiming to foresee harm on a journey, then marched at the hour he forbade and won at Nahrwaan.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Auf bin Ahmar reports that when Hadhrat Ali (RA) was leaving Ambaar to go to Nahrwaan, Musaafir bin Auf bin Ahmar said to him, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Auf bin Ahmar reports that when Ali (RA) was leaving for Nahrwaan, the fortune-teller Musaafir urged him to delay; Ali refused, rebuked him for claiming knowledge of the unseen, and said trust should be placed in Allaah alone, then marched and won.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Taariq bin Ziyaad reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was travelling to Shaam, Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) was accompanying him. When they arrived at a…
narrations.summary: Taariq bin Ziyaad reports that Umar (RA) waded across water in humility, and when Abu Ubaydah objected, Umar said honour comes only through Islaam.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) arrived in Shaam and was received bythepeople,hewasridingacamel. "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" someone said, "If only you would…
narrations.summary: Qais and Abul Aaliya Shaami report that Umar (RA) entering Shaam declined a Turkish horse and fine clothing, keeping his own camel and simple dress because Islaam gave him honour.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Nuhayk and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Handhala report, "We were with Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) in an army when someone recited Surah Maryam. Another man (probably a…
narrations.summary: Abu Nuhayk and Abdullaah bin Handhala report that they beat a man who reviled Maryam and Isa while they recited Surah Maryam, and Salmaan (RA) rebuked them and taught respect for others' beliefs and nafl salaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jubayr bin Nufayr (RA) says, "When Cyprus was conquered, its inhabitants were separated from each other, because of which they cried for each other. 1 then saw…
narrations.summary: Jubayr bin Nufayr (RA) reports seeing Abu Dardaa (RA) weeping after Cyprus was conquered, saying that the people were degraded because they forsook Allaah's commands and became obsessed with enslaving others.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Abu Maryam reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA), he asked, "What are the factors that will hold the foundations…
narrations.summary: Ibn Abu Maryam reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) told Umar (RA) that sincerity, salaah and obedience to the leader keep the Ummah steady, and later foretold that Umar would live only a short while.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Abdah Ambari reports that when the Muslims arrived (as conquerors) in Madaa'in and were gathering the booty together, a man arrived with a dish (full of…
narrations.summary: Abu Abdah Ambari reports that after Madaa'in was conquered a man brought a dish of jewels to the booty, refusing praise out of fear of Allaah, and was identified as Aamir bin Abd Qays.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad, ﷺ Talha, Hadhrat Muhajlab and several others reports that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) said (on the occasion of the Battle of Qaadisiyyah), "By…
narrations.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) and Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) vouch for the integrity of the army at Qaadisiyyah, and Jaabir names three men they had doubted, Tulayha, Amr bin Ma'dikarib and Qais bin Makshooh, who proved trustworthy and abstinent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) said, "I swear in the name of Allaah besides Whom there is none worthy of worship that we found no one amongst the army fighting at…
narrations.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah swears that the army at Qaadisiyyah sought the Aakhirah, and names three men whom they had doubted but who proved trustworthy and abstinent.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Qais Ijli narrates that when the Persian Emperor's sword, belt and jewels were brought to Hadhrat Umar is he remarked, "Those who have brought this must truly be…
narrations.summary: Qais Ijli reports that when the Persian emperor's sword, belt and jewels were brought to Umar (RA), Umar praised the trustworthiness of those who brought them, and Ali (RA) replied that the subjects are trustworthy because the ruler is.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) felt that Egypt was taking too long to conquer, he wrote the following letter to Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas…
narrations.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports Umar's letter to Amr bin al-Aas urging him to seek Allaah's help with sincere intentions and prayer, and a later letter sending four thousand reinforcements under commanders including Zubayr, Miqdaad, Ubaadah and Maslamah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Iyaadh Ash'ari reports that he was present during the Battle of Yarmook where there were five commanders over the Muslim army (because the five armies had merged…
narrations.summary: Iyaadh Ash'ari reports that at Yarmook five commanders shared the army with Abu Ubaydah as commander-in-chief, and the army wrote to Umar (RA) that the enemy outnumbered them and asked for reinforcements.

narrations.excerpt: "Your letter requesting me for reinforcements has reached me. 1 shall therefore refer you to one who is a more powerful helper and who has a ready army. He is Allaah. Ask…
narrations.summary: Umar (RA) replies to the army's request for reinforcements by directing them to Allaah, who helped Muhammad ﷺ at Badr when his forces were fewer than theirs.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) added, "When this letter reaches you, I want you to fight them without writing back to me." The narrator says, "We then…
narrations.summary: Umar (RA) adds that the army should fight without writing back, and after victory Iyaadh (RA) proposed exchanging ten prisoners for each Muslim, while Abu Ubaydah (RA) raced a youngster who beat him.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad, ﷺ Talha and Hadhrat Ziyaad all report that after leading the Zuhr salaah, Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) instructed a youngster to recite the Surah of Jihaad (Surah…
narrations.summary: After Zuhr, Sa'd (RA) had a young Qaari recite Surah Anfaal to the army at Qaadisiyyah, and the whole army learned it and drew tranquillity from it; another report says he ordered them to recite it to one another.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Haarith Tameemi (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent them on an expedition and instructed them to recite the following verse every morning and…
narrations.summary: Ibraheem bin Haarith Tameemi (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent a force with instructions to recite Surah Mu'minoon verse 115 every morning and evening, and they gained booty and remained safe.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad, ﷺ Talha and Hadhrat Ziyaad all report that Hadhrat Sa'd commanded the Muslims saying, "Remain in your positions and do not move until after you have…
narrations.summary: Sa'd (RA) commands the Muslims to hold position until after Zuhr, call Allaahu Akbar with each of his calls, and finally charge while reciting 'Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Illaa Billaah'.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that when the Qurraa had completed (reciting the verses of Jihaad), Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) called out (RA) ijJl)('Allaahu Akbar'). Those closest to…
narrations.summary: Sa'd (RA) calls the Takbeer three times while the Qurraa finish reciting the verses of Jihaad, the army mobilises, and the most courageous go forward; the narration is cut off.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ja'far bin Abdullaah bin Hakam reports that when Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed lost his hat during the Battle of Yarmook, he gave the order for it to be found. When…
narrations.summary: Ja'far bin Abdullaah bin Hakam reports that Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) kept a hat containing hairs of the Prophet ﷺ taken at Umrah, and was granted victory whenever he wore it into battle.

narrations.excerpt: Another narration states that Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) had a hat in which were the hairs of Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) used to say, "Whenever I confront…
narrations.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed kept a hat containing hairs of the Prophet and said he was always granted victory when he faced an enemy wearing it.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Shaqeeq says, "We started off the Battle of Qaadisiyyah at the beginning of the day and the time for Zuhr had arrived by the time we returned (from the…
narrations.summary: Shaqeeq reports that at Qaadisiyyah, when the muadhin was injured, the Sahabah eagerly competed to call the adhaan, and Sa'd (RA) settled it by drawing lots.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ma'qal bin Yasaar (RA) reports a lengthy narration concerning the conquest of Isfahaan which took place under the command of Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Muqarrin. Part of…
narrations.summary: Ma'qal bin Yasaar (RA) reports the conquest of Isfahaan, where Mughiera bin Shu'ba (RA) went as envoy to the Persian ruler Dhul Haajibayn, and Mughiera contrasted the Arabs' former poverty and the Prophet's message with the Persian splendour.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Muhammad ﷺ, Hadhrat Talha, Hadhrat Amr and Hadhrat Ziyaad all reports that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) sent for Hadhrat Mughiera and few others and said to…
narrations.summary: Rib'ee bin Aamir, Hudhayfah bin Mihsin and Mughiera bin Shu'ba (RA) each go before Rustam at Qaadisiyyah in turn; they reject the Persian display of wealth and call the Persians to Islaam, Jizya or battle.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports, "I participated in the Battle of Mu'ta. When the Mushrikeen arrived, we saw what none 'of us could ever hope to match. Their numbers…
narrations.summary: Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that at Mu'ta, daunted by the enemy's numbers, he was reminded by Thaabit bin Aqram (RA) that victory comes through Allaah, not through large numbers.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr wrote the following letter to Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) "Salaamun Alayk Your letter detailing the…
narrations.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas reports Abu Bakr's letter to Amr bin Al Aas that victory never depended on numbers, recalling Uhud and the scarce horses and camels of the Prophet's time, and urging obedience to Allaah.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ubaadah (RA) and Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) both report that a man once said to Hadhrat Khaalid (RA), "The Romans are so many and the Muslims so few!" To this, Hadhrat…
narrations.summary: Ubaadah (RA) and Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) report that Khaalid answered a man who feared the Romans' numbers by saying Muslims win through Allaah's help, not numbers, and wished the Romans were double.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Zuhri reports that after Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) assumed the office of Khilaafah, some Arabs left the fold of Islaam. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then personally marched…
narrations.summary: Zuhri reports that after some Arabs apostatised, Abu Bakr sent Khaalid bin Waleed, who defeated the false prophet Tulayha, and one of Tulayha's own men said his side fought people who wanted to die before their companions.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) says, "I was the commander of the Muslim army that marched to Alexandria. The king of the city made a request saying, 'Send out one of your…
narrations.summary: Amr bin Al Aas (RA) reports his conversation with the king of Alexandria, in which he described the Arabs' former state and the Prophet's message, and the king advised that they would prevail only while they followed their prophet's teachings.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq reports that no enemy could stand his ground before any of the Sahabah (RA) for even the time it took between two successive squeezes of a camel's…
narrations.summary: Abu Is'haaq reports that Heraclius asked why his defeated Roman army lost to Muslims who pray at night, fast by day and keep promises, and an elderly leader replied that the Romans drank, fornicated and oppressed.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Yahya bin Yahya Ghassaani reports that two men from his tribe reported, "When the Muslims set up camp outside Jordan, we talked amongst ourselves that Damascus…
narrations.summary: Yahya bin Yahya Ghassaani reports that two Arab Christians spied on the Muslims at Damascus and described them as monks by night, horsemen by day, always reciting the Qur'aan and making dhikr, and the Damascus commander said they could not be resisted.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that when the two armies confronted each other (during the Battle of Yarmook), Qubuqalaar (the Roman general) sent for an Arab man whom the…
narrations.summary: Qubuqalaar, the Roman general at Yarmook, sends a spy into the Muslim army, who reports that they are devout by night, brave horsemen by day and strict in applying justice.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Ibn Rufayl narrates that when Rustam camped at Najaf, he sent a spy from there to the Muslim army. The spy infiltrated their ranks so well at Qaadisiyyah that he…
narrations.summary: Rustam's spy reports on the Muslims' worship at Qaadisiyyah, and Rustam, watching them prepare for salaah, remarks on how Umar has shaped them.

narrations.excerpt: Hadhrat Abu Zahraa Qushayri reports from a man of the Qushayr tribe that as Heraciius was leaving for Constantinople, he met with a Roman who had been held captive by the…
narrations.summary: A Roman who had been held captive by the Muslims and then escaped describes them to Heraclius, who concludes they will inherit the land under his feet.

narrations.excerpt: (The Emperor of Persia) Yazdgird once wrote to the Emperor of China to seek reinforcements. Addressing the Persian envoy, the Chinese Emperor said, "I know well that it…
narrations.summary: After Yazdgird asks China for reinforcements, the Chinese Emperor questions the Persian envoy about the Sahabah and advises a treaty with them rather than war.
